title: The Maiden Heist
tagline: They're not bad guys, just bad thieves.
overview: A comedy centered on three museum security guards who devise a plan to steal back the artworks to which they have become attached after they are transferred to another museum.
plot:
The Maiden Heist is a 2009 American crime comedy directed by Peter Hewitt and written by Michael LeSieur. Christopher Walken plays Roger Barlow, Morgan Freeman plays Charles Peterson and William H. Macy plays George McLendon, three museum security guards, with Marcia Gay Harden as Roger's wife, Rose.

Roger spends long hours at the art museum where he works gazing at his favorite painting, The Lonely Maiden, a portrait of a woman gazing wistfully into the distance. Rose, his wife, wants him to retire so they can move to Florida. When Roger learns that the Maiden and several other works are to be sent permanently to a museum in Copenhagen, he sinks into despair, until he discovers that his colleague Charles feels the same about a painting of a woman with cats on another floor. George is devoted to a nude sculpture of a Greek warrior and often strips to pose beside it during his night shifts. George proposes that they steal their beloved pieces and substitute replicas.

Roger volunteers to tag the works being shipped while the others arrange copies. Charles, himself a painter, reproduces the cat picture flawlessly but cannot capture the Maiden, so the men hire a street artist, and Roger dips into Rose's Florida savings to pay him. Rose grows suspicious. With George's replica statue and the new Maiden finished, George hides in the crate with the statue on the night of the switch and successfully exchanges all three pieces, but he cannot resist posing naked once more, and when a guard appears he must hide in the crate without his clothes. The next morning, as Roger and Charles arrive to collect him, accompanied by an unwitting Rose, his crate is loaded onto the wrong van, and after a frantic chase they free George, who emerges naked to Rose's astonishment. Their heist undetected, the three men retire. On a trip to Florida, Roger is captivated by Rose as she gazes out at the ocean in a pose resembling the Maiden, and their romance revives. The friends keep their treasures in a shack on the roof of Charles's building, but Roger finds the painting no longer moves him as his wife does, while in Copenhagen a guard smiles at the fake.

Produced under the working title The Lonely Maiden, the film was shot mainly in Boston, with scenes at the Worcester Art Museum. A planned May 2009 release was shelved when distributor Yari Film Group went bankrupt; the film debuted at the Edinburgh International Film Festival on June 25, 2009.

title: The Shepherd: Border Patrol
tagline: Welcome To Mexico
overview: A Texas cop battles ex-navy seals who are trying to traffic drugs from Mexico into the USA.
plot:
The Shepherd: Border Patrol, also known as The Shepherd, is a 2008 American action film directed by Isaac Florentine. It stars Jean-Claude Van Damme as Jack Robideaux, a former New Orleans police officer who joins the U.S. Border Patrol, with a supporting cast including Natalie J. Robb, Stephen Lord, Gary McDonald, Scott Adkins and Van Damme's daughter Bianca Van Varenberg.

Jack arrives in Columbus, New Mexico, with a pet rabbit to take up a post with the border patrol under Captain Ramona García, played by Robb. The patrol is struggling against a dangerous smuggling operation that moves illegal immigrants and heroin across the porous border between Mexico and the United States, sometimes strapping explosive vests onto migrants so that any agent who intervenes risks being blown up. The smugglers turn out to be a rogue special forces unit led by Benjamin Meyers, played by Lord, and his right-hand man Karp, played by Adkins, who have taken over the region's trade by killing the major drug lords. Jack and his partner Billy Pawnell, played by McDonald, set out to bring the operation down.

When Meyers's men rig a missionary bus to carry drugs, Jack and Billy chase it across the border, beyond their jurisdiction, and Jack is arrested by Mexican police on Meyers's payroll and taken to the gang's compound. There he discovers that Billy is in league with Meyers, who has also kidnapped Ramona and her uncle Emile and kills Emile by throwing him into electrified water. Jack's crusade is personal: three months earlier his sixteen-year-old daughter, Kassie, played by Van Varenberg, died because of Meyers's drugs, and the rabbit he carries was hers. He swore at her grave to destroy whatever drug operation he could find. Jack and Ramona break free and kill Billy, and Ramona calls the Mexican police before being knocked out in a car crash while looking for a getaway vehicle. Jack fights the martial arts expert Karp, survives a brutal kick to the head and beats him to death. Abandoned by his would-be investors, Meyers prepares to shoot Jack, but Jack throws an explosive collar at him and detonates it. Afterward, Ramona advises Jack to return to New Orleans and his wife.

The film was shot over 47 days in Bulgaria between February and March 2007. It was released direct-to-DVD by Sony Pictures Home Entertainment in the United States on March 4, 2008, and in the United Kingdom that July.

title: Cirque du Freak: The Vampire's Assistant
original_title: Cirque du Freak: The Vampire's Assistant
tagline: Meet Darren. He's sixteen going on immortal.
overview: Darren Shan is a regular teenage kid. He and his friend Steve find out about a Freak Show coming to town and work hard at trying to find tickets. They do, and together they go to "Cirque du Freak" where they see many strange acts including a wolf-man and a bearded lady
plot:
Cirque du Freak: The Vampire's Assistant is a 2009 American vampire fantasy film directed by Paul Weitz, who wrote the screenplay with Brian Helgeland. It is loosely based on the first three books of Darren Shan's twelve-part young adult series The Saga of Darren Shan: Cirque du Freak, The Vampire's Assistant and Tunnels of Blood. Chris Massoglia stars as Darren Shan, with John C. Reilly as the vampire Larten Crepsley, Josh Hutcherson, Ken Watanabe, Salma Hayek, Willem Dafoe, Patrick Fugit and Michael Cerveris. Universal Pictures released it on 23 October 2009.

In an American town, high school student Darren Shan and his rebellious best friend Steve Leonard sneak out at night to see a traveling freak show, the Cirque du Freak. During the performance, Steve recognizes one of the performers, Larten Crepsley, as a vampire more than a century old, and goes looking for him afterward. Darren, meanwhile, is fascinated by Crepsley's performing spider, Madame Octa, and steals her. Hiding in Crepsley's dressing room, he overhears Steve begging to be made a vampire, a request that Crepsley refuses after tasting Steve's blood and declaring that it tastes of evil.

Darren escapes, and he soon encounters the mysterious Mr. Tiny and the brutish Murlough. When Madame Octa bites Steve, Darren makes a deal with Crepsley: in exchange for the antidote, he agrees to become a half-vampire and Crepsley's assistant. To protect his family, Darren fakes his own death and joins the Cirque, where he meets its remarkable performers, including the bearded lady Madame Truska, the snake boy Evra and Rebecca, a girl with a monkey's tail, with whom he begins a romance. Darren struggles with his refusal to drink human blood, while he learns that the peaceful vampires are on the brink of war with the Vampaneze, a faction of vampires who kill when they feed. Mr. Tiny, who secretly manipulates both sides, recruits a resentful Steve to the Vampaneze, setting the former friends on a collision course.

The film received poor reviews, with a 37 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus described it as an overstuffed, scattershot vampire film with poor characterization and an unwieldy mix of scares and laughs, and a Metacritic score of 43. It was a commercial failure, grossing $39.2 million against a $40 million budget, and planned sequels were never made.

title: The Time Traveler's Wife
overview: Due to a genetic disorder, handsome librarian Henry DeTamble involuntarily zips through time, appearing at various moments in the life of his true love, the beautiful artist Clare Abshire.
plot:
The Time Traveler's Wife is a 2009 American romantic science fiction drama directed by Robert Schwentke, adapted from Audrey Niffenegger's 2003 novel. Brad Pitt and Jennifer Aniston's company Plan B Entertainment optioned the book with New Line Cinema before it was even published, and the screenplay passed from Jeremy Leven to Bruce Joel Rubin, while Gus Van Sant was in talks to direct before Schwentke was hired in 2006. Eric Bana and Rachel McAdams were cast in April 2007, and filming began in Toronto that September, with additional shooting in Hamilton, Ontario. Planned for autumn 2008, the release slipped while reshoots waited for the outdoor location to match the season and for Bana to regrow his hair after Star Trek. Warner Bros. Pictures released it on August 14, 2009.

As a boy in the early 1970s, Henry DeTamble survives the car crash that kills his mother by involuntarily jumping two weeks back in time, where an older version of himself helps him. He has a genetic disorder that throws him unpredictably through time, usually toward important people and moments in his life, which he cannot alter, and he always arrives naked, so he learns early to pick locks and steal clothes. In 1991 Clare Abshire greets him joyfully at the Chicago library where he works, though he has never met her. She explains that his future self has been visiting her since she was a little girl and told her they would meet; when she turned 18, he kissed her, and she realized he would be her husband.

Their romance is strained by his sudden disappearances. At their wedding, Henry vanishes and an older version arrives to take his place. He wins the lottery with numbers learned in advance, and the couple are shaken when a wounded, middle-aged Henry briefly appears. Because their unborn children inherit his condition, Clare suffers repeated miscarriages, and Henry secretly has a vasectomy, but a visiting younger Henry fathers a child she carries to term. On a trip forward, Henry meets their daughter, Alba, a time traveler with growing control, who tells him he will die when she is five. After a frostbitten Henry jumps through time again, he is accidentally shot by Clare's father while hunting and dies in Clare's arms. Years later, a younger Henry visits and urges Clare not to spend her life waiting for him.

Bana plays Henry and McAdams plays Clare, with Ron Livingston. Reviews were mixed, with 38% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but the film was a commercial success.

title: Partly Cloudy
tagline: Charming and cute and clever
overview: Everyone knows that the stork delivers babies, but where do the storks get the babies from? The answer lies up in the stratosphere, where cloud people sculpt babies from clouds and bring them to life. Gus, a lonely and insecure grey cloud, is a master at creating "dangerous" babies. Crocodiles, porcupines, rams and more - Gus's beloved creations are works of art, but more than a handful for his loyal delivery stork partner, Peck. As Gus's creations become more and more rambunctious, Peck's job gets harder and harder. How will Peck manage to handle both his hazardous cargo and his friend's fiery temperament?
plot:
All day long, cheerful clouds in the sky make cute and cuddly babies, such as human boys and girls, kittens, puppies, and other creatures, and give them to storks for delivery to the expectant parents. However, one lonely gray cloud named Gus has the task of creating animals that are cute but not so cuddly. His delivery stork, Peck, gets the worst of it, being bitten by a crocodile, butted by a bighorn sheep, and pricked by a porcupine. When Peck sees that his next delivery is a baby shark, he grows more than a little fearful and flies away.
Feeling rejected, despondent, and angry, Gus unleashes a brief thunderstorm, then starts crying with rain pouring from below him. Peck, however, soon returns with a football helmet and shoulder pads, created for him by another cloud to keep him safe (alluded to in an earlier scene, where the same cloud creates a baby that would grow to love football). Gus instantly cheers up and gives Peck an electric eel to deliver, which shocks him despite the protective equipment; this time, though, Peck remains in good (but slightly frazzled) spirits.

title: Into the Sun
tagline: Only one man can stop the Yakuza.
overview: After the assassination of Tokyo's Governor by Yakuza members, the CIA bureau chief (William Atherton) for Tokyo puts out a call to an agent (Steven Seagal) that had been raised in Japan and trained by ex-Yakuza. Using his former ties, he quickly determines that a war is brewing between old-guard Yakuza members and a young, crazed leader (Takao Osawa) with ties to the Chinese Tong.
plot:
Into the Sun is a 2005 American action thriller directed by Christopher Morrison, credited as "mink". Steven Seagal stars and also served as producer and co-writer, with Matthew Davis, Takao Osawa, Eddie George, Juliette Marquis, Ken Lo and William Atherton in supporting roles. Filmed on location in Tokyo, the film casts Seagal as a CIA operative caught up in a conflict between the Japanese yakuza and Chinese triads. It received a theatrical release in Japan, while in the United States it was released directly to home video.

The story begins with the assassination of Takayama, the governor of Tokyo, a killing that sparks public outrage. The FBI suspects yakuza involvement and asks the CIA's Tokyo office to look into the case. Agent Travis Hunter, a veteran operative who was raised in Japan, speaks the language and understands the codes and rituals of the criminal underworld, is assigned to the investigation. He is partnered with Sean Mack, a young and inexperienced FBI agent who knows little about either CIA procedures or Japanese customs and often proves more of a hindrance than a help.

Hunter and Mack uncover a scheme by Kuroda, the ruthless leader of a new yakuza faction who rejects the traditions of the older crime families. Kuroda plans to use his export business to build a vast drug-trafficking network in partnership with Chen, the head of a Chinese triad, and he is prepared to eliminate anyone who stands in his way. As the agents examine surveillance footage and close in on the conspiracy, the case becomes personal for Hunter when people close to him are targeted, pushing him to abandon official channels and pursue his own form of justice, which culminates in a sword fight against Kuroda and his men.

The film draws on Seagal's long-standing interest in Japanese culture and martial arts, mixing gunfights, sword combat and scenes of yakuza ritual with a story about honour and revenge.

Critical reaction was mixed. Beyond Hollywood argued that the film's extensive dialogue scenes felt like padding and did not play to Seagal's strengths as an action star, while DVD Talk awarded it three stars out of five and described it as one of his better films of that period.

title: The Land Before Time X: The Great Longneck Migration
original_title: The Land Before Time X: The Great Longneck Migration
overview: A bedtime story leads Littlefoot and his grandparents on a journey to a new land, where Littlefoot discovers someone who vanished before he was born: his father! Now Littlefoot must decide between two worlds. Will he leave to be with his friends in the Great Valley, or stay behind and start a new life with his father?
plot:
The Land Before Time X: The Great Longneck Migration, also known as The Great Migration, is a 2003 American direct-to-video animated adventure musical film and the tenth installment in The Land Before Time series. Produced by Universal Cartoon Studios and released by Universal Studios Home Video on December 2, 2003, it features the voices of Alec Medlock as Littlefoot, Kenneth Mars and Miriam Flynn as his grandparents, Anndi McAfee as Cera, Aria Curzon as Ducky, Jeff Bennett as Petrie and Rob Paulsen as Spike, with Kiefer Sutherland as Bron, James Garner as Pat, Bernadette Peters as Sue and John Ingle as the narrator.

Littlefoot has a frightening "sleep story" in which the Great Circle, the sun, falls out of the sky, and he is astonished to learn that his grandparents have been having the same dream. Driven by an instinct they cannot explain, the three Longnecks set out on a journey, and Cera, Spike, Ducky and Petrie secretly follow them. Along the way Littlefoot is saved from a hungry Sarcosuchus by a Supersaurus named Sue, who feels the same pull, and dozens of other Longnecks soon join the trek. His friends, meanwhile, have their own close calls, escaping the same swamp predator and a Tyrannosaurus they mistake for a boulder, and they take shelter with Pat, a kindly old Apatosaurus. At a vast crater where hundreds of Longnecks have gathered, Littlefoot meets his biological father, Bron, for the first time. Bron explains that he was separated from Littlefoot's mother during the great earthshake and has since become the leader of a herd and guardian to Shorty, a mischievous young Brachiosaurus who quickly grows jealous of the attention Bron gives his son. Pat tells the children about the reason for the migration: according to Longneck tradition, during a solar eclipse the jealous Night Circle tries to knock the sun out of the sky, and Longnecks from everywhere gather to stretch their necks upward and push it back. As the day of the eclipse approaches, Littlefoot must win over his resentful new brother, while the herd faces a group of Sharpteeth that threaten the gathering just as the sky begins to darken.

The film was nominated for Best Animated DVD Premiere Movie and Best Original Song at the 2003 DVD Exclusive Awards, losing to 101 Dalmatians II: Patch's London Adventure and Run Ronnie Run!, respectively.

title: The Land Before Time XI: Invasion of the Tinysauruses
original_title: The Land Before Time XI: Invasion of the Tinysauruses
overview: While trying to obtain "Tree Sweets", Littlefoot falls into the tree and knocks down all the blossoms attracting the Tinysauruses. They devour the plants and disappear. But Littlefoot isn't blamed for the disappearance. Instead, he accidentally makes the adults believe the tiny dinosaurs were the main cause. Now Littlefoot and his friends must protect the tiny herd and learn the value of honesty.
plot:
The Land Before Time XI: Invasion of the Tinysauruses is a 2005 American direct-to-video animated film and the eleventh installment in The Land Before Time series, which began with Don Bluth's 1988 feature. Released by Universal Studios Home Entertainment on January 11, 2005, it follows the young dinosaur Littlefoot and his friends Cera, Ducky, Petrie and Spike in a story about honesty, size and friendship.

Every year, as the warm season begins, a single tree in the Great Valley blooms with sweet pink flowers that the inhabitants consider a delicacy. Because there are so few, the dinosaurs gather to eat them together on Nibbling Day, and Cera's father, Mr. Threehorn, guards the tree until then. He is visited by his childhood friend Tria, to whom he promises the first treesweet, making Cera jealous. When Cera teases Littlefoot about his size, he tries to prove himself by climbing a cliff to reach the treesweets early, but falls into the tree and knocks all of them down.

When Littlefoot wakes up, he sees a group of tiny dinosaurs eating the fallen treesweets. When the adults discover that the tree is bare, everyone suspects Littlefoot, who, afraid of being punished, blames the whole thing on the "Tinysauruses". The adults set out to hunt down the little creatures as pests. Littlefoot later finds the Tinysauruses living underground, befriends them and secretly brings them food, but their leader, Big Daddy, distrusts the larger dinosaurs. As the lie spirals out of control and the adults close in on the Tinysauruses' home, Littlefoot must tell the truth, repair his friendships and help protect his tiny new friends when two hungry Utahraptors invade the valley.

The film teaches that honesty matters and that even small creatures can make a big difference, ending with all the dinosaurs sharing the treesweets together on Nibbling Day.

Like the earlier sequels, the film was made for young children and released directly to home video, continuing the long-running franchise. Its story introduces the Tinysauruses, small dinosaurs whose scale lets the film explore its theme of size and importance.

title: Dug's Special Mission
overview: Dug is sent on foolish missions by Alpha, Beta, and Gamma so they can hunt for the Bird of Paradise Falls by themselves. Dug may find that where he belongs is not where he's been looking.
plot:
Dug's Special Mission is a 2009 American computer-animated short film from Pixar, directed by Ronnie del Carmen and released as a companion to the feature Up on its Blu-ray and DVD editions, and later on Pixar Short Films Collection: Volume 2. Bob Peterson voices the talking golden retriever Dug as well as the pack leader Alpha, with Delroy Lindo as Beta, Jerome Ranft as Gamma, and Ed Asner and Jordan Nagai reprising their roles as Carl Fredricksen and Russell. Up's producer Jonas Rivera described the short as a glimpse of what Dug was doing on his mysterious mission when audiences first meet him in the feature.

The story takes place during the events of Up. It is Dug's birthday, and the cheerful, simple-minded dog, whose special collar allows him to speak, hopes it will be the happiest day of his life. Instead, he gets in the way of the pack of dogs serving the explorer Charles F. Muntz, who are hunting the giant exotic bird Kevin. The pack's leaders, Alpha, a Doberman with a malfunctioning collar that makes his voice comically high-pitched, Beta, a Rottweiler, and Gamma, a bulldog, are irritated by his blundering and invent a series of "special missions" for him that are really meant to keep him out of their way.

Each assignment backfires spectacularly. Told to guard the bird's "favourite rock" and make sure it does not move, Dug dislodges a pebble that sends a boulder rolling toward the pack. Ordered to sit in the bird's "favourite hole", he sinks through quicksand and lands on the others just as they are about to spring their trap. Told to sit on a rock, he sends Alpha, Beta and Gamma tumbling down a cliff. A string of further mishaps follows, as Dug's obedient attempts to follow orders trigger the very traps laid for Kevin, entangling the pack in nets, firing tranquilliser darts and toppling rock columns with Alpha on top.

Furious, Alpha reports to Muntz that Dug has ruined their hunt. Seeing Muntz's airship, the Spirit of Adventure, in the sky and fearing punishment, Dug flees into a misty, rocky landscape, while Beta sarcastically wishes him a happy birthday. There he notices rocks shaped like a turtle and a man, and when he hears a voice saying "I see you back there", he realises he has found what he wished for: a new master, Carl. The short then joins the moment in Up when Russell first mistakes Dug for a rock, and ends with Dug's greeting, "Hi there!"

Reviewers noted its mild slapstick violence, more humorous than upsetting.

title: Blind Horizon
overview: Left for dead in the remote Southwest, Frank is found clinging to life and in a state of amnesia. As he recovers, ominous memories begin to flash back...
plot:
Blind Horizon is a 2003 American conspiracy mystery thriller directed by Michael Haussman from a screenplay by F. Paul Benz and Steve Tomlin. Val Kilmer stars as a man who wakes with amnesia and a premonition of a presidential assassination, alongside Neve Campbell, Sam Shepard, Amy Smart and Faye Dunaway.

On the outskirts of rural New Mexico, two ranch hands discover an unconscious man, Frank Kavanaugh, suffering from a gunshot wound to the head. He is rushed to the hospital in the small town of Black Point and placed in intensive care under the watch of a trauma nurse named Liz. When he wakes, he is questioned by Sheriff Kolb but cannot explain what happened because the injury has left him with temporary amnesia. Kavanaugh, increasingly agitated, insists that he knows of a plot to assassinate the president of the United States. The hospital's doctor attributes this to paranoid delusions caused by his brain trauma.

Kavanaugh is haunted by fragmentary images that might be real memories or pure fantasy, the most vivid of which shows a shadowy figure discussing an assassination with a mysterious woman known as Ms. K. Unable to separate reality from imagination, he finds an unexpected ally in Sheriff Kolb, who begins to think his story may have some credibility. The situation grows more complicated with the arrival of Chloe, who says she is his fiancée and provides documents showing that they live in Chicago, that Kavanaugh works for the Internal Revenue Service and that the couple were in New Mexico on vacation. Still convinced of the danger, Kavanaugh telephones the Secret Service to warn of an attempt on the president's life in Black Point, just as news reports announce that the president's campaign tour will soon pass through the area.

When the president arrives to address a crowd, Kavanaugh tries to follow the clues he has pieced together. In a building overlooking the event, he finds a set of sniper's equipment and gradually confronts the truth about who he really is and what his own role in the plot was meant to be. Spotting another gunman preparing to fire from across the way, Kavanaugh takes aim and kills him, preventing the assassination.

Kilmer was attached in October 2002, and the rest of the principal cast joined that December. The New Mexico Investment Council invested $4.7 million through an interest-free loan in exchange for a share of profits, and the film was shot in the state.

title: An Education
tagline: An education isn't always by the book.
overview: Despite her sheltered upbringing, Jenny is a teen with a bright future; she's smart, pretty, and has aspirations of attending Oxford University. When David, a charming but much older suitor, motors into her life in a shiny automobile, Jenny gets a taste of adult life that she won't soon forget.
plot:
In 1961 London, Jenny Mellor is a bright and attractive 16-year-old schoolgirl who aspires to attend the University of Oxford. Her studies are controlled by her strict father, Jack. After youth orchestra rehearsals, Jenny waits at a bus stop on the street in heavy rain when David Goldman, an older man, stops his Bristol 405 and tells her that he is a music lover and is worried about her cello getting wet. He persuades Jenny to put her cello in his car while she walks alongside. As the rain becomes heavier, Jenny asks David if she can sit inside the car. The two talk about music and, before being dropped off, Jenny confides that she is looking forward to attending university and being able to live a life of culture, doing things such as going to art galleries and watching French films. The following week, David has flowers delivered to Jenny's house, wishing her luck at her youth orchestra's concert. Later, she sees him in town and approaches him. David asks Jenny if she is free to go and see a concert and have supper with him and his friends. She happily agrees and thanks him.
On the night of the concert, Jack disapproves of Jenny going, but when David comes by to pick up Jenny, he easily charms Jack into letting him take Jenny and bring her home later than her normal curfew. Arriving at the concert, Jenny meets David's friends, Danny and Helen. Afterwards, they go to dinner at a fancy restaurant with live music much to Jenny's liking. Finding she is also interested in art, they invite Jenny to an art auction. David picks up Jenny at school and they go to the auction, winning a bid for a painting by Edward Burne-Jones and going to Danny's place afterwards. They talk about Oxford and all agree to go and visit together the following weekend.
Jenny hears a commotion late one night and sees David drinking with her parents. He then uses the opportunity to ask them if he can take Jenny to Oxford, saying that he used to study there and would like to visit his old teacher, Clive Lewis, the author of The Chronicles of Narnia. Her parents are reluctant at first, but agree, seeing it as a good opportunity. At Oxford, Jenny discovers that David makes his money through a variety of shady practices, and although initially shocked succumbs to David's persuasive talk. Back outside her home, Jenny and David have their first kiss. Jenny then shows a signed copy of The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe to her parents (in fact, she had seen David sign it, and they had never met Lewis). Impressed by David's apparent connections and charisma, Jack and Marjorie approve of their romantic relationship.
On the night of Jenny's 17th birthday, David arrives with presents and tells her parents that he intends to take them all to Paris as a special birthday gift. Her father demurs, but following a conversation with David agrees to Jenny going with him alone. In Paris, the two go sight-seeing, take photos, and go dancing, and Jenny loses her virginity to David.

A long fight ensues between our heroes and Cooler, in which he transforms into the fourth stage of his evolution and has the edge in the fight... until Goku transforms into a Super Saiyan.
plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge is a 1991 Japanese animated science fantasy martial arts film directed by Daisuke Nishio and produced by Toei Animation. The movie takes place after the events of the Dragon Ball Z series, specifically during the Frieza Saga.

The story begins with Goku (Gō Tenryūbu no Shain) and his friends, including Krillin (Kuririn), Tenshinhan (Tenshīhan), Yamcha (Yamucha), and Bulma (Burmā), returning to Earth after their battle against Frieza. However, they soon discover that a new threat has emerged in the form of Cooler, Frieza's brother.

Cooler is determined to surpass his brother's power and become the most powerful being in the universe. He sets his sights on destroying Earth and its inhabitants, with Goku and his friends standing in his way. The movie follows their epic battle against Cooler, who possesses incredible strength and abilities that rival those of Frieza.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Cooler's motivations are not entirely driven by a desire for power, but also by a sense of revenge against his brother, whom he feels has wronged him in the past. This adds a layer of complexity to Cooler's character, making him a more nuanced and interesting villain than Frieza.

Throughout the movie, Goku and his friends face numerous challenges as they attempt to defeat Cooler. They are aided by their allies, including Piccolo (Pikku), who has returned from the dead to help them in their battle against Cooler. The movie features epic battles, intense training sequences, and emotional moments that explore the relationships between the characters.

One of the most notable aspects of Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge is its exploration of Goku's character development. As he faces off against Cooler, Goku is forced to confront his own limitations and weaknesses, leading to a significant growth in his abilities and understanding of himself.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Goku and Cooler, which pushes both characters to their limits. In the end, Goku emerges victorious, but not without suffering some serious injuries. The movie concludes with Goku reflecting on the lessons he has learned from his battle against Cooler, setting the stage for future adventures in the Dragon Ball Z universe.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge is a thrilling and action-packed adventure that explores themes of power, revenge, and friendship. With its epic battles, memorable characters, and emotional moments, it remains a beloved entry in the Dragon Ball Z franchise.

title: Julie & Julia
tagline: Based on Two True Stories.
overview: Julia Child and Julie Powell – both of whom wrote memoirs – find their lives intertwined. Though separated by time and space, both women are at loose ends... until they discover that with the right combination of passion, fearlessness and butter, anything is possible.
plot:
Julie & Julia is a 2009 film that weaves together two seemingly disparate narratives: the life of French chef Auguste Gusteau and the story of American blogger Julie Powell. At its core, the movie explores the universal themes of passion, creativity, and the pursuit of one's dreams.

The film delves into the idea of finding one's true calling and the importance of following one's heart. Julie Powell, a struggling writer, embarks on a journey to cook all 524 recipes from Julia Child's iconic cookbook "Mastering the Art of French Cooking." Through her culinary adventures, she discovers a sense of purpose and confidence that transforms her life.

The movie also touches upon the theme of legacy and the impact one person can have on others. Auguste Gusteau, the legendary chef, left behind a culinary empire built on the principles of "anyone can cook," which becomes a guiding philosophy for Julie as she navigates her own creative journey.

Furthermore, the film highlights the importance of community and connection in our lives. Through Julie's blog and her interactions with fellow food enthusiasts, she finds a sense of belonging and support that helps her stay motivated and inspired throughout her culinary journey.

Ultimately, Julie & Julia is a heartwarming story about embracing one's passions, taking risks, and finding joy in the process of creating something beautiful. The movie celebrates the power of food to bring people together and transcend cultural boundaries, leaving viewers with a deeper appreciation for the art of cooking and the importance of living life to the fullest.

The elves, along with Max's dog Buddy (a Golden Retriever), embark on a mission to retrieve the crystal and save Christmas. Along the way, they meet a group of puppies, including Buddy, who are also being used by St. Nick for evil purposes.

As the story unfolds, the puppies, led by Buddy, work together with the elves to outsmart St. Nick's henchmen and retrieve the magical crystal. The puppies use their unique skills and abilities to help the elves in their mission, showcasing their loyalty and teamwork.

Meanwhile, Max struggles with his own identity as an elf, feeling like he doesn't quite fit in with the rest of the group. With the help of Buddy and the other puppies, Max finds his place and learns to believe in himself.

As Christmas Eve approaches, the elves and puppies face off against St. Nick in a final showdown. The puppies use their skills and teamwork to defeat St. Nick's henchmen, while Max and Buddy work together to retrieve the magical crystal.

In the end, the elves and puppies succeed in retrieving the crystal, and Santa is able to deliver presents on Christmas Eve. Max finds his place among the elves, and Buddy becomes a hero for saving Christmas. The movie ends with a heartwarming scene of the elves and puppies celebrating Christmas together.

Overall, Santa Buddies is a fun and entertaining holiday film that showcases the importance of teamwork, loyalty, and believing in oneself. With its lighthearted tone and adorable canine characters, it's a great choice for families to enjoy during the holiday season.

title: Still Walking
original_title: 歩いても 歩いても
overview: Twelve years after their beloved eldest son, Junpei, drowned while saving a stranger's life, Kyohei and Toshiko welcome their surviving children home for a family reunion. Younger son Ryota still feels that his parents resent that he isn't the one who died; his new wife, Yukari, is awkwardly meeting the rest of the family for the first time. Daughter Chinami strains to fill the uncomfortable pauses with forced cheer.
plot:
Still Walking (Japanese: 歩いても 歩いても, Aruitemo aruitemo) is a 2008 Japanese family drama film written, directed and edited by Hirokazu Kore-eda. It portrays a family over roughly twenty-four hours as they gather to mark the anniversary of the eldest son's death. Hiroshi Abe stars as Ryota Yokoyama, with Yui Natsukawa as his wife Yukari, You as his sister Chinami, Kirin Kiki as his mother Toshiko and Yoshio Harada as his father Kyohei. Kore-eda has said that much of the film was inspired by memories of his own childhood and of his mother's death.

Every year the Yokoyama family come together to remember Junpei, the eldest son, who drowned twelve years earlier while saving a boy's life. Kyohei, a retired doctor, and Toshiko welcome their surviving son Ryota, who has recently married Yukari, a widow with a young son named Atsushi, and their daughter Chinami with her husband and children. Ryota resents the knowledge that Junpei was the favorite, whose belongings Toshiko still keeps untouched, while the bitter Kyohei has never forgiven Ryota for becoming an art restorer instead of following Junpei into medicine and taking over the family practice. Chinami, meanwhile, pushes to move her family into her aging parents' home. The elderly couple are at first cool toward Yukari, thinking it unlucky for their son to marry a widow, but gradually warm to her and to the shy Atsushi. Over a day of reminiscing and small talk, Ryota privately admits to Yukari that he is struggling to find work. In the evening they receive their annual visit from Yoshio, the boy Junpei saved, now an aimless young man whom most of the family resent; when Ryota asks his mother to stop inviting him, Toshiko reveals that making him come back each year is the least he owes them, since the grief would be unbearable without someone to blame. Small moments at dinner and through the night, including a revelation about a favorite song, expose decades of quiet disappointment in the parents' marriage, as the family's unspoken wounds rise to the surface before the visitors leave.

Still Walking received wide critical acclaim, holding a perfect 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from 64 reviews, whose consensus describes it as a modest-seeming family drama that casts a delicate, entrancing spell. Roger Ebert gave it four stars and called Kore-eda an heir of Yasujirō Ozu. It won the Golden Astor for Best Film at the 2008 Mar del Plata International Film Festival and the Asian Film Award for Best Director.

title: Miracles
tagline: Meet the original gangster!
overview: A country boy becomes the head of a gang through the purchase of some lucky roses from an old lady. He and a singer at the gang's nightclub try to do a good deed for the old lady when her daughter comes to visit.
plot:
Miracles (Chinese: 奇蹟) is a 1989 Hong Kong action comedy directed by and starring Jackie Chan, who co-wrote the screenplay with Edward Tang. Set in 1930s Hong Kong, it is an adaptation of Frank Capra's Lady for a Day (1933) and its remake Pocketful of Miracles (1961), both based on Damon Runyon's 1929 short story "Madame La Gimp." Anita Mui co-stars, with Gua Ah-leh, Richard Ng, Ko Chun-hsiung, Wu Ma and Bill Tung. Chan is a devoted fan of Hollywood musicals, and the film pays tribute to the genre; it is often considered one of his most sophisticated works as a director and is known in some markets as The Canton Godfather or Mr. Canton and Lady Rose.

Kuo Cheng-wah, a kind-hearted young man from the countryside, arrives in Hong Kong and is immediately cheated out of all his money. Penniless, he meets Madame Kao, a poor old woman who sells flowers on the street, and she persuades him to buy a red rose for luck. His fortunes change when he stumbles into a gang fight and helps a dying gang boss, who unexpectedly names him as his successor before he dies. Believing that the rose brought him his luck, Kuo buys one from Madame Kao every day thereafter.

Kuo's new position angers Fei, a gang member who expected to inherit the leadership, but with help from the late boss's loyal right-hand man, Uncle Hoi, Kuo wins the respect of the gang. He reluctantly accepts his role but tries to find legitimate businesses for his men, eventually opening a nightclub with Yang Luming, a singer who comes to him to settle a debt owed to the gang. When Kuo learns that Madame Kao has been deceiving her daughter, who has been raised abroad and is returning to Hong Kong with her fiancé and his aristocratic father, into believing that she is a wealthy society lady, he decides to help her keep up the illusion. Kuo, Luming and the gang transform the flower seller into a grand dame, staging an elaborate deception while dealing with gang rivals, the police and the collapsing facade of the charade.

Miracles was a success in Asia and has been praised for its elaborate set pieces, including a celebrated fight sequence in a rope factory, and for its period production design. Rotten Tomatoes reports that 60 percent of five surveyed critics gave it a positive review. Chan has said that it is his favorite among the films he directed.

title: Beyond a Reasonable Doubt
tagline: Why would a man frame himself... for murder?
overview: Remake of a 1956 Fritz Lang film in which a novelist's investigation of a dirty district attorney leads to a setup within the courtroom.
plot:
Beyond a Reasonable Doubt is a 2009 American crime thriller written, photographed and directed by Peter Hyams, starring Jesse Metcalfe, Amber Tamblyn and Michael Douglas. A reworking of Fritz Lang's 1956 film of the same name, it was Hyams' second remake of an RKO property after Narrow Margin (1990). It opened in Spain in July 2009, ahead of a limited US release.

C.J. Nicholas, a Shreveport television reporter, made his name with an award-winning documentary about a teenage prostitute who died of an overdose. Now trying to revive his career through an investigative unit with his colleague Corey Finley, he is convinced that District Attorney Mark Hunter, a former detective with gubernatorial ambitions, owes his flawless conviction record to evidence planted at the last minute. While dating Assistant District Attorney Ella Crystal, who works for Hunter, he finds indications that Hunter's former partner, Lieutenant Merchant, plants suspects' DNA, but he cannot prove it, and budget cuts kill his unit.

Determined to expose Hunter, Nicholas sets out to frame himself for the recent murder of a prostitute. With Finley filming, he buys items tying him to the crime, holding dated newspapers to prove they were acquired after the killing. The footage is stored in Finley's desk, with a backup in a safe-deposit box. After a staged arrest he is charged with the murder, but Merchant discovers the scheme. Finley is killed in a car chase with Merchant and both videos are destroyed, so when Nicholas reveals his plan in court, he has only receipts, and Hunter persuades the jury that the victim's blood found on the planted items proves his guilt. Nicholas is sentenced to death.

Crystal investigates on her own and learns that crime-scene photographs from Hunter's cases were digitally altered. When Merchant tries to run her down, he is shot dead by a detective who had been tailing him, and Hunter is arrested in disgrace. Nicholas is freed and becomes a celebrity. Rewatching his documentary, however, Crystal recognises the hands of the supposed prostitute as those of the murder victim, and realises that Nicholas hired the woman to fake his documentary and later killed her when she tried to blackmail him. Because his case ended in a mistrial, he is not protected by double jeopardy, and she leaves as police arrive to arrest him.

The film was panned, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 7% approval, its consensus calling it a hackneyed courtroom drama with a predictable twist.

title: The Banishment
tagline: If you want to kill, kill. If you want to forgive, forgive.
overview: After receiving an unexpected visit from his mysteriously injured brother Mark, Alex decides to take his family back to the country home of his childhood, but once there, Alex's wife Vera confesses that she is pregnant again and that the child is not his. Agony ensues as Alex attempts to figure out how best to react.
plot:
The Banishment (Russian: Изгнание, Izgnanie) is a 2007 Russian psychological drama film directed by Andrey Zvyagintsev, loosely adapted from The Laughing Matter, a 1953 novel by the Armenian-American writer William Saroyan. Konstantin Lavronenko stars as Alex and Maria Bonnevie as his wife Vera, with Aleksandr Baluev as Alex's brother Mark, Maksim Shibayev and Katya Kulkina as the couple's children Kir and Eva, and Dmitri Ulyanov as Alex's friend and co-worker Robert. The screenplay came to Zvyagintsev from Artyom Melkumian, an Armenian friend and television cameraman who had spent ten years adapting Saroyan's novel, and the director cut much of its original dialogue after testing it with actors.

The film begins with Mark arriving at his brother Alex's house with a bullet wound in his arm, which Alex removes because Mark's criminal connections make a hospital visit too risky. Soon afterwards Alex takes Vera and their two children to his childhood home in the countryside. The rural calm is shattered when Vera tells Alex that she is pregnant and that the child is not his. The couple keep up appearances in front of the children and visiting friends while the rift between them deepens, and Alex turns to Mark for advice. When Kir mentions that Alex's friend Robert visited the house while Alex was away on business, Alex concludes that Robert is the father. Vera, increasingly isolated, fears that her son will follow his father and uncle into the criminal world. Determined to save the marriage by removing the unborn child, Alex forces Vera to undergo an abortion, which Mark arranges through his criminal contacts to be performed at home while the children are away. The decision sets off a chain of tragedy that engulfs the whole family, and Alex eventually returns to the city intent on revenge against Robert, where a long-hidden truth about Vera's pregnancy and her despair awaits him.

The Banishment premiered in competition for the Palme d'Or at the 2007 Cannes Film Festival, where Lavronenko won the award for Best Actor, and opened in Russian cinemas on 2 October 2007. Reviews were mixed: it holds a 65% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 59, while David Gritten of The Daily Telegraph called it a mythic masterpiece.

title: Leap Year
tagline: Anna planned to propose to her boyfriend on February 29th. This is not her boyfriend.
overview: When yet another anniversary passes without a marriage proposal from her boyfriend, Anna decides to take action. Aware of a Celtic tradition that allows women to pop the question on Feb. 29, she plans to follow her lover to Dublin and ask him to marry her. Fate has other plans, however, and Anna winds up on the other side of the Emerald Isle with handsome, but surly, Declan -- an Irishman who may just lead Anna down the road to true love.
plot:
Leap Year is a 2010 romantic comedy directed by Anand Tucker and written by Harry Elfont and Deborah Kaplan. Amy Adams and Matthew Goode star, with Adam Scott and John Lithgow in supporting roles. Principal photography took place across Ireland, in locations including County Wicklow, Dublin, County Mayo, County Galway, the Aran Islands and Connemara.

Anna Brady is a Boston real estate stager who has grown frustrated that Jeremy, her boyfriend of four years, has still not proposed, even though the couple are about to move into an upscale apartment together. When Jeremy travels to Dublin for a cardiology conference, Anna decides to follow him and take matters into her own hands by invoking an Irish tradition, sometimes called Bachelor's Day, that allows a woman to propose to a man on February 29.

Her journey goes wrong almost immediately. A storm diverts her flight to Cardiff in Wales, and the boat she hires to cross the Irish Sea is forced to put her ashore in the small seaside village of Dingle, on the opposite side of Ireland. There she asks Declan O'Callaghan, the gruff owner of the struggling local pub, to drive her to Dublin. He refuses at first, but because his pub faces foreclosure, he agrees to take her for 500 euros. Declan openly mocks her plan, and the trip turns into a string of mishaps: a herd of cows blocks the road, their car rolls into a stream, they miss a train, and they are forced to pose as a married couple to secure a room at a bed and breakfast. Along the way, the bickering pair grow closer and Anna begins to question what she really wants.

When she finally reaches Dublin, Jeremy unexpectedly proposes to her first, and she accepts. Back in Boston, however, she comes to suspect that his gesture was motivated by securing their apartment rather than by love, and she returns to Dingle to find Declan, leading to a final romantic reversal of the leap-day tradition.

The film was poorly received by critics. Rotten Tomatoes gives it a 24% approval rating from 144 reviews, with an average of 4.3/10; its consensus said that Adams was as appealing as ever but that the film succumbed to an overabundance of clichés. It was nevertheless a modest commercial success, earning more than its production budget at the worldwide box office, and its Irish scenery was frequently singled out as one of its main attractions.

title: Crazy Heart
tagline: The harder the life, the sweeter the song.
overview: When reporter Jean Craddock interviews Bad Blake—an alcoholic, seen-better-days country music legend—they connect, and the hard-living crooner sees a possible saving grace in a life with Jean and her young son.
plot:
Otis "Bad" Blake is a 57-year-old alcoholic singer-songwriter who was once a country music star. He now earns a modest living by performing in small-town bars across the southwestern United States. Having a history of failed marriages (four that he admits to, although a reference is made to a fifth he does not discuss), Blake is without a family. He has a son, aged 28, with whom he has not had contact in 24 years. He is mostly on the road performing, staying in cheap motels, and travelling alone in his 1978 Chevrolet Suburban. The film opens with his arrival at a bowling alley for a show.
In Santa Fe, he meets Jean Craddock, a young journalist after a story, divorced and with a four-year-old son, Buddy. She interviews Blake one evening after his gig, and then as they become close, Jean visits again ostensibly to gather more material, and the two enter into a relationship. Jean and her son become a catalyst for Blake to get his life back on track. In doing so, he lets himself be pushed into renewing a professional relationship with Tommy Sweet, a popular and successful country music star he once mentored, and plays as the opening act at one of his concerts, despite his initial balking and wounded pride at being the opening act to his former student. He asks Tommy to record an album with him, but Tommy says his record company insists on a couple more solo albums before a duet project can be recorded. He instead suggests that Blake concentrate on writing new songs that Tommy can record solo, telling him he writes better songs than anyone else.
Blake's drinking soon gets out of control and he ends up running off the road while driving drunk. In the hospital, the doctor informs him that although he only sustained a broken ankle from the crash, he is slowly killing himself, and must stop drinking and smoking and lose 25 pounds if he wants to live more than a few more years. Blake's relationship with Jean makes him start to rethink his life. While in Houston, he calls up his son to make amends, only to learn that his mother, Bad's ex-wife, has died. Jean and her son begin to visit more frequently, but after Blake briefly loses Buddy at a shopping mall while drinking at a bar, Jean breaks up with him.
Blake resolves to quit drinking, and after going through a treatment program at a rehab center, with support from an Alcoholics Anonymous group and old friend Wayne, he finally manages to get sober. Having cleaned up his act, he tries to reunite with Jean but, despite congratulating him on getting sober and wishing him well, she tells Blake that the best thing he can do for her and Buddy is to leave them alone. Later, Blake finishes writing a song that he thinks is his best ever, "The Weary Kind", and sells it to Tommy.
Sixteen months later, Tommy plays "The Weary Kind" to an appreciative audience while Blake watches backstage, as his manager presents him with another of the large royalty checks for the song.

title: The True Story of Puss 'n Boots
original_title: La véritable histoire du Chat Botté
overview: A free adaptation of Charles Perrault's famous Puss'n Boots, "The True Story of Puss'n Boots" is a story for young and old for the first time on cinema screens.
plot:
The True Story of Puss 'n Boots (French: La Véritable Histoire du chat botté), also released in English as The True History of Puss 'N Boots, is a 2009 French computer-animated comedy directed by Jérôme Deschamps, Pascal Hérold and Macha Makeïeff, who also wrote it. A free, comic adaptation of Charles Perrault's fairy tale, it was produced by Hérold and Family with partners including MK2, France 3 Cinéma, Nadeo and the Deschamps–Makeïeff company, and was released in France on 1 April 2009. The animation was rendered with technology from the video game studio Nadeo, best known for the TrackMania series.

When a miller dies, his two elder sons inherit the mill, while the youngest, Pierre, is left only his father's cat. Pierre is disappointed until he discovers that the animal is no ordinary cat: he talks nonstop, walks on his hind legs and, once Pierre makes him a pair of red leather boots, proves endlessly resourceful. In return the cat promises to help his young master win the heart of the princess he adores, a free-spirited girl who secretly sings and dances, and whose hand is also coveted by the king's scheming chamberlain, who has designs on the throne.

Posing as a baron, the cat brings gifts of game to the royal court on behalf of an imaginary Marquis of Carabas, then stages the famous trick in which Pierre bathes in a lake as the royal coach passes and claims that robbers stole his clothes. The queen dresses him in finery and invites him to dine and attend a ball. With the help of his friend Doc Marcel, a chimpanzee who plays music to calm a fearsome ogre in his mountain castle, the cat discovers that the chamberlain is allied with the ogre and makes magic sweets that turn people into animals. Using one of them, the cat turns the ogre into a duck, letting Pierre present the castle as his own. Pierre confesses the truth to the princess, who values his honesty and agrees to marry him; the chamberlain ends up transformed by his own sweets, and the cat declines the post offered to him and goes his own way.

The French voice cast features Jérôme Deschamps as the cat, Arthur Deschamps as Pierre, Louise Wallon as the princess, Yolande Moreau as the queen, Jean-Claude Bolle-Reddat as the chamberlain, Atmen Kelif as Doc Marcel and André Wilms as the ogre. The music, by the band Moriarty, mixes original songs with reworked classical pieces by composers including Beethoven, Mozart and Verdi. In the American English dub, the cat is voiced by William Shatner.

title: The Secret in Their Eyes
tagline: An unsolved crime. A love story. An unwritten ending.
overview: A retired legal counselor writes a novel hoping to find closure for one of his past unresolved homicide cases and for his unreciprocated love with his superior - both of which still haunt him decades later.
plot:
In June 1974, judiciary agent Benjamín Espósito investigates the rape and murder of Liliana Colotto. Espósito promises her husband, Ricardo Morales, that he will find the killer and ensure a life sentence. Espósito is assisted by his alcoholic partner Pablo Sandoval and the new department chief, Irene Menéndez-Hastings. Romano, Espósito's rival, accuses a pair of construction workers (one of whom is a Bolivian immigrant) of the murder, angering Espósito upon discovering that both of them were tortured to obtain a confession.
Espósito finds a lead while looking at old photos of Liliana, which Ricardo gave him. Many of them feature a man, identified as Isidoro Gómez, staring obsessively at her. Espósito and Sandoval sneak into Gómez's mother's house in Chivilcoy. During the break-in, they find some letters from Gómez to his mother. Sandoval steals them, and Espósito finds out upon returning to Buenos Aires. Their "visit" only causes trouble with their higher-ups, and they are unable to find any evidence in the letters. Gómez remains at large due to a careless phone call from Ricardo to Gómez's mother in a desperate quest for his wife's killer. Ultimately, the case is closed.
In 1975, Espósito finds Ricardo in a train station in Retiro and discovers that he was trying to find Gómez in multiple stations. Espósito convinces Irene to reopen the investigation. Meanwhile, while getting drunk in a bar, Sandoval makes a discovery: an acquaintance of his identifies several names on the letters—seemingly without any connection—as footballers of Racing Club. After identifying him as a Racing fan, Espósito and Sandoval attend a game between Racing and Huracán, hoping to find Gómez.
While keeping an eye on the game's attendees in Huracán's stadium, Espósito and Sandoval locate Gómez among the crowd, but a sudden goal causes a hubbub and allows Gómez to flee. A chase ensues, and Gómez is caught by the stadium's security guards as he invades the pitch. Espósito and Irene then grill him illegally, and Irene makes Gómez confess by calling him physically weak and attacking his masculinity. Gómez is tried and sentenced, but Romano bails him out one month later to get revenge on Espósito and hires him as a hitman for the right-wing faction of the Peronist Party. Espósito and Irene try to reverse it but are stopped by Romano's intervention. Espósito informs Ricardo that his wife's killer will never go to prison.
Weeks later, Sandoval gets into a bar fight, causing Espósito to take him to his flat and fetch his wife. When Espósito and Sandoval's wife return, they find the door pried open, Espósito's pictures flipped over, and Sandoval shot dead in his room. Espósito soon concludes that Romano sent assassins after him, but Sandoval impersonated him to protect his friend. Fearing for his life, Espósito goes into hiding for 10 years in Jujuy Province with Irene's cousins. Espósito returns to Buenos Aires in 1985 to find Gómez missing and Irene married with two children.

title: Merry Madagascar
overview: The Zoosters are back in an all-new holiday adventure. When Santa and his reindeer crash onto the island of Madagascar it's up to Alex, Marty, Gloria, Melman and those wacky penguins to save Christmas. Get ready for a sleigh full of laughs in this hilarious new holiday classic.
plot:
Merry Madagascar is an American animated Christmas television special produced by DreamWorks Animation, first broadcast on NBC on November 17, 2009. Set between the first two Madagascar films, it was the studio's second holiday special after Shrek the Halls. It features Ben Stiller as Alex the lion, Chris Rock as Marty the zebra, David Schwimmer as Melman the giraffe and Jada Pinkett Smith as Gloria the hippo, with Danny Jacobs as King Julien XIII, Cedric the Entertainer as Maurice, Andy Richter as Mort, Tom McGrath as Skipper, Carl Reiner as Santa Claus, Nina Dobrev as the reindeer Cupid and Willow Smith as a little girl named Abby.

Still stranded on Madagascar, Alex, Marty, Melman and Gloria try to return to New York for Christmas in a hot air balloon. Their escape is ruined by the lemurs, who mistake them for the Marauding Red Night Goblin, a figure that visits the island every year and pelts it with coal. When the real goblin appears, Alex shoots it down, only to discover that it is actually Santa Claus, who has been throwing lumps of coal at King Julien for being naughty.

The crash leaves Santa with amnesia, unable to remember who he is or what he is supposed to do. Hoping to deliver the presents and then use the sleigh to fly home, the friends take over Santa's job, but the reindeer will only obey Santa, so the penguins use his magic dust to make the sleigh fly. Their first deliveries are disastrous, and they consider simply dumping the gifts at post offices, until they accidentally crash into an apartment and see the joy a present brings to a little girl. Meanwhile, back on the island, Santa rediscovers his talent for making toys during King Julien's own holiday, Julianuary, and the self-centered lemur learns something about giving. With their magic dust running low, the animals must choose between going home and helping Santa.

The special combines the franchise's slapstick humor with a classic Christmas message about generosity and friendship.

Merry Madagascar was nominated for six Annie Awards, winning one for storyboarding in a television production. It was released on DVD in the United States in 2009 through Walmart stores, with a wider release in 2011 and later holiday compilations.

plot:
Tinker Bell and the Lost Treasure is a 2009 animated adventure film produced by DisneyToon Studios, directed by Kevan Brighting, and written by Ron Clements. The movie follows Tinker Bell's journey as she searches for her lost treasure.

The story begins with Tinker Bell (voiced by Mae Whitman) living in Pixie Hollow, a magical community of fairies who live among the flowers and trees of Neverland. Tinker Bell is known for her exceptional tinkering skills and creates innovative gadgets to help her friends. However, she has lost her most prized possession - a small, golden treasure that holds sentimental value.

The movie begins with Tinker Bell's best friend, Fawn (voiced by Lucy Hale), who has recently discovered the location of the Lost Treasure of Pixie Hollow. The treasure is hidden in a cave deep within Neverland, guarded by the infamous pirate, Captain Hook (voiced by Brian Blessed). Tinker Bell sets out on a journey to find the treasure and prove herself as a valuable member of the fairy community.

Along the way, Tinker Bell meets a new friend, Vidia (voiced by Raven-Symoné), a sassy and confident fairy who is initially skeptical of Tinker Bell's abilities. However, as they work together, Vidia becomes Tinker Bell's ally and helps her navigate the challenges of Neverland.

As Tinker Bell and Vidia journey deeper into Neverland, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, ferocious creatures, and even Captain Hook himself. The two fairies must use their wit, courage, and teamwork to overcome these challenges and reach the treasure before it falls into the wrong hands.

Throughout her adventure, Tinker Bell learns valuable lessons about friendship, perseverance, and believing in herself. She also discovers that the true value of the treasure lies not in its monetary worth but in the memories and experiences it represents.

In the end, Tinker Bell and Vidia successfully retrieve the Lost Treasure of Pixie Hollow, but not before facing a final confrontation with Captain Hook. With the help of her friends and newfound confidence, Tinker Bell outsmarts the pirate and returns to Pixie Hollow as a hero.

The movie concludes with Tinker Bell reflecting on her journey and realizing that the true treasure was the friendships she made along the way. The film ends on a heartwarming note, showcasing the beauty of Neverland and the magic of friendship among its inhabitants.

title: The Ghost of Lord Farquaad
overview: Lord Farquaad was eaten by the dragon, but his ghost has returned, and he's still evil. With the help of his henchman, Thelonious, he kidnaps Fiona. Shrek and the donkey set out to save her, with help from the dragon, before she goes over a waterfall on a raft.
plot:
The Ghost of Lord Farquaad is the title used for some media releases of Shrek 4-D, a 2003 animated short film based on the Shrek franchise, created for a 4D simulator attraction with water and motion effects at Universal theme parks. The film features the voices of Mike Myers as Shrek, Eddie Murphy as Donkey, Cameron Diaz as Princess Fiona and John Lithgow as the ghost of Lord Farquaad, with Conrad Vernon as Gingy and Cody Cameron as Pinocchio and the Three Little Pigs. It follows Shrek and Donkey as they rescue Fiona, kidnapped by Farquaad's ghost on her honeymoon.

Shrek and Fiona are searching for the Honeymoon Hotel, escorted by Donkey, when Thelonious appears and seizes Fiona. Shrek and Donkey give chase into a graveyard, where Farquaad's ghost brings to life the stone dragon on his tomb and sends it after them. The real Dragon arrives, and in the ensuing chase the stone dragon smashes its wings against the walls of a chasm and plunges into the water below. Farquaad sends Fiona on a raft toward a waterfall, intending that she die and rule the underworld with him; Thelonious, not realizing he was supposed to get off, is still aboard. Fiona breaks free of her bonds and knocks Thelonious off the raft, and Shrek and Donkey reach her just before it goes over the falls, but all of them tumble over the edge. Dragon catches them and burns Farquaad's ghost, destroying him again, then carries Shrek and Fiona to the hotel before flying off with Donkey. The fairy tale creatures crash the honeymoon, but Shrek and Fiona join the celebration, and Shrek pops a champagne cork that sends Tinker Bell flying out of the frame.

The attraction opened at Universal Studios Hollywood on May 23, 2003, followed by Universal Studios Florida and Japan that June and later Universal Studios Singapore. It also ran at Warner Bros. Movie World in Australia and Movie Park Germany. The Hollywood version closed in 2017 and the Orlando version in 2022. Dark Horse Comics adapted the story in 2003, and in 2004 the film was released on DVD as Shrek 3-D alongside the original Shrek, in both anaglyph 3-D and conventional versions. In October 2011 it appeared on Netflix as The Ghost of Lord Farquaad, part of DreamWorks Spooky Stories, and in 2012 it was included on the Shrek's Thrilling Tales DVD.

title: The Land Before Time IX: Journey to Big Water
original_title: The Land Before Time IX: Journey to Big Water
overview: When heavy rains create a mysterious "new water", Littlefoot sets off to explore the Great Valley and quickly becomes friends with Mo, a fun-loving dolphin-like creature, who has been isolated from his pod by the weather. When Littlefoot and friends get separated from their parents because of an Earthshake, they help Mo get back home to the Big Water, while avoiding a hungry "Sharptooth Swimmer".
plot:
After a period of harsh rain, the Great Valley is partially flooded and covered in debris. Littlefoot tries to play with his friends, but they are preoccupied: Cera and her father are removing a large log from their nesting area, Ducky and Spike are relocating their nest with their family, and Petrie has gotten a cold. A bored Littlefoot wishes for a brother, but eventually explores on his own and discovers a large area flooded by the rains. The adults advise their children to stay away, fearing that dangerous creatures from the outside may have been washed into the Valley. However, Littlefoot returns and meets Mo, a playful young Ophthalmosaurus that had been caught in the floodwater.
Littlefoot quickly strikes a friendship with Mo and describes him as his mud brother. His other friends also eventually befriend him. Mo explains that he is from the Big Water, and he swam into the Valley during the flooding. He confirms that he is alone, but soon after, a Liopleurodon attacks the group. Littlefoot requests help from the adults to help Mo return home, but they refuse, not wanting to risk leaving the Valley to aid an outsider. A subsequent earthshake separates the children and Mo from the rest of the Valley, but it also imprisons the Sharptooth in an underwater cavern. Unable to return, they decide to take Mo home on their own.
The children follow a river that they believe leads to the ocean. A Diplodocus mother allows them to take refuge at her nest for the night, and the friends are present to witness the hatching of her offspring. The next day, Littlefoot and the others realize that they are near the ocean, as they have begun to taste salt in the water. Suddenly, the Sharptooth – who has escaped from the cave – attacks them that night. The land – which surrounds the river – is steep and slick with mud, and the children are unable to escape. Mo distracts the Sharptooth and lures it further down the river. Reappearing the next day, Mo explains that the Sharptooth had smelled the ocean in the distance and abandoned the chase, choosing to return to the sea.
The children reach the ocean, but Mo is saddened to learn that his friends must depart. He wishes to remain with them, but the others explain that he cannot, and Littlefoot reminds Mo that the two will always be brothers. Mo reunites with his family and asks them for directions to the smoky mountains, as the children know how to find the Valley from that location. Before leaving, Mo offers to show Littlefoot his home. Littlefoot accepts the offer, and is amazed by the underwater world's beauty. Littlefoot and his friends say goodbye to Mo and return home, where they are greeted by the adults.

title: Transformers: Beginnings
tagline: See what happened before Optimus Prime and Megatron came to Earth.
overview: On their home planet of Cybertron, the Autobots and Decepticons are involved in an explosive battle over the coveted AllSpark. With the fate of the universe at stake, the Autobots send it far from the reaches of the ruthless Megatron, leader of the Decepticons. plot:
Transformers: Beginnings is a 2007 American animated short that serves as a prequel to Michael Bay's live-action film Transformers. Rather than full animation, it is presented as a motion comic: a shortened, voiced adaptation of the prequel comic book published by IDW Publishing ahead of the film, with artwork set in motion by the studio Sunny Boy Creative. Running about 19 minutes, it is narrated by the Autobot Bumblebee, voiced by Mark Ryan, who also performed the character's voice in the feature. Peter Cullen returns as Optimus Prime and Frank Welker, the voice of Megatron in the original 1980s cartoon, plays the Decepticon leader, with Patrick Hallahan as Starscream, Brian Stepanek as Blackout and Sector Seven agent Seymour Simmons, Kevin Dunn as Ron Witwicky and Patrick Viall as Captain Archibald Witwicky.

Bumblebee's account begins on Cybertron, where the AllSpark, the source of all Transformer life, once allowed the planet to flourish under the joint leadership of Optimus Prime and Megatron. Megatron, however, becomes corrupted and tries to seize the artifact for himself, igniting the war between the Autobots and the Decepticons. Bumblebee fights to protect it, and the Autobots finally launch the AllSpark into space to keep it from Megatron, who destroys Bumblebee's voice before setting off in pursuit. Megatron tracks the cube to prehistoric Earth but becomes trapped in Arctic ice. Some four million years later, an expedition led by Captain Archibald Witwicky stumbles upon the frozen robot; Witwicky ends his days in a mental institution after filling page after page with alien designs, which draw the attention of the secret government agency Sector Seven. The agency excavates Megatron, discovers the AllSpark in Colorado and, decades later, oversees the building of the Hoover Dam. The story then jumps to 2003, when Bumblebee's arrival on Earth is detected and Sector Seven, led by Simmons, begins hunting the robot disguised as a yellow Camaro, while Sam Witwicky learns of his great-great-grandfather's legacy.

The short was not sold on its own: it was included on a bonus disc available only with the Walmart edition of the Transformers DVD, released in North America on 16 October 2007. The Transformers DVD itself became the fastest-selling DVD of 2007 in North America, with 8.3 million copies sold in its first week.

plot:
The Land Before Time VIII: The Big Freeze is a 2001 American direct-to-video animated musical adventure directed by Charles Grosvenor and written by John Loy, the eighth entry in The Land Before Time series. Produced by Universal Cartoon Studios, it features the voices of Aria Curzon as Ducky, Rob Paulsen as Spike, Thomas Dekker as Littlefoot, Anndi McAfee as Cera, Jeff Bennett as Petrie, Robert Guillaume as Mr. Thicknose and Kenneth Mars as Grandpa Longneck.

Ducky is growing frustrated with her brother Spike, whose snoring keeps her up at night and who ate the tree stars their mother packed for her first day of school. She asks Cera to teach her how to express anger. At school, the young dinosaurs are taught by Mr. Thicknose, an elderly Pachyrhinosaurus who claims to have been everywhere and seen everything, and Littlefoot's constant questions irritate him. As Ducky gives Spike the cold shoulder, he befriends Tippy, a young member of a migrating Spiketail herd that has arrived in the Great Valley, and Ducky begins to miss him as he spends more time with them.

An unexpected snowfall blankets the Valley, and while the children enjoy it, the adults grumble that Mr. Thicknose failed to predict it and doubt his wisdom. As the cold deepens and food grows scarce, the hungry Spiketails prepare to leave, and Tippy's mother offers to take Spike. Asked to choose, Spike hesitates until Ducky angrily tells him to go. Regretting it, she slips away to bring him back, and her friends follow into the Mysterious Beyond, joined by Mr. Thicknose. They drive off a sharptooth with a giant snowball, find Ducky, and break through ice to discover a warm spring surrounded by food. There Mr. Thicknose admits that most of his knowledge came from travelers' tales he heard as a child, then redeems himself by sending a log rolling to knock the returning sharptooth off a cliff. Finding a wall of snow blocking the Valley, Ducky urges Cera to vent her anger, and her furious shouting brings the snow down so the residents can reach the spring. Spike leads the starving Spiketails there too, and after Mama Swimmer saves him from drowning, Tippy's mother agrees he belongs with his family, and Ducky promises never again to get angry about his snoring.

Universal Studios Home Video released the film on VHS and DVD on December 4, 2001. It sold 2.5 million copies. Guillaume was nominated for a Video Premiere Award for his performance, and Curzon won a Young Artist Award for voicing Ducky.

Ben 10: Alien Swarm is a computer-animated science fiction film based on the Cartoon Network series Ben 10. The movie was released in 2009 and directed by Alex Winter.

The story begins with Ben Tennyson (voiced by Meagan Smith), a 10-year-old boy who has the ability to transform into different alien creatures using an Omnitrix, a powerful device that allows him to change his appearance and abilities. Ben's grandfather, Max Tennyson (voiced by Paul Eiding), is a retired superhero who helps Ben control the Omnitrix.

The movie starts with Ben and his cousin Gwen (voiced by Ashley Johnson) visiting their grandparents in Bellwood, New Jersey. However, their trip takes a turn when they discover that an alien invasion is underway. The aliens, led by Aggregor (voiced by Jim Ward), are seeking to harvest the Earth's energy source, known as the "Nebula," which is hidden beneath the planet.

Ben and Gwen soon find themselves in the middle of the battle against the aliens, with Ben using his Omnitrix to transform into different alien creatures to fight back. Along the way, they meet a new ally, Four Arms (voiced by Greg Cipes), an ancient warrior who joins forces with Ben to take down the aliens.

As the story unfolds, Ben and his friends discover that Aggregor is actually a powerful being from another dimension who seeks to destroy the Earth's energy source. The group must work together to stop Aggregor and save the planet.

Throughout the movie, Ben faces various challenges as he navigates his relationships with Gwen and Four Arms, while also learning to control his powers and work with his new allies. The action-packed sequences showcase Ben's ability to transform into different alien creatures, each with unique abilities and strengths.

In the end, Ben and his friends successfully defeat Aggregor and destroy the Nebula, saving the Earth from destruction. However, the movie concludes on a bittersweet note as Ben says goodbye to Four Arms, who returns to his own dimension, leaving Ben to continue his adventures alone.

Overall, Ben 10: Alien Swarm is an action-packed animated film that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and self-discovery. The movie's engaging storyline and lovable characters make it a fun and entertaining ride for fans of the Cartoon Network series.
