title: Post Grad
tagline: A Pre-Life Crisis.
overview: Ryden Malby has a master plan. Graduate college, get a great job, hang out with her best friend and find the perfect guy. But her plan spins hilariously out of control when she’s forced to move back home with her eccentric family.
plot:
Ryden Malby, who has had her life carefully planned out since she was eleven years old, prepares to graduate from college with a bachelor's degree in English, albeit during the late-2000s recession, having planned her academic life since she was in high school to get a college scholarship. At the graduation ceremony, Ryden's family arrives late, causing a commotion. In addition to her optimistic father Walter, who wants to do everything by himself, her mother Carmella, who carefully administrates the short resources of the household, and younger brother Hunter, who aspires to race in a boxcar derby, her eccentric grandmother Maureen arrives, accompanied by her ever-present oxygen tank. Ryden's longtime rival, Jessica Bard, gives the graduation speech and then Ryden and her family go out to celebrate, accompanied by Ryden's best friend, Adam Davies, who has had passionate feelings for Ryden since they met during their freshman year. Adam has applied to law school at Columbia, but is undecided between a career in music or studying law. Meanwhile, Ryden reveals to her family that she has an interview scheduled the following week for her dream job as an assistant editor at the prestigious publishing company Happerman and Browning in Los Angeles, and that she has even found a fabulous loft that she plans to rent.
En route to the job interview, Ryden gets her car into a collision with a truck and when the driver departs without giving her his insurance information, she is forced to walk to Happerman and Browning. Upon arriving, disheveled and stressed, she is directed to a waiting area filled with other applicants. When Ryden is finally called in to interview and asked why she desires the job, she eloquently explains that she has been preparing for this opportunity for her entire life and would never imagine herself doing anything else, after which the interviewer awkwardly thanks her for her time. As she is departing, Jessica arrives and is greeted warmly by the interviewer, and is ultimately successful in obtaining the job.
Now unemployed, a frustrated Ryden gives up on the loft and moves back in with her family. As they are unloading her belongings, Walter steps in poop left by a cat belonging to his next-door neighbor, David Santiago, and furiously confronts him. Adam observes Ryden meeting and forming a romantic connection with David. She then proceeds to interview for numerous jobs, all without success, while suffering various embarrassing encounters with Jessica. When Walter accidentally runs over David's cat with Ryden's car, she and David further connect, and he offers her a job as a production assistant on the infomercials that he directs. One night, they become physically intimate, but the moment is interrupted when Ryden's family arrives to shockingly find them in a compromising position. Still undecided about his plans, Adam obtains a gig headlining at a local venue and plans a big night with a fancy celebration dinner with Ryden.

title: Children of the Corn: Revelation
tagline: The All-New, Terror-Filled Chapter!
overview: When a girl named Jamie repeatedly tries to contact her grandmother to no avail, she investigates by going to her apartment in Omaha Nebraska - only to find that it's been condemned and overtaken by possessed children. As she digs deeper, she discovers a dark secret about her grandmother and awakens a dark, demonic force that wants Jamie dead and will stop at nothing.
plot:
Children of the Corn: Revelation is an American slasher horror film of 2001 directed by Guy Magar, the seventh installment in the Children of the Corn series. Claudette Mink stars as Jamie Lowell, a young woman searching for her missing grandmother, with Kyle Cassie as Detective Armbrister, Troy Yorke as the manager Jerry Ulrich and Michael Ironside as a mysterious priest.

After her calls to her grandmother go unanswered, Jamie travels to Omaha, Nebraska, and finds the old woman's apartment building, which stands beside a cornfield, almost deserted apart from two strange children wandering its halls. Her grandmother has been served an eviction notice, Armbrister is unhelpful, and a priest watches Jamie from the street. Back at the apartment she finds a message telling her to go home. In the basement she discovers carrots and tomatoes growing and flees at the sound of children laughing, then meets an armed tenant who warns her to stay out of there, a foul-mouthed old man in a wheelchair and a stripper, Tiffany.

Jerry invites Jamie to a rooftop barbecue, but before she arrives he bites into an ear of corn full of blood and is pushed off the roof by the children. Jamie learns from Armbrister that her grandmother, as a child, belonged to a religious cult whose young members, led by a boy preacher named Abel, burned themselves to death in a tent. Only her grandmother survived, and the apartment building stands on the site of the fire. One by one the tenants die: Tiffany is strangled with corn in her bath, the old man is pushed through a stair railing, and the armed tenant dies of fright in an elevator.

The priest tells her about the history of Gatlin and the devilish creature known as He Who Walks Behind the Rows, warning that her grandmother is dead and she will be too if she stays. The children then drag Jamie to the basement, now filled with rows of corn, where Abel appears and one child reveals herself as Jamie's grandmother, speaking in an old woman's voice. Pretending to accept their invitation to join them, Jamie sets off a gas explosion that leaves Abel unharmed; he binds her with cornstalks, but Armbrister rescues her and they escape before the building blows up, destroying the corn and, it is implied, freeing the children's souls.

Released direct to video, the film was poorly reviewed; DVD Talk called it uninvolving and unremarkable, and Total Film ranked it 49th of 50 Stephen King adaptations.

title: Carriers
tagline: The rules are simple. You break them, you die...
overview: A deadly virus has spread across the globe. Contagion is everywhere, no one is safe, and no one can be trusted. Four friends race through the back roads of the American West on their way to a secluded utopian beach in the Gulf of Mexico where they could peacefully wait out the pandemic. Their plans take a grim turn when their car breaks down on an isolated road starting a chain of events that will seal their fates.
plot:
Carriers is a 2009 American post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Chris Kentis and written by J. Mackye Gruber. The movie stars Christian Bale, Emily Mortimer, Sam Reilly, and Mike Vogel.

The story begins with a series of unexplained events: people are dying in the United States, seemingly without any apparent cause or connection to one another. The main character, Steve Gillis (played by Chris Evans), is a young man who has recently lost his girlfriend, Susan, to cancer. He is struggling to cope with his grief and feeling disconnected from the world around him.

As the mysterious deaths continue to occur, Steve's brother, Patrick (played by Sam Reilly), becomes increasingly paranoid and isolated. The two brothers are forced to confront their own mortality when they discover that a deadly virus has been spreading rapidly across the country, causing widespread panic and chaos.

The virus is highly contagious and airborne, making it nearly impossible to contain or treat. As the death toll rises, Steve and Patrick embark on a perilous journey to find a safe haven, hoping to escape the outbreak and reconnect with their loved ones.

Along the way, they meet a young woman named Amy (played by Emily Mortimer), who is also searching for safety. The three form an uneasy alliance, navigating through treacherous landscapes and avoiding hordes of infected people. As they journey on, they begin to realize that the virus may not be as random or natural as initially thought.

As the story unfolds, Steve's character undergoes significant development. He begins to confront his own emotional baggage and learn to let go of his grief. Through his experiences with Amy and Patrick, he discovers a new sense of purpose and resilience.

The movie builds towards a tense and suspenseful climax as Steve and his companions face off against the infected in a desperate bid for survival. The ending is both haunting and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the true nature of the virus and the human condition.

Throughout the film, Chris Kentis masterfully crafts a sense of tension and unease, using the eerie atmosphere and stunning visuals to create a truly unsettling viewing experience. The cast delivers strong performances, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Carriers is a gripping and intense horror film that explores themes of grief, loss, and redemption in the face of catastrophic uncertainty.

title: Precious
tagline: We are all precious
overview: Set in Harlem in 1987, Claireece "Precious" Jones is a 16-year-old African American girl born into a life no one would want. She's pregnant for the second time by her absent father; at home, she must wait hand and foot on her mother, an angry woman who abuses her emotionally and physically. School is chaotic and Precious has reached the ninth grade with good marks and a secret; She can't read.
plot:
Precious, released in full as Precious: Based on the Novel "Push" by Sapphire, is a 2009 American drama directed and co-produced by Lee Daniels from a screenplay by Geoffrey S. Fletcher, adapted from Sapphire's 1996 novel Push. Gabourey Sidibe makes her acting debut in the title role, opposite Mo'Nique, with Paula Patton, Mariah Carey, Sherri Shepherd and Lenny Kravitz in supporting parts. Shot in New York City in late 2007, it premiered without a distributor at the 2009 Sundance Film Festival, where it won both the Audience Award and the Grand Jury Prize for drama, and then played at Cannes.

In Harlem in 1987, sixteen-year-old Claireece "Precious" Jones lives in a welfare-dependent tenement with her unemployed mother Mary, who abuses her physically, sexually and verbally. Precious has been raped by her absent father, Carl, and has borne him one child, a daughter with Down syndrome who is cared for by her grandmother, and is pregnant with a second. She escapes her misery through vivid daydreams of fame and love. When her pregnancy is discovered, her principal arranges for her to attend an alternative school, Each One Teach One, despite Mary's demand that she go on welfare instead.

There, under the patient teacher Blu Rain and among classmates from similarly troubled backgrounds, Precious slowly learns to read and write and begins to believe in herself. She also meets regularly with the social worker Mrs. Weiss, to whom she accidentally reveals who fathered her children. After giving birth to a son, Abdul, she returns home, where Mary, furious that the revelation has cost her welfare payments, drops the baby and attacks her. Precious escapes with Abdul and takes shelter in her classroom, and Ms. Rain helps her find a place in a halfway house where she can raise her son and keep studying.

Mary later visits to announce that Carl has died of AIDS, and Precious learns she is HIV-positive, though Abdul is not. In a final meeting in Mrs. Weiss's office, Mary tearfully admits that she resented her daughter for "taking" Carl and allowed the abuse to continue. Precious cuts ties with her, leaving with both of her children and resolving to earn her GED and go to college.

The film was widely acclaimed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 92% positive reviews. It received six Academy Award nominations, winning Best Supporting Actress for Mo'Nique and Best Adapted Screenplay for Fletcher.

title: Aladin
tagline: and the Mystery of the lamp
overview: Based in the municipality of Khwaish, abused by his classmates, Aladin Chatterjee, who was orphaned when his parents, Arun and Riya, died in an accident in Siachen Valley, lived with his paternal grandfather until the later's passing. Now alone, grown up, studying in Khwaish University, and still being abused by fellow-college mates, he finds himself smitten by the lovely US Exchange Student, Jasmine. Unable to express his feelings for her, he rubs a lamp that was gifted to him on his birthday, which summons a genie named Genius. He gets 3 wishes, but wastes 2 of them, but on the 3rd one he insists that Genius assist him to win Jasmine's heart without any magical tricks. Hilarious chaos result when everything seems to fail while an immortal and deadly entity, Ringmaster, and his hordes, prepares to confront Genius and Aladin so that he can acquire more magical powers with the help of the lamp on the day of the sighting of a rare comet and the truth behind the death of Aladin's parents.
plot:
Aladin is a 2009 Indian Hindi-language fantasy action comedy directed by Sujoy Ghosh, a modern reworking of the Aladdin legend. It stars Riteish Deshmukh as Aladin Chatterjee, Amitabh Bachchan as the genie Genius, Sanjay Dutt as the villainous Ringmaster and Jacqueline Fernandez, in her film debut, as Jasmine, with Sahil Khan and Ratna Pathak Shah. The film was adapted from the Marathi play Pati Sagle Uchapati, itself based on the play Right Bed, Wrong Husband by Neil and Caroline Schaffner, and its music was composed by Vishal–Shekhar.

As a baby, Aladin loses his parents when his archaeologist father, who has found and hidden a magic lamp, is murdered along with his wife by a gang searching for it. Raised by his grandfather, Aladin grows up lonely in the fictional city of Khwaish, where he is constantly bullied by Kasim and his gang. His life changes when Jasmine, a beautiful newcomer, arrives in town and he falls for her. At Aladin's birthday party, organized by Kasim to humiliate him, Jasmine gives him an old lamp as a present, which turns out to be the very lamp his parents' killers were seeking.

When Aladin rubs the lamp, he releases Genius, a flamboyant, rock-star genie who is desperate to grant three wishes so that his contract with the lamp can end. Aladin is reluctant to make any wishes, but Genius cleverly extracts them, turning his life upside down. With Genius's help, Aladin stands up to Kasim and begins a relationship with Jasmine. Their happiness is threatened by Ringmaster, a former genie who wants to regain his lost powers. He tricks Aladin into turning against Genius and steals the lamp, setting in motion a scheme involving an approaching comet, and Aladin and Genius must join forces to rescue Jasmine and stop him.

The film combines fairy-tale fantasy with comedy, musical numbers and visual effects, and gives the classic story a contemporary setting.

Aladin was released in 2009 and was a commercial failure, grossing an estimated 10 crore rupees. Critics were largely negative: Bollywood Hungama gave it one star, calling it a terrible waste of a terrific opportunity, and the Hindustan Times criticized its hollow storytelling while acknowledging Bachchan's enduring appeal.

title: Balto II: Wolf Quest
overview: Balto and his daughter Aleu embark on a journey of adventure and self discovery.
plot:
A few months after his heroic journey, Balto mated with Jenna, and they now have a new family of six puppies in Alaska. Five of their puppies resemble their husky mother, while one pup, named Aleu, inherits her wolfdog father's features. When the puppies reach eight weeks old, all but Aleu are adopted into new homes. Her wild animal appearance deters potential adopters, leaving her to live with her father.
A year later when she is grown, Aleu is almost killed by a hunter who mistakes her for a wild wolf. Balto tells Aleu the truth about her wolf heritage, causing her to run away, hoping to find her place in the world. Balto then goes out into the Alaskan wilderness to find her. At the same time, Balto has been struggling with strange dreams of a raven and a pack of wolves, and he cannot understand their meaning. Balto resolves to find the meaning of these dreams as he searches for Aleu. His friends Boris, Muk, and Luk attempt to join him, but after they are halted by some unknown force, they realize that this journey is meant only for the father and daughter themselves, making them unable to join the journey to ensure Balto is completely alone.
Taking refuge in a cave, Aleu meets the field mouse Muru, who explains that Aleu should not be ashamed of her lineage, which tells her what she is but not who she is. Muru reveals himself to be Aleu's spirit guide and tells her to go on a journey of self-discovery. Balto and Aleu reunite when he saves her from the grizzly bear and reconcile, and find their way to the ocean, where they are attacked by a group of starving Northwestern wolves led by Niju, an arrogant and vicious wolf.
The confrontation is defused by the elderly Nava, the true leader of the pack, who welcomes Balto and Aleu. Nava announces to his pack that the wolf spirit Aniu has contacted him in "dream visions". Aniu has told him that the caribou herd they depend on during the winter has moved across the ocean and will not return and that they will soon be led by a new leader, "the one who is a wolf but does not know". Nava believes that Balto, who is half wolf himself, is the chosen one that Aniu was speaking of. However, Niju refuses to abandon his homeland and takes control of the pack, and plots to steal from other animal clans in the area to survive the winter.
Aleu has a "dream vision" of the caribou herd crossing a bridge made of ice floes. The next morning, Niju prepares to lead an attack on a clan of bears, but is stopped by Balto just as a large group of ice floes in the ocean come together to form a land bridge. Balto then leads the pack across the bridge until Nava falls behind. When Aleu attempts to help Nava, Niju attacks, and Balto doubles back to save them, leaving the pack leaderless. Nava cannot make the journey across the ice in his old age, and Balto tells Niju to go lead the clan.
Niju refuses, too afraid to leave his home, and soon returns to the shore.

title: The House of the Devil
tagline: Talk on the phone. Finish your homework. Watch TV. Die.
overview: In the 1980s, college student Samantha Hughes takes a strange babysitting job that coincides with a full lunar eclipse. She slowly realizes her clients harbor a terrifying secret.
plot:
In the 1980s, Samantha Hughes, a cash-strapped college student, responds to an ad for a babysitting job for a Mr. Ulman. Her best friend Megan gives her a ride to the Ulmans' remote mansion. Mr. Ulman reveals the job is actually tending to his wife's mother. Samantha reluctantly agrees to a fee of $400. On the way home, Megan is shot in the head by a stranger, later identified as Victor.
Samantha orders a pizza from a number Mr. Ulman recommended. After accidentally breaking a vase, she cleans up and discovers a closet containing old family photographs. In one photograph, a family that is not the Ulmans stands next to the Volvo that she and Megan saw at the house. Later, three corpses are shown in one of the rooms, implying that they were the family in the photographs and the true owners of the house. Unnerved by the noises in the house and the arrival of the pizza, delivered by Victor, Samantha dials 911, but tells the operator it was an accidental call. Samantha then grabs a knife from the kitchen and goes upstairs to explore the creaking sounds. Drugs in the pizza cause her to pass out just as she sees movement behind a door on the third floor.
Samantha comes to during a lunar eclipse and finds herself bound in the center of a pentagram on the floor. Mr. and Mrs. Ulman, along with their son Victor, begin a ritual. "Mother" is revealed to be a grotesque, witch-like figure. She slices her arm and pours her blood into a goat skull. She then uses it to draw occult symbols on Samantha's belly and forehead, and forces Samantha to drink the blood. Samantha stabs Mother and escapes. After finding Megan's corpse in the kitchen, she kills Victor and Mrs. Ulman, but horrific images of Mother begin appearing in her mind. Mr. Ulman chases her into a nearby cemetery, telling her that she has been chosen and destined to accept "him". Samantha threatens to shoot Ulman, but he is resigned, telling her it is too late. Instead, Samantha shoots herself in the head.
The next day, TV news reports the strange lunar eclipse the night before, which confounded scientists with its abrupt ending. Samantha lies unconscious on a hospital bed having survived her suicide attempt. A nurse states that "both of them" will be fine, implying that she has been impregnated.

title: My Name Is Khan

overview: Rizwan Khan, a Muslim from the Borivali section of Mumbai, has Asperger's syndrome. He marries a Hindu single mother, Mandira, in San Francisco. After 9/11, Rizwan is detained by authorities at LAX who treat him as a terrorist because of his condition and his race.
plot:
Rizvan Khan, an Indian Muslim with Asperger's syndrome, grows up in Mumbai with his mother, Razia, and his brother, Zakir. Due to his condition, Rizvan receives specialized tutoring from a reclusive local scholar, Mr. Wadia, earning him extra affection from his mother—a dynamic that breeds resentment in Zakir. Following their mother's death, Zakir, who has relocated to San Francisco and is now married to a college professor, Hasina, sponsors Rizvan to join him in the United States. Upon his arrival in California, Hasina formally diagnoses Rizvan's condition, and he begins working as a distributor for Zakir’s beauty product company. While working, he falls in love with Mandira Rathod, a Hindu single mother and hairstylist. Despite Zakir's disapproval of the interfaith match, Rizvan and Mandira marry, and she and her young son, Sameer "Sam" Rathore, take his surname. The family moves to the peaceful suburb of Banville, striking up a warm friendship with their neighbors, the Garricks, comprising reporter Mark, his wife Sarah and their son Reese.
Their idyllic life is shattered in the aftermath of the September 11 attacks. As Islamophobia spikes across the nation, Mark travels to cover the war in Afghanistan and is killed in action. Traumatized and angry, Reese begins to turn against Sam. The latter's persistent endeavour to rekindle talking terms with the former culminates in a violent confrontation at a community soccer field, where a group of older students attack Sam. During the assault, he dies from a spleen rupture; Reese is threatened by the older boys with consequences in case he confesses anything.
A grieving and devastated Mandira blames Rizvan, shouting that her son died solely because they carried the surname "Khan." Still seething with anger, she demands that he leave. When a confused Rizvan asks when he may return, Mandira sarcastically tells him he can come back only when he has traveled across the country to tell the American people and the President of the United States that his "name is Khan" and he "is not a terrorist". Taking her words literally, Rizvan sets out on a cross-country journey to track down President George W. Bush on his campaign trail.
During his travels, Rizvan stops in Wilhelmina, a small, impoverished rural town in Georgia, where he befriends a young boy named Joel and his mother, Jenny, earning the gratitude of the tight-knit local community. Later, in Los Angeles, Rizwan visits a mosque where he overhears a radical doctor, Faisal Rehman, inciting his followers to violence. Disturbed by the message, Rizwan publicly confronts Faisal, rejects his extremist views, and reports him to the FBI.
Rizwan’s quest leads him to a presidential rally at the UCLA. Standing in the crowd, he repeatedly shouts, "My name is Khan, and I am not a terrorist!" His behavior is misinterpreted by the tense crowd, sparking a panic that leads to his arrest and detention.

American Pie Presents: The Book of Love is a 2009 American teen comedy film directed by Jesse Moss and written by Adam Herz, Jon Lucas, and Scott Moore. The movie is the eighth installment in the American Pie franchise.

The story revolves around Jim Levenstein (Eddie Kaye Thomas), who has just been dumped by his girlfriend, Michelle Flaherty (Amanda Crew). Feeling heartbroken, Jim turns to an old high school friend, Kevin (Jason Friedberg), for advice. Kevin suggests that Jim read "The Book of Love," a self-help book written by a mysterious author.

As Jim reads the book, he becomes convinced that it holds the secrets to winning back Michelle and finding true love. The book's advice is based on a series of cryptic messages and codes that Jim must decipher in order to unlock the secrets of love.

Meanwhile, Stifler (Seann William Scott) has become increasingly obsessed with a new girlfriend, who turns out to be a manipulative and controlling woman. As Jim delves deeper into "The Book of Love," he begins to realize that the book's advice is not as straightforward as it seems.

Throughout the movie, Jim's friends, including Finch (Paul Sado), Ozzy (Erik Stolhanske), and Kevin, provide comedic relief and support as Jim navigates his way through the ups and downs of love. Along the way, Jim also encounters a series of eccentric characters who claim to be experts on love and relationships.

As the story unfolds, Jim becomes increasingly obsessed with deciphering the codes in "The Book of Love." He enlists the help of his friends and together, they embark on a series of misadventures as they try to unlock the secrets of true love.

In the end, Jim's journey leads him to a surprising revelation about Michelle and himself. The movie concludes with Jim having learned a valuable lesson about love and relationships, but not necessarily in the way he expected.

Overall, American Pie Presents: The Book of Love is a lighthearted and comedic take on the challenges of love and relationships. While it may not be as sophisticated or nuanced as some other romantic comedies, the movie provides plenty of laughs and entertainment for fans of the franchise.

plot:
Momoko Ryugasaki is a high school student who admires the Rococo style and Lolita fashion. In contrast to her idyllic lifestyle, she is forced to flee her hometown Amagasaki to live in her grandmother's house in Shimotsuma, Ibaraki Prefecture, after her father, a former yakuza member, ran into legal trouble from selling counterfeit Versace apparel. Initially, Momoko is excited to move closer to Tokyo, where her favorite clothing brand Baby, the Stars Shine Bright is located, but she is dismayed at discovering Shimotsuma is a rural, countryside town. When she runs out of spending money, she resorts to selling her father's remaining merchandise. Ichigo Shirayuri, a member of the all-female biker gang Ponytails who goes by the name "Ichiko", visits Momoko frequently to purchase clothing for her gang. Despite their opposite personalities and interests, the girls develop an unlikely friendship.
When Momoko runs out of merchandise to sell, Ichiko takes her to pachinko parlors for more spending money. Momoko hits the jackpot, which draws the attention from the manager, but Ryuji comes to their defense. Ichiko falls in love with him, but she learns that he is the fiancé of Akimi, the Ponytails' leader. When Momoko tells Ichigo about her day trips to visit the Baby, the Stars Shine Bright store in Tokyo, Ichiko mentions that she would like to visit Emma, an embroidery service located in the same area, as she plans on getting her kamikaze coat embroidered to honor Akimi's marriage and retirement from the Ponytails. When the two visit Tokyo, Momoko's embroidery work catches the attention of Akinori Isobe, the founder of Baby, the Stars Shine Bright. Meanwhile, to Ichiko's disappointment, Emma has permanently closed, but Momoko offers to embroider her jacket instead.
Isobe later contacts Momoko and commissions her to embroider a jumper skirt for the store's display. She completes the embroidery on both the jumper skirt and Ichiko's jacket in three days. While visiting Baby, the Stars Shine Bright to drop off the jumper skirt, Ichiko is asked to model for the brand's catalog after one of their models is injured. At Isobe's advice, Ichiko pursues a part-time modeling career. Momoko, on the other hand, turns down Isobe's suggestion to work for Baby, the Stars Shine Bright but decides to become Ichigo's manager.
Under Miko's new leadership, the Ponytails are unhappy with Ichiko becoming a model. Likewise, Ichiko is unsatisfied with the direction of the Ponytails and decides to quit the gang. As punishment for deserting the Ponytails, they challenge her to a fight, which Momoko overhears Ichiko accepting over the phone. Concerned for Ichiko, Momoko locates their fight and causes the Ponytails to flee by throwing her grandmother's scooter and water balloons at them. The two girls ride home on Ichiko's motorbike.

title: Taking Woodstock
tagline: A Generation Began In His Backyard.
overview: The story of Elliot Tiber and his family, who inadvertently played a pivotal role in making the famed Woodstock Music and Arts Festival into the happening that it was. When Elliot hears that a neighboring town has pulled the permit on a hippie music festival, he calls the producers thinking he could drum up some much-needed business for his parents' run-down motel. Three weeks later, half a million people are on their way to his neighbor’s farm in White Lake, New York, and Elliot finds himself swept up in a generation-defining experience that would change his life–and American culture–forever.
plot:
Set in 1969, the film is based on the true story of Elliot Tiber, an aspiring Greenwich Village interior designer whose parents, Jake and Sonia, own the small dilapidated El Monaco Resort in White Lake, in the town of Bethel, New York. A hippie theater troupe, The Earthlight Players, rents the barn, but can barely pay any rent. Due to financial trouble, the motel may close. Elliot pleads with the local bank not to foreclose on the mortgage and Sonia delivers a tirade about her struggles as a Russian refugee. The family is given until the end of the summer to pay up.
Elliot plans to hold a small musical festival and has obtained a $1 permit from the town's chamber of commerce (of which he is also the president). Upon hearing the Woodstock Festival organizers face opposition against the originally planned location, he offers his permit and the motel accommodations to organizer Michael Lang. A neighbor, Max Yasgur, provides his nearby farmland; they agree on a $5,000 fee, but after realizing how many people will attend, Yasgur demands $75,000, which the organizers reluctantly accept. Elliot comes to agreement about the fee for the motel more smoothly. Initial objections by his mother quickly disappear when she sees the cash paid in advance.
Elliot and Yasgur encounter some expected opposition. The local diner refuses to continue serving Elliot, inspectors target the motel (and only his) for building code violations, and some local boys paint a swastika and hate words on the motel. However, resistance quickly dissolves in the tidal wave of peace and love (and commerce) brought to the area. The Tiber family works hard serving the massive influx of visitors and become wealthy in the process. A cross-dressing veteran, Vilma, is hired as a security guard. Elliot also struggles with hiding his homosexuality from his family, when he connects romantically with one of the event organizers staying at the motel.
On the concert's first day, Elliot, his father, and Vilma hear the music begin in the distance. Elliot's father, transformed and enlivened by all the new life in town, tells Elliot to go watch the concert. Elliot hitches a ride through the peaceful traffic jam on the back of a benevolent state trooper's motorcycle and arrives at the event. He meets a hippie couple, who invite him to join them on an LSD trip in their VW Bus a short distance from the crowd. Elliot initially has trouble relaxing but gradually melts into a psychedelic union with them. When they finally emerge after sundown, Elliot watches the vast crowd and brilliant lights of the distant concert ripple with harmonious hallucinatory visuals that swell into serene white light.
Elliot returns home from his liberating experience and has breakfast with his parents. He suggests to his mother that they now have enough money to replace him, but she cannot bear to release him. Elliot storms out, facetiously suggesting his mom eat the hash brownies Vilma has just offered.

title: Triangle

overview: When Jess sets sail on a yacht with a group of friends, she cannot shake the feeling that there is something wrong. plot:
Triangle is a 2009 British-Australian psychological horror film written and directed by Christopher Smith. Melissa George stars as Jess, a single mother who joins friends on a boating trip and, after their yacht capsizes, boards a seemingly deserted ocean liner where someone appears to be hunting them. Michael Dorman, Rachael Carpani, Henry Nixon, Emma Lung and Liam Hemsworth also star. The screenplay draws partly on the myth of Sisyphus, condemned to push a boulder uphill for eternity, and Smith cited influences ranging from The Twilight Zone to Dead of Night, Back to the Future and Memento.

Jess, mother of an autistic son, Tommy, arrives at a Florida harbour alone, saying the boy is at school, and sets sail with her friend Greg, his deckhand Victor, the married couple Sally and Downey, and Sally's friend Heather. A sudden storm hits after Greg picks up a woman's distress call saying someone is killing everyone; Heather is swept away and the others cling to the overturned hull. When a liner, the Aeolus, passes, they climb aboard, though it seems empty. Jess feels a strong sense of déjà vu, finds her own keys, and sees "go to theater" written in blood. A wounded Victor attacks her, and in the theatre she finds Greg shot dead before a masked gunman kills Sally and Downey. Jess disarms the attacker, who tells her she must kill the others to get home, and knocks the figure overboard. She then watches a second version of her group arrive and realizes the events repeat whenever everyone dies; she finds dozens of her own lockets and notes urging her to kill them all, and a third Jess carries out the killings. Desperate to escape, Jess sets the cycle in motion herself, puts on the burlap mask and is knocked overboard by the newest Jess. She washes up on a beach and, returning home earlier that morning, sees her earlier self abusing Tommy. She kills that version of herself and drives off with Tommy, promising things will change, but after finding a pile of dead seagulls she crashes into a truck, killing her son. Hoping to undo it, she takes a taxi to the harbour, promises the driver she will return and boards Greg's boat, starting the loop again.

Shot in Queensland, Australia, with support from the UK Film Council, Triangle premiered at London's FrightFest in August 2009 and opened in British cinemas on 16 October 2009. It received generally positive reviews, with a 78% Rotten Tomatoes rating, but grossed only about $1.3 million worldwide.

title: The Secret
tagline: The secret has traveled through centuries to reach you
overview: Interviews with leading authors, philosophers and scientists, with an in-depth discussion of the Law of Attraction. The audience is shown how they can learn and use 'The Secret' in their everyday lives.
plot:
The Secret is a 2006 Australian-American self-help film presented in the form of a documentary, created by television producer Rhonda Byrne and directed by Drew Heriot. It consists of a series of interviews with motivational speakers, authors and self-described teachers, including Bob Proctor, Joe Vitale, John Assaraf, Loral Langemeier and Marie Diamond, intended to demonstrate the New Thought idea known as the "law of attraction". The film was followed by Byrne's book of the same name, and the two together became a major commercial phenomenon, especially after their promotion on The Oprah Winfrey Show.

Rather than telling a fictional story, The Secret presents its central idea through narration, testimonials and dramatised reconstructions. According to the film, thoughts and feelings act like magnets that attract corresponding events and experiences into a person's life, so that anyone who focuses intensely and positively on what they want, whether wealth, health, love or success, will eventually receive it. Conversely, negative thoughts are said to bring negative outcomes. The speakers apply this principle to every sphere of life, from personal relationships and careers to physical illness, and offer practical routines such as visualising desired results, expressing gratitude and acting as if a goal had already been achieved.

The film frames the law of attraction as an ancient piece of wisdom that was known to great figures throughout history but deliberately kept hidden from ordinary people by those in power. Dramatised scenes depict a mysterious scroll being passed down through the ages, reinforcing the idea of a long-suppressed secret that is now being revealed. Contributors recount personal anecdotes in which they claim to have obtained money, possessions or recovery from illness by applying the principle.

The Secret attracted a large and enthusiastic audience and generated a wide range of spin-off books and products. It was also heavily criticised by scientists, psychologists and journalists, who described its central claims as pseudoscience with no basis in physics or evidence. Critics argued that it misrepresented concepts from quantum mechanics, encouraged a materialistic outlook and implied that victims of illness, poverty or misfortune were responsible for attracting their own suffering through their thoughts.

title: Nine Miles Down
tagline: Lead us not into temptation but deliver us from evil.
overview: In the Sahara desert, a sandstorm batters a deserted drilling station. A security patrolman, battles through the high winds to investigate why all contact with the station has been lost. Originally built for gas exploration, and then abandoned, the site had recently been taken over by a multi-national research team intent on drilling deeper into the earth’s crust than ever before.
plot:
Nine Miles Down is a 2009 horror film inspired by the "Well to Hell", an urban legend widely circulated in the 1990s, which claimed that Russian scientists had drilled so deep that they broke through into hell and recorded the screams of the damned. An international co-production between the United Kingdom, Hungary and the United States, it was the last feature film credit for the writer Everett De Roche. The cast includes Adrian Paul, Kate Nauta, Meredith Ostrom and Amanda Douge.

Jack Jackmann, a former police officer working as an inspector for the energy company GNE, arrives in a sandstorm at the Jevel Afra drilling site, a remote station in the Sahara whose 25 staff, led by Professor Borman, have not been heard from for days. He finds the base deserted, with signs of a struggle, Arabic messages written in blood on the walls and a ritually sacrificed jackal. Video records show that Borman set up the dig to investigate an air pocket nine miles underground and that the scientists then became increasingly paranoid. When the storm clears, Jack meets Dr. Jenny "JC" Christensen, the only scientist left, who tells him that Borman was murdered by the chief geologist and that another scientist died of a heart attack. Ordered to stay put, Jack grows suspicious of JC, who does not appear in any of the team's records and tries to steal his vehicle and explains that Borman falsified her details because the budget allowed no separate women's quarters. JC recounts that the drill's microphones had picked up what sounded like human screams, after which the terrified crew began seeing dead loved ones and turning violent. Jack, too, begins to hallucinate. Over his birthday dinner he tells her how his wife killed herself and their two children six years earlier, and the two sleep together, but his torment worsens. Convinced that JC is a demon, he finds human remains in the cesspit, attacks her, hears Borman's hidden recording suggesting they released the Devil, and finally wounds her and sets the base ablaze before a GNE rescue team evacuates them. In hospital, officials confirm JC's account: gas released from the cavity caused victims to confuse reality with memory and imagination, and JC was less affected because of her separate quarters. Jack's paranoia nonetheless returns, and after trying to kill JC he is left on the brink of suicide, haunted by his dead wife's laughter.

Ain't It Cool News called it a pleasant surprise that lives up to its promising concept.

title: Prep & Landing
tagline: No one does stealth like an Elf.
overview: Wayne gets a new rookie partner, Lanny, after his previous partner got the promotion he wanted. Lanny has to remind Wayne of the Spirit of Christmas and the importance of being an elf in Santa's Prep and Landing elite unit.
plot:
Prep & Landing is an American computer-animated Christmas television special produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. Based on an idea by Chris Williams and developed into a half-hour special by Kevin Deters and Stevie Wermers-Skelton, it premiered on ABC on December 8, 2009, a week later than planned. Dave Foley voices the veteran elf Wayne and Derek Richardson his rookie partner Lanny, with Sarah Chalke, David DeLuise and Mason Vale Cotton in the cast. It launched a small franchise of follow-up shorts and specials.

Behind Santa Claus's yearly journey stands Prep & Landing, an elite unit of elves who slip into homes around the world ahead of the sleigh and make sure everything is ready for his arrival. Wayne has served with the outfit for 227 years and fully expects to be rewarded with a promotion to director of the naughty list. To his dismay, the post goes to Peterson, his own former trainee and partner, and Wayne is instead saddled with Lanny, an eager young recruit fresh out of training.

Resentful about being passed over, Wayne decides to coast through the night's assignment, the home of a young boy named Timmy. He leaves the enthusiastic but inexperienced Lanny to handle everything on his own, and the preparations quickly go wrong. While Santa is in the air, the North Pole learns that a heavy snowstorm is closing in and that the house has not been properly prepared. Santa is advised to skip the stop altogether, something that has never happened before, and the elves are told that Timmy will simply be compensated later.

When the two elves learn that the decision to reroute the sleigh is final, Wayne at first accepts it. Then he hears Timmy murmur his thanks in his sleep, and his holiday spirit returns. He contacts Santa directly and insists that the sleigh must land at Timmy's house after all. Working together at last, Wayne and Lanny guide Santa through the storm and onto the roof so the presents can be delivered.

On Christmas morning, Santa shows Wayne that Timmy is enjoying a happy Christmas, and offers him a promotion to director of the nice list. Wayne declines, choosing to remain in the field with Lanny. The special was released on DVD in 2011 together with later shorts, and was followed by the shorts Operation: Secret Santa (2010) and the special Naughty vs. Nice (2011).

title: Wit
tagline: It appears to be a matter of life and death.
overview: A renowned professor is forced to reassess her life when she is diagnosed with terminal ovarian cancer.
plot:
Vivian Bearing is a professor of English literature known for her intense knowledge of metaphysical poetry, especially the Holy Sonnets of John Donne. Her life takes a turn when she is diagnosed with metastatic Stage IV ovarian cancer. Oncologist Harvey Kelekian prescribes various chemotherapy treatments to treat her disease, and as she suffers through the various side-effects (such as fever, chills, vomiting, and abdominal pain), she attempts to put everything in perspective. The story periodically flashes back to previous moments in her life, including her childhood, her graduate school studies, and her career prior to her diagnosis. During the course of the film, she continually breaks the fourth wall by looking into the camera and expressing her feelings.
As she grows increasingly ill, Vivian agrees to undergo more tests and experimental treatments, even though she realizes the doctors treating her, including former student Jason Posner, see her less as someone to save and more as a guinea pig for their treatments. The only person who seems to care for her as a person is Susie Monahan, one of the nurses on the staff.
Late in Vivian's illness, the only visitor she receives in the hospital is her former graduate school professor and mentor, Evelyn Ashford, who reads her excerpts from Margaret Wise Brown's The Runaway Bunny. Ashford observes that the story is "a little allegory of the soul. No matter where it hides. God will find it".
As she nears the end of her life, Vivian manages to maintain her dignity and wit even as she is finally confronted with her own frailty and need for compassion. Vivian dies at the end of the film, with her voiceover reciting "death be not proud".

title: The Sorcerer's Apprentice
tagline: It's The Coolest Job Ever.
overview: Balthazar Blake is a master sorcerer in modern-day Manhattan trying to defend the city from his arch-nemesis, Maxim Horvath. Balthazar can't do it alone, so he recruits Dave Stutler, a seemingly average guy who demonstrates hidden potential, as his reluctant protégé. The sorcerer gives his unwilling accomplice a crash course in the art and science of magic, and together, these unlikely partners work to stop the forces of darkness.
plot:
The Sorcerer's Apprentice is a 2010 fantasy adventure film directed by Jon Turteltaub and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, based on the 1939 poem of the same name by Goethe. The movie stars Nicolas Cage as Balthazar Blake, a sorcerer who must find an apprentice to help him defeat the evil sorceress, Morgana.

The story begins with Balthazar Blake (Nicolas Cage), a powerful sorcerer who has been tasked with defeating the dark sorceress, Morgana (Alfred Molina). However, Morgana has stolen the magical staff of Merlin and is using its power to destroy the world. To defeat her, Balthazar must find an apprentice to help him gather the magical artifacts needed to break the staff's hold.

Balthazar meets his new apprentice, Dave Stutler (Jay Baruchel), a young college student who is struggling to pay for his tuition fees. Unbeknownst to Dave, he has been chosen by Balthazar as the perfect candidate to become his apprentice. As they embark on their quest, Balthazar teaches Dave the basics of magic and they set out to gather the magical artifacts needed to defeat Morgana.

However, things take a turn when Dave discovers that he is not just an ordinary college student, but also the reincarnation of Merlin's son, who was killed by Morgana. This revelation sets off a chain of events as Dave begins to uncover his true identity and the reason behind his selection as Balthazar's apprentice.

As they journey through ancient temples and mystical realms, Balthazar and Dave face numerous challenges and obstacles, including fierce creatures and treacherous landscapes. Along the way, Dave learns more about his magical abilities and the history of Merlin's staff, which holds the key to defeating Morgana.

In the climactic final battle, Balthazar and Dave face off against Morgana in an epic showdown. With the help of his newfound magical powers and the guidance of Balthazar, Dave is able to harness the power of the staff and defeat Morgana, saving the world from destruction.

Throughout the movie, Nicolas Cage delivers a memorable performance as the eccentric and powerful sorcerer, Balthazar Blake. Jay Baruchel shines as the awkward but lovable Dave Stutler, who finds himself caught up in a world of magic and adventure. The film's visual effects and action sequences are also noteworthy, bringing the magical world to life in a thrilling and entertaining way.

Overall, The Sorcerer's Apprentice is a fun and action-packed fantasy adventure that explores themes of identity, power, and friendship. With its memorable characters, stunning visuals, and exciting plot twists, it's a must-see for fans of magic and adventure movies.

title: Inception
tagline: Your mind is the scene of the crime.
overview: Cobb, a skilled thief who commits corporate espionage by infiltrating the subconscious of his targets is offered a chance to regain his old life as payment for a task considered to be impossible: "inception", the implantation of another person's idea into a target's subconscious.
plot:
Inception is a 2010 science fiction action film written, directed, and produced by Christopher Nolan. The movie follows Cobb, a skilled thief who specializes in entering people's dreams and stealing their secrets.

The story begins with Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio), a former soldier who lost his wife, Mal (Marion Cotillard), in a tragic accident. Cobb is haunted by the guilt of not being able to save her and is unable to return to the United States to see his children due to a past mistake that led to her death.

Cobb is approached by a wealthy businessman named Saito (Ken Watanabe) who offers him a chance to redeem himself and clear his name. Saito wants Cobb to perform a task known as "inception" - planting an idea in someone's mind instead of stealing one. The target is Robert Fischer (Cillian Murphy), the son of a dying business magnate, who needs to be convinced to dissolve his father's company.

To accomplish this, Cobb assembles a team of experts: Arthur (Joseph Gordon-Levitt), a point man; Ariadne (Ellen Page), an architect who designs the dreamscapes; Eames (Tom Hardy), a forger who can impersonate people in the dreams; and Saito, who joins the team as a consultant.

The team plans to perform "inception" by entering Fischer's dreams and convincing him to break up his father's company. However, things become complicated when Cobb's subconscious, fueled by guilt and anger, begins to sabotage the mission. Mal appears in Cobb's dreams, causing tension among the team.

As the team navigates multiple levels of dreams within dreams, they face various obstacles and challenges. The dream world becomes increasingly unstable, and the team must work together to stay one step ahead of their projections and maintain control over the dream state.

The climax of the movie features a thrilling sequence where Cobb's team performs a complex "inception" on Fischer, planting an idea in his mind that ultimately leads to the dissolution of the company. However, just as they think they've succeeded, Cobb is forced to confront his own guilt and emotions, which threaten to destroy the entire operation.

In the end, Cobb returns to the United States to see his children, but not before he performs a final " extraction" from his subconscious, allowing him to move on from his past and find closure. The movie ends with Cobb reunited with his children, but the audience is left wondering whether he's truly in a dream state or if he's finally found peace.

Throughout the film, Nolan explores themes of reality, identity, and the power of the human mind. The movie's complex plot and multiple layers of dreams create a sense of tension and uncertainty, keeping the audience engaged until the very end.

title: Grotesque
tagline: King of Japanese Grotesque Movie
overview: An unnamed doctor has always had everything he's ever wanted, but that has only made him develop more extreme and depraved needs. He kidnaps a young couple in the prime of their life together and forces them into a game of torment that slowly extinguishes their hopes for survival.
plot:
Grotesque (Japanese: Gurotesuku) is a 2009 Japanese exploitation horror film written and directed by Kōji Shiraishi, starring Hiroaki Kawatsure, Tsugumi Nagasawa and Shigeo Ōsako. Made on a small budget, it became one of the most notorious entries in the so-called torture horror cycle of the late 2000s, and it gained international attention when the British Board of Film Classification refused to certify it for release in the United Kingdom, judging that its sadistic content offered little beyond the infliction of pain and humiliation.

The plot is deliberately minimal. A young couple, Aki and Kazuo, are snatched from the street during their very first date and wake up restrained in a basement whose walls are covered in plastic sheeting. Their captor, a calm and well-dressed man, offers no explanation for what he is doing. Over a long series of scenes he subjects them to escalating physical abuse, sexual degradation and mutilation, forcing each to witness the suffering of the other. It eventually emerges that he is driven purely by his own gratification and by a twisted fascination with how people cling to life and to one another under extreme pain.

In a sudden change of tone, the captor moves the couple to a clean, hospital-like room, treats their injuries and reveals that he is a wealthy and respected physician. He promises that once they recover they will be released, that he will surrender to the police and that they will receive his fortune as compensation. Left alone, Aki and Kazuo vow to stay together after their ordeal. The promise proves to be another cruel game, and the couple are returned to the basement for a final round of torment that pushes the film toward a gruesome and bleakly absurd conclusion.

Shiraishi, previously known for found-footage horror such as Noroi: The Curse, shot the film with a stark, clinical style and a running time of little more than an hour, concentrating almost entirely on the three characters. Critical response was sharply divided. Variety gave a lukewarm review, acknowledging the committed acting and solid production values while finding the special effects uneven and the over-the-top finale more likely to provoke laughter than dread. Some horror outlets praised its audacity, while others dismissed it as pointless shock cinema.

title: Pulse
tagline: Do you want to meet a ghost?
overview: In the immense city of Tokyo, the darkness of the afterlife lurks some of its inhabitants who are desperately trying to escape the sadness and isolation of the modern world.
plot:
Pulse (Japanese: Kairo, literally "Circuit") is a 2001 Japanese techno-horror film written and directed by Kiyoshi Kurosawa. Released in Japan by Toho in February 2001, it screened in the Un Certain Regard section of that year's Cannes Film Festival. Its two intertwined stories follow ordinary Tokyo residents as ghosts begin entering the world of the living through the Internet and people vanish en masse.

Michi Kudo, who has recently moved to Tokyo, works at a plant shop. When her colleague Taguchi stops coming in, she visits his apartment, where he seems strangely distant, then finds him hanged moments later. A disk he left behind shows endless images of him staring at his monitor, with a ghostly face on another screen. Her coworker Yabe receives a call pleading "help me", enters a door sealed with red tape near Taguchi's apartment and meets a ghost; he returns changed and soon disappears, leaving only a dark stain on a wall. Junko, another coworker, is left catatonic after a similar "forbidden room" encounter and later dissolves into a stain in Michi's apartment.

Meanwhile, economics student Ryosuke Kawashima signs up with a new Internet provider, and his computer starts opening a website of eerie images of people alone in dark rooms. Harue Karasawa, a computer science graduate student, offers to examine them, but she becomes convinced the ghosts want to trap the living in eternal loneliness rather than kill them. After watching a man take his own life on her screen, she embraces an unseen presence and says happily that she is not alone, then disappears. As the vanishings sweep the Kantō region and Tokyo is evacuated, Ryosuke and Michi meet and find Harue in an abandoned factory, where she shoots herself. Ryosuke enters a forbidden room himself, where a ghost tells him that death is eternal loneliness, and loses the will to live. Michi drives him through the deserted city to Tokyo Bay, where survivors on a ship explain that the same thing is happening worldwide. As the ship heads for Latin America, Ryosuke fades into a stain, and Michi reflects on her last friend in the world.

Kumiko Asō plays Michi, Haruhiko Katō plays Ryosuke and Koyuki plays Harue. The film was well received, earning 76% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 68, with critics praising its power of suggestion and its portrait of loneliness. It became a cult favorite, inspired a 2006 American remake with two sequels, and Kurosawa turned the story into a novel.

title: Lake Mungo
tagline: If you've never seen a ghost... Look closer.
overview: After 16-year-old Alice Palmer drowns in a local dam, her family experiences a series of strange, inexplicable events centred in and around their home. Unsettled, the Palmers seek the help of psychic and parapsychologist, who discovers that Alice led a secret, double life. At Lake Mungo, Alice's secret past emerges.
plot:
While swimming with her family at a dam in Ararat, Australia, 16-year-old Alice Palmer disappears. Days later, her body is found in a stormwater drainage basin. Her parents, Russell and June, are called to identify the remains. Russell confirms the identity, but June refuses to view the body. Ten days after the funeral, Alice's brother Mathew develops unexplained bruises, and the family begins hearing strange noises. Russell reports an aggressive encounter with an apparition, while June experiences recurring nightmares of Alice's drenched corpse. Mathew takes up photography and appears to capture Alice's figure in the backyard and in a photograph taken at the lake.
Hoping Alice may still be alive, the Palmers request an exhumation and DNA test, which confirms that the body is hers. Meanwhile, Mathew installs cameras around the house to record apparent sightings of Alice. June consults self-proclaimed psychic Ray Kemeney, who conducts a séance but cannot explain the phenomena. Months later, Mathew confesses that he fabricated the ghostly photographs and videos to persuade his parents to exhume Alice's body, allowing June another opportunity to see her and find closure.
A home video recorded while the family is away appears to show Alice's apparition and their neighbour Brett Toohey, whom Alice had babysat for, searching her bedroom. June subsequently discovers a hidden videotape showing Alice in a threesome with Brett and his wife, Marissa. Russell concludes that Brett was searching for the tape after learning of Alice's death. The Tooheys soon sell their house and disappear. The Palmers are informed that legal action would probably result only in a suspended sentence, as the encounter would be considered consensual.
Ray later reveals that Alice visited him months before her death, describing recurring dreams about drowning and death, as well as her fear that her mother would be unable to see or help her. She had also recorded these fears in her journal. Alice's boyfriend, Jason Whittle, provides mobile phone footage from a school trip to Lake Mungo, showing Alice burying something beneath a tree. The Palmers visit the site and recover her phone. Its footage shows Alice walking along the shoreline at night before encountering a bloated, disfigured version of herself, identical to the body recovered at the dam, floating slowly towards her.
The Palmers come to believe that Alice wanted them to understand her experiences, although they disagree over whether the encounter at Lake Mungo motivated her death. Believing the haunting has ended, they move out of their home. As June takes one final look into Alice's bedroom, audio from Alice's interview with Ray plays, recalling her fear that her mother could not see her. Alice remarks, "she's gone," as June leaves.

title: Gacy
tagline: Friend. Neighbor. Killer.
overview: Based on a true story of serial killer a model citizen, loving father and husband and serial killer John Wayne Gacy, a man with over 30 dead men and boys entombed in the crawl space underneath his house which he shared with his family.
plot:
Gacy, also known as The Crawl Space, is a 2003 American crime horror film written and directed by Clive Saunders, with David Birke as co-writer. Released direct to video, it dramatizes the crimes of John Wayne Gacy, the serial killer who raped, tortured and murdered at least thirty-three men and boys in the Chicago area during the 1970s. Mark Holton plays Gacy in his first leading role.

A prologue set in 1953 shows the young Gacy being belittled and kicked by his father, who tells him he will never be brave enough. In 1976 the adult Gacy has a family lunch interrupted by a neighbor complaining about a stench from his crawl space, and then by Steve, an employee who has gone unpaid for two weeks. Advised by a friend to use lime against the smell, Gacy continues to lead a double life. He abducts a man, confides his troubles to him in his garage and lets him go and invites a new hire to wrestle in his yard, and when Steve mocks him with a homophobic slur, Gacy is enraged. Steve and two other men beat and rob Gacy, and soon afterward Gacy's wife, Kara, sees him bring a handcuffed Steve into the garage at night, then finds clothes scattered there and catches Gacy emerging from the crawl space.

Gacy throws a Fourth of July costume party at which he is praised as an asset to the community and offers a job to a young man, Tom Kovak. He hires an exterminator for the maggots and cockroaches under the house and tells police that Steve left for Costa Rica or Puerto Rico. After Kara finds handcuffs and gay magazines in the garage, she leaves with their two daughters, leaving him with his mother. Tom, troubled at home, rents Gacy's spare room. Gacy chloroforms a male prostitute, holds him in chains overnight and leaves him in a park, pours concrete into the crawl space to mask the smell, and drowns a man in his bathtub after agreeing to buy his car. When a video about Gacy's business turns into pornography, Tom becomes terrified and tries to leave, but Gacy handcuffs him and begins strangling him. Tom escapes and goes to the police, who search the house, find dozens of watches and driver's licenses, arrest Gacy and exhume the bodies. The film closes with Gacy's defiant last words before his execution.

Critics were negative: the film holds 17% on Rotten Tomatoes from six reviews. LA Weekly called it unconvincing and unenlightening, faulting its dime-store psychology, and DVD Talk gave it half a star out of five.

title: Touchez Pas au Grisbi
tagline: It Bristles With Violence!
overview: Gentleman gangster Max and his partner, Riton, pull off their last, most successful heist and find themselves comfortable enough to retire in the style they enjoy. However, Max confides the details of the theft to his younger mistress, Josey -- who has secretly taken up with ambitious young rival gangster Angelo. Angelo then has Riton kidnapped and demands the stash of gold as ransom, which threatens Max's dreams of the perfect retirement.
plot:
Max, a successful middle-aged Parisian gangster, has dinner at Madame Bouche's restaurant, his hangout, with his longtime crime partner Riton. Riton has brought his girlfriend Josy, a burlesque dancer half his age, and her act partner Lola, who craves Max. Max's down on his luck protégé Marco shows up. The group leaves for the girls' club, with Riton slapping Josy for snorting some heroin. To settle a dispute between local drug kingpin Angelo and club owner Pierrot, Max gets Marco a job as a pusher working for Angelo. After the show, Max discovers Josy making out with Angelo, but does not tell Riton, then leaves early for home.
On the way, Max's cabbie notices they are being followed by a suspicious ambulance. Max gets the drop on its two hoodlums and sends them packing, then calls Riton and warns him not to go with Angelo, who has just invited him go out at 2 AM. Max takes Riton to his hideout and shows him the eight bars of gold they stole during a recent heist hidden in the trunk of a car locked in the building's garage. Upstairs, the two friends share a simple snack, with Max telling Riton about Josy and Angelo, then getting him to admit he had told Josy about the big score to impress her. Max concludes Josy told Angelo, who planned to beat the loot's location out of them that night. He confesses he is sick of the criminal lifestyle and plans to retire with the money from the gold, and tells Riton to leave Josy to the younger Angelo.
The next morning Max leaves early to fence the gold with his uncle, who needs time to raise the cash. Max leaves it, then returns to an empty apartment. He calls Josy's, and is told by the nervous porter that Riton had just been taken away in an ambulance, and that Josy is out.
Max rounds up Marco, then roughly, but unsuccessfully, interrogates Josy and the porter over where Angelo has taken Riton. Marco captures Fifi, one of Angelo's henchmen on a stakeout for Max. They go to tough-guy Pierrot for help interrogating the punk, but Fifi does not know anything useful. Angelo telephones and proposes to trade Riton for the gold, and Max agrees. He, Marco, and Pierrot arm themselves, retrieve the gold, and head out in Fifi's car.
On a deserted country road Max hands over the gold and Riton is returned unharmed. After his captors leave Riton warns Max that there had been a second car, which appears in the distance. Angelo's henchmen blow up Fifi's car with hand grenades, killing Marco, but are gunned down by the others. They use the henchmen's car to chase Angelo. A rolling shootout ensues, Riton is wounded, and Angelo's car crashes. Angelo is shot attempting to throw a grenade, which explodes and sets his car on fire. As it is engulfed Max is forced to leave the loot before they get caught.
Back at Pierrot's, Riton is patched up by a mob doctor. Riton urges Max to go about his normal routine to avoid suspicion, so Max takes wealthy mistress Betty to Bouche's for lunch.

title: The Bounty Hunter
tagline: It's a Job. It Isn't Personal. Well, Maybe a Little...
overview: A revered bounty hunter's latest gig is rather satisfying, as his bail-skipper is his ex-wife, who has no intention of getting nabbed without a fight.
plot:
The Bounty Hunter is an American romantic action comedy of 2010 directed by Andy Tennant. Gerard Butler stars as Milo Boyd, a former New York police detective turned bounty hunter, and Jennifer Aniston as his former wife, the reporter Nicole Hurley, with Jason Sudeikis as her admiring colleague Stewart, Jeff Garlin as the bail bondsman Sid, Cathy Moriarty as the bookmaker Irene, Peter Greene as the corrupt officer Earl Mahler and Dorian Missick as Milo's friend and former partner Bobby.

Nicole, awaiting trial for assaulting a police officer, skips her court date to chase a tip about a suicide that may have been a murder, and the judge issues a warrant for her arrest. Her informant, Jimmy, is kidnapped before she can meet him. Milo is delighted when Sid offers him $5,000 to bring her in, and with unwitting help from Nicole's mother he tracks her to a New Jersey racetrack, throws her in the boot of his car and heads for Manhattan. They are pursued on several fronts: Irene's thugs want Milo's gambling debts, Earl Mahler, implicated in Nicole's story, wants her dead, and Stewart is trying to rescue her, until the thugs mistake him for Milo and abduct him.

After Earl tries and fails to shoot Nicole on the road, Milo learns that her investigation implicates his old partner, Bobby, and agrees to look into it. Clues lead them to a country club and then towards Earl's tattoo parlour in Queens. Lying low at the very inn where they honeymooned, the exes rediscover their feelings, but when Nicole overhears Milo saying he will still deliver her to jail, she handcuffs him to the bed and drives off. She frees Jimmy but is seized by Irene's men, and Milo rescues her at a strip club. At the police evidence warehouse, Earl, who has exploited Bobby's name to steal drugs and cash, shoots Bobby, but Milo and Nicole overpower him, and the wounded Bobby explains he had been waiting for Earl to make his move. Despite their reconciliation, Milo still hands Nicole over for the bounty, then punches an officer who had insulted him, landing in the neighbouring cell so that they can spend their anniversary together, declaring their love through the bars.

Released in the United States on 19 March 2010, the film was panned by critics, scoring 13% on Rotten Tomatoes, yet grossed about $136.3 million worldwide on a budget of $40-45 million.

title: Salt
tagline: Who is Salt?
overview: As a CIA officer, Evelyn Salt swore an oath to duty, honor and country. Her loyalty will be tested when a defector accuses her of being a Russian spy. Salt goes on the run, using all her skills and years of experience as a covert operative to elude capture. Salt's efforts to prove her innocence only serve to cast doubt on her motives, as the hunt to uncover the truth behind her identity continues and the question remains: "Who is Salt?"
plot:
Salt is a 2010 American action spy thriller film directed by Phillip Noyce and starring Angelina Jolie as Evelyn Salt, a CIA operative accused of being a Russian sleeper agent.

The movie begins with Evelyn Salt (Angelina Jolie) living a seemingly ordinary life in Boston with her husband, Col. Hanin "Hank" Salt (Chiwetel Ejiofor), and their young daughter, Sophia. However, it is revealed that Evelyn's life is actually a carefully constructed cover for her true identity as a Russian sleeper agent.

The CIA discovers that Evelyn has been compromised by the Russians, who have been manipulating her since she was a teenager in Kazakhstan. The agency believes that Evelyn is about to be activated and will carry out a mission to assassinate several high-ranking government officials in Washington D.C.

As Evelyn tries to clear her name and prove her loyalty to the CIA, she must also evade the Russian agents sent to kill her. She teams up with a former CIA operative, Ted Beck (Liev Schreiber), who helps her uncover the truth about her past and the conspiracy against her.

Throughout the movie, Evelyn's character is revealed through flashbacks, showing her training as a sleeper agent in Russia and her subsequent recruitment by the CIA. The film also explores Evelyn's complicated relationship with her husband, Hank, who is unaware of her true identity.

As the plot thickens, Evelyn discovers that she has been framed for the assassination attempts, and that the real traitor is a high-ranking government official named Peter Krilov (Michael York). With the help of Ted and other allies, Evelyn must use her skills as a spy to take down Krilov and his accomplices before it's too late.

The movie culminates in an intense showdown between Evelyn and Krilov at the White House. In the end, Evelyn is able to clear her name and bring the real traitor to justice, but not before she suffers a serious injury that leaves her with a permanent scar on her neck.

Overall, Salt is a fast-paced and action-packed thriller that explores themes of loyalty, identity, and redemption. Angelina Jolie delivers a strong performance as Evelyn Salt, bringing depth and nuance to the character despite the film's somewhat predictable plot.

title: The American
overview: Dispatched to a small Italian town to await further orders, assassin Jack embarks on a double life that may be more relaxing than is good for him.
plot:
Jack and his lover, Ingrid, are relaxing in Sweden. As they walk in the wilderness outside their cabin, Jack becomes alarmed by a trail of footprints in the snow. A sniper's shots ring out, but Ingrid sees Jack pull a gun from his pocket and shoot the sniper; without hesitation, he kills her too before locating and killing another armed man. He flees to Rome and contacts a man named Pavel, who insists that Jack cannot stay in Rome and sends him to Castelvecchio, a small town in the mountains of Abruzzo. A nervous Jack disposes of the cell phone, which Pavel gave him, and goes to nearby Castel del Monte instead, where he goes by the name of Edward.
While in Abruzzo, Jack contacts Pavel, who sets him up with a job. He meets a woman named Mathilde, who wants him to build her a custom sniper rifle. A local priest named Father Benedetto takes notice of Jack, and befriends him. Jack also begins soliciting a local prostitute named Clara, and they start a relationship.
In the meantime, Jack suspects that he's being followed by a man, but still meets with Mathilde in a secluded river area to test the weapon. Although impressed by the craftsmanship, she asks Jack to make a few more adjustments and provide specific types of ammunition before they complete their transaction.
Later, the man follows Jack, planning on killing him. Realising he is being tailed, Jack doubles back, getting behind the man, and prepares to kill him. However, a motorbike enters the lane where Jack and the man are standing right as Jack goes to shoot the would-be assassin. The assassin shoots the motorist instead, and flees in a car. Jack pursues him through the town on the bike, eventually shooting out a tire on his car, causing him to crash, before approaching the car and killing him.
The next day, Benedetto asks Jack if he has anything to confess. Although he is tormented by dreams of the events in Sweden and has regrets for killing Ingrid, Jack shares nothing. When Benedetto says that he senses Jack lives in a special kind of hell, "a place without love", Jack starts to let himself feel love for Clara and envisions a life with her.
Jack calls Pavel to ask how the Swedes found him, and Pavel tells Jack that he's losing his edge. In his growing fear, he even suspects Clara when he discovers a small pistol in her purse. They go on a picnic to the secluded river, where Jack prepares to kill Clara. But when she does not try to kill him, Jack begins to trust her and agrees to meet with her later back in town.
Finally, Jack agrees to deliver the completed weapon and ammunition to Mathilde as his last job, but at the last moment, he re-opens the briefcase he has stored it in and makes some adjustments to the weapon. During the drop-off, Jack becomes suspicious that Mathilde plans to kill him, but a busload of schoolchildren arrive, preventing a confrontation. Mathilde gives Jack a padded envelope of cash before they separate.

title: The Other Guys
tagline: When the cops are busy... Our only hope is...
overview: Unlike their heroic counterparts on the force, desk-bound NYPD detectives Gamble and Hoitz garner no headlines as they work day to day. When a seemingly minor case turns out to be a big deal, the two cops get the opportunity to finally prove to their comrades that they have the right stuff.
plot:
The Other Guys is a 2010 American action comedy film directed by Adam McKay and starring Will Ferrell and Mark Wahlberg.

In the beginning, we are introduced to two mismatched police detectives, Allen Gamble (Will Ferrell) and Terry Hoitz (Mark Wahlberg). Gamble is a desk-bound, by-the-book detective who has never had to face real danger in his life. He's a bit of an awkward, nerdy guy who often finds himself at odds with his partner.

Hoitz, on the other hand, is a hot-headed, aggressive cop who has always dreamed of being a hero. However, he's been stuck working with Gamble for years and feels like he's never gotten the recognition he deserves.

The story takes a turn when two high-profile crimes occur in New York City: a bank robbery and a kidnapping. The police department is abuzz with excitement as they try to catch the perpetrators, but Gamble and Hoitz are left out of the action.

As it turns out, the real heroes of the case are two young, up-and-coming detectives, P.K. Highsmith (Dwayne Johnson) and Christopher Danson (Samuel L. Jackson). The two men are reckless, arrogant, and completely unqualified for the job, but they manage to stumble their way into the spotlight.

Gamble and Hoitz are left feeling like they're being overshadowed by these new heroes, and they begin to feel like they're not good enough. However, when Highsmith and Danson start to get in over their heads, Gamble and Hoitz see an opportunity to prove themselves.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Highsmith and Danson are actually a pair of bumbling, incompetent detectives who have been given a high-profile case by mistake. They're more interested in getting attention than solving the crime, and they start to put themselves and others in danger.

Gamble and Hoitz team up with Highsmith and Danson to take down the real villains behind the crimes. Along the way, they learn to work together and trust each other, despite their differences.

In the end, Gamble and Hoitz manage to save the day, but not before they've had a chance to prove themselves as capable detectives. The film ends with a heartwarming moment between Gamble and Hoitz, who have finally found a sense of camaraderie and respect for each other.

Overall, The Other Guys is a hilarious and action-packed comedy that pokes fun at the conventions of police procedurals while still delivering plenty of excitement and thrills.
