title: The Mechanic
tagline: Someone has to fix the problems.
overview: Arthur Bishop is a 'mechanic' - an elite assassin with a strict code and unique talent for cleanly eliminating targets. It's a job that requires professional perfection and total detachment, and Bishop is the best in the business. But when he is ordered to take out his mentor and close friend Harry, Bishop is anything but detached.
plot:
Hitman Arthur Bishop sneaks into the home of a Colombian cartel boss and drowns him in his own pool. Upon returning home to Louisiana, he meets with his friend and mentor Harry McKenna.
Bishop is assigned by his employer Dean to kill Harry. Dean says this is due to a failed mission in South Africa, in which his team of assassins were killed; since the mission was known only to Dean and Harry, Dean attributes the failure of the mission to Harry ratting them out to the South African police, making him a threat. Bishop reluctantly kills Harry and makes it look like a carjacking. At Harry's funeral, Bishop meets Harry's estranged son Steve, whom he later stops from killing another carjacker in revenge.
Steve asks Bishop to train him as a hitman; Bishop thus takes him under his wing and gives Steve his next contract, fellow assassin Burke. He also brings Steve to another contract killing to observe. Ignoring Bishop's instructions to overdose Burke with Rohypnol, Steve goes with him to his house and attempts to strangle the much larger man with a belt, imitating Bishop's last killing. He barely manages to kill Burke after a lengthy fight. Dean expresses disapproval of Bishop using Steve, which violates the rules of the contract.
Bishop's next target is cult leader Andrew Vaughn, whom Steve suggests they inject with adrenaline to simulate a heart attack. However, Vaughn's doctor administers an IV of ketamine, which would inhibit the adrenaline's effects. The two choke Vaughn to death instead with a mini camera.
They are discovered by the guards, shoot their way out, and fly home separately to avoid suspicion. At the airport, Bishop catches sight of a hitman who was supposedly killed in the South Africa mission that Harry sold out. The hitman reveals that Dean engineered the failed mission to cover up his own shady dealings. Bishop realizes Dean framed Harry and tricked Bishop into killing him.
Angry at being tricked, Bishop takes down the team Dean sends to kill him and helps Steve when Steve is also ambushed. Steve finds his father's gun in Bishop's belongings, and realizes that Bishop killed him. Bishop and Steve kill Dean together. Bishop plans to disappear with a new identity now that his employer is dead. When they stop for gas, Steve, in revenge, blows up the truck with Bishop still inside.
Steve returns to Bishop's home and does two things Bishop told him not to: plays a record on the turntable and steals Bishop's 1966 Jaguar E-Type. As he drives, Steve finds a note on the passenger seat; it reads: "Steve, if you're reading this, then you're dead." The car then explodes, killing him. Another explosion from the rigged turntable destroys the house. Bishop had seen Steve carrying his father's gun, and knew beforehand that Steve would betray him.
Security footage at the gas station reveals that Bishop had escaped from the truck before the explosion. He gets into a spare truck and drives away.

title: High School
tagline: Random drug tests? You just can't study for them.
overview: A high school valedictorian who gets baked with the local stoner finds himself the subject of a drug test. The situation causes him to concoct an ambitious plan to get his entire graduating class to face the same fate, and fail.
plot:
High School is a 2010 American teen stoner comedy and the feature directorial debut of John Stalberg Jr. It stars Matt Bush as Henry Burke, a model student, and Sean Marquette as his former best friend Travis, with Adrien Brody as the eccentric drug dealer Psycho Ed, Michael Chiklis as the school's principal, Dr. Gordon, and Colin Hanks, Adhir Kalyan, Mykelti Williamson, Yeardley Smith, Curtis Armstrong and Michael Vartan in supporting roles.

Henry Burke is Morgan High School's top student, on track to become valedictorian and headed for a bright future, while Travis is the school's resident stoner and troublemaker. Reconnecting just before graduation, Travis persuades Henry to smoke marijuana for the first time. The next day, after the school's spelling bee champion is caught high during a competition, the principal announces a zero-tolerance drug test for the entire student body, and anyone who fails will be expelled. Facing the destruction of everything he has worked for, Henry panics.

Travis comes up with a desperate plan: if every student in the school fails the test, the results will be invalid. He knows of a psychotic drug dealer, Psycho Ed, who possesses a powerful stash of cannabis extract, and the two boys steal it in order to secretly get the entire school high before the test. As the students and teachers become increasingly intoxicated, chaos spreads through Morgan High, while Henry and Travis are pursued by both the furious Psycho Ed and the suspicious Dr. Gordon, and Henry's academic rival threatens to expose them.

The film satirizes zero-tolerance school policies and high school culture through broad, outrageous humor.

High School was shot in 2008 in Howell, Michigan, and premiered at the Sundance Film Festival, where it was well received on the festival circuit, including at the Edinburgh International Film Festival. Its release was delayed for more than two years while the producers made changes, and it was eventually distributed by Anchor Bay Films in 2012, receiving mostly negative reviews, with 28 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31.

title: The Runaways
tagline: It's 1975 and they're about to explode.
overview: Joan Jett and Cherie Currie, two rebellious teenagers from Southern California, become the frontwomen for the Runaways -- the now-legendary group that paved the way for future generations of female rockers. Under the Svengali-like influence of impresario Kim Fowley, the band becomes a huge success.
plot:
The Runaways is a 2010 American biographical drama film about the 1970s rock band of the same name, written and directed by music video director Floria Sigismondi in her feature debut. Based on Neon Angel: A Memoir of a Runaway (1989) by the band's lead singer Cherie Currie, it stars Dakota Fanning as Currie, Kristen Stewart as rhythm guitarist and vocalist Joan Jett and Michael Shannon as the record producer Kim Fowley, with Riley Keough and Stella Maeve. Jett served as an executive producer. The film depicts the band's formation in 1975 and focuses on the relationship between Currie and Jett.

In Los Angeles, teenager Cherie Currie dreams of becoming a rock star; she idolizes David Bowie, styles herself after his Aladdin Sane persona and wins her school talent show despite hecklers. Joan Jett, another teenager with the same dream, meets the flamboyant producer Kim Fowley at a club and tells him she wants to form an all-girl rock band. Fowley introduces her to drummer Sandy West, and the two begin playing together while Fowley insists that they need a striking blonde singer in the style of Brigitte Bardot. Scouring the city's clubs, Joan and Kim find Cherie and invite her to audition at a trailer park in the San Fernando Valley. When her chosen song falls flat, Joan and Kim write "Cherry Bomb" on the spot, and Cherie wins the job. With Lita Ford on lead guitar, the Runaways sign with Mercury Records and the success of their first album takes them to Japan for a concert, where overexcited fans mob them. Fame brings its own pressures, however. Magazine photo shoots that focus on Cherie's sex appeal breed resentment within the band, Cherie's drug use spirals out of control, and Fowley's harsh treatment of the girls takes its toll. As Cherie struggles with addiction and the strain of her troubled family life, the intense bond between her and Joan is tested, and the band begins to come apart under the weight of its own success, while Joan remains fiercely determined to keep playing rock and roll.

The film received generally favorable reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 69% rating based on 193 reviews, with a consensus that, while viewers expecting an in-depth biopic will be disappointed, it is as electric as the band's music thanks to strong performances by Shannon, Fanning and Stewart, and Metacritic gave it a score of 65 out of 100. It grossed around $4.6 million worldwide.

title: Night of the Demons
tagline: All Hell Is Going To Break Loose
overview: Angela is throwing a decadent Halloween party at New Orleans' infamous Broussard Mansion. But after the police break up the festivities, Maddie and a few friends stay behind. Trapped inside the locked mansion gates, the remaining guests uncover a horrifying secret and soon fall victim to seven vicious, blood-thirsty demons.
plot:
In 1925, Evangeline Broussard hosts an evening gathering hoping to catch the eye of her crush Louis, who is into black magic. At a séance, a group of demons are summoned and state that they need seven human sacrifices to rise again. Frightened by this, Evangeline prepares to hang herself from her balcony to stop their plans. Louis attempts to stop her, but she jumps, decapitating herself in the process. Louis stares over the balcony as his eyes become demonic.
In the present, Maddie and her friends Lily and Suzanne attend a party held by Angela Feld. Also attending are Maddie's drug dealing ex-boyfriend Colin, Lily's ex-boyfriend Dex, and Dex's friend Jason. At the party, Angela prompts everyone to go wild, as she must make money off the party to avoid living on the streets. Lily and Dex eventually reunite while Suzanne becomes incredibly drunk. When Maddie goes to the bathroom, a hand grabs her through the mirror, with the others dismissing it off as an elaborate trick placed by Angela.
Eventually police officers arrive and break up the party, leaving an upset Angela alone in the house. Maddie, Lily, Dex and Jason soon return to find Suzanne, who has passed out. Colin and Angela go into the basement to find the drugs he had hid earlier. They discover a hidden door, and Angela remarks that the house is full of hidden rooms, including a tunnel that leads to the next estate over. They enter the room and find six skeletons, whom Angela believes are the remains of the missing party guests of Evangeline Broussard. One of the skeletons bites Angela's hand. Colin attempts to leave the house, only to discover that the gate is locked. While everyone plans to wait the night out, Suzanne tells the group the story of the night that led to Evangeline and her friends' deaths. The only person found alive was the maid, who was found scribbling spells on her walls, having been driven insane by the night's events.
Angela slowly succumbs to the skeleton bite and turns into a demon. She returns to the group and infects Dex by kissing him, who in turn infects Lily. While Maddie, Jason, and Colin leave to find another exit, Angela seduces Suzanne and turns her into a demon. Jason finds a demonic Lily and goes to warn the others. They are initially skeptical until a demonic Suzanne attacks them. They decide to escape through the tunnel, only to discover it has caved. The group is then attacked by Lily and Dex as Jason is injured. The survivors run upstairs and tend to Jason's injury and realize they are in the maid's room with the symbols she drew still on the walls, acting as a ward against the demons. They discover that the demons were thrown out of hell for trying to usurp Satan's rule and need seven human vessels to be free. The demons had tricked Evangeline into hosting the party so they could take over the guests, but failed after she hanged herself, as they cannot possess corpses.
Soon the walls begin pouring with blood and wash the spells away.

title: Love Wrecked
tagline: She's shipwrecked on an island with the guy of her dreams. The last thing she wants is to be rescued.
overview: On a Caribbean cruise, Jenny is marooned on a beach with her rock and roll idol. Deliriously in love with the idea of time alone with him, she manages to hide the fact that they're a stone's throw away from their resort.
plot:
Jenny Taylor is a huge fan of Jason Masters, a world-famous rock star, but her efforts to meet him are constantly thwarted by her nemesis, Alexis Minetti. Hoping for another chance to meet Jason, Jenny takes a job at his favorite Caribbean resort, joined by her best friend Ryan.
Jenny sneaks aboard a party vessel Jason is on, and when he is washed overboard, she jumps in to save him. Though the pair find themselves marooned in a secluded cove of a seemingly deserted island, she soon discovers that they have landed a short distance from the resort. Jenny does not let on to Jason that they are not stranded so she can get him to fall in love with her.
Jenny is secretly helped by Ryan, who drives out to her location to provide her with supplies. When Alexis discovers Jenny's ruse by following Ryan, she also pretends to be marooned with them. While Ryan has been helping, he has also decided to act on his long-standing crush on Jenny, seeking advice on asking her out.
Ryan completely transforms himself, yet when Jenny sees him, all she talks about is Jason. He confesses he cannot stop thinking about her and kisses her, but when she protests that they are friends, he tells her that he is going home and drives off.
Jenny feels bad and after learning that the coast guard has called off the search for them and seeing mourning fans around the world, she tells Jason the truth about not being stranded. He becomes upset at both her and Alexis, promises to sue them both, and leaves them behind as he hitches a ride back to the resort.
When Ryan hears that a storm is going to hit the side of the island where Jenny is, he drives out to save her. As the storm builds, she gets stuck in the car he had abandoned to look for her. Ryan returns just in time to save her as the car is about to slide over a muddy embankment. When he takes Jenny into a cave and lights a fire to keep her warm, she realizes that he is the one that cares for her the most.
After the storm passes, Jenny and Ryan return to the resort, where Jason and his manager Brent Hernandez tell Jenny that they need her help to maintain the "stranded" story at a press conference. Ryan proclaims his love for her before he is thrown out the door by Brent.
At the press conference, Jenny tells everyone that her boyfriend is Ryan and that Alexis is Jason's fiancée, then walks off with Ryan. Some time later, while performing on stage in Winnipeg, Jason unhappily dedicates a song to his wife, Alexis, who is standing at his side.

title: Airport 1975
tagline: Something hit us... The crew is dead... Help us, please, please help us!
overview: When an in-flight collision incapacitates the pilots of an airplane bound for Los Angeles, stewardess Nancy Pryor is forced to take over the controls. From the ground, her boyfriend Alan Murdock, a retired test pilot, tries to talk her through piloting and landing the 747 aircraft. Worse yet, the anxious passengers — among which are a noisy nun and a cranky man — are aggravating the already tense atmosphere.
plot:
Airport 1975 is a 1974 American disaster film directed by Jack Smight, produced by William Frye and written by Don Ingalls, the second installment in the Airport series. Charlton Heston stars as Captain Al Murdock and Karen Black as stewardess Nancy Pryor, with George Kennedy as Joe Patroni, Efrem Zimbalist Jr. as Captain Stacy, Dana Andrews as Scott Freeman, Roy Thinnes as Urias and Ed Nelson as Major John Alexander. Gloria Swanson, in her final film, Linda Blair and Helen Reddy, in her debut, also appear.

Columbia Airlines Flight 409, a Boeing 747, flies overnight from Washington to Los Angeles, while businessman Scott Freeman pilots his Beechcraft to Boise. Bad weather diverts both to Salt Lake City. As Flight 409 is cleared to land ahead of him, Freeman suffers a heart attack, and his plane climbs out of control and slams into the jet's cockpit. First Officer Urias is sucked out, the flight engineer is killed and Captain Stacy is blinded. Stacy engages the autopilot before passing out, and Nancy radios that no one can fly the plane. Patroni, a Columbia executive whose family is aboard, turns to Murdock, the chief flight instructor and Nancy's estranged boyfriend.

The autopilot keeps the jet level but cannot turn it, and the plane is heading toward the Wasatch Range. Murdock talks Nancy through manual turns until radio contact fails, and with Stacy's help she climbs over the peaks. A military helicopter then attempts a midair pilot transfer. Major Alexander is lowered toward the hole in the cockpit, but his harness snags on the torn metal, he comes loose and falls to his death. Murdock, the only other person aboard qualified to land a 747, is lowered successfully. He lands at Salt Lake City, using high-speed taxiing to stop as brake pressure fails. The passengers escape down the evacuation slides, and Nancy and Murdock reconcile. Reddy, as a nun, sings "Best Friend" to an ailing girl played by Blair.

The production rented a 747 from American Airlines and filmed at Salt Lake City and Dulles. Universal released it on October 18, 1974. Made for $3 million, it grossed $47.3 million in the United States and Canada, the seventh-highest total of the year, and about $103 million worldwide. Reviews were largely negative. Pauline Kael dismissed it as "cut-rate swill" and Roger Ebert called it "corny escapism", while both Kael and Ebert criticized the condescending treatment of Black's character. Reddy received a Golden Globe nomination.

title: The Gruffalo
overview: The magical tale of a mouse who sets foot on a woodland adventure in search of a nut. Encountering predators who all wish to eat him - Fox, Owl and Snake - the brave mouse creates a terrifying, imaginary monster to frighten them away. But what will the mouse do when he meets this frightful monster for real?
plot:
In an autumn forest, a red squirrel mother finds a nut. Her children are playing until they see an owl. The mother squirrel drops the nut as she escapes from the owl, but her children ask her to tell them a story before she retrieves it. So she tells the story of a mouse strolling through a deep dark wood.
The mouse, who is hungry, makes a journey to a nut tree and encounters a fox, who tries to persuade him to have lunch with him. The mouse responds by making up a story that he is instead having lunch with a "Gruffalo", a monster with "terrible tusks and terrible claws and terrible teeth in his terrible jaws". When he tells the fox that the Gruffalo's favorite food is "roasted fox", the fox runs away in fright.
The mouse uses the same trick to survive encounters with an owl and a snake, telling them that the Gruffalo's favorite food is "owl ice cream" and "scrambled snake", respectively, while adding details about the Gruffalo's appearance at each encounter. Later, the three animals meet and talk about their encounters with the mouse and realize that they have been tricked.
The mouse finally reaches the nut tree and suddenly encounters with a real Gruffalo, which is exactly as he had described it. When the Gruffalo catches and threatens to eat him, the mouse uses his wits again and says that everyone in the wood is afraid of him, asking the Gruffalo to follow him and see. As the two of them meet the predators, the presence of the Gruffalo frightens them away, but the Gruffalo believes they are afraid of the mouse. As the Gruffalo prepares to eat the mouse, the mouse's stomach growls and he says his favorite food is Gruffalo crumble, causing the Gruffalo to retreat in fear. Finally safe, he finds the nut from earlier, which the Gruffalo had knocked down, and eats it in peace.
When the mother squirrel ends her story, the children feel better and they all go to retrieve their nut as snow begins to fall.

title: Hachi: A Dog's Tale
tagline: A true story of faith, devotion and undying love.
overview: A drama based on the true story of a college professor's bond with the abandoned dog he takes into his home.
plot:
Hachi: A Dog's Tale is a 2009 American drama film directed by Lasse Hallström and written by Stephen P. Lindsey, based on the 1987 Japanese film Hachikō Monogatari, written by Kaneto Shindo and directed by Seijirō Kōyama. Both films are inspired by the true story of Hachikō, an Akita dog in Japan who continued to wait at a Tokyo train station for his owner for nearly ten years after the man's death. The American version transfers the story to a modern New England setting. Richard Gere, who also produced the film, stars with Joan Allen, Sarah Roemer, Jason Alexander and Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa.

The film is framed by a schoolboy named Ronnie, who tells his class that his hero is Hachi, the dog that belonged to his grandfather. Parker Wilson, a college music professor who commutes to Providence, finds a lost Akita puppy at the train station in the small town of Bedridge and takes him home for the night. When no one claims the dog, Parker grows attached to him despite the reluctance of his wife Cate. His Japanese friend Ken identifies the breed and translates the symbol on the dog's collar as "Hachi," meaning eight, a lucky number, and the name sticks.

Hachi becomes devoted to Parker. Ken explains that Akitas are independent dogs that will not do tricks on command, and that if Hachi ever fetches a ball for Parker, it will be for a special reason. One day Hachi slips out of the yard and follows Parker to the station, and that evening Parker finds him waiting at the station when the train arrives. A daily ritual begins: every morning Hachi walks with Parker to the station, and every afternoon at five o'clock he returns to meet his train. Their routine, and the friendships it creates with the station master, a hot dog vendor and other townspeople, continue for years until a tragedy changes everything, and Hachi's loyalty becomes a source of wonder for the town.

The film premiered at the Seattle International Film Festival in June 2009 and was released theatrically in many countries, although Sony released it directly to DVD in the United States. It received mixed-to-positive reviews, with a 64 percent Rotten Tomatoes rating. Critics described it as an unashamed tear-jerker; Christopher Lloyd of the Sarasota Herald-Tribune admitted that viewers may resent the manipulation but still gave it four out of five stars. It grossed about $47 million worldwide.

title: The Class
tagline: The Chronicle of a Catastrophe.
overview: An average guy of an Estonian high-school decides to defend his bullied classmate. This starts a war between him and the informal leader of the class. As teenagers' honour is a touchy thing, everything ends in bloodshed.
plot:
The Class (Klass) is an Estonian drama film of 2007 directed by Ilmar Raag about bullying and school violence. Pärt Uusberg plays the persecuted teenager Joosep Rääk and Vallo Kirs plays Kaspar Kordes, the classmate who takes his side, with Lauri Pedaja as the ringleader Anders, Paula Solvak as Kaspar's girlfriend Thea, Mikk Mägi as Paul and Margus Prangel as Joosep's father. A seven-episode television sequel, Class: Life After, followed.

Joosep is tormented by his entire high school class, with Anders and his friends Paul, Toomas, Tiit and Olav leading the abuse: they beat him repeatedly and, after a basketball game, strip him and shove him into the girls' changing room. When Kaspar starts helping him, the class turns on Kaspar too, and Thea grows distant. After the teacher, Laine, catches Paul stealing Joosep's notebook, Paul blames Kaspar, and the school calls Joosep's parents. His father Margus, a gun enthusiast obsessed with making his son a real man, urges him to fight the ringleader. Anders's gang later locks Kaspar in a burned-out shed and makes him watch as they beat Joosep until he can barely breathe, warning that any further defense will only make things worse. Joosep asks Kaspar to stop protecting him, hoping simply to endure until graduation.

The class mocks the pair as supposedly gay, and Thea leaves Kaspar, believing he cares more for Joosep than for her. When Joosep's mother finds bruises on him and complains to the school, the class is blamed, and in revenge the students lure both boys to a beach with fake emails. There Thea publicly breaks up with Kaspar; when he knocks Anders down, a knife is drawn, and the two are forced into a sexual act that the class photographs.

Seeking revenge, Joosep takes his father's pistols, a sawed-off rifle and ammunition, and Kaspar apologizes to his grandmother before the two walk into school armed. Joosep tells a teacher to call the police, and the boys begin shooting their tormentors: Tiit, Olav and Thea's friend Riina die, Kaspar accidentally hits a younger girl, Paul is shot after he and Anders grab Joosep's rifle, and Joosep kills Anders. Kaspar stops him from shooting Thea. Facing each other, the boys agree to kill themselves on a count of three; Joosep fires, while Kaspar is left holding the gun to his head.

The film won awards at the Karlovy Vary and Warsaw film festivals in 2007 and was Estonia's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

title: Case 39
tagline: Some cases should  never be opened.
overview: In her many years as a social worker, Emily Jenkins believes she has seen it all, until she meets 10-year-old Lilith and the girl's cruel parents. Emily's worst fears are confirmed when the parents try to harm the child, and so Emily assumes custody of Lilith while she looks for a foster family. However, Emily soon finds that dark forces surround the seemingly innocent girl, and the more she tries to protect Lilith, the more horrors she encounters.
plot:
Case 39 is a 2009 supernatural horror film directed by Christian Alvart and written by Ray Wright. Renée Zellweger stars as a social worker who tries to rescue a young girl from her abusive parents, with Jodelle Ferland, Bradley Cooper and Ian McShane in supporting roles. Shot in Vancouver in late 2006, the film was released in several territories in 2009 but did not reach US theaters until October 1, 2010, when Paramount Pictures distributed it.

Emily Jenkins, an overworked child services caseworker, is assigned to investigate the family of ten-year-old Lillith Sullivan, whose grades have declined and who appears estranged from her strange, withdrawn parents. Emily suspects abuse and pushes for Lillith's removal, and her fears seem confirmed when the parents are caught trying to kill the girl by shutting her inside the oven. With the help of police detective Mike Barron, Emily rescues her. The parents are committed to a psychiatric institution, and at Lillith's pleading Emily agrees to look after her until a foster family can be found.

Soon after Lillith moves in, disturbing events begin to occur. Another of Emily's young clients murders his parents after receiving a phone call from her house. Her friend, the psychologist Dr. Douglas Ames, evaluates Lillith and finds himself subtly threatened by her; that night he hallucinates hornets bursting from his body and dies in a fall. Visiting Lillith's parents, Emily learns that they believe the girl is a demon that feeds on emotions and can only be stopped while she sleeps. The parents die violently soon afterward, and Barron, after receiving one of Lillith's calls, is driven by terrifying visions to shoot himself.

With her closest allies gone and her other cases in danger, Emily drugs Lillith and sets fire to her own house, but the girl survives unharmed. While being escorted to temporary accommodation, Emily drives off a pier with Lillith in the car. Underwater, Lillith appears in her true monstrous form and tries to drag Emily down, but by overcoming her fear Emily breaks free and swims to shore as the creature sinks.

A fire destroyed the set and studio during production in October 2006, though no one was seriously injured. After lengthy delays, the film was panned by critics and grossed about $28 million worldwide against a $26 million budget.

title: Universal Soldier: Regeneration
tagline: Reanimated. Rearmed. The ultimate rematch
overview: When terrorists threaten nuclear catastrophe at Chernobyl, the world's only hope is to reactivate decommissioned Universal Soldier Luc Deveraux. Rearmed and reprogrammed, Deveraux must take on his nemesis from the original Universal Soldier and a next-generation "UniSol" that seems almost unstoppable.
plot:
Universal Soldier: Regeneration is a 2009 American science fiction action film directed and co-edited by John Hyams and written by Victor Ostrovsky. The fifth installment in the Universal Soldier franchise, it serves as an alternative sequel to the original 1992 film, ignoring the events of Universal Soldier: The Return and the made-for-television sequels. Jean-Claude Van Damme and Dolph Lundgren star, with mixed martial artist Andrei Arlovski as NGU, a Next-Generation Universal Soldier, and fellow fighter Mike Pyle as Captain Kevin Burke. Corey Johnson also appears.

Terrorists of the Pasalan Liberation Front, led by Commander Topov, kidnap the two children of the Ukrainian Prime Minister, seize the crippled Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant and threaten to blow it up unless their imprisoned comrades are freed within 72 hours. Among them is the NGU, smuggled in by the rogue scientist Dr. Robert Colin. The NGU massacres the American and Ukrainian troops sent to the plant, and four revived UniSols deployed by Colin's former colleague Dr. Richard Porter are wiped out in turn. The military then retrieves former UniSol Luc Deveraux from therapy in Switzerland. When the prisoners are released and the terrorists shut down the bomb, Colin, unsatisfied, unleashes a cloned and upgraded Andrew Scott, Deveraux's old nemesis, who kills Topov and then Colin himself before restarting the bomb and hunting the children. Captain Burke reaches the hostages and leads them out, but the NGU kills him after a brutal fight. With thirty minutes left on the timer, the reconditioned Luc storms the plant and finds Scott cornering the children; after a punishing fight he kills Scott. The NGU then attacks, and with under two minutes remaining Luc jams the detonator into the back of the NGU's uniform as both leap from the reactor chamber, and the NGU is destroyed in the blast. American soldiers take charge of the children as Luc leaves, while Burke's body and the NGU's remains are taken away; in Langley, Virginia, Burke is shown stored in a cryogenic chamber as a new UniSol, alongside multiple clones of him.

Shot mostly in Bulgaria, with a former steel factory standing in for Chernobyl, the film premiered at Fantastic Fest in Austin on October 1, 2009. It was released directly on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States in February 2010 and theatrically in parts of the Middle East and Asia, grossing about $844,000 against a $9 million budget. Reviews were mixed; a sequel came in 2012.

title: The Poseidon Adventure
overview: A cruise ship succumbs to a terrorist act and capsizes on New Year's eve. A rag-tag group of survivors, spearheaded by a priest and a homeland security agent, must journey through the upside down vessel and attempt an escape.
plot:
The Poseidon Adventure is a 2005 American made-for-television disaster film based on Paul Gallico's 1969 novel and a remake of the 1972 film of the same name. Developed as a miniseries by Larry Levenson Productions, it was directed by John Putch and written by Bryce Zabel, with Adam Baldwin, Rutger Hauer and Steve Guttenberg in the leading roles. Filmed in late 2004, it was originally intended for the Hallmark Channel before NBC picked it up, and it was produced shortly before Warner Bros. made its own theatrical adaptation, Poseidon, released in 2006.

This version updates the story to the age of terrorism. The SS Poseidon is a vast luxury cruise liner sailing from Cape Town to Sydney with 3,700 passengers and crew aboard. Four terrorists smuggle two bombs onto the ship, and Mike Rogo, a sea marshal played by Baldwin, has been assigned to watch for suspicious activity. Among the passengers is Richard Clarke, played by Guttenberg, whose marriage is collapsing because of his affair with a crew member, to the distress of his young son Dylan and his daughter Shelby, a nursing student who falls for the ship's doctor.

On New Year's Eve, one of the bombs explodes and tears a hole in the hull, while the officers on the bridge are shot by terrorists disguised as waiters. Rogo defuses the second bomb, but water pours in on one side and the ship rolls over and capsizes, killing many of those aboard. In the overturned ballroom, the hotel manager urges survivors to stay put and wait for rescue, but a small group, guided by Rogo, decides to climb upward through the inverted ship toward the hull. Shelby remains behind to care for the wounded, while her mother and brother join the escape. As the survivors struggle through flooded corridors, fires and collapsing decks, family tensions, sacrifices and the hunt for the remaining terrorists shape their attempt to survive until a naval rescue team arrives.

The remake keeps the central premise of the original, with survivors moving through a world turned upside down, but adds terrorism and a broader cast of characters.

Reviews were mixed. Alessandra Stanley of The New York Times wrote that it avoided the weariness of many remakes and came close to the delicious awfulness of the 1972 film, while Tom Shales of The Washington Post found its characters flabby and weightless.

title: Fame
overview: An updated version of the 1980 musical, which centered on the students of the New York Academy of Performing Arts.
plot:
Fame is a 2009 American teen musical drama directed by Kevin Tancharoen from a screenplay by Allison Burnett, a remake of Alan Parker's 1980 film of the same name. It follows a group of gifted students through four years at New York City's High School of Performing Arts. The young cast includes Naturi Naughton, Collins Pennie, Kay Panabaker, Asher Book, Paul Iacono, Anna Maria Perez de Tagle, Paul McGill, Kherington Payne and Walter Perez, while the faculty are played by Debbie Allen, Charles S. Dutton, Bebe Neuwirth, Megan Mullally and Kelsey Grammer.

Denise Dupree (Naughton), a classically trained pianist with strict parents, secretly longs to sing, and Malik Washburn (Pennie), an aspiring actor and rapper, hides his enrollment from his overworked mother and refuses to talk in drama class about the death of his sister. When Malik overhears Denise singing, he and the musician Victor Tavares (Perez) persuade her to record with them, and a record executive later tells them that her voice is what interests him. The shy actress Jenny Garrison (Panabaker) begins a romance with the singer Marco Ramonte (Book), which is shaken when she meets a former student who promises to introduce her to his agent.

Other students face harder lessons. Joy Moy (Perez de Tagle) lands a role on Sesame Street but eventually drops out as her grades suffer, while the aspiring filmmaker Neil Baczynsky (Iacono) is swindled out of five thousand dollars by a supposed producer. In senior year the dancer Kevin Barrett (McGill) is told by Ms. Kraft (Neuwirth) that he lacks the talent to dance professionally and, devastated, tries to throw himself in front of a subway train before his friends stop him; he later resolves to go home and become a dance teacher. Denise defies her father by performing at a club concert, winning over her mother, and Jenny and Marco reconcile before the class comes together for the graduation performance of "Hold Your Dream".

Fame premiered in Los Angeles on September 23, 2009, and MGM released it in the United States two days later. Critics were largely negative, with only 23 percent of reviews on Rotten Tomatoes positive and a Metacritic score of 39, and the consensus faulted its choppy editing and incomplete characters; Parker himself called the remake awful. It was nevertheless a moderate commercial success, grossing about 77 million dollars worldwide on an 18 million dollar budget.

title: Cabin Fever 2: Spring Fever
tagline: This time it's spreading.
overview: A high school prom faces a deadly threat: a flesh-eating virus that spreads via a popular brand of bottled water.
plot:
Cabin Fever 2: Spring Fever is a horror-comedy film that explores several themes, primarily revolving around the consequences of playing with nature and the dangers of underestimating the power of the natural world. The movie delves into the idea of a group of friends who, while initially excited to spend their spring break together, soon find themselves facing a deadly outbreak of a mysterious illness that threatens to destroy them.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the characters' actions have unintended and devastating consequences, highlighting the importance of respecting the environment and the potential risks associated with tampering with nature. The film also touches on themes of friendship, loyalty, and the bonds that hold people together in times of crisis.

Furthermore, Cabin Fever 2: Spring Fever critiques the notion of "playing hooky" or taking time off from responsibilities to indulge in leisure activities. The characters' decision to abandon their studies and responsibilities for a carefree spring break ultimately leads to chaos and destruction, serving as a cautionary tale about the importance of staying grounded and responsible.

Overall, Cabin Fever 2: Spring Fever is a lighthearted yet entertaining horror-comedy that uses its premise to explore themes of environmental responsibility, friendship, and the consequences of one's actions.

title: Detective Conan: The Raven Chaser

overview: A new member from the Black Organization that shrunk Shinichi's body manages to find out about Shinichi's transformation into Conan. This discovery starts to put those around him in danger as Gin and the other Black Organization members start to take action.
plot:
A man driving down a hillside road suddenly realizes that his car Alfa Romeo Brera's brakes don't work. Traveling at a high speed, his car crashes into a toll station. As a man succumbs to his injuries, he leaves a mysterious dying message: "Tanabata kyo" with a mysterious Mahjong tile next to him, linking this case to six other homicide cases in Tokyo, Kanagawa, Shizuoka, Nagano, and other places in Japan. Because of the Mahjong tiles left beside each victim, the police conclude that the same person or organization committed these large-scale murders. The police of prefectures across Japan unite to find the murderer.

He and Heiji find out that two years ago, there was a fire accident in a hotel in Kyoto, and a young woman named Nanako Honjou died. The elevator could only hold seven, but eight people needed to escape. Nanako wasn't on the last elevator and couldn't escape. Conan tracks down her neighbor, Shun Sawamura, and asks him some questions. Conan finds out that Nanako and her boyfriend, Kosuke Mizutani, often went star gazing together. Conan realizes that the crime scenes form the Big Dipper constellation along with the North Star Polaris.
When the polices arrive at a deserted Tokyo Tower, Conan sneaks past them and confronts Mizutani, who confesses to the crimes and intends to commit suicide by poison. Mizutani thought one of the seven must have pushed Nanako out of the elevator during the hotel fire, but Nanako's brother, Kazuki, who was one of the seven in the elevator, shows up and testifies that she voluntarily stepped out. Conan reveals that the real murderer is Kazuki and not Mizutani because Mizutani would never commit murder to stain the memory of Nanako and his precious stars. However, Kazuki, obsessively fond of his younger sister, decided after her death to take revenge on all those who "took her away from him", including Mizutani. Meanwhile, Irish knocks the polices unconscious.
To this purpose, Kazuki tricked Mizutani to become a scapegoat by persuading him to take the blame for the revenge murders. The Mahjong tiles left at the murder scenes were deliberate clues to point the police investigation into Mizutani's direction, with the final stone pinpointing the location of Tokyo Tower - a fact which both Conan and Kogoro Mouri have managed to deduce.

He eventually rebels and escapes, taking with him the crippled young servant boy Smike. As they journey to London, they stumble upon a theatrical troupe owned and operated by Mr and Mrs Crummles. They cast them in a production of Romeo and Juliet, but despite a successful first night and the couple's invitation to stay, Nicholas is determined to continue their journey to London after hearing that Kate is in trouble.
Nicholas discovers his sister has been subjected to humiliating sexual harassment from the lecherous Sir Mulberry Hawk, a client of their uncle, who has encouraged the man to seduce his niece in the hope that she will succumb and thus cement Hawk's business relationship with him. Nicholas confronts Sir Mulberry and his uncle, renouncing the latter.
Nicholas is reunited with his family, who welcome Smike as one of their own, and finds clerical employment with the kindly Cheeryble brothers, who offer him more than double his previous salary. While thus employed, Nicholas makes the acquaintance of Madeline Bray, an artist who financially supports both herself and her tyrannical father, as her father gambled away his fortune and that of his late wife.
Nicholas' determination to defend his sister's honour leads his uncle to vow he will destroy the young man. What ensues is a series of adventures in which the upstanding Nicholas manages to survive the schemes of his evil uncle, which includes an attempt by him to return Smike to Squeers by kidnapping him and an effort to abort Nicholas' growing relationship with Madeline by promising her father he will excuse his debts if the girl weds Hawk. Ralph's designs on Madeline are thwarted when her father dies unexpectedly. Unfortunately, Smike falls ill and then dies. Soon after, a sinister secret Ralph has harbored for years surfaces, and it is revealed that Smike was Ralph's son, whom he had thought dead. Realizing that his son had died whilst being the best friend of his most hated enemy, Ralph hangs himself. Kate marries the Cheeryble brothers' nephew Frank, while Nicholas marries Madeline and settles with her in Devon at his father's house and estate where Smike is also buried.

title: The Crazies
tagline: Fear Thy Neighbor
overview: Four friends find themselves trapped in their small hometown after they discover their friends and neighbors going quickly and horrifically insane.
plot:
The Crazies is a 2010 American horror-thriller film directed by Breck Eisner and starring Timothy Olyphant, Radha Mitchell, and Joe Manganiello. The movie is a remake of the 1973 film of the same name.

The story begins in the small town of Ogden, Maine, where a mysterious outbreak occurs, causing residents to become violent and erratic. The main character, David Dutton (Timothy Olyphant), returns to his hometown after being away for several years. He reunites with his high school sweetheart, Judy (Radha Mitchell), who is now working as a nurse at the local hospital.

As the outbreak worsens, David and Judy team up with their friends, including Wyatt (Joe Manganiello) and Dr. Gibbs (Jill Hennessy), to uncover the source of the strange occurrences. They soon discover that the town's water supply has been contaminated with a mysterious chemical, which is causing the residents to become violent and paranoid.

As the situation spirals out of control, David and Judy find themselves at the center of the chaos. They must navigate through the increasingly hostile environment, trying to stay one step ahead of the infected townsfolk. Along the way, they uncover clues that suggest the contamination was not an accident, but rather a deliberate act of sabotage.

As the body count rises, David and Judy's relationship is put to the test. They must confront their own demons and work together to survive the outbreak. The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as David and Judy face off against the mastermind behind the contamination.

Throughout the film, Breck Eisner uses the small-town setting to create a sense of claustrophobia and isolation. The camera work is often handheld and frenetic, capturing the chaos and panic that grips the town. The special effects are also noteworthy, creating convincing and terrifying depictions of the infected townsfolk.

One of the standout aspects of the film is its commentary on the dangers of unchecked corporate power. The movie suggests that the contamination was orchestrated by a large corporation seeking to exploit the town's resources for their own gain. This theme adds an extra layer of tension to the story, making it more than just a simple horror film.

Overall, The Crazies is a tense and suspenseful thriller that effectively builds up to its thrilling climax. While it may not be as original or groundbreaking as some other horror films, it delivers on its promise of intense action and terror.

title: The Man Who Cried
overview: A young refugee travels from Russia to America in search of her lost father and falls in love with a gypsy horseman.
plot:
The Man Who Cried is a 2000 historical musical drama written and directed by Sally Potter. Christina Ricci stars as Suzie, with Cate Blanchett as her friend Lola, Johnny Depp as the Romani horseman Cesar, John Turturro as the Italian opera singer Dante Dominio, Harry Dean Stanton as the theatre director Felix Perlman, and Oleg Yankovsky as Suzie's father. It was the last film photographed by the French cinematographer Sacha Vierny. The film premiered at the Venice Film Festival in September 2000.

In 1927, Fegele Abramovich, a young Jewish girl in a Russian village, is separated from her father when he leaves for America, promising to send for her and her grandmother. Before he departs, he sings to her the aria "Je crois entendre encore" from Bizet's opera The Pearl Fishers. Soon afterwards, the village is destroyed in a pogrom. Fegele escapes with the help of neighbours and eventually ends up on a boat to Britain, carrying only a photograph of her father and a coin from her grandmother. An official renames her Susan, and she is placed with foster parents, where she is mocked by schoolmates until a teacher hears her singing and helps her learn English.

As a young woman, Suzie joins a dance troupe and moves to Paris shortly before the Second World War, sharing an apartment with Lola, an ambitious Russian dancer. At a society party they meet Cesar, a silent and brooding Romani performer with horses, to whom Suzie is drawn, and Dante, a vain opera tenor whose wealth attracts Lola. Both women are hired for an opera company, and Suzie begins a passionate romance with Cesar. As the Nazis advance toward Paris, the city's Jews and Romani face growing danger, and Dante reveals his fascist sympathies. Suzie must decide whether to remain with Cesar or flee, and she eventually travels to America in search of the father she has not seen since childhood.

The film is notable for its emphasis on music and for its sparse dialogue, with opera and Romani music carrying much of the emotional weight. It explores displacement, identity and the persecution of minorities during the war.

Critical reception was mixed to negative. On Rotten Tomatoes the film holds an approval rating of about 35 percent; the consensus describes the storyline as overwrought and awkward and the characters as flatly drawn, keeping the audience at a distance, although its cinematography and music were praised.

title: Batman Unmasked: The Psychology of the Dark Knight
original_title: Batman Unmasked: The Psychology of the Dark Knight
overview: Delve into the world of Batman and the vigilante justice that he brought to the city of Gotham. Batman is a man who, after experiencing great tragedy, devotes his life to an ideal--but what happens when one man takes on the evil underworld alone? Examine why Batman is who he is--and explore how a boy scarred by tragedy becomes a symbol of hope to everyone else.
plot:
Batman Unmasked: The Psychology of the Dark Knight is a 2008 American television documentary written and directed by Steven C. Smith and produced by Prometheus Entertainment for the History channel, with narration by Robert Clotworthy. Running about 45 minutes, it was first broadcast on 16 July 2008, the same month Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight reached cinemas, and it approaches the comic book hero not as a piece of pop entertainment but as a subject for psychological analysis.

The programme asks what drives a man who, after suffering a devastating tragedy, devotes his whole life to a single ideal, and what happens when one person takes it upon himself to fight a city's criminal underworld alone. It traces Bruce Wayne back to the formative trauma of witnessing his parents' murder as a child and examines how that loss shaped him, how he channels fear and grief into a disciplined double life, and how a boy scarred by violence turns himself into a symbol of hope for Gotham City. Along the way it weighs the appeal and the dangers of vigilante justice, and looks at the costumed villains of Batman's rogues' gallery as reflections of the hero's own psyche, including foes who had not appeared in the Nolan films.

The film is built mainly around interviews, illustrated with dynamic treatments of comic book panels and covers and with clips from Batman Begins and The Dark Knight. Contributors include the clinical psychologist Robin S. Rosenberg, who discusses the effect of the Waynes' murder on their son, alongside DC Comics figures Paul Levitz and Dan DiDio and the veteran Batman writers and editors Denny O'Neil and Len Wein. Christopher Nolan and Christian Bale also appear, speaking about their interpretation of the character.

The documentary was later included as a high-definition special feature on the second disc of Warner Home Video's Blu-ray release of The Dark Knight in December 2008, where it was described as a look into the psyche of Bruce Wayne through real-world psychotherapy, and it reappeared in later Dark Knight Trilogy box sets. It holds a favourable user rating on IMDb, where one reviewer called it a thorough, credible and engaging examination of the character.

title: Exam
tagline: How far would you go to win the ultimate job?
overview: The final candidates for a highly desirable corporate job are locked together in an exam room and given a test so simple and confusing that tension begins to unravel.
plot:
Eight candidates dress for an employment assessment exam at the company Biorg. The group enters a room and sits at individual desks. Each desk has a paper printed with the word "candidate" and a number from one to eight. The Invigilator explains that they have 80 minutes to answer one question, but there are three rules: the candidates must not spoil their paper, leave the room, or talk to him or the armed guard at the door. If they do, they will be disqualified. The Invigilator asks them if they have any questions, then leaves.
As the exam starts, it turns out that the papers are otherwise blank. Within minutes, Candidate 2 is disqualified for spoiling her paper by writing on it. The seven remaining candidates realize it is permissible to talk to each other and collaborate. One candidate, "White", assigns nicknames to each candidate based on hair color and skin color: Black, Blonde, Brown, Brunette, Dark, and Deaf (for one candidate who does not speak or respond to the group).
In the hour that follows, the candidates use lights, bodily fluids, and fire sprinklers in attempts to reveal hidden text on their papers, to no avail. They speculate on the exam's purpose and the nature of the company. Dark claims that the CEO is highly secretive and has not been seen since the initial public offering. It is gradually revealed that the company is responsible for a miracle drug designed to treat a condition afflicting a large part of the population due to a viral pandemic. In the chaos, White takes control of the group and engineers the disqualifications of Brunette and Deaf for spoiled papers.
White also begins taunting the others, saying he has figured out the question but will not tell them. In response, Black knocks White unconscious and ties him to a chair. As White passes out, he pleads for his medication, implying he has the virus. Brown turns his attention to Dark, who demonstrates knowledge of the company's internal workings, and tortures her into revealing that she works for the company. It is revealed that Black is a carrier of the disease. White goes into convulsions; Dark pleads to the Invigilator for help and is disqualified.
Blonde retrieves White's medication, which was stolen from him earlier by Brown, and uses it to revive him. The others release White and demand to know the question. White suggests that there is no question and the company will simply hire the last remaining candidate. Black steals the guard's gun, but it requires the guard's fingerprint to fire, giving White time to retrieve it. By forcing the guard's hand into the trigger, White coerces Brown to leave the room, disqualifying him. As Blonde also exits, she turns off the voice-activated lights, allowing Black to attack White.
The lights come back on after Black is hit by a gunshot. Blonde hides in the hallway, still holding one foot inside the room. Before White can kill her, the exam timer runs to zero.

overview: A middle-aged Tehranian man, Mr. Badii is intent on killing himself and seeks someone to bury him after his demise. plot:
Badii, a middle-aged man, drives through Tehran looking for someone to do a job for him, for which he offers a large sum of money. During his drives with prospective candidates, Badii reveals that he plans to kill himself and has already dug the grave. He tells the people he is soliciting to go to the spot he has chosen the next morning, and either help him up if he has chosen to live or bury him if he has chosen to die. He does not discuss why he wants to commit suicide.
His first recruit is a young, shy Kurdish soldier who refuses to do the job and flees from Badii's car. His second recruit is an Afghan seminarist who also declines because he has religious objections to suicide. The third is Bagheri, an Azeri taxidermist. He is willing to help Badii because he needs the money for his sick child. He tries to convince Badii not to commit suicide and reveals that he too wanted to commit suicide in 1960 but chose to live when, after failing in his attempt, he tasted mulberries which dropped from a tree. Bagheri reveals that he then went home with the mulberries and gave them to his wife, who enjoyed them. He continues to discuss what he perceives to be the beauty of life, including sunrises, the moon, and stars. Bagheri promises to throw dirt on Badii if he finds him dead in the morning. Badii drops him back at his workplace but suddenly runs back to meet him, requesting that in the morning Bagheri should confirm if he is actually dead by throwing some stones at him and jolting him awake in case he is asleep.
That night, Badii lies in his grave while a thunderstorm begins. After a long blackout, the film ends by breaking the fourth wall with camcorder footage of Kiarostami and the film crew filming Taste of Cherry, leaving Badii's choice unknown.

overview: A heroic version of Lex Luthor from an alternate universe appears to recruit the Justice League to help save his Earth from the Crime Syndicate, an evil version of the League. plot:
Justice League: Crisis on Two Earths is a 2010 American animated superhero film directed by Lauren Montgomery and Sam Liu and written by Dwayne McDuffie, the seventh entry in the DC Universe Animated Original Movies line. It reworks an abandoned project meant to bridge the series Justice League and Justice League Unlimited, and borrows its premise from the 1964 comic "Crisis on Earth-Three!" and Grant Morrison's JLA: Earth 2. Mark Harmon voices Superman and William Baldwin Batman, with Chris Noth as Lex Luthor, James Woods as Owlman and Gina Torres as Superwoman.

In a parallel universe where heroes and villains are reversed, a heroic Lex Luthor and his ally the Jester steal a device called the Quantum Trigger from the Crime Syndicate, the world's ruling villains. The Jester sacrifices himself so that Luthor can escape to the Justice League's Earth. Superman's X-ray vision reveals that Luthor's organs are reversed, proving his story, and on the Watchtower he explains the Syndicate's threat, secretly hiding the Trigger aboard the satellite.

All the League except Batman travel to Luthor's world and begin striking at Syndicate targets, even capturing Ultraman. But the President of that Earth, Slade Wilson, releases him, explaining that cooperation with the Syndicate saves millions of lives. Martian Manhunter falls for the President's daughter, Rose. Meanwhile, Superwoman and her lieutenants raid the Watchtower and retrieve the Trigger, but Batman pursues them back across dimensions and captures Superwoman.

The Syndicate's true aim is nuclear blackmail, but Owlman has a more nihilistic plan. Convinced that in a multiverse no choice has any meaning, he has built the Quantum Eigenstate Device, a bomb with which he intends to destroy Earth Prime, the original world from which all realities spring, and thus erase existence itself. The League storms the Syndicate's lunar base, and Luthor reasons that a speedster could vibrate to open a portal to Owlman's destination. Batman forbids the Flash from risking it, so the Syndicate's Johnny Quick volunteers.

Batman fights Owlman on Earth Prime and transports him and the bomb to a lifeless, frozen world. Realising that another version of himself would choose to survive, Owlman lets the bomb explode and dies. Johnny Quick dies from the strain, President Wilson arrests the Syndicate, and Martian Manhunter bids Rose farewell. The film was well received, critics praising McDuffie's script and the voice cast.

title: Bunraku
tagline: A civilized weapon for uncivilized times
overview: In a world with no guns, a mysterious drifter, a bartender and a young samurai plot revenge against a ruthless leader and his army of thugs, headed by nine diverse and deadly assassins.
plot:
Bunraku is a 2010 martial arts action film written and directed by Guy Moshe from a story by Boaz Davidson. It stars Josh Hartnett, Demi Moore, Woody Harrelson, Ron Perlman, Kevin McKidd and Gackt, and follows a young drifter on a quest for revenge. Named after the 400-year-old form of Japanese puppet theatre, it reimagines a classic tale in a world mixing skewed reality with shadow-play fantasy, drawing on samurai films and Westerns.

In the aftermath of a devastating global war, guns have been outlawed, yet people continue to fight and kill with blades and bare fists. The most powerful man east of the Atlantic is Nicola the Woodcutter, a shadowy crime boss who rules his territory through nine elite assassins known as the Killers. His right-hand man is Killer No. 2, a smooth-talking murderer in a red hat who carries a cane-sword, and he keeps an unwilling lover, Alexandra, a woman with a secret past. One night a mysterious drifter walks into the Horseless Horseman Saloon and asks the bartender for a shot of whisky and a game of cards, only to learn that the one place offering both, the Russian Roulette, is controlled by Nicola and open only to the rich. Soon after, another stranger arrives: Yoshi, a lone samurai who has travelled far to fulfil his father's dying wish by recovering a medallion stolen from his village. Guided by the bartender, the two men join forces against Nicola. After a series of clashes in which they injure police officers and many of Nicola's thugs, Killer No. 2 murders Yoshi's uncle and abducts his cousin Momoko to work in Nicola's brothel. With the bartender and an army of freedom fighters, the pair storm Nicola's palace. The bartender rescues Momoko and is briefly reunited with Alexandra, his long-lost love, before she is lost in the burning brothel. Yoshi kills Killer No. 2, while the drifter, wounded by an axe thrown by Nicola, slashes the crime boss's throat with an arrowhead taken from Yoshi and reveals that he came to avenge his father, whom Nicola killed. With the Woodcutter's reign ended and the medallion recovered, the heroes part ways hoping to meet again.

Bunraku premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the 2010 Toronto International Film Festival, with a limited theatrical release in 2011. Critics praised its visual style and ideas but faulted the screenplay and characters, and it holds an 18% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

title: The Miracle Maker
tagline: A visually stunning animation of the greatest story ever told.
overview: A mother and father in search of help for their sick daughter cross paths with an extraordinary carpenter named Jesus, who has devoted his life to spreading God's word. An amazing miracle brings to light the true meaning of Christ, and the sacrifices he endured for the deliverance of mankind. A compelling story of faith, trust, and devotion.
plot:
The Miracle Maker, sometimes subtitled The Story of Jesus, is a 1999 animated biblical drama directed by Derek W. Hayes and Stanislav Sokolov from a screenplay by Murray Watts. It was a co-production between companies in Wales and Russia and was made in separate English and Welsh versions. Ralph Fiennes voices Jesus in English and Ioan Gruffudd in Welsh, and the English cast also includes Julie Christie, Richard E. Grant, Ian Holm, Emily Mortimer and Alfred Molina. Most of the film uses stop-motion puppets, while hand-drawn animation marks flashbacks, parables, visions and spiritual encounters.

The life of Jesus is told largely through the eyes of people around him, especially Tamar, the sick daughter of the synagogue leader Jairus. In Sepphoris, where a doctor declares her illness incurable, Tamar sees a carpenter named Jesus defend the tormented Mary Magdalene. After his baptism by John and his temptation in the wilderness, Jesus begins preaching in Capernaum. He calls the fishermen Simon, James and John after a miraculous catch, and he draws Judas Iscariot away from Barabbas's band of zealots. As his following grows, he drives the demons out of Mary Magdalene and forgives her sins. This alarms the Temple priests, above all Ben Azra, who fears a revolt. When Tamar dies, Jesus urges her parents to keep faith and raises her to life, healed. After Herod executes John the Baptist, Herod and the priests agree that Jesus must be stopped before Pontius Pilate reports an uprising.

Tamar's family follows Jesus to Jerusalem for Passover. There he drives the merchants out of the Temple and foretells his death. Fearing Jesus will bring Roman reprisals rather than liberation, Judas helps the priests arrest him after the Last Supper and the prayer in Gethsemane. Pilate finds no fault in him, but Caiaphas pressures him into ordering the crucifixion. After the sabbath, the tomb is found empty. The risen Jesus appears to his followers, convinces the doubting Thomas and sends them out to spread his teachings.

Welsh broadcaster S4C began production in 1996, using six sets at once for over a year. The Welsh version premiered on S4C in November 1999. The English version opened in UK cinemas on March 31, 2000, and aired on ABC in the US that April. Reviews were mostly positive. The Independent called it powerfully engaging, and the National Catholic Register praised its grounding in the realities of first-century Judea, while The Guardian found it plodding.

title: Ticker
tagline: When the countdown hits zero, you're dead
overview: Ray Nettles, a detective of San Francisco, and his partner Fuzzy must take up to one of the most dangerous terrorist gangs of the city. When one of the terrorists, the beautiful scientist Claire Manning is arrested, Swan, the leader of the terrorists, claims he will detonate bombs throughout the city if she is not released. Because of the possible bloodshed, Nettles calls for the help of explosive expert Frank Glass...
plot:
Ticker is a 2001 American action film directed by Albert Pyun and starring Tom Sizemore, Steven Seagal, Dennis Hopper and Jaime Pressly, with Ice-T, Kevin Gage, Romany Malco and Nas in supporting roles. Made with Nu Image, with backing from Emmett/Furla's Family Room Entertainment and domestic distribution through Artisan Entertainment, it was released straight to video in the United States on November 13, 2001.

The film opens with a hostage standoff at the home of a United States senator. While a SWAT team battles the hostage takers, bomb squad chief Frank Glass, played by Seagal, disarms a device in the basement, only to realize that it was too easy and intended as a decoy; the real bomb explodes, killing everyone inside. A year later in San Francisco, narcotics detective Ray Nettles, played by Sizemore, is still unable to grieve for his wife and son, who were killed in a car bombing. When Ray and his partner Art "Fuzzy" Rice investigate suspicious activity at a warehouse, Fuzzy is shot by the leader of a gang of bombers, an Irish terrorist named Alex Swan, played by Hopper. Ray arrests a member of the group, Claire Manning, who wears a bracelet that turns out to contain Semtex and detonation cord. Swan demands Claire's release within an hour and, when the deadline passes, blows up a bar. Ray teams up with Glass to track down the remaining bombers, and Claire, claiming she will be killed for having been caught, begins to cooperate, revealing the names of Swan and his associate Vershbow. Swan, however, keeps escalating his campaign, detonating bombs across the city and preparing a massive attack with a crew led by Vincent Cruichshank, played by Ice-T. Hoping to prevent further bloodshed, the police release Claire with a tracking device, but her true loyalties prove more complicated than they seem, and Ray and Glass are forced into a race against time to find and defuse Swan's ultimate "masterpiece".

During post-production, Nu Image imposed many changes that Pyun denounced as horrible, in particular the removal of character-building scenes for Seagal, because the company, according to Pyun, simply wanted him fighting. Pyun later posted an "Anti-Studio Director's Cut" of the film online.

title: Moonlight Mile
tagline: In life and love, expect the unexpected.
overview: As he copes with the death of his fiancee along with her parents, a young man must figure out what he wants out of life.
plot:
Following the murder of Diana Floss in a restaurant in Cape Ann, Massachusetts, in 1972, her fiancé, Joe Nast, elects to stay with her parents. Her father, Ben, is a realtor whose business partner has recently left. Ben and Joe go into business as Floss & Son, as this was their plan before Diana's death. Joe goes to the post office to retrieve all the invitations that had been sent out for his and Diana's wedding, and, with the help of Bertie Knox, he retrieves seventy-four of seventy-five. She finds the last invitation and takes it to his house later that night. He drops her off at a local bar and returns home, despite her inviting him in for a drink. Joe and Ben attend a local property fair, and Ben pitches the idea of redeveloping a block in the town to developer Mike Mulcahey. Mulcahey agrees, but they need to get all the tenants to agree.
Diana's friends come to look through her possessions, much to the consternation of her mother, Jojo. Her friends take out Joe for a drink at the same bar Bertie went to the previous night. Joe puts "Moonlight Mile" on the jukebox, and Bertie emerges from the restroom to dance with him. Joe convinces Ben to let him talk to the bar's owner to convince them to sell. Feeling trapped at the Floss home, he meets Bertie and tells her about Diana. He confesses to her that he had split up with Diana three days before she was killed. Bertie tells Joe about her boyfriend, the owner of the bar, who is lost in Vietnam.
One night, Joe sneaks out the window to see Bertie again. They sleep together, and he leaves the next morning, slipping back into Diana's house through the window. Jojo is sitting in the room, drinking, knowing he was out seeing another woman, and saddened by the idea that she had always known he would have never ended up with her daughter. She does not want Joe to leave, as they have formed a bond.
Joe goes to dinner at the Mulcaheys', where Mike's wife presumes aloud that Joe was not still "tied up" with thoughts of his fiancée's murder. Joe states that this is not the case, upsetting the mood at the dinner table. Mike calls Ben and ends their deal.
Bertie confronts Joe about what happened between them, and they have an argument, during which he tells her that no one believes her boyfriend is coming home, and that she deserved better anyway. She leaves, upset.
The family attends the trial of Diana's murderer. However, the murderer's wife elicits sympathy from the jury, and the prosecutor, Mona Camp, asks Joe to testify to help the jury gain sympathy for Diana. On the witness stand, Joe confesses that he and Diana had broken up prior to her death, and that he had not told her parents. Ben and Jojo are happy with the confession, and gain closure. Joe writes a symbolic 75 letters expressing his newfound clarity about what course his life ought to take, as well as his love for Bertie, and he places them in mailboxes around town, hoping one will get to her.

title: Mr. Nobody
tagline: Nothing is real, everything is possible.
overview: Nemo Nobody leads an ordinary existence with his wife and 3 children; one day, he wakes up as a mortal centenarian in the year 2092.
plot:
In 2092, humanity has conquered mortality. The world watches as 118-year-old Nemo Nobody, the last mortal, approaches death. Psychiatrist Dr. Feldheim uses hypnosis to help Nemo remember his life. A journalist also interviews Nemo, whose recollections are from three points in his life: ages 9, 15, and 34. Nemo makes contradictory statements, describing his past as having unfolded in multiple ways. He says that, before birth, children know everything that will happen in their lives, but at the moment of conception the Angels of Oblivion erase the knowledge. He says the Angels missed him, allowing him to "remember" his different possible futures.
After his parents' divorce, 9-year-old Nemo had to choose whether to live with his mother or his father. He describes what happened in both scenarios.
Life with his mother
Nemo and his mother move to Montreal. When he is a teenager, he is attracted to Anna. At the beach, Anna asks Nemo to swim with her and her friends. He insults her friends, and they hardly see each other again.
In an alternate timeline, Nemo admits to Anna that he cannot swim, and they spend time together. Anna's father Harry marries Nemo's mother, and the step-siblings begin an affair, pledging their lives to one another. Harry and Nemo's mother divorce, and Anna goes to New York with her father. The teenagers lose touch. Years later, Nemo and Anna pass at a train station and immediately recognize each other. After a passionate reunion, Anna says she is not ready for a relationship. She asks Nemo to call her and meet at a lighthouse, but he loses her number. Nemo waits at the lighthouse every day, but Anna does not come.
In another timeline, Anna and Nemo are married with children. He works at a television studio. Driving home, he loses control of his car, plummets into a lake, and drowns.
Life with his father
As a teenager, Nemo lives in England with his disabled father and is writing a science fiction story about a journey to Mars. He falls in love with Elise, whose boyfriend is 22-year-old Stefano. Nemo has a motorcycle accident and is hospitalized in a vegetative state or pseudocoma. He can still perceive the world and detects his parents' reunion at his bedside. He imagines his fingers on his typewriter keyboard and continues working on his story.
In another timeline, Elise says she is in love with Stefano, but he does not love her. Nemo assures her of his feelings until she gives in, and they marry. In one version of this timeline, Elise dies in an explosion on their wedding day, and Nemo takes her ashes to Mars as he had promised when they were teenagers. On the way back to Earth he meets Anna, but the ship is destroyed by asteroids. In another version, one of Nemo's television studio coworkers drowns in the lake. Their widow is Anna, whom Nemo feels he has seen before. Another timeline has Nemo and Elise married with three children.

title: Little Nicholas
overview: Nicolas has a happy existence, parents who love him, a great group of friends with whom he has great fun, and all he wants is that nothing changes. However, one day, he overhears a conversation that leads him to believe that his life might change forever, his mother is pregnant! He panics and envisions the worst.
plot:
Nicholas' class is instructed by their teacher to write about what they want to be when they grow up. Gluttonous best friend Alceste, rich boy Geoffrey, dimwitted Clotaire, quarrelsome Eudes, eccentric Rufus and spoiled top student Agnan already have plans for the future. However, Nicholas is unsure as he enjoys his life and does not want it to change.
One day, the class is interrupted by the arrival of another student, Joachim, who has a new baby brother and is not pleased about it, as no one prioritizes him anymore. Joachim was not aware of the arrival, but did observe his father's uncharacteriscally affectionate behavior towards his mother. The next morning, Nicholas sees that his parents are affectionate to each other too, causing him to suspect that they plan to have a baby. He informs his friends about this; their suspicions are further fueled by Joachim's sudden absence from the school.
Returning home, Nicholas overhears half of a conversation his parents are having about inviting Mr. Moucheboume, Nicholas' father's hard-to-please boss, and his wife over for dinner, mistakenly assuming that it is about the new baby's arrival. When his father suggests a weekend escapade to the woods, Nicholas thinks this is a ploy to abandon him for his baby brother. The next few days, Nicholas becomes determined to please his mother in everything, even attending a tea party with her friends, where he spends time with a girl named Marie-Edwige and her girlfriends. Nonetheless, Nicholas' parents still take him to the woods and he refuses to come out, forcing them to push the car back home when they cannot persuade him otherwise and spend the rest of the day arguing.
Nicholas' friends vow to protect him by forming a secret club to propose ideas on how to make his parents proud of him. They try to clean up the house while his parents are away. However, their attempt results in failure, the house becomes a mess and Nicholas gets grounded for the night. Losing all hope, Nicholas decides to run away from home, but he immediately regrets it and returns. Later on, they decide to hire a gangster who can assist them in kidnapping the child. They learn that Blind Jack is on the loose, but Nicholas instead calls someone working in a garage, who charges 500 francs to strip the "body" down.
They eventually manage to make money out of selling a "formula" with superhuman strength, earning 530 francs in the process. Nicholas once again contacts Blind Jack, who requests a car, forcing him and his friends to steal Geoffrey's father's car by tricking Albert, Geoffrey's butler, into stopping by at an ice cream shop to distract him. Just as they arrive, Nicholas and his friends are surprised to see Joachim, who only got chickenpox, with his little brother. After Joachim expresses how good brotherhood really is, Nicholas has second thoughts and ultimately decides not to go through with the scheme.

title: I Can't Think Straight
tagline: Two cultures. Two women. One love.
overview: I CAN'T THINK STRAIGHT is a 2007 romance movie about a London-based Jordanian of Palestinian descent, Tala, who is preparing for an elaborate wedding. A turn of events causes her to have an affair and subsequently fall in love with another woman, Leyla, a British Indian.
plot:
In the upper echelons of traditional Middle Eastern society, wealthy Christian Palestinians Reema and Omar prepare for the marriage of their visiting daughter Tala to Hani in Jordan. But back at work in London, Tala encounters Leyla, a young British Indian Muslim woman who is dating Tala's best friend Ali. Tala sees something unique in the artless, clumsy, sensitive Leyla who secretly works to become a writer. And Tala's forthright challenges to Leyla's beliefs begins a journey of self-awareness for Leyla. After a weekend getaway into the countryside, Tala and Leyla sleep together and the two women begin to fall in love. However, Tala's own sense of duty and cultural restraint cause her to pull away from Leyla and fly back to Jordan where the preparations for an ostentatious wedding are well under way.
As family members descend and the wedding day approaches, the pressure mounts until Tala finally cracks and extricates herself. Back in London, Leyla is heartbroken but learns to break free of her own self-doubt and her mother's expectations, ditching Ali and being honest with her parents about her sexuality. When Ali and Leyla's feisty sister, Yasmin, help try to get Tala and Leyla together again, Tala finds that her own preconceptions of what love can be is the final hurdle she must jump to win Leyla back.

Overall, Three Fugitives is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of personal growth, redemption, and the importance of human connection.
