title: The Land Before Time XII: The Great Day of the Flyers
original_title: The Land Before Time XII: The Great Day of the Flyers
overview: As the Great Day of the Flyers nears, the Great Valley's flying youngsters are eager to participate in the annual exhibition to show off their skills. Everyone, that is, except free-spirited pterodactyl Petrie, whose individualism causes problems when it comes to staying in formation. Enter his dinosaur pals Littlefoot, Cera, Spike and Ducky, who encourage Petrie to embrace his uniqueness.
plot:
The Land Before Time XII: The Great Day of the Flyers is a 2006 American animated musical film, the twelfth instalment of The Land Before Time series, produced for Universal Studios Home Entertainment. It was first shown on television in December 2006 and released on DVD on February 27, 2007, with sing-along and game extras. Its voice cast includes John Ingle, Nick Price, Frank Welker, Aria Noelle Curzon and Rob Paulsen, and it was the final film role of Kenneth Mars, who retired afterwards.

In the Great Valley, the young flyers are preparing for the Day of the Flyers, a ceremony in which they must perform a precise formation flight to show they are ready to fly with the adults. Petrie, always a nervous and clumsy flier, struggles badly to keep pace with his siblings in the tight group manoeuvres, and fears that he will fail in front of everyone. At the same time a strange newcomer turns up in the valley: Guido, a small, feathered creature who has no idea what kind of dinosaur he is. Littlefoot and his friends set out to help him discover his identity and eventually learn that he is a Microraptor, a gliding dinosaur.

Cera has her own worries. Her gruff father and his new mate, Tria, are expecting a hatchling, and Cera feels uncertain about her place in the family. When the baby, Tricia, arrives, Cera gradually warms to her and begins to grow close to her little sister.

The various storylines collide on the eve of the ceremony. Guido begins to sleepwalk and glide, and Petrie and the others follow him, unwittingly leading the whole group out of the valley into the dangerous Mysterious Beyond. When Guido wakes up, the friends find themselves face to face with a hungry Spinosaurus that chases them. Working together, they trap the predator by wedging it between two rocks and make their way safely home.

On the Day of the Flyers, Petrie takes Guido's advice to be himself and performs his own distinctive style of flying, which inspires the other young flyers to follow his lead. During the festivities, little Tricia tumbles into a river and is carried towards a waterfall. Guido, Petrie and his siblings swoop in to rescue her, and when they lose their grip, Cera catches her sister before she falls back into the water. Tricia then speaks her first word, "Cera", and the family celebrates together while the other dinosaurs look on.

title: Black
tagline: An unending darkness... A world of shadows... A ray of light that found its way... A teacher's dream... A student's miracle... A valiant journey... From ignorance to knowledge... From darkness to light... An extraordinary story of an ordinary life.
overview: Black is an adaptation of Helen Keller's autobiography. Black revolves around a blind and deaf girl, and her relationship with her teacher who himself later develops Alzheimer's disease.
plot:
Black is a 2005 Indian drama co-written, directed and co-produced by Sanjay Leela Bhansali. Rani Mukerji stars as Michelle McNally, a deafblind woman, and Amitabh Bachchan as Debraj Sahai, the eccentric, hard-drinking teacher who transforms her life and who later develops Alzheimer's disease. Ayesha Kapur plays the young Michelle, with Shernaz Patel and Dhritiman Chatterjee as her parents, Catherine and Paul.

In Shimla, the 42-year-old Michelle, her younger sister Sara and their mother find Debraj, Michelle's long-lost teacher, wandering near the fountain outside their home. Doctors at a mental hospital say he has incurable Alzheimer's and can barely remember his past or even speak, but Michelle vows to help him recover, just as he once helped her find her identity. The story then returns to her childhood. An illness at the age of two left Michelle blind, deaf and mute, and by eight she is a furious, uncontrollable child, especially after Sara's birth, leaving her parents desperate.

Debraj, an ageing alcoholic who teaches deaf and blind children in Dehradun and fancies himself a magician, arrives determined to bring her out of the darkness, giving up his salary and his drinking. His tough methods horrify Paul, who orders him to leave, but while Paul is away for twenty days Catherine lets him continue. On the verge of departing, Debraj loses patience, drags Michelle outside and throws her into the fountain, and in that moment she grasps the meaning of the word "water".

Twenty-two years later, Michelle is a confident 30-year-old who can dance and sign fluently, and Debraj secures her admission to a university's arts degree course, the first deafblind student there. She fails year after year, hampered by her dependence on Debraj and by poor typing, but perseveres with help from the principal, who has the course produced in braille. As Debraj's memory starts to fail, Michelle reconciles with Sara, who always resented the attention her sister received, and after Sara's wedding asks Debraj to kiss her; he does so reluctantly and then leaves her. Twelve years after enrolling, Michelle graduates, and she visits Debraj in hospital wearing her gown, where a flicker of recognition returns as they reach together into the rain.

Black was a commercial and critical success. It won 11 Filmfare Awards, including Best Film, Best Director, Best Actor and Best Actress, and three National Film Awards, among them Best Feature Film in Hindi and Best Actor for Bachchan.

title: Case Closed: Countdown to Heaven
original_title: 名探偵コナン 天国へのカウントダウン
tagline: Detective Conan: Count Down to Heaven
overview: As a pair of towers in Tokyo are being prepared for their grand opening, there is a series of murders of people connected to the towers. Conan suspects that the mysterious Syndicate may also be involved.
plot:
Case Closed: Countdown to Heaven, known in Japan as Detective Conan: Countdown to Heaven (名探偵コナン 天国へのカウントダウン), is a 2001 Japanese animated mystery disaster film and the fifth feature based on the Case Closed manga and anime series. It marked the Black Organization's first appearance in the film series. The Japanese voice cast includes Minami Takayama, Wakana Yamazaki, Akira Kamiya, Kappei Yamaguchi and Ikue Otani.

Returning from a camping trip, Conan Edogawa, Vi Graythorn, Dr. Agasa and the Junior Detective League stop at the newly built Twin Towers in West Tama City, the tallest buildings in Japan, dubbed "the closest thing to heaven". Meanwhile the Black Organization agents Gin and Vodka, hunting Vi's former identity Shiho Miyano, learn from messages left for her late sister Akemi that she will attend a private viewing of the towers, and plan to kill her there. Also present are Richard and Rachel Moore, Serena Sebastian, Richard's old college friend Madison Monroe and her secretary, the artist Kisaragi Hosui, the executive Zachary Hara, the councilman Augustine Odell and the architect Theodore Radcliff. That night Odell is murdered in his suite, leaving a broken sake cup and a missing painting; Hara is then found shot with a silver knife in his hand beside another broken cup, and police suspect a serial killer. Refusing to postpone the grand opening, Madison is found hanged on stage before Kisaragi's painting with an unbroken cup beneath her. As Conan solves the case, the Black Organization's bombs set the building ablaze. In a glass elevator, Conan saves Serena, whose new perm makes her resemble Shiho from behind, from Gin's bullet, and Rachel leaps to safety with him using a fire hose. Conan returns for the trapped children and confronts Kisaragi, who hid Madison's real pearl necklace in his cane and left the cups as symbols of Mount Fuji, his view of which the towers had blocked. Conan stops his suicide attempt and reveals that Hara was killed by Gin, the knife pointing to his name, as "gin" means silver in Japanese. As the floors burn, Conan propels a convertible into the pool with the children, Kisaragi is arrested and Gin and Vodka, convinced Shiho was absent, abandon the hunt.

The film earned 2.9 billion yen. Funimation released an English dub on DVD in 2010, and Anime News Network gave it a mixed review, faulting its tonal shifts but praising Gin and Vodka's role and its action-packed finale in the skyscrapers.

title: Blade: House of Chthon
tagline: Blade sets up shop in yet another abandoned warehouse in Detroit to take on the House of Chthon.
overview: The brutal hunt for the pure bloods continues as the ultimate vampire hunter, Blade, battles to defeat the House of Chthon, an ancient evil sect of vampires that is growing stronger everyday. Led by the vampire overlord Marcus, their objective is to create a vaccine that will give rise to a new breed of super vampires, immune to vampire weaknesses.
plot:
Blade: House of Chthon is the two-hour 2006 pilot of the American television series Blade: The Series, created by David S. Goyer for Spike TV and based on the Marvel Comics vampire hunter. Directed by Peter O'Fallon from a script by Goyer and Geoff Johns, it was later released on DVD as a standalone film. Rapper Sticky Fingaz, credited as Kirk "Sticky" Jones, takes over the role of Eric Brooks / Blade from Wesley Snipes, with Jill Wagner as Krista Starr, Neil Jackson as Marcus van Sciver, Jessica Gower as Chase and Nelson Lee as Shen.

Set after the events of the film Blade: Trinity (2004), the story follows Krista Starr, a soldier who comes home from service in Iraq to learn that her twin brother, Zack, has died in mysterious circumstances. Investigating, she discovers that Zack had become a "familiar", a human who serves a vampire in the hope of one day being rewarded with eternal life. Her search leads her to Marcus van Sciver, a powerful vampire and high-ranking member of the House of Chthon, who killed Zack, and to Blade, the half-vampire hunter who realizes that hacking and slashing alone is getting him nowhere and that he needs to understand the inner workings of vampire society. Smitten with Krista, Marcus turns her into a vampire by injecting her with his own blood. Blade then injects her with the serum he uses to control his own thirst, prepared by his weaponsmith and hacker ally, Shen, and offers her the chance to avenge her brother by helping him bring down Marcus and his house. Revealing that Zack had been helping him with a sting operation, Blade forms a reluctant partnership with Krista, who must now maintain her cover inside the House of Chthon while battling her growing predatory instincts.

Goyer described the premise as a vampire take on the undercover crime drama Wiseguy, with Krista acting as a double agent and the vampires treated as the ultimate crime family. The pilot was shot in 2005 as Spike's first original scripted series, and it premiered on June 28, 2006, drawing 2.5 million viewers, the most-watched original series premiere in the network's history at the time. The series that followed ran for a single season before its cancellation. Critics were mixed, praising the action while faulting clichés, with 50% on Rotten Tomatoes for the series.

title: Under the Same Moon
tagline: The love between a mother and a son knows no Boundraries.
overview: Tells the parallel stories of nine-year-old Carlitos and his mother, Rosario. In the hopes of providing a better life for her son, Rosario works illegally in the U.S. while her mother cares for Carlitos back in Mexico.
plot:
Rosario, a single mother, illegally crossed the US-Mexico border to Los Angeles, leaving behind her young son, Carlitos, in his Mexican hometown with his ailing grandmother. As a part of their weekly calls, Rosario describes the area around the payphone to Carlitos in detail. On his ninth birthday, after his grandmother unexpectedly dies in her sleep, Carlitos learns that his aunt and uncle are trying to take custody of him for his mother's remittances.
Determined to reunite with his mother, Carlitos pays coyotes to help him cross through El Paso–Juárez into Mexico. However, the coyotes' car is towed by police for unrelated offenses. Carlitos exits the vehicle in a lot in El Paso, Texas, unwittingly dropping his money. Unable to buy a bus ticket alone, Carlitos asks a man to buy him a ticket. Realizing he has lost his money, Carlitos offers the man $100 to drive him to the impound lot, but upon arriving, Carlitos can't find the money. In desperation, the man tries to sell Carlitos to a pimp, but a local woman intervenes, taking Carlitos in and introducing him to life with other undocumented immigrants. One of the immigrants agrees to take Carlitos to Los Angeles after they get off work. Carlitos decides to help them as they work, however immigration officers raid the tomato farm. Carlitos escapes with an immigrant named Enrique, who initially wants nothing to do with him. The two hitchhike to Tucson, Arizona, where an angered Enrique tells Carlitos to leave. Seeing that some men are about to steal his backpack, Enrique decides to save Carlitos, who manages to gain employment for both Enrique and himself at a restaurant. Carlitos looks up his absent father, Oscar Aguilar Pons, and with Enrique's help, they meet. Oscar promises to help but ultimately abandons Carlitos, leaving Carlitos disappointed. Enrique decides to take Carlitos to Los Angeles. The two take a bus ride and reach LA. Meanwhile, Rosario loses one of her jobs due to racism.
Following an address, Carlitos and Enrique arrive in East LA, only to find a PO box. Carlitos and Enrique decide to search the city for the payphone his mother calls from. After a day of unsuccessful searching, the two rest on a bench (while she unknowingly walks right past them). Rosario after much persuasion from her friend decides to marry a U.S. citizen to for a green card however decides to bail last minute. Suddenly, Doña Carmen calls Rosario, letting her know that Carlitos crossed the border and that her mother is dead. Rosario, hearing this, decides to go back to Mexico to search for Carlitos. When boarding the bus, she sees a little boy at a payphone out the window of the bus at the bus station, and she realizes that Carlitos does know where to find her. In the morning, Enrique and Carlitos get surprised by a pair of police officers, and Enrique, noticing that Carlitos is about to be apprehended, throws his coffee at the cops to distract them.

title: Snow White: The Fairest of Them All
tagline: Deception never looked so sweet
overview: Snow White's mother dies during childbirth, leaving baby Snow and father John for dead on an icy field, who then receives a visit from one of Satan's representatives, granting him three wishes.
plot:
A young husband and wife, John and Josephine, wish for a child with skin as white as snow, lips as red as blood and hair as black as ebony. Their wish is granted and they are gifted a baby girl, whom they name Snow White. However, Josephine dies in childbirth. In the winter, John struggles to find food for his daughter, eventually collapsing and shedding a tear over a frozen lake, which frees the “Green-Eyed One”, an imprisoned djinn. As thanks for freeing him, the djinn asks John what he desires. John requests milk for his daughter, and the djinn grants his wish. John then asks to have Josephine back, calling her his Queen, but the djinn cannot resurrect the dead. Instead, he makes John a wealthy king and promises him a Queen.
The djinn pays a visit to Elspeth, his hideous witch sister who resents him for abandoning her years earlier when he was mortal. He offers to make up for his failure by transforming her into a beautiful woman and offering her John's hand. The djinn also provides Elspeth with a magical mirror that allows her to see others unseen and to deceive John. As years pass, Elspeth forms a relationship with her new husband and stepdaughter, now a sixteen-year-old princess. Her beauty, however, causes jealousy and resentment from the queen to the point where she keeps a room full of magical mirrors that constantly assure her that she "is the fairest of them all".
When Prince Alfred arrives in the kingdom and falls in love with Snow White, Elspeth is furious to discover that images of Snow White are appearing in her mirrors, which means that her stepdaughter is now more beautiful than her. Overcome with jealousy, Elspeth orders hunter Hector to take Snow White into the forest and kill her, and then return with Snow White's heart for her to consume. To keep Alfred from interfering, she curses him into the form of a bear and chases him off into the wilderness. Unable to kill Snow White, Hector presents Elspeth with the heart of a wild boar instead. After learning the truth, Elspeth kills Hector, imprisons John in her mirrors, and binds Snow White with an enchanted ribbon. Dwarf Sunday arrives and removes the ribbon. Snow White faints, so he carries the Princess, aided by six other dwarfs, inside their cottage to rest.
Snow White is introduced to the dwarfs each named after the days of the week and possessing the power to transform into a rainbow to move from one place to another (but are only capable of this if all seven of them are present). The eldest is Sunday, who is a victim of one of Elspeth's spells which left half of him as a garden gnome. The dwarfs allow Snow White to clean their home, though dwarf Wednesday is initially suspicious. When Elspeth learns that Snow White is still alive, she prepares a poisoned apple and disguises herself as Josephine.

title: Scooby-Doo! Abracadabra-Doo
tagline: The all-new Scooby-Doo movie with a magic touch!
overview: The gang goes on a trip to check on Velma's younger sister, Madelyn. She's been studying stage magic at the Whirlen Merlin Magic Academy, where apparently there have been sightings of a giant griffin. The gang decides to investigate.
plot:
After helping Mystery Inc. solve a factory mystery, Velma Dinkley receives a call from her mother to check on her younger sister Madelyn, a student of the Whirlen Merlin Magic Academy, after learning it is being terrorized by a gryphon. Upon their arrival, the gang meet Madelyn, who has a years-long crush on Shaggy Rogers; the academy's namesake Whirlen Merlin; his brother Marlon, the academy's cook and butler; Crystal, Whirlen's former stage assistant; Amos the groundskeeper; and Alma Rumblebuns, the school's head maid. They also learn that the gryphon has been scaring off students and staff.
Madelyn takes Shaggy on a tour of the school, explaining that the gryphon originally protected the castle the academy is based in before they are attacked by the beast. As the remaining students save for Madelyn leave, Mystery Inc. attend classes themselves. Amidst this, they learn of ice cream mogul Calvin Curdles' repeated attempts to buy the castle and suspect him of being behind the attacks. Velma and Daphne Blake soon find a secret passage leading to the school's attic, where they learn Rumblebuns used to date Curdles. Meanwhile, Madelyn finds a book on Lord O'Flannery, the castle's original owner who wielded a staff said to be able to control the gryphon and was laid to rest on a nearby island that is said to be haunted by a banshee. Despite this, the gang travel to O'Flannery's crypt and successfully recover the staff, but are chased off by the banshee before the gryphon attacks them. In the confusion, Shaggy and Madelyn lose the staff. She attempts to retrieve it, but is kidnapped by the gryphon. Concurrently, the others learn that Amos is secretly working for Curdles, but are forced to focus on saving Madelyn while Curdles renews his effort to make Whirlen sign over the castle.
While moving through the castle, they discover the Banshee is a hologram before the gryphon separates Shaggy and his dog Scooby-Doo from the others, who flee to get help. Nonetheless, Shaggy uses the staff to locate the gryphon's roost and rescue Madelyn before throwing it at the beast, causing it to lose control and eventually crash, revealing it was actually a puppet operated by Marlon via a blimp hidden by a fog machine. After discovering O'Flannery used hidden mechanical devices to make outsiders believe the castle was protected by a gryphon, Marlon restored them and created the banshee illusion to scare off trespassers. Having grown tired of Whirlen taking credit for his work, Marlon sought to use the devices to go solo, but was forced to use them to facilitate Curdles' plot to make the necessary capital. Marlon subsequently apologizes, which Whirlen accepts. Additionally, Velma reveals Amos knew of Marlon's work with the gryphon and told Curdles, who reveals further he wanted the castle to win back Rumblebuns.
Afterward, Curdles and Rumblebuns renew their relationship, the Merlin brothers make Madelyn their apprentice, and Curdles sponsors the academy's reopening.

title: And Soon the Darkness
tagline: Alone. Stranded. No One to Trust.
overview: When two American girls on a bike trip in a remote part of Argentina split up and one of them goes missing, the other must find her before her worst fears are realized.
plot:
And Soon the Darkness is a 2010 mystery horror film directed by Marcos Efron, who wrote the screenplay with Jennifer Derwingson. A remake of the 1970 British film of the same name, it stars Karl Urban, Amber Heard and Odette Annable, with Adriana Barraza and César Vianco in supporting roles. It is also known as Prisioneras de la oscuridad.

Stephanie and Ellie, two young American women backpacking through South America, decide to spend their last day in Argentina at a small hotel. After a drunken night at the local bar, where they meet some of the local men, they miss the bus that was to take them to their next stop. Since it runs only once a day, they head to a nearby river to relax and enjoy the unexpected extra day. After a heated argument, the friends separate, and Ellie is abducted. Searching frantically, Stephanie is joined by Michael, an American who says he is looking for his girlfriend, who disappeared months earlier. The town's lone police officer helps them but behaves suspiciously.

Stephanie tracks down the hideout where Ellie is being held and frees her, but the kidnapper kills Ellie during their escape. The policeman then appears and coaxes Stephanie into his car, where finding a passport makes her realize that he is a sadistic human trafficker responsible for the town's missing women. Michael seizes the officer's gun, and the policeman offers to exchange Michael's girlfriend, Camila, for Stephanie; Michael agrees, but the officer shoots him with a second weapon. Stephanie is taken by boat to be sold, but she escapes by jumping overboard, killing the kidnapper in the process. Reaching the Paraguayan shore, she is caught by the buyer and the pursuing policeman but breaks free again. The officer chases her, killing a fisherman who tries to help, and she hides in a boat, arming herself with a knife. When he comes aboard, they struggle; she stabs him in the leg, takes his gun and kills him. At dawn, as Stephanie walks toward the nearest town, a jeep pulls up, and a Paraguayan soldier steps out to rescue her.

The film was shot in Argentina in March 2009. It was presented at the European Film Market in Germany in February 2010, and Anchor Bay acquired U.S. rights that May, giving it a limited theatrical run beginning December 17, 2010, while Optimum Releasing scheduled a British release for February 2011. Critical response was poor, with only 17% approval on Rotten Tomatoes from six reviews.

title: Cell 211
tagline: To survive inside, he has to become one of them.
overview: The story of two men on different sides of a prison riot -- the inmate leading the rebellion and the young guard trapped in the revolt, who poses as a prisoner in a desperate attempt to survive the ordeal.
plot:
Cell 211 is a Spanish thriller film directed by Ramón Salazar, released in 2009. The movie is based on a true story and stars Karra Elejalde as José Manuel Bleda, a prisoner who masterminds an escape from the Madrid Central Prison.

The film begins with José Manuel Bleda (Karra Elejalde), a young man wrongly convicted of murder, serving his sentence at the Madrid Central Prison. The prisoners use a makeshift tunnel, hidden behind a false wall, to make their way out of the prison.

However, as Bleda and his accomplices try to evade capture, they realize that their actions have consequences beyond their control. The police launch a massive manhunt for the escaped prisoners, and tensions rise as they struggle to stay one step ahead of their pursuers.

Cell 211 received critical acclaim for its gripping storyline, strong performances, and tense atmosphere. The film's success can be attributed to its well-crafted plot, which keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: Millennium Actress
tagline: The magic of movies, the mystery of memory.
overview: Documentary filmmaker Genya Tachibana has tracked down the legendary actress Chiyoko Fujiwara, who mysteriously vanished at the height of her career. When he presents her with a key she had lost and thought was gone forever, the filmmaker could not have imagined that it would not only unlock the long-held secrets of Chiyoko’s life... but also his own.
plot:
Chiyoko Fujiwara, a renowned former actress and prominent star for film company Ginei, accepts a request for a retrospective interview amidst the demolition of the company's obsolete studio, her first interview in thirty years after her sudden retirement from the entertainment industry. Documentarian Genya Tachibana, a fan of Chiyoko, visits her house with his cameraman Kyoji Ida. Genya gives Chiyoko a small box containing an old-fashioned key. She remarks that the key "opens the most important thing" and begins reflecting on her life.
Chiyoko was born during the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake, which took the life of her father. As a schoolgirl, she is scouted by Ginei's general manager to appear in a government-sponsored film to inspire troops serving in the Second Sino-Japanese War. While her mother opposes, intending for Chiyoko to inherit the family's confectionery store, Chiyoko remains uncertain. She meets a political dissident painter being pursued by police and hides him in her home's storehouse. The next day, he leaves for Manchuria to join his allies, leaving Chiyoko the key to his box of art supplies. Chiyoko fails to catch him before his train departs, but vows to reunite with him. Genya tearfully recognizes this as a scene from one of Chiyoko's films; from this point forward, Chiyoko's memories and films become intertwined.
Recalling that Ginei's film is set in Manchuria, Chiyoko becomes an actress and travels there in the hopes of reuniting with the artist. She meets the general manager's nephew, aspiring director Junichi Ōtaki, and Ginei's lead actress, Eiko Shimao. During filming, Chiyoko is led to northern Manchuria by a fortuneteller bribed by Eiko. Her train is attacked by bandits before the setting shifts to a burning Sengoku period castle; Chiyoko, in the role of a princess, is tricked by an old wraith into drinking a cursed tea that will cause her to "burn forever in the flames of eternal love". In Chiyoko's continuing search for the artist, the setting and Chiyoko's role changes in quick succession, ranging from a courtesan in a brothel at the end of the Edo period to a schoolgirl in the Taishō era. Her family's store is destroyed in an air raid, but on a surviving wall, she finds a portrait of her painted by the artist and a promise of their reunion.
After World War II, Chiyoko's career flourishes, but she never forgets the artist. One day during filming, Eiko secretly steals the key. When asked by the film crew about the significance of the key, Chiyoko despondently realizes that she can no longer remember the artist's face, and resigns herself to a married life with Junichi. She eventually finds the key hidden in their home and confronts Junichi about it; Junichi, having been aware of Eiko's role in the fortuneteller incident, coerced her into stealing the key on his behalf in order to secure Chiyoko's hand in marriage. Eiko admits to being motivated by jealousy toward Chiyoko's youth and innocence.

title: The Stoning of Soraya M.
tagline: When a deadly conspiracy became a shameful cover-up One witness refused to be silent
overview: A drama set in 1986 Iran and centered on a man, Sahebjam, whose car breaks down in a remote village and enters into a conversation with Zahra, who relays to him the story about her niece, Soraya, whose arranged marriage to an abusive tyrant had a tragic ending.
plot:
Stranded in the remote Iranian village of Kuhpayeh, a journalist is approached by Zahra, a woman with a harrowing tale to tell about her niece, Soraya, and the bloody circumstances of Soraya's death by stoning the previous day. The two sit down as Zahra recounts the story to Freidoune, who records the conversation. The journalist must escape with his life to tell the story to the rest of the world.
Ali is Soraya's abusive husband who tries to get the village's mullah to convince Soraya to grant him a divorce so that he can marry a 14-year-old girl. Ali is able to convince the mullah by making threats to tell the village about his past as a convict.
Ali's marriage to the teenager is conditional upon Ali's ability to save the girl's father, a doctor who has been sentenced to death for an unspecified crime. Ali and Soraya have two sons, and Ali does not want to lose them. After a woman dies, Ali asks Zahra to persuade Soraya to care for the woman's now-widowed husband. Soraya starts working for the widower, and Ali uses this situation to spread lies that Soraya is being unfaithful to him so that she will be stoned and he can remarry. Ali knows if Soraya were dead, he would not have to pay child support either. Ali and the mullah start a rumor about her infidelity so they can charge her with adultery. They need one more witness to her "infidelity" to be able to formally charge her. They manipulate and threaten the widower into backing up their story. Ali then drags Soraya through the streets, beating her and publicly declaring that she has been unfaithful. Zahra intervenes, and takes her niece, Ali, and the mayor to talk privately. They bring the widower to the home, and, after he lies as instructed, a trial is pursued. Only men, including Soraya's father, are allowed while Soraya is confined in Zahra's house. She is quickly convicted. Zahra tries to flee with her and after realizing she cannot, pleads with the mayor for her life, even offering to switch places with Soraya. The conviction is upheld.
Soraya's father is given the first stone to throw, but he misses her repeatedly. A woman in the crowd pleads to the mayor that the stones missing are a sign that Soraya is innocent, but none of the men listen. Ali takes up stones and throws them himself. Her two sons are also forced to throw stones. The widower is given stones as well but instead walks away in tears. The crowd finally joins in and Soraya is stoned to death.
In the present, the widower informs the journalist that his car is fixed. The mullah and the widower are informed by Ali that his marriage to the teenage girl is off, implying that he could not spare her father from execution. Angry at Ali and the mullah, the widower admits that he lied. As the journalist attempts to leave, the mullah orders a Revolutionary Guard to stop him at gunpoint. They seize his tape recorder and destroy the tapes. Zahra then appears with the true tape in her hand.

title: LEGO: The Adventures of Clutch Powers
original_title: LEGO: The Adventures of Clutch Powers
tagline: First Full-Length LEGO Movie!
overview: Clutch Powers ventures on a mission assigned to him by his boss to solve the chaos that occurred on the Space Police prison planet.
plot:
Lego: The Adventures of Clutch Powers is a 2010 computer-animated action comedy, the first feature-length film based on the Lego toy line. It was directed by Howard E. Baker and released direct to home video. The voice cast includes Ryan McPartlin as the title character, along with Yvonne Strahovski, Roger Rose, Jeff Bennett, Paul Michael Glaser, Gregg Berger, Christopher Emerson and Alex Désert.

Clutch Powers is a daring explorer based in Lego City. The film opens as he tunnels underground to find a Power Crystal and wakes the Crystal King, a rock monster. After a chase, Clutch realizes that the crystal he is carrying is actually the king's baby and returns it, earning a real Power Crystal as a reward. Back in Lego City, his boss Kjeld Playwell assigns him to lead a team on his next mission: firefighter Brick Masterson, biologist Peg Mooring and engineer Bernie von Beam. Their first task is to investigate a breakout on the Space Police prison planet.

Clutch prefers to work alone, and the mismatched team struggles to cooperate. On the prison planet they are attacked by the unseen wizard Mallock the Malign, who escapes along with two other criminals, stealing the team's ship and sabotaging the rest. Clutch builds a new ship by himself and later admits that he was distracted during the mission by a symbol connected to one of the criminals, Omega. Playwell explains that Mallock once terrorized the medieval planet Ashlar, whose king, Revet, sacrificed himself to protect the realm, leaving his inexperienced son, Prince Varen, as heir.

On Ashlar, the team finds that Mallock has seized control with an army of skeletons and goblins. While Peg, Brick and Bernie build a battle chariot, Clutch sets off to persuade Varen to fight. Along the way he outwits a riddle-loving troll named Hogar, who becomes an ally and tells him of the late king's golden sword, the key to defeating Mallock. Varen at first feels unworthy, but with encouragement he and his knights join the battle. Clutch and Varen are captured in Mallock's castle, until Peg calls on a dragon she has befriended to free them, and Varen finds the courage to wield his father's sword.

The film was praised for its action and humor, though its animation and product placement drew criticism. It inspired a 4D attraction, A Clutch Powers 4D Adventure, which ran at several Legoland parks from 2010 until it was replaced in 2016, and Clutch Powers later appeared as a recurring character in the animated series Ninjago.

title: Stomp the Yard 2: Homecoming
overview: Chance Harris looks to find a balance between his school, work, relationships and opportunity to perform at the nationally televised step competition during homecoming weekend at Truth University.
plot:
Stomp the Yard 2: Homecoming, also titled Stomp the Yard: Homecoming, is an American dance drama released in 2010, helmed by Rob Hardy with Will Packer producing, and serves as a direct-to-video sequel to the 2007 hit Stomp the Yard. Collins Pennie leads the cast as Chance Harris, with Keith David as his father Terry and Tika Sumpter as his girlfriend Nikki; the ensemble also features Jasmine Guy as Janice, David Banner as Jay, Pooch Hall, Teyana Taylor, Kiely Williams, Terrence J, Columbus Short and Stephen "tWitch" Boss.

The film returns to the fictional Truth University in Atlanta, where the Theta Nu Theta fraternity is determined to dethrone its chief rival, Mu Gamma Xi, at a nationally televised step competition held during homecoming weekend, with full college scholarships at stake for the winners. Chance, who left home after his mother's death, has come back to Georgia to study while working at his father's struggling diner. Now a full member of the fraternity rather than a pledge, he is ready to contribute his own choreography to the team. At the start of the film, however, he is hustled in a rigged underground dance battle while trying to raise money for tuition, and ends up owing money to a dangerous gambler and his thugs, who threaten him with violence if he does not pay. Keeping his debt secret from his fraternity brothers, his father and his girlfriend Nikki, Chance becomes increasingly stressed and stretched thin as he tries to balance school, work, his relationships and practice while the competition approaches. To succeed, he must learn the value of responsibility, brotherhood and teamwork, the ideals that the precise, percussive art of stepping, with its combination of footwork, chanting and hand-clapping, comes to represent.

Filming began in Atlanta in November 2009, and Sony released the film on DVD on 21 September 2010. The soundtrack features tracks by artists including Ace Hood, Roscoe Dash, G-Side and John Forté. Reviewers praised the energetic stepping routines and Pennie's relatable lead performance but noted that the short running time rushes through predictable plot points, resolving major conflicts offscreen or in a single line. Film Intuition nonetheless considered it a solidly entertaining straight-to-disc sequel that gives fans more of what they enjoyed in the original.

title: Nowhere Boy
tagline: As a boy all John Lennon needed was love.
overview: The drama tells the story of John Lennon's teenage years in Liverpool and the start of his journey to becoming a successful musician. The story also examines the impact on his early life and personality of the two dominant females in his childhood.
plot:
The drama tells the story of John Lennon's teenage years from 1955 to 1960. John was separated from his mother, Julia Lennon, when he was five. His aunt and uncle, Mimi and George Smith, raised him like a son. John is close to his Uncle George, who dies suddenly when John is 14. John becomes curious about his mother, who has since had three daughters, one of whom was placed for adoption. He becomes obsessed with rock and roll music during a visit to Blackpool with Julia. When John is suspended from school, Julia allows him to stay at her house during the day to keep Mimi from finding out. Julia teaches John how to play the banjo. Mimi discovers their arrangement, but John refuses to go home with her and stays at Julia's. A week later, John overhears Julia and her common-law husband arguing about him, so he returns to Mimi's.
When John wants to start a rock 'n' roll band, Mimi buys him a guitar. John forms a band named the Quarrymen. At their first gig at a village fête, John meets Paul McCartney. Paul auditions and joins the band. Paul and John soon begin composing songs together. As the Quarrymen gain popularity, John meets Paul's friend, George Harrison, who becomes the band's lead guitarist.
At a birthday party which Julia throws for John, he confronts her about his absent father, Alf Lennon. He wants to know why Julia gave him up. He also confronts Mimi, who says Julia cheated on Alf and did not want to stay with him. Alf had asked 5-year-old John to choose whom he wanted to live with. John initially chose his father, though he then wanted to stay with his mother. Without either parent having the time or money to legally determine custody, Mimi became John's custodian. John is upset by this revelation, and leaves in a drunken anger.
John moves out to live on his own. Over time, he, Julia, and Mimi become friendly. When Julia is fatally hit by a car, John is consumed by anger, and physically assaults Paul and fellow bandmate Pete during Julia's wake, though the two soon forgive him. Two years later, he goes to travel to Hamburg with his newly formed band, the Beatles. Mimi asks John to call her as soon as he arrives. The film ends with the caption, "John phoned Mimi as soon as he arrived in Hamburg...and every week thereafter for the rest of his life".

title: Temple Grandin
tagline: Autism gave her a vision. She gave it a voice.
overview: A biopic of Temple Grandin, an autistic woman who has become one of top scientists in humane livestock handling.
plot:
Temple Grandin is an uncommunicative child who is prone to meltdowns and is diagnosed with autism. The medical consensus at the time is that autism is a form of schizophrenia resulting from insufficient maternal affection. Despite recommendations to place her in an institution, Temple's mother hires therapists and works to help her daughter adapt to social interaction.
In 1962, at the age of 15, Temple travels to her aunt and uncle's ranch to work. She observes cows being placed into a squeeze chute to calm them, and, during an anxiety attack, she uses the chute to calm herself. Inspired by her teacher, Dr. Carlock, to pursue science, she is admitted to Franklin Pierce College where she develops an early version of the squeeze machine to calm herself during stressful times. Her college misinterprets the use of the machine as an unlawful sexual act and informs the police, who seize and destroy it. In response, she develops a scientific protocol to test subjects' reactions to the machine, proving it to be a purely therapeutic device. Temple graduates with a degree in psychology and pursues a master's degree in animal science.
Temple faces sexism while attempting to integrate into the world of cattle ranching but ultimately designs a new dip structure designed to allow cattle to voluntarily move through rather than being forced. Initially, the device works as intended, and garners favorable coverage in local press, but the ranch hands are dismissive of her design and alter it, resulting in the drowning of several cows. Angered, Temple visits Dr. Carlock, and leaves the meeting encouraged to continue her efforts to improve the industry and start her own slaughterhouse.
Several days after visiting Dr. Carlock, Temple gets a call from her mother revealing that he has died. Later, while shopping, Temple meets a woman named Betty whose husband works for a slaughterhouse. Temple meets with Betty's husband at the slaughterhouse and explains her plan for the layout of the slaughterhouse. Her idea is tested, and works.
Years later, in 1981, Temple arrives at the National Autism Convention and shares her story.

title: Possession
tagline: What if the person you loved became someone else?
overview: A woman's life is thrown into chaos after a freak car accident sends her husband and brother-in-law into comas. Thrills arrive after the brother-in-law wakes up, thinking he's his brother.
plot:
Possession is a 2009 American psychological thriller directed by Joel Bergvall and Simon Sandquist, a remake of the 2002 South Korean film Addicted. It stars Sarah Michelle Gellar as Jess, a San Francisco lawyer, Lee Pace as her troubled brother-in-law Roman and Michael Landes as her husband Ryan, with Tuva Novotny as Roman's girlfriend Casey, Chelah Horsdal and William B. Davis. The film was shot in Vancouver from October 2006 under the working title Addicted.

Jess is a driven attorney who often puts her career ahead of her marriage to Ryan, a gentle artist. As they approach their first anniversary, the one source of friction in their happy life is Ryan's younger brother Roman, a moody, violent man whom Jess first met when she defended him on an assault charge and of whom she is deeply afraid. When Roman overhears the couple discussing sending him to a halfway house, he storms off in his car, and Ryan rushes after him. The brothers' cars collide on the Golden Gate Bridge, and both men fall into comas.

Weeks later, Roman wakes up and insists that he is actually Ryan, claiming that something inexplicable happened when the two were revived side by side and that his brother's soul now inhabits his body. Jess is at first hostile and convinced that he is confused by brain damage, but Roman keeps offering romantic gestures and recalling intimate memories only her husband could know. Gradually she comes to believe him, and despite the disapproval of her colleagues and Casey, she resumes her married life with the man in Roman's body and becomes pregnant. Yet small inconsistencies begin to surface, and when Casey goes missing and Jess finds that her private letters and photographs have been tampered with, she must face the terrifying possibility that she has been deceived.

The film explores grief, desire and identity, playing on the question of whether love can recognize a person beyond their physical form.

Because of financial problems at its distributor Yari Film Group, which filed for bankruptcy, the film's U.S. release was postponed repeatedly. It was released in theaters in several territories in South America, Europe and Asia between 2009 and 2011, and went straight to DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on March 9, 2010.

title: Merry Christmas, Drake & Josh
overview: Step brothers Drake and Josh must give a foster family the best Christmas ever or face years in jail for a Christmas party gone wrong.
plot:
Merry Christmas, Drake & Josh, also known as Drake & Josh: Best Christmas Ever, is a 2008 American Christmas comedy television film based on the Nickelodeon sitcom Drake & Josh and a sequel to the 2006 film Drake & Josh Go Hollywood. Drake Bell, Josh Peck, Miranda Cosgrove, Nancy Sullivan and Jonathan Goldstein return as their characters, joined by Bailee Madison. Premiering on Nickelodeon on December 5, 2008, a year after the show ended, it serves as the narrative conclusion of the franchise.

A year after the series finale, Walter and Audrey leave for a tropical vacation over Christmas, leaving Drake, Josh and their sister Megan at home. Drake plans a party on the roof of the Premiere Theater, where Josh works, and Josh's boss Helen agrees on the condition that Drake fill in as a mall Santa. While hiding in his costume from an admirer, Drake makes an earnest promise to a little girl named Mary Alice to give her family the best Christmas ever. The party is soon overrun by uninvited guests, and when Josh calls the police, a mix-up leads to his own arrest.

When Mary Alice tells Drake about her sick foster mother and overworked foster father, Drake realizes he needs Josh's help and attempts to break him out of jail, only to be arrested himself. Helen, acting as their lawyer, explains Drake's promise to the judge, who agrees to spare them from jail as long as they keep it. Their embittered parole officer, Perry Gilbert, insists that every member of Mary Alice's foster family must vote that they had the best Christmas ever, or the brothers will be locked up.

The household includes squabbling twins Lily and Violet, a boy named Zigfee who speaks an unknown language, the know-it-all Trey and Mary Alice's cynical older brother Luke. As Gilbert sabotages their efforts and Megan drives a hard bargain for her help, Drake and Josh scramble to deliver the holiday magic they promised, while Walter and Audrey's vacation turns into a disaster. In the end, the brothers win over the family and create snow from grated hard cheese, and Walter and Audrey return home to join everyone playing in the "cheese snow."

The premiere drew 8.1 million viewers, a record for a Nickelodeon original movie and one of the most-watched cable TV films of its time. The film features Cosgrove's cover of "Christmas Wrapping" and a cast version of "The Twelve Days of Christmas," and it was released on DVD on December 19, 2008.

title: Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps
tagline: Gordon never gives up.
overview: As the global economy teeters on the brink of disaster, a young Wall Street trader partners with disgraced former Wall Street corporate raider Gordon Gekko on a two tiered mission: To alert the financial community to the coming doom, and to find out who was responsible for the death of the young trader's mentor.
plot:
In 2008, seven years after former corporate raider Gordon Gekko was released from prison after serving time for insider trading and securities fraud, Gekko is promoting his new book Is Greed Good?, warning about a possible 2008 financial crisis. His estranged daughter, Winnie, runs a small, non-profit news blog and is dating Jacob "Jake" Moore, a top prop trader at Keller Zabel Investments (KZI). Jake, a protégé of KZI managing director Louis Zabel, has been raising money for Dr. Masters and a fusion research project which promises abundant clean energy. Jake also supports his mother Sylvia, who quit nursing to speculate in residential real estate.
In the early stages of the downturn predicted by Gekko, KZI's stock loses more than half its value. Louis Zabel's attempt to secure a bailout for KZI from other Wall Street banks is blocked by Bretton James, head of rival firm Churchill Schwartz (Church). KZI had refused to help Church during the dot-com bubble years earlier. Zabel kills himself by jumping in front of a subway train and Winnie accepts Jake's marriage proposal. Jake introduces himself to Gekko at a lecture. Gekko tells him that KZI collapses when James spread rumours of it having toxic debt. Jake agrees to reconcile Winnie and Gekko's relationship if Gekko can supply evidence of James' actions against KZI.
Jake spreads rumors about nationalization of an oil field in Equatorial Guinea, which Church has invested in. Church loses $120 million to this market manipulation. James is impressed by Jake's initiative and hires him, and Jake convinces Chinese investors to invest in Church's fusion project. Jake arranges for Gekko and Winnie to meet at a fundraiser. When Gekko confronts James about providing evidence against him in 2001, and his more recent actions against KZI, James tells Gekko he's no longer relevant. Gekko also encounters Bud Fox, who turned Bluestar Airlines into a huge success after his release from jail, then sold it for millions, and retired. Winnie confronts Gekko about their failed relationship, his affairs and her brother Rudy's suicide. When Gekko explains he obtained successful therapists in prison, and paid off a drug dealer to stop selling to Rudy, Winnie forgives him.
As the 2008 financial crisis accelerates, James and Church's chairman, Julius Steinhardt, advise federal regulators to buy their multi-billion-dollar subprime loans. When the real estate market collapses, Jake helps Sylvia with his own money. Winnie informs Jake she's expecting their first child. Jake learns James is diverting funds earmarked for the Chinese investment into underperforming solar panels, which pose far less threat to his fossil fuel investments. Gekko tells Jake that James had secretly made huge profits betting against subprime loans, yet still accepted massive bailout from the federal government.
Gekko surrenders a $100 million trust account he hid in Switzerland in the 1980s so Winnie can fund the fusion research.

title: Desert Flower
tagline: The extraordinary true story of the woman who crossed the desert and changed the world.
overview: The autobiography of a Somalian nomad who was sold in marriage at 13, fled from Africa a while later to become finally an American supermodel and is now at the age of 38, the UN spokeswoman against female genital mutilation.
plot:
Desert Flower (German: Wüstenblume) is a 2009 biographical drama written and directed by Sherry Hormann and produced by Peter Herrmann, adapted from the best-selling autobiography of the Somali-born model and activist Waris Dirie. Liya Kebede stars as Waris, with Sally Hawkins as her friend Marylin, Craig Parkinson as Neil, Timothy Spall as the fashion photographer Terry Donaldson, Juliet Stevenson as Lucinda, Meera Syal as Pushpa Patel and Anthony Mackie as Harold Jackson. A German-led international co-production, it was shot in 2008 in Djibouti, New York, London, Cologne, Berlin and Munich.

Unlike the book, which tells Waris's story in chronological order, the film opens on the day she flees the Somali embassy in London and reveals her earlier life in flashbacks. Born into a nomadic herding family in the Somali desert, she grows up in a daily struggle for survival and is subjected to genital cutting at the age of three. When her father tries to marry her off at thirteen to a much older man, she runs away and wanders across the desert until she reaches Mogadishu. Her mother's relatives take her in and find her a position as a maid at the Somali embassy in London, where for years she is not allowed to leave the house.

When the embassy is abandoned because of the war in Somalia, Waris escapes and disappears into the city. She befriends Marylin, a lively shop assistant who takes her in, learns English and finds work cleaning at a fast-food restaurant. There she is discovered by Donaldson, and soon designers are competing for her and the press is captivated by the former nomad girl. Her expired passport makes her an illegal immigrant, however, and after forged papers fail she obtains residency only through a sham marriage. She becomes one of the world's highest-paid models, yet the secret of her childhood weighs on her. At the height of her fame she speaks publicly in an interview about female genital mutilation, and the wave of sympathy and outrage that follows leads her to devote her life to fighting the practice.

The film premiered at the Venice Film Festival in September 2009 and opened in German cinemas that month, reaching the United States in 2011. It won the audience award for best European film at the San Sebastián International Film Festival and was nominated for the German Film Award for best film, though some critics found it simplified and sentimental.

title: She's Out of My League

overview: When he starts dating drop-dead gorgeous Molly, insecure airport security agent Kirk can't believe it. As his friends and family share their doubts about the relationship lasting, Kirk does everything he can to avoid losing Molly forever.
plot:
She's Out of My League is a romantic comedy film released in 2010 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of Moe Flinders (played by Jay Baruchel), a shy and awkward hockey player who works as a flight attendant for a small airline.

Moe lives with his mother, Nora (played by Wendy Crewson), and his best friend, Stu (played by Craig Robinson). Despite his unassuming nature, Moe has a secret crush on Lauren Reynolds (played by Alice Eve), a beautiful and charming flight attendant who works at the same airline. However, he is too shy to approach her.

One day, Lauren transfers to Moe's airline, and he sees an opportunity to get close to her. He enlists the help of his friend Stu, who has a more outgoing personality, to help him woo Lauren. Stu agrees to pretend to be Moe's girlfriend in order to impress Lauren and make Moe jealous.

As the story progresses, Moe becomes increasingly frustrated with Stu's antics, which only seem to drive Lauren further away from him. Meanwhile, Lauren starts to develop feelings for Moe, but she is hesitant to express them due to her fear of rejection.

The plot takes a turn when Lauren suffers an injury and is forced to take time off work. During this period, Moe has the opportunity to get close to her and win her heart. However, he struggles with his own insecurities and fears of rejection, which causes him to make mistakes and lose Lauren's trust.

In the end, Moe realizes that he needs to be true to himself and take a chance on love. He confesses his feelings to Lauren, and they share a romantic moment together. The movie ends with Moe and Lauren flying off into the sunset, symbolizing their newfound love and happiness.

Throughout the movie, the supporting characters add comedic relief and depth to the story. Stu's antics provide much of the humor, while Nora's motherly instincts and advice offer a heartwarming contrast to the more lighthearted moments.

Overall, She's Out of My League is a charming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, vulnerability, and self-discovery. The movie features a talented cast, witty dialogue, and a relatable protagonist who will resonate with audiences.

tagline: A very familiar Aura Guardian...
overview: In the legendary past, before Poké Balls were invented, an aura-guiding hero Pokémon named Lucario sensed two groups of armies about to clash, and a threat of a massive war in front of Oldoran Castle in Kanto that would leave no survivors. He transferred this message to his master, the legendary hero Arlon, while he was being attacked by a violent group of Hellgar. plot:
Pokémon: Lucario and the Mystery of Mew is a 2005 Japanese animated fantasy film directed by Kunihiko Yuyama and produced by OLM, Inc. The eighth Pokémon film and the third connected to Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire, it features the voices of Rica Matsumoto, Ikue Ōtani, Yūji Ueda, Kaori, Fushigi Yamada and Megumi Hayashibara.

Long ago, as a war between Pokémon is about to break out near the Tree of Beginning, the Pokémon Lucario warns his master, the Aura Guardian Sir Aaron, but Aaron appears to abandon him, sealing Lucario inside his staff. The queen of Cameron Palace receives the staff and sees the Tree of Beginning glow as the war is averted. More than a thousand years later, Ash Ketchum and his friends arrive at Cameron Palace during a festival honoring Aaron. Ash, dressed like Aaron by coincidence, wins a tournament and is named that year's Aura Guardian. When he receives the staff, his aura, which resembles Aaron's, frees Lucario, who tells everyone of his master's betrayal.

Meanwhile, Pikachu and the other Pokémon play with a Mew that lives near the palace until two Weavile, sent by an adventurer named Kidd to tag Mew, chase them. Pikachu protects Mew, which teleports him and Team Rocket's Meowth away to the Tree of Beginning. Kidd joins Ash's group, and Lucario reluctantly agrees to guide them. Lucario's contempt for humans leads to a fight with Ash, but Ash eventually wins his trust. Along the way, "time flowers" replay visions of the past. After battling the tree's guardians, Regirock, Regice and Registeel, they enter, and Kidd's survey robots trigger the tree's antibody-like defenses, which absorb everyone until Mew reasons with the tree. The disruption sends the tree into shock, and Mew, which depends on it to survive, falls gravely ill. At the tree's heart a vision reveals that Aaron sacrificed himself, pouring his aura into the tree to stop the war. Ash and Lucario combine their aura to save the tree and Mew, but Lucario pushes Ash away to spare him. Exhausted, Lucario sees a final vision in which the dying Aaron explains that he sealed Lucario away to keep him alive and thanks him for his friendship, and Lucario passes away. Kidd keeps her discovery secret, and Ash vows to remember Lucario.

The film opened in Japan on July 16, 2005, and grossed ¥4.3 billion, the year's second-highest-grossing domestic film after Howl's Moving Castle. Anime News Network gave it a B−, praising its epic premise and animation but faulting the plot.

title: Ted Bundy
tagline: Not every serial killer fits the profile.
overview: Docu-drama based on the life of Ted Bundy, a serial killer who killed at least 19 young women during the 1970's (though some sources say as many as 30 to 35 were murdered). Set from his college student years, to his first victims, his capture, escape from prison (twice), his final killing spree to his trial, conviction and execution.
plot:
Ted Bundy is a 2002 independent biographical crime thriller directed by Matthew Bright, who wrote it with Stephen Johnston. A sardonic dramatisation of the crimes of the American serial killer who raped and murdered numerous young women during the 1970s, it stars Michael Reilly Burke as Bundy and Boti Bliss as his girlfriend Lee, with Tracey Walter, Deborah Offner and Tom Savini in supporting roles.

In 1974 Ted Bundy is a law student in Seattle with a long-term girlfriend and a part-time job at a crisis hotline. Hidden from those around him is a sadistic personality given to stalking, voyeurism and theft. He commits his first murder, killing a woman who called the hotline, and soon develops a pattern: breaking into the homes of young women or luring them to his car by pretending to be injured or posing as a police officer, then abducting, assaulting and killing them. His knowledge of police methods helps him avoid suspicion, although investigators have composite sketches and have learned his name from witnesses.

In Utah in 1975 a young woman escapes from his moving car, and her description of the vehicle later leads to his arrest, when officers find his kit of restraints and tools in the trunk. Convicted of kidnapping, he becomes the prime suspect in a series of murders. When he assures Lee that the authorities can never prove the killings, she realises he is guilty and leaves him.

Acting as his own lawyer in Colorado in 1977, Ted escapes by jumping from a courthouse library window, is recaptured days later, and then escapes again, landing on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted list. Settling in Tallahassee, Florida, he attacks four women in a Florida State University sorority house, killing two, and then murders a young girl before being caught. Sentenced to die in the electric chair, he spends a decade filing appeals that all fail. In 1989 guards drag him to the execution chamber, and later Lee, watching the news with her husband, wonders who Ted Bundy really was.

The film had a limited theatrical run in American cities including New York and Los Angeles in September 2002 and grossed under $70,000 worldwide. It holds a 41% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Barbie in A Mermaid Tale
tagline: Barbie Makes A Big Splash!
overview: Barbie stars as Merliah, a surfer who learns a shocking secret: she's a mermaid! She and her dolphin friend set out for an undersea adventure to rescue her mother, the queen of Oceana.
plot:
Barbie in a Mermaid Tale is a 2010 computer-animated adventure film directed by Adam L. Wood and produced by Mattel Entertainment with Rainmaker Entertainment. The seventeenth entry in the Barbie film series, it follows Merliah Summers, a champion surfer from Malibu who learns that she is a mermaid princess and travels beneath the sea to rescue her long-lost mother, the rightful queen of an ocean kingdom. The voice cast includes Kelly Sheridan, Kathleen Barr, Nakia Burrise, Garry Chalk and Haryke Hendrikse.

During a surfing competition, Merliah's hair suddenly develops pink streaks and she wipes out, only to discover that she can breathe underwater and is approached by Zuma, a talking pink bottlenose dolphin. Her grandfather Break reveals that her mother was a mermaid who handed Merliah to him as a baby because she was born with legs. Zuma tells Merliah and her friends Fallon and Hadley that her mother is Calissa, former queen of Oceana, whose sister Eris seized the throne after Calissa vanished. Merliah at first refuses to get involved, but when her childhood pendant breaks and shows a magical image of her living mother, she agrees to go, hoping Calissa can make her normal. The ocean is weakening because Eris cannot properly spin Merillia, the magical substance that sustains the sea; the Merillia she hands out at her festivals is in fact spun by Calissa, who is held in the palace dungeon. Disguised with a fake tail by the mermaids Kayla and Xylie, Merliah consults the Destinies, three prophetic mermaids, who tell her she must collect the Celestial Comb, a Dreamfish and Eris's protective necklace. After finding the first two, Merliah snatches the necklace during a performance at Eris's festival, but her disguise is torn away and Eris casts her into a whirlpool. Offered the chance to return to Malibu as a normal human, Merliah instead embraces her role as princess, gains a true tail and escapes. She proves her identity with the Comb, traps Eris in the whirlpool and frees Calissa, who restores Oceana. Admitting she misses life on land, Merliah receives a magical gift from her mother, returns home to her grandfather and wins the surfing competition.

The film was released on DVD on March 9, 2010, and had its television premiere on Nickelodeon on April 4, 2010. It was followed by a 2012 sequel, Barbie in a Mermaid Tale 2.

title: Return to Halloweentown
tagline: Unlock The Ultimate Secret This October!
overview: As Halloweentown prepares to celebrate its 1,000th anniversary, Marnie Piper and her brother Dylan return to Witch University, where trouble is in session from the Sinister Sisters and from someone who's plotting to use Marnie's powers for evil.
plot:
One year after the events of the last film, a now eighteen-year-old Marnie is offered a full scholarship to Halloweentown's Witch University, headed by its chancellor Luxana Goodwyn, for her good deeds and help in the previous years. Much to her mother Gwen's dismay, Marnie decides to forgo her original college plans and instead attends the Halloweentown school. Gwen forces Marnie's brother Dylan to accompany and keep an eye on her. The school is not what it seems, as witches and warlocks cannot use magic; instead their curriculum seems to be no different than a mortal college curriculum: Shakespeare analysis, with old magic history. Marnie had thought she would learn how to use her magic and is now crestfallen.
Marnie runs into her old friend Ethan and makes a new friend named Aneesa the Genie. She also makes three new enemies in the Sinister Sisters: Scarlett, Sage and Sapphire, a triad of malevolent, extremely snobby, spoiled, and manipulative witches who are the daughters of Silas Sinister and with whom Dylan is immediately infatuated. Marnie learns that she is responsible for the university's restriction of magic. The university was originally established exclusively for warlocks and witches to learn how to use magic, but when the portal between Halloweentown and the human world was opened permanently instead of just on Halloween, most of them went to college in the mortal realm. Since then, Witch University has allowed other magical creatures to attend. Magic was banned on campus grounds to level the academic playing field, but the Sinister Sisters still use theirs discreetly. The classes are boring for Marnie until during one class with Dr. Ichabod Grogg, she uncovers within the dungeon of the college, a box, with the name "S. Cromwell" inscribed on it, magically appearing in front of her, but the box is locked and has no key with it.
Marnie meets with one of her professors, Miss Periwinkle, and asks for an explanation. Periwinkle only tells Marnie that the S. stands for Splendora and that she and her were very good friends. Marnie and Dylan learn that the box contains the Gift, a magical power only a Cromwell can use, which Splendora locked in the box centuries ago. Meanwhile, the Sinister sisters use Dylan's infatuation with them to make him do their homework and use as bait for Marnie. Later, Ethan tells Marnie about a mysterious group, his father was part of, known as the Dominion that will try to use Marnie to open the box and use the Gift to take over Halloweentown and turn everyone into their permanent slaves, and Goodwyn and Grogg are part of them, but Marnie does not believe him. Marnie later travels to the past to meet Splendora and learn about the true nature of the enigmatic gift. Splendora explains that the Gift is an amulet that bestows the wearer with the power to control anyone, a power that witches are forbidden to use, and its power can tempt a good witch to turn bad.

title: Inuyasha the Movie 3: Swords of an Honorable Ruler
original_title: 映画犬夜叉 天下覇道の剣
tagline: The Three Swords of the Fang collide in an epic battle!
overview: Inuyasha and his brother, Sesshomaru, each inherited a sword from their father after his death. However, their father had a third sword, named Sounga, that he sealed away. Seven hundreds years after his death, Sounga awakens and threatens mankind's very existence. How will the children of the Great Dog Demon stop this unimaginable power?
plot:
Inuyasha the Movie 3: Swords of an Honorable Ruler (Japanese: 映画犬夜叉 天下覇道の剣) is a 2003 Japanese animated fantasy adventure film based on Rumiko Takahashi's manga series Inuyasha. Produced by Sunrise, it was directed by Toshiya Shinohara and written by Katsuyuki Sumisawa, and is the third Inuyasha film, following The Castle Beyond the Looking Glass and preceding Fire on the Mystic Island. Its voice cast includes Kappei Yamaguchi, Satsuki Yukino and Koji Tsujitani. The story has the half-brothers Inuyasha and Sesshomaru reluctantly joining forces against So'unga, their late father's third sword.

Two hundred years earlier, the great dog demon Tōga refuses to give his elder son Sesshomaru his swords Tessaiga and So'unga. He then rescues his human wife, Lady Izayoi, from the samurai leader Takemaru of Setsuna, who loves her and has stabbed her and set fire to the mansion where she is giving birth. Reviving her with his sword Tenseiga, Tōga lets her escape with their newborn son, Inuyasha, and dies fighting Takemaru as the mansion collapses on them.

In the present, Kagome Higurashi's family finds an ancient sword among their shrine's treasures; it is So'unga, and the spirit of its sheath, Saya, warns that Inuyasha must master it before it destroys the modern world. When Inuyasha grasps it, the sword possesses him and turns him into his demon form. Back in the feudal era it drives him against Sesshomaru until Kagome breaks the spell with the command of his subjugation beads. The swordsmith Totosai explains that So'unga harbors an ancient evil demon. The sword then revives Takemaru, who seizes a castle, raises its slain soldiers as an undead army and opens a portal to the netherworld. Inuyasha, Kagome, Miroku, Sango, Shippo and Kirara fight alongside Sesshomaru, and Miroku risks his life using his Wind Tunnel against the army. Inuyasha kills Takemaru, forcing So'unga to take a body of its own, and after failing separately the brothers combine Tessaiga's Backlash Wave and the Dragon Strike of Sesshomaru's Tōkijin to send the sword into the netherworld, as Tōga's spirit declares his pride in his sons.

Toho released the film in Japan on December 20, 2003; it opened at number three behind Finding Nemo and The Last Samurai. Its theme song, "Four Seasons", was performed by Namie Amuro, and Viz Media issued it on DVD in 2005. Reviewers praised its action and its expanded family backstory while criticizing its pacing and some corny moments.

overview: While the Saiyan Paragus persuades Vegeta to rule a new planet, King Kai alerts Goku of the South Galaxy's destruction by an unknown Super Saiyan.
plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Broly - The Legendary Super Saiyan is a 1993 Japanese animated science fantasy martial arts film directed by Daisuke Nishio and produced by Toei Animation. The movie takes place during the Dragon Ball Z series, specifically after the events of the Androids Saga.

The story begins with a flashback of Broly's childhood on Planet Vegeta, where he is shown to be a powerful warrior from a lower-class family. However, his father, Paragus, is killed by Vegeta, who sees Broly as a threat to his own power and status. This event sets the stage for Broly's desire for revenge against Vegeta.

The film then jumps forward in time to the present, where Broly has grown up on a remote planet and has become an even more powerful warrior. He is drawn to Earth by the energy of Goku and his friends, who are training on the planet. When Broly arrives, he is met with hostility from the Z Warriors, who are unaware of his true identity.

As tensions rise between Broly and the Z Warriors, a series of intense battles ensue, showcasing Broly's incredible strength and power. Meanwhile, Goku and Vegeta begin to realize that Broly is their long-lost brother, and they must work together to stop him before he destroys the Earth.

Throughout the film, Broly's backstory is slowly revealed, showing his tragic past and his desire for revenge against Vegeta. The movie also explores the themes of family, power, and redemption, as Goku and Vegeta grapple with their complicated feelings towards each other.

As the battle between Broly and the Z Warriors reaches its climax, it becomes clear that Broly's true intentions are not to destroy Earth, but to find his father's grave and avenge his death. In the end, Goku and Vegeta manage to calm Broly down and convince him to spare the Earth, using their combined strength to defeat him.

The film concludes with Broly finally finding peace and closure, having avenged his father's death and found a new sense of purpose. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Goku and Vegeta reflecting on the lessons they learned from their battle with Broly and the importance of family and forgiveness.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: Broly - The Legendary Super Saiyan is an action-packed and emotionally charged film that explores themes of family, power, and redemption. With its stunning animation and epic battles, it remains a beloved entry in the Dragon Ball Z franchise.

title: Julius Caesar
overview: Twenty year-old Julius Caesar flees Rome for his life during the reign of Sulla but through skill and ambition rises four decades later to become Rome's supreme dictator.
plot:
Julius Caesar is a 2002 television miniseries directed by the German filmmaker Uli Edel and written by Peter Pruce and Craig Warner, dramatising the life of the Roman statesman from 82 BC to his death in 44 BC. Jeremy Sisto plays Caesar, with Richard Harris, in one of his final screen roles, as Sulla, Christopher Walken as Cato, Chris Noth as Pompey and Valeria Golino as Calpurnia. It aired on German television in December 2002 and on TNT in two parts in June 2003.

The story opens as the dictator Sulla marches on Rome and posts lists of men marked for death. The eighteen-year-old Caesar tries to save his father-in-law, is arrested by Sulla's officer Pompey and refuses to divorce his wife Cornelia. Pompey secretly spares him and sends him into exile, and on the voyage he is captured by pirates and survives only when his ransom arrives. After Sulla dies, Caesar returns to political life, but Cornelia falls ill and dies, and he vows to become the great man she believed he could be.

Years later, as Pompey celebrates a triumph, Caesar has been elected consul and conceals the seizures of his "falling sickness" with help from Calpurnia, whom he later marries. To seal an alliance, his daughter Julia marries Pompey, who gives Caesar the forces to conquer Gaul. There Caesar spares the defiant warrior Vercingetorix, who later raises a vast Gallic army against him, and Caesar wins the decisive Battle of Alesia.

Julia's death in childbirth ends the alliance. Pompey and Cato push the Senate to strip Caesar of his command, and Caesar responds by crossing the Rubicon. He makes himself dictator, defeats Pompey at Pharsalus, follows him to Egypt, where the boy king Ptolemy XIII has Pompey killed, and becomes involved with Cleopatra. After his victory at Thapsus, Cato takes his own life rather than ask for mercy.

Convinced that Caesar intends to become king, a group of senators led by Cassius brings the respected Brutus into a conspiracy. Ignoring Calpurnia's warning dream, Caesar goes to the Senate on the Ides of March and is stabbed to death.

The miniseries received two Primetime Emmy nominations, for makeup and for sound editing.

plot:
The Descent Part 2 is a 2009 British horror film directed by Jon Harris and a sequel to Neil Marshall's 2005 film The Descent. Written by James McCarthy, J Blakeson and James Watkins and produced by Christian Colson and Ivana MacKinnon, with Marshall as executive producer, it stars Shauna Macdonald, returning as Sarah, and Natalie Mendoza as Juno. Harris had served as the editor of the first film.

The film begins two days after the events of the original, in which six women ventured into an uncharted cave system and were attacked by blind, humanoid predators known as crawlers. Sarah emerges from the caves covered in blood and suffering from amnesia. When doctors discover that some of the blood belongs to one of her missing friends, Sheriff Vaines suspects that she may be responsible for the women's disappearance. He forces the traumatized Sarah to accompany him, his deputy Rios and a team of experienced cave rescuers back underground through an abandoned mine shaft to search for the others.

As the team descends, they find the body of one of the missing women and Sarah begins to recover fragments of her memory. A cave-in separates the group, and soon the crawlers begin hunting them in the dark tunnels. The rescuers discover a damaged video camera that reveals what happened to the women, and Sarah, now fully remembering, must use what she has learned about the creatures, which hunt by sound, to keep the survivors alive. Deep in the caves, the group discovers that Juno, whom Sarah left for dead after a bitter betrayal, is still alive, and the two women are forced into an uneasy alliance as they search for a way out of the crawlers' lair.

The sequel follows the American ending of the first film, in which Sarah escapes the caves, and expands the claustrophobic setting with more extensive gore and action.

The Descent Part 2 was released in British cinemas on 2 December 2009 and went directly to DVD in the United States on 27 April 2010. Reviews were mixed, with 48 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said it lacked the unnerving power of its predecessor but offered enough nasty set pieces for gore fans.

title: Sorry if I Love You
overview: Alex Belli is a 37 year old advertising executive whose fiancée Elena has just left him, and who is having difficulty at work trying to think of a good advertising campaign for a new Japanese product. Niki is a bubbly 17 year old student. She has three best friends with whom she shares all her problems, and an annoying ex-boyfriend Fabio who is set on getting her back, but Niki's not interested. plot:
Niki is a seventeen-year-old girl in her last year of high school who spends her free time with her trusted group of friends, the O.N.D.E. (waves) a name created from the first letters of each of their names: Olimpia (Olly), Nicoletta (Niki), Diletta and Erica. Alex is almost thirty-seven and a career publicist who is struggling with the loss of his longtime girlfriend, Elena, who recently left him. One morning, Niki and Alex crash into each other while commuting. After giving her a ride to school, Alex gives Niki his contact information for any repairs needed for her moped, which soon becomes the means by which their romance blossoms.
Diletta meets a guy at school and they quickly develop feelings for each other. Soon after making plans with him, Diletta gets into a tragic car accident that leaves her in a coma for weeks. Olly, Niki, and Erica spend their time with her in the hospital, singing and playing her songs and reviewing for la maturità, the final exam at the end of Italian high school. While Niki reviews for the test, Diletta wakes up and the girls celebrate.
Elena returns and Alex leaves Niki for his old life, but soon realizes that he is no longer in love with the woman he is supposed to be with, nor with the job he is supposed to be glad to have. Alex finds that Elena had been sleeping with the man with whom he had been competing for the "La Luna" advertisement bid and kicks her out. He then rejects his new promotion and work and quits, buying a house on an island and leaving a note for Niki to join him there. They reunite and live happily ever after.
