title: The A-Team
tagline: There Is No Plan B
overview: A group of Iraq War veterans goes on the run from U.S. military forces while they try to clear their names after being framed for a crime they didn't commit. Along the way, Col. Hannibal Smith, Capt. H.M. ‘Howling Mad’ Murdock , Sgt. Bosco ‘B.A.’ Baracus, and Lt. Templeton ‘Faceman’ Peck help out various people they encounter.
plot:
The A-Team is a 2010 American action comedy based on the 1980s television series created by Frank Lupo and Stephen J. Cannell. Joe Carnahan directed and co-wrote it with Brian Bloom and Skip Woods, and Cannell and Tony Scott produced, with Ridley Scott as executive producer. In development since the mid-1990s, the project went through several writers and pauses before the cast assembled in 2009 and filming took place in Canada, including Vancouver. 20th Century Fox released it on June 11, 2010.

In Mexico, Army Ranger John "Hannibal" Smith escapes from corrupt police working for the renegade general Javier Tuco, rescues Templeton "Face" Peck with help from B.A. Baracus, and recruits the eccentric pilot H.M. "Howling Mad" Murdock from an Army hospital to fly them away in a medical helicopter. Eight years later in Iraq, a CIA operative named Lynch hands the team a black operation to recover U.S. Treasury printing plates and a large amount of cash leaving Baghdad. They succeed, but the cash and their commander, General Morrison, are apparently blown up by Brock Pike's private security firm Black Forest. With no proof the mission was authorized, the four are court-martialed and sent to separate prisons, and Face's former girlfriend Charissa Sosa, a Defense Criminal Investigative Service officer, is demoted.

Six months later Hannibal accepts Lynch's offer of reinstatement in return for the plates, breaks his men out of prison, and escapes a drone attack by flying a tank under parachutes out of a doomed cargo plane. They discover that Morrison faked his death and stole the plates with Pike and Lynch, who then double-crossed him. After an elaborate showdown on a container ship in the Port of Los Angeles, the pacifist B.A. kills Pike, and Lynch is tricked into confessing and arrested by Sosa. The team is taken into custody for escaping prison, but Sosa slips Face a handcuff key with a kiss, and they survive as soldiers of fortune.

Liam Neeson plays Hannibal, Bradley Cooper plays Face, Quinton Jackson plays B.A., Sharlto Copley plays Murdock and Jessica Biel plays Sosa, with Patrick Wilson. Original stars Dirk Benedict and Dwight Schultz make cameos. Reviews were mixed, praising the cast and action but faulting the script, with 48% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. Grossing $177 million on a $110 million budget, it underperformed, and plans for a sequel were dropped.

title: Halloweentown High
tagline: Too ghoul for school.
overview: Marnie Piper prepares to begin a new school year, she asks the Halloweentown Hot Witches' Council to work toward openness between Halloweentown and the mortal world. She proposes to bring a group of Halloweentown students to her own high school in the mortal world.
plot:
Halloweentown High, also known as Halloweentown 3, is a 2004 American fantasy comedy television film produced as a Disney Channel Original Movie and the third installment in the Halloweentown series. It stars Kimberly J. Brown as Marnie Piper, Debbie Reynolds as her grandmother Aggie Cromwell, Judith Hoag as her mother Gwen and Joey Zimmerman as her brother Dylan, with Clifton Davis as Principal Flanagan and Finn Wittrock as Cody, Marnie's love interest.

Two years after the events of the previous film, Marnie Piper is starting a new school year and wants to bring the magical world of Halloweentown and the mortal world closer together. She asks the Halloweentown Council to let a group of young people from Halloweentown attend her high school in the mortal world. The council members are wary because of the legend of the Knights of the Iron Dagger, a fanatical order dedicated to destroying everything magical. When Marnie rashly bets all of her family's magic on the success of the program, the council agrees, but if she cannot prove her point by midnight on Halloween, the entire Cromwell family will lose its powers.

The Halloweentown students arrive at Marnie's school disguised by magic as ordinary humans, and Marnie introduces them as exchange students from Canada. Aggie works as a substitute teacher so she can keep an eye on them, though she proves hopeless at teaching. At first the newcomers keep to themselves, hiding in a magical refuge Aggie creates inside a school locker, but Marnie gradually encourages them to join teams, take part in school activities and make friends. Meanwhile, she is drawn to Cody, a charming new student. When warnings appear that seem to come from the Knights of the Iron Dagger, Marnie must find out who is threatening the students and protect her family's magic before Halloween night ends.

The film emphasizes tolerance, acceptance and the idea that differences need not divide people, framing its themes within a lighthearted high school comedy.

Halloweentown High premiered on Disney Channel on October 8, 2004, and drew more than 6 million viewers on its premiere. It was followed by a fourth film, Return to Halloweentown, in 2006.

title: The Final
tagline: This lesson can't be learned in the classroom.
overview: A group of high school outcasts get revenge on the students that torment them.
plot:
The Final is a 2010 American independent psychological horror thriller film directed by Joey Stewart and written by Jason Kabolati. It stars Marc Donato, Jascha Washington, Justin S. Arnold, Lindsay Seidel, Julin, Laura Ashley Samuels, Ryan Hayden and Travis Tedford, and was released as part of the After Dark Horrorfest series.

A disfigured teenage girl walks into a diner, drawing stares from the customers, and begins to cry as the story unfolds in flashback. At a high school, a group of outcasts suffers relentless cruelty from the popular students: Ravi is bullied by Bradley and Bernard, Emily is tormented by Heather, Bridget and Kelli, and the quiet Dane, who has inherited a secluded house in the woods from his late uncle, is also a target. The only popular student who treats them decently is Kurtis, an aspiring actor who stands up to Bradley after the bullies break Ravi's camera at a video shoot.

Emily, Jack, Ravi, Andy and Dane decide to take revenge and send a message to their community, inspired by horror films and historical torture methods. They intend to spare Kurtis. They host a costume party at Dane's house, invite their tormentors and drug the punch, and the guests wake to find themselves chained together. The outcasts announce that rather than killing them, they will make them suffer a fate worse than death by disfiguring them so they will live with the scars for the rest of their lives.

The torture begins as Bernard is pierced with needles and Emily burns Heather's face with a corrosive compound. Bridget, forced to choose between mutilating Bradley and suffering herself, loses two fingers and half her face. Ravi, uneasy with the violence, secretly frees Kurtis and is stabbed to death by the increasingly unhinged Dane. Kurtis seeks help, but a deputy who comes to his aid is shot, and an elderly war veteran living nearby investigates alone, triggering a trap but killing two of the outcasts' accomplices. Dane paralyzes Bradley with a switchblade. Kurtis returns to the house, kills Andy and is wounded by Dane before Emily kills Dane. Emily then has Jack shoot her, and as police storm the house, Jack takes his own life after warning that there are more like them.

In the aftermath, news reports describe the torture of the popular students as an attack without reason, and the disfigured girl in the diner is revealed to be Bridget. The film received largely negative reviews, holding a 13% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from a small sample of critics.

title: The Back-Up Plan
tagline: Fall in love, get married, have a baby. Not necessarily in that order.
overview: When Zoe tires of looking for Mr. Right, she decides to have a baby on her own. But on the day she's artificially inseminated, she meets Stan, who seems to be just who she's been searching for all her life. Now, Zoe has to figure out how to make her two life's dreams fit with each other.
plot:
The Back-up Plan, previously known as Plan B, is a 2010 American romantic comedy film directed by Alan Poul in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Kate Angelo. It stars Jennifer Lopez, in her first film in three years, alongside Alex O'Loughlin, Eric Christian Olsen, Anthony Anderson and Linda Lavin, and it was the last film featuring Tom Bosley before his death. Shot in Los Angeles beginning in May 2009, it was released in the United States by CBS Films on April 23, 2010.

Having given up on finding the man of her dreams, Zoe decides to become a single mother and undergoes artificial insemination. That same day she meets Stan when they both try to hail the same taxi, and after running into him twice more, at a farmers market and at a book signing, she agrees to go on a no-strings date with him. Unsure whether she is pregnant, and whether she should tell him, Zoe keeps seeing Stan, enduring a disastrous romantic dinner in a garden before learning that the insemination has worked just as he invites her to spend the weekend at his farm. When she finally tells him the truth, Stan is confused and angry, but he soon decides that he still wants to be with her. A visit to the doctor reveals that Zoe is carrying twins, and the couple must learn to navigate an unusual relationship in which the pregnancy comes before the romance. Stan, overwhelmed, finds a sympathetic friend at a children's playground, while Zoe finds little support from her single mothers' group once its members learn that she is no longer single. As the pregnancy progresses through a series of comic mishaps and misunderstandings, Zoe struggles to trust that Stan is really prepared to raise children who are not biologically his, and a chance encounter with his ex-girlfriend threatens to drive them apart just as the babies' arrival draws near, at the same time as her grandmother prepares for her own wedding.

The Back-up Plan received negative reviews; critics generally praised Lopez's performance but faulted the generic script. On Rotten Tomatoes, 17% of 150 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 34 out of 100. It was nevertheless a commercial success, grossing about $77 million worldwide against a $35 million budget and becoming CBS Films' highest-grossing film at the time.

title: The Losers

overview: On a mission deep in the Bolivian jungle, a team of elite commandos finds itself on the receiving end of a lethal betrayal. Now presumed dead, the men join forces with a mysterious operative named Aisha to hunt down their enemy and even the score.
plot:
The Losers is a 2010 action-comedy film directed by Sylvain White and written by Andy Diggle and Stephen Levenson, based on the comic book series of the same name by Robert Venditti.

The movie begins with a group of mercenaries, known as The Losers, who are hired for various missions. They consist of Jake (Jeffrey Dean Morgan), Aimee (Zoe Saldana), Ms. Bishop (Isla Fisher), and Chip (Chris Evans). However, their latest mission goes awry when they discover that the target is a group of innocent civilians.

The team manages to escape with their lives but not without being betrayed by their employer, Max (Idris Elba). The Losers are left with no choice but to take revenge on Max and his organization. They hatch a plan to infiltrate Max's headquarters and gather evidence of his wrongdoing.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Jake's troubled past, which is revealed to be connected to his relationship with Aimee. The team faces numerous challenges as they work together to complete their mission. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including henchmen, traps, and double-crosses.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities are showcased through their interactions and banter. Ms. Bishop's sarcastic wit and Chip's awkwardness provide comedic relief, while Aimee's tough exterior hides a vulnerable side. Jake's leadership is put to the test as he tries to keep his team together and focused on their goal.

As the final showdown approaches, The Losers face off against Max and his henchmen in an intense battle. The film culminates with a thrilling sequence of action and suspense, where the team uses their skills and teamwork to take down their enemies.

In the end, The Losers succeed in their mission, but not without sacrifices. Jake's past is revealed to be connected to Max's organization, and Aimee's true loyalties are called into question. The film concludes with a sense of closure for the characters, as they part ways, forever changed by their experiences.

Overall, The Losers is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of loyalty, trust, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the comic book series and action movies will likely enjoy this thrilling ride.

title: Predators
tagline: The hunt is on.
overview: A group of cold-blooded killers find themselves trapped on an alien planet to be hunted by extraterrestrial Predators.
plot:
Predators is a 2010 science fiction action film directed by Nimród Antal and produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie serves as a reboot of the Predator franchise, ignoring the events of the previous films.

The story begins with Royce (Adrien Brody), a former Special Forces operative who has lost his way after a traumatic event in his past. He is hired by a wealthy client to lead an elite team of mercenaries on a mission to retrieve a valuable artifact from the remote jungles of South America. The team consists of Noland (Topher Grace), a skilled sniper; Stans (Lawrence Fishburne), a seasoned soldier; Mombasa (Alice Braga), a Brazilian mercenary; and Cuchillo (Danny Trejo), a Mexican fighter.

Upon arrival, the team discovers that they are not alone in the jungle. They soon realize that they are being hunted by a technologically advanced alien species known as the Yautja, also referred to as Predators. The Yautja are skilled warriors who have been hunting humans for sport and scientific study.

As the team tries to survive and escape the jungle, they discover that each member of their group has a unique skillset that makes them vulnerable to the Yautja's tactics. Noland is forced to confront his own demons when he discovers that one of his teammates is being hunted by the aliens. Meanwhile, Stans becomes increasingly paranoid and aggressive as the situation spirals out of control.

Throughout the film, Royce begins to realize that the team's only hope for survival lies in understanding the Yautja's motivations and weaknesses. He also starts to uncover clues about the artifact they were hired to retrieve, which may hold the key to their escape.

As the body count rises, the team is forced to work together to take down the Yautja. In a thrilling climax, Royce faces off against the leader of the Yautja, Isabelle (Alice Braga's character), who has been hunting him throughout the film. The final confrontation takes place in an ancient temple deep within the jungle, where Royce uses his wits and combat skills to outsmart the Yautja.

In the end, only a few members of the team manage to escape the jungle alive, including Royce and Stans. As they emerge from the jungle, they are met with a surprise: the artifact they were hired to retrieve is actually a device that can track and locate other Predators. The film ends on a cliffhanger, setting up the possibility for future adventures in the Predator franchise.

Overall, Predators offers a fresh take on the Predator franchise, exploring themes of survival, teamwork, and the psychological effects of being hunted by an alien species. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film has developed a loyal fan base over the years, and its action-packed sequences and suspenseful plot have made it a staple of the sci-fi genre.

plot:
Nanny McPhee and the Big Bang, released in North America as Nanny McPhee Returns, is a 2010 British period fantasy comedy directed by Susanna White and written by Emma Thompson, based on Christianna Brand's Nurse Matilda books. A sequel to Nanny McPhee (2005), it stars Thompson in the title role, with Maggie Gyllenhaal, Ralph Fiennes, Rhys Ifans, Ewan McGregor, Asa Butterfield and Maggie Smith.

During the Second World War, Isabel Green is struggling to run the family farm and work in the village shop of the scatterbrained Mrs. Docherty while her husband, Rory, is away fighting. Her three unruly children, Norman, Megsie and Vincent, are joined by their spoiled, snobbish cousins from London, Cyril and Celia, who have been sent to the country for safety, and the children's fighting soon drives Isabel to despair. The magical Nanny McPhee arrives and, with her unusual methods, teaches the children to stop fighting and to share, and gradually the cousins learn to work together.

Meanwhile Rory's brother Phil, who has gambled away his half of the farm and is pursued by two hired assassins sent by the casino owner Mrs. Biggles, schemes to make Isabel sell her share. His plots, including releasing the piglets she plans to sell, are foiled by the children. Then Phil delivers a telegram announcing that Rory has been killed in action. Only Norman refuses to believe it, and Nanny McPhee takes him and Cyril to the War Office in London, where Cyril's cold, distant father, Lord Gray, holds a senior post. Confronted by his son about his neglect and his impending divorce, Lord Gray discovers that Rory is only missing and that no telegram was ever sent; Phil had forged it.

At home, the other children try to delay Isabel's signing of Phil's papers, until a German plane accidentally drops a huge bomb into the barley field. It fails to explode, but the impact spills ink across the contract. When Mr. Docherty faints while trying to defuse the bomb, Megsie completes the task with the others' help. Nanny McPhee helps harvest the barley with a touch of magic, and Mrs. Docherty is revealed to be the baby Agatha from the first film. As Nanny McPhee departs, Rory returns, wounded but alive.

The film opened at number one in the United Kingdom and grossed about $93 million worldwide against a $35 million budget. It received generally positive reviews, with some critics finding it an improvement on the first film, and Metacritic gave it 52 out of 100.

title: Cracks
tagline: Innocence isn't lost. It's taken.
overview: Jealousy flares after the headmistress of an elite boarding school for girls becomes obsessed with a new student.
plot:
Cracks is a 2009 independent psychological drama directed by Jordan Scott in her feature debut, adapted by Scott, Ben Court and Caroline Ip from Sheila Kohler's 1999 novel. Eva Green stars as the charismatic teacher Miss G, with Juno Temple, María Valverde and Imogen Poots as her students. Ridley and Tony Scott served as executive producers, and the film was shot mostly in County Wicklow, Ireland. It was released in the United Kingdom and Ireland on 4 December 2009, and in the United States by IFC Films in March 2011.

In the 1930s, at St. Mathilda's, a strict and isolated British boarding school, a clique of girls on the diving team idolises their glamorous instructor, Miss G, herself a former pupil of the school. She tells them thrilling stories of travels and adventures abroad and encourages them to embrace desire and freedom. Di Radfield, the team captain and leader of the dormitory, is fiercely devoted to her and enjoys her status as Miss G's favourite.

The arrival of Fiamma Corona, a beautiful and sophisticated aristocratic girl from Spain, disrupts the group. Miss G becomes infatuated with Fiamma, who in turn is disturbed by the teacher's increasingly obvious advances and sees through the falsehoods she tells about her past. Jealous of the attention Fiamma receives, Di turns the other girls against her and makes her life miserable. Meanwhile, a trip to a nearby village reveals Miss G's secret: she suffers from severe agoraphobia when outside the school grounds, and the exotic adventures she recounts are stories borrowed from books, since she has hardly ever left the school since childhood. As the bullying escalates and Miss G's obsession with Fiamma becomes more dangerous, a night of manipulation and cruelty leads to tragedy, forcing Di to confront the truth about the woman she has worshipped.

The film explores adolescent desire, jealousy and the dangers of idolising adults, and it offers a study of the closed, hierarchical world of a girls' boarding school. Its period setting and lush cinematography contrast with the darkness of the story.

Cracks received a mixed reception. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a score of about 45 percent, with the consensus describing it as atmospheric but formless, while Metacritic assigned it 54 out of 100. Eva Green's performance was frequently praised.

title: Starstruck
overview: Pop star Christopher Wilde has fame, fortune and a big-budget Hollywood movie awaiting him. But after meeting Jessica Olson, a down-to-earth girl from the Midwest, he is faced with following his heart or doing what's best for his career.
plot:
Starstruck, stylized as StarStruck, is a 2010 American teen musical drama television film starring Sterling Knight as pop idol Christopher Wilde, alongside Danielle Campbell, Brandon Mychal Smith, Chelsea Kane and Maggie Castle. It premiered as a Disney Channel Original Movie on February 14, 2010, and was shot on location in Los Angeles in 2009.

Jessica Olson, a teenager from Kalamazoo has little patience for her older sister Sara's obsession with teen heartthrob Christopher Wilde. During a spring break visit to their grandmother in Hollywood, Sara drags Jessica along on her quest to meet the star. Christopher, meanwhile, is close to landing a major movie role, but the director is wary of his growing reputation as a "spoiled punk" who brawls with paparazzi, so he promises to stay out of the tabloids. When the sisters sneak into a birthday party for his model girlfriend Alexis Bender, Christopher, slipping out unnoticed, accidentally knocks Jessica down with an exit door. He takes her to a hospital to check for a concussion, then to his Beverly Hills mansion, and after the paparazzi pick up his trail, Jessica lets him hide in her grandmother's garage. The next day she recognizes him in disguise on a Malibu beach, and the two spend the day exploring Los Angeles, escaping photographers and stranding her grandmother's car in a mud pit. Christopher admits he enjoys being with someone who sees him as a person rather than a celebrity, but when they nearly kiss, he panics about being recognized and tells her no one can ever know about their day together. When photos of the pair surface, his parents, who also serve as his managers, persuade him to dismiss Jessica as just a fan, leaving her branded a liar by the media back home. Encouraged by his best friend Stubby to make his own choices, Christopher must decide whether his career matters more than the girl who liked him for himself.

The premiere drew 6.0 million viewers, making it Disney Channel's most-watched February original movie premiere, and 987,000 viewers watched its UK and Ireland premiere in May 2010. The soundtrack, released by Walt Disney Records, peaked at number 23 on the Billboard 200; most of its songs are sung by Drew Ryan Scott rather than Knight.

title: Lady Chatterley's Lover
tagline: The most notorious novel of the century.
overview: A film adaptation of D.H. Lawrence's novel. After a crippling injury leaves her husband impotent, Lady Chatterly is torn between her love for her husband and her physical desires. With her husband's consent, she seeks out other means of fulfilling her needs.
plot:
Lady Chatterley's Lover is a 1981 erotic romantic drama directed by Just Jaeckin and adapted from D. H. Lawrence's 1928 novel of the same name. Sylvia Kristel stars as Lady Constance Chatterley and Nicholas Clay as the gamekeeper Oliver Mellors, with Shane Briant as Sir Clifford Chatterley, Ann Mitchell as Ivy Bolton and Elizabeth Spriggs as Lady Eva; Anthony Head and Bessie Love appear in smaller roles.

Constance, known as Connie, has only recently married Sir Clifford, a baronet, when a wound suffered in the Great War leaves him paralysed and impotent. She remains devoted to him but is tormented by her own physical longings, and Clifford not only consents to her finding satisfaction elsewhere but encourages it, even to the extent of having her bear him an heir by another man. One day Connie secretly watches Mellors washing outside his hut and is immediately drawn to him. When she later visits him openly, he resents her intrusion, conscious of the gulf in class between a labourer and an aristocrat. On a further visit, made on the pretext of seeing some newly hatched birds, she breaks down in tears at the sight of them; Mellors tenderly holds her, and the two begin an affair.

Their physical relationship deepens into love, and both come to want her to have his child. Sir Clifford, meanwhile, grows suspicious. After a number of secret meetings, the lovers decide that Connie will spend a whole night at Mellors' cottage. That night Clifford painfully hauls himself up the stairs to her bedroom and finds it empty, and he is waiting for her when she returns at dawn. Outraged that his wife has given herself to a man of the lower classes, he sends her away to Venice and dismisses Mellors. Discovering that she is pregnant, Connie tries to return to her husband, but Clifford rejects her, refusing to accept a commoner's child as his heir. She stays on at the house while Mellors waits for his divorce from his first wife, who is never seen.

The film was produced by Cannon Films, with Yoram Globus as executive producer. Ken Russell, who had once hoped to film the novel himself, predicted a glossy romp, and Kristel complained about the label of soft pornography that had followed her since Emmanuelle. Accounts differ on its finances: one report in 1982 claimed it had already recouped its costs, while another source says Cannon recorded a loss. It later grew more popular on home video and through late-night showings on cable channels such as Cinemax and Showtime.

title: The Last Song
tagline: A story about family, first love, second chances and the moment in life that lead you back home.
overview: A drama centered on a rebellious girl who is sent to a Southern beach town for the summer to stay with her father. Through their mutual love of music, the estranged duo learn to reconnect.
plot:
Following her parents’ divorce three years ago, 17-year-old Veronica "Ronnie" Miller has shown rebellious and defiant behavior. She has not spoken to her father, Steve, since the divorce, and has given up playing piano, which she loved since childhood because of her father’s influence.
Ronnie and her younger brother, Jonah, travel to Georgia to spend the summer with their father, a former Juilliard professor and concert pianist who now lives quietly in his hometown of Wrightsville Beach.
Upon arrival, Ronnie befriends Blaze, an outcast who lives with her boyfriend Marcus. That night, Marcus makes advances towards Ronnie. Blaze, mistakenly believing Ronnie had initiated the flirting, vengefully frames her for shoplifting.
Later, Ronnie discovers a loggerhead sea turtle nest by her dad's house. While protecting it from raccoons, she meets Will Blakelee, a charming and popular aquarium volunteer whose attempts at friendship she had initially rebuffed. After spending the whole night defending the eggs together, she finds herself intrigued by him.
The next day, Will takes Ronnie to the aquarium. Upon learning that he has an extensive dating history, furious, she tries to break it off with him, but he kisses her passionately. Will takes Ronnie to the large, gated mansion he lives, where she meets his parents and sister, whom he assumed were away. After Will confides that his brother died recently, he and Ronnie profess their mutual love.
At Will’s volleyball game, Ronnie overhears locals discussing a church that burned down, hinting that Steve was responsible for the fire. When Ronnie later laments this to Will, he urges his best friend Scott to divulge the truth about what happened, but Scott refuses.
While Will, Ronnie, Jonah, and Steve are watching the turtle eggs hatch, Steve collapses so they rush him to the hospital. There, Ronnie and Jonah learn that their father has terminal cancer, which has spread to his lungs. Ronnie stays with Steve in the hospital, while Jonah and Will return home to continue rebuilding the stained-glass window to replace one lost in the fire. As Steve’s cancer progresses, he eventually requests hospice.
Eventually, Scott and Will confess to Steve that the church had accidentally ignited while they and their other friends were playing with fire behind it; they allowed Steve to accept the blame. Steve opts not to relay the truth to law enforcement, but Ronnie breaks up with Will, horrified that he has allowed her father to carry the guilt for so long.
Ronnie and Jonah’s mother Kim arrives to take Jonah back home to New York City, while Ronnie stays in Georgia to take care of Steve and make up for lost time with him. Because his hands are aching, she continues working on a composition he has written, titled "For Ronnie." He listens to her play and dies just as she finishes.

title: Pola X
tagline: An erotically charged descent into madness.
overview: A writer leaves his upper-class life and journeys with a woman claiming to be his sister, and her two friends.
plot:
Pierre lives a carefree life with his widowed mother in a Normandy chateau, enjoying rising fame as a pseudonymous author. He also visits Lucie, his fiancée and childhood friend, at her parents' chateau. In a bar he sees his cousin Thibault, a stockbroker, who says he is welcome to stay at Thibault's apartment in Paris but wonders why Pierre is being followed by a young vagrant woman. When Pierre turns to look, the woman runs away.
Driving through the forest, Pierre is disturbed to see the vagrant woman, who resembles a ghostly figure from his dreams. She tells him in a strong foreign accent that she is his half-sister Isabelle and recounts her unhappy life. She and her two companions (a Romanian woman, Razerka, and a small girl) are apparently refugees from conflict in Eastern Europe.
Abandoning his home, mother and fiancée, Pierre takes Isabelle to Paris. Trying to find Thibault, a cab driver refuses to take them any further and says that the girls stink. When they finally find Thibault, he bitterly insists he does not recognise Pierre and throws them out. Wandering the streets of Paris, fearful of deportation, the group find a cheap hotel. Pierre rejects his previous ideas for a second novel in favour of a grittier, more mature work that reflects the hidden truths of life. His publisher warns that his sophomoric pursuit of harsh truths will result in affected and inferior work compared to the youthful innocence that comes naturally to him, and refuses his request for an advance.
At the zoo, Pierre tells the small girl that to animals all humans stink. After the small girl subsequently starts telling random people in the street that they stink, a man viciously slaps her and she falls, hitting her head. She dies the next day. Again fearful of deportation, Pierre, Isabelle, and Razerka leave the girl's body and proceed to a run-down warehouse where a strange para-military group training for guerrilla warfare and rehearsing industrial music. Apparently in exchange for chaperoning Razerka safely to a man she knows there, Pierre and Isabelle are given lodging with the group. Pierre and Isabelle initially sleep separate but eventually succumb to the incestuous passion that had been coalescing between them.
Broke, Pierre tries to write his second novel, punctuated by learning of his mother's death while riding his father's motorcycle. Against the wishes of Thibault, Lucie finds Pierre at the warehouse and demands to stay there without revealing her past relationship to Pierre to Isabelle. Although she suffers from a fever and the harshness of their life in the cold warehouse, she accepts Pierre's disappearance and relationship with Isabelle and does not ask any questions. Isabelle offers to take care of Lucie during her periods of sickness, but both women suffer in silence.

title: Boogie
tagline: Based on the work of the great Fontanarrosa.
overview: Hoping to make some money, Boogie, a violent and ruthless assassin, kidnaps a witness a mafia boss wants dead.
plot:
Boogie (Boogie, el aceitoso) is an Argentine adult animated action thriller and black comedy of 2009 directed by Gustavo Cova and based on Boogie the Oily, the ruthless hitman created by the cartoonist Roberto Fontanarrosa. Pablo Echarri voices Boogie and Nancy Dupláa voices Marcia, with Nicolás Frías as the rival assassin Blackburn and Rufino Gallo as the mob boss Sonny Calabria. It was the first 3D animated feature made in Argentina and in Latin America.

In a bar, Boogie meets Marcia, the girlfriend of the mafia boss Sonny Calabria, who asks him whether he finds her attractive; Boogie rudely tells her she is fat and walks away. Some time later Calabria goes on trial, threatened by a mysterious witness whose testimony could convict him. His people try to hire Boogie to eliminate the witness, but balking at his fee, they give the job to Blackburn, a competing killer, instead. Furious at being passed over, Boogie decides to kidnap the witness himself and force Calabria to pay. The witness turns out to be Marcia, who slimmed down after Boogie's insult, only for Calabria, who prefers heavier women, to leave her for someone else.

Marcia falls for her apparent rescuer despite his constant brutality and coldness, until she discovers what he really intends. She tries to escape, but Boogie recaptures her and negotiates her handover to Calabria. After the exchange, however, he begins to feel guilty and goes back to rescue her, then races across the country to deliver her to the courtroom where her testimony is awaited. During the trial Calabria's lawyer tries to kill Marcia, and Boogie shoots him first. Sonny calls in a horde of hitmen who have infiltrated the court, and Boogie starts gunning them down. Marcia, who until then had recoiled from his violence, grabs two of his guns and joins in, finishing by shooting Calabria for abandoning her. Seeing her armed and covered in blood, Boogie falls in love with her. Three months later Marcia writes that she has not heard from him and imagines him in some war zone doing what he does best. In the final scene Boogie is indeed on a battlefield as a mercenary, pointing his rifle at the camera and promising there is some for the audience too.

Fontanarrosa read and edited an early draft of the script before his death, and the producers at Illusion Studios decided to carry on with the project. Released in October 2009, the film opened third at the Argentine box office, behind Surrogates and The Secret in Their Eyes.

title: Flash Point
tagline: They made it personal... He'll make them pay.
overview: Detective Sergeant Ma Jun, known for dispensing his own brand of justice during arrests, teams up with an undercover cop, Wilson, to try and bring down three merciless Vietnamese brothers running a smuggling ring in the months before mainland China's takeover of Hong Kong. Jun pursues the gang tirelessly, sometimes ignoring police protocols. A showdown is inevitable!
plot:
Flash Point (Chinese: 導火綫) is a 2007 Hong Kong action film directed by Wilson Yip and written by Szeto Kam-yuen and Nicholl Tang. Donnie Yen, who also produced and choreographed the action, stars as Sergeant Ma Jun, with Louis Koo as his undercover partner Wilson, Collin Chou, Ray Lui and Xing Yu as three Vietnamese gangster brothers, and Fan Bingbing. Although widely described as a prequel to SPL: Sha Po Lang (2005), Yip and Yen's earlier collaboration, Yen denied that the films were connected, and it is generally considered a standalone story.

The film is set in Hong Kong in the period before the territory's handover to China in 1997. Three brothers from Vietnam, Archer, Tony and Tiger, run a violent criminal operation and are negotiating a drug deal with a rival gang leader named Sam. Ma Jun is a hard-hitting detective with a reputation for injuring suspects, for which he has been repeatedly reprimanded. His partner Wilson has been planted inside the brothers' gang as a mole, and when Ma's team raids a nightclub, the two have to stage a fight to preserve Wilson's cover.

As the brothers grow increasingly ruthless, intimidating both their rivals and the elders of their own gang, Wilson foils an attempt by Tiger to kill Sam, and Sam agrees to testify against the brothers in court. The gang discovers Wilson's true identity, and he is badly wounded. With the trial approaching, the brothers set out to eliminate witnesses and take revenge on the officers who betrayed them, threatening Wilson's girlfriend Julie. Ma Jun, determined to protect Wilson and bring the brothers to justice, takes them on in a series of brutal confrontations, culminating in a long one-on-one fight with Tony in a village field.

Flash Point was praised for its action choreography, which blended traditional martial arts with mixed martial arts techniques such as grappling and submission holds, and its climactic fight between Yen and Chou is often cited as one of the finest in modern Hong Kong cinema. The film won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Action Choreography and was a commercial success in Asia.

title: Boa vs. Python
tagline: Get Ready To Rumble...
overview: After an overly ambitious businessman transports an 80-foot python to the United States, the beast escapes and starts to leave behind a trail of human victims. An FBI agent and a snake specialist come up with a plot to combat the creature by pitting it against a bioengineered, 70-foot boa constrictor. It's two great snakes that snake great together!
plot:
Boa vs. Python is a 2004 science fiction horror television film directed by David Flores from a script by Chase Parker and Sam Wells, filmed in Sofia, Bulgaria. A crossover between Python (2000) and New Alcatraz (2002, also known as Boa), it stars David Hewlett as a herpetologist, Jaime Bergman as a marine biologist, Kirk B.R. Woller as an FBI agent, Adamo Palladino, and Angel Boris Reed. It premiered on the Sci Fi Channel in 2004.

A wealthy casino owner named Broddick, who enjoys extreme entertainment, arranges for an enormous genetically engineered reticulated python to be smuggled into the United States from overseas. He plans to use the creature as the quarry in an illegal big-game hunt for his rich friends, another diversion for the ultra-wealthy. During transport through Pennsylvania, however, the snake awakens and becomes enraged. When the convoy stops so that a tranquilizer can be administered, the python smashes through the container, kills the men transporting it and escapes, surviving even the explosion meant to destroy it.

Broddick's hunt goes ahead, but the python, about 80 feet long and weighing several tons, proves far too powerful and kills several of his companions before slipping away into the countryside and heading for populated areas. An FBI agent turns for help to a brilliant but eccentric herpetologist who has bred and trained a giant boa constrictor, and to a marine biologist. Their plan is to release the boa, which is linked to them by a tracking implant, to hunt down the python. With the python leaving a trail of victims, and with Broddick and his hired hunters determined to take the kill themselves, the two giant snakes are drawn toward each other, leading to a climactic battle between the reptiles while the authorities try to prevent a catastrophe.

Boa vs. Python was panned by reviewers, who criticized its acting, special effects and story. It was described as a rip-off of Alien vs. Predator, released the same year, and as an attempt to capitalize on the popularity of Python. Reel Film gave it one and a half out of four stars, faulting its effects and its lack of satisfying action.

It is the sixth film in the Pokémon anime series and the first set during the Advanced Generation (Ruby and Sapphire) season, featuring Ash Ketchum, Pikachu and their friends May, Max and Brock. The Japanese voice cast includes Rica Matsumoto, Ikue Ōtani, Yūji Ueda, KAORI and Fushigi Yamada. Toho released it in Japan on 19 July 2003, accompanied by the short Gotta Dance, and Miramax distributed the English-language version direct to video in June 2004.

Once every thousand years, the Millennium Comet passes through the night sky for seven days, and the Mythical Pokémon Jirachi awakens from its long sleep to absorb its energy, which also brings life to the land of Forina where it rests. This time, a stage magician named Butler and his girlfriend Diane unearth the crystal encasing the sleeping Jirachi and take it away. Ash and his friends, meanwhile, arrive at a traveling festival held to celebrate the comet, where May buys a charm said to grant a wish if one panel is closed on each night the comet appears.

During one of Butler's magic shows, Max hears a voice coming from the crystal Diane is holding and meets Jirachi, which soon emerges and befriends him. Jirachi can grant wishes, but its powers are not quite as they seem. Butler, a former member of Team Magma, secretly plans to use Jirachi's energy to resurrect the legendary Groudon and prove his old theories correct. Max and his friends, joined by Absol, set out to take Jirachi safely back to Forina before its brief waking period ends, pursued by Butler and Team Rocket. Butler's experiment creates a monstrous false Groudon that begins absorbing everything around it, forcing Ash and Butler to work together to undo the damage while Max must prepare to say goodbye to his new friend.

The film was a box-office hit in Japan, earning ¥4.5 billion and becoming the country's second highest-grossing domestic film of the year. Its theme song in the Japanese version was "A Small Thing" by Asuca Hayashi, while the English version featured "Make a Wish" performed by Cindy Mizelle. The Jirachi featured in the film was distributed to players of the Pokémon games as a promotion.

title: Godzilla, Mothra and King Ghidorah: Giant Monsters All-Out Attack
original_title: ゴジラ・モスラ・キングギドラ大怪獣総進撃
tagline: The God of Destruction Godzilla lands in Japan!
overview: Godzilla has become a distant memory for Japan when the destruction of a US submarine raises alarms for Admiral Tachibana. His estranged daughter Yuri investigates the legend of the guardian monsters, who must rise to protect Japan against the vengeful spirits within Godzilla that seek to destroy both the nation and its people for the suffering they inflicted in the Pacific conflict.
plot:
In 2002, during a Japan Self-Defense Forces (JSDF) briefing for cadets regarding the first Godzilla's attack and death in 1954, Admiral Taizō Tachibana warns the trainees to remain vigilant. He notes that reports of monster sightings are increasing worldwide, including a similar monster that recently attacked New York City. Tachibana is then alerted that an American nuclear submarine has gone missing off Guam. Search-and-rescue units find the submarine destroyed and capture footage of an undead Godzilla's dorsal plates moving in the vicinity.
Meanwhile, Tachibana's daughter Yuri, a reporter working for the pseudo-documentary television company BS Digital Q, is filming with her crew at Mount Myōkō when an earthquake strikes. That night, another earthquake buries a group of bōsōzoku bikers who had vandalized a roadside shrine; the lone surviving trucker witnesses the subterranean monster Baragon emerge. The next day, Yuri's colleague, Mitsuaki Takeda, supports her theory that a monster may have caused the mysterious earthquakes and gives her a book about Japan's legendary Guardian Monsters: Baragon (God of the Earth), Mothra (God of the Sea), and King Ghidorah (God of the Sky).
At Lake Ikeda, Mothra, in her larval form, attacks a group of teenage vandals who disturbed her shrine and spins a cocoon. Yuri interviews Professor Hirotoshi Isayama, a mysterious elder arrested by Motosu police for destroying a shrine. Unbeknownst to the authorities and Yuri's team, Isayama authored the Guardian Monsters book. He warns that the guardians must be awakened to prevent Godzilla from destroying Japan. Yuri and her colleagues visit the Guardian Monsters' shrine, where she finds a stone, then returns to continue interviewing Isayama. In the process, she discovers that the vengeful souls of soldiers and civilians who were killed during the Pacific War are embedded within Godzilla and are lashing out due to modern Japan's denial of its past crimes. Elsewhere, in Aokigahara, a suicidal man accidentally discovers a frozen, 1,000-year-old dragon, Ghidorah.
Godzilla surfaces in Yaizu and battles Baragon in Hakone, killing the smaller guardian. Yuri is injured during the fray and goes on her own after Takeda refuses to take her to Godzilla's location. When the JSDF's jets fail to stop Godzilla's course toward Tokyo, Tachibana sets up a defensive line in Yokohama. As Mothra emerges from her cocoon in her imago form, Isayama awakens Ghidorah to combat Godzilla. However, Godzilla overpowers both guardians and attempts to attack the JSDF soldiers. Mothra sacrifices herself, transferring her spirit to Ghidorah. The empowered dragon injures and drags Godzilla underwater. Amidst this, Tachibana and his colleague Yutaka Hirose board miniature Satsuma submarines to launch D-03 missiles into Godzilla's wound.
As the battle continues, the Yokohama Bay Bridge collapses under Godzilla's atomic breath while Yuri and Takeda are reporting from it.

title: After.Life
tagline: Life is the symptom. Death is the cure.
overview: Following a terrible car crash, a woman awakes to find an enigmatic mortician preparing her for burial.
plot:
After.Life is a 2009 American psychological horror thriller film written and directed by Agnieszka Wójtowicz-Vosloo. Liam Neeson stars as a mysterious funeral director, with Christina Ricci as a young woman in his care and Justin Long as her boyfriend. It premiered in November 2009.

Eliot Deacon, a softly spoken funeral director in a small town, talks gently to the bodies he prepares for burial. Anna Taylor, an unhappy middle school teacher, meets him at the funeral of her old piano teacher. That night, after a bitter argument with her boyfriend, Paul, at a restaurant, she drives off in distress and crashes her car. She wakes on a table in Eliot's mortuary as he cuts away her clothes. He tells her that she is dead and that he has a gift that allows him to hear the dead and help them make the transition to the afterlife, and he injects her with a drug that he says will relax her muscles and prevent rigor mortis.

Over the following days, Anna veers between disbelief and despair. She tries repeatedly to escape and at one point reaches Paul by telephone, but he hangs up, believing it a prank. Eliot tells her that she was never truly living anyway and must let go of life, and when he shows her reflection, her pale, corpse-like appearance convinces her that she has died. Meanwhile, Paul, denied permission to see her body, grows suspicious, especially after one of Anna's students, Jack, claims to have seen her alive at the funeral home. At the police station, Paul learns of a drug that can mimic death by causing paralysis. Eliot tells Jack that they share a special gift.

Before her funeral, Anna asks to see herself once more and notices her breath fogging the mirror, realizing that Eliot has lied to her, but he sedates her again. At the funeral, Paul places on her finger the engagement ring he had planned to give her on the night of the accident. Afterward, as Anna wakes inside her coffin while it is being buried, Eliot goads the drunken Paul into going to the cemetery. Paul appears to reach her and they embrace, but he is suddenly back on Eliot's table. Eliot tells him he died in a car crash on the way, and as Paul insists that he is alive, Eliot begins to embalm him.

After.Life was poorly received by critics, who found its premise intriguing but felt it lacked thrills and tension; Rotten Tomatoes reported 24% approval.

title: The Prince & Me 4: The Elephant Adventure
original_title: The Prince & Me 4: The Elephant Adventure
overview: One year after their royal wedding, King Edvard and Queen Paige of Denmark receive an invitation to attend the wedding of Princess Myra of Sangyoon. Upon their arrival, Paige finds Myra is unhappy with her arranged marriage to the brooding and sinister Kah and is secretly in love with a young elephant handler named Alu.
plot:
The Prince & Me: The Elephant Adventure, also known as The Prince & Me 4 and shown on television as The Prince & Me 4: Royal Adventures in Paradise, is a 2010 American romantic adventure comedy directed by Catherine Cyran and released direct-to-video by Millennium Films on March 23, 2010. The fourth film in the series and a sequel to The Prince & Me 3: A Royal Honeymoon, it stars Kam Heskin as Paige Morgan and Chris Geere as Edvard, with Jonathan Firth as their aide Søren, Selina Lo, Ase Wang, Prinya Intachai, Vithaya Pansringarm and Amarin Cholvibul.

A year after their royal wedding, King Edvard and Queen Paige of Denmark, who still practises medicine, are celebrating their first anniversary when they travel to the fictional Asian kingdom of Sangyoon for the wedding of Princess Myra, daughter of King Saryu. On arriving, Paige quickly realizes that Myra is desperately unhappy about her arranged marriage to Kah, a brooding, ambitious and bullying factory owner, and that she is secretly in love with Alu, a young stable hand who looks after the royal elephant. When the romance is revealed, Alu is thrown into prison, and after an altercation between Myra and Kah the sacred elephant needed for the wedding ceremony runs off into the jungle. The king postpones the wedding for two days until the animal is returned.

Determined to save Myra, Paige and Edvard set out through the jungle with Rayen, a tough, highly educated guide and bodyguard who proves a skilled fighter. Their journey brings them chases by armed men, a kidnapping, a fight in a dark cave and a contest with bamboo sticks to settle a dispute, as well as an encounter with a remote and oppressed village whose people are falling increasingly ill, a problem Paige realizes she unwittingly helped to create. To rescue the princess, the couple must find the elephant, free Alu and convince the king of Sangyoon that true love matters more than tradition, while Edvard hopes to use diplomacy to bring aid to the kingdom's poor and sick.

Rated PG, the film runs 93 minutes. Common Sense Media found it a so-so sequel, praising its exotic setting, its more diverse cast and the character of Rayen, but criticizing the uneven acting, stock characters, negative stereotypes about the locals and an implied need for Western saviours. The blog Dan's Movie Report thought the opening slow but enjoyed the scenery, costumes and family-friendly adventure, singling out Selina Lo's energetic performance as Rayen.

title: Casino Royale
tagline: Everyone has a past. Every legend has a beginning.
overview: Le Chiffre, a banker to the world's terrorists, is scheduled to participate in a high-stakes poker game in Montenegro, where he intends to use his winnings to establish his financial grip on the terrorist market. plot:
Casino Royale is a 2006 spy film directed by Martin Campbell, produced by Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli, and written by Neal Purvis, Robert Wade, and Paul Haggis. The film is the 21st James Bond film and marks the beginning of Daniel Craig's tenure as the iconic secret agent.

The story begins with a young James Bond (Daniel Craig), who has just graduated from the Secret Intelligence Service training program. He is assigned to investigate a mysterious banker named Le Chiffre (Mads Mikkelsen), who is suspected of financing terrorism. Bond is given a small budget and a single objective: to defeat Le Chiffre in a high-stakes game of baccarat at the Casino Royale in Montenegro.

As Bond delves deeper into the world of espionage, he meets Vesper Lynd (Eva Green), a Treasury agent who has been assigned to work with him. The two begin a romantic relationship, which adds an element of complexity to Bond's mission. However, it becomes clear that Vesper is also working for MI6, and her true loyalties are unclear.

Bond's investigation leads him to Le Chiffre, who is revealed to be a former Soviet agent seeking revenge against the West. He plans to use the money he wins at the casino to fund his terrorist activities. Bond's mission becomes personal when he discovers that Vesper has been compromised by her employer and is working to sabotage his efforts.

As the game of baccarat reaches its climax, Bond faces off against Le Chiffre in a tense showdown. However, just as it seems Bond is about to emerge victorious, Vesper reveals that she has been playing him all along, using their relationship to manipulate him into losing the game. The film's ending is left open to interpretation, with some viewers believing Bond and Vesper will reunite, while others see her betrayal as a defining moment in Bond's character development.

The film's success can be attributed to its gritty realism, which marked a departure from the more lighthearted tone of previous Bond films. Daniel Craig's performance as Bond was widely praised for its intensity and vulnerability, setting the stage for his iconic portrayal of the character. The film's themes of loyalty, betrayal, and redemption added depth to the franchise, making it a standout entry in the series.

Overall, Casino Royale is a gripping spy thriller that sets the tone for Daniel Craig's tenure as James Bond. Its complex characters, tense plot twists, and realistic action sequences make it a must-see for fans of the franchise.

Blade (Wesley Snipes) has been tracking a series of mysterious murders in Los Angeles, which seem to be connected to an ancient vampire virus that is spreading rapidly across the city. The virus, known as the "Virus," is created by the Reapers, a group of vampires who have been infected with the virus and are now seeking to destroy humanity.

Blade soon discovers that the source of the Virus is a powerful and ancient vampire named Bloodsucker (Ron Perlman), who has been awakened from his centuries-long slumber. As Blade delves deeper into the mystery of the Virus, he teams up with a group of scientists, including Dr. Karen Jenson (Leigh Whannell), who are working on a cure for the virus. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Bloodsucker and his minions from spreading the Virus further.

Meanwhile, Blade also encounters a new ally in the form of Nyssa (Jessica Biel), a vampire hunter who is determined to help him defeat Bloodsucker. As they work together, Blade begins to question whether he can truly trust Nyssa, as she seems to be hiding secrets about her own past.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between Blade and Bloodsucker, with the two engaging in a fierce and intense fight that takes them across the city. In the end, Blade emerges victorious, but not before realizing that the Virus has already spread too far, and that humanity is now at risk of being wiped out.

Throughout the movie, del Toro's direction brings a dark and gothic atmosphere to the film, with a focus on practical effects and makeup to create the vampires. The action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, making for an exciting and thrilling ride.

Overall, Blade II is a gripping and entertaining sequel that expands on the world of the first film while introducing new characters and plot twists. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

plot:
The World Is Not Enough is a 1999 action spy film directed by Michael Apted and starring Pierce Brosnan as James Bond. The movie marks the 19th installment in the James Bond series.

The film opens with a dramatic sequence showing a terrorist named Elektra King (Sophie Marceau) being kidnapped by a group of terrorists led by Renard (Robert Carlyle). The story then shifts to London, where Bond is sent to investigate the kidnapping. He soon discovers that Elektra's father, Alec Trevelyan (Sean Bean), has been killed in a car bombing.

Bond learns that Elektra's father was involved in a plot to sell nuclear warheads on the black market. The main villain, Renard, is revealed to be a former KGB agent who seeks revenge against Alec for his betrayal. As Bond delves deeper into the case, he discovers that Elektra is being held captive by Renard and his accomplices.

Bond's investigation leads him to a beautiful and mysterious woman named Wai Lin (Carrie-Anne Moss), an Australian intelligence officer who has been tracking Renard. Together, they form an alliance to take down Renard and rescue Elektra. Along the way, Bond also encounters a group of rogue Russian agents who are working with Renard.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Alec Trevelyan's death was not a random act of terrorism, but rather a deliberate move to distract from his true intentions. It is revealed that Alec had discovered Renard's plan and was trying to stop him, but ultimately fell victim to his own betrayal.

Ending:
The film culminates in an action-packed sequence where Bond confronts Renard at the Elektra King's family estate in Scotland. In a thrilling finale, Bond faces off against Renard and his accomplices, leading to a dramatic showdown that results in Renard's demise.

In the aftermath of the battle, Bond is left shaken but unharmed. He also finds himself drawn to Wai Lin, who has become an ally and potential love interest. The film ends with Bond reflecting on the events that have transpired, as he sets his sights on his next mission.

Overall, The World Is Not Enough is a classic Bond film that delivers on action, suspense, and intrigue. With its complex plot twists and memorable characters, it has become a fan favorite in the James Bond franchise.

title: Blade
tagline: Part man. Part vampire. All hero.
overview: The Daywalker known as "Blade" - a half-vampire, half-mortal man - becomes the protector of humanity against an underground army of vampires.
plot:
Blade is a 1998 American superhero horror film directed by Stephen Norrington and starring Wesley Snipes as the titular character. The movie is based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name.

The story begins with a young Deacon Frost (played by Donald Sutherland), a vampire who seeks to bring about a blood war between humans and vampires. Frost, once a human, was turned into a vampire by the ancient vampire Thaddeus (played by Stephen Rea) and has since become one of the most powerful vampires in existence.

The movie then cuts to a young Blade (played by Wesley Snipes), who is revealed to be the son of Abraham Whistler (played by Ron Perlman), a human who was turned into a vampire by Thaddeus. However, Whistler's transformation was reversed when he drank his own blood, which contained a unique genetic marker that made him immune to vampirism.

As Blade grows up, he is trained by Abraham in the ways of combat and vampire hunting. He becomes a skilled warrior and sets out on a mission to track down Deacon Frost, who has escaped from a maximum-security prison.

Blade soon discovers that Frost plans to bring about a blood war between humans and vampires, which would result in the destruction of both species. Blade also learns that he is the last living heir of Abraham Whistler, making him the only one capable of stopping Frost's plan.

As Blade delves deeper into the world of vampires, he meets Nyssa Damaskinos (played by N'Bushe Wright), a vampire who becomes his ally and potential love interest. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Frost and prevent the blood war from occurring.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Blade and Deacon Frost, with the fate of humanity hanging in the balance. In the end, Blade emerges victorious, but not without sustaining significant injuries. The movie concludes with Blade standing watch over the city, ready to defend it against any future threats from vampires.

Throughout the film, Wesley Snipes delivers a memorable performance as Blade, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The movie's blend of action, horror, and humor helped establish the Blade franchise as a beloved part of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

Overall, Blade is a thrilling and entertaining ride that explores themes of identity, community, and the struggle between good and evil. With its unique blend of vampire lore and superhero elements, it has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

title: Blade: Trinity
tagline: The final hunt begins.
overview: For years, Blade has fought against the vampires in the cover of the night. plot:
Blade: Trinity is a 2004 American superhero horror film directed by David S. Goyer and starring Wesley Snipes as the titular character, Blade. The movie serves as the third installment in the Blade franchise.

The story begins with Blade (Wesley Snipes) living in New Orleans, where he has been hiding from his vampire-hunting duties for several years. He is approached by a mysterious woman named Abigail Whistler (Parker Posey), who claims to be working for a secret organization known as the Blood Gods. The Blood Gods are an ancient and powerful group of vampires who seek to bring about a new era of human-vampire coexistence.

Abigail reveals that she has been searching for Blade, believing him to be the key to unlocking the secrets of his father's past. She tells him that his father, Danica Talos (N'Bushe Wright), was a powerful vampire hunter who had discovered a way to harness the power of the Blood Gods. However, their plans were foiled by the leader of the Blood Gods, Deacon Frost (Dominic Purcell).

Deacon Frost is a charismatic and cunning vampire who seeks to use his newfound powers to bring about a new era of human-vampire coexistence. He believes that humans and vampires can live together in harmony, but only if they submit to the will of the Blood Gods.

title: Die Another Day
tagline: He's never been cooler.
overview: James Bond is sent to investigate the connection between a North Korean terrorist and a diamond mogul, who is funding the development of an international space weapon.
plot:
Die Another Day is a 2002 spy action film directed by Lee Tamahoni and produced by Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli, under the Eon Productions banner.

The movie begins with James Bond (played by Pierce Brosnan), who has been presumed dead after his last mission in Russia. However, he is actually being held captive by North Korean agents, led by the enigmatic and beautiful Gi (played by Kim Hye-ok). Gi is revealed to be a former lover of Bond's, who had faked her own death to escape from him.

Bond is eventually rescued by a British agent named Jinx Johnson (played by Halle Berry), who has been sent to extract him. However, their mission is compromised when they are ambushed by North Korean agents, and Bond is left for dead.

Meanwhile, in London, M (played by Judi Dench) informs Bond that he has been declared dead and that his replacement, a new 00 agent named Johnny English (played by Colin Farrell), will be taking over his duties. However, Bond soon discovers that this is not the case, as he receives a message from M, revealing that she has been kidnapped by North Korea.

Bond sets out on a mission to rescue M and uncover the truth behind Gi's betrayal. Along the way, he encounters a new villain, Zao (played by Rick Yune), who is revealed to be a skilled martial artist and assassin. Bond also meets a wealthy businessman named Gustav Graves (played by Toby Stephens), who is revealed to be working with North Korea.

As Bond delves deeper into the plot, he discovers that Gi has been working for Gustav, who plans to use a satellite-based laser system to hold the world hostage. The plan involves using the laser to destroy major cities around the world, and only Bond can stop it.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Bond and Zao, as well as a thrilling chase sequence through the streets of Seoul. In the end, Bond is able to defeat Gustav and Gi, and rescue M. The movie concludes with Bond reflecting on his past and his feelings for Gi, who has been revealed to be working against her own country.

Overall, Die Another Day was met with mixed reviews from critics, but it remains a popular entry in the James Bond franchise. The film's action sequences and visual effects were praised, while some critics felt that the plot was convoluted and the villainous characters underdeveloped.

title: Never Say Never Again
tagline: Sean Connery is James Bond 007
overview: James Bond returns as the secret agent 007 to battle the evil organization SPECTRE. Bond must defeat Largo, who has stolen two atomic warheads for nuclear blackmail. But Bond has an ally in Largo's girlfriend, the willowy Domino, who falls for Bond and seeks revenge.
plot:
After the MI6 agent James Bond fails a routine training exercise, his superior M sends him to a health clinic outside London to get back into shape. While there, Bond witnesses a nurse beating a male patient with a bandaged face. While the patient's eye is being scanned with a machine, she spots Bond and sends an assassin after him, whom he kills in a lengthy fight. An angry M is forced to pay for the damage the fight causes to the clinic, and he consequently suspends Bond from active duty.
The nurse is Fatima Blush, an agent of the criminal organisation SPECTRE, which is run by Ernst Stavro Blofeld. The man she was beating is Jack Petachi, a United States Air Force pilot who has undergone an operation on his eye to make it match the retinal pattern of the US President. He uses his altered retina to authorize the replacement of dummy warheads with live nuclear warheads in two cruise missiles. SPECTRE then steals the warheads, intending to extort billions of dollars from NATO. Blush covers up the crime by murdering Petachi.
M is ordered to reactivate the double-0 section, and Bond is tasked with tracking down the missing weapons. He follows a lead to the Bahamas and finds Domino Petachi, Jack's sister, and her wealthy lover Maximillian Largo, who is SPECTRE's top agent. Bond has sex with Blush aboard her boat, after which she tries to kill him. He then follows Largo's yacht to France, where he joins forces with his CIA ally Felix Leiter and his French contact Nicole. Posing as a masseur, Bond gives a massage to Domino, who reveals that Largo is hosting a charity event that evening. At the event, Bond beats Largo at a video game and wins money from him, but says he will accept a dance with Domino instead of a check. While dancing, Bond informs Domino that her brother was killed on Largo's orders.
Returning to his villa, Bond finds Nicole killed by Blush. He pursues her, but she captures him. She then demands that he declare in writing that she was his best sexual partner. Bond pulls out a pen to write, then shoots Blush with an explosive dart from the pen.
Bond boards Largo's yacht in search of the missing warheads. He finds Domino, and attempts to make Largo jealous by kissing her. Enraged, Largo traps Bond and takes him and Domino to Palmyra, his base of operations in North Africa. Largo punishes Domino for her betrayal by offering her to a group of men, but Bond escapes from captivity and rescues her.
Bond and Domino reunite with Leiter on a US Navy submarine. After the first warhead is found and defused in Washington, D.C., they track Largo to the Tears of Allah, a location on the coast. Bond and Leiter infiltrate the underground facility and a gun battle ensues between Leiter's team and Largo's men. Amidst the chaos, Largo flees with the second warhead. Bond catches and fights him underwater. As Largo is about to shoot Bond with a spear gun, Domino arrives and kills him. Bond defuses the warhead, then returns to the Bahamas with Domino.

title: Solitary Man
tagline: Ben loves his family almost as much as he loves himself
overview: A car magnate watches his personal and professional life hit the skids because of his business and romantic indiscretions.
plot:
Solitary Man is a 2009 American drama film directed by Allen Coulter and starring Michael Douglas. The movie follows the story of Ben Kalmen, a used car salesman who has spent his life chasing after women and making poor decisions.

At its core, Solitary Man explores themes of loneliness and isolation. Despite being surrounded by people, Ben's life is marked by emptiness and disconnection. He struggles to form meaningful relationships, often using his charm and good looks to manipulate those around him. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Ben's shallow existence has left him feeling unfulfilled and alone.

The film also delves into the consequences of a life of selfishness and poor decision-making. Ben's actions have hurt those he cares about, including his daughter, and he is forced to confront the damage he has caused. This serves as a catalyst for Ben's journey towards self-discovery and redemption.

Furthermore, Solitary Man touches on the theme of regret and the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions. As Ben navigates his way through life, he is confronted with the choices he has made and the opportunities he has missed. The film suggests that it's never too late to make amends and start anew, but this requires a willingness to confront one's past mistakes and take ownership of them.

Overall, Solitary Man is a poignant exploration of the human condition, highlighting the complexities and challenges of living a life of purpose and connection.

title: Naruto Shippuden the Movie: The Will of Fire
original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO -ナルト- 疾風伝 火の意志を継ぐ者
overview: Ninjas with bloodline limits begin disappearing in all the countries and blame points toward the fire nation. By Tsunade's order, Kakashi is sacrificed to prevent an all out war. After inheriting charms left by Kakashi, Naruto fights through friends and foes to prevent his death while changing the minds of those who've inherited the will of fire.
plot:
Naruto Shippuden the Movie: The Will of Fire is a 2009 Japanese animated martial arts fantasy film based on Masashi Kishimoto's manga and anime series. It is the sixth Naruto film and the third set during Naruto: Shippuden, taking place after episode 126 of the series.

With a fourth Great Ninja World War looming, ninjas with rare hereditary powers known as Kekkei Genkai have vanished from the Lands of Lightning, Earth, Water and Wind. Only the Land of Fire has been spared, so the other nations suspect it and gather armies on its borders. The Land of Fire's feudal lord orders Tsunade, the Fifth Hokage, to catch the real culprit and prove the Leaf Village's innocence. If she fails, he will destroy the village himself to preserve peace. The culprit is Hiruko, a rogue ninja and former comrade of the Legendary Sannin Tsunade, Jiraiya and Orochimaru. He left the village long ago after creating the Chimera Technique, which lets him absorb other ninjas' chakra and bloodline abilities. From his base on Mount Shumi, with his followers Ichi, Ni and San, he projects his image into the sky over the Leaf Village and announces that he will take the Land of Fire's Kekkei Genkai. He plans to use the power of a solar eclipse to become immortal, start the war and conquer the world.

His target is Kakashi Hatake's Sharingan. Hiruko activates a Puppet Curse he placed on Kakashi years earlier, and Kakashi asks Tsunade to put a seal on him that will trigger his Kamui ability if Hiruko tries to absorb him. He then leaves the village, and Tsunade publicly declares him a rogue ninja and forbids anyone to follow him. Naruto Uzumaki and Sakura Haruno set out anyway to rescue their teacher, and Teams 8, 10 and Guy are sent after them. With Sai, Naruto and Sakura defeat Hiruko's subordinates and reach his temple. During the eclipse, Kakashi's Mangekyō Sharingan distorts the absorption, and Naruto pulls him free with a barrage of Rasengan. Hiruko survives and summons a chimera beast, which the other teams defeat. Hiruko absorbs Kakashi's Raikiri and Naruto's giant Rasengan, but he cannot absorb Naruto's Wind Style: Rasenshuriken, which kills him. The ninjas celebrate at Mount Shumi, and Kishimoto adds a closing note.

The film opened in Japan on August 1, 2009, and Viz Media released it in North America on October 23, 2012. Anime News Network gave it a C+, praising its fluid action, background art and ties to the series but criticizing its formulaic story.

title: The Drawn Together Movie: The Movie!

plot:
The Drawn Together Movie: The Movie! is a 2010 American adult animated musical black comedy based on the Comedy Central sitcom Drawn Together. Written and executive produced by the show's creators, Dave Jeser and Matt Silverstein, produced by Richard Quan and directed by Greg Franklin, it was the first Drawn Together production after the series was cancelled. The film premiered at the South by Southwest festival in Austin in March 2010 and was released direct to home video in April 2010.

The film picks up after the show's cancellation. Foxxy Love discovers that she can suddenly swear without being bleeped and calls the network to find out why the series was taken off the air, learning that it was replaced by another animated show, a crude parody of South Park. The head of the network, who has always hated the series, discovers that the housemates are still alive, a fact the show's producer has hidden from him, and he summons I.S.R.A.E.L., a robot designed to erase cartoon characters, to wipe them out. The robot destroys the Drawn Together house and captures the producer, while the housemates escape in Foxxy's van.

Learning that they are not original creations but parodies of other cartoon characters, the housemates split up. Foxxy believes their survival depends on getting their show back on the air, while Princess Clara refuses to accept that she is not a real princess and insists that her father can protect them. Captain Hero, Xandir and Ling-Ling follow Clara, while Spanky Ham and Wooldoor Sockbat join Foxxy, and Toot Braunstein steals the van and drives off on her own. As I.S.R.A.E.L. pursues them across a series of animated worlds, the characters encounter grotesque creatures and parodies of famous animation styles, and they must reunite to confront the network and persuade it to give them another chance, perhaps in the form of a direct-to-DVD film.

Like the television series, the film relies on shock humour, satirical musical numbers and deliberately offensive jokes about race, sexuality and religion, while also mocking the television industry and the decision to cancel the show.

The film received negative reviews from critics. Common Sense Media awarded it one star, criticising it as filled to the brim with lewd sexual acts, language and violence, and arguing that its attempts to push the boundaries of taste overwhelmed whatever satire it contained.

title: You Don't Know Jack
tagline: Angel of mercy… or murderous “Doctor Death”?
overview: Controversy and legal problems follow Dr. Jack Kevorkian as he advocates assisted suicide.
plot:
You Don't Know Jack is a 2010 American television biographical film written by Adam Mazer and directed by Barry Levinson for HBO. Al Pacino stars as Jack Kevorkian, the Michigan pathologist and right-to-die activist dubbed "Dr. Death" by the press, with Brenda Vaccaro as his sister Margo Janus, John Goodman as his friend and medical technician Neal Nicol, Susan Sarandon as Janet Good, founder of a regional chapter of the Hemlock Society, and Danny Huston as his lawyer Geoffrey Fieger. It premiered on HBO in April 2010.

Moved by the case of David Rivlin, a quadriplegic man who went to court to be removed from his respirator, by the sight of a dying woman in a hospital and by the memory of his mother's painful death decades earlier, Kevorkian builds his first suicide machine, the "Mercitron," from parts bought at flea markets. The device allows a patient to self-administer, through an intravenous line, a harmless saline solution followed by drugs that induce a coma and then stop the heart. Because the drugs are expensive and difficult to obtain, he also develops a method using carbon monoxide. Rivlin, however, becomes agitated during their meeting, and he later dies after his respirator is removed and food and water are withheld. In an interview with the journalist Jack Lessenberry, Kevorkian condemns the cruelty of such a drawn-out death and begins offering his services as a "death counselor."

His first patient is Janet Adkins, a woman from Portland, Oregon, in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease, whose death in the back of his van in 1990 makes national headlines. Over the following years Kevorkian helps more than a hundred people end their lives, provoking outrage and admiration in equal measure. Fieger defends him in a series of trials, winning acquittals, while prosecutors, religious groups and medical authorities try to stop him. Increasingly determined to force a legal confrontation, Kevorkian videotapes himself directly administering a lethal injection to a man with ALS and allows it to be broadcast on 60 Minutes in 1998, leading to his conviction for second-degree murder.

The film received positive reviews, with an 83 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes praising Levinson's direction and Pacino's outstanding performance. Pacino won the Primetime Emmy Award and the Golden Globe Award for his portrayal, and the real Kevorkian attended the premiere.
