title: Dragon Ball Z: The History of Trunks
original_title: ドラゴンボールZ・絶望への反抗!!残された超戦士・悟飯とトランクス
tagline: This is the story of the future that never was.
overview: It has been thirteen years since the Androids began their killing rampage and Son Gohan is the only person fighting back. He takes Bulma's son Trunks as a student and even gives his own life to save Trunks's. Now Trunks must figure out a way to change this apocalyptic future
plot:
Dragon Ball Z: The History of Trunks is a Japanese anime television special based on Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball manga, adapted from a bonus chapter of the series. It originally aired in Japan on February 24, 1993, between episodes 175 and 176 of the Dragon Ball Z television series. The special depicts the bleak alternate future from which the time traveler Trunks came, showing how he and Gohan fought to survive against the Androids 17 and 18, two artificial beings created by Dr. Gero to destroy Goku.

In this timeline, Goku dies of a viral heart disease, and because his death is from natural causes, he cannot be revived with the Dragon Balls. Six months later, two androids appear and kill Earth's greatest fighters, including Piccolo, Vegeta, Krillin, Tien and Yamcha. With Piccolo's death, Kami also dies and the Dragon Balls cease to exist, leaving no way to bring anyone back to life.

Thirteen years later, the androids have killed most of humanity and continue to terrorize the remaining survivors for sport. Gohan, Goku's son and the only surviving warrior, has become a Super Saiyan but still cannot defeat them. He trains Trunks, the teenage son of Vegeta and Bulma, who longs to reach the Super Saiyan level himself. After a battle in which Gohan loses an arm, he knocks Trunks unconscious and goes to face the androids alone, fearing that Earth would be left without a defender if both of them died. When Trunks finds Gohan's body, his grief and rage finally transform him into a Super Saiyan. Years later, after failing to defeat the androids alone, Trunks travels back in time in a machine built by his mother to bring Goku a cure for his heart disease, setting up the events of the main series.

The special is known for its dark, tragic tone, which contrasts with much of the series, and for its focus on the bond between Gohan and Trunks.

In North America, the special was released on VHS and DVD in October 2000 by Funimation and later as a remastered double feature with Bardock – The Father of Goku. Anime News Network praised its sympathetic characters and exceptional action sequences, while noting that familiarity with the television series is recommended.

title: Little Fockers
tagline: Kids bring everyone closer, right?
overview: It has taken 10 years, two little Fockers with wife Pam and countless hurdles for Greg to finally get in with his tightly wound father-in-law, Jack. After the cash-strapped dad takes a job moonlighting for a drug company, Jack's suspicions about his favorite male nurse come roaring back. When Greg and Pam's entire clan descends for the twins' birthday party, Greg must prove to the skeptical Jack that he's fully capable as the man of the house.
plot:
Five years after their wedding, Greg Focker and his wife Pam are preparing to celebrate the fifth birthday of their twin children Samantha and Henry, while planning to move to a new house. However, things go awry for Greg when his in-laws Jack and Dina Byrnes visit them, and Jack announces that he is looking for his successor as the head of the Byrnes family.
Recently, Jack has been diagnosed with a heart condition and has become embittered by his daughter Debbie's divorce from her husband Bob. As Jack's original plan to declare Bob as his successor has failed, and his son Denny is a disappointment to him, he decides to pass the role to Greg, naming him "The Godfocker".
Despite Greg reluctantly accepting the role, Jack remains skeptical and begins to suspect Greg of infidelity when he sees him with drug representative Andi Garcia, who openly flirts with him. The presence of Sustengo, an erectile dysfunction drug that Greg promotes as a side job, also prompts Jack to think that he is no longer sexually attracted to Pam. Furthermore, he starts to doubt his ability to provide for his family when he is initially reluctant to enroll his children in a private school.
During a medical conference promoting Sustengo, Greg meets Bob at a bar and he tells him of Jack's original intention to name him "The Bobfather" as his successor. His relief and happiness with leaving Jack's family makes Greg slightly uncomfortable. Meanwhile, Jack tries to convince Pam to consider divorcing Greg and renewing her relationship with her ex-fiancé Kevin Rawley, whom Jack thinks is more financially and personally suitable for her.
Eventually, following a confrontation with Jack at a clinic, Greg escapes to his and Pam's unfinished new house, where Andi shows up. She tries to cheer him up, but drinks too much wine and makes sexual advances towards him. Watching from a window and misunderstanding the situation, a disappointed Jack leaves and lies to Pam and Dina about not finding Greg.
Greg's parents Bernie and Roz rejoin the family the next day at the twins' birthday party. Enraged at Greg's apparent infidelity, Jack engages him in a physical fight despite Greg insisting that he was rejecting Andi. The fight ends with Jack having a heart attack and collapsing. Greg quickly takes charge of the situation, looking after Jack. As paramedics take him away, Jack quietly admits that he believes Greg after observing his carotid artery, which remained stable while he proclaimed his innocence. Impressed with his integrity and quick thinking, Jack approves of him to be "The Gregfocker".
Four months later, on Christmas Day, Greg and Pam's parents celebrate the holidays with them in their new house. Bernie informs Greg and Pam that he and Roz have sold their Miami home and are moving to Chicago, only two houses away from theirs.

title: Godzilla: Tokyo S.O.S.
original_title: ゴジラ×モスラ×メカゴジラ／東京SOS
tagline: Three giant monsters, one violent final battle!!
overview: Mothra and her fairies return to Japan to warn mankind that they must return Kiryu to the sea, for the dead must not be disturbed. However Godzilla has survived to menace Japan leaving Kiryu as the nation's only defense.
plot:
The Shobijin visit the elderly Shinichi Chujo, his scientist nephew Yoshito, and his grandson Shun to warn them that Godzilla continues returning to Japan because the Japanese government used the first Godzilla's skeleton in the cyborg MFS-3 Kiryu's construction. If the government returns the skeleton to the ocean, Mothra, the descendant of the first Mothra who attacked Japan forty-three years ago, will take Kiryu's place in defending Japan.
As Kiryu undergoes repair and modifications, the Kiryu squadron is sent to the United States for further training, with Kyosuke Akiba taking Akane Yashiro's place should Godzilla return while she is away. Due to the first Mothra's attack, Japanese prime minister Hayato Igarashi denies Chujo's request, but agrees to discontinue the Kiryu project once the cyborg exterminates Godzilla. Sometime later, Godzilla resurfaces to attack Tokyo despite his injuries sustained since the last battle with Kiryu. Chujo and Shun summon Mothra to battle Godzilla. With the repairs finished, the government deploys Kiryu, but Godzilla knocks both it and Mothra out, injuring Chujo and Shun during the fray.
Meanwhile, on Himago Island, the uncharted volcanic island in Ogasawara island chain, twin Mothra larvae hatch from their egg and rush to help their mother. As Yoshito, with help from the Shobijin, uses a maintenance hatch to enter and repair Kiryu from its internal backup cockpit, the Japan Xenomorph Self-Defense Forces (JXSDF) and larvae try to hold Godzilla off, but the injured Mothra sacrifices herself to protect the latter from Godzilla's atomic breath while a separate attack warps Kiryu's maintenance hatch, trapping Yoshito inside. Nonetheless, he completes the repairs, allowing Kiryu to wound Godzilla before its spirit is reawakened by Godzilla's roar.
After the larvae bind Godzilla in a silk cocoon, Akiba is ordered to kill Godzilla per Yoshito and the Shobijin's request. However, Kiryu lifts Godzilla and uses its boosters to carry them both out to sea. Akiba's fellow pilot, Azusa Kisaragi, blasts the hatch open. Kiryu turns over to let Yoshito escape before it plunges into the ocean and drifts into an underwater trench with Godzilla. As Japan celebrates their victory, Yoshito salutes Kiryu while the larvae return to Infant Island with the Shobijin.
In a post-credits scene, an undisclosed laboratory is shown with canisters containing the DNA of numerous monsters.

title: Secretariat
tagline: The Impossible True Story
overview: Housewife and mother Penny Chenery agrees to take over her ailing father's Virginia-based Meadow Stables, despite her lack of horse-racing knowledge. Against all odds, Chenery - with the help of veteran trainer Lucien Laurin - manages to navigate the male-dominated business, ultimately fostering the first Triple Crown winner in 25 years.
plot:
In 1969, Denver housewife and mother Penny Chenery learns of her own mother's death and returns to her childhood home, where she reunites with Mrs. Ham, her father's secretary, and comforts her confused and elderly father. At her mother's funeral, Penny meets Arthur "Bull" Hancock and his son, Seth Hancock, of Claiborne Farm in Kentucky. The Hancocks offer any help she may need during her efforts to bring Meadow Stables back to profitability. Penny's brother Hollis informs her of a dishonest sale that was about to be made by the trainer until their mother stopped him. Penny fires the trainer and asks Bull Hancock to help her find a new trainer. He recommends Lucien Laurin, an aging French Canadian, who initially turns down Penny's offer.
Penny's father make a deal with leading owner Ogden Phipps that if Phipps bred his best stallion (Bold Ruler) to Chenery's two best mares (Somethingroyal and Hasty Matelda), the two owners would each receive one foal, flipping a coin to decide who would choose. Bold Ruler, the stallion, was fast but couldn't last over distances. Hasty Matelda is the obvious choice for her young age, but Somethingroyal's bloodline is made up of many horses with good stamina. Penny hopes to choose Somethingroyal's foal for the interesting mix of speed and stamina. Phipps wins the toss and chooses Hasty Matelda's foal, leaving Penny with Somethingroyal's foal, Secretariat.
When Secretariat enters his first race at Aqueduct race track in Queens, New York City, everyone has high expectations. The jockey, Paul Feliciano, is young with little experience, which worries Penny, but Lucien reassures her. During the race, Secretariat is repeatedly hit by other horses and comes in fourth. Penny and Lucien argue, and Lucien blames Paul for the loss, but Penny realizes the only way that Secretariat will ever win is if he has an experienced jockey. Penny's flight back home is canceled on the day of the race, and she misses her daughter Kate's solo in a play, but her son holds up the pay phone so Penny can hear Kate sing.
Penny gets experienced Canadian jockey Ron Turcotte to ride Secretariat to many victories. Secretariat is named horse of the year after a successful two-year-old season. Penny's father suffers a stroke and dies, leaving Penny and her brother Hollis to inherit the estate. Although she needs six million dollars to pay estate taxes, Penny refuses to sell Secretariat and instead syndicates him, selling 32 shares worth more than six million dollars, as long as he can win a three-year-old distance race. She tries to sell a share to Ogden Phipps, who instead offers to buy the horse for seven million dollars. Penny refuses to sell him. When Phipps demands to know why, she tells him Secretariat's value will triple when he wins the Triple Crown – a feat no horse has accomplished in twenty-five years. During this time, Frank "Pancho" Martin, trainer of rival horse Sham, tries to provoke a match race with Secretariat.

title: RED
tagline: Still armed. Still dangerous. Still got it.
overview: After surviving an assault from a squad of hit men, retired CIA black ops agent Frank Moses reassembles his old team for an all-out war. Frank reunites with old Joe, crazy Marvin and wily Victoria to uncover a massive conspiracy that threatens their lives. Only their expert training will allow them to survive a near-impossible mission -- breaking into CIA headquarters.
plot:
RED is a 2010 action comedy film directed by Robert Schwentke, based on the comic book series of the same name by Warren Ellis and Cully Hamner. The movie stars Bruce Willis, Helen Mirren, John Malkovich, Morgan Freeman, and Mary-Louise Parker.

The story begins with Frank Moses (Bruce Willis), a retired CIA operative who lives a quiet life in Asheville, North Carolina, under an assumed identity. However, his peaceful existence is disrupted when he receives a mysterious phone call from his old colleague, Marvin Boggs (John Malkovich). Boggs reveals that he has been murdered and leaves behind a cryptic message for Moses.

Moses soon discovers that he is being hunted by the CIA and other government agencies, who want to silence him due to his knowledge of classified information. He teams up with Sarah Ross (Mary-Louise Parker), his ex-wife, and Marvin's widow, Victoria (Helen Mirren). Together, they embark on a mission to uncover the truth behind Boggs' murder and clear Moses' name.

As they delve deeper into the conspiracy, they are joined by Harry Bellafonte (Morgan Freeman), another retired CIA operative who has been hiding in plain sight as a florist. The group soon realizes that they are being pursued by a ruthless agent named Beck (Brian Cox) and his team.

Throughout their journey, Moses and his team encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, deadly assassins, and unexpected allies. Along the way, they also uncover a web of deceit and corruption within the CIA, which threatens to destroy their lives.

As the stakes grow higher, Moses and his team must use their skills and experience to stay one step ahead of their pursuers. In a thrilling climax, they engage in an intense battle with Beck's team, resulting in a dramatic showdown that will determine their fate.

Ultimately, Moses and his team succeed in exposing the truth behind Boggs' murder and bringing down the corrupt agents who have been hunting them. The movie concludes with Moses and Sarah reuniting, while Harry finds redemption by finally revealing himself to the world as a retired CIA operative.

Overall, RED is an action-packed comedy that pays homage to the classic spy films of the 1960s and 1970s. With its witty dialogue, memorable characters, and high-octane action sequences, it has become a beloved favorite among fans of the genre.

title: Mega Piranha
tagline: They were created to save mankind. Something went wrong.
overview: When a science experiment goes horribly wrong, gigantic fish gain appetites for human flesh.
plot:
The film focuses on the Orinoco River in Venezuela, where a strain of genetically modified piranha have escaped into an isolated tributary of the river. Through human interference of the local environment, the megapiranha manage to escape from their isolated spot and swim downstream, killing all that cross their path. The megapiranha gradually make their way towards Florida at the height of the tourist season.
After the outbreak, a team including Special Agent Fitch and Sarah Monroe, work to contain the megapiranhas within Venezuela. They begin to get into trouble with the authorities when they attempt to cross over the Venezuelan border. Not having proper clearance and documentation, Special Agent Fitch resorts to using the diplomacy of his fist and drives off. He is pursued by Colonel Antonio Diaz in a high-speed chase through the jungle. Throughout the chase, Fitch alternates driving a Toyota Camry and Hyundai Elantra while Diaz is seen at different points in a GMC Jimmy, Chevrolet Suburban, Suzuki XL-7, and Ford Explorer. Fitch escapes by stealing a helicopter and heads to the International Super Bunker (ISB). During the journey, the helicopter runs out of fuel and Sarah Monroe rigs the emergency oxygen tank to the fuel line to make it to the ISB safely.
The megapiranhas continue to move north, consuming two battleships and a nuclear submarine. They eventually reach south Florida, where they kill at least five Puerto Ricans on a beach and manage to blow up two hotels. Meanwhile, the only force that can stop them is located at the ISB. After the megapiranhas prove impervious to both torpedoes and depth charges—and even a nuclear torpedo fails to stop them—Special Agent Fitch and Professor Sarah Monroe conclude that the only way to stop the megapiranhas is to face them in their own terrain: underwater. An army of SCUBA divers armed with guns would make the huge fish bleed, causing them to enter a feeding frenzy and kill each other. If this were to fail, then a massive nuclear strike would be used to destroy the megapiranha, as well as most of Florida.
In the middle of the operation, Colonel Diaz arrives in a helicopter, presumably using multiple fuel tanks to do this journey. The Colonel aims to get revenge on Agent Fitch and throws a rope into the water to trick him into climbing up into the enemy helicopter. Fitch, upon his arrival, shoots the pilot in the mouth with a flare gun, which causes the pilot's head to explode. Fitch then uses a homing beacon (which is actually a canister of CO2) to attract a megapiranha, jumping out of the helicopter shortly before it is consumed by the fishy behemoth.
Fitch is pursued by the megapiranha that ate the helicopter, eventually hiding in a reef where the megapiranha is unable to follow. When the piranha opens its mouth, Fitch shoots his gun at the helicopter still in the beast's jaws. The helicopter explodes, killing the fish.

title: Contagion
tagline: Nothing spreads like fear
overview: As an epidemic of a lethal airborne virus - that kills within days - rapidly grows, the worldwide medical community races to find a cure and control the panic that spreads faster than the virus itself.
plot:
Contagion is a 2011 medical thriller film directed by Steven Soderbergh, produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, and distributed by Warner Bros. The movie stars Matt Damon, Kate Winslet, Jude Law, Laurence Fishburne, Gwyneth Paltrow, Marion Cotillard, and Bryan Cranston.

The story begins with a mysterious outbreak of pneumonia-like symptoms in Shanghai, China. Dr. Ian Sussman (Laurence Fishburne), an epidemiologist at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), is called to investigate the source of the illness. He soon discovers that the disease is highly contagious and spreading rapidly around the world.

As the outbreak spreads, a young woman named Beth Emhoff (Gwyneth Paltrow) returns home from a business trip in Shanghai, only to fall ill with the mysterious pneumonia-like symptoms. Her husband, Mitch (Matt Damon), is frantic with worry as he tries to find out what's happening to his wife.

Meanwhile, Dr. Ally Hextall (Kate Winslet), an infectious disease specialist at the University of Wisconsin, is working on a vaccine for the disease. She teams up with Dr. Jeremy Renner (Jude Law) and Dr. Ellis Cheever (Laurence Fishburne) to develop a treatment.

As the outbreak spreads globally, the world descends into chaos. Governments struggle to contain the spread of the disease, while citizens are left to fend for themselves. The CDC works tirelessly to identify the source of the outbreak and find a cure.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when it is revealed that the disease was not created in a lab, but rather originated from a bat in China. The virus mutates rapidly, making it even more contagious and deadly.

As the world teeters on the brink of disaster, Dr. Sussman and his team work around the clock to develop a vaccine. Meanwhile, Mitch is desperate to find out what happened to his wife and how he can save her.

The movie's climax features a dramatic showdown between Dr. Hextall and the virus, as she works tirelessly to develop a cure. In the end, she succeeds in creating a vaccine that can be mass-produced and distributed globally.

The final scene shows the world slowly returning to normal, with people going about their daily lives once again. The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that humanity has learned from its mistakes and is better equipped to handle future pandemics.

Overall, Contagion is a gripping thriller that explores the rapid spread of a deadly disease and the global response to it. With its talented cast, intricate plot, and timely themes, the movie is both entertaining and thought-provoking.

title: Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore
original_title: Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore
tagline: Just like real spies... only furrier.
overview: The ongoing war between the canine and feline species is put on hold when they join forces to thwart a rogue cat spy with her own sinister plans for conquest.
plot:
Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore is a 2010 American live-action/animated comedy film directed by Chris Columbus and produced by Warner Bros. Entertainment.

The movie begins with the introduction of Kitty Galore (played by Michelle Monaghan), a wealthy socialite and inventor who has lost her cat, Snowball III, to a group of dogs led by Fifi LaFume (voiced by Shirley MacLaine). The dogs, who are secretly working for their owner, Warren Lightman (played by Chris Kattan), have been stealing valuable items from around the world.

Kitty Galore teams up with her former flame, Buddy Cooper (played by Chris Pine), a dog who is also an agent of the FELIS (Federation for the Enforcement of Laws and Inter Species) organization. Together, they hatch a plan to take down Warren Lightman and his canine accomplices.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Kitty Galore's true intentions are not entirely pure. She has a personal vendetta against Warren Lightman, who she believes wronged her in the past. Meanwhile, Buddy Cooper is struggling with his own identity as a dog who was raised by cats and feels like an outsider among both species.

The plot thickens when Snowball III, Kitty Galore's cat, returns to her side, revealing that he has been working undercover for FELIS all along. Together, they concoct a plan to infiltrate Warren Lightman's headquarters and steal the valuable item he is hiding: a powerful device that can control the minds of animals.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between Kitty Galore and her canine enemies. In the end, Kitty Galore emerges victorious, but not without realizing that her true feelings for Buddy Cooper are still strong. The film concludes with Kitty Galore and Buddy Cooper sharing a romantic moment, as Snowball III looks on.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, including cameos from other celebrities like Jack McBrayer and Bobby Cannavale. The film's blend of live-action and animation adds to its visual appeal, making it an entertaining watch for both kids and adults.

Overall, Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore is a lighthearted, family-friendly comedy that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and love. While it may not be the most complex or sophisticated film, it delivers plenty of laughs and action to keep audiences entertained.

title: Burning Bright
tagline: His Feeding. Your Frenzy.
overview: After her lousy stepfather steals her savings to buy a vicious tiger, Kelly loses all hope of going to college. But Kelly's situation worsens when a hurricane leaves her and her autistic brother boarded up in their house with the man-eating beast. This edge-of-your-seat thriller follows the gutsy heroine and her younger sibling as they struggle to outwit the ravenous predator and find a way to survive.
plot:
Burning Bright is an American horror thriller of 2010 directed by Carlos Brooks. Briana Evigan stars as Kelly Taylor, a young woman trapped with her autistic younger brother Tom, played by Charlie Tahan, and a starving tiger inside their boarded-up house during a hurricane, with Garret Dillahunt as their stepfather John Gaveneau, Mary Rachel Dudley as their mother Catherine and Meat Loaf in an uncredited role.

Planning to open a safari attraction, John buys a Bengal tiger named Lucifer from a travelling circus. When Kelly tries to place Tom in a care facility before she leaves for college, her payment bounces, and she learns that John has spent the money, which their late mother intended for Tom's care, on the tiger. John refuses to give it back, arguing that there was no will, and has the house boarded up against an approaching hurricane. Kelly is warned that she will lose her scholarship if she defers college yet again. That night someone frees Lucifer inside the house and nails the front door shut.

In the morning Kelly finds a note saying John has gone to the store, spots the tiger prowling the foyer and discovers that Tom is missing from his bed. With the house sealed and emergency lines jammed by the storm, she escapes the tiger by climbing a laundry chute, finds Tom and struggles to keep him safe through his sensory meltdowns. They hide under a bed doused in perfume, in a cupboard from which Kelly smashes an escape route through the wall, and Lucifer wounds her leg. In John's study she discovers life insurance policies on both siblings and a gun, but the first chamber is empty. Kelly breaks out through a window and reaches her car, then returns for Tom, promising never to leave him. Fending Lucifer off with a makeshift torch, she hides Tom in an empty chest freezer and lulls him to sleep. At dawn John returns to unseal the door, and Kelly realises he trapped them; he confesses that he murdered their mother when she planned to leave him. Lucifer then mauls him to death, and Kelly and Tom slip out into the storm-wrecked landscape, hand in hand.

Shot in Florida from July 2008, the film was released straight to DVD by Lionsgate on 17 August 2010. Retrospective reviews were warmer: Bloody Disgusting praised its solid direction and performances, and CHUD called it entertaining and at times surprisingly good.

title: The Cutting Edge: Fire & Ice
overview: Alexandra "Alex" Delgado, a pairs figure skater, found her career come to an abrupt halt after her partner (on and off the ice) became injured. As their love affair cooled, a heartbroken Alex stopped competing and turned to teaching. Enter James Van Behr the smoldering bad boy of speed skating, who has had fiery Alex in his sights as a skating partner ever since he was banned from speed skating. There aren't many girls who say no to him but she may well be the first. However, he pushes her buttons, challenging her like no one else - and her fighting spirit returns. She agrees to be his partner and they begin a grueling practice regimen fueled (and occasionally derailed) by their own tempestuous relationship, which heats up as they get closer to competition. But will their passion destroy Alex's chance to bring home the gold again?
plot:
The Cutting Edge: Fire & Ice is a 2010 American sports romance television film directed by Stephen Herek and written by Holly Brix. Made for the ABC Family cable channel, which first aired it on March 14, 2010, it is the sequel to The Cutting Edge: Chasing the Dream (2008) and the fourth instalment of The Cutting Edge series. Francia Raisa reprises her role as figure skater Alexandra "Alex" Delgado from the third film, opposite Brendan Fehr as a hot-headed speed skater who wants to become her pairs partner.

Alex's competitive career came to an abrupt end when her skating partner, who was also her boyfriend, was injured, and as their romance cooled she stopped competing altogether. Heartbroken, she now earns her living teaching children to skate, avoids dating, and worries her mother, who fears she is throwing away her dreams and will end up alone. James McKinsey, meanwhile, is the cocky bad boy of speed skating, banned from his sport after punching a teammate. With his agent he hatches a plan to switch to pairs figure skating, recruiting Zhen Zheng, a coach who loves a challenge but speaks no English and works through a translator, Mr. Wan. Finding a partner is harder, since most assume the move is merely a publicity stunt until his suspension is lifted. James has long had the fiery Alex in his sights, and she becomes perhaps the first woman to turn him down, but his provocations rekindle her fighting spirit and she agrees to partner him. Their gruelling training regime is repeatedly derailed by their tempestuous relationship. James parties the night before practice and shows up hungover, while the disciplined but cautious Alex hesitates over a daring new move he devises. Gradually, though, they find common ground: they bond during a bar fight, Alex learns that James is good with children, and he discovers she can shoot pool. A game of strip poker is interrupted when Alex's mother drops by. As their mutual attraction grows and the national championships in Montreal draw near, Alex must stay focused and learn to trust both her partner and her own feelings, while James works to overcome his selfish reputation.

Raisa plays Alex and Fehr plays James, with Zhenhu Han as Zhen Zheng, Russell Yuen as Mr. Wan and Dan Jeannotte as Angus Dwell. Reviewers considered it sweet but predictable, praising the chemistry between Raisa and Fehr and the energetic skating sequences, while noting the film's heavy reliance on montages.

title: Mortal Kombat: Rebirth
overview: MORTAL KOMBAT: REBIRTH is a short film released by Kevin Tancharoen (Director) in 2010. It was originally made as a proof of concept for Tancharoen's pitch to Warner Brothers for a reboot movie franchise. This 8-minute short features an intricate fight scene choreographed by Larnell Stovall. plot: Deacon City Police Captain Jackson Briggs informs the assassin Hanzo Hasashi about the criminals Reptile and Baraka; the latter has recently killed actor-turned-undercover-officer Johnny Cage in a fight. Briggs believes they were both working for a man named Shang Tsung. He asks Hasashi to kill them in a mysterious tournament hosted by Tsung. When offered his freedom in exchange for accomplishing such tasks, Hasashi reveals that he willingly had himself incarcerated—and could free himself at any time. Then Sonya Blade arrives with a folder and informs Hasashi that his enemy Sub-Zero is alive and the one he killed was his brother. It becomes clear to Hasashi that the terms of his participation in the tournament involve killing Reptile, Baraka and Shang Tsung in return for access to Sub-Zero. Since the real Sub-Zero will be at the tournament, Hasashi, now calling himself Scorpion, agrees to participate.

title: Woochi: The Demon Slayer
tagline: World beware. The wizard is coming.
overview: Spanning four centuries in Korea, this epic action-adventure concerns a powerful pipe and a trio of wizards who will do anything to protect it.
plot:
Five hundred years ago in the Joseon period, the Flute of the prophecy fell into the hands of evil goblins, propelling the world into a whirlwind of disorder. The ancient Taoist wizards turn to the greatest ascetics of their time, the Master (Baek Yoon-sik) and Hwadam (Kim Yoon-seok) for help in vanquishing the goblins and trust each wizard with one-half of the Flute. Meanwhile, the Master's rascal student Jeon Woochi (Gang Dong-won) tricks the king with the art of transformation and creates a fiasco, which makes the three Taoist wizards and Hwadam visit the Master. But they find the Master murdered and his half of the Flute missing. Woochi is framed for the murder, and as punishment, he and his trusty dog Chorangyi (Yoo Hae-jin) are imprisoned inside a scroll by the wizards.
Seoul, 2009. For some strange reason, goblins that had been sealed up in the past begin to appear one by one, wreaking havoc on the city. The three Taoist wizards had been enjoying their years of retirement as a priest, a monk, and a shaman, while Hwadam has long disappeared in order to polish his Taoist art. After much discussion, the three wizards unseal the scroll and call forth Jeon Woochi and Chorangyi. Being offered freedom in return for catching the goblins, Woochi sets out on his task. But what began as a hunt for goblins slowly turns into Woochi's personal sightseeing expedition of the modern-day world. And to top it off, he meets a woman with the same face as the one that had captivated him so many centuries ago (Im Soo-jung). Together with Seo In-kyung (his new, yet old love), Woochi begins his adventure.
Unbeknownst to anyone, Hwadam has been secretly releasing the goblins to distract the Taoist wizards away for his own personal motive. Having taken the Flute for himself, Hwadam intends to release the Arch God who has been imprisoned in a human body. He discovers In-kyung whom he suspects is the Arch God. After failing to make it in the acting business partially due to her innocent and cute looks, Hwadam uses his powers and changes her into a self-assured and savvy actress. The director having been frustrated with his chosen actress' behavior, takes notice of In-kyung and has her cast as his new leading lady. Both Woochi and Chorangyi discover Hwadam's true motive in murdering the Master in order to steal the flute for himself.
Soon the truth comes out when Chorangyi reveals to the three Taoist wizards that Hwadam played them for fools and had murdered the Master in order to take the Flute for himself. Confronting him, the wizards realize that they had wrongfully imprisoned Woochi and trick Hwadam into believing they're giving up the flute. Woochi takes the flute and it leads to a battle between him and Hwadan. The Flute is destroyed, but Hwadam makes his final stand. He is stopped by In-kyung using the Arch-God's power and making the Taoist wizards realize that she was the Arch-God herself.

title: Man, Woman & the Wall
tagline: Some fantasies should never be fulfilled.
overview: When Ryo, a young magazine reporter, moves into a new apartment he is greeted by the passionate sounds of his astonishingly beautiful neighbor Satsuki. Realizing the wall dividing their apartments is paper thin, the captivated journalist begins to eavesdrop on every detail of the girl next door's life: her conversations, her bubble baths... her breathless cries. While Ryo's fantasies escalate into something bordering on love and obsession, Satsuki becomes increasingly hysterical over the bizarre and dirty phone calls terrorizing her every night. When their lives finally converge delusions and reality blur forcing the unthinkable to happen.
plot:
Man, Woman & the Wall (Japanese: Kikareta Onna) is a 2006 Japanese erotic drama written and directed by Masashi Yamamoto, the filmmaker behind Junk Food. It stars the pinup and adult-video star Sora Aoi, also credited as Sola Aoi, who had moved into mainstream acting a few years earlier, alongside Keita Ōno, Hiroto Katō, Takashi Oda and Shō Nishino. Produced by Transformer, Inc. and running 84 minutes, the film plays with the conventions of the Japanese pink film, the low-budget softcore genre, while gently parodying them.

Ryo Kawase (Ōno) is a reporter for a small magazine who writes about organized crime. His modest income is enough to rent a small apartment with a tiny bathtub and, unfortunately, an extremely thin wall, through which he can hear almost everything that happens next door. His neighbor is the beautiful Satsuki (Aoi), and Ryo soon becomes captivated by the sounds coming from her home: her bubble baths, her lovemaking with her boyfriend Yuta (Katō), and the obscene, frightening phone calls she receives at night. Methodical rather than desperate, he installs a movable microphone along the wall to hear more clearly, and even tells a co-worker casually about what he is doing, while imagining the scenes that go with the sounds. When he and Satsuki eventually meet, their series of platonic dates develops into a sweet friendship. A blind spot in his listening setup, however, leads him to discover that someone else has already bugged her apartment, and Ryo sets out to identify the intruder without revealing what he knows. When Satsuki at last wants to give herself to him, his desire fades: the real woman cannot match the one he has built in his imagination.

The film was released on DVD in the United States by TLA Releasing. Jeffrey M. Anderson of Combustible Celluloid gave it three stars out of four, likening it to an old-fashioned "nudie cutie" but finding it cheerful and spirited, praising Aoi's appeal and the fact that she is given a real role, and noting the director's use of sound, color and the Japanese cityscape, though he found the DVD transfer poor. The Swiss site Molodezhnaja considered it mediocre overall, finding the story thin and the voyeurism theme quickly exhausted, but singled out the ending as its most intelligent part.

title: 16 Wishes
tagline: Everyone's sweet 16 is special, Abby's is magical.
overview: The story about Abby Jensen, a girl who's been eager to reach her 16th birthday and has kept a secret wish list since she was a little girl. When the Big Day actually arrives, utter disaster strikes, leaving Abby to think her birthday is ruined. But when a mysterious box of magical birthday candles arrives to turn things around, Abby's 16 Wishes start to come true. Her day gets better and better...until she makes one wish that threatens to change everything.
plot:
Abby Jensen has been planning her sweet sixteen since she was a little girl and keeps a list of wishes that she wants to come true. When her sixteenth birthday finally arrives, she adds her crush, Logan, as her sixteenth and final wish to the list. Throughout the day, Abby is visited by a peculiar woman named Celeste. Celeste first appears as an exterminator when the Jensens' house is swarmed by wasps from a nest that had been building up for 16 years. Celeste saves Abby's list, but the family is unable to return inside until the wasps are exterminated.
Abby meets her best friend, Jay Kepler, at the bus stop, where he gives her a necklace as a birthday gift. Celeste returns, dressed as a mailwoman, and gives Abby 16 candles and a matchbox. Abby lights the first candle, and her first wish—meeting celebrity Joey Lockhart—is fulfilled. Realizing that the numbers on the candles correspond to the numbers of the wishes on her list, Abby lights the eighth candle, granting her wish for a car. When Celeste emerges from the car, Abby deduces that Celeste is a magical being, as she appears every time a wish is granted.
Abby unsuccessfully attempts her third wish. Celeste warns her that there is a limit to how many wishes can be granted within an hour and that at midnight, the wishes she made will become permanent. Throughout the school day, Abby uses the candles to beat her rival, Krista Cook (who has the same birthday), in a volleyball match and to become student body president.
Jay agrees to take Abby shopping for a dress for her party but drops his wallet. They are followed by Krista, who convinces the clerk to eject them. Abby uses the ninth candle to make a wish to be treated like an adult, creating consequences of adulthood that she did not previously consider: Abby is suddenly 22 years old and no longer in high school. None of her classmates remember her, and she cannot live with her parents due to the ongoing wasp infestation in their home. She has an apartment, but the landlord is ready to evict her for nonpayment of rent. Desperate for an explanation, Abby makes a wish to beckon Celeste. Celeste arrives and reveals that the candles grant her wishes literally, as shown when her wish to be treated like an adult physically turned her into one.
Abby unsuccessfully tries to alter and add to her wish list. When she makes a wish for her parents to understand her, it is granted, but her parents only understand her under the impression that she is an adult. Finding Jay at Krista’s sweet sixteen, she manages to restore his memories of their friendship by showing him the necklace he gave her, but he remains unable to help her. After talking to Krista, Abby learns that the two are on good terms in adulthood and that Jay wanted to be student body president.
Abby returns to her apartment, where she meets Celeste and laments her selfishness.

title: Crocodile
tagline: Ever feel like something is watching you?
overview: A group of friends including Brady Turner, Claire and Duncan McKay go out on a boat trip on a lake in Southern California, but their joyful weekend turns into horror, when a giant killer crocodile searching for its stolen eggs, picks off anyone who gets in its way. Can they all escape in one piece or will they slowly and painfully fall to the mammoth reptile.
plot:
Crocodile is a 2000 direct-to-video horror film directed by Tobe Hooper, an international co-production between the United States and Mexico. Mark McLachlan, Caitlin Martin, Chris Solari, D. W. Reiser and Julie Mintz star in a story about college students on a spring-break houseboat trip who unknowingly enrage a giant crocodile that hunts them one by one. It was followed by Crocodile 2: Death Swamp, which has no connection to the original beyond featuring the same giant crocodile and its sole surviving offspring.

Eight young friends, among them Brady, Claire, Duncan, Kit, Annabelle, Sunny, Foster and Hubs, set off on a weekend boat trip on a remote lake in Southern California for spring break. Before they leave, the local sheriff warns them to stay out of trouble. At a bonfire that night, Kit tells the others a local legend about Harlan, an eccentric hotel owner who decades earlier kept an enormous crocodile named Flat Dog as an attraction. Believing the animal to be an avatar of the ancient Egyptian crocodile god Sobek, Harlan built a shrine to it and led a cult of worshippers, until the townspeople drove him out and burned his hotel.

Nearby, two local fishermen destroy a nest of crocodile eggs and are attacked and eaten by a huge crocodile. The next day, while the friends continue to party, Annabelle's dog runs off and the group stumbles upon the same nest, with one of them pocketing an egg. Soon the furious mother crocodile begins stalking them, picking them off as they try to escape through the swamps and back roads around the lake. The survivors seek help from the sheriff, and they must figure out how to stop the animal before it kills them all, while tensions within the group over romance and old grudges complicate their efforts to stay alive.

Crocodile received poor reviews and holds a 25 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on a small number of reviews. Joseph O'Brien of Rue Morgue noted occasional flashes of Hooper's characteristic weirdness, including a scene in which a crocodile hunter attacks the creature that killed his father, and likened the film to an episode of Dawson's Creek in which most of the cast is eaten by a giant reptile, an experience he did not consider entirely unrewarding.

title: Batman: Under the Red Hood
tagline: Dare to Look Beneath the Hood.
overview: One part vigilante, one part criminal kingpin, Red Hood begins cleaning up Gotham with the efficiency of Batman, but without following the same ethical code.
plot:
Ra's al Ghul hires the Joker as a distraction so that Ra's could destroy Europe's financial districts. He realizes his mistake when he is unable to control
Joker, who captures Jason Todd, the second Robin and Batman's partner. In Sarajevo, Bosnia, Joker brutally assaults and tortures Jason in an abandoned warehouse with a crowbar. Joker eventually leaves and locks Jason inside the warehouse with a bomb, which explodes and kills Jason before Batman arrives.
Five years later in Gotham City, a mysterious vigilante called Red Hood assembles a meeting of the city's most prominent drug dealers. He announces a takeover of their drug trade, taking 40 percent of their profit while offering them protection from Black Mask and Batman, but threatens to kill them if anyone is caught dealing drugs to children. Batman stops an attempted theft of a shipment that belonged to Black Mask, which contains the advanced android Amazo. Batman destroys Amazo with the help of Jason's predecessor Dick Grayson, using the name Nightwing, and discovers the thieves are working for Red Hood. The thieves are killed by a sniper shot before they can reveal any more. Batman identifies the shooter as the Red Hood, and chases him to Ace Chemicals. The Red Hood references the creation of the Joker in this same building before blowing up the facility. Batman and Nightwing interrogate Joker at Arkham Asylum about Red Hood, but he denies any involvement.
An infuriated Black Mask puts a hit on Red Hood for Amazo's destruction. Batman and Nightwing prevent Red Hood from hijacking Black Mask's next weapon shipment. They chase Red Hood to a train station, where he escapes after detonating a bomb, which injures Nightwing. As Alfred Pennyworth tends to Nightwing, Batman realizes that the Red Hood is trained and has knowledge of Batman's tactics, gear and his secret identity. Batman recalls Jason performing the same maneuvers as Robin and that Jason grew more violent as he aged.
Black Mask sends the Fearsome Hand of Four to lure Red Hood. They nearly overpower him until Batman helps incapacitate three of them and Red Hood kills the fourth, horrifying Batman. Red Hood explains that he is doing what Batman will not: killing criminals who are not afraid. Batman analyzes a blood sample of Red Hood drawn from the battle and it matches to Jason. After discovering that Jason's corpse is fake, Batman confronts Ra's al Ghul and demands to know the truth. Ra's explains that he felt responsible for Jason's death and, as a peace offering, swapped Jason's body for a fake and revived him in the Lazarus Pit, but following his resurrection, Jason was driven insane and escaped.
After surviving an assassination attempt by Red Hood, Black Mask sets the Joker free, tasking him with killing Red Hood. However, Joker instead abducts Black Mask and the drug dealers and plans to set them on fire. Red Hood appears and reveals his real target is Joker. Batman saves the hostages and Red Hood takes Joker.

title: Trouble Every Day
tagline: The hunger to love.

title: Men in Black 3
tagline: Back in time.
overview: Agents J and K are back...in time. J has seen some inexplicable things in his 15 years with the Men in Black, but nothing, not even aliens, perplexes him as much as his wry, reticent partner. But when K's life and the fate of the planet are put at stake, Agent J will have to travel back in time to put things right. J discovers that there are secrets to the universe that K never told him - secrets that will reveal themselves as he teams up with the young Agent K to save his partner, the agency, and the future of humankind.
plot:
Men in Black 3 is a science fiction comedy film directed by Barry Sonnenfeld and released in 2012 by Columbia Pictures.

The movie takes place in 2012, with Agent J (Will Smith) and Agent K (Tommy Lee Jones) on a mission to stop an alien threat. However, during the mission, Agent K is killed by an alien, leaving Agent J alone to carry on his work.

In order to prevent the destruction of the world, Agent J travels back in time to 1969, where he meets a younger version of Agent K (played by Josh Brolin). The two agents must work together to stop an evil alien named Boris the Animal (Jemaine Clement) from killing Agent K and taking over the world.

As they travel through time, Agent J learns about the origins of the Men in Black organization and the history of Agent K. He also discovers that Boris was once a member of the organization but became corrupted by his own power and desire for revenge against Agent K.

Throughout their journey, Agent J and Agent K encounter various characters from the 1960s, including a young version of Agent Z (Michael Stuhlbarg) and a young version of Agent O (Emma Thompson). They also visit iconic locations such as Woodstock and the Apollo 11 launch site.

As they get closer to stopping Boris, Agent J and Agent K must navigate through time and confront their own personal demons. Along the way, Agent J learns more about his own past and the origins of the Men in Black organization.

In the end, Agent J and Agent K successfully stop Boris and prevent him from killing Agent K. However, Agent J is left to return to his own time, where he finds that 2012 has been destroyed by an alien invasion. The movie ends with Agent J and Agent Z (played by Michael Stuhlbarg) working together to rebuild the world.

Men in Black 3 received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $624 million worldwide. The movie's blend of action, comedy, and science fiction elements made it a fun and entertaining ride for audiences.

title: Noel
tagline: Miracles are closer than you think
overview: Christmas Eve in New York, and the lonely divorced publisher, Rose Collins, needs a miracle to improve the health of her mother, interned in a hospital with Alzheimers. She feels sorry for another patient and meets his visitor. Meanwhile, Nina Vasquez breaks her engagement with her beloved fiancé Mike due to his suffocating jealousy, but misses him. Mike is stalked by a stranger, bartender Artie Venzuela. The poor Jules arranges to spend Christmas Eve in the hospital, where he spent the best Christmas of his life when he was a teenager. The lives of some of these characters cross with others along the night.
plot:
Noel is a 2004 American Christmas drama directed by Chazz Palminteri and written by David Hubbard. Its ensemble cast includes Penélope Cruz, Susan Sarandon, Paul Walker, Alan Arkin and Daniel Sunjata, with Robin Williams in an uncredited role. The film follows several intersecting stories that unfold on Christmas Eve in New York City,.

Rose Collins, a divorced publisher, struggles to care for her mother, who has Alzheimer's disease. As she considers suicide on a riverbank, a former priest named Charlie Boyd saves her, and they spend the night together at her apartment. Charlie admits he has lost his faith, but the next morning he tells Rose that it has been restored by a telepathic conversation with her mother, who wants Rose to move on with her life. Furious, Rose throws him out.

A young couple, Nina Vasquez and Mike Riley, are close to breaking up because of Mike's growing jealousy, and when he attacks one of Nina's platonic friends, she leaves him. At her family's Christmas celebration she meets Rose, who has ended up at the house through a series of coincidences, and the two women go to a bar. Meanwhile, an elderly waiter, Artie Venizelos, searches for his late wife every Christmas and becomes convinced that Mike is her reincarnation, making advances toward him. When Artie collapses and is taken to the hospital, Mike learns from a colleague that Artie once committed manslaughter in a jealous rage and that his wife then died in a car crash that was a suicide. Mike takes this as a sign that he must conquer his own jealousy. A depressed young man, Jules Calvert, whose only happy memory is a Christmas party in a hospital when he was a teenager, lets a criminal break his hand in hope of reliving it, only to learn that the past cannot be recovered. Rose, ashamed of how she treated Charlie, returns to the hospital and finds that he has been in a coma for some time and has no visitors. Across the hall, her mother has finally started eating thanks to Dr. Baron, and Rose agrees to have dinner with him.

Noel premiered at the 2004 Toronto International Film Festival and was acquired by Convex Group, owner of the Flexplay disposable DVD technology, which gave it a "trimultaneous" release in cinemas, on self-expiring Flexplay discs and on TNT within the same month. Critics largely dismissed it as sentimental; it holds a 28% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and Dave Kehr of The New York Times called it a heap of platitudes.

title: The Illusionist
tagline: When life loses its wonder, all it takes is one person who still believes in magic
overview: A French illusionist travels to Scotland to work. He meets a young woman in a small village. Their ensuing adventure in Edinburgh changes both their lives forever.
plot:
In 1959 Paris, an out-of-work illusionist packs his belongings, including an ill-tempered rabbit, and moves to London. Unable to compete with modern entertainment such as rock and roll, he plies his trade at smaller gatherings in bars, cafés, and parties. He accepts the invitation of a drunken party patron to visit a remote Scottish island, where he entertains the locals. Staying in a room above the pub, he meets a girl, Alice, who is captivated by his illusions and kindness, including a gift of red shoes.
Alice believes the downtrodden performer possesses genuine magical powers, and follows him to Edinburgh, where he performs at a modest theatre. They share a room in a run-down guest house favoured by other fading performers. The illusionist sleeps on a couch, and the girl keeps busy by cleaning and cooking food that she shares with the neighbours. The girl's affections even tame the rabbit, but the illusionist's increasingly meagre wages, spent on gifts for Alice, lead him to pawn his magic kit and secretly take on demeaning jobs.
Alice attracts the affection of a handsome young man. After the illusionist sees them walking together, he leaves her with money and a note stating "Magicians do not exist". He also releases the rabbit on Arthur's Seat, where it soon meets other rabbits. As Alice moves in with her boyfriend, the illusionist departs on a train hauled by a locomotive bearing the number 4472. On the train, he performs one last simple magic trick for a child.

overview: Soren, a young barn owl, is kidnapped by owls of St. Aggie's, ostensibly an orphanage, where owlets are brainwashed into becoming soldiers. plot:
In a world where owls are the dominant species, the story begins with a young owl named Soren, who lives on the island of Ga'Hoole. Soren is an outcast among his peers due to his unusual appearance and behavior. He is fascinated by the stories of the Great Tree, a sacred place where the ancient wisdom of the owls is stored.

Soren's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets a wise old owl named Ewan, who tells him about the prophecy of the Owls of Ga'Hoole. According to legend, five owls will gather at the Great Tree and choose a new leader to save their world from the evil Pure Ones. Soren is chosen by Ewan to embark on this perilous journey.

Soren sets out with his friends, Kludd, a skilled but arrogant owl, and Gylfie, a young and curious owl. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious predators, and rival owls who seek to claim the leadership of Ga'Hoole for themselves.

As Soren and his companions journey deeper into the unknown, they discover that the Pure Ones are led by a ruthless leader named Blind Eye, who seeks to destroy all non-Pure owls. The group soon realizes that their quest is not just about choosing a new leader but also about saving their world from destruction.

Throughout their journey, Soren and his friends face numerous challenges, including treacherous mountain passes, dark forests, and treacherous rivers. Along the way, they meet other owls who join their cause, including Gylfie's brother, Alaric, and a mysterious owl named Rook.

As the group nears the Great Tree, they are ambushed by Blind Eye's minions, leading to a fierce battle that tests Soren's leadership skills. In the heat of the battle, Soren discovers his true potential as a leader and proves himself worthy of the prophecy.

In the end, Soren and his companions reach the Great Tree, where they face off against Blind Eye in an epic showdown. With the help of his friends and allies, Soren defeats Blind Eye and claims the leadership of Ga'Hoole. The movie concludes with Soren standing atop a mountain, looking out over the land he has saved, surrounded by his fellow owls.

The Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga'Hoole is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of leadership, friendship, and self-discovery. With stunning animation and a richly detailed world, this movie is sure to captivate audiences of all ages.

plot:
Step Up 3D is a 2010 American dance drama film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Michael Genet, John Stockwell, and Stephen Peters. The movie stars Kenny Wormald, Amanda Seyfried, Adam G. Sevani, and Sharni Vinson.

The story begins with Tyler Gage (Kenny Wormald), a rebellious teenager who has just been released from juvenile detention after getting into a fight in his hometown of Baltimore. He meets Emily (Amanda Seyfried), the daughter of a wealthy businessman, at an art gallery opening where she is showcasing her mother's artwork.

Tyler and Emily meet again at a high school dance competition, where they bond over their shared passion for dance. Tyler is impressed by Emily's talent and decides to ask her out on a date. As they spend more time together, Tyler learns that Emily is struggling to find her place in the world after being diagnosed with a rare eye condition.

Meanwhile, Tyler's friend Chase (Adam G. Sevani) is trying to make it big as a dancer by performing at various events and competitions. However, his rival, Moose (Sharni Vinson), is also vying for attention and tries to sabotage Chase's performances.

As the story unfolds, Tyler and Emily grow closer, but their relationship is put to the test when Tyler's past comes back to haunt him. His ex-girlfriend, Nora (Mary Elizabeth Winstead), returns to town and tries to win him back. Tyler must choose between his old life and his new one with Emily.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Moose's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and threatening. In a tense confrontation, Moose attacks Chase, leaving him severely injured. Tyler and his friends band together to protect their friend and take down Moose.

In the end, Tyler and Emily confess their love for each other and decide to pursue their dreams together. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Tyler and Emily performing a romantic dance routine in 3D, surrounded by their friends and family.

Throughout the film, the dance sequences are showcased in stunning 3D, adding an extra layer of excitement and energy to the performances. The movie features a range of dance styles, from hip-hop to contemporary, and showcases the talents of its cast.

Overall, Step Up 3D is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of love, friendship, and redemption. With its impressive dance sequences and strong performances, it's no wonder why this movie became a fan favorite among dance enthusiasts and music lovers alike.

title: Python
tagline: Created by nature... redesigned by man.
overview: Sleepy New Haven California is a small town with a big problem. A sixty foot slithering horror has arrived and shattered the town's tranquillity on it's path of death and destruction... Growing violent and more savage with each attack the gigantic creature soon becomes an unstoppable feeding machine raging beyond control of it's creator, leaving only the stripped bones of it's victims in it's wake.
plot:
Python, released theatrically in the Philippines as Anaconda 2000, is a 2000 American made-for-television horror film directed by Richard Clabaugh about a genetically engineered snake loose near a small town. Its cast of cult favorites includes Frayne Rosanoff as John Cooper, Robert Englund as scientist Anton Rudolph, Casper Van Dien as NSA agent Bart Parker, William Zabka as Deputy Greg Larston, Dana Barron as Kristin, Wil Wheaton as Tommy, Jenny McCarthy as Francesca Garibaldi.

An NSA plane crashes near the town of Ruby after its cargo, an enormous reticulated python, breaks free. The snake survives and kills two women camping in the woods. When one victim's body is found corroded by acid, suspicion falls on John, who works at a plating plant that uses acid. Parker prepares to recapture the creature with Anton, one of its creators, who explains that it is a hybrid of several snake species able to spray corrosive stomach acid and warns that Parker's men are outmatched. The python kills a real estate agent and his client, Francesca, and after more bodies turn up, Sheriff Griffin Wade closes the plant and arrests John, though he must free him when the NSA arrives with a cover story blaming a rogue operative.

Tracking the snake by radar, the NSA team open fire on what proves to be its shed skin, and the python wipes them out, leaving Anton as the only survivor. The next morning it kills Tommy and attacks his girlfriend, Theresa, who hides after it wrecks her truck. John and Kristin find the wreck, are chased to the water treatment center, and meet Theresa and the shaken Anton there. With Greg's help over the radio, they lure the python inside with John as bait, but the bomb fails to go off, and Anton sacrifices himself to detonate it manually. The python emerges unharmed, so the survivors trick it into the plating plant and push its vulnerable underbelly into a vat of acid, killing it. Six months later the plant has become a bar and bike shop that trades on the story, Greg has been accepted to Quantico to train with the FBI, and John announces that Kristin is pregnant.

Shot in Los Angeles and Malibu, Python premiered on U.S. television on August 9, 2000, and opened in Philippine theaters on October 25, 2000, under a title linking it to the unrelated 1997 film Anaconda. Reviews were mixed, praising the ensemble while faulting the effects and story. It was followed by three made-for-TV sequels: Pythons 2, New Alcatraz and Boa vs. Python.

title: Faster
tagline: Slow justice is no justice
overview: After 10 years in prison, Driver is now a free man with a single focus - hunting down the people responsible for brutally murdering his brother.
plot:
Faster is a 2010 American action thriller directed by George Tillman Jr. from a script by Tony and Joe Gayton. Dwayne Johnson stars as a recently released convict on a mission of revenge, with Billy Bob Thornton, Oliver Jackson-Cohen, Carla Gugino, Maggie Grace, Mike Epps, Moon Bloodgood, Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje and Tom Berenger in the supporting cast. CBS Films released it in the United States on November 24, 2010, with Sony handling international distribution.

Upon walking out of prison, Jimmy Cullen, credited only as "Driver," picks up a 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle, a handgun and a list of names. He drives straight to a telemarketing office in Bakersfield, California, and shoots a man named Prescott Ashton. He then confronts Roy Grone, who supplied the car and weapon, and pressures him for more information. Driver is soon pursued on two fronts: by a pair of detectives, the veteran Slade Humphries and his partner Cicero, and by a wealthy, highly skilled hitman known only as "Killer," who has been hired to stop him.

The next name on the list leads Driver to Kenneth Tyson, a man who records snuff films, whom he kills before escaping a hallway shootout with Killer. The encounter troubles the assassin, who proposes to his girlfriend Lily and becomes personally fixated on finishing the job. Meanwhile, the detectives dig into Driver's past and learn that he was double-crossed after a bank robbery years earlier. Cicero recalls a video, filmed by Tyson, showing the murder of Driver's older half-brother Gary and a man shooting Driver in the head; he survived only because of a metal plate surgically placed in his skull. As Driver works his way through the gang responsible, the hunters and the hunted converge, and the true identity of the man who orchestrated the betrayal is revealed.

Faster received mixed reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes about 41% of 128 reviews were positive, and the site's consensus welcomed Johnson's return to hard-hitting action roles while judging that the film did not deliver enough of the thrills it promised. Commentators often compared its lean, brooding tone to the revenge thrillers of the 1970s, and it marked a deliberate shift by Johnson away from the family comedies he had made in the preceding years.

title: Paranormal Activity 2
tagline: In 2009 you demanded it. Nothing can prepare you for what's next.
overview: Days after welcoming a newborn baby, Dan and Kristi Rey return home one day to find their house ransacked with seemingly no explanation. Their fear forces them to put in security cameras, which begin to capture strange activity around the house.
plot:
Paranormal Activity 2 is a 2010 American supernatural horror film directed by Todd Lincoln and written by Marcus Nispel, Christopher Landon, and Oren Peli. The movie serves as a prequel to the first film and explores the events that led up to the original story.

The film begins with Katie Featherston's character, Katie, now 19 years old, living in a new apartment with her boyfriend, Micah (Mark Fredrichs). They are trying to start their life together after the traumatic events of the previous year. However, strange occurrences begin to happen, and they soon discover that their apartment is haunted by an evil spirit.

As the haunting intensifies, Katie starts experiencing terrifying visions and nightmares, which she believes are connected to her sister, Kristi (Sprague Grayden), who died in a car accident two years ago. The entity seems to be targeting Katie, and Micah tries to help her cope with the situation.

Meanwhile, a documentary crew, led by Dr. Fredric Foster (John Gulager), is filming Katie's experiences as part of an experiment to capture evidence of paranormal activity. As the haunting escalates, the crew becomes increasingly entangled in the events unfolding before their cameras.

plot:
Scream 4 is a 2011 American slasher film directed by Wes Craven and written by Kevin Williamson. The movie takes place 10 years after the events of the original Scream, with the Ghostface killer still at large.

The story begins with Sidney Prescott (Neve Campbell), now a successful author, returning to Woodsboro for the release of her new book, "Truth or Dare." She is accompanied by her husband, Phil (David Arquette), and their teenage daughter, Jill (Emma Roberts). The town has changed little since the original murders, and Sidney is still haunted by the traumatic events of her past.

As the story unfolds, a series of murders takes place in Woodsboro, with the killer using the same tactics as the original Ghostface. The main suspect is Charlie Walker (Rory Culkin), a high school student who has been obsessed with Sidney since childhood. However, it becomes clear that there are multiple killers involved, each with their own motivations and backstories.

One of the new characters introduced in Scream 4 is Jill Roberts, Sidney's daughter, who becomes the target of the Ghostface killer. As the body count rises, Jill finds herself at the center of a new wave of terror, forcing her to confront the dark legacy of her mother's past.

Throughout the movie, the characters are forced to navigate their own personal demons and relationships, all while trying to uncover the identity of the killer. The film pays homage to the original Scream, with many nods to the first two movies, including a memorable scene in which Jill is stalked by the Ghostface killer in a similar fashion to Sidney's experiences.

As the plot thickens, it becomes clear that the killers are not just random psychopaths, but rather individuals who have been influenced by the original murders. The film's climax features a shocking twist, as the true identity of the killer is revealed, and the motivations behind their actions are exposed.

Ultimately, Scream 4 delivers on its promise of a thrilling and suspenseful ride, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats. While some may find the film's self-awareness and meta-humor to be a bit too much, it is undeniable that Wes Craven and Kevin Williamson have crafted a movie that is both a loving tribute to the original Scream and a fresh take on the horror genre.

In conclusion, Scream 4 is a masterclass in suspenseful storytelling, with a complex web of characters and plot twists that will keep viewers guessing until the very end. With its blend of humor, horror, and social commentary, it is a must-see for fans of the franchise and horror enthusiasts alike.

plot:
One Piece Film: Strong World is a 2009 Japanese animated fantasy adventure film directed by Munehisa Sakai from a screenplay by Hirohiko Kamisaka, and the tenth feature film based on Eiichiro Oda's manga One Piece. Oda served as executive producer and created the original story and character designs, a first for the franchise. Mayumi Tanaka voices Monkey D. Luffy, with Kazuya Nakai, Akemi Okamura, Kappei Yamaguchi and Hiroaki Hirata, and actor Naoto Takenaka voices the villain Shiki. It was released in Japan on 12 December 2009.

Shiki, the legendary pirate known as the Golden Lion, who escaped from the prison Impel Down twenty years earlier, uses his Devil Fruit power to make objects float and destroys a fleet of Navy ships, sending a warning to Vice Admiral Garp and Fleet Admiral Sengoku. Days earlier, the Straw Hat Pirates read news of attacks in the East Blue, their home sea, and Luffy vows to protect it, just as Shiki's flying ship appears above them. During a storm, Nami's skill as a navigator impresses Shiki, who learns that she warned of the danger. He offers to take the crew to the East Blue, but instead abducts Nami and scatters the rest of the Straw Hats across his floating islands.

The islands are inhabited by monstrous animals created through genetic experiments by Shiki's eccentric scientist, Doctor Indigo. Luffy fights his way through the beasts, while the crew, split into groups, struggles to survive. Shiki tries to persuade Nami to become his navigator, revealing his plan to use the evolved creatures to conquer the East Blue as a demonstration of his power against the World Government. To protect her friends and the villagers of the islands, Nami pretends to accept, while secretly trying to sabotage his plan. With the help of a small electric bird named Billy, whom Shiki rejected, Luffy and the reunited crew storm Shiki's fortress to rescue Nami, leading to a climactic battle between Luffy and the Golden Lion.

Strong World received praise for its story, animation and action, and was a major box-office success in Japan, grossing over 4.8 billion yen and becoming the highest-grossing One Piece film at the time.

The Smurfs are living in harmony in the forest, but they know that Gargamel's return is imminent.

However, Gargamel and his cat, Azrael, also discover the book's location and follow the Smurfs to the city.

As the Smurfs navigate the urban jungle, they encounter various obstacles, including traffic, skyscrapers, and humans who are unaware of their existence. Meanwhile, Brainy Smurf becomes smitten with a human woman named Sophie (played by Emma Stone), who is initially oblivious to the Smurfs' presence.

As Gargamel's plan unfolds, he uses Azrael to capture the Smurfs and extract their essence. However, Brainy Smurf's book allows him to travel back in time and warn his friends about the impending danger. The Smurfs work together to outsmart Gargamel and Azrael, using their unique skills to evade capture.

Climax:
The final confrontation takes place at the Empire State Building, where the Smurfs face off against Gargamel and Azrael. Brainy Smurf uses his book to create a portal that allows him to travel back in time and prevent Gargamel from capturing the Smurfs' essence.

Ending:
In the end, the Smurfs successfully defeat Gargamel and return to their forest home. Sophie, who has grown attached to the Smurfs, decides to leave New York City with Brainy Smurf, starting a new life together. The film concludes with the Smurfs returning to their village, where they are welcomed back as heroes.

Overall, The Smurfs is a lighthearted and entertaining film that brings the beloved comic book characters to life on the big screen. While it may not be a critically acclaimed movie, it provides plenty of humor and action for fans of all ages.

plot:

At first, they struggle to get along, but they all become friends in the end.
One of the teachers at the ballet school, Helena (Charlotte Rampling), takes Carly to a ballet where she starts getting ideas for their routine. When she arrives home, Carly finds Jay waiting for her and the two spend the night having sex. During a dance battle in a club the next night, the team learn that Jay has betrayed the team by joining The Surge, a rival crew. All for the sake of winning the competition. Jay brags about his sex with Carly and Tomas (Richard Winsor), a ballet dancer, punches Jay out of anger. Carly, upset over her boyfriend's betrayal, flees the club and is nearly hit by a car before Tomas pulls her out of the way. Tomas then takes Carly back to his apartment where they dance on the roof, eventually kissing. Carly then leaves him alone on the roof, while they both look at the sunrise and smile.
The next day at the school, Carly announces that they won't try to be better, they will be themselves by performing a routine that is both street and ballet. And that the new name of their dance crew is "Breaking Point". Another teacher at the school, outraged that her students are being corrupted, deliberately plans a Royal Ballet audition for the same day as the street dance finals. The ballet dancers promise Carly they will make it, but the auditions were running overtime.
In an attempt to give Breaking Point more time to wait for the ballet dancers to arrive, Carly's friend Eddie (George Sampson) goes out onto the dance floor and starts dancing, surprising the crew and wowing the audience. Jay tries to convince Carly to just give up but she states that she is sorry for him. The ballet team turn up in time, and their teacher Helena drives the Royal Ballet judges to the street dancing final so they can see the dancers perform. The routine is a success, Carly and Tomas kiss during the performance, and the crowd is enthralled. Jay is shocked that The Surge have been beaten and he's lost Carly.
The film ends with Breaking Point and The Surge dancing to N-Dubz' "We Dance On".

Due Date is a comedy film released in 2010, directed by Todd Phillips and starring Robert Downey Jr. and Zach Galifianakis.

As they travel across the country, the trio faces various challenges, including run-ins with eccentric characters, traffic jams, and unexpected detours. Along the way, Peter learns valuable lessons about life, love, and the importance of family. He also begins to see Dwayne as a surrogate son figure, who reminds him of his own father.

As they near their destination, the group encounters a series of comedic misadventures, including a wild night in Albuquerque and a disastrous encounter with a group of bikers. However, despite the setbacks, Peter's bond with Dwayne grows stronger, and he begins to see the world through his friend's eyes.

As they prepare to welcome their new baby, Peter reflects on the journey he shared with Dwayne and realizes that it was a transformative experience that taught him the value of friendship and family.

Throughout the movie, Downey Jr.'s wit and charm shine through as he brings Peter to life, while Galifianakis's deadpan humor provides plenty of comedic moments. The chemistry between the two leads is undeniable, making their unlikely friendship one of the film's most memorable aspects.

Overall, Due Date is a heartwarming comedy that explores themes of family, friendship, and redemption. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and hilarious antics, it's no wonder this movie became a box office hit.

title: Tekken
tagline: Survival is no game
overview: In the year of 2039, after World Wars destroy much of the civilization as we know it, territories are no longer run by governments, but by corporations; the mightiest of which is the Mishima Zaibatsu. In order to placate the seething masses of this dystopia, Mishima sponsors Tekken, a tournament in which fighters battle until only one is left standing.
plot:
Tekken is a 2009 American science fiction martial arts film loosely based on the video game series developed and published by Namco Bandai Games. Directed by Dwight Little from a screenplay by Alan B. McElroy, it stars Jon Foo as Jin Kazama and Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa as Heihachi Mishima, with Kelly Overton, Ian Anthony Dale, Cung Le, Darrin Dewitt Henson, Candice Hillebrand and Luke Goss. Announced by Namco Bandai in 2002, the film did not begin development until 2007; Little, experienced with sports films, aimed for realism, removing the games' supernatural elements and comic relief characters and casting trained martial artists for its fights.

After a devastating conflict known as the Terror Wars, governments have collapsed and eight megacorporations divide the world, with North America ruled by the Tekken Corporation. To maintain their power, the corporations stage an annual fighting tournament, the Iron Fist, whose champion wins fame and fortune. In 2039, Jin Kazama lives with his mother Jun in the Anvil, a slum surrounding Tekken City, and earns money smuggling contraband for resistance groups. Jun, who raised and trained him alone and told him his father was dead, forbids him from entering the tournament. When Tekken's enforcers hunt Jin down after a run, Jun is killed, and Jin swears revenge against the corporation's chairman, Heihachi Mishima. Finding an old fighter ID revealing that his mother was once an Iron Fist competitor, he wins a wild card place by defeating Marshall Law and enters Tekken City with the backing of former boxer Steve Fox, who reveals that he knew Jun. There Jin befriends the fighter Christie Monteiro and wins brutally against Miguel Caballero Rojo, impressing Heihachi's son Kazuya, whose job offer Jin refuses. After surviving an assassination attempt by Nina and Anna Williams on Kazuya's orders, Jin fights his way through the tournament as Kazuya imprisons his father and seizes control of the corporation, setting the stage for a confrontation that reveals the truth about Jin's family.

Tekken premiered at the American Film Market in November 2009 and was released in Japan by Warner Bros. on March 20, 2010. It was a box-office bomb, grossing $1.6 million worldwide, and critics praised its fight scenes but criticized its unfaithful story and acting, as did the game series' director Katsuhiro Harada. A prequel, Tekken 2: Kazuya's Revenge, followed in 2014.
