overview: A Saiyan Space pod crash-lands on Earth out of which a wounded Saiyan crawls: Broly, the Legendary Super Saiyan. The wounded Broly shouts out in frustration and turns into normal form. The place soon freezes, trapping him in it and he falls into a coma.
plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Broly - Second Coming is a 1994 Japanese animated science fantasy martial arts film directed by Daisuke Nishio and produced by Toei Animation. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1993 film Dragon Ball Z: Broly - The Legendary Super Saiyan.

The story begins with Goku, Trunks, and Pan training on Earth when they are suddenly attacked by a group of powerful warriors from the planet Vagar. These warriors are revealed to be members of the Ginyu Force, a group of elite fighters who serve under Frieza, the main antagonist of the Dragon Ball Z series.

The Ginyu Force is led by Captain Ginyu, a skilled fighter with the ability to transform into different forms. The team's mission is to capture Goku and use his power to awaken Broly, a powerful warrior from the planet Vegeta who was thought to be dead.

Meanwhile, on Planet Vegeta, Broly is awakened by the energy of the Ginyu Force's attack on Earth. He quickly becomes enraged and begins to wreak havoc on the planet, destroying everything in his path.

Goku, Trunks, and Pan soon discover that Broly has been awakened and are forced to flee from him. They eventually team up with Vegeta, who is initially reluctant to help them but ultimately joins forces to stop Broly.

As the battle between Goku's allies and Broly intensifies, it becomes clear that Broly's power is far greater than anyone had anticipated. Despite his incredible strength, however, Broly struggles with his own emotions and identity, which makes him a complex and sympathetic character.

In the end, Goku and Vegeta are able to defeat Broly using a combination of their skills and teamwork. However, not before Broly's true nature is revealed: he is actually the long-lost son of Vegeta and the one who was responsible for his father's downfall on Planet Vegeta.

The movie concludes with Broly's spirit being sent back to Planet Vegeta, where he will be able to find peace and redemption. Goku and his friends are left to reflect on the events that transpired and the true nature of their enemy, Frieza, who is still at large.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: Broly - Second Coming is a thrilling and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, power, and redemption. The movie's complex characters and intricate plot make it a must-see for fans of the Dragon Ball Z series.

title: Our Lady of the Assassins
overview: World-weary arthur Fernando has returned to his native Colombia to live out his days in peace.  But Fernando's once-quiet hometown has become a hotbed of violence, drugs and corruption.  On the brink of despair, Fernando meets Alexis, a beautiful but hardened street kid who lives by the rule of the gun.  Together, they forge an unlikely relationship.
plot:
Our Lady of the Assassins (Spanish: La virgen de los sicarios) is a 2000 Spanish-language romantic crime drama directed by Barbet Schroeder from a screenplay by Fernando Vallejo, adapted from his own 1994 novel. Germán Jaramillo stars as Fernando, a Colombian writer in his fifties who returns to his native Medellín after some thirty years away, with Anderson Ballesteros as Alexis, Juan David Restrepo as Wilmar and Manuel Busquets as Alfonso.

Fernando has come home to die and finds the city he remembers transformed by the violence of the drug cartel wars. At a party given by an old friend he meets Alexis, a handsome young man, and falls for him at once. Their relationship, beyond sex, consists largely of Fernando reminiscing about the peaceful city of his youth while Alexis explains the everyday reality of robberies, shootings and killings. Alexis's company softens Fernando's sardonic, bitter outlook a little.

Fernando soon discovers that Alexis is himself a member of a gang and a hired killer, or sicario, and that rival gangs want him dead. Alexis fends off several attempts on his life with his skill with a pistol, but he is eventually shot dead by two boys on a motorcycle, at a moment when he no longer has his gun, which had been lost partly because of Fernando's own suicidal impulses.

After giving money to Alexis's mother, Fernando wanders the streets and meets Wilmar, a boy who resembles Alexis strikingly in both appearance and manner. He takes him to lunch and the two begin an affair that recreates his earlier relationship. Fernando is shocked to learn that Wilmar, also a killer, was the one who shot Alexis, and he vows to kill him, until he finds out that Alexis had begun the feud by murdering Wilmar's brother. The two plan to leave Colombia together, but Wilmar is killed when he goes to bid his mother farewell. Recognising that the endless cycle of violence in Medellín leaves no room for happiness, Fernando appears, in the final scene, to be contemplating taking his own life.

Shot on early high-definition video cameras, which gave it a documentary-like look, the film was among the first features made in HD. It won the President of the Italian Senate's Gold Medal at the 2000 Venice Film Festival, where it competed for the Golden Lion, and holds 77% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 73.

title: Frozen
tagline: No one knows you're up there.
overview: When three skiers find themselves stranded on a chair lift at a New England ski resort that has closed for the next week, they are forced to make life or death choices that prove to be more perilous than staying put and freezing to death.
plot:
Frozen is a 2010 American psychological horror survival film written and directed by Adam Green, starring Shawn Ashmore and Kevin Zegers and introducing Emma Bell. It follows three friends stranded on a chairlift after a day of skiing, forced to make life-or-death choices. It was filmed at Snowbasin near Ogden, Utah, in February 2009.

Dan Walker, his girlfriend Parker O'Neal and his best friend Joe Lynch spend a day at a ski resort. On the last evening, with the resort about to close for the week because of incoming bad weather, they persuade the lift operator to let them take one final run. A replacement operator takes over and, mistaking three other skiers for them, shuts down the lift, leaving the friends stranded high above the ground. As a snowstorm sets in, a snow groomer passes below without its driver noticing them.

Realizing that no one knows where they are and that they will not survive until the resort reopens, Dan jumps from the chair, breaking both legs. Unable to reach him, Parker and Joe can only listen as a pack of wolves tears him apart. Grieving, the two blame each other before finding comfort, and Parker admits that she had hoped to marry Dan. The next morning, Joe shimmies along the razor-sharp cable to a support tower, badly cutting his hands and loosening the bolt that secures their chair. Climbing down, he fends off the wolves with a ski pole and sets off down the mountain on Parker's snowboard, promising to bring help, with the pack in pursuit. Parker spends another night alone on the lift. When Joe does not return, she tries to reach the tower herself, but the chair's bolt gives way and it drops to a few meters above the ground. She jumps, and the falling chair crushes her ankle. Sliding and crawling down the slope, she passes the wolves feeding on Joe's body, but they ignore her. Reaching a road, she is picked up by a passing driver who takes her to hospital, and she closes her eyes remembering Dan's words.

Frozen premiered at the 2010 Sundance Film Festival, where audience members reportedly fainted, and was released by Anchor Bay Films in North American theaters on February 5, 2010, grossing slightly less than $2.7 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed to positive, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 64% approval and Metacritic a score of 43. Bell later reprised her role in an epilogue scene in Hatchet II.

title: The King of Fighters
tagline: A tournament of legends.
overview: The King of Fighters movie will introduce a new science fiction spin into the setting established in the games universe by following the surviving members of three legendary fighting clans who are continually whisked away to other dimensions by an evil power. As the fighters enter each new world they battle that universes native defenders, while the force that brought them seeks to find a way to invade and infect our world.
plot:
The King of Fighters is a science fiction martial arts film directed by Gordon Chan from a screenplay by Rita Augustine and Matthew Ryan Fischer, based on SNK's long-running fighting game series. Maggie Q stars as Mai Shiranui, with Sean Faris as Kyo Kusanagi, Will Yun Lee as Iori Yagami, Ray Park as Rugal Bernstein and David Leitch as Terry Bogard. It was shot in North Vancouver, Canada, in 2008 and 2009.

The King of Fighters tournament takes place in an alternate dimension that fighters enter through special wireless headsets. In Boston, Mai and her boyfriend Iori attend the unveiling of three sacred relics, the Kagura Mirror, the Yagami Necklace and the Kusanagi Sword, when the renegade fighter Rugal steals them and vanishes through a dimensional portal, intending to awaken the Orochi, an ancient entity that grants limitless power. The sword proves to be a fake. The wounded Chizuru Kagura, who oversees the tournament, tells Mai that the real sword lies with Saisyu Kusanagi, now confined in a mental institution, and warns her to keep Iori out of the quest. Saisyu dies after a violent reaction to Iori's presence, leaving his son Kyo to take up the fight.

Meanwhile the CIA agent Terry Bogard investigates Rugal and learns that Mai is an undercover CIA operative. Kyo learns of the ancient rivalry between his clan and the Yagami, whose ancestor was once consumed by the Orochi's rage. Rugal plans to merge the tournament dimension with the real world. Iori enters the tournament alone and defeats Rugal's henchwomen Mature and Vice, but his mind is taken over by the Orochi. Kyo is defeated by Rugal and spared only as a warning, before learning that years earlier the possessed Iori was responsible for destroying his father's mind. Kyo fights Iori and frees him from the Orochi's grip.

In a final battle, Chizuru returns with the mirror and the necklace, but is mortally wounded when the heroes' first attempt to trap Rugal fails. Mai takes her place, and as Rugal prepares to kill Kyo, the young fighter conjures a new sword with his inherited power and uses it to destroy his enemy. Back in the real world, Kyo resolves to continue his family's tradition in the tournament as Iori watches from a distance.

The film was released direct to DVD in the United States in September 2010 and was poorly received; critics complained that it spent too much time on convoluted mythology and too little on the fighting that defines its source material.

overview: Joshua “J” is taken in by his extended family after his mother dies of an overdose. After his mother overdoses, 18-year-old Joshua "J" Cody asks his estranged grandmother, Janine "Smurf" Cody, for help, and she invites him to move in with her. Smurf is the affectionate matriarch of a Melbourne crime family that uses her home as a base. Her home is also being watched by cops who are looking for her oldest son, Andrew "Pope" Cody, who is in hiding. The volatile middle brother, Craig, deals drugs successfully enough to have bought the house for his mother. The youngest brother, Darren, follows the lead of his siblings, while family friend "Baz" leads the gang, which specialises in armed robbery.
J is quickly exposed to the criminal underworld. Craig takes J along to meet with a crooked cop, from the drug squad, who tells Craig that renegade cops on the armed-robbery squad are on the lookout for all of them. At a traffic light, Craig is verbally abused by the passenger of a passing car. Craig passes J a handgun before pursuing. As the car stops, two men exit and begin to threaten Craig. J steps out and points the pistol at the two men, who flee as Craig looks on. J, exhilarated, passes the gun back to Craig who asks J if he enjoyed himself.
Later, Baz goes to meet Pope at a shopping centre, where they discuss quitting crime and going straight. As Baz gets in his car to leave, police approach, falsely claim he has a gun, and shoot him dead. Angry and distraught, Pope and Craig want revenge and ask J to steal a Commodore and take it to Darren's place. The car is then parked after 2:00 am in the middle of the street as a lure. Two policemen are called to the scene, where they are ambushed and shot dead by Pope and Craig. The next day, Pope, Darren, and J are taken in for questioning, where J meets Detective Senior Sergeant Nathan Leckie, who also leads the armed-robbery squad. Leckie, one of the few non-corrupt police officers, recognises J's predicament and begins to lean on him. The three are later released from custody, and J returns with his girlfriend, Nicky, to her parents' home.
Craig, who has avoided being picked up by the police, meets Pope, Darren, and Smurf at a restaurant, where they realise J is the weak link. After Smurf suggests Craig give himself up for questioning, he panics and goes to visit a friend in rural Bendigo. Craig learns that the house is already being monitored, and as the police arrive he tries to flee through a field but is gunned down.
Pope and Darren take J to meet their solicitor, Ezra. He coaches J to not tell the police anything and pressures him to break up with Nicky, which J does. Leckie takes J into custody again, where he proposes that J be moved to witness protection, but J turns down the offer. Meanwhile, Nicky, unsure what to do, shows up at Smurf's home, looking for J. Pope gives her heroin, questions her, then suffocates her. When J returns to Smurf's house the next morning he discovers Nicky's bracelet outside the house.

title: The Tempest
overview: An adaptation of the play by William Shakespeare. Prospera (a female version of Shakespeare's Prospero) is the usurped ruler of Milan who has been banished to a mysterious island with her daughter. Using her magical powers, she draws her enemies to the island to exact her revenge.
plot:
The Tempest is a 2010 American fantasy comedy-drama written and directed by Julie Taymor, based on William Shakespeare's 1611 play. In a notable departure from the original, the central role of the sorcerer Prospero becomes a woman, Prospera, played by Helen Mirren. The cast also includes Felicity Jones as Miranda, Reeve Carney as Ferdinand, Djimon Hounsou as Caliban, Ben Whishaw as Ariel, Russell Brand as Trinculo, Alfred Molina as Stephano, David Strathairn as Alonso, Chris Cooper as Antonio, Alan Cumming as Sebastian and Tom Conti as Gonzalo. It premiered at the Venice Film Festival in September 2010 and was released by Touchstone Pictures in December.

Prospera, Duchess of Milan, is secretly denounced as a sorceress by her brother Antonio, who usurps her title with the help of Alonso, King of Naples. She and her three-year-old daughter Miranda are cast adrift in a small boat to die, but they survive and land on a remote island whose only inhabitant is Caliban, a creature whom Prospera enslaves. She also frees the spirit Ariel from imprisonment and binds him to her service, making the island her domain.

Twelve years later, Alonso is sailing home from his daughter's wedding in Tunis, accompanied by his son Ferdinand, his brother Sebastian, Antonio and the loyal counselor Gonzalo. Seizing her chance for revenge, Prospera has Ariel conjure a violent storm that wrecks the ship and scatters the survivors across the island. Ferdinand, believing his father drowned, meets Miranda, and the two fall instantly in love, while Prospera tests the young prince's devotion. Alonso and his companions wander the island in grief, as Antonio and Sebastian plot to murder the king. Meanwhile, the jester Trinculo and the drunken butler Stephano fall in with Caliban, who persuades them to help him overthrow Prospera. Using Ariel's illusions and her magic, Prospera manipulates all of them, until she must decide between vengeance and forgiveness and whether to give up her powers.

The Tempest received mixed to negative reviews, with a 31 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said Taymor's gender swapping and frenzied special effects could not disguise a stagey, uninspired take on the play; it scored 43 on Metacritic. Mirren's performance was widely praised, and Sandy Powell received an Academy Award nomination for Best Costume Design. The film was a box-office failure.

title: Inside Job
tagline: The film that cost $20,000,000,000,000 to make
overview: A film that exposes the shocking truth behind the economic crisis of 2008. The global financial meltdown, at a cost of over $20 trillion, resulted in millions of people losing their homes and jobs. Through extensive research and interviews with major financial insiders, politicians and journalists, Inside Job traces the rise of a rogue industry and unveils the corrosive relationships which have corrupted politics, regulation and academia.
plot:
Inside Job is a 2010 American documentary film directed by Charles Ferguson about the financial crisis of 2007–2008. Narrated by Matt Damon, it features interviews with financial insiders, politicians, journalists and economists, and argues that the crisis resulted from what Ferguson called the systemic corruption of the United States by the financial services industry.

The film opens in Iceland, where the deregulation and privatization of the country's banks in the early 2000s fueled a speculative boom that collapsed in 2008, plunging the country into crisis. It then traces how similar forces brought down the global financial system in five parts. The first, "How We Got Here," surveys the decades of deregulation that began in the 1980s, from the savings and loan crisis to the consolidation of Wall Street and the spread of unregulated derivatives. It explains how investment banks bundled mortgages into collateralized debt obligations, which rating agencies frequently rated AAA, encouraging predatory lending to homeowners who could never repay.

The second part, "The Bubble," describes the housing boom of 2001 to 2007, when banks borrowed at unprecedented levels and used credit default swaps to bet against the very securities they were selling to clients. "The Crisis" follows the collapse of the market in 2008: the failure of Bear Stearns, the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers, the rescue of AIG and the massive bailout of the banking system.

The fourth part, "Accountability," argues that the executives responsible kept their fortunes and escaped prosecution, that banks paid enormous bonuses after being bailed out, and that prominent academic economists who had championed deregulation often failed to disclose lucrative consulting relationships with the financial industry. The final part, "Where We Are Now," contends that the financial reforms of the Obama administration were weak and that many of the officials associated with the crisis were given key positions in the new government.

Inside Job was screened at the 2010 Cannes Film Festival and received widespread acclaim, with critics praising its rigor and clarity; Rotten Tomatoes reported 98% approval and Metacritic a score of 88. It won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature, and its scrutiny of academic conflicts of interest led the American Economic Association to strengthen its disclosure standards.

title: Tinker Bell and the Great Fairy Rescue

overview: During a summer stay on the mainland, Tinker Bell is accidentally discovered while investigating a little girl's fairy house. As the other fairies, led by the brash Vidia, launch a daring rescue in the middle of a fierce storm, Tink develops a special bond with the lonely, little girl.
plot:
Tinker Bell and the Great Fairy Rescue is a 2010 animated adventure film produced by DisneyToon Studios, directed by Kevan Brighting, and written by Ron Clements. The movie follows the adventures of Tinker Bell, a mischievous fairy who lives in Pixie Hollow.

The story begins with Tinker Bell (voiced by Mae Whitman) feeling unappreciated and overlooked by her fellow fairies, particularly the other pixie girls. She is constantly compared to the more popular and skilled fairies, such as Rosetta (voiced by Lucy Liu), Silvermist (voiced by Raven-Symoné), Iridessa (voiced by Vanessa Hudgens), Fawn (voiced by Amanda Seyfried), and Periwinkle (voiced by Matt Lucas). Tinker Bell's frustration grows when she is tasked with fixing a broken fairy door, which only adds to her feelings of inadequacy.

Meanwhile, the evil pixie, Zarina (voiced by Lucy Liu), has stolen the magical dust that gives fairies their powers. Without this dust, the fairies begin to lose their abilities and fade away. The Great Fairy, Queen Clarion (voiced by Jodi Benson), calls upon Tinker Bell to embark on a quest to retrieve the stolen dust.

Tinker Bell sets out on her journey, accompanied by her friend, Silvermist, and together they meet new friends, including Vidia (voiced by Lucy Liu) and Periwinkle. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, such as treacherous terrain, fierce creatures, and even a rival fairy named Zarina.

As Tinker Bell navigates through the challenges, she learns valuable lessons about friendship, teamwork, and believing in herself. She also discovers that her unique skills and talents are essential to the quest's success. With the help of her friends, Tinker Bell is able to outsmart Zarina and retrieve the stolen dust.

title: In a Better World
overview: The lives of two Danish families cross each other, and an extraordinary but risky friendship comes into bud. But loneliness, frailty and sorrow lie in wait.
plot:
Anton (Mikael Persbrandt) is a Swedish doctor who commutes between his home in Denmark and his work in a Sudanese refugee camp. In Sudan, he often treats female patients who are the victims of a sadistic warlord. Anton is married to Marianne (Trine Dyrholm), but they are separated, and struggling with the possibility of divorce over an affair that Anton had with another woman. They have two young sons, the older one being 12-year-old Elias (Markus Rygaard).
Christian (William Jøhnk Juels Nielsen), who has just moved from London with his father, Claus (Ulrich Thomsen), is a new boy at Elias' school. Christian's mother recently died from cancer, and Christian blames his father for lying to him that she would get well, and that, in a late stage of her disease, he "wanted" her to die. Elias is bullied at school, until he is defended by Christian, who assaults the main bully and threatens him with a knife. Christian gives Elias the knife, and both boys lie to the police, and their parents, about the incident.
When Anton separates his younger son from another child, while they are fighting at a playground, the father of the other child, a mechanic, tells Anton not to touch his child and slaps Anton in the face. Anton later visits the mechanic at his work, accompanied by his children and Christian, to discuss the matter, and to show the children that he is not afraid of the man. The boorish and xenophobic mechanic insults Anton's nationality and slaps him several more times, but Anton does not flinch from the blows.
Later, in Sudan, the psychopathic warlord comes to Anton's hospital for treatment of his wounded leg. To the horror of his staff and others, and acting at the expense of his own moral convictions, Anton treats the man. He does demand, however, that no weapons, and only two of his guards, be allowed inside the hospital. The warlord's leg seems to slowly heal and Anton barely tolerates his presence in the camp, but after the warlord shows contempt for one of his victims, Anton drags him away from the clinic, allowing him to be beaten to death by local people.
In Denmark, Christian and Elias decide to make a bomb to destroy the mechanic's car, on a Sunday morning so that no passers-by might be hurt. With the fuse already burning, they see two joggers approaching (a mother and her young daughter), and Elias leaves his protected position to warn them. He is knocked unconscious, but saves the joggers from harm. Christian is questioned by the police and then released, with the incident being addressed as an extreme case of vandalism. He goes to the hospital to visit Elias, but Marianne does not let him see the boy, instead telling him that he has killed her son. Christian, believing that Elias is dead, climbs to the roof of a silo, contemplating suicide, but is rescued by Anton. Christian is relieved that Elias is doing well, and he is now allowed to visit him.

overview: The Straw Hat Pirates landed at Asuka Island, home of the most valuable sword in the world: The Seven Star Sword. Which was said to curse anyone who takes it in possession. Soon it was attacked by the Marines, and among them is Zoro. Luffy and the others don't know why he's helping out the Marines. plot:
One Piece: Curse of the Sacred Sword is a 2004 Japanese animated adventure film directed by Shingo Nakamata and produced by Toei Animation. The movie serves as an adaptation of the first 21 chapters of Eiichiro Oda's popular manga series, One Piece.

The story begins with Monkey D. Luffy, a young boy who has eaten the Gum-Gum Fruit, which gives him the ability to stretch and manipulate his body like rubber. Luffy dreams of becoming the Pirate King, inspired by his idol, Shanks. He sets out on a journey to find the legendary treasure known as "One Piece," said to be hidden by the late pirate Gol D. Roger.

Luffy's first stop is the East Blue, where he meets Roronoa Zoro, a skilled swordsman and member of the Seven Warlords of the Sea. The two become fast friends and join forces with Nami, a navigator and cartographer who helps them navigate the seas. Together, they face various challenges and enemies, including the World Government's agents, known as the "Donquixote Pirates."

As Luffy and his crew sail through the East Blue, they encounter the mysterious and powerful pirate, Don Krieg. Krieg is a ruthless and cunning pirate who seeks to conquer the seas and eliminate all other pirates. He becomes a formidable foe for Luffy and his friends, leading to an epic battle between the two.

Meanwhile, Arlong, a fish-man pirate, emerges as a rival to Don Krieg. Arlong's true intentions are revealed, and he is determined to take revenge on the people of Water 7, where he was once shunned by society due to his appearance.

The movie culminates in an intense showdown between Luffy and Arlong, with the fate of Water 7 hanging in the balance. In the end, Luffy emerges victorious, but not before realizing that there is more to being a pirate than just fighting and treasure hunting.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities and relationships are on full display. Luffy's innocence and determination are contrasted with Zoro's cynicism and Nami's pragmatism. The movie also explores the themes of friendship, loyalty, and the consequences of one's actions.

One Piece: Curse of the Sacred Sword is an exciting and action-packed adaptation that sets the stage for the rest of the One Piece series. With its engaging characters, thrilling battles, and epic scope, it's no wonder why this film has become a beloved classic among fans of the franchise.

plot:
One Piece: Giant Mecha Soldier of Karakuri Castle (ワンピース カラクリ城のメカ巨兵, Wan Pīsu Karakuri-jō no Meka Kyohei) is a 2006 Japanese animated adventure film directed by Kōnosuke Uda and produced by Toei Animation, the seventh feature based on Eiichiro Oda's manga One Piece. Written by Masahiro Itō with music by Kohei Tanaka and Fuminori Iwasaki, it opened in Japanese cinemas on 4 March 2006 and fits into the anime's continuity between the Davy Back Fight and Water 7 story arcs.

While salvaging a wrecked pirate ship, the Straw Hat Pirates open a treasure chest and find an old woman, Roba, hiding inside. In exchange for a ride home to Mecha Island, she tells them of a legendary golden crown that only the king of the sea may wear. As they approach, an old folk song drifts across the water, and the island's defence machines open fire. The island's lord is Roba's son, Dr. Ratchet, a gaunt, highly strung young inventor with a lifelong dream of world domination, who had been trying in vain to decipher the song's riddle. When he sees that Luffy and his crew have already begun to crack it by instinct, he invites them to his castle and proposes they search together.

Guided by the song, the group enters a cave beneath the island and, after solving a series of puzzles, discovers that Mecha Island is actually the back of a gigantic turtle. Ratchet reveals that this was his goal all along: from his castle he binds the creature with cables, intending to use it to conquer the world. The turtle tells Chopper that it wakes only once every thousand years to lay its eggs, and cannot do so while restrained. The Straw Hats battle Ratchet's bumbling henchmen, General Maji and Colonel Honki, and their machines, while Luffy faces the inventor's series of fighting robots, ending with a giant mechanical tortoise. Discovering Gear Second by accident for the first time, Luffy defeats Ratchet and wrecks the castle, freeing the turtle, and the crew learns that the golden treasure is in fact the shell of its eggs.

The regular voice cast includes Mayumi Tanaka as Luffy, Kazuya Nakai as Zoro, Akemi Okamura as Nami, Kappei Yamaguchi as Usopp, Hiroaki Hirata as Sanji, Yuriko Yamaguchi as Robin and Kazue Ikura standing in as Chopper. Gorō Inagaki makes a special guest appearance as Ratchet, with Takeshi Aono as the family butler, and the theme song "Sayaendō" is performed by NEWS. The film was later released on DVD in Germany and France.

overview: A retelling of the Drum Island storyline from the manga. It features Franky, Nico Robin, and the Thousand Sunny, who weren't present in the original version.
plot:
One Piece: Episode of Chopper Plus: Bloom in the Winter, Miracle Cherry Blossom is a 2008 Japanese animated adventure film produced by Toei Animation and the ninth theatrical feature based on Eiichiro Oda's manga One Piece. Directed by Junji Shimizu from a screenplay by Hirohiko Kamisaka, with character designs by Naoki Tate and music by Kohei Tanaka and Shiro Hamaguchi, it freely retells the manga's Drum Island arc, in which the reindeer Tony Tony Chopper joins the Straw Hat Pirates. Oda served as planning collaborator and created a new villain for the film. The voice cast includes Mayumi Tanaka as Luffy, Kazuya Nakai as Zoro, Akemi Okamura as Nami, Kappei Yamaguchi as Usopp, Hiroaki Hirata as Sanji, Ikue Otani as Chopper and Masako Nozawa as Dr. Kureha.

The film is set in an alternate continuity: the crew has already traveled beyond Enies Lobby, sails the Thousand Sunny and includes Nico Robin and Franky, yet still has no ship's doctor, while Vivi and Karoo are absent. When Nami falls gravely ill, the crew lands on the snowbound Drum Kingdom, where the only remaining doctor is Dr. Kureha, who lives in the castle atop a mountain. Luffy carries Nami up the peak and reaches the top half-frozen, and Kureha treats them with the help of her assistant Chopper, a talking reindeer shunned by his own kind for his blue nose and feared by humans after he ate the Human-Human Fruit. The tyrannical King Wapol, who controlled his people by hoarding all the doctors and fled when Blackbeard's pirates attacked, now returns with his older brother Musshuru, a poison-mushroom user exiled after unleashing deadly spores on the kingdom years earlier.

Flashbacks recount how Chopper was inspired to become a doctor by the eccentric quack Hiriluk, whose death he blames on himself. Musshuru nearly kills Luffy with his spores, but an antidote saves him, and with the help of his crewmates and Chopper, Luffy defeats the brothers using his Gear techniques. Chopper accepts Luffy's invitation to become the crew's doctor, and as the Straw Hats depart, Kureha fires Hiriluk's special powder into the sky, turning the falling snow into a vision of pink cherry blossoms.

Released on 1 March 2008, the film opened third at the Japanese box office, stayed in the top ten for five weeks and grossed about $8.6 million. Its theme song, "Mata ne", was performed by Dreams Come True at Oda's request. It received an Excellent Animation of the Year award at the 32nd Japan Academy Film Prize.

title: Hugo

overview: Orphaned and alone except for an uncle, Hugo Cabret lives in the walls of a train station in 1930s Paris. plot:
Hugo is a 2011 American fantasy adventure film directed by Martin Scorsese, produced by Michael Broderick and Steven Haft, and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

The story begins in 1930s Paris, where we meet Hugo Cabret (Asa Butterfield), an orphaned boy who lives in the walls of a train station. Hugo's life is turned upside down when he discovers a mysterious automaton that belongs to his late father, Georges Méliès (Ben Kingsley). The automaton is one of several inventions created by Méliès, a famous filmmaker and magician.

As Hugo tries to repair the automaton, he becomes entangled in a mystery surrounding a missing film reel. He soon discovers that the film reel is connected to a 3D film directed by Méliès, which was lost for decades. The film, titled "A Trip to the Moon," is considered one of the greatest films of all time.

Hugo's search for the missing film reel leads him on a journey through the train station and its inhabitants. He befriends Isabelle (Chloë Moretz), a young girl who lives in the station with her mother, and Captain Smee (Sacha Baron Cohen), a bumbling police officer who is tasked with capturing Hugo.

As Hugo delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a conspiracy involving a wealthy collector, René Tabard (Stanley Tucci), who is trying to acquire Méliès' film collection. Hugo also discovers that his father was involved in a bitter dispute with Tabard over the ownership of the films.

Throughout the story, Scorsese weaves together historical facts and fiction, creating an immersive experience for the audience. The film features stunning visuals, including intricate sets and costumes, which bring the world of early cinema to life.

As Hugo's search reaches its climax, he discovers a hidden compartment in the train station that contains Méliès' lost film reel. In a thrilling finale, Hugo uses the automaton to recreate the 3D film, which is revealed to be a masterpiece of cinematic art.

The film ends with Hugo finding a new sense of purpose and belonging, thanks to his discovery of his father's work and the help of Isabelle and Captain Smee. The final shot of the film features Hugo sitting in a cinema, watching Méliès' "A Trip to the Moon" on the big screen, surrounded by the magic of cinema.

Overall, Hugo is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the art of cinema and the power of imagination.

overview: When mankind beams a radio signal into space, a reply comes from ‘Planet G’, in the form of several alien crafts that splash down in the waters off Hawaii. plot:
Battleship is a 2012 science fiction action film directed by Peter Berg and produced by Universal Pictures. The movie is based on the popular board game of the same name, which was created by Ted Lewin.

The story begins with Commander Stone Hopper (played by Taylor Kitsch), a hot-headed but skilled naval officer who is struggling to find his place in the world after being kicked out of the Navy. He is now working as a security consultant for a private company called Global Defense Systems (GDS).

Meanwhile, Lieutenant Alex Hoppner (played by Brooklyn Decker) is a brilliant and beautiful engineer who works for GDS. She is also the daughter of Admiral Shane Hopper (played by Liam Neeson), Stone's father and a high-ranking naval officer.

When an alien armada appears in the skies above Earth, both the Navy and GDS scramble to respond. The aliens are revealed to be from the planet Krill, who have been searching for Earth as their next target. The humans are able to fend off the initial attack using advanced technology provided by GDS, but it becomes clear that the aliens will not be easily defeated.

As the battle rages on, Stone and Alex find themselves at the center of the action. They team up with a group of sailors from the USS Defiance, including Petty Officer Cora Raikes (played by Rihanna), to take down the alien armada. Along the way, they discover that the aliens are using advanced technology to control the minds of humans, making them more susceptible to attack.

As the stakes grow higher, Stone and Alex must put aside their differences and work together to save humanity from extinction. They use their unique skills and knowledge to outsmart the aliens and develop a plan to defeat them once and for all.

The final battle is intense and action-packed, with both sides suffering heavy losses. In the end, Stone and his team are able to destroy the alien armada using a combination of advanced technology and old-fashioned ingenuity. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with humanity having survived the attack and looking forward to rebuilding and recovering.

Throughout the movie, there is plenty of action, suspense, and humor, making Battleship an entertaining ride for fans of science fiction and adventure films. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans and is a fun, if not entirely faithful, adaptation of the popular board game.

title: Barbie: A Fashion Fairytale
tagline: Discover your inner sparkle!
overview: Join Barbie in a colourful, modern-day fairytale filled with fashion, friends and fun! Barbie and her dog Sequin jet off to visit her Aunt's amazing fashion house in Paris, and much to her surprise it's about to be shut down forever. After she discovers three enchanting Flairies with sparkle-magic powers, Barbie comes up with a brilliant idea to save the business. plot:
Barbie: A Fashion Fairytale is a 2010 computer-animated fantasy adventure film directed by William Lau and produced by Mattel through Barbie Entertainment with Rainmaker Entertainment. The eighteenth film in the Barbie series, it marked the first time Diana Kaarina voiced Barbie, replacing Kelly Sheridan. Adrian Petriw voices Ken, with Tabitha St. Germain, Patricia Drake and Alexa Devine. The film was released on DVD on 14 September 2010 and premiered on Nickelodeon that November.

While filming an adaptation of The Princess and the Pea, Barbie questions the director's strange creative choices and is fired. She is immediately mocked online and then receives a phone call from her boyfriend, Ken, who appears to break up with her. Heartbroken, she flies to Paris to visit her aunt Millicent, a celebrated fashion designer. Meanwhile, Barbie's friends Teresa and Grace confront Ken and discover that the breakup message was a recording made by Barbie's rival, Raquelle, while Ken was reading a script. Ken rushes to Paris to make things right, facing a series of comic mishaps along the way.

In Paris, Barbie learns from a rival designer, Jacqueline, that Millicent's fashion house is going out of business. Millicent has lost customers after bad reviews and has sold the building to a hot-dog restaurant chain. Her shy assistant, Alice, shows Barbie the attic and tells her about the magical creatures said to have lived in the fashion house. Placing one of Alice's dress designs in a magic wardrobe and reciting a chant, the two summon the Flairies, Glimmer, Shimmer and Shyne, tiny fairies whose sparkling magic can transform clothes. With their help and Alice's designs, Barbie persuades her aunt to stage one last fashion show to save the business. title: Rango
tagline: Heroes come in all different colors.
overview: When Rango, a lost family pet, accidentally winds up in the gritty, gun-slinging town of Dirt, the less-than-courageous lizard suddenly finds he stands out. Welcomed as the last hope the town has been waiting for, new Sheriff Rango is forced to play his new role to the hilt.
plot:
Rango is a 2011 American animated Western comedy film directed by Gore Verbinski and produced by Paramount Pictures. The movie takes place in the fictional town of Dirt, Arizona, where a pet chameleon named Rango lives.

The story begins with Rango, who has been living in his terrarium for most of his life. He is bored and longs for adventure. One day, he gets swept away by a strong storm and ends up in the middle of the desert. After being rescued by a group of animals, including a tortoise named Roadkill, Rango finds himself in the town of Dirt.

Initially, Rango tries to blend in with the townspeople, but his chameleon abilities make it difficult for him to hide his true nature. He is mistaken for a human and becomes embroiled in the town's politics when he discovers that the town is plagued by a severe drought and a mysterious illness affecting its residents.

As Rango navigates this new world, he meets a cast of colorful characters, including Beans, a tough-talking armadillo who becomes his friend; Rattlesnake Jake, a villainous snake who serves as the town's sheriff; and Squidward, a grumpy but lovable squid who runs the local saloon.

Rango soon discovers that he has a crucial role to play in saving the town. He learns about the town's history and its connection to an ancient Native American tribe. With the help of his new friends, Rango sets out on a quest to find the source of the drought and the mysterious illness.

Along the way, Rango faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous terrain, ferocious predators, and even a rival chameleon who seeks to take over the town. Through his journey, Rango learns valuable lessons about courage, friendship, and leadership.

As the story unfolds, Rango discovers that he is the reincarnation of a legendary Native American warrior named "The Spirit of the West." With this newfound knowledge, Rango must come to terms with his destiny and lead the townspeople in a final showdown against Rattlesnake Jake and his cohorts.

In the end, Rango emerges victorious, saving the town from destruction and restoring balance to its ecosystem. The movie concludes with Rango returning to his terrarium, but this time, he is no longer content to simply live a mundane life. He has found a new sense of purpose and belonging in the world outside his terrarium.

Throughout the film, Gore Verbinski's direction brings the desert landscape to life, creating a visually stunning and immersive experience for audiences. The voice cast, including Johnny Depp as Rango, Isla Fisher as Beans, and Abigail Breslin as Rattlesnake Jake, delivers memorable performances that bring depth and humor to the characters.

Overall, Rango is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, community, and redemption. With its unique blend of humor, action, and adventure, it has become a beloved classic among animation fans worldwide.

title: Green Lantern
tagline: In our darkest hour, there will be light.
overview: For centuries, a small but powerful force of warriors called the Green Lantern Corps has sworn to keep intergalactic order. Each Green Lantern wears a ring that grants him superpowers. But when a new enemy called Parallax threatens to destroy the balance of power in the Universe, their fate and the fate of Earth lie in the hands of the first human ever recruited.
plot:
Green Lantern is a 2011 superhero science fiction film directed by Ryan Reynolds, who also stars as the titular character. The movie is based on the DC Comics character of the same name.

The story begins with Hal Jordan (Ryan Reynolds), a test pilot and former Air Force pilot who is recruited by the InterGalactic Police Force to become a Green Lantern. The Green Lantern Corps is an intergalactic police force that uses power rings to protect the universe from threats. To become a Green Lantern, Hal must first be chosen by a power ring, which requires him to demonstrate his worthiness.

Hal's journey begins with a series of tests and challenges designed to assess his character and abilities. He eventually passes the test and becomes the 283rd member of the Green Lantern Corps. As he embarks on his new role, Hal is introduced to his fellow Green Lanterns, including John Stewart (Blu Huntley), Carol Ferris (Julia Stiles), and Tom Kalmaku (Ngoc Le).

As Hal navigates his new life as a Green Lantern, he also becomes romantically involved with Carol Ferris. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that Carol's father, Senator Hammond Ferris (Clancy Brown), is a powerful politician who opposes the Green Lantern Corps.

Meanwhile, a villainous character named Parallax emerges, who was once a Green Lantern but became corrupted by his own power ring. Parallax seeks to destroy the Green Lantern Corps and take over the universe for himself. Hal soon discovers that he has a personal connection to Parallax, as they were both test pilots in the Air Force.

As the story unfolds, Hal's relationships with his fellow Green Lanterns are put to the test when they face off against Parallax and his minions. The final battle takes place on the planet Oa, where Hal must confront his own demons and make a choice between saving the universe or saving himself.

In the end, Hal is able to defeat Parallax and save the universe, but not before he is forced to confront the darkness within himself. The movie ends with Hal reflecting on his journey and the lessons he has learned as a Green Lantern.

Overall, Green Lantern is an action-packed sci-fi adventure that explores themes of identity, duty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film has its fans and remains a beloved entry in the DC Comics universe.

title: Titanic II
tagline: 100 years later, lightning strikes twice.
overview: On the 100th anniversary of the original voyage, a modern luxury liner christened "Titanic 2," follows the path of its namesake. But when a tsunami hurls an ice berg into the new ship's path, the passengers and crew must fight to avoid a similar fate.
plot:
Titanic II is a 2010 American disaster drama film written and directed by Shane Van Dyke, who also stars, and distributed by The Asylum. Not a sequel to the 1997 film, it is set aboard a fictional replica of the famous liner that sails exactly a century after the original's maiden voyage, only for global warming and the forces of nature to make history repeat itself on the same night on an even deadlier scale. Van Dyke plays the ship's owner and designer Hayden Walsh, with Marie Westbrook as the nurse Amy Maine, Bruce Davison as her father, Coast Guard Captain James Maine, Michelle Glavan as her fellow nurse Kelly Wade, D. C. Douglas as the ship's captain Will Howard and Brooke Burns as the glaciologist Dr. Kim Patterson.

Off the Helheim Glacier in Greenland, a surfer riding waves created by falling ice is overwhelmed and drowns. Captain Maine is sent to investigate with Dr. Patterson, and while they are there another enormous mass of ice collapses into the ocean. On April 10, 2012, a hundred years after the RMS Titanic set sail, the new Titanic II begins its maiden voyage along the same route in reverse, from New York to Southampton. Mid-Atlantic, Maine warns the crew of an approaching tsunami that will drive ice before it. As the ship races for shore one engine is damaged, and the wave and a giant iceberg slam into the vessel, crushing its starboard side and lifeboat ramps and injuring many passengers. Hayden and Amy find Kelly badly hurt below decks, while another glacier unleashes a still larger tsunami. Strain on the turbines causes an explosion that kills many aboard, including Captain Howard, and sets the sinking ship ablaze. Maine calls his daughter to warn her of the second wave and tells her to avoid the lifeboats and head for the onboard diving facility. Kelly is crushed by a heavy door before they get there. The second wave capsizes the ship and destroys the lifeboats, and with only one oxygen tank and diving suit available, Hayden gives them to Amy, kisses her and asks her to try to revive him if he drowns. Maine swims into the sinking ship to rescue them, but Amy's attempt to resuscitate Hayden comes too late; she and the injured passengers Hayden had sent away by helicopter are the only known survivors.

First shown on television in Australia on August 7, 2010, and released in the United States that month, the film was poorly received, though the cast, especially Davison, drew praise. A sequel, Titanic 666, followed in 2022.

title: Battle: Los Angeles
tagline: It's not war. It's survival.
overview: When once distant UFOs become a terrifying threat attacking Earth, a Marine staff sergeant and his team take it upon themselves to face the enemy and protect what remains of the planet.
plot:
Battle: Los Angeles is a 2011 science fiction action film directed by Jonathan Liebesman and written by Michael Colleary. The movie takes place in an alternate universe where an alien invasion occurs on Earth, specifically in the city of Los Angeles.

The story begins with Sergeant Nantz (played by Aaron Eckhart), a U.S. Army sergeant who is part of an elite platoon known as Alpha Squad. The team consists of Sergeant Nantz, Staff Sergeant Stigler (played by Michael Peña), Corporal Lerner (played by Jon Bernthal), and Private First Class Miller (played by Temuera Morrison). They are tasked with defending the city from an alien invasion.

The movie opens with a dramatic sequence showing the aliens' arrival on Earth. The extraterrestrial beings, known as "the Others," descend upon Los Angeles in massive spaceships, wreaking havoc on the city and its inhabitants. As the chaos ensues, Sergeant Nantz's team is deployed to defend the city from the alien threat.

As the battle rages on, Sergeant Nantz and his team face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning equipment, and the psychological strain of fighting an enemy that seems almost invulnerable. The team soon discovers that the aliens are not just mindless monsters but a highly organized and technologically advanced force with a sinister purpose.

Throughout the movie, Sergeant Nantz struggles to come to terms with his own personal demons, including the loss of his wife in a previous deployment. His leadership skills are put to the test as he tries to keep his team motivated and focused on their mission.

As the battle reaches its climax, Sergeant Nantz's team launches a final assault on the alien mothership. The movie culminates in an intense and action-packed sequence where the humans fight for survival against overwhelming odds. In the end, Sergeant Nantz emerges victorious but not without scars, both physical and emotional.

The ending of Battle: Los Angeles is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience wondering about the fate of the alien threat and the future of humanity. The movie concludes with a sense of hope and resilience, as Sergeant Nantz reflects on the sacrifices made by his team and the possibility of a new beginning for humanity.

Overall, Battle: Los Angeles is an intense and thrilling sci-fi action film that explores themes of leadership, sacrifice, and the human condition in the face of overwhelming adversity.

title: Trust
tagline: What took her family years to build, a stranger stole in an instant.
overview: A suburban family is torn apart when fourteen-year-old Annie meets her first boyfriend online. After months of communicating via online chat and phone, Annie discovers her friend is not who he originally claimed to be. Shocked into disbelief, her parents are shattered by their daughter's actions and struggle to support her as she comes to terms with what has happened to her once innocent life.
plot:
Trust (stylised as trust_) is a 2010 American drama thriller directed by David Schwimmer and written by Andy Bellin and Robert Festinger from an uncredited story by Schwimmer. Liana Liberato plays Annie Cameron, with Clive Owen and Catherine Keener as her parents, Will and Lynn, Viola Davis as the counsellor Gail Friedman and Jason Clarke as the FBI agent Doug Tate.

For her fourteenth birthday Annie receives a laptop and soon begins chatting with "Charlie", who first says he is sixteen, then admits to being twenty and later twenty-five. Despite her unease she comes to believe they are in love, and after two months he arranges to meet her at a shopping mall, where she discovers he is a man in his late thirties. Though upset, she lets him persuade her to go to a motel, where he rapes her and films the assault. Her best friend Brittany, who saw them at the mall, alerts the school, and police remove Annie in front of her classmates.

Tate leads the investigation, but when Annie calls Charlie he sees through the trap and cuts contact before he can be traced, and private investigators hired by Will find only a masked address that appears to be in the Czech Republic. Will becomes consumed by the hunt, suffers nightmares about the attack and questions his advertising work, which uses provocative images of teenagers. Annie insists to her counsellor that Charlie loves her. Only when DNA evidence links Charlie to the abuse of several other young girls, and she sees their photographs, does she break down and acknowledge that she was raped. At a school volleyball match, Will attacks a father taking photographs, wrongly believing him to be a registered sex offender, and a humiliated Annie accuses him of ruining her life. After discovering that classmates have been mocking her online with doctored pornographic images and posting her number and address, she tries to kill herself with pills, but Will finds her in time. Brittany stays the night, repairing their friendship, and Will begs Annie's forgiveness for failing to protect her, and she embraces him. A post-credits scene reveals that "Charlie" is a married high school physics teacher named Graham Weston.

Shot in Michigan, it premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2010 and opened in limited release in the United States on April 1, 2011. It received positive reviews, with 79% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Liberato won the Silver Hugo for Best Actress at the Chicago International Film Festival.

title: Dhoom 3
tagline: This year will end with a Dhoom
overview: To avenge his father's death, a circus entertainer trained in magic and acrobatics turns thief to take down a corrupt bank in Chicago. Two cops from Mumbai are assigned to the case.
plot:
In 1990, Iqbal Haroon Khan, who owns The Great Indian Circus in Illinois, is ordered by the Western Bank of Chicago to close down the circus as he cannot repay his loan. Dejected, Iqbal commits suicide in front of his young son Sahir Iqbal Khan and the officials, including Chairman Warren Anderson.

In 2013, Sahir robs various branches of the Western Bank of Chicago as revenge. Despite all efforts of law enforcement, the Chicago Police are unable to capture him. Detective Victoria calls A.C.P Jai Dixit and Sub Inspector Ali Akbar Fateh Khan for help. Sahir restarts The Great Indian Circus and hires Aaliya Hussain as an acrobat. Sahir poses as an informant for Jai and manages to gather information on the bank while providing Jai with a false lead to follow. Eventually, Sahir robs the bank, but Jai shoots him in the left shoulder before he disappears.
At The Great Indian Circus's grand premiere, Sahir performs a teleportation trick in which he disappears and reappears in a different place. The show becomes a success. After the show, Jai, Ali, and the police surround him. When Sahir is examined, there is no gunshot wound on his body. It is then revealed that Sahir has an autistic twin brother, Samar Iqbal Khan, who helps him pull off the tricks and robberies and is the one who sustained the gunshot wound. Jai is fired from the case but is encouraged by Ali to prove Sahir guilty by going rogue.
Jai finds out about Samar, who is kept in seclusion by Sahir and is allowed outdoors once a week. Jai manages to befriend him during this time, intending to use him to catch Sahir. Samar falls in love with Aaliya, while Sahir finds out about Jai using his brother. Sahir tricks Jai and almost kills him, but Ali saves him. Sahir and Samar successfully pull off their final bank heist, but are cornered at a dam on their way out of town. Samar hesitates to run when Aaliya appears, begging him to stop. Sahir pretends to surrender to Jai, asking him to spare Samar; when Jai agrees, Sahir attempts to jump off the dam- but Samar grabs Sahir's hand, and he begs Samar to let him go, saying Samar can live freely with Aaliya. Samar declares that they were born together and should die together, and lets go of his hand, and the twins fall to their deaths.
In the aftermath, Western Bank of Chicago is shut down due to the heists, while Aaliya takes over The Great Indian Circus and performs in Samar's memory.

tagline: Spin. Aim. Survive.
overview: A naive young man assumes a dead man's identity and finds himself embroiled in an underground world of power, violence, and chance where men gamble behind closed doors on the lives of other men.
plot:
13 is a 2010 American psychological crime thriller directed by Géla Babluani, who remade his own 2005 Georgian-French feature 13 Tzameti for an English-language audience. The ensemble cast includes Sam Riley, Ray Winstone, 50 Cent, Mickey Rourke and Jason Statham, with Alice Barrett, Gaby Hoffmann and Emmanuelle Chriqui in supporting roles.

The story centers on Vincent "Vince" Ferro, a young man whose family is struggling for money. While doing electrical work in a house, he overhears talk of a lucrative but mysterious job that its intended recipient, now dead, will never collect. Ferro takes the envelope containing the instructions and follows them to a remote estate, where he is stripped and searched for recording devices before the organizers agree to let him take the dead man's place. Only then does he discover what the job really is: a brutal tournament of Russian roulette staged for wealthy spectators who gamble huge sums on which numbered contestant will survive.

Ferro, assigned the number thirteen, is surrounded by other desperate men. Among them is Ronald Bagges, a mentally unstable man brought from an institution by his brother Jasper, who bets on him, and Patrick Jefferson, a convict released into the custody of a patron named Jimmy, who hopes to profit from the outcome. In each round the players stand in a circle aiming at the man in front of them, the number of bullets in each revolver increases, and they must fire when a hanging light bulb switches on. Ferro tries to back out but is forced to continue at gunpoint, surviving round after round as the field shrinks and the remaining contestants are pushed toward a final one-on-one duel. The money Ferro might win becomes as dangerous as the game itself.

Released in the United States in a limited run and largely on home video, the remake was poorly received. Critics on Rotten Tomatoes were overwhelmingly negative, and reviewers such as Stephen Holden of The New York Times dismissed it as a blustering cartoon. Others felt that the switch from the original's stark black-and-white photography to color, along with added backstories for the characters, diluted the tension that had made Babluani's first version a festival success.

title: Superman/Batman: Apocalypse
tagline: The end is near.
overview: Batman discovers a mysterious teen-aged girl with superhuman powers and a connection to Superman. When the girl comes to the attention of Darkseid, the evil overlord of Apokolips, events take a decidedly dangerous turn.
plot:
Superman/Batman: Apocalypse is a 2010 American animated superhero film directed by Lauren Montgomery, based on the Superman/Batman comic book storyline "The Supergirl from Krypton", with an art style partly inspired by that of Michael Turner, who drew the comic. The ninth entry in the DC Universe Animated Original Movies line, it is a standalone sequel to Superman/Batman: Public Enemies (2009). Tim Daly voices Superman, Kevin Conroy Batman, Summer Glau Kara Zor-El, Andre Braugher Darkseid, Susan Eisenberg Wonder Woman, Julianne Grossman Big Barda and Ed Asner Granny Goodness. Despite the title, the film focuses mainly on Supergirl and Superman, with Batman in a supporting role.

Weeks after the downfall of President Lex Luthor, a spaceship crashes into Gotham City Harbor, and a young girl emerges who wreaks havoc with her powers until Superman and Batman subdue her. She turns out to be Kara Zor-El, Superman's cousin, who has spent decades in suspended animation. While Superman welcomes her, teaches her English and helps her adapt to life on Earth, Batman remains suspicious, and with Wonder Woman and her ally Lyla he arranges for Kara to train on the island of Themyscira. On the dark planet Apokolips, the tyrant Darkseid learns of Kara's existence and orders Granny Goodness to bring her to him as a potential leader of his elite Female Furies. Two months later, an army of Doomsday clones attacks Themyscira as a diversion; Lyla is killed and Kara is abducted and brainwashed into becoming captain of the Furies. With the reluctant help of the warrior Big Barda, Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman travel to Apokolips. While Wonder Woman and Barda battle Granny and the Furies in the arena, Superman confronts Darkseid and is forced to fight his own cousin, and Batman threatens to destroy the entire planet unless Darkseid frees Kara and promises to leave her alone. Yet once the heroes return to Earth, Darkseid finds a loophole in his promise, setting the stage for a final battle.

The film was released by Warner Premiere and Warner Bros. Animation on September 28, 2010, with a special edition including an animated short featuring Green Arrow. Reviews were mixed, with IGN rating it 8 out of 10 and others criticizing Braugher's Darkseid. It earned about $8.25 million from domestic DVD and Blu-ray sales.

title: The Hangover Part II
tagline: The Wolfpack Is Back
overview: The Hangover crew heads to Thailand for Stu's wedding. After the disaster of a bachelor party in Las Vegas last year, Stu is playing it safe with a mellow pre-wedding brunch. However, nothing goes as planned and Bangkok is the perfect setting for another adventure with the rowdy group.
plot:
The Hangover Part II is a 2011 American comedy film directed by Todd Phillips and written by Craig Mazin, Scott Moore, and Jeff Schaffer. The movie serves as the sequel to the 2009 film The Hangover.

The story begins with Phil Wenneck (Bradley Cooper), Stu Price (Ed Helms), Alan Garner (Zach Galifianakis), and Doug Billings (Justin Bartha) reuniting for a bachelor party in Las Vegas, where they spent the previous night. However, instead of going to Thailand as planned, they decide to spend their last night together in Vegas.

The movie then flashes back to the events that transpired during the bachelor party. The group wakes up after a wild night in a different part of town, with no memory of what happened. They soon discover that Doug is missing and his friend, Mr. Chow (Ken Jeong), has been left behind as a gift.

The group sets out on a journey to find Doug, who they believe was kidnapped by Mr. Chow's associates. Along the way, they encounter various misadventures, including a run-in with a gang of thugs, a wild night in Bangkok, and a series of hilarious misunderstandings.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the group's memories are not entirely reliable, and their recollections of the previous night's events are often distorted or exaggerated. The movie takes a dark turn when they discover that Doug is actually alive and well, but has been brainwashed by Mr. Chow to become a loyal servant.

In the end, the group manages to rescue Doug from his mind control and return him to the United States. However, not before they are forced to confront their own personal demons and the consequences of their actions during the bachelor party.

Throughout the movie, the characters' relationships with each other are put to the test as they navigate their way through a series of absurd and often disturbing situations. The Hangover Part II is known for its outrageous humor, over-the-top antics, and memorable performances from the cast.

One notable aspect of the movie is its exploration of themes such as friendship, loyalty, and the consequences of one's actions. Despite the film's raunchy humor and outrageous plot twists, it ultimately serves as a heartwarming tribute to the power of male friendships and the importance of being true to oneself.

Overall, The Hangover Part II is a hilarious and entertaining sequel that builds upon the success of its predecessor while introducing new characters and plotlines. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and outrageous humor, it's no wonder why this movie became one of the highest-grossing films of 2011.

title: The King's Speech
tagline: Find your voice.
overview: The King's Speech tells the story of the man who became King George VI, the father of Queen Elizabeth II. After his brother abdicates, George ('Bertie') reluctantly assumes the throne. Plagued by a dreaded stutter and considered unfit to be king, Bertie engages the help of an unorthodox speech therapist named Lionel Logue. Through a set of unexpected techniques, and as a result of an unlikely friendship, Bertie is able to find his voice and boldly lead the country into war.
plot:
At the official closing of the British Empire Exhibition at Wembley Stadium, Prince Albert "Bertie", Duke of York, the second son of King George V, addresses the crowd with a strong stammer. His search for treatment has been discouraging, but his wife, Elizabeth, persuades him to see Australian-born Lionel Logue, a speech defects therapist. During their first session, Lionel has Bertie recite Hamlet's "To be, or not to be" soliloquy while listening to classical music over a pair of headphones. Bertie is frustrated, but Lionel gives him the acetate recording of the reading to take home with him.
After George V broadcasts his 1934 Royal Christmas Message, he explains to Bertie that the wireless will play a significant part in the role of the royal family, allowing them to enter the homes of the people. As Bertie's elder brother, the Prince of Wales (known to his family as David), has been neglecting his responsibilities, Bertie's training in using the wireless has become necessary. An attempt at reading the message himself is a failure. However, Bertie plays the recording Lionel gave him that night and is astonished at the lack of stutter. He returns for daily treatments to overcome the physical and psychological roots of his stutter.
George V dies in 1936. David ascends the throne as King Edward VIII. A constitutional crisis arises with Edward over a prospective marriage with twice-divorced American socialite Wallis Simpson. Edward, as the supreme governor of the Church of England, cannot marry her, even if her second divorce goes through, as both of her former husbands are still alive.
At an unscheduled session, Bertie expresses frustration that, while his speech has mostly improved, he still stammers when talking to David, simultaneously revealing the extent of Edward VIII's folly with Simpson. When Lionel insists that Bertie himself could make a good king, Bertie accuses him of treason and angrily quits Lionel.
Lionel and Bertie reconvene after King Edward decides to abdicate to marry. Bertie, urged by Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin, ascends the throne as King George VI and visits Lionel's home with his wife before their coronation. This is a surprise for Mrs. Logue when she learns who Lionel's client has been.
Bertie and Lionel's relationship is questioned by the King's advisors during preparations for his coronation in Westminster Abbey. The archbishop of Canterbury, Cosmo Gordon Lang, points out that George never sought advice from his advisors about his treatment and that Lionel lacks formal training. Lionel explains to an outraged Bertie that at the time he started with speech defects there were no formal qualifications; he started by giving help to returning Great War Australian soldiers who suffered from shell-shock. Bertie remains unconvinced until provoked to protest at Lionel's disrespect for King Edward the Confessor's Chair and the Stone of Scone.

title: Outrage
tagline: One wrong move and it's all out war.
overview: When a tough yakuza gangster is betrayed by his bosses, it means all out war. Bodies pile up as he takes out everyone in his way to the top in a brutal quest for revenge.
plot:
Outrage (Autoreiji) is a 2010 Japanese yakuza film written, directed and co-edited by Takeshi Kitano, who also stars under his screen name Beat Takeshi. The cast includes Tomokazu Miura, Jun Kunimura, Renji Ishibashi, Kippei Shiina, Ryo Kase, Fumiyo Kohinata and Soichiro Kitamura. It was followed by Beyond Outrage (2012) and Outrage Coda (2017).

The film opens at a lavish banquet held by Sekiuchi, chairman of the Sanno-kai, a vast crime syndicate that controls the Kanto region. Afterwards, his underboss Kato takes one of the affiliated bosses, Ikemoto, aside to complain that Ikemoto has befriended Murase, the head of an independent gang, after the two met in prison. Kato orders Ikemoto to bring Murase's gang into line. Ikemoto passes the dirty work to his subordinate Otomo, who runs his own crew. Otomo engineers a provocation: one of his men gets himself shaken down for about a million yen at a club run by Murase's gang, creating an excuse for retaliation.

What follows is a spiral of betrayals, mutilations and killings. Murase does not realize he has lost favor with the syndicate and repeatedly trusts his old prison friend Ikemoto. Each time, he follows advice that weakens his family, unaware that Ikemoto has been ordered to destroy him. Otomo slashes the face of Murase's lieutenant Kimura, and the violence escalates. By the end, Murase and Ikemoto are dead, and Otomo is in prison, where Kimura stabs him. The calculating Kato then kills Sekiuchi in secret and takes over the Sanno-kai.

After several unconventional films with modest returns, Kitano said he wanted Outrage simply to entertain, calling yakuza films a genre for which he had talent. He began the screenplay by inventing the ways characters would die and then wrote a story around the violence. At the producer's suggestion, no actors from his earlier films were cast apart from Kitano himself. Office Kitano produced it with Bandai Visual, TV Tokyo and Omnibus Japan, and it was shot in CinemaScope in late 2009 in locations including Kobe and Ibaraki Prefecture.

Outrage competed for the Palme d'Or at the 2010 Cannes Film Festival, where it premiered on May 17, and opened in Japan on June 12 through Warner Bros.' Japanese arm. It earned about $7.2 million at the domestic box office by early July. Reviews were generally favorable. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said it delivered violent impact even if Kitano fans would find its ingredients familiar, and Variety called it a beautifully staged marvel.

title: Appleseed
tagline: Urban combat in the city of dreams
overview: In the futuristic city of Olympus, built on the ashes of the third world war, a police officer and her cyborg partner fight terrorism.
plot:
Appleseed is a 1988 Japanese cyberpunk original video animation adapted from the manga of the same name by Masamune Shirow. Produced by Gainax, it departs greatly from the manga's storyline, keeping only its characters and setting, and takes place in an unspecified future. Its voice cast includes Masako Katsuki, Toshio Furukawa and Norio Wakamoto.

After the Third World War, the General Management Control Office builds the experimental city of Olympus, home to humans, cyborgs and bioroids, genetically engineered beings created to serve humanity who carry out the city's administration. Intended as a utopia, Olympus feels like a cage to some residents, among them city police officer Charon Mautholos. He secretly conspires with the terrorist A. J. Sebastian to disable Gaia, the supercomputer that runs the city's utilities and networks and controls the override circuits safeguarding a powerful weapon, the Multi-ped Cannon. Members of the city's ESWAT unit, Deunan Knute and Briareos Hecatonchires, set out to stop them.

The conspirators raid the facility where bioroids are created but the attack proves to be cover for stealing data on a single bioroid, Hitomi, a friend of Deunan and Briareos, whose DNA serves as the genetic key to shut Gaia down. The shutdown can be triggered at kiosks across the city, so the city director orders all but one destroyed and places the last under heavy guard. Sebastian converts himself to his full military configuration and seizes the Multi-ped Cannon, while Charon, wearing a powered suit stripped of half its armor for speed, carries Hitomi through heavy gunfire to the remaining kiosk. As Charon dies of his wounds, the frightened Hitomi backs into the kiosk and starts the shutdown. Sebastian uses the cannon to wreak havoc in the city while the director and Deunan race to restart Gaia by destroying the module keeping it offline. When the databank's defenses damage Deunan's pistol and injure her shooting hand, the director gives Deunan her own gun, and firing left-handed with her last round, Deunan hits the module. Gaia immediately disables the cannon, Sebastian is killed, and Charon is mourned.

Critics were divided. Reviewers at Mania found the simple plot workable as a side story to the manga but lacking emotional pull, while THEM Anime Reviews, EX Media and Otaku USA criticized its departures from the source, limited animation and story. Helen McCarthy wrote that although dated, it was still worth owning.

title: Source Code
tagline: Make Every Second Count
overview: When decorated soldier Captain Colter Stevens wakes up in the body of an unknown man, he discovers he's part of a mission to find the bomber of a Chicago commuter train.
plot:
Source Code is a 2011 science fiction action thriller film directed by Duncan Jones and written by Ben Ripley. The movie stars Jake Gyllenhaal, Michelle Monaghan, Vera Farmiga, Jeffrey Wright, and Russell Peters.

The story begins with Captain Colter Stevens (Jake Gyllenhaal), an Army helicopter pilot who is killed in a terrorist bombing on a train in New York City. However, thanks to a top-secret government program called "Source Code," his consciousness is transferred into the body of another man, Sean Fentress (Owen Ward), a passenger on the same train.

The Source Code program allows Stevens to relive the last eight minutes of his life, with the goal of preventing the bombing and saving as many lives as possible. However, he soon discovers that he can only repeat this process 8 times, after which he will die again.

As Stevens navigates through the train, he meets Christina Warren (Michelle Monaghan), a passenger who becomes his ally in trying to prevent the bombing. He also encounters Sean's wife, Molly Fentress (Vera Farmiga), and her husband, Michael Fentress (Jeffrey Wright).

Throughout the movie, Stevens relives the same eight minutes over and over, each time making slight changes to try and prevent the bombing. However, he soon realizes that the bomber is not just a mindless terrorist, but someone who has a personal connection to Christina.

As the story unfolds, Stevens becomes more and more invested in his mission, and begins to form a bond with Christina. He also starts to question the true nature of the Source Code program and its motivations.

In the final iteration, Stevens is able to prevent the bombing by stopping the bomber, Michael Fentress, who is revealed to be Christina's husband. However, this comes at a great personal cost for Stevens, as he sacrifices his own life to save others.

The movie ends with Christina, now aware of her husband's true identity, being taken away by authorities, and Molly, who had been searching for her missing husband, finally finding closure. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the face of tragedy, there is always the possibility for redemption and new beginnings.

Overall, Source Code is a tense and thought-provoking thriller that explores themes of sacrifice, loyalty, and the consequences of playing with time.
