title: The Boy Who Cried Werewolf
overview: A Californian family inherits a castle in Romania. This is especially exciting to the son, who is obsessed with monsters. And he is not disappointed.
plot:
Jordan Sands is an awkward and nerdy 17-year-old girl with a bad case of allergies who became the woman of the house after the recent death of her mother. Her father, David, struggles to make ends meet, while her 14-year-old brother Hunter (Chase Ellison) drives the family crazy with gory pranks as he loves monsters. They inherit their mother's great-uncle Dragomir Ducovic's castle in Wolfsberg, Romania, which they did not know existed. After arriving in Wolfsberg, they meet the strange and steely castle housekeeper, Madame Varcolac, whose name, when pronounced, causes a wolf to howl in the distance.
Meanwhile, the kids explore the town. Hunter learns about the "Wolfsberg Beast", a monster that protects both the castle and the town, and Jordan falls in love with the local butcher Goran. Varcolac discourages David from selling the property, but he decides to, so that they can end their financial struggles. He dates the bubbly real estate agent Paulina von Eckberg, who handles the selling and only appears at night.
While snooping around Dragomir's lab, Jordan accidentally steps on a vial of blood. Although Hunter pulls the bloody glass from her foot, her behavior changes. She becomes a carnivore (at the beginning of the film, she mentions having tofu stir-fry for dinner, because of her vegetarian diet), her senses heighten, gains a playful dog-like temperament, she plays with the dogs at a nearby park, her hair starts to curl up naturally, her allergies disappear, no longer needs glasses and starts to grow body hair rapidly. Hunter's friends explain that Jordan has become a werewolf due to either a bloodline curse, a werewolf bite or becoming infected with the blood of a werewolf. Hunter realizes it was the vial of blood, revealed to have been LB-217, short for "Lycanthrope Blood".
Jordan transforms into a werewolf, which Hunter witnesses. She holds back from attacking Hunter and flees. Hunter's friends reveal that there is no cure they know of, other than killing a werewolf with a silver bullet. Hunter refuses to do this. His friends warn that if Jordan is not cured by next sunrise, she will remain a werewolf, cursed to shift every night until she dies.
Hunter turns to Varcolac, who reveals that Dragomir was also a werewolf and was the famed "Wolfsberg Beast". Vampires attempted to take over the castle and rise to power, but Dragomir had stopped them before he was killed. Before his death, he had been working on a cure for lycanthropy. As Varcolac quickly gathers the ingredients for the treatment, Paulina captures the siblings, revealing herself as a vampire and the one who had killed Dragomir. She wants to take over the manor, but must kill Jordan first, as she is unable to take the castle as long as Dragomir's werewolf relatives are alive. Jordan is restrained in her werewolf form while Hunter escapes and leads David to the hideout, but they are also captured.

title: Alvin and the Chipmunks Meet the Wolfman
original_title: Alvin and the Chipmunks Meet the Wolfman
overview: It's the Chipmunks' third and final full-length feature! Alvin is struggling with nightmares of werewolves. Alvin believes that the new next-door neighbor Mr. Talbot is a werewolf. Of course, no one believes him. Meanwhile, the boys are working on the school production of Dr. Jekyll & Mr. Hyde. When Alvin blows up the school auditorium, he is expelled from the production. Theodore is put in to rise his lack of confidence. Alvin and Simon are trying to discover the secret of Mr. Talbot. Will the play go as planned or will the Chipmunks mess it up?!
plot:
Alvin and the Chipmunks Meet the Wolfman is a 2000 American animated musical comedy horror film produced by Bagdasarian Productions and Universal Cartoon Studios and released direct-to-video. It is the second Alvin and the Chipmunks direct-to-video film, after Alvin and the Chipmunks Meet Frankenstein (1999), and the final traditionally animated production featuring the characters, with animation by Tama Productions in Tokyo. Ross Bagdasarian Jr. and Janice Karman voice the Chipmunks and Chipettes, with Maurice LaMarche and Miriam Flynn joining the voice cast.

After watching a series of horror films, Alvin begins having nightmares about the Wolfman. He tells his brother Simon and their adoptive father, Dave Seville, that he is unsettled by their new neighbor, Lawrence Talbot, whom he suspects of hiding a monstrous secret. After Alvin causes an accident in the school auditorium and Miss Miller complains that the Chipettes were frightened by a mysterious presence while walking home with the Chipmunks, Dave and Principal Milliken take Alvin out of his starring role as Mr. Hyde in the school's production of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. The part goes to the shy Theodore to boost his confidence, Alvin is demoted to the role of the butler, and Dave confiscates his collection of monster memorabilia.

Alvin and Simon begin searching for proof that Talbot is a werewolf. Meanwhile, on his way home from seeing his crush Eleanor, Theodore is bitten by what he takes to be a large dog. The next morning, the formerly gentle chipmunk suddenly wants to eat meat, and at rehearsal he gives a terrifying performance as Mr. Hyde that wins great applause. Soon Theodore is transforming into a werewolf at night, though in that form he behaves like a harmless puppy, while by day he becomes rude and sarcastic. Realizing that their brother has been cursed with lycanthropy, Alvin and Simon try to find a cure and save the school play without Dave finding out. With no other options, they turn to the eccentric psychic Madame Raya for advice, whose predictions lead them deeper into the mystery of who is really behind the curse as the night of the play approaches.

The film was released on VHS and DVD by Universal Studios Home Video in August 2000. It continued the formula of Meet Frankenstein, pairing the Chipmunks with a classic Universal movie monster and incorporating several original songs.

title: Certified Copy
overview: In Tuscany to promote his latest book, a middle-aged English writer meets a French woman who leads him to the village of Lucignano.
plot:
British writer James Miller makes a stop in Arezzo, Tuscany, on a tour to promote his new book, Certified Copy, which argues that, in art, issues of authenticity are irrelevant because every reproduction is itself an original, and even the original is a copy of another form. A French antiques dealer, who is never named, attends the event with her 11-year-old son in order to have Miller sign several copies of the book she has purchased, but has to leave early because her son is hungry and becomes a distraction. She leaves her phone number with Miller's book's translator. Later, her son suggests that she is romantically interested in Miller, which she denies.
Miller and the woman later meet at her shop. Though she had intended for them to browse antiques together, he instead suggests that they go for a drive, as long as they are back for his 9 p.m. train. On their aimless trip, Miller signs six copies of his book for the woman, including a copy for her sister, Marie, in which he inscribes a note that the woman dislikes. The two debate the premise of his book, including the relationship between authenticity and simplicity. During the conversation, which occasionally becomes strained, Miller points out that even the Mona Lisa is a "copy" of the woman who modeled for the painting, real or imagined.
The woman takes Miller to an art museum to see another famous "copy", but he is uninterested, saying that he has already finished work on the book and is not interested in further examples. The woman becomes increasingly distraught as she complains about her rebellious son to Miller, but he attempts to rationalize her son's behavior, frustrating the woman.
At his insistence, they visit a nearby café for coffee. When Miller steps out to take a phone call, the café owner begins speaking to the woman, mistaking Miller for her husband. The antiques dealer plays along as the café owner espouses the importance of marriage, regardless of the flaws of one's partner. Miller returns and the woman tells him about the café owner's assumption of their relationship.
Once they leave the café, the nature of their discussion changes, and they begin to speak in a combination of French and English instead of just English (Miller states that he only learned French, not Italian, in school). They also begin to behave as though they are a married couple, referring to the woman's son as "our" son. She expresses unhappiness over their 15th wedding anniversary the previous night, during which he fell asleep while she was getting ready in the bathroom, and tells him his constant traveling for work has made him emotionally distant.
Walking through the city, they encounter an older couple and discuss their interpretations of a nearby statue. The older man pulls Miller aside and offers unsolicited "fatherly" advice: that a small gesture of affection could mend the rift between Miller and his wife.

Seventeen-year-old Joshua "Josh" McGuire, expedition bank-roller Carl and his girlfriend, Victoria "Vic", travel to the Esa'ala Cave, an underwater cave exploration site in Papua New Guinea. Josh's father, Frank, a master diver, has already established a forward base camp at a lower level inside the cave, where the team has been exploring for weeks. The team below prepares to dive into an unexplored area of the system.
While exploring the entrance to the new system, Judes loses use of her air mask, forcing Frank to buddy breathe. Judes panics and tries to keep the mask on, but Frank forces the mask off of her knowing he will not have enough air to make it back to the team. As Judes drowns, Josh watches on a monitor at "forward camp" and presumes the worst of his father. Frank reveals that Judes had dived in an exhausted state since they had to retrieve the extra bailout tanks, a task Josh did not do. Meanwhile, their above-ground crew realises that a big storm is preparing to hit their location. They attempt to warn the team below, but are unsuccessful.
Wanting to return to the surface, Josh climbs back with Luko, Liz, and J.D, but water begins rushing in from their exit. The storm has turned into a cyclone, causing flash floods that begin to fill the cave. As J.D. and Liz make their way up through "the elevator" (an area leading up to the main entrance of the cave), Josh is unable to leave his father and the dive team behind to their doom and turns back with Luko. They discover that Frank and the team have already evacuated their camp and are assisting Victoria as she climbs up out of the cavern. Josh leaps in to help, strapping a rope around a nearby boulder and forming a belay. Unfortunately, the boulder begins to give way. The water rushes through and forces Victoria and Josh to fall back down into the flooded base camp. Luko is injured when the boulder breaks loose, sealing the shaft and throwing him back down into the cavern. He is swept into an underwater tunnel.
The team decides to use the unexplored tunnel as an escape route from the flooding cavern. Before the team can leave, a severely injured and mutilated Luko surfaces. Seeing that his friend is in pain and near death, Frank mercifully drowns him.
The team makes it through to the other side of the system. Having refused to wear Judes' old wetsuit, Victoria suffers from the cold water. Meanwhile, George—an experienced, veteran diver—has become ill due to the dive and is dying, unbeknownst to the rest of the team. The team continues through the system, following the flow of water out toward the sea. George realises that he cannot continue and hides himself so as not to burden the rest of the team.
The team arrives at a seemingly dead end. A hole in the bottom of the cave separates them from the other side of their path. Josh fishes a line across and begins to transfer their gear and each other.

title: Hall Pass
tagline: One week. No rules.
overview: When best buds Rick and Fred begin to show signs of restlessness at home, their wives take a bold approach to revitalize their marriages, they grant the guys a 'hall pass'—one week of freedom to do whatever they want. At first, it seems like a dream come true, but they quickly discover that their expectations of the single life—and themselves—are completely and hilariously out of sync with reality.
plot:
Hall Pass is a 2011 American comedy produced and directed by Peter and Bobby Farrelly, who co-wrote it with Pete Jones. Owen Wilson and Jason Sudeikis star as Rick and Fred, with Jenna Fischer and Christina Applegate as their wives, Maggie and Grace. Richard Jenkins and Stephen Merchant also appear.

Rick and Fred are best friends in a Providence suburb whose marriages have gone stale. They openly long for their single days and their wives finally give each of them a "hall pass": one week off from marriage, during which they are free to sleep with anyone. With friends Gary, Flats and Hog Head, the husbands try to pick up women, with little success. Rick flirts with Leigh, a coffee shop waitress, angering her co-worker Brent, then falls asleep for hours in a gym hot tub. Maggie and Grace take hall passes of their own: Grace grows close to Gerry, a minor league ballplayer, and Maggie is drawn to his coach.

On day six, at a bar with the womanizing Coakley, Rick meets his children's babysitter, Paige, who has just turned 21 and is out with her aunt Meg. Rick turns Paige down in favor of Leigh. Fred's hotel date fizzles, but Meg later arrives and, mistaking him for Rick, seduces him. Maggie rebuffs the coach, while Grace sleeps with Gerry. Feeling guilty, she crashes her car on the way home. At Coakley's, Rick surprises himself by refusing Leigh because he loves Maggie. Learning of the accident, he rushes to find Fred, and a fight erupts with Brent, Meg's son, who is arrested at the hospital. Rick goes home and confesses to Maggie that he never used his pass and that she is the only woman he has ever been with. Maggie tells him she did not use hers either. Fred and Grace reconcile and agree to keep their secrets, though Fred soon lets slip what happened with Meg.

The Farrellys bought Jones's spec script in 2005. Although set in New England, it was shot in Atlanta in 2010, for Georgia's film incentives. Warner Bros. released it on February 25, 2011, and it opened at number one with $13.5 million before grossing $83.2 million worldwide on a $36 million budget. Reviews were mixed to negative. Rotten Tomatoes noted that the film defends traditional domestic values but lacks laughs, and Roger Ebert gave it two and a half stars out of four.

Cars 2 is a 2011 animated adventure comedy film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures.

However, things take a turn when Mater (voiced by Larry the Cable Guy), Lightning's best friend and tow truck, gets caught up in a spy plot involving the villainous Professor Zündapp (voiced by Peter Fonda) and his henchmen. Mater is recruited by the British Secret Service to help them infiltrate the World Grand Prix and gather intel on the nefarious plans of the evil organization.

The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, witty humor, and heartwarming moments as Mater forms new friendships and learns to trust himself.

As the story unfolds, Lightning McQueen discovers that Francesco is actually working for Professor Zündapp's organization, leading him to confront his rival in a thrilling finale. In the end, Lightning emerges victorious, but not without learning valuable lessons about friendship, loyalty, and staying true to oneself.

Overall, Cars 2 offers an exciting adventure filled with humor, heart, and stunning animation. The film explores themes of identity, friendship, and the importance of staying true to oneself, making it a delightful addition to the Cars franchise.

overview: Vlad Tepes is a great hero, but when he learns the Sultan is preparing for battle and needs to form an army of 1,000 boys, he vows to find a way to protect his family. Vlad turns to dark forces in order to get the power to destroy his enemies and agrees to go from hero to monster as he's turned into the mythological vampire, Dracula.
plot:
Dracula Untold is a 2014 action-horror film directed by Gary Shore and produced by Universal Pictures. The movie serves as a prequel to the classic Bram Stoker novel, exploring the origins of the iconic vampire Count Dracula.

The story begins in medieval Wallachia (now part of Romania), where we meet our protagonist, Vlad Tepes (played by Luke Evans). A young and ambitious prince, Vlad is determined to unite his people against the Ottoman Empire's threat. However, his father, Vlad III Dracul (played by Dominic Cooper), is more focused on maintaining peace with the Ottomans.

As Vlad struggles to balance his desire for power with his sense of duty, he meets a mysterious and beautiful woman named Mirena (played by Sarah Gadon). The two fall in love, but their happiness is short-lived. Mirena is revealed to be a vampire, and she has been sent to seduce Vlad and turn him into one of the undead.

Initially, Vlad resists Mirena's charms, but eventually, he succumbs to his desires and becomes a vampire. As he struggles to come to terms with his new identity, Vlad discovers that he has developed supernatural abilities, including superhuman strength and speed.

With his newfound powers, Vlad sets out to defeat the Ottoman Empire and protect his people. However, his actions attract the attention of the evil Prince Valois (played by Art Parkinson), who seeks to exploit Vlad's powers for his own gain.

As Vlad navigates his new existence as a vampire, he must also confront the darkness within himself. He is forced to make difficult choices and confront the consequences of his actions. Ultimately, Vlad emerges victorious, but not without scars.

The movie concludes with Vlad, now an immortal vampire, setting out on a journey to protect humanity from the forces of evil. The film ends with a sense of foreboding, as we see Vlad's iconic cape fluttering in the wind, hinting at his future role as the legendary Count Dracula.

Throughout the movie, Luke Evans delivers a strong performance as Vlad Tepes, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Dominic Cooper and Sarah Gadon, also deliver solid performances that add to the film's overall impact.

While Dracula Untold takes some creative liberties with the original story, it provides an interesting and action-packed take on the iconic vampire legend. The movie's visuals are stunning, with impressive fight choreography and a haunting score that perfectly captures the mood of the film.

Overall, Dracula Untold is a thrilling and entertaining ride that explores the origins of one of cinema's most iconic villains.

title: Submarine
tagline: A comedy that doesn't let principles stand in the way of progress.
overview: 15-year-old deep-thinking Welsh schoolboy Oliver Tate struggles to initiate and maintain a relationship with Jordana, his devilish, dark-haired classmate at their Swansea high school. As his parents' marriage begins to fall apart, similar problems arise in his relationship with Jordana.
plot:
Submarine is a 2010 British coming-of-age comedy-drama written and directed by Richard Ayoade in his feature directorial debut, based on the 2008 novel by Joe Dunthorne. It stars Craig Roberts as Oliver Tate, Yasmin Paige as Jordana Bevan, Noah Taylor and Sally Hawkins as Oliver's parents Lloyd and Jill, and Paddy Considine as Graham Purvis. Original songs for the soundtrack were written and performed by Alex Turner, the frontman of the Arctic Monkeys.

In the Welsh seaside city of Swansea, Oliver Tate is a precocious, socially awkward fifteen-year-old who is infatuated with his mischievous classmate Jordana Bevan. After an awkward courtship, she becomes his girlfriend, and the two begin a relationship built on shared cynicism and small rituals. At the same time, Oliver grows worried about his parents' marriage. His father Lloyd seems depressed and passive, and Oliver suspects that his mother Jill is being drawn into an affair with Graham Purvis, her former boyfriend and a New Age self-help guru who has moved in next door.

Determined to save his parents' marriage, Oliver begins monitoring their love life and spying on his mother and Graham, while also trying to be a good boyfriend. His intentions are good, but his schemes are clumsy and self-absorbed. When Jordana reveals that her mother is seriously ill with a brain tumour, Oliver struggles to offer her the support she needs, and his preoccupation with his family's problems threatens to destroy their relationship. As both crises come to a head, Oliver has to learn that he cannot control the people he loves.

Ayoade's direction is noted for its stylized visuals and deadpan humor, and Roberts received several awards for his performance.

Submarine premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on 12 September 2010 and was released in the United Kingdom in March 2011. It received positive reviews, with 88 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 76, and it won Best Feature Film at the 2012 BAFTA Cymru awards.

title: Killer Elite
tagline: May the best man live.
overview: Based on a shocking true story, Killer Elite pits two of the world’s most elite operatives—Danny, an ex-special ops agent and Hunter, his longtime mentor—against the cunning leader of a secret military society. Covering the globe from Australia to Paris, London and the Middle East, Danny and Hunter are plunged into a highly dangerous game of cat and mouse—where the predators become the prey.
plot:
Killer Elite is a 2011 action spy thriller film directed by Gary McKendry and starring Jason Statham, Clive Owen, and Dominic Cooper.

The story begins with Daniel Oxford (Clive Owen), an assassin who works for the British Secret Intelligence Service (MI6). Oxford is betrayed by his employer and left for dead in the desert. He manages to survive and seeks revenge against those responsible for his betrayal.

Years later, Oxford is found by a wealthy businessman named Sir Miles (Tom Wilkinson) who hires him for a high-stakes mission: to assassinate David Hunter (Dominic Cooper), a former MI6 agent turned mercenary. The target is a rogue operative who has stolen a deadly virus from the British government.

Oxford accepts the job, but things become complicated when he discovers that his employer's true intentions are not what they seem. He also meets Dan (Jason Statham), an old friend and fellow assassin who was thought to be dead. Dan is now working for a mysterious organization known as The Syndicate, which seems to have its own agenda.

As Oxford delves deeper into the mission, he uncovers a web of deceit and betrayal that goes all the way to the top. He must use his skills and cunning to stay one step ahead of his enemies and complete his objective.

Meanwhile, Dan is also on the hunt for Hunter, who has stolen a deadly virus that could be used to wipe out millions of people. The two former friends engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with Oxford trying to take down Hunter while also navigating the complex web of allegiances and rivalries within The Syndicate.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Sir Miles is not what he seems, and that his true intentions are far more sinister than initially thought. Oxford must use all his skills and resources to stay alive and complete his mission, while also confronting the dark secrets of his own past.

The film's climax features an intense showdown between Oxford and Hunter, with Dan caught in the middle. In the end, Oxford emerges victorious, but not without scars and a newfound understanding of the true nature of The Syndicate.

Throughout the film, the action is fast-paced and intense, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats. The cast delivers strong performances, with Statham and Owen bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

title: The Dark Knight Rises
tagline: The Legend Ends
overview: Following the death of District Attorney Harvey Dent, Batman assumes responsibility for Dent's crimes to protect the late attorney's reputation and is subsequently hunted by the Gotham City Police Department. Eight years later, Batman encounters the mysterious Selina Kyle and the villainous Bane, a new terrorist leader who overwhelms Gotham's finest. The Dark Knight resurfaces to protect a city that has branded him an enemy.
plot:
The Dark Knight Rises is a 2012 superhero thriller film directed by Christopher Nolan, written by Nolan and Jonathan Nolan, and produced by Nolan and Emma Thomas.

Beginning:
The film takes place eight years after the events of The Dark Knight (2008). Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) has retired from being Batman, and Gotham City is still recovering from the aftermath of the Joker's (Heath Ledger) chaotic reign. However, a new threat emerges in the form of Bane (Tom Hardy), a physically imposing and intelligent terrorist who seeks to destroy Gotham and its people.

Plot Development:
The story begins with Bruce Wayne living a quiet life as a philanthropist, but he is haunted by his past and the fear that he has failed to protect Gotham. Meanwhile, Bane arrives in Gotham, seeking revenge against the city's corrupt government and its citizens. He uses a new toxin called Venom to break the bones of those who resist him, including Commissioner James Gordon (Gary Oldman).

As Bane's attacks escalate, Bruce Wayne is forced back into action as Batman. However, he soon realizes that his skills are no longer sufficient to take on Bane, and he must rely on his allies, including John Blake (Joseph Gordon-Levitt), a young cop who becomes his protégé.

Plot Twist:
The film's plot takes a surprising turn when it is revealed that Bane has been manipulating events from behind the scenes. He has been using the Venom toxin to break the bones of those who resist him, but he also uses it to heal himself and become stronger.

As Batman struggles to stop Bane, he must also confront his own demons and the fear that he has failed to protect Gotham. Meanwhile, Selina Kyle (Anne Hathaway), a cat burglar, becomes embroiled in the conflict and helps Batman in his quest to defeat Bane.

Climax:
The film's climax features an epic battle between Batman and Bane at the Gotham City Opera House. Bane uses his Venom toxin to break Batman's back, leaving him paralyzed and unable to move. However, Bruce Wayne is able to use his knowledge of chemistry to create a new serum that will neutralize the toxin.

Ending:
In the end, Batman is able to defeat Bane by using the serum to heal himself and then overpowering Bane in hand-to-hand combat. The film concludes with Bruce Wayne's return as Batman, but this time he is more determined than ever to protect Gotham City from threats like Bane.

The Dark Knight Rises received widespread critical acclaim for its action sequences, performances, and themes of redemption and sacrifice. It was also a commercial success, grossing over $1 billion worldwide.

title: The Bourne Legacy
tagline: There Was Never Just One
overview: New CIA operative Aaron Cross experiences life-or-death stakes that have been triggered by the previous actions of Jason Bourne.
plot:
Six weeks after Jason Bourne's escape from Russia, Operation Outcome agent Aaron Cross (Number Five) is assigned a training exercise in the Alaskan wilderness as punishment for going AWOL. He must traverse the rugged terrain to find a remote cabin while being stalked by wolves. The cabin is operated by Number Three, another Outcome agent assigned there as punishment. Cross lies and tells Number Three that he has lost his program medication dog tags containing "chems" that Outcome agents must take to maintain their mental and physical enhancements.
Colonel Eric Byer is tasked with containing the fallout from CIA Deputy Director Pamela Landy's exposure of Operations Treadstone and Blackbriar. He and his team find several online videos in which Treadstone and Outcome medical directors Albert Hirsch and Dan Hillcott appeared together; if discovered, the videos could lead investigators to discover Operation Outcome. Byer orders Outcome to be shut down and its agents and doctors killed to protect the secrecy of other clandestine programs.
Byer deploys an armed Reaper drone to eliminate Cross and Number Three. Number Three is killed, but Cross survives. He shoots down the drone with a rifle and removes a subdermal tracking implant from his hip. He traps an aggressive wolf and forces it to swallow his tracker. Another drone targets the tracker and kills the wolf, leading Byer's team to conclude that Cross was killed. At Sterisyn Morlanta, the pharmaceutical company supporting Outcome, researcher Dr. Donald Foite seemingly snaps and methodically shoots down Hillcott and his colleagues who have been working on Outcome. After being cornered by guards, Foite shoots himself, leaving Dr. Marta Shearing as the program's sole surviving scientist.
Cross travels from Alaska to Chicago to recover a stashed car, money, and fake identification. Running low on "chems" and seeing news that his Outcome provider, Dr. Shearing, had survived the shooting, he drives to her home in Maryland. Meanwhile, Byer sends four assassins disguised as federal agents to kill Dr. Shearing and make it look like a suicide. Cross intervenes, kills the assassins, and burns down Dr. Shearing's house to cover their escape. Shearing tells Cross that the program already used a virus to make his physical enhancements permanent, eliminating his need for physical "chems". Since it is impossible for Cross and Shearing to obtain more mental "chems", they plan to fly to the Philippines to obtain a live virus to make Cross's mental enhancements permanent.
Cross and Shearing use false identities to fly to Manila, bluff their way into a pharmaceutical plant where Sterisyn Morlanta has a research lab, and infect Cross with the live virus. Meanwhile, Byer's team finds CCTV footage of Shearing at JFK airport and determines her itinerary. Byer also learns that Cross is alive and that he, too, flew to Manila.

title: All Quiet on the Western Front
overview: Paul Baumer and his friends Albert and Muller, egged on by romantic dreams of heroism, voluntarily enlist in the German army. Full of excitement and patriotic fervour, the boys enthusiastically march into a war they believe in. But once on the Western Front, they discover the soul-destroying horror of World War I.
plot:
All Quiet on the Western Front (German: Im Westen nichts Neues) is a 2022 German epic anti-war film co-written, directed and co-produced by Edward Berger, based on Erich Maria Remarque's 1929 novel. It is the third screen adaptation of the book, after the 1930 and 1979 films, and the first in German. Felix Kammerer stars as Paul Bäumer, with Albrecht Schuch, Daniel Brühl, Sebastian Hülk, Aaron Hilmer, Edin Hasanović and Devid Striesow. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2022 and was released on Netflix in October.

In 1917, three years into the First World War, seventeen-year-old Paul Bäumer enthusiastically enlists in the Imperial German Army with his schoolmates Albert Kropp, Franz Müller and Ludwig Behm, inspired by a patriotic speech. Unaware, they are issued uniforms recycled from soldiers killed in earlier battles. Sent to the Western Front in northern France, they are befriended by Stanislaus "Kat" Katczinsky, an older, experienced soldier, but their romantic ideas about war are destroyed by the horrors of trench warfare, and Ludwig is killed on their first night.

Eighteen months later, in November 1918, the German politician Matthias Erzberger, appalled by the mounting death toll, urges the high command to seek an armistice with the Allies and leads the German delegation to negotiate with the French at Compiègne, where the terms offered are harsh. At the front, Paul, Kat and their comrades, including the veteran Tjaden, have become hardened survivors, finding brief moments of comradeship amid the slaughter, such as stealing a goose from a farm. As the armistice negotiations drag on, the soldiers are sent into ever more futile attacks, facing tanks, flamethrowers and gas. Even as the end of the war approaches, a German general determined to finish with a final victory orders one last offensive in the hours before the ceasefire is due to take effect at 11 a.m. on 11 November 1918.

The film received widespread acclaim for its direction, cinematography, score and depiction of the brutality of war. It won seven BAFTA Awards, including Best Film, and four Academy Awards, for Best International Feature Film, Best Cinematography, Best Original Score and Best Production Design, out of nine nominations.

title: Gravity
tagline: Don't Let Go
overview: Dr. Ryan Stone, a brilliant medical engineer on her first Shuttle mission, with veteran astronaut Matt Kowalsky in command of his last flight before retiring. But on a seemingly routine spacewalk, disaster strikes. The Shuttle is destroyed, leaving Stone and Kowalsky completely alone-tethered to nothing but each other and spiraling out into the blackness of space. The deafening silence tells them they have lost any link to Earth and any chance for rescue. As fear turns to panic, every gulp of air eats away at what little oxygen is left. But the only way home may be to go further out into the terrifying expanse of space.
plot:
Gravity is a 2013 science fiction thriller film directed by Alfonso Cuarón and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie follows the story of two astronauts, Dr. Ryan Stone (played by Sandra Bullock) and Lieutenant Matt Kowalski (played by George Clooney), who are on a space mission to repair the Hubble Space Telescope.

The film begins with a stunning visual representation of the Earth from space, showcasing the beauty and fragility of our planet. We then see Dr. Ryan Stone, a medical engineer who is part of a three-person crew sent to the International Space Station (ISS) to perform routine maintenance tasks. However, during the mission, an explosion occurs on the ISS, killing two of the astronauts and leaving only Stone and Kowalski stranded in space.

The movie then shifts to a thrilling sequence where Stone and Kowalski try to navigate their way back to the ISS using a damaged shuttle. Unfortunately, they soon realize that their ship is malfunctioning, and they are drifting further away from Earth with each passing minute. The tension builds up as they face numerous challenges, including a catastrophic failure of their life support systems.

As the story unfolds, we see Stone's emotional struggle to cope with the loss of her husband, who died in a car accident just before she left for space. Her grief and sense of isolation are palpable, making her character even more relatable and human. Kowalski, on the other hand, is portrayed as a seasoned astronaut who tries to keep Stone's spirits up despite his own growing concern about their situation.

The plot development in Gravity is expertly handled by Cuarón, who uses stunning visuals and clever editing to create an immersive experience for the audience. The film's cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the vastness of space and the fragility of human existence. The sound design is equally impressive, with a haunting score that complements the on-screen action.

As the story reaches its climax, Stone and Kowalski find themselves hurtling towards a massive asteroid field, where they must use all their skills to survive. In a heart-stopping sequence, they narrowly avoid being crushed by debris and eventually manage to escape the asteroid field using a makeshift solution.

The ending of Gravity is both poignant and uplifting. After a harrowing journey, Stone finally finds herself back on Earth, where she is reunited with her daughter. The film's final shot is of Stone looking up at the sky, symbolizing her newfound appreciation for life and her connection to the universe.

Overall, Gravity is a masterclass in storytelling, visuals, and performances. It's a thrilling ride that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its stunning cinematography, clever editing, and outstanding performances, Gravity is a must-see film that will leave you breathless and inspired.

title: The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey
tagline: From the smallest beginnings come the greatest legends.
overview: Bilbo Baggins, a hobbit enjoying his quiet life, is swept into an epic quest by Gandalf the Grey and thirteen dwarves who seek to reclaim their mountain home from Smaug, the dragon.
plot:
The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey is a 2012 fantasy adventure film directed by Peter Jackson, based on the novel of the same name by J.R.R. Tolkien. The film is set in Middle-earth and follows the journey of Bilbo Baggins (Martin Freeman), a hobbit who joins a group of dwarves led by Thorin Oakenshield (Richard Armitage) on a quest to reclaim their treasure from the dragon Smaug.

The film begins with Bilbo, a comfortable and quiet hobbit living in Bag End, receiving an unexpected visit from the wizard Gandalf (Ian McKellen). Gandalf informs Bilbo that he has been recruited by the dwarves to join them on their perilous journey to reclaim their treasure. Initially reluctant, Bilbo eventually agrees to join the group.

As they set out, the company is ambushed by goblins and trolls, leading to a thrilling escape through the Misty Mountains. The group soon discovers that they are being pursued by the goblin king, Azog (Manu Bennett), who seeks revenge for his defeat at the hands of Thorin's father.

The journey takes them across treacherous landscapes, including the forest of Mirkwood, where they encounter the woodland elves and their leader, Thranduil (Lee Pace). The group also meets Beorn (Mikael Persbrandt), a shape-shifting bear who provides them with shelter and assistance.

As they near the Lonely Mountain, the company faces numerous challenges, including navigating treacherous tunnels and avoiding deadly traps set by Smaug. They eventually reach the mountain, where Bilbo discovers that Smaug has taken over the treasure hoard and is guarding it fiercely.

The film culminates in a dramatic confrontation between Thorin and Smaug, with Bilbo playing a crucial role in distracting the dragon long enough for the dwarves to escape. The journey ends with the company returning to Lake-town, where they are met with suspicion and hostility by the people.

Throughout the film, Jackson's direction brings the world of Middle-earth to life, with stunning visuals and impressive action sequences. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Freeman as Bilbo, who brings a likable and relatable quality to the character.

Overall, The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey sets the stage for the rest of the trilogy, introducing key characters and themes that will be explored in greater depth in the subsequent films.

title: The Croods
tagline: Meet the first modern family.
overview: The prehistoric Croods family live in a particularly dangerous moment in time. Patriarch Grug, his mate Ugga, teenage daughter Eep, son Thunk, and feisty Gran gather food by day and huddle together in a cave at night. When a more evolved caveman named Guy arrives on the scene, Grug is distrustful, but it soon becomes apparent that Guy is correct about the impending destruction of their world.
plot:
The Croods is a prehistoric animated adventure comedy film released in 2013 by DreamWorks Animation. The movie follows the story of an ancient family, the Croods, who live in a cave during the Ice Age.

The story begins with Grug (voiced by Nicolas Cage), the overprotective and stubborn father of the family, who is determined to keep his family safe from the dangers of the outside world. He believes that the only way to survive is to stay inside their cave and follow a strict routine. However, this approach has become stale for Grug's wife, Ugga (voiced by Catherine Keener), and their three children: Eep (voiced by Emma Stone), Thunk (voiced by Clark Duke), and Sandy (voiced by Cloris Leachman).

Eep, the eldest child, is a free-spirited and adventurous young girl who longs to explore the world outside. She dreams of discovering new things and experiencing life beyond their cave. Grug's overprotectiveness has made Eep feel stifled and trapped.

One day, a massive earthquake hits, causing the cave to collapse. The family is forced to flee and embark on a perilous journey through uncharted territory. Along the way, they meet Guy (voiced by Ryan Reynolds), a charming and resourceful caveman who becomes their unlikely ally.

As they travel together, Eep begins to learn about the world beyond her cave and discovers that there's more to life than just following rules and traditions. She also develops feelings for Guy, which complicates her relationship with her father. Meanwhile, Grug struggles to let go of his fears and trust his family to take care of themselves.

The group faces numerous challenges, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious predators, and rival cavemen. However, through their shared experiences, they learn to rely on each other and develop a deeper understanding of one another's strengths and weaknesses.

As the journey progresses, Eep and Guy grow closer, but Grug's disapproval creates tension between them. In the end, Grug must confront his own fears and trust his family to make it back home safely. The movie culminates in an emotional reunion with the Croods' cave, where they learn that sometimes taking risks and embracing change can lead to growth and happiness.

The Croods features stunning animation, lovable characters, and a heartwarming story that explores themes of family, love, and self-discovery. With its engaging plot and memorable voice cast, this film is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

title: R.I.P.D.
tagline: To protect and serve the living.
overview: A recently slain cop joins a team of undead police officers working for the Rest in Peace Department and tries to find the man who murdered him.
plot:
R.I.P.D. is a supernatural action-comedy film directed by Robert Schwentke and written by Scott Waugh and David Koepp, based on the comic book series of the same name by Peter Craig and Matt Holness.

The movie follows the story of Nick Walker (played by Ryan Reynolds), a Los Angeles police detective who dies in the line of duty. However, instead of moving on to the afterlife, Nick is brought back as a "Reaper" - an undead law enforcement agent tasked with maintaining order and justice in the living world.

Nick's new partner is Jonesy (played by Jeff Bridges), a seasoned Reaper who has been working for over 100 years. Jonesy is initially hesitant to take on a new partner, but eventually warms up to Nick's enthusiasm and determination.

The two Reapers are tasked with solving a series of murders that have taken place in Los Angeles. The victims all have one thing in common: they were involved in a massive conspiracy involving the corrupt businessman Captain Zane (played by Peter Firth) and his accomplices.

As Nick and Jonesy delve deeper into the case, they discover that the murders are connected to an ancient evil known as the "Devil's Gate", which has been unleashed on the world. The Devil's Gate is a portal that allows spirits from the afterlife to enter the living world, causing chaos and destruction.

Nick and Jonesy must work together to stop Captain Zane and his accomplices, while also navigating their own complicated relationship with each other. Along the way, Nick learns more about the Reaper program and the true nature of his existence.

As the story unfolds, Nick and Jonesy face off against a series of increasingly formidable foes, including a group of rogue Reapers who are working to undermine the authority of the program. The stakes are raised when Nick discovers that he has a personal connection to one of the victims, which makes the case even more urgent for him.

In the end, Nick and Jonesy succeed in stopping Captain Zane and closing the Devil's Gate, but not before they both suffer significant losses. The movie concludes with Nick finally finding some measure of peace and acceptance as a Reaper, while also forming a bond with his partner that transcends their differences.

Overall, R.I.P.D. is a fun and action-packed supernatural thriller that explores themes of mortality, identity, and the complexities of human relationships. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of Ryan Reynolds and Jeff Bridges will likely enjoy this entertaining and visually stunning film.

plot:
Man on a Ledge is a 2012 American action thriller film directed by Chris Cayille and starring Sam Worthington, Elizabeth Banks, and Anthony Mackie. The movie follows the story of Nick Cassidy (Worthington), a former FBI hostage negotiator who has lost his job after being involved in a scandal.

The plot begins with Nick Cassidy, who is now working as a security consultant for a private company called "The Company". He is hired to guard a high-rise building in New York City. However, things take a turn when Nick's estranged brother, Pete (Mackie), calls him and tells him that their father has been murdered by the same people who killed their mother.

Nick's brother Pete is being held captive by the same group of terrorists who killed their family, and he wants Nick to rescue him. However, Nick knows that if he tries to escape from his job at The Company, he will be arrested and charged with treason. He also knows that the FBI has been monitoring his activities, and they are not going to let him go.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that The Company is actually a front for a group of terrorists who are planning to take over the United States government. Nick's brother Pete is being held captive in a high-rise building in New York City, and Nick must use his skills as a hostage negotiator to rescue him without getting caught.

The plot thickens when it becomes clear that The Company has infiltrated the FBI, and Nick's former boss, Agent Harris (Anthony Mackie), is actually working for them. This creates a moral dilemma for Nick, who must decide whether to follow his orders or do what he thinks is right.

As the story reaches its climax, Nick uses his skills as a hostage negotiator to rescue his brother Pete from the high-rise building. However, in doing so, he also puts himself at risk of being caught by The Company and the FBI. In the end, Nick manages to escape from The Company's clutches and clear his name.

The movie ends with Nick reflecting on the events that have transpired, and realizing that he has been given a second chance to make things right. He is seen walking away from the high-rise building, symbolizing his newfound freedom and determination to start anew.

Overall, Man on a Ledge is an action-packed thriller that explores themes of loyalty, duty, and redemption. The movie features impressive stunts and suspenseful plot twists, making it a thrilling ride for audiences.

title: John Carter
tagline: Lost in our world, found in another.
overview: John Carter is a war-weary, former military captain who's inexplicably transported to the mysterious and exotic planet of Barsoom (Mars) and reluctantly becomes embroiled in an epic conflict. It's a world on the brink of collapse, and Carter rediscovers his humanity when he realizes the survival of Barsoom and its people rests in his hands.
plot:
In 1881, Edgar Rice Burroughs arrives at the estate of his recently deceased uncle, John Carter, a former American Civil War Confederate Army captain. Per Carter's instructions, the body is put in a tomb that can be unlocked only from the inside. His attorney gives Carter's journal to Burroughs, to whom Carter bequeathed his fortune.
In a flashback to 1868 in the Arizona Territory, Union Colonel Powell arrests Carter with hopes that he will help in fighting local Apache. Carter escapes his holding cell with cavalry soldiers in close pursuit. After a run-in with a band of Apaches, Carter and a wounded Powell hide in a cave that is filled with gold. A mysterious man, later revealed to be a Thern, appears in the cave and attacks them with a knife; Carter kills him but accidentally activates the Thern's medallion and is transported to a ruined and dying planet, Barsoom, known to Carter as Mars. Because of his different bone density and the planet's lower gravity, Carter can jump high and perform feats of incredible strength. He is captured by the Tharks, a nomadic tribe of Green Martians and their Jeddak, Tars Tarkas.
Elsewhere on Barsoom, the Red Martian cities of Helium and Zodanga have been at war for a thousand years. Sab Than, Jeddak of Zodanga, armed with a weapon obtained from the Thern leader Matai Shang, proposes a cease-fire and an end to the war by marrying the Princess of Helium, Dejah Thoris. The Princess escapes and is rescued by Carter.
Carter, Dejah, and Tarkas's daughter, Sola, reach a spot in a sacred river to find a way for Carter to get back to Earth. They discover that the medallions are powered by a "ninth ray" that is also the source of Sab Than's weapon. They are then attacked by a vicious race called the Warhoon under the direction of Shang. Carter and Dejah are taken back to Zodanga. Dejah grudgingly agrees to marry Sab Than and gives Carter instructions on how to use the medallion to return to Earth. Carter decides to stay but is captured by Shang, who explains how Therns manipulate the civilizations of different worlds to their doom, feeding off the planet's resources in the process, and intend to do the same thing with Barsoom by choosing Sab Than to rule the planet. Carter escapes and returns to the Tharks with Sola to request their help. There they discover that a brute, Tal Hajus, has overthrown Tarkas. Carter and an injured Tarkas battle with two enormous Great White-Apes in an arena before Carter kills Hajus, thereby becoming the leader of the Tharks.
The Thark army storms Zodanga, but it is empty; realizing that their army is waiting outside Helium, Carter and the Tharks commandeer the Zodangan airships and fly to Helium. Carter defeats the Zodangan army, while Sab Than is killed and Shang escapes. Carter becomes prince of Helium by marrying Dejah. On their first night, Carter decides to stay on Mars and throws away his medallion.

title: In Time
tagline: Time Is Power
overview: In the not-too-distant future the aging gene has been switched off. To avoid overpopulation, time has become the currency and the way people pay for luxuries and necessities. The rich can live forever, while the rest try to negotiate for their immortality. A poor young man who comes into a fortune of time, though too late to help his mother from dying. He ends up on the run from a corrupt police force known as 'time keepers'.
plot:
In Time is a 2011 science fiction action film directed by Andrew Niccol and written by Niccol. The movie takes place in a dystopian future where time has become the ultimate currency.

The story follows Will Salas (played by Justin Timberlake), a poor man living on the outskirts of society, who lives in a world where people trade years of their lives for material possessions. The rich live forever, while the poor are left with mere minutes to live. Will's life changes when he meets Sylvia Weis (played by Amanda Seyfried), a wealthy woman who gives him 100 hours of her time.

With this newfound wealth, Will sets out on a journey to change his fate and that of those around him. He teams up with Henry Hamilton (played by Matt Bomer), a wealthy man who is struggling with the consequences of his own immortality. Together, they embark on a mission to redistribute time among the poor, challenging the existing social hierarchy.

As Will and Henry navigate this new world, they attract the attention of the authorities, led by Raymond Leon (played by Cillian Murphy). Leon is determined to capture Will and maintain the status quo, which has kept him in power for years. The two men engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with Will using his newfound wealth to evade capture.

Throughout the movie, Will's character undergoes significant development as he grapples with the consequences of his actions. He begins to question the morality of the system and the true cost of immortality. As he gets closer to his goal, he must confront the harsh realities of a world where time is currency, and the rich will stop at nothing to maintain their power.

The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Will and Leon, with the fate of humanity hanging in the balance. In the end, Will emerges victorious, but not without scars. He has changed the course of history, but at what cost? The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that a new era of equality and justice may be possible.

Overall, In Time is a thought-provoking commentary on class inequality and the consequences of unchecked power. With its unique premise and engaging characters, it offers a thrilling ride that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: Smile
tagline: Point. Shoot. Die.
overview: A carefree summer vacation turns into an inescapable terror trap for a group of young students who buy a vintage instant camera from a mysterious local shop owner...
plot:
Smile is a 2009 English-language Italian supernatural horror film written and directed by Francesco Gasperoni in his feature debut. Set and shot in Morocco, it follows a group of young friends on holiday who are picked off one by one after being photographed with a cursed instant camera. The cast includes Harriet MacMasters-Green, Antonio Cupo, Giorgia Massetti, Manuela Zanier, Mourad Zaoui, Robert Capelli Jr. and Tara Haggiag, with Armand Assante as the mysterious Tollinger. It was produced by Luce Cinecittà, Morocco Movie Group and Moviemaker with support from the Italian Ministry of Cultural Heritage and Activities.

The film opens with Tollinger at work as a forensic photographer, moving from one violent crime scene to the next. A group of university students then sets off by battered van for a relaxing, adventurous holiday in the mountains of Morocco, where they want to camp and have heard legends of black demons with flaming hands. Their leader, Clarissa, is an aspiring photojournalist determined to record every moment, but after her own camera is stolen and the van suffers a flat tyre following a near accident, she visits an antique shop in a nearby village. There the sinister owner, Tollinger, sells her a vintage Polaroid camera for a fraction of its value, throws in a roll of film and urges her to take lots of pictures of her friends. As the trip continues, a local hunter warns them not to use the camera bought in the bazaar, and gruesome deaths begin among the group. They realize that the camera has the power to kill anyone it photographs and that the deaths match the images, and the survivors, among them Tommy, who panics as the killings mount, race to decipher the supernatural clues in the photographs before they become the next victims.

Smile opened in about 150 Italian cinemas on August 28, 2009, with releases in France and elsewhere in Europe that autumn and a direct-to-DVD release planned for the United States. Filming took place over five weeks with a half-Italian, half-Moroccan crew assisted by the Casablanca film school. Italian critics were largely negative: Valerio Ceddia of Quinlan.it found it predictable and unintentionally ridiculous, though he praised the unusual misty mountain locations. HorrorNews.net was kinder, calling it a straightforward possessed-object horror film in the vein of Final Destination, with brisk pacing and decent effects. A sequel was later planned.

title: I Saw the Devil
tagline: Abandon all compassion.
overview: Kyung-Chul is a dangerous psychopath who kills for pleasure. Soo-Hyun, a top-secret agent, decides to track down the murderer himself. He promises himself that he will do everything in his power to take vengeance against the killer, even if it means that he must become a monster himself.
plot:
Jang Kyung-chul, a school bus driver, encounters a woman named Jang Joo-yun and offers to fix her flat tire. After beating her unconscious and bringing her to his house, Kyung-chul methodically dismembers her, unaware of her ring falling into a floor drain. Kyung-chul scatters the body parts into a local river, where it is discovered, prompting the police to conduct a search led by Squad Chief Jang, Joo-yun's father, and Squad Chief Oh. Joo-yun's fiancé, Kim Soo-hyun, an NIS agent, vows to exact revenge on the perpetrator.
After learning of the four suspects from Jang, Soo-hyun privately interrogates two of them. The violent encounter (part torture) of the first two suspects absolves them as his wife's killer. But they are not without fault, one suspect turns himself in for killing multiple schoolgirls in fear of Soo-hyun's return and seeks help from the police in the hospital. Upon searching the home of Kyung-chul (the third suspect), Soo-hyun finds Joo-yun's ring which confirms Jang Kyung-chul to be his fiancée's killer.
A short time later, Kyung-chul brings a schoolgirl home and begins to rape her. Soo-hyun interrupts and knocks him unconscious. Instead of killing Kyung-chul, Soo-hyun forces him to swallow a GPS tracking transmitter, allowing him to track Kyung-chul's movements and listen to his conversations while also fracturing his left arm.
Waking up, Kyung-chul is offered a ride by a taxi, which already carries a passenger. The taxi has a license with a profile picture of the taxi's owner, which Kyung-chul notices is not the one driving this taxi. He has stepped into a hijacked vehicle, and the occupants are acting strangely. Kyung-chul attacks them seconds before they attack and murders them. Kyung-chul checks the trunk of the taxi and finds a murder victim (presumably the taxi driver) and a bag of fresh clothes. He leaves their bodies on the side of the road, and cleans up in a nearby river.
Kyung-chul drives to a clinic to have his wounds looked at. After being treated, Kyung-chul proceeds to rape a nurse. Soo-hyun arrives, subdues him, and slashes his achilles tendon before leaving. At this point, Soo-hyun's intention becomes clear: he wants to torture Kyung-chul as long as possible. Kyung-chul visits the home of his friend Tae-joo, a cannibalistic murderer and meets his girlfriend Se-jung who seems nonchalant about the meeting.
After learning of the situation, Tae-joo remarks that his tormentor must be related to one of his victims. Kyung-chul deduces Soo-hyun's identity after recalling that his wedding ring matched that of Joo-yun. Soo-hyun arrives and incapacitates Kyung-chul, Tae-joo, and his girlfriend Se-jung. The next day, Tae-joo and Se-jung, still unconscious, are arrested by the police and sent to the hospital. Soo-hyun and Kyung-chul receive treatment for their wounds, aided by Soo-hyun's trusted subordinate, who helps them evade the cops.

title: The Nutcracker: The Untold Story
tagline: Experience the Holiday Classic as You've Never Seen it Before
overview: Set in 1920s Vienna, this is the tale of a little girl, whose godfather gives her a special doll one Christmas Eve.
plot:
The Nutcracker in 3D, also released as The Nutcracker: The Untold Story, is a 2010 Christmas musical fantasy film adapted from Tchaikovsky's 1892 ballet The Nutcracker. Andrei Konchalovsky directed, co-wrote and produced the film, a co-production of the United Kingdom, Russia and Hungary that sets the story in 1920s Vienna and sets lyrics to Tchaikovsky's music. First screened at the European Film Market in February 2009, it opened in the United States and Canada on November 24, 2010.

Young Mary lives with her parents, Joseph and Louise, and little brother, Max. On Christmas Eve, while her parents are at a party, her Uncle Albert gives the children a dollhouse and a nutcracker named NC, who comes to life that night and grows to human size. In the sitting room, now enormous, Mary meets NC's toy friends: Gielgud, a courtly chimpanzee; Tinker, a fussy opera-singing clown; and Sticks, a drummer boy. Atop the Christmas tree the Snow Fairy, who resembles Mary's mother, reveals that NC is a prince whose kingdom was seized by the Rat King and his mother, the Rat Queen, who cursed him. Because Mary believes in him, NC briefly becomes a boy again, and she sees his city, where the light-fearing Rat King forces people to burn children's toys in factories so that the smoke blots out the sun.

The rats' robotic dogs topple the tree, and Mary wakes in bed to parents who dismiss her story. The next night NC is captured along with Tinker and Sticks, and Max is lured to the rat city and imprisoned. With Gielgud, Mary slips through a portal in the attic and, disguised as a rat, finds the factory where NC lies lifeless. Her declaration of love breaks the curse for good, the workers rise up, and after a fight aboard the rats' helicopter, the King and Queen revert to rats and flee into the sewers. NC is crowned and promises Mary they will meet again. Back home, her parents apologize and vow to spend more time with her, and Uncle Albert introduces his new neighbor, a boy who looks like the prince and asks to be called NC.

tagline: 2,000 colleges. 8 million roommates. Which one will you get?
overview: When Sara, a young design student from Iowa, arrives for college in Los Angeles, she is eager to fit in and get to know the big city. plot:
Sara Matthews is starting her freshman year of college in Los Angeles. She meets party girl Tracy, frat boy Stephen—her love interest—and Rebecca, her wealthy but shy college roommate who bears an uncanny resemblance to her. The girls begin to bond and Rebecca learns that Sara had an older sister, Emily, who died when Sara was nine, and an ex-boyfriend, Jason, who keeps calling her in attempts to reconcile.
Over time, Rebecca's obsession with Sara grows, which causes her to drive away anyone who could come between them. Claiming that she is a bad influence, Rebecca attacks Tracy in the shower, pins her down, rips out her belly button ring, and threatens to kill her unless she stays away from Sara. Tracy moves to another dorm, fearful of Rebecca. An old friend of Sara's named Irene invites Sara to move in with her when Sara's cat Cuddles is discovered by an RA. Rebecca kills Cuddles, lying to Sara that the cat ran away, inflicts injuries upon herself, and says she was assaulted by a thug.
Feeling sympathetic, Sara decides to spend Thanksgiving with Rebecca. When Sara's fashion design professor, Roberts, kisses her, Rebecca plans to get the professor out of the picture by seducing him while recording their dialogue on a tape recorder to make it sound like he was trying to rape her. During her Thanksgiving stay, Sara overhears a conversation between Rebecca and her father, hinting Rebecca has had trouble making friends in the past. After Rebecca's mother mentions that Rebecca is supposed to be taking medication, Sara and Stephen find a bottle of unused Zyprexa pills, used to treat schizophrenia or bipolar disorder.
Sara decides to move in with Irene; however, that evening at a club, Rebecca seduces Irene and they go back to Irene's place. The following morning, Sara goes to Irene's apartment, but she is not there. Meanwhile, Rebecca gets Sara's sister's name tattooed in the same place on her breast as Sara. Alarmed, Sara finally realizes Rebecca is obsessed with her and removes her belongings from the dorm. Jason arrives at Sara's dorm and slips a note under her door, saying that he wants to see her. Rebecca intercepts it, and disguises herself as Sara. She then goes to Jason's hotel room and stabs him to death.
Sara receives a text message from Irene saying she needs to meet with her right away, and she calls Stephen so he can meet her there. She arrives and finds a gagged Irene handcuffed to the bed. Rebecca reveals herself and points a gun at Sara, proclaiming her love and loyalty, before tearfully revealing she was responsible for what happened to Tracy, Cuddles, Professor Roberts, Irene, and Jason, and that she did it all to win Sara's friendship.
Rebecca moves to smother Irene, and Sara attempts to stop her. Sara tries to call for help, but the phone is dead. Bound and helpless, Irene pleads for Sara to save herself. Sara tries to get out the window to get help.

title: The Help
tagline: Change begins with a whisper.
overview: Aibileen Clark is a middle-aged African-American maid who has spent her life raising white children and has recently lost her only son; Minny Jackson is an African-American maid who has often offended her employers despite her family's struggles with money and her desperate need for jobs; and Eugenia "Skeeter" Phelan is a young white woman who has recently moved back home after graduating college to find out her childhood maid has mysteriously disappeared. These three stories intertwine to explain how life in Jackson, Mississippi revolves around "the help"; yet they are always kept at a certain distance because of racial lines.
plot:
The Help is a drama film released in 2011, directed by Tate Taylor and produced by 1492 Pictures, DreamWorks Pictures, and Playtone. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Kathryn Stockett.

The story takes place in Jackson, Mississippi, during the early 1960s, a time of great social change and racial tension. The film follows three main characters: Skeeter Phelan (played by Emma Stone), Aibileen Clark (played by Viola Davis), and Minny Jackson (played by Octavia Spencer).

Skeeter, a young white woman, returns to her hometown after graduating from college with a degree in journalism. She decides to write a book about the experiences of African American maids in the South during that era, which was largely unseen and unheard by the general public.

Aibileen, a wise and kind black maid who has been working for various white families in Jackson, becomes Skeeter's confidant and guide. Aibileen shares her own story of raising white children while struggling with racism and sexism in her daily life. She also introduces Skeeter to Minny, another black maid who is known for her sharp wit and outspoken nature.

As the story unfolds, Skeeter begins to gather stories from other African American maids, including Hilly Holbrook (played by Jessica Chastain), a well-meaning but clueless socialite who inadvertently perpetuates racist stereotypes. The maids share their experiences of being treated poorly, being forced to do menial tasks, and facing humiliation at the hands of their white employers.

Through Aibileen's guidance, Skeeter learns about the complexities of racial relationships in Jackson during that time period. She also begins to question her own privilege as a white woman growing up in a predominantly black community.

As the book nears completion, Hilly discovers that one of the maids has been secretly writing about their experiences and decides to take action against them. The maids are forced to confront the consequences of speaking out against racism and sexism.

The film culminates with Aibileen's story being published in a local newspaper, which sparks a wave of outrage and change in Jackson. The publication of the book also brings attention to the struggles faced by African American women during that era, highlighting their resilience and strength in the face of adversity.

Throughout the movie, the characters' relationships are complex and multifaceted, reflecting the nuances of racial dynamics in the South during the 1960s. The film ultimately celebrates the power of storytelling and the importance of giving voice to those who have been silenced for too long.

The Help received widespread critical acclaim, earning several Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, Best Actress for Viola Davis, and Best Supporting Actress for Octavia Spencer, who won the award.

title: Fallen
tagline: A prophecy. A destiny. A fallen angel.
overview: For high schooler Aaron Corbett, turning 18 means becoming not just a man but a nephilim, too -- half human, half angel, with supernatural abilities.
plot:
Fallen is a 2006 American supernatural fantasy television film, the first part of a three-part miniseries made for ABC Family and based on the young-adult novels by Thomas E. Sniegoski. Directed by Mikael Salomon, known for his work on Band of Brothers and Rome, from a script by Sara Cooper, it stars Paul Wesley as Aaron Corbett, Tom Skerritt as Zeke, Lisa Lackey as Verchiel, Fernanda Andrade as Vilma and Rick Worthy as the archangel Camael, with Chelah Horsdal, Alex Ferris and Byron Mann. It premiered on 23 July 2006, and this first part is subtitled The Beginning.

Each part opens with narration over biblical images telling the legend of the fallen angels and of the Nephilim, half-angel, half-human beings considered abominations, whom soldier angels known as the Powers are determined to purge from the world. Aaron is a troubled orphan who has spent three years with a loving foster family in a small American town. He has become a popular wrestling star at school and has learned to control the violent urges that plagued his past. On his eighteenth birthday, however, he begins to suffer intense headaches, discovers he can understand and speak languages he has never studied, displays sudden bursts of strength and is alarmed to hear the thoughts of his dog Gabriel, all of which disrupts his studies and his budding romance with his classmate Vilma. A homeless man named Zeke, actually a fallen angel in disguise, reveals that Aaron is a Nephilim and that few like him survive the transformation. Aaron also learns that he may be the Redeemer of prophecy, able to absolve fallen angels and send them back to Heaven, which puts him in the sights of the Powers, led by the ruthless Verchiel, who hunt him down.

The two later parts, The Journey and The Destiny, aired in 2007, bringing the full miniseries to over four hours. In Variety, Laura Fries noted that the film follows the books closely in plot, though Verchiel, male in the novels, is played by a woman. She found Cooper's script talky and its symbolism simplistic, and Salomon's camera gimmicks distracting, but credited the film with deeper character development than expected and decent effects. Reviewing the miniseries on DVD Talk, Thomas Spurlin praised Wesley's performance and the supporting cast but found the exposition-heavy story far too long.

title: Animals United
overview: A group of animals waiting for the annual flood they rely on for food and water discover that the humans, who have been destroying their habitats have built a dam for a leisure resort. The animals endeavour to save the delta and send a message to the humans not to interfere with nature.
plot:
Animals United (German: Konferenz der Tiere) is a 2010 German animated adventure comedy directed and produced by Reinhard Klooss and Holger Tappe, loosely based on Erich Kästner and Walter Trier's 1949 book The Animals' Conference. In the German version, Ralf Schmitz voices Billy the meerkat and Thomas Fritsch voices Socrates the lion, alongside Christoph Maria Herbst, Bastian Pastewka and Oliver Kalkofe, while the English dub features James Corden, Stephen Fry and Andy Serkis. It was released in Germany on October 7, 2010.

In Africa's Okavango Delta, the yearly flood has failed to arrive, and as water grows scarce the animals, including a herd of rhinos and a herd of buffaloes, quarrel fiercely over what little remains. Billy, a young meerkat, and his friend Socrates, a lion, set out to find water. Their journey takes them into a feared place known as the Valley of Death, and along the way they meet a ragtag band of animals from around the world, including Sushi the polar bear, Toby the kangaroo, Smiley the Tasmanian devil, an elderly pair of Galápagos tortoises and Charles the rooster, all of whom have been driven from their homes by human activity and have made their way to Africa.

The animals discover the cause of the drought: a dam has been built to supply a luxury resort, the Eden Paradise Hotel, which is hosting an international climate conference. With the help of Toto, a chimpanzee kept as the hotel's mascot, they try to restore the river, but the poacher Hunter captures Socrates. The animals then hold their own conference, where the old tortoises warn of the bleak future facing wildlife before passing away.

Determined to act, Billy and his friends cross the Valley of Death to the dam. Toto foils Hunter's attempt to stop them from a biplane, and the animals send a swarm of locusts into the conference hall, where they devour everything, including the delegates' documents and clothes. Billy rescues Socrates, the animals turn the tables on Hunter, and the dam is breached, sending water flowing back into the delta. The animals celebrate, invite Toto to live with them, and set off to hold humanity to account.

Produced by Ambient Entertainment, the film drew more than 1.5 million viewers in German cinemas and grossed over $50 million worldwide. International reviews were largely unfavorable; The Hollywood Reporter called it bombastic, preaching too much while entertaining too little. A sequel, Pets United, followed on Netflix in 2019.

overview: When a scam goes horribly wrong and leaves the neighborhood kids furious, the Eds embark on a journey to find Eddy's brother in the "Ed, Edd, n Eddy" series finale.
plot:
"The Eds"—Ed, Edd and Eddy—anxiously flee their devastated cul-de-sac after their most recent money-making scheme backfires heavily and severely injures their neighbors Jonny, Kevin, Nazz and Rolf, who plot to retaliate violently. After narrowly escaping, Eddy recommends seeking protection from his older brother. Since Eddy does not actually know where he lives, Edd tries to piece together Eddy's inconsistent facts about him to determine a location. To find the Eds, Jonny takes his wooden board Plank with him on a city bus, Rolf rides on his pig Wilfred, and Nazz joins Kevin to travel via Kevin's prized bicycle. While Jimmy and Sarah, Ed's younger sister, were not involved or affected by the scheme, they decide to have a picnic while watching their retaliation. On the way over, they run into the Kanker Sisters; Lee, Marie and May. Upon learning about the other children's intent from them, the Kankers set out to save the Eds while taking the duo hostage.
Meanwhile, the Eds are left to wander aimlessly under Eddy's direction. In a cow pasture, Edd profiles Eddy's brother and reasons that given his con artistry, he would likely be found at a place involving pranks. Ed uses one of his decade-old comic books to suggest visiting the Lemon Brook Gag Factory. Upon arriving, they discover that it has been out of business ever since and Edd finds no clues in the office. Meanwhile, Wilfred, fed up with Rolf's abrasive attitude towards him, attacks his owner in a frenzy and abandons him.
After leaving the factory, Eddy claims his brother was once a whaler, so Edd deduces he must live by the sea. They build a boat and ride on it over a river to find him. The river ends in a swamp, where the boat is destroyed. Ed and Eddy then prank Edd into believing that they sank to their demises in quicksand. Enraged, Edd berates Eddy for the prank and his scamming before deciding to return home. As Ed laments over their damaged friendship, Eddy is initially enraged by this, but soon breaks down crying and accepts responsibility for their predicament, prompting Edd to forgive him as the Eds continue their adventure.
Elsewhere, Nazz loses her patience with Kevin prioritizing his bicycle over her well-being and feelings while Jimmy and Sarah escape from the Kankers and are accompanied by Wilfred. The Kankers abduct Kevin, Nazz and Rolf before the Eds come across a coastal amusement park the next morning called "Mondo A-Go Go", which matches a postcard Eddy received from his brother. They conclude that Eddy's brother works there and find his whale-based trailer as the Kankers catch up to them. Eddy's brother reveals himself and, although he originally seems willing to help Eddy, is eventually shown to be physically abusive towards him without reason, leaving everyone appalled. When Edd tries to interfere, Eddy's brother assaults him, prompting everyone to defend Eddy.

plot:
Mars Needs Moms is a 3D science fiction comedy film directed by Simon Wells and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie was released on March 18, 2011.

In the beginning of the story, we are introduced to Milo (played by Seth Green), an 11-year-old boy who lives with his mother, Marta (played by Mindy Sterling), in a suburban town. Milo's life is ordinary and uneventful, but he longs for adventure and excitement. One day, while out on a walk, Milo discovers that Marta has been abducted by aliens from Mars.

The aliens, known as the Martian Moms, arrive on Earth to collect human mothers to take back to their planet. They use a device called the "Moms' Transporter" to abduct the mothers, leaving behind only one child per family. The Martian Moms believe that human children are inferior and will eventually grow up to be loyal servants.

Milo soon discovers that his mother has been taken by the aliens and sets out on a journey to rescue her. He meets a robot named Gadget (voiced by Dan Fogler), who was also left behind by his own mother, and together they embark on a quest to Mars to find Marta.

Upon arrival on Mars, Milo and Gadget encounter various obstacles and challenges as they navigate the planet's harsh environment. They meet a group of Martian kids who are being raised by the alien mothers, but have grown up to be rebellious and independent. The kids, led by a character named Lopax (voiced by Elisabeth Harnois), join forces with Milo and Gadget to help them on their mission.

As they journey deeper into Mars, Milo and his new friends face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, hostile aliens, and the harsh conditions of the Martian environment. Along the way, Milo learns valuable lessons about responsibility, loyalty, and the importance of family.

In the end, Milo and Gadget successfully rescue Marta from the clutches of the Martian Moms. However, in a surprising twist, it is revealed that the Martian Moms' plan was not to enslave humans, but to protect them from an even greater threat: a massive asteroid that is on a collision course with Earth.

With the help of the Martian kids and their mothers, Milo and Gadget are able to deflect the asteroid and save humanity. The movie ends with Milo returning home to his mother, who has been reunited with him, but not before learning about the incredible adventure he had on Mars.

Overall, Mars Needs Moms is a fun and action-packed sci-fi comedy that explores themes of family, loyalty, and responsibility. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans and offers a unique blend of humor, adventure, and heart.
