plot:
Firebreather is an American computer-animated superhero television film of 2010 based on the Image Comics series created by Phil Hester and Andy Kuhn. Directed by Peter Chung from a screenplay by James Krieg, it premiered on Cartoon Network on 24 November 2010. Jesse Head voices the teenage hero Duncan Rosenblatt, with Dana Delany as his mother Margaret, Kevin Michael Richardson as his monstrous father Belloc, Amy Davidson as Jenna, Tia Texada as Isabel, Dante Basco as Kenny and Reed Diamond as Agent "Blitz" Barnes.

On the last day of the war between humans and the giant monsters called Kaiju, their dragon-like king Belloc attacks a city, but when a woman named Margaret confronts him, the two fall in love and he withdraws. Their son, Duncan, is born with Kaiju features and powers. Sixteen years later, Margaret and Duncan move to a new town, where he fears his appearance will make him a target. He falls for the popular Jenna, makes an enemy of her former boyfriend Troy, and befriends the outcasts Kenny and Isabel, a Kaiju-obsessed girl who develops a crush on him. Blitz Barnes, an agent of a monster-defence agency posing as a gym teacher, discovers that Duncan can breathe fire.

At a party, Duncan grows closer to Jenna, but Belloc arrives and carries him off to his desert lair, presenting him to the other Kaiju as his heir and hurling him into a lava pit, from which Duncan emerges transformed. Back at school, Isabel has made him a celebrity by claiming he saved everyone from Belloc. Duncan secretly leaves a precious red crystal in Jenna's locker to replace the Homecoming money stolen by Troy's friends, and asks her to the dance. On a mission with Blitz, he spares a Kaiju he could have killed. At Homecoming, a jealous Kenny tells Duncan that Isabel likes him only because of his father, and Jenna, overhearing, storms out. Two Kaiju, Abaddon and Astaroth, then attack. Duncan holds them off, sprouts wings to save Blitz from a fall, and with the help of Belloc, summoned by Margaret and Jenna, buries the monsters in an avalanche instead of killing them. Belloc lets himself be captured so as to stay close to his son, Jenna, who has realised Duncan left the crystal, apologises, and Duncan soars away on his new wings.

Reviewing it at New York Comic Con, Mania.com gave the film a B+, praising its blend of teenage angst and monster battles while noting that the characters sometimes looked puppet-like.

title: Just Go with It
tagline: Sometimes a guy's best wingman... is a wingwoman
overview: A plastic surgeon, romancing a much younger schoolteacher, enlists his loyal assistant to pretend to be his soon to be ex-wife, in order to cover up a careless lie. When more lies backfire, the assistant's kids become involved, and everyone heads off for a weekend in Hawaii that will change all their lives.  A remake of Cactus Flower (1969).
plot:
Just Go with It is a 2011 American romantic comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan and starring Adam Sandler, Jennifer Aniston, and Brooklyn Decker.

The movie begins with Danny Maccabee (Adam Sandler), a successful plastic surgeon who has been married to his high school sweetheart, Palmer Dodge (Brooklyn Decker), for three years. However, their marriage is on the rocks due to Palmer's lack of interest in sex and her desire to have children. Feeling suffocated by the situation, Danny decides to end the relationship.

One day, while working on a new face, Danny meets Katherine Murphy (Jennifer Aniston), his receptionist who has been secretly admiring him from afar. Katherine is a single mother with a young son, who is struggling to make ends meet after her husband's death. Despite their instant attraction, Danny tries to keep his distance, fearing that he will get hurt again.

However, when Palmer reveals that she is pregnant, Danny sees an opportunity to win her back and proposes a fake engagement to Katherine, claiming that they are having an affair. The plan works initially, but things start to get complicated as Katherine begins to develop real feelings for Danny.

As the story unfolds, Katherine's son, Gabe (Nathan Parsons), becomes a catalyst for change in Danny's life. Through his interactions with Gabe, Danny starts to see Katherine in a different light and realizes that he has fallen in love with her. Meanwhile, Palmer's pregnancy progresses, and she begins to realize that she is not ready to be a mother.

The plot thickens when Katherine discovers the truth about Danny's fake engagement and feels betrayed. However, instead of being angry, she decides to give it another chance and proposes a real relationship to Danny. The movie culminates with Danny and Katherine confessing their love for each other and starting a new life together.

Throughout the film, Adam Sandler delivers his signature comedic charm, while Jennifer Aniston brings warmth and depth to her character. Brooklyn Decker shines as Palmer, providing a perfect foil to the on-screen chemistry between Sandler and Aniston. The movie's lighthearted tone, witty dialogue, and engaging storyline make it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Just Go with It is a heartwarming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, relationships, and self-discovery. With its talented cast, engaging plot, and uplifting message, this movie is sure to leave viewers feeling entertained and inspired.

title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 1
original_title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 1
tagline: Forever is just the beginning
overview: The new found married bliss of Bella Swan and vampire Edward Cullen is cut short when a series of betrayals and misfortunes threatens to destroy their world.
plot:
Several months after the events of the previous film, human Bella Swan and vampire Edward Cullen are getting married. During the reception, werewolf Jacob Black, who had left town upon receiving his invitation to the wedding, returns, much to Bella's delight. They share a dance in the woods, where Bella says that she and Edward plan to consummate their marriage on their honeymoon while she is still human. Jacob becomes furious, fearing that such an act could kill her.
After the wedding, Bella and Edward travel to an island off the coast of Rio de Janeiro for their honeymoon, and they have sex for the first time. Two weeks later, Bella vomits after waking and realizes her period is late. She informs Carlisle Cullen, a medical doctor and Edward's adoptive father, that she believes she is pregnant.
Edward is distraught, as it is highly unlikely a human could survive giving birth to a vampire's baby. He encourages Bella to receive an abortion from Carlisle. She refuses and convinces Edward's sister Rosalie to be her bodyguard. The couple flies back home to Forks, Washington, where Jacob rushes to the Cullens' house to find a pale, underweight, and visibly pregnant Bella. He implores her to terminate the pregnancy immediately, but she refuses.
Jacob storms out of the Cullens' residence and meets in the woods with his packmates, including their leader Sam, who soon feels they should kill Bella to ensure her half-vampire child does not harm anyone. Jacob refuses, and he and several other werewolves separate from the pack.
As Bella's pregnancy progresses, her health declines rapidly. She soon realizes the fetus is craving blood, so she begins drinking human blood obtained by Carlisle from the hospital, improving her health. As a half-vampire, the fetus's development is far more accelerated than that of a human fetus, and thus Bella's pregnancy progresses at an alarming rate.
Edward's resentment for the baby dissolves when he discovers he can read its thoughts. When Bella suddenly goes into labor, Edward, Jacob, and Rosalie begin performing an emergency C-section while Carlisle is out obtaining blood. The procedure is excruciatingly painful, and Bella falls unconscious, though she wakes to find she has delivered a healthy daughter, whom she names Renesmee—a combination of her mother's name and Edward's mother's name.
Bella's heart suddenly stops, and Jacob desperately attempts CPR. Edward injects Bella's heart with his venom in an attempt to transform her into a vampire, but his action seems futile as Bella remains lifeless. A distraught Jacob decides to kill Renesmee for apparently causing Bella's death; however, when he looks into the baby's eyes, he "imprints" on her: a werewolf phenomenon in which one realizes one's soulmate. This prevents his pack from killing her as their most absolute law is not to harm anyone who has been imprinted on.
Over the course of two days, though still unconscious, Bella's injuries heal and her figure returns to normal.

plot:

The story begins with the Volturi, an ancient vampire coven, believing that the Cullens have created an "immortal child," which is against the law of the vampire world. The Volturi, led by Aro (Michael Sheen), believe that the Cullens are hiding a secret and plan to destroy them.

The Cullens gather witnesses from around the world to testify on their behalf, including Jacob Black (Taylor Lautner), who has fallen in love with Renesmee. The Cullens also prepare for a potential battle against the Volturi, while Bella and Edward try to protect their daughter from the danger that surrounds her.

As the story unfolds, the Cullens face off against the Volturi in a dramatic showdown. The movie features stunning action sequences, impressive visual effects, and emotional moments between the characters.

Throughout the film, Bella struggles with her newfound motherhood and her relationship with Edward, who is still struggling to accept their daughter as one of his own. Meanwhile, Jacob's love for Renesmee deepens, and he must come to terms with his role in the Cullens' lives.

Ultimately, the Cullens are able to prove that Renesmee is not an immortal child, but a half-human, half-vampire hybrid, which changes the rules of the vampire world. The Volturi are defeated, and the Cullens are finally able to live in peace with their daughter by their side.

The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2 concludes the series on a hopeful note, with Bella and Edward's love stronger than ever, and Renesmee growing up as a powerful and unique individual. The movie features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and emotional moments that will leave audiences satisfied and fulfilled.

Overall, The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2 is a satisfying conclusion to the series, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers engaged until the very end.

title: Prison-A-Go-Go!
overview: A women-in-prison action comedy featuring girls running amok! Multiple Shower Scenes! Kung Fu Food Fights! Mutant Zombies! Evil Scientists, Prominent Product Placement, and Mud Wrastlin!
plot:
Prison-A-Go-Go! is a 2003 American low-budget action comedy directed by Barak Epstein, who wrote it with Mike Wiebe, and produced by WorldWide International Picture Studios, known for campy B-movies. A deliberate parody of and homage to the women-in-prison exploitation genre, it also borrows from zombie horror, mad-scientist pictures and ninja films. Laurie Walton plays the heroine Janie, with Lauren Graham as her sister Callista, Travis Willingham as the villainous Dr. Hurtrider, Rhonda Shear as the inmate Jackpot and Ilram Choi as a ninja, while Mary Woronov and the Troma Entertainment chief Lloyd Kaufman make cameo appearances and Wiebe plays the prison's new warden.

Janie, a small-town veterinarian, sees her sister kidnapped by the henchmen of Dr. Hurtrider, a self-described scientist and torturer who intends to experiment on Callista in his absurd quest to cure the common cold, using torture, lobotomies and genetic mutation even on people who are not sick. The abductors conveniently leave behind a business card giving the doctor's address as the biggest prison in the Philippines, and the dim-witted Janie concludes that the only way to reach her sister is to get herself locked up there. She kills a local vagrant, receives her sentence and is shipped off to the institution.

Inside, she finds a surreal place where the guards are gay, the women are more victims of fashion than of violence and the newly hired warden, appointed by an executive played by Woronov, is spectacularly lazy. An on-screen shower clock counts down to the next of the film's many shower scenes. Teaming up with the queen bee Jackpot, a gang of fellow inmates and a reluctant, acrobatic ninja, Janie must find Callista before Hurtrider turns her into a human-porcupine hybrid, while his laboratory experiments also produce flesh-eating zombies. The film also promised kung fu food fights and mud wrestling.

Shot on 35 mm film with rented equipment, Prison-A-Go-Go! premiered at the 2003 Deep Ellum Film Festival, where it was named best feature, and it won four prizes at that year's B-Movie Film Festival, including best B-movie, best director and best actress for Shear, followed by festival awards in 2004. It was released on DVD in 2005. Critics were largely unimpressed. DVD Talk found it a tiresome spoof with occasional laughs, praising Woronov, Wiebe and Choi, and Film Blitz felt it pointed out the genre's clichés without exaggerating them enough to be truly funny.

title: Crazy, Stupid, Love.
tagline: This is crazy. This is stupid. This is love.
overview: Cal Weaver is living the American dream. He has a good job, a beautiful house, great children and a beautiful wife, named Emily. Cal's seemingly perfect life unravels, however, when he learns that Emily has been unfaithful and wants a divorce. Over 40 and suddenly single, Cal is adrift in the fickle world of dating. Enter, Jacob Palmer, a self-styled player who takes Cal under his wing and teaches him how to be a hit with the ladies.
plot:
Cal Weaver is a middle-aged family man whose wife Emily asks for a divorce after she reveals an affair she had with co-worker David Lindhagen. The news stuns Cal, who jumps out of their moving car when Emily tries to talk about the affair. The divorce also ends his friendship with best friend Bernie Riley, whose wife sides with Emily over Cal.
After moving into his own apartment, Cal begins frequenting an upscale bar, where he talks loudly about his wife cheating and divorce. He meets Jacob Palmer, a young man and womanizer who frequently beds different women but was recently rejected by a law school graduate, Hannah. Jacob takes pity on Cal and offers to teach him how to pick up women. After a few awkward attempts to talk to women, Cal seduces a woman named Kate at the bar. This experience gives him the confidence to seduce other women, and he begins to emulate Jacob's example successfully.
Eventually, Cal and Emily reunite at their 13-year-old son Robbie's parent–teacher conference, where she is impressed by his newfound confidence and fitted clothes. Their reunion goes well until they meet Robbie's teacher, who turns out to be Kate, and who spitefully reveals her and Cal's tryst because he never called her afterwards. In the ensuing argument, Cal inadvertently confesses to having sex with nine women since their separation, so Emily leaves in disgust that Cal did this as payback for her cheating while also openly dating David.
Robbie makes numerous grand gestures to win the heart of his babysitter Jessica, who is Bernie's daughter. She eventually dissuades him after revealing she likes someone older, without revealing it is Cal. On the advice of a promiscuous classmate, she takes nude photos of herself, intending to give them to him. Emily calls Cal under the guise of needing help with the pilot light on her water heater, but he sees through the ruse. Realizing that she called just because she missed him, Cal decides to win her back.
Meanwhile, Hannah is offended by her boyfriend when he offers her a position at his firm instead of proposing as expected. She returns to the bar, finds Jacob, and throws herself at him. As Jacob ends up walking her through his process of seducing women, they end up developing genuine chemistry and start dating.
Jacob returns Cal's calls, asking for advice about being in a real relationship and meeting his girlfriend's parents. Jessica's mother finds the naked photos, which make her and Bernie believe that Cal and Jessica are in an illicit relationship. He furiously drives to Cal's, with Jessica following to stop him.
Cal and his kids create a makeshift mini golf set in their backyard to remind Emily of their first date. During the gathering, Jacob and Hannah show up, and Hannah is revealed to be Cal and Emily's daughter. Cal is appalled that Jacob is dating his daughter, and forbids her from seeing him. Emily supports their relationship.

title: The Resident
tagline: She Thought She Was Living Alone
overview: Juliet, a beautiful doctor, has found the perfect New York apartment to start a new life after separating from her husband. It's got spacious rooms, a spectacular view, and a handy, handsome landlord. But there are secrets behind every wall and terror in every room as Juliet gets the unnerving feeling that she is not alone.
plot:
The Resident is a 2011 American psychological thriller directed by Antti Jokinen and starring Hilary Swank and Jeffrey Dean Morgan, with Lee Pace, Aunjanue Ellis and Christopher Lee in supporting roles. Produced by the revived Hammer Films, it marked Lee's return to the studio for the first time since To the Devil a Daughter in 1976. Swank plays a newly separated woman who moves into a New York apartment and comes to suspect that someone is watching her.

Juliet Devereau, an emergency room physician, rents a spacious Brooklyn apartment from its charming landlord, Max. She has recently left her husband Jack after discovering his affair, though she still has feelings for him. Unknown to Juliet, someone is stalking her, watching from across the street and apparently entering the apartment when she is away. At a party she runs into Max and flirts with him, and the two begin a tentative romance, but when they are about to sleep together she stops, admitting that she cannot stop thinking about Jack, and she ends things with Max.

A flashback reveals that Max is the one stalking her. He has rebuilt the apartment with hidden passageways and a two-way mirror that allow him to spy on her, and he lives with his elderly grandfather August, played by Lee. After Juliet's rejection, Max's obsession grows darker. He enters her apartment while she is at work and violates her private space, watches her reconcile with Jack and begins drugging her wine so he can be near her while she is unconscious. After oversleeping repeatedly, Juliet suspects something is wrong and installs security cameras. Max attacks and injures Jack and, one night, attempts to assault the drugged Juliet before she stirs and he flees. Tests at the hospital reveal high levels of Demerol in her system, and the camera footage finally shows her the truth. When Max returns and attacks her again, Juliet must fight for her life inside the hidden spaces of the building he controls.

Critical response was mostly negative: Rotten Tomatoes reports that 35% of 31 critics gave it a positive review. The Guardian called it generic and intermittently silly, while the Financial Times praised Swank's performance and Total Film described it as a sturdy, moody thriller undone by its over-the-top climax. A novelization by Francis Cottam was published in 2011.

Naruto Shippuden the Movie: The Lost Tower is a 2010 Japanese animated action-adventure fantasy film based on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga and its anime adaptation. It is the fourth film in the Naruto Shippuden series, directed by Masahiko Murata and produced by Studio Pierrot, and it was released in Japan on July 31, 2010. The Japanese voice cast includes Junko Takeuchi as Naruto, Chie Nakamura as Sakura, Toshiyuki Morikawa as Minato, Kazuhiko Inoue as Kakashi and Satoshi Hino as Sai. A comic short, Naruto, the Genie, and the Three Wishes!!, was screened alongside it, and the theme song "if" was performed by Kana Nishino.

Naruto Uzumaki, Sakura Haruno, Sai and their captain Yamato are sent to capture Mukade, a rogue ninja. They track him to the thousand-year-old ruins of Loran, a desert city, where he plans to dominate the ninja world by seizing the power of the Ryūmyaku, an ancient stream of chakra flowing deep underground. Mukade breaks a seal placed long ago by Minato Namikaze, Naruto's father and the Fourth Hokage, unleashing a blast of light that engulfs Naruto and Yamato while Sakura and Sai escape on one of Sai's ink birds.

Naruto awakens twenty years in the past, in the time of Loran's prosperity, and meets the city's young queen, Sāra. Mukade, it turns out, was thrown back six years earlier and has taken the identity of Anrokuzan, a minister who murdered Sāra's mother and now uses the kingdom's kidnapped citizens to build an army of puppet ninjas. Naruto vows to protect Sāra, and he is soon joined by a younger Minato, along with Kakashi Hatake, Shibi Aburame and Chōza Akimichi, who are on their own mission to stop Anrokuzan. Fighting side by side with the father he never knew, though neither recognizes the other, Naruto helps rescue Loran's people. When Anrokuzan transforms the tower into a gigantic puppet, Naruto and Minato combine their chakra in a powerful attack, and Minato finally seals the Ryūmyaku and erases everyone's memories so that history remains unchanged.

Back in the present, the team reunites in the ruins and meets Sāra's daughter, who carries a chakra blade that her mother received from a "hero in a dream." Naruto recognizes it as his own, while Sakura insists he must have been dreaming.

The film is set after episode 143 of the Naruto: Shippuden anime. It was released on DVD in Japan in April 2011, and Viz Media released it in North America on September 17, 2013.

title: Ticking Clock
overview: A reporter stumbles upon the journal of a murderer with plans to butcher specific girls, and he begins to investigates on his own, and finding that every trail leads to a 9-year-old orphan living in a group home.
plot:
Ticking Clock is a 2011 American mystery thriller directed by Ernie Barbarash and released direct to DVD in the United States on January 4, 2011. Cuba Gooding Jr. stars as the investigative reporter Louis Hicks, with Neal McDonough as the serial killer Keech, Nicki Aycox as Polly, Austin Abrams as the boy James, Danielle Nicolet as Louis's wife Gina and Yancey Arias as a detective.

The film opens as Keech kills a woman and then comforts her crying baby son. Louis is struggling with a faltering career and a troubled marriage, and is having an affair with a district attorney, Felicia, who ends their relationship. That same day Keech murders her at her home. Louis fights the intruder, who escapes but leaves behind his journal, which lists two more murders planned over the next three days. Louis copies down the names, but Keech steals back both the journal and the note, and when Louis goes to the police he becomes a suspect in Felicia's death.

Louis tracks down one of the intended victims, a schoolteacher named Vicki, but Keech reaches her first and kills her in a bar after talking with her about a boy she reported for hurting a cat. With the police still unconvinced, Louis sends a scrap of Keech's coat and a bloody fingerprint to a friend at a crime lab. The blood matches an eleven-year-old orphan, James, who lives in a boys' home run by Polly, and the coat's fabric behaves unlike any known material. James, a disturbed boy who wishes he could go back in time and fix his life, shows Louis a box of dead animals and then angrily sends him away.

Realising that Polly is the next name on the list, Louis concludes that Keech is James grown up and returned from the future. Jailed by sceptical police, he is visited by Keech posing as his lawyer, who confirms that he has travelled back from 2032 with a pocket-watch time machine. Keech explains that he killed his abusive mother hoping to change his childhood, but every change has led someone else to condemn him to the same fate, and he now plans to kill Polly and frame Louis. On the roof of the boys' home, young James confronts his older self and slashes him with a dropped knife, Keech accidentally knocks the boy off the roof and shoots Louis, and with James's death Keech vanishes and all of his victims are restored to life.

Ticking Clock received negative reviews, with Dread Central calling it an iffy thriller with an intriguing but underdeveloped premise.

title: The Beaver
tagline: He's here to save Walter's life.
overview: Suffering from a severe case of depression, toy company CEO Walter Black begins using a beaver hand puppet to help him open up to his family. With his father seemingly going insane, adolescent son Porter pushes for his parents to get a divorce.
plot:
The Beaver is a 2011 American psychological drama directed by Jodie Foster and written by Kyle Killen. It stars Mel Gibson as Walter Black, Foster as his wife Meredith, Anton Yelchin as their teenage son Porter and Jennifer Lawrence as Norah, with Cherry Jones and Riley Thomas Stewart. The film marked the second collaboration between Gibson and Foster, after the 1994 western comedy Maverick.

Walter Black is the chief executive of a family toy company that is sliding toward bankruptcy, and he has sunk into a deep, paralyzing depression. Unable to reach him, Meredith asks him to leave the family home, much to the relief of Porter, who resents his father and fears becoming like him. Living alone in a hotel and at his lowest point, Walter finds a beaver hand puppet in a dumpster. He begins to wear the puppet constantly and to speak only through it in a gruff voice, as if the beaver were a separate personality guiding him.

At first the strange arrangement seems to work miracles. Walter reconnects with his younger son Henry and wins back Meredith, and the company enjoys an unexpected revival thanks to a new line of building kits for children inspired by the beaver. Meanwhile, Porter, who earns money writing papers for classmates, is hired by Norah, a classmate, to write her graduation speech, and the two grow close as he senses that she is hiding grief over the death of her brother. Yet as Walter's dependence on the puppet deepens, Meredith realizes that the beaver is not a therapy but a sign of how ill her husband is, and the family must face the darkness behind the puppet before it consumes Walter entirely.

The film treats mental illness with a mix of dark humor and sincerity, exploring depression, identity and the burdens that parents pass on to their children.

The Beaver premiered at the SXSW Film Festival on March 16, 2011, and was released in the United States by Summit Entertainment on May 6, 2011. It received mixed reviews, with about 62 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 60; Gibson's performance and Foster's direction were praised, but the film was a box-office flop against its 21 million dollar budget.

title: Martha Marcy May Marlene
tagline: You can get away. But you can never escape.
overview: After several years of living with a cult, Martha finally escapes and calls her estranged sister, Lucy, for help. Martha finds herself at the quiet Connecticut home Lucy shares with her new husband, Ted, but the memories of what she experienced in the cult make peace hard to find. As flashbacks continue to torment her, Martha fails to shake a terrible sense of dread, especially in regard to the cult's manipulative leader.
plot:
A 22-year-old woman named Martha has been abused by a cult in the Catskill Mountains for two years. The patriarch, Patrick, named her Marcy May. She escapes into the woods, arriving at a nearby town. In a diner, she is confronted by Watts, a cult member, who attempts to persuade her to return, but when she refuses, he lets her leave. Martha calls her sister, Lucy, who picks her up and takes her to the vacation lake house in Connecticut that she shares with her husband, a successful architect named Ted.
Martha exhibits strange behavior by skinny dipping in public, sleeping all the time, not eating, and arguing with Lucy and Ted about how to live, specifically arguing over the need for career and possessions. Lucy reveals she abandoned Martha and is now attempting to get her back into her life, while she and Ted are also trying to have their own child. One night, Martha climbs into bed with Ted and Lucy while they are having sex, angering Ted and Lucy. Martha attempts to phone the cult because she misses them, accidentally finds out her friend Zoe is not on the farm with the cult, and hangs up when cult matriarch Katie answers using the code name "Marlene Miller."
In flashbacks, Martha recalls a series of disturbing events that led to her escape from the cult. She was originally recruited into the cult by Zoe. Martha was initially receptive but somewhat wary of Patrick, Katie, and Zoe. She was later convinced by Zoe and Patrick to let her guard down and "share herself", only to end up being drugged by Katie and brutally raped by Patrick; Katie and Zoe later explained to her that the rape was a cleansing ritual and told her she should be happy. Martha later "prepared" new initiate Sarah to be abused in the same way Katie had. Patrick urged Martha to kill a cat, which Martha refused. Her refusal prompted him to berate her for failing to follow the cult's ideals. Patrick constantly attempted to impregnate Martha to spread his genes, despite her resistance. Martha subsequently began participating in burglaries with the other cultists, including one where they murdered a homeowner who walked in on them. After witnessing the murder, Martha had a mental breakdown, to which Patrick responded by forcefully subduing her and berating her again; he then shifted to telling her that she was his favorite person and that he would never let her go.
Lucy and Ted host a party at their home, inviting numerous friends from the city. Martha is visibly nervous during the gathering. She has a psychotic episode when she misidentifies the bartender as a cult member; Lucy and Ted sedate her. Ted attempts to convince Lucy to send Martha to a psychiatric hospital, an idea Lucy rejects.
Later that night, Martha has a nightmare of being sexually abused by Patrick. Ted tries to calm her down, but Martha, thinking he is Patrick, kicks him down the staircase in a frightened panic.

title: Arthur Christmas
tagline: Ever wonder how 2 Billion presents get delivered all in 1 night?
overview: Each Christmas, Santa and his vast army of highly trained elves produce gifts and distribute them around the world in one night. However, when one of 600 million children to receive a gift from Santa on Christmas Eve is missed, it is deemed ‘acceptable’ to all but one—Arthur. plot:
Arthur Christmas is a heartwarming animated comedy film released in 2011 by Columbia Pictures. The movie follows the story of Arthur, the eldest son of Santa Claus, who is struggling to live up to his father's expectations.

The film begins on Christmas Eve at the North Pole, where Santa and his wife, Mrs. Claus, are preparing for the big night. However, with the help of their elves, they manage to deliver all the presents in record time, thanks to a high-tech system that allows them to track every child's gift. The system is so efficient that it becomes redundant, and Arthur finds himself feeling unappreciated and overlooked.

As Christmas Eve comes to an end, Santa announces his retirement and names Arthur as his successor. However, Arthur is not interested in taking over the reins of the North Pole, and he spends most of his time trying to avoid his responsibilities. Meanwhile, a young girl named Sophie receives a gift that was left behind by Santa's high-tech system, which fails to deliver it on time.

Sophie teams up with Arthur's younger brother, Steve, who is more interested in playing video games than helping out at the North Pole. Together, they embark on a mission to find the missing gift and return it to its rightful owner. Along the way, they encounter a series of hilarious misadventures, including a run-in with a group of bumbling burglars.

As Arthur and Steve journey through the city, they begin to realize that Christmas is not just about presents, but about the joy and love that comes with giving and receiving. They also learn more about their father's legacy and the importance of following in his footsteps.

In the end, Arthur and Steve successfully deliver the gift, and Sophie returns home with a newfound appreciation for the magic of Christmas. Meanwhile, Santa is forced to come out of retirement and help his sons on their mission, proving that he still has what it takes to be a great Santa Claus.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a mix of traditional and computer-generated imagery. The voice cast, including James McAvoy as Arthur, Hugh Laurie as Steve, and Bill Nighy as Santa, brings the characters to life in a way that is both humorous and heartwarming.

Overall, Arthur Christmas is a delightful holiday film that celebrates the spirit of giving and the importance of family. With its witty humor, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for families around the world.

title: Donkey's Christmas Shrektacular
overview: Deck the halls with Donkey’s laughter in this all-new holiday collection. Donkey presents his very own carolling stage show featuring his Far Far Away pals in this merry, musical treat with all the trimmings! plot:
Donkey's Christmas Shrektacular, whose short is also titled Donkey's Caroling Christmas-tacular, is a 2010 American computer-animated musical holiday short from DreamWorks Animation, set in the world of the Shrek films. Directed by Walt Dohrn, with Raman Hui also credited as co-director in some sources, and written by Dohrn and Ryan Crego, it was produced by Gina Shay, Teresa Cheng and Chad Hammes with music by Matt Mahaffey. It was released on 7 December 2010 as a bonus holiday DVD packaged with the home release of Shrek Forever After, and as a special feature on that film's Blu-ray.

The short takes place in the Candy Apple, the friendly new incarnation of the Poison Apple tavern, where Donkey hosts a Christmas party and persuades everyone to join him in a caroling stage show. He opens with "It's the Most Wonderful Time of the Year" alongside his fairy-tale friends. Shrek, who surprises everyone by agreeing to sing, joins Fiona, their three ogre children and the ogre army in a gleefully gross ogre version of "Jingle Bells", with lyrics about bug cocoons and cricket slurps. Puss in Boots follows with "Fleas Navidad", a take on "Feliz Navidad" that he claims is a classic from his village, and the whole company closes with "Fairy Tale Rock", a rendition of "Jingle Bell Rock". Running gags in the background include Gingy trying to rescue lifeless gingerbread cookies, the Three Little Pigs preparing for swimsuit weather and Rumpelstiltskin trapped in a cage.

Eddie Murphy returns as Donkey, after being replaced by Dean Edwards in Scared Shrekless, alongside Mike Myers as Shrek, Cameron Diaz as Fiona and Antonio Banderas as Puss. Walt Dohrn voices Rumpelstiltskin, Jon Hamm the ogre Brogan, Cody Cameron Pinocchio and the pigs, Conrad Vernon Gingy and Aron Warner the Big Bad Wolf, with Craig Robinson and Jane Lynch also among the ogres. It was the last Shrek production to reunite the core original cast until Shrek 5.

The holiday disc rounds out the main short with a Donkey decoration game and Shrek's Yule Log, a half-hour virtual fireplace in Shrek's house in which characters such as Rumpelstiltskin, Puss, Fiona and Gingy wander through with festive gags.

title: Mean Girls 2
tagline: The Plastics are back!
overview: After a clique of girls makes life difficult, a new student forms a rival group to take control of the school's corridors.
plot:
Mean Girls 2 is a 2011 American teen comedy TV film directed by Melanie Mayron from a script by Cliff Ruby, Elana Lesser and Allison Schroeder. A sequel to the 2004 film Mean Girls, it stars Meaghan Martin as Jo Mitchell, Maiara Walsh as Mandi Weatherly, Jennifer Stone as Abby Hanover, Nicole Gale Anderson, Claire Holt, Diego Boneta as Tyler and Linden Ashby, with Tim Meadows returning as Principal Ron Duvall.

Jo, a tomboy who has changed schools many times because of her father's work rebuilding NASCAR engines, arrives at North Shore High School in Ohio hoping to get into Carnegie Mellon, which her late mother attended. There she meets the Plastics, a clique led by Mandi, with the airheaded Chastity and the germ-phobic Hope. Jo befriends Mandi's outcast rival Abby, and the two are drawn into a prank war. Abby's wealthy father offers to pay Jo's college tuition if she stays friends with his daughter, and Jo reluctantly agrees. She falls for Tyler, a classmate from shop class, and the group gains Quinn, a student journalist. Mandi bugs the car Tyler borrows for a date in order to humiliate Jo, who then learns that Tyler is Mandi's stepbrother.

The feud escalates: Mandi tries to wreck Jo's Carnegie Mellon prospects and sabotages one of her father's engines. When Mandi plans her invitation-only birthday party, Jo throws an open party for Abby on the same night. The Plastics lace Abby's pizza with ipecac, but Jo hides it and later hands a slice to Mandi's boyfriend Nick, who vomits on Mandi. Jo, Abby and Quinn form the "Anti-Plastics", and Jo challenges Mandi for homecoming queen, but Jo realises she is becoming just like Mandi and tries to return the money. Mandi learns of the arrangement and persuades Quinn to expose it in the school paper, straining Jo's friendship with Abby. Mandi and Nick then steal the homecoming charity money meant for an animal shelter and plant it in Jo's shed, getting her expelled. Jo challenges Mandi to flag football. Learning that Jo was probably framed, Tyler and Abby recruit the tech-savvy Elliott, who finds video of the theft and sends it to the whole school. The Anti-Plastics win the game, Mandi and Nick are arrested, Jo is allowed to graduate, and she and Abby go on to Carnegie Mellon together.

Shot in Atlanta over twenty days in July 2010 the film premiered on ABC Family on January 23, 2011, and came out on DVD a month later. Reviews were negative; Entertainment Weekly saw it as a cheap remake of the original.

title: Horrible Bosses
tagline: Ever wish your boss was dead?
overview: For Nick, Kurt and Dale, the only thing that would make the daily grind more tolerable would be to grind their intolerable bosses into dust. Quitting is not an option, so, with the benefit of a few-too-many drinks and some dubious advice from a hustling ex-con, the three friends devise a convoluted and seemingly foolproof plan to rid themselves of their respective employers... permanently.
plot:
Nick Hendricks, Dale Arbus, and Kurt Buckman are friends working in Riverside, California, who despise their bosses: Nick works at a financial firm for the sadistic Dave Harken, who hints at a possible promotion for Nick for months, only to award it to himself; Dale is a dental assistant being sexually harassed by his boss, Dr. Julia Harris, who threatens to tell his fiancée Stacy that he had sex with her unless he actually has sex with her; Kurt enjoys working for the kind-hearted Jack Pellit at his chemical company, but after Jack unexpectedly dies of a heart attack, the company is taken over by Jack's arrogant, cocaine-addicted son Bobby, whose apathy and incompetence threaten the future of the company.
One night, over drinks, Kurt jokingly suggests that their lives would be happier if their bosses were no longer alive. Initially hesitant, they eventually agree to kill their bosses. In search of a hitman, the trio meet Dean "Motherfucker" Jones, an ex-con who offers to be their "murder consultant." Jones suggests that they kill each other's bosses to hide their motives, while making the deaths look like accidents.
The trio sneak into Bobby's house, and Kurt steals his phone. They next go to Harken's house, where Kurt and Nick go inside while Dale waits in the car as a lookout. Harken returns home and confronts Dale for littering, and then has an allergic reaction from the peanut butter on the litter. Dale saves him by stabbing him with an EpiPen, but Nick and Kurt think he is stabbing Harken to death and flee, with Kurt accidentally dropping Bobby's phone in Harken's bedroom.
The next night, Kurt watches Julia's home, but she seduces and has sex with him. Nick and Dale wait outside Bobby's and Harken's houses, respectively, to commit the murders, but are hesitant to follow through. Harken discovers Bobby's phone in his bedroom and uses it to find his address, suspecting his wife, Rhonda, is having an affair with Bobby. Harken drives over and shoots Bobby dead, while Nick secretly witnesses the murder.
Nick flees at high speed, setting off a traffic camera. The trio meet at a bar and plan to leave the police an anonymous tip to get Harken arrested. However, the police bring them in for questioning, as the camera footage makes Nick the prime suspect in Bobby's murder.
Dale points out that they lack sufficient evidence to hold them there, forcing the police to release them. However, the trio are warned that forensics is sweeping the house for DNA, so they realize the prank Kurt pulled during their first break-in has left enough evidence to convict them. The trio consult with Jones again, but learn that he never actually killed anyone or committed any felonies, having been imprisoned for only bootlegging a film. Jones suggests that they get Harken to confess and secretly tape it.

plot:
Prom is a 2011 American teen romantic comedy directed by Joe Nussbaum, written by Katie Wech and produced by Ted Griffin and Justin Springer for Walt Disney Pictures. Aimee Teegarden stars as Nova Prescott and Thomas McDonell as Jesse Richter, with Danielle Campbell as Simone, Nolan Sotillo as Lucas, DeVaughn Nixon as Tyler, Kylie Bunbury as Jordan and Nicholas Braun as Lloyd. It follows students at a Michigan high school before their prom.

Nova, on the prom committee, hopes her crush Brandon will ask her to the dance. Mei fears telling her boyfriend Justin she got into a different university. Shy Lucas wants to ask his lab partner Simone, and Lloyd cannot find a date at all. When the popular Tyler takes his girlfriend Jordan on a candlelit date in the shed where the prom decorations are stored, a candle left burning sets it on fire. Nova must rebuild everything, and the principal tells Jesse, a disrespectful student indifferent to prom, to help her or not graduate. The two reluctantly begin working together, and as Brandon fails to ask her out, Nova grows closer to Jesse. A spying mission at a rival school ends with police catching them.

As Lucas courts Simone, Tyler, who has been cheating on Jordan, begins pursuing her too. Simone surprises Lucas with concert tickets, and he drops his friend Corey to take her, but after Jordan dumps Tyler, Tyler asks Simone to prom that night, and she accepts. Mei finally tells Justin the truth, and he is proud of her. Nova admits to her friends that she has feelings for Jesse, but her father, who overhears, tells Jesse he is dragging her down and must not ask her to prom. On prom night, Lucas begs Simone not to go, then makes amends by taking Corey to the concert. Nova learns what her father did and storms out, while Jesse's mother persuades him to go after her. At the dance, Tyler abandons Simone, who leaves to dance with Lucas outside. As a heartbroken Nova is about to leave, the broken fountain springs back to life; Jesse has fixed it, and he asks her to prom.

Disney developed the film after the success of High School Musical 3, in the vein of John Hughes, with a modest budget and newcomers. Shot in Los Angeles, it was the first major release filmed on Arri Alexa cameras. Released on April 29, 2011, it opened fifth and grossed $10.1 million domestically. Reviews were mixed to negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported 36% approval, calling it more nuanced and less cynical than expected but just as corny and clichéd.

title: The Man from Nowhere
tagline: Nothing to lose, nothing to compromise.
overview: His only friend called him 'the man from nowhere'... Taesik, a former special agent becomes a loner after losing his wife in a miserable accident and lives a bitter life running a pawnshop. He only has a few customers and a friend named Somi, a little girl next door. As Taesik spends more and more time with Somi, he gets attached to her. Then Somi is kidnapped by a gang, and as Taesik tries to save Somi by becoming deeply associated with the gang his mysterious past is revealed.
plot:
Cha Tae-sik is a quiet man running a pawnshop. His only friend is So-mi, a little girl living next door. So-mi's mother Hyo-jeong is a go-go dancer and opium addict. Instructed by her lover, Hyo-jeong steals a large pack of opium being sold at the bar where she works and hides it in a camera bag, which she pawns to Tae-sik for safekeeping. Drug lord Oh Myung-gyu tasks his subordinate brothers, Man-seok and Jong-seok, with retrieving the opium. Jong-seok locates Hyo-jeong and tortures her in front of So-mi until she reveals the location of the drugs.
Jong-seok's lackeys Du-chi and Bear go to the pawnshop, but Tae-sik easily overpowers them. Holding So-mi hostage, Jong-seok forces Tae-sik to deliver the opium to Myung-gyu. Man-seok, tired of working for his brother, informs the police, but Myung-gyu evades arrest. Tae-sik is arrested after discovering Hyo-jeong's body, with her organs harvested, in the trunk of his car. Tae-sik escapes from the police station, alarming them with his display of combat skills. Upon further investigation, the officers discover that Tae-sik was a former covert operative for South Korean Army Intelligence, but retired after an assassin killed his pregnant wife.
The brothers track down Hyo-jeong's lover and kill him, while the brothers' bodyguard Ramrowan kills Myung-gyu, thus allowing the brothers to take over his operations. Following a lead from the burner phone Jong-seok gave him, Tae-sik tracks Du-chi to a nightclub. As Tae-sik asks about the brothers, Ramrowan walks in and shoots at them, killing Du-chi and wounding Tae-sik. Tae-sik escapes and finds his former partner, who gives Tae-sik medical care and helps him acquire a gun. Tae-sik goes back to the city and discovers a drug manufacturing plant; in the process of destroying it, he kills Jong-seok and frees the enslaved child workers.
Tae-sik confronts Man-seok's gang at his condominium. Claiming that he had So-mi's eyes harvested, Man-seok shows Tae-sik a container with two preserved eyeballs. Enraged, Tae-sik brutally kills the gang members, including Ramrowan and Man-seok. As Tae-sik prepares to commit suicide out of grief, a dirty but unharmed So-mi finds him. Ramrowan, who took pity on her because she had been kind to him, had spared her life—the eyes in the container belonged to the gangsters' surgeon. The police allow Tae-sik and So-mi to ride together after Tae-sik's arrest. When So-mi falls asleep, Tae-sik asks them to stop at a small convenience store where he buys a backpack along with other school supplies. Tae-sik tells So-mi that she is going to be on her own as the police have to take him away. Before leaving, Tae-sik asks her for a hug and breaks down in tears as they embrace.

title: Death Race 2
tagline: 10 killer drivers, 20,000 rounds of ammo. 1 survivor.
overview: In the world's most dangerous prison, a new game is born: Death Race. The rules of this adrenaline-fueled blood sport are simple, drive or die. When repentant convict Carl Lucas discovers there's a price on his head, his only hope is to survive a twisted race against an army of hardened criminals and tricked-out cars.
plot:
A gang robs a bank on behalf of crime boss Markus Kane. When two police officers unexpectedly enter the building, getaway driver Carl "Luke" Lucas urges his accomplices to abort the robbery, but they refuse. Luke intervenes, resulting in the death of one of the robbers. He then kills a police officer and abandons the remaining accomplices to complete Markus's plan. After a high-speed chase, Luke is captured, sentenced to life in prison, and eventually transferred to Terminal Island. Markus, convinced Luke will trade information for immunity despite Luke's vow of silence, orders his assassination.
Terminal Island is a for-profit, maximum-security prison operated by business magnate R. H. Weyland of Weyland Corporation. One of Weyland's primary revenue streams is "Death Match", a televised, pay-per-view gladiatorial combat event in which inmates fight using weapons or improvised defensive gear. September Jones, a disgraced former Miss Universe now employed by Weyland, hosts the spectacle.
Upon arrival, Luke befriends fellow inmates "Lists", Goldberg, and Rocco. He draws September's attention after defending Lists from an attempted assault. September makes sexual advances toward Luke and pressures him to participate in a Death Match in exchange for privileges, but he refuses. In retaliation, she selects Lists to fight "Big Bill", the massive prisoner who attacked Luke earlier. Luke jumps into the arena to protect Lists, briefly aided by convict ring girl Katrina Banks. Racial tensions escalate, sparking a riot as prisoners flood the arena and attempt to rape the female inmates. Katrina fights back, and the women are evacuated. Guards regain control, Luke surrenders, and afterward, he speaks privately with Katrina. Learning Luke is still alive, Markus places a $1 million bounty on his head.
Seeking greater profits, September launches a new event called "Death Race". Inmates can earn their freedom by winning five races over three days, driving heavily armed, reinforced cars. Female prisoners serve as navigators. Luke enters the race with Katrina as his navigator and Lists, Goldberg, and Rocco as his pit crew. Luke wins the first race and is congratulated by Weyland, who offers Katrina as his prize. Alone together, Luke and Katrina tease each other and have sex. Later, September places Luke in solitary confinement under the guise of protecting him from bounty hunters. Katrina is taken to Markus, who offers her freedom in exchange for killing Luke.
During the second race, nearly all competitors target Luke, except for triad member "14K", whom Luke previously saved. Katrina tells Luke about Markus's offer. Near the end of the race, Luke's car malfunctions due to sabotage. He ejects Katrina before the vehicle is struck by Big Bill's heat-seeking missile. Luke's pit crew and Katrina are unable to rescue him from the burning wreck. Meanwhile, Big Bill's navigator kills her partner after he murders his pit crew and attacks her.

title: Bloomington
overview: A former child actress attends college in search of independence and ends up becoming romantically involved with a female professor. Their relationship thrives until an opportunity to return to acting forces her to make life-altering decisions.
plot:
Bloomington is a 2010 independent coming-of-age drama written and directed by Fernanda Cardoso, filmed in Indianapolis, Indiana, and Los Angeles. It follows a former child actress who goes to college seeking independence and becomes romantically involved with a female professor, a relationship tested when the younger woman is offered a chance to return to acting.

Jackie Kirk, once the star of a television series, enrolls at a college in Bloomington, Indiana, where her classmates are in awe of her acting past and she tries to fit in as an ordinary student. At an on-campus mixer she meets Catherine Stark, a lesbian professor who has noticed her, and the two begin a secret affair that would cause a scandal if discovered. The relationship draws Jackie away from campus social life as the two women grow closer and help each other discover more about themselves.

When Jackie is suddenly offered the chance to return to acting, Catherine becomes uneasy, believing they would always have to hide what they are to each other. She pulls away, insisting they were never in a real relationship and that Jackie is not worth the risk, while Jackie argues that Catherine is. Jackie also clashes with her classmate Sandy, who resents her for competing for a scholarship she does not need and believes the affair has earned her special treatment. After Jackie slaps her, Sandy punches her in the face. The next day Jackie turns up at Catherine's door with a black eye, and Catherine hurries her inside as photographers take pictures. Learning that Catherine is going to a party with an unnamed date, Jackie insults her by suggesting she cannot support herself. When Catherine comes home with a man and takes him to her bedroom, Jackie leaves for a party with her own friends and flirts with a friend named Zach. After Jackie departs for Los Angeles to film a new movie based on her old series, the affair is partly exposed and Catherine loses her job. Months later the two spend one last night together and say a formal goodbye, and Jackie returns to California and her new role.

Allison McAtee plays Catherine and Sarah Stouffer plays Jackie, with Erika Heidewald as Sandy, Ray Zupp as Zach and Katherine Ann McGregor as Lillian. Reviews were mixed. AfterEllen called it a sexy, offbeat and fantastic little drama, while Autostraddle complained that its issues were left unresolved and that it lacked subtlety.

title: The Secret World of Arrietty
original_title: 借りぐらしのアリエッティ
tagline: Do not be seen by humans. That's been the law of children of the underfloor.
overview: 14-year-old Arrietty and the rest of the Clock family live in peaceful anonymity as they make their own home from items "borrowed" from the house's human inhabitants. However, life changes for the Clocks when a human boy discovers Arrietty.
plot:
The Secret World of Arrietty is a 2010 Japanese animated fantasy film directed by Hiromasa Yonebayashi, based on the novel "The Borrowers" by Mary Norton. The movie follows the story of an 11-year-old boy named Sho and his relationship with a young girl named Arrietty.

In post-war Japan, Sho lives in a small house with his father, who is a widower. One day, while exploring the attic, Sho discovers a tiny door that leads to a secret world inhabited by the Borrowers, a family of tiny people who live in the walls and floors of houses. The Borrowers are skilled at "borrowing" small items from humans, which they use to survive.

Arrietty, the protagonist, is the daughter of the Borrower family. She is curious and adventurous, but also kind and gentle. Sho befriends Arrietty, who borrows a spoon from him, and they begin to communicate through notes and drawings. As their friendship grows, Sho learns about the world of the Borrowers and their struggles to survive in a human-dominated society.

However, their friendship is threatened by the Borrower family's need to borrow more and more items from humans, which puts them at risk of being discovered. The Borrowers' leader, Pod Clock, is determined to find a way to live safely among humans, but his methods are often reckless and put the entire family in danger.

As Sho and Arrietty spend more time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their social differences make it difficult for them to express their emotions. Meanwhile, Sho's father is struggling to come to terms with his own grief and loneliness after the loss of his wife.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when the Borrower family is discovered by a human, who threatens to expose their secret world to the outside world. Arrietty must make a difficult decision to save her family and protect Sho's friendship, while also considering the consequences of revealing the existence of the Borrowers to humans.

In the end, Sho and Arrietty find a way to resolve their differences and come up with a plan to coexist peacefully. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Sho and Arrietty looking forward to a future where they can live together in harmony.

The Secret World of Arrietty is a beautifully animated film that explores themes of friendship, love, and acceptance. The movie's attention to detail and its imaginative world-building make it a delight to watch, while its thoughtful portrayal of complex emotions and relationships makes it a relatable and engaging story for audiences of all ages.

title: One Day
tagline: Twenty years. Two people.
overview: A romantic comedy centered on Dexter and Emma, who first meet during their graduation in 1988 and proceed to keep in touch regularly. The film follows what they do on July 15 annually, usually doing something together.
plot:
One Day is a 2011 romantic drama directed by Lone Scherfig, with a screenplay by David Nicholls adapted from his 2009 novel. It stars Anne Hathaway and Jim Sturgess as two friends whose relationship is traced through a single date, St. Swithin's Day, 15 July, over twenty years, with Patricia Clarkson, Ken Stott and Romola Garai in supporting roles.

Emma Morley, from a working-class northern family, and Dexter Mayhew, a privileged Winchester-educated southerner, spend a chaste night together after graduating from Edinburgh University in 1988 and agree to stay friends. Emma moves to London hoping to write but ends up waitressing in a Mexican restaurant, where she meets the would-be comedian Ian, while Dexter drifts abroad, teaching English in Paris. On a 1992 holiday in Dinard, Emma rebuffs him because he will not commit. Dexter becomes a brash late-night television host, arrives drunk to see his terminally ill mother, who tells him he is not yet a nice person, and grows increasingly obnoxious; Emma, now a teacher living unhappily with Ian, breaks with him in 1996 after a coke-fuelled dinner at which he mocks her profession, saying she loves but no longer likes him. By the late 1990s Dexter's career has collapsed and he is with Sylvie, while Emma leaves Ian, who nonetheless urges her to publish her stories. Reconciled at a friend's wedding in 2000, Emma has a book deal and Dexter is engaged to a pregnant Sylvie, who later cheats on him with his old friend Callum. In 2003 Dexter visits Emma, now a successful author in Paris; she chases after him, and they finally become a couple, marry and try for a child while he runs a café. In 2006 Emma is killed by a lorry while cycling. Dexter spirals, but is eventually steadied by his daughter Jasmine, his father, Sylvie and even Ian. In 2011 he climbs Arthur's Seat with Jasmine, and a flashback returns to the day after they first met in 1988.

Hathaway plays Emma and Sturgess plays Dexter, with Clarkson and Stott as his parents, Garai as Sylvie and Rafe Spall as Ian. A Random House Films and Focus Features production co-financed by Film4, it was shot from July 2010 in Edinburgh, London and Brittany. Focus released it in the US on 19 August 2011. Reviews were largely negative, at 36% on Rotten Tomatoes, though Roger Ebert praised its wit; Hathaway's Yorkshire accent drew particular criticism.

title: Trigun: Badlands Rumble
original_title: トライガン バッドランド ランブル
overview: In a quicksand surrounded town called Makka, rumors spread of a legendary robber named Gasback is after the town. To protect it, Mayor Kepler has hired bounty hunters. These hunters have been following Gasback from town to town in hopes of getting the bounty. Vash the Stampede is in town, along with Meryl and Milly, along with the female bounty hunter Amelia and Nicholas D. Wolfwood.
plot:
Trigun: Badlands Rumble is a 2010 Japanese animated science fiction action film directed by Satoshi Nishimura and produced by Madhouse, based on Yasuhiro Nightow's manga Trigun. It follows the gunman Vash the Stampede as he arrives in a city where bounty hunters have gathered to claim a huge reward on the robber Gasback. The film was Hiromi Tsuru's final performance as the insurance agent Meryl Stryfe before her death in 2017.

Twenty years before the story, Gasback's gang robs a bank and then betrays him; their leader, Cain, shoots him and leaves him for the police. Vash stops Gasback from killing his former partners, and Gasback escapes to continue his career of crime. In the present, Cain is mayor of Macca City, having used his loot to upgrade its power plant and erect a bronze statue of himself. He insures the statue with the Bernardelli Insurance Society, which sends Meryl and Milly Thompson to protect it, and the city fills with bounty hunters expecting Gasback to strike. Vash helps a young woman, Amelia, fend off thugs, but she scorns his flirting. Gasback, meanwhile, is guarded by Nicholas D. Wolfwood, who owes him his life but refuses to take part in his robberies, and he destroys the businesses of his other former accomplices.

When the bounty hunters give up and leave, Gasback fights his way into Cain's mansion. In the standoff, Cain shoots his old associates, and Amelia learns that Vash let Gasback escape two decades earlier. Vash lets Gasback go again, and the robber detaches the city's power plant and hauls it away, crushing Cain's statue. Pursuing Gasback to kill him, Amelia is followed by Vash, who is shot and vanishes into quicksand, but he survives thanks to a piece of tough smoked meat in his coat and is rescued by Meryl and Milly. In a final duel, Gasback unleashes an electrical weapon against Vash, and Amelia blocks it with a glove that he recognizes as one he made for his wife. Amelia is his daughter, born after he abandoned her mother, who died in poverty and shunned for her connection to him. Embracing Vash's ideals, Amelia spares her father. Gasback, his gang and his former accomplices are arrested, and the plant is restored to the city. Vash and Wolfwood set off across the desert after a new group of outlaws.

The film had its North American premiere at Sakura-Con in Seattle on April 2, 2010, and debuted at number fourteen on ten screens. Funimation later licensed it for English-language release.

title: Limitless
tagline: What if a pill could make you rich and powerful?
overview: A paranoia-fueled action thriller about an unsuccessful writer whose life is transformed by a top-secret "smart drug" that allows him to use 100% of his brain and become a perfect version of himself. His enhanced abilities soon attract shadowy forces that threaten his new life in this darkly comic and provocative film.
plot:
Limitless is a 2011 science fiction thriller film directed by Neil Burger and written by Luke Evans and Eric Warren Singer. The movie stars Bradley Cooper, Robert De Niro, and Abbie Cornish.

The story follows Eddie Morra (played by Bradley Cooper), a struggling writer who works as a janitor at a publishing company in New York City. One day, while cleaning up after a party, Eddie stumbles upon a mysterious pill that he finds on the floor. The pill is labeled "NZT-48" and is produced by the pharmaceutical company PerkinReidy.

Eddie takes the pill, which gives him an extraordinary boost of intelligence, memory, and cognitive abilities. He becomes incredibly intelligent, able to learn new information at an incredible rate, and his memory expands exponentially. Eddie's newfound abilities allow him to excel in his job as a writer, and he quickly becomes a successful author.

However, Eddie soon realizes that the pill has a dark side effect: it slowly kills him over time. As the days pass, Eddie's body begins to deteriorate, and he must find a way to reverse the effects of the NZT-48 before it's too late.

Eddie's newfound abilities also attract the attention of the pharmaceutical company PerkinReidy, which wants to exploit his brain for their own gain. The company's CEO, Carl Van Loon (played by Robert De Niro), will stop at nothing to get Eddie to work for them and help develop a new line of NZT-based products.

As Eddie navigates this treacherous world, he meets Sarah (played by Abbie Cornish), a beautiful and intelligent woman who becomes his love interest. Together, they try to uncover the truth about the NZT-48 pill and its effects on Eddie's body.

Throughout the movie, Eddie's character undergoes significant development as he struggles with the consequences of his newfound abilities. He must confront the darker aspects of his own personality and the moral implications of using a powerful substance like NZT-48 to enhance his cognitive abilities.

The movie builds towards a thrilling climax as Eddie and Sarah try to outsmart Van Loon and his henchmen, who will stop at nothing to get their hands on Eddie's brain. In the end, Eddie must make a choice between saving himself or using his abilities to help others.

Overall, Limitless is a gripping sci-fi thriller that explores themes of identity, morality, and the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to human cognition. The movie features impressive performances from its cast, particularly Bradley Cooper, who brings depth and nuance to Eddie's character.

title: Romantics Anonymous
overview: What happens when a man and a woman share a common passion? They fall in love. And this is what happens to Jean-René, the boss of a small chocolate factory, and Angélique, a gifted chocolate maker he has just hired. What occurs when a highly emotional man meets a highly emotional woman? They fall in love, and this is what occurs to Jean-René and Angélique who share the same handicap. But being pathologically timid does not make things easy for them. So whether they will manage to get together, join their solitudes and live happily ever after is a guessing matter.
plot: With his beloved chocolate business turning sour, socially awkward boss Jean-René decides to enlist an extra pair of hands. Enter Angélique, a chronically shy young woman who shares Jean- René's passion for all things sugar and sweet. She is the answer to his prayers, in ways he didn t realise. title: Ultramarines: A Warhammer 40,000 Movie
tagline: In the grim darkness of the far future there is only war.
overview: A squad of Ultramarines answer a distress call from an Imperial Shrine World. A full Company of Imperial Fists was stationed there, but there is no answer from them. The squad investigates to find out what has happened there.
plot:
The film opens with footage from the planet Mithron with a group of Space Marines of the Imperial Fists Chapter under attack from an unknown enemy. A Space Marine by the name of Nidon is told to protect "the Codex" and races to obey his orders, just before a fireball engulfs them all. Elsewhere, aboard a Space Marine Strike Cruiser, Brother Proteus and Captain Severus of the Ultramarines Chapter's 2nd Company spar in a training duel. Proteus manages to disarm Severus; however, he quickly escapes Proteus's grasp and in turn defeats him, proclaiming that a Space Marine never yields. Following this, Proteus and the other newly initiated members of the 2nd Company's Ultima Squad are then shown a sacred weapon in their ship's reclusium, a Relic Thunder Hammer. The Captain and his right-hand man, Apothecary Pythol, lead the initiates in a swearing-in ceremony on the Hammer. With the ceremony finished, Ultima Squad prepare themselves for their first mission as a squad—a sortie to the planet of Mithron.
In orbit above the planet, Captain Severus departs the cruiser with only Pythol and the ten-strong Ultima Squad as support, all of whom are highly eager to prove themselves in battle finally. En route to the planet's surface, Severus addresses the squad, informing them of the distress call received shortly before all contact with the planet was lost, and how it is still unclear whether it is automated or not. Soon enough, they arrive on the tough and unforgiving desert surface of Mithron, and head in the direction of the only location of importance on the planet: a shrine guarded by a full company of one hundred Marines from the Imperial Fists. En route to the shrine, Proteus senses something shadowing them and opens fire on it, but when the others fail to find any evidence of their supposed pursuer, they quickly dismiss his concerns as just nerves, something which Proteus denies. Soon afterward though, Ultima Squad discovers that a terrible battle has indeed taken place, with the garrison force annihilated and the planet's Imperial shrine desecrated. It is also evident that the forces of Chaos are responsible, and against Pythol's advice to retreat, Severus decides they must continue the mission to search for any remaining survivors.
While approaching the ruins, the Ultramarines are ambushed by the Black Legion. Three of the Ultramarines (squad leader Veteran Sergeant Crastor, Brother Lycos, and Brother Boreas) are killed, but the ambush is thwarted. The squad then continues on, and eventually makes it inside the shrine. While traveling through a dark passage, though, they are attacked by a Daemon Prince, which kills Brother Maxillius and grapples with Severus, causing them both to fall through a wall and down a ravine. With Severus gone and Crastor dead, command of the squad then falls to Proteus, who decides to continue with the mission.

title: Julia's Eyes
tagline: You can't hide in the dark
overview: The story of a woman who is slowly losing her sight whilst trying to investigate the mysterious death of her twin sister.
plot:
Julia's Eyes (Spanish: Los ojos de Julia) is a 2010 Spanish psychological horror thriller film directed by Guillem Morales and written by Morales and Oriol Paulo. Belén Rueda stars in the dual role of Julia and her twin sister, Sara, with Lluís Homar as Julia's husband, Isaac, Pablo Derqui, Joan Dalmau and Clara Segura. The film was produced by Guillermo del Toro, Joaquín Padró and Mar Targarona.

In the opening scene, Sara, a blind woman tormented by an unseen presence, prepares to hang herself in her basement but changes her mind; as she tries to remove the noose, the stool is kicked away from beneath her. Far away, Julia, who suffers from the same degenerative eye disease as her sister but can still see, collapses, sensing that something is wrong. Refusing to believe that Sara killed herself, particularly since she had been awaiting surgery that might restore her sight, Julia begins to investigate, despite the objections of Isaac, who has learned from a doctor that Sara's operation had failed.

Julia meets Sara's blind elderly neighbor, Soledad, who predicts that Isaac will leave her, just as Soledad's own son abandoned her after she lost her sight. Learning that Sara had a mysterious boyfriend, Julia follows the trail to a nearby hotel, where an elderly janitor warns her of people who live in the shadows and are so ignored that they become invisible. Soon after, Isaac vanishes, and Julia becomes convinced that the same unseen figure who stalked Sara has taken him, though the police are skeptical. As witnesses connected to the case begin to die, Julia's eyesight deteriorates rapidly under the stress, forcing her to undergo an operation of her own. Recovering with her eyes bandaged and dependent on a caregiver, she becomes increasingly vulnerable to the presence she has been hunting, and must uncover the identity of the invisible man before she loses her sight completely.

Julia's Eyes received mostly positive reviews, with 90 percent of 39 critics on Rotten Tomatoes giving it a favorable review; the consensus called it a smart, suspenseful and visually distinctive Spanish thriller. Philip French of The Guardian commented on its use of blindness as both a plot device and a metaphor, and critics praised Rueda's performance and Morales's stylish direction.

title: The Three Musketeers
tagline: Every legend has a new beginning.
overview: The hot-headed young D'Artagnan along with three former legendary but now down on their luck Musketeers must unite and defeat a beautiful double agent and her villainous employer from seizing the French throne and engulfing Europe in war.
plot:
The Three Musketeers is a 2011 period action-adventure film directed by Paul W. S. Anderson, a loose adaptation of Alexandre Dumas's 1844 novel adding fantastical airships. Logan Lerman stars as D'Artagnan, with Matthew Macfadyen, Ray Stevenson and Luke Evans as the musketeers Athos, Porthos and Aramis, Milla Jovovich as Milady de Winter, Mads Mikkelsen as Rochefort, Orlando Bloom as the Duke of Buckingham and Christoph Waltz as Cardinal Richelieu.

In Venice, the musketeers Athos, Porthos and Aramis, aided by Milady de Winter, steal Leonardo da Vinci's designs for a flying warship, only for Milady to betray them and sell the plans to the Duke of Buckingham. A year later, the young D'Artagnan leaves Gascony for Paris, hoping to become a musketeer like his father, only to find that the regiment has been disbanded. After a humiliating encounter with Rochefort, the captain of Cardinal Richelieu's guard, he unwittingly offends Athos, Porthos and Aramis and arranges to duel each of them, but when Richelieu's guards interrupt, the four fight side by side. Summoned before the young King Louis XIII, they are honored rather than punished.

Richelieu, scheming to seize power, has Milady plant forged love letters among the queen's possessions and steal her diamond necklace, taking it to London to suggest an affair with Buckingham. If the queen cannot wear the necklace at an upcoming ball, the king will be forced to execute her and go to war with England. Learning of the plot from the queen's lady-in-waiting, Constance the musketeers travel to London. There they outwit Milady and Buckingham, steal Buckingham's airship and recover the necklace, while Milady leaps from the ship rather than face execution.

On their return to France, they are attacked by Rochefort aboard a larger airship built from Milady's copies of the plans, and the battle ends with both vessels crashing onto Notre-Dame Cathedral, where D'Artagnan kills Rochefort in a duel. The necklace is returned to the queen in time for the ball, and the musketeers cover up the affair using Milady's written authorization from Richelieu, who vows revenge after they refuse to serve him. Meanwhile, Buckingham rescues Milady and advances on France with an armada of ships and airships.

The film received negative reviews, with critics faulting its writing and characters; Rotten Tomatoes reported 27% approval. It grossed $132 million worldwide against a production budget of $75 million.

title: The Other Woman
tagline: Love makes everything possible.
overview: Emilia, a law-school graduate, falls in love with her married boss, Jack. After Emilia marries Jack, her happiness turns unexpectedly to grief following the death of her infant daughter. Devastated, Emilia nonetheless carries on, attempting to forge a connection with her stepson William and to resist the interference of Jack's jealous ex-wife.
plot:
The Other Woman is an American drama written and directed by Don Roos, completed in 2009 and adapted from Ayelet Waldman's novel Love and Other Impossible Pursuits, the title under which it was released in the United Kingdom. Natalie Portman stars alongside Scott Cohen, Lisa Kudrow, Charlie Tahan and Lauren Ambrose, and the film was distributed in the United States by IFC Films.

Emilia is a young New York lawyer whose relationship with the married Jack ended his first marriage and led to their own. Her life has since been shattered by the death of their newborn daughter Isabel from what was recorded as sudden infant death syndrome. Emilia treats the loss as a punishment, believes she cannot have more children, and finds her marriage straining under her grief. She is regarded as a homewrecker by Jack's furious ex-wife Carolyn, who is now expecting another child herself.

Emilia also struggles with her precocious young stepson William, whose blunt remarks about Isabel wound her, including his observation that under Jewish law the baby had not lived long enough to count as a full person. Her clumsy attempts to bond with the boy backfire and lower her standing with both Carolyn and Jack. Eventually Emilia confesses the secret she has never told anyone: on the morning Isabel died, the baby had not been in her crib but asleep on Emilia's breast, and Emilia has been tormented by the belief that she smothered her daughter after falling asleep. She moves out, reconciles with her father, whose infidelity once hurt her mother, and returns to work with old friends at a Legal Aid office.

Carolyn unexpectedly asks to see her and admits she had told William that Emilia might have caused Isabel's death, adding that her son had rebuked her for it. She then tells Emilia that she has reviewed the autopsy report, which shows Emilia did not kill her child. Freed of her guilt, Emilia tells Jack the whole story, and a later crisis involving William brings them together again, with Jack asking her on a date. On the day Carolyn's baby is born, Emilia gives William a toy boat from her own childhood and tells him she loves him; after a moment he replies that he does too.

The film received mostly negative reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 37% approval; critics praised Portman and Kudrow but faulted Roos's direction.
