title: Johnny English Reborn
tagline: A little intelligence goes a long way
overview: The most prominent heads of state in the world begin gathering for a conference that could have a major impact on global politics. When MI-7 receives word that the Chinese premier has become the target of some high-powered killers, it falls on Johnny English to save the day. Armed with the latest high-tech weaponry and gadgets that would make even James Bond jealous, the once-disgraced agent uncovers evidence of a massive conspiracy involving some of the world's most powerful organisations, and vows to redeem his tarnished reputation by stopping the killers before they can strike.
plot:
Johnny English Reborn is a 2011 spy comedy film directed by Oliver Parker and starring Rowan Atkinson as the titular character, Johnny English.

The movie begins with Johnny English, a bumbling but lovable British spy, who has been retired from active duty due to his ineptitude. However, when a former KGB agent named Dominic (played by Ross Kemp) is released from prison after serving time for treason, Johnny is forced back into action to stop him.

As Johnny delves deeper into the world of espionage once again, he discovers that Dominic has stolen a deadly virus known as "The Phoenix," which can be used to create an army of mindless drones. The virus is being sold on the black market, and it's up to Johnny to track down the buyer and prevent a global catastrophe.

Along the way, Johnny teams up with his new partner, Nancy (played by Natalie Imbruglia), a tough and capable agent who is initially skeptical of Johnny's abilities. As they work together, they develop a romantic connection, which adds an extra layer of complexity to their mission.

As the plot thickens, Johnny and Nancy find themselves in a series of hilarious misadventures, from infiltrating a high-stakes poker game to escaping from a group of henchmen. Despite his best efforts, Johnny consistently manages to botch his missions, leading to plenty of comedic moments.

However, as the stakes grow higher, Johnny begins to prove himself to be more than just a bumbling spy. He uses his unique skills and resourcefulness to outwit his enemies and stay one step ahead of Dominic's henchmen.

In the end, Johnny and Nancy successfully stop Dominic from selling the Phoenix virus, but not before he escapes with it. In a thrilling finale, Johnny and Nancy track down Dominic to an abandoned warehouse, where they engage in a high-speed car chase through the streets of London.

As the dust settles, Johnny emerges victorious, having saved the world from certain destruction. The movie ends on a romantic note, with Johnny and Nancy sharing a kiss as the credits roll.

Throughout the film, Rowan Atkinson's signature physical comedy and wit shine through, making Johnny English Reborn a hilarious and entertaining ride. Despite its lighthearted tone, the movie also explores themes of redemption and self-discovery, as Johnny learns to come to terms with his own limitations and find success in his own unique way.

Overall, Johnny English Reborn is a fun and action-packed spy comedy that will keep you laughing from start to finish. With its witty dialogue, physical humor, and charming performances, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

title: Pride and Prejudice and Zombies
tagline: Bloody lovely.
overview: A zombie outbreak has fallen upon the land in this reimagining of Jane Austen's classic tale of the tangled relationships between lovers from different social classes in 19th century England. Feisty heroine Elizabeth Bennet is a master of martial arts and weaponry and the handsome Mr. Darcy is a fierce zombie killer, yet the epitome of upper class prejudice. As the zombie outbreak intensifies, they must swallow their pride and join forces on the blood-soaked battlefield in order to conquer the undead once and for all.
plot:
Pride and Prejudice and Zombies, stylized as Pride + Prejudice + Zombies, is a 2016 action comedy horror film based on Seth Grahame-Smith's 2009 novel of the same name, itself a parody of Jane Austen's 1813 classic Pride and Prejudice. Written and directed by Burr Steers, it stars Lily James as Elizabeth Bennet and Sam Riley as Mr. Darcy, with Jack Huston, Bella Heathcote, Douglas Booth, Matt Smith, Charles Dance and Lena Headey in supporting roles. The film follows the general outline of Austen's novel while adding a plague of the undead.

In an early nineteenth-century England overrun by zombies, the five Bennet sisters, Elizabeth, Jane, Kitty, Lydia and Mary, have been trained by their father in weaponry and Chinese martial arts so they can defend themselves, while their mother is chiefly concerned with marrying them off to wealthy men. At a country ball the Bennets meet newcomers including the amiable and rich Charles Bingley, who is immediately taken with Jane, and Colonel Darcy, an aloof but formidable zombie hunter trained in Japanese martial arts. When the undead attack the ball, the sisters fight them off, and Darcy is quietly impressed by Elizabeth's skill, though his outward coldness and contempt for Mrs. Bennet's mercenary ambitions offend her.

Elizabeth is drawn to the charming officer George Wickham, who tells her that Darcy cheated him out of his inheritance and who claims that some zombies can be kept civilized by feeding them pig brains. When Darcy proposes, Elizabeth rejects him, angered by his role in separating Jane from Bingley, and the two literally come to blows. A letter from Darcy later reveals Wickham's true character. After Wickham runs off with Lydia and London falls to the undead, Darcy discovers that Wickham has been building a zombie army in a bid to rule the country. In the ensuing battle Wickham is exposed as undead himself, and Darcy is wounded as the army destroys a bridge to stop the horde. Elizabeth admits her love, accepts his second proposal, and the couple share a double wedding with Jane and Bingley, before a mid-credits scene shows Wickham's army arriving.

The film spent years in development, passing through directors including David O. Russell, Mike White and Craig Gillespie, with Natalie Portman originally set to star before remaining only as a producer. Burr Steers took over in 2013. Released in February 2016, it received mixed reviews and was a box office disappointment.

title: Senna
tagline: No Fear. No Limits. No Equal.
overview: The remarkable story of Brazilian racing driver Ayrton Senna, charting his physical and spiritual achievements on the track and off, his quest for perfection, and the mythical status he has since attained, is the subject of Senna, a documentary feature that spans the racing legend's years as an F1 driver, from his opening season in 1984 to his untimely death a decade later.
plot:
Senna is a 2010 documentary directed by Asif Kapadia about the life and death of the Brazilian Formula One champion Ayrton Senna. It follows his career from his debut at the 1984 Brazilian Grand Prix to his fatal crash at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix, with particular emphasis on his rivalry with Alain Prost. It avoids narration and "talking head" interviews, using archival footage, voiceovers and Senna family home movies.

The film opens with footage of a young Senna racing go-karts, as he later recalls that in those days there was "no money, no politics – it was real racing." After brief early spells with Toleman and Lotus, Senna joins McLaren and becomes world champion. He clashes with his teammate Prost and with the sport's powerful regulator, Jean-Marie Balestre, and wins three titles in four years. The rivalry peaks in 1989 and 1990, when controversial collisions between the two decide the championship, and Senna blames Balestre's rulings for costing him the 1989 title. In 1991 he finally wins his home Grand Prix despite gearbox failure. A national icon, he champions driver safety and helps poor children in Brazil.

In 1992 and 1993, the computer-controlled cars of the rival Williams team dominate, and Senna watches Nigel Mansell and then Prost win the title. Prost, still resentful, blocks Senna from joining Williams. Senna takes Prost's seat for 1994 just as new rules ban the team's electronic aids. Williams struggles, and Senna suspects Benetton, whose Michael Schumacher wins the opening races, of cheating. The San Marino Grand Prix weekend brings crash after crash: Rubens Barrichello is badly hurt on Friday, Roland Ratzenberger is killed on Saturday, and two cars collide on race day. Shortly afterward, Senna crashes fatally after a mechanical failure. The film ends with his funeral and notes that no Formula One driver had died since, and that his family founded the Instituto Ayrton Senna to continue his charitable work.

After a screening at the 2010 Japanese Grand Prix, it premiered in São Paulo. It opened in Brazil in November 2010 and in the United Kingdom in June 2011. Rotten Tomatoes reported 93% approval, promising thrills and heartbreak even for non-fans. Empire called it deeply compelling, and The New York Times praised its editing while noting that viewers unfamiliar with the sport might find some episodes confusing. At the BAFTA Awards it won Best Documentary and Best Editing and was nominated for Outstanding British Film.

title: 10 Years
tagline: Who Got Fat? Who Didn't Change? Who Got Rich? Who Got Hot?
overview: A group of friends reunite ten years after their high-school graduation.
plot:
10 Years is a 2011 American independent romantic comedy film written and directed by Jamie Linden in his directorial debut. Set over a single night at a ten-year high school reunion, it features an ensemble cast including Channing Tatum, Jenna Dewan, Justin Long, Kate Mara, Rosario Dawson, Oscar Isaac, Chris Pratt, Aubrey Plaza and Anthony Mackie.

On the day of the reunion, Jake and his girlfriend, Jess, arrive at the home of his old friends Cully and Sam, now married. Others gather, including best friends Marty and AJ, the famous musician Reeves, and the adventurous Scott with his wife, Suki, and at the reunion they meet up with Garrity, his wife, Olivia, and his best friend, Andre. Elise, a reclusive classmate, arrives alone and is ignored by the organizer, former prom queen Anna. Jake shows his friends an engagement ring he has long meant to give Jess, but he is thrown when he meets his high school sweetheart, Mary, and her husband, Paul. Reeves reminisces with Elise after spotting an old photo of her in bright yellow shoes. Cully drunkenly attempts to apologize to classmates he bullied, and Marty and AJ compete for Anna. Jake and Mary recall the prom they never attended because her father had a heart attack that night.

The group moves on to a karaoke bar. Noticing Jake's behavior around Mary, Jess returns to the hotel, as does Paul. Pressured by his friends, Reeves sings his hit song "Never Had", and the line about yellow shoes tells Elise that it is about her; they kiss and spend the night together. Catching Marty and AJ toilet-papering her house, Anna reveals that she is an unhappy single mother of two, and the men admit their own failures: Marty is broke and AJ is divorcing. Cully's drunkenness upsets Sam, and Scott announces that he and Suki are returning to Japan. Mary asks Jake for the dance they missed at prom, giving them closure; she reveals that she is pregnant, and both agree they are happy with their lives. Back at the hotel, Jess tells Jake she left so that he could make his peace with Mary, and as they join their friends at a diner, Jake retrieves the ring from his car.

Shot around Albuquerque, the film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2011 but received only a limited theatrical release on September 14, 2012, grossing under $1 million. Reviews were mixed to positive, with 60% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 67; critics called it sweet and well cast but predictable.

title: Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows

tagline: The game is afoot.
overview: There is a new criminal mastermind at large (Professor Moriarty) and not only is he Holmes’ intellectual equal, but his capacity for evil and lack of conscience may give him an advantage over the  detective.
plot:
Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows is a 2011 action mystery film directed by Guy Ritchie, starring Robert Downey Jr. as Sherlock Holmes and Jude Law as Dr. John Watson.

The movie begins with Sherlock Holmes (Robert Downey Jr.) and Dr. John Watson (Jude Law) living in London, England, in the year 1891. The story starts with a mysterious woman named Irene Adler (Rachel McAdams), who is revealed to be a former adversary of Holmes'. She has been presumed dead for years but returns, seeking revenge against Holmes.

Meanwhile, a series of murders takes place across Europe, all connected to a mysterious figure known as the "Severing Hand". The victims are all members of a secret society called the "Thaddeus Wadja" or "The Thaddeus Society", which is dedicated to the study and practice of alchemy.

As Holmes delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the murders are linked to an ancient text known as the "Severing Hand's" manifesto. The text reveals a plan to unleash a deadly poison on London, which would kill millions of people.

Holmes and Watson team up with Irene Adler, who has her own reasons for wanting to stop the Severing Hand. Together, they embark on a thrilling adventure across Europe, following a trail of clues that lead them from Paris to Vienna.

As the story unfolds, Holmes' mental health is put to the test when he begins to experience hallucinations and paranoia. He becomes convinced that his arch-nemesis, Professor Moriarty (Jared Harris), has returned and is behind the murders.

The climax of the movie takes place in a train station in Paris, where Holmes and Watson confront the Severing Hand. In a thrilling showdown, Holmes uses his exceptional detective skills to outwit the villain and prevent the poison from being released.

In the end, Holmes and Irene Adler share a moment of mutual respect and admiration for each other's intellects. The movie concludes with Holmes returning to London, where he is greeted as a hero by the public.

Throughout the movie, Robert Downey Jr.'s portrayal of Sherlock Holmes is on full display, showcasing his wit, intelligence, and eccentricities. Jude Law's performance as Dr. Watson provides a perfect foil to Holmes' antics, while Rachel McAdams brings a sense of sophistication and danger to her character, Irene Adler.

Overall, Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows is an entertaining and action-packed adventure that stays true to the spirit of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's original stories.

Snow White and the Huntsman is a 2012 American dark fantasy film directed by Rupert Sanders and produced by Universal Pictures. The movie is based on the classic fairy tale "Snow White" but with significant changes to its storyline, characters, and tone.

The story begins in medieval Europe, where Queen Ravenna (Charlize Theron) has stolen the magical mirror that allows her to maintain her youth and beauty. She uses the mirror's power to control the kingdom and rule with an iron fist. When the mirror reveals that Snow White (Kristen Stewart), a beautiful princess, is the fairest of them all, Ravenna becomes obsessed with killing Snow White.

Meanwhile, in a small village on the outskirts of the kingdom, a huntsman named Gary (Chris Hemsworth) is tasked by King Magnus (Nick Frost) to take Snow White into the forest and kill her. However, when Gary discovers that Snow White is innocent and kind-hearted, he decides to spare her life and sets her free in the forest.

Snow White soon finds herself facing numerous challenges as she tries to survive in the harsh wilderness. She befriends a group of dwarfs, including Doc (Bob Clark), Grumpy (Ray Stevenson), Happy (Nick Frost), Sleepy (Sam Spruell), Bashful (Lee Homsworth), Sneezy (Jack Davenport), and Dopey (Jonathan Sells). Together, they form a tight-knit community that helps Snow White to heal from her past traumas.

As the story unfolds, Ravenna becomes increasingly desperate to kill Snow White, and she orders her huntsman, William (Sam Claflin), to bring back Snow White's heart. However, William is torn between his loyalty to the queen and his growing feelings for Snow White. In a dramatic twist, William ultimately betrays Ravenna and helps Snow White to escape.

The movie takes a dark turn as Snow White and her dwarfs discover that they are being hunted by Ravenna's army of woodland creatures, including wolves, bears, and other mythical beasts. The group must fight for their lives in a desperate bid to reach the safety of the kingdom.

In the climactic final battle, Snow White and her allies face off against Ravenna and her minions. In a shocking turn of events, William sacrifices himself to save Snow White, and she ultimately kills Ravenna with the queen's own magic mirror.

The movie ends with Snow White being crowned the new queen of the kingdom, and she rules with kindness, wisdom, and justice. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that Snow White has finally found her true home and happiness.

Overall, Snow White and the Huntsman is a dark and action-packed retelling of the classic fairy tale. The movie features stunning visuals, impressive stunts, and a strong performance from Kristen Stewart as the titular character. While it deviates significantly from the original story, the film remains faithful to its core themes of beauty, kindness, and the struggle for power.

title: 13 Assassins
tagline: Take up your sword.
overview: A bravado period action film set at the end of Japan's feudal era in which a group of unemployed samurai are enlisted to bring down a sadistic lord and prevent him from ascending to the throne and plunging the country into a war-torn future.
plot:
13 Assassins (Jūsannin no Shikaku) is a 2010 Japanese samurai film directed by Takashi Miike, a remake of Eiichi Kudo's 1963 period drama of the same name. Koji Yakusho leads the cast as the veteran samurai Shimada Shinzaemon, with Takayuki Yamada, Yusuke Iseya, Hiroki Matsukata, Mikijirō Hira and Gorō Inagaki as the depraved Lord Naritsugu.

In 1844, late in the Edo period, the Tokugawa shogunate is weakening. Lord Matsudaira Naritsugu of Akashi rapes, tortures and kills nobles and commoners at will, shielded by his half-brother, the Shōgun. When Naritsugu is slated for a seat on the shogunate council, the justice minister Sir Doi Toshitsura fears his elevation will plunge the country into civil war, and after a lord whose family Naritsugu murdered commits seppuku in protest, Doi secretly engages Shinzaemon to kill him. Shinzaemon assembles a band of samurai, including his wayward nephew Shinrokurō and a rōnin, while Naritsugu's loyal retainer Hanbei, an old acquaintance of Shinzaemon, discovers the plot.

The conspirators plan an ambush at the town of Ochiai on Naritsugu's journey home from Edo. Attacked by hired rōnin along the way, they take to the mountains, get lost and free a hunter, Kiga Koyata, who leads them to Ochiai and becomes the thirteenth assassin. Lord Makino, whose son Naritsugu killed, blocks the highway to force a detour, then takes his own life to hide his role. With Doi's money, the assassins buy the town and turn it into a maze of traps and fortifications. Naritsugu arrives with some 200 men, far more than expected, and a long, savage battle ensues as the assassins fight with arrows, explosives and swords while Naritsugu revels in the slaughter. Most of the thirteen die. Shinzaemon kills Hanbei in a duel, and he and Naritsugu mortally wound each other; the terrified lord thanks him for the most exciting day of his life before Shinzaemon beheads him and dies. Shinrokurō and the seemingly indestructible Koyata survive and go their separate ways. An epilogue records that the death was blamed on illness and that the shogunate fell 23 years later.

The film competed for the Golden Lion at the 67th Venice International Film Festival in September 2010. Made for about $6 million, it grossed $17.6 million worldwide. Critics praised its 45-minute final battle, giving it 95% on Rotten Tomatoes and 84 on Metacritic; Roger Ebert called it terrifically entertaining. It won four Japan Academy Prizes.

title: Tower Heist
tagline: Ordinary guys. An extraordinary robbery.
overview: A luxury condo manager leads a staff of workers to seek payback on the Wall Street swindler who defrauded them. With only days until the billionaire gets away with the perfect crime, the unlikely crew of amateur thieves enlists the help of petty crook Slide to steal the $20 million they’re sure is hidden in the penthouse.
plot:
Josh Kovaks is the building manager of The Tower, an upscale apartment complex in New York City that has Wall Street billionaire Arthur Shaw as its penthouse tenant. Josh, a friend of Shaw's, has asked him to manage the staff's pensions. One day, Shaw is placed under house arrest by the FBI for masterminding a Ponzi scheme, embezzling up to $2 billion. Realizing they will lose their pensions, the staff members are distraught and the doorman Lester even attempts suicide. Josh, his brother-in-law and The Tower's concierge Charlie, and elevator operator Enrique are fired by general manager Mr. Simon after angrily confronting Shaw for his scheme.
Claire Denham, the FBI agent in charge of Shaw's case, drunkenly suggests to Josh that Shaw has concealed $20 million as a reserve, and that he should steal it. Josh gets Charlie, Enrique, and evicted Tower tenant Mr. Fitzhugh to help him steal the money.
They supplement their inexperience by enlisting Josh's childhood friend Slide, a petty criminal, and The Tower's maid Odessa, who has locksmith experience. Denham informs Josh that Shaw is scheduled to attend court on Thanksgiving during the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to avoid publicity, which Josh and his team orchestrated with a supposed call from the judge's clerk, so their plan to break into Shaw's apartment then is confirmed. Prior to this, Charlie is rehired as The Tower's new building manager. Uncomfortable with the plan, Charlie warns Josh to abandon it or Charlie will turn him over to the police.
Slide attempts to betray the team by reaching the safe ahead of them and taking all of the money for himself, having tricked Odessa into giving him lessons. The team intercepts him at Shaw's apartment and breaks down a false wall, revealing Shaw's safe, which turns out to be empty. During the ensuing altercation, the group find gold underneath the paint of a Ferrari 250 GT Lusso which Shaw has displayed in his apartment, realizing that he invested his money in gold, turned it into car parts, and reassembled the car inside the apartment to hide the money in plain sight. Fitzhugh estimates the car's value at $45 million. They then decide to lower it to Fitzhugh's old apartment using a window-washing platform. Charlie rejoins the team after realizing their presence and saves Fitzhugh from falling to his death. They push the car on top of one of the elevators, and Josh finds a ledger of Shaw's illegal finances in the car's glove box, detailing the latter's long history of fraud.
Shaw and the FBI return, realizing the Thanksgiving Day court date to be part of Josh's plan. Denham notes the missing car and Shaw's hidden safe, and forfeits Shaw's $10 million bail, remanding him into federal custody until his real court date for not informing the FBI of the safe even if it was empty. The FBI arrests Josh's conspirators (except Slide, who somehow manages to slip away) while Denham catches up to Josh in Central Park.

title: The Prey
overview: A robber escapes from prison with a single objective in mind: to track down his former cellmate, a serial killer who intends to pin his crimes on him. A cop is sent after the robber who, despite his best efforts, soon becomes Public Enemy Number One. As the protagonists are driven to their limits, it becomes increasingly unclear who is the hunter and who is the prey.
plot:
The Prey (French: La proie) is a 2011 French action thriller directed by Éric Valette and written by Laurent Turner and Luc Bossi. Albert Dupontel stars as Franck Adrien, a bank robber who escapes from prison, with Alice Taglioni as Claire Linné, the determined police officer who hunts him, Stéphane Debac as the serial killer Jean-Louis Maurel, Natacha Régnier and Sergi López. It was released in France in April 2011.

After a successful robbery, Franck Adrien and his accomplice are caught and sent to prison. Adrien alone knows where the loot is hidden, and he refuses to reveal its location even to his wife or his partner. Despite an initially distant relationship, he comes to trust his cellmate, Jean-Louis Maurel, a timid man accused of rape, and saves him from a savage beating by a gang of Russian prisoners. When Adrien's former partner has him beaten and sent to the prison infirmary, Maurel visits him. About to be released early after his alleged victim withdraws her accusation, Maurel offers to deliver a message to Adrien's wife, Anna, and Adrien, though still wary, gives him a clue to the location of the money.

Adrien's peace of mind is shattered when Manuel Carrega, an officer of the National Gendarmerie, visits him and tells him that Maurel is in fact a serial killer and rapist. Fearing for the safety of his wife and young daughter, Adrien fights off the Russian inmates and a corrupt guard who ambush him and escapes from prison disguised in the guard's uniform. As he tries to reach his family, he is confronted by Claire Linné, a rising police star assigned to recapture him. Betting that she will not shoot an unarmed man, he slips away and begins a desperate pursuit of Maurel across France, while Maurel cleverly frames Adrien for his own crimes, turning him into the most wanted man in the country. Hunted by the police and racing against time, Adrien must track down the killer and rescue his daughter before it is too late.

The Prey received generally positive reviews, holding a 70 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 58. Xan Brooks of The Guardian found it derivative of The Fugitive, Se7en and Tell No One, while Manohla Dargis of The New York Times called it ridiculously diverting and praised its relentless pace and Dupontel's physical performance.

title: The Powerpuff Girls Movie
tagline: Saving the world before bedtime!
overview: Based on the hit animated television series, this feature film adaptation tells the story of how Blossom, Bubbles and Buttercup - three exuberant young girls - obtain their unique powers, become superheroes and join forces to foil evil mutant monkey Mojo Jojo's plan to take over the world.
plot:
In the crime- and injustice-riddled city of Townsville, Professor Utonium mixes sugar, spice and everything nice, hoping to produce the "perfect little girls" to improve Townsville. However, Jojo, the professor's pet chimpanzee and destructive laboratory assistant, breaks a flask of Chemical X, which spills onto the concoction. The experiment succeeds, producing three little girls whom the Professor names Blossom, Bubbles, and Buttercup. He also discovers that the girls have gained superpowers from the added Chemical X. Despite the girls' recklessness with their powers, they all immediately grow to love each other as a family.
On their first day of school, the girls learn about the game of tag and begin to play it among themselves, which quickly grows destructive once they use their powers. The girls take their game downtown, where they cause extensive damage to the city until the Professor calms them down. That night, the Professor tells the girls to not use their powers in public anymore. The next day, the citizens of Townsville treat the girls as outcasts due to their destructive behavior. The Professor is arrested and jailed as responsible for the incident, which forces the girls to try to make their way home from school on foot. After a while, they become lost in an alleyway, where the Gangreen Gang corners them. Suddenly, Jojo – now superintelligent after the Chemical X explosion mutated his brain – rescues the trio.
Seeking revenge at the Professor for favoring the girls instead of him, Jojo gains their sympathy by convincing them that he is also hated for his powers and tricks them into helping him build a laboratory and a machine powered by Chemical X, which he claims will "improve the city". Afterward, Jojo rewards them with a trip to the local zoo, where he secretly implants small transportation devices on all the primates there. That night, Jojo teleports the primates to his lab and uses his new machine to inject them with Chemical X, which turns them into evil mutants like himself. The next morning, after the Professor is released from prison, the girls show him all the "good" they have done, only to discover that the primates are attacking the city. Jojo, renaming himself as Mojo Jojo, publicly announces the girls assisted him, which damages their reputation further and makes the Professor completely heartbroken beyond his criminal conviction. Dejected, the girls exile themselves on an asteroid in outer space.
Mojo announces his intention to rule the planet but becomes angry when his minions disobey him and concoct their own plans to terrorize Townsville. Meanwhile, on the asteroid, the banished girls hear Mojo trying to strangle the Professor and return to Earth, where they start rescuing the citizens. After Buttercup uses her powers to defeat a giant ape, Blossom convinces the former and Bubbles that they can use their powers to fight back.

title: Midnight in Paris
tagline: Anything can happen in the city of light.
overview: A romantic comedy about a family traveling to the French capital for business. The party includes a young engaged couple forced to confront the illusion that a life different from their own is better.
plot:
Midnight in Paris is a 2011 romantic comedy film written and directed by Woody Allen. The movie stars Owen Wilson, Rachel McAdams, and Adrien Brody.

The story begins with Gil Pender (Owen Wilson), an American writer who has just moved to Paris with his fiancée Inez (Rachel McAdams). However, their relationship is strained due to Inez's disinterest in art and literature. One evening, while exploring the city, Gil stumbles upon a mysterious train that takes him back in time to the 1920s.

In this new era, Gil meets famous artists and writers such as F. Scott Fitzgerald (Tom Hiddleston), Ernest Hemingway (Adrien Brody), and Gertrude Stein (Kathy Bates). He also encounters his idol, Pablo Picasso (Marcial Di Fonzo Bo). As the night progresses, Gil becomes fast friends with these literary giants and experiences a magical world of art, literature, and music.

Gil's adventures in 1920s Paris are filled with excitement and romance. He falls for Adriana (Marion Cotillard), a beautiful and charming woman who is also an artist. However, their love is complicated by the fact that Adriana is already engaged to a wealthy man named Salvador Dali (Jordi Mollà).

As the night wears on, Gil finds himself torn between his life in the present and his experiences in the past. He must decide whether to return to his fiancée Inez or stay with Adriana in the 1920s.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Salvador Dali's true nature is revealed, and Gil realizes that he has been living in a fantasy world. The film then shifts back to the present, where Gil returns to Paris and reunites with Inez. However, their relationship has changed due to Gil's experiences in the past.

In the end, Gil must choose between his love for Inez and his connection with Adriana. He decides to stay with Inez, but not before realizing that he has been given a rare gift – the chance to experience the magic of Paris at midnight.

Midnight in Paris is a film about the power of art and literature to transform our lives. It explores themes of love, loss, and the human condition, all set against the backdrop of one of the most romantic cities in the world. The movie features stunning visuals, witty dialogue, and memorable performances from its cast.

title: Beautiful Boy
tagline: To confront the truth, first they had to face each other.
overview: A married couple on the verge of separation are leveled by the news their 18-year-old son committed a mass-shooting at his college, then took his own life.
plot:
Beautiful Boy is a 2010 American drama directed by Shawn Ku, who wrote it with Michael Armbruster. Michael Sheen and Maria Bello play Bill and Kate Carroll, a married couple whose lives fall apart when their eighteen-year-old son Sam, played by Kyle Gallner, dies in a shooting at his school and is revealed to be the gunman. Alan Tudyk, Moon Bloodgood, Austin Nichols and Meat Loaf appear in supporting roles.

Bill, a businessman, and Kate, a proofreader, have drifted into a cold and distant marriage held together mainly by their son, who is having a hard time at college. One morning the news reports a shooting spree on Sam's campus, and police arrive to tell the couple that Sam is dead and that he was responsible. Kate refuses to believe it and obsessively restores his searched bedroom. Besieged by reporters, the couple take refuge with Kate's brother Eric and his wife Trish, whose son Dylan has seen a video message Sam left about the massacre. Bill reads a statement asking for privacy, and Sam is buried at a small family funeral.

Tensions rise in the crowded house as Trish resents Kate's controlling behaviour toward Dylan, and Bill and Kate move to a motel, where they briefly find a moment of closeness. Returning home, Bill surprises a teenage intruder going through Sam's belongings and cuts his hand in the struggle. On the family laptop the couple find a short video in which Sam apologises and asks them not to hate him.

Grief turns into blame. Bill suggests Kate's constant criticism fuelled their son's anger, Kate accuses Bill of putting work before his family, and in a bitter argument Bill says he wishes Sam had never been born. Kate returns to the house alone, where a young co-worker she invites in turns out to be researching Sam for an article, and she throws him out. Bill tries to go back to work, but after confronting staring colleagues he quits. At Sam's grave he finds the word "killer" scrawled on the headstone and breaks down trying to scrub it off.

Called by the motel manager, Kate finds Bill despondent and takes him home, where they face their loss together as Sam's voice is heard finishing a story about lives changed forever.

The lead performances were widely praised, though critics faulted the storytelling, and the film won the FIPRESCI prize for the Discovery programme at the 2010 Toronto International Film Festival.

title: Warrior
tagline: Family is worth fighting for.
overview: The youngest son of an alcoholic former boxer returns home, where he's trained by his father for competition in a mixed martial arts tournament – a path that puts the fighter on a collision course with his estranged, older brother.
plot:
Warrior is a 2011 American sports drama film directed by Gavin O'Connor and written by Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa. The movie stars Tom Hardy, Joel Edgerton, and Nick Searcy.

The story begins with Tommy Riordan (Tom Hardy), a former Marine who returns to his hometown of Pittsburgh after serving in Iraq. Tommy's life is marked by tragedy: his father, Paddy (Nick Nolte), was a boxer who abandoned the family when Tommy was young, and his brother, Brendan (Joel Edgerton), has become a successful lawyer.

Tommy's mother, Bonnie (Charlize Theron), tries to keep the family together, but her efforts are met with resistance from Paddy. The tension between the two brothers comes to a head when Paddy dies, leaving behind a will that stipulates Tommy must train for and win a boxing match against Brendan in order to inherit his father's share of the family's boxing gym.

Tommy is initially hesitant to take on the challenge, but eventually decides to pursue his dream of becoming a boxer. He begins training with a grizzled old trainer, Mickey (Ron Perlman), who helps him prepare for the big fight against Brendan.

As Tommy trains, he also starts to reconnect with his brother and mother, and begins to understand the complexities of their family dynamics. Through his boxing journey, Tommy learns valuable lessons about perseverance, redemption, and the importance of family.

The movie's climax features a thrilling boxing match between Tommy and Brendan, which ends in a stunning upset victory for Tommy. The film concludes with Tommy finally finding closure and acceptance from his family, and beginning to forge a new path forward in life.

Throughout the movie, the director uses vivid imagery and powerful performances to bring the characters to life. Tom Hardy delivers a standout performance as Tommy Riordan, capturing the character's raw emotion, vulnerability, and determination. The supporting cast, including Joel Edgerton and Nick Nolte, also deliver memorable performances that add depth and complexity to the story.

Overall, Warrior is a powerful and moving drama that explores themes of family, redemption, and perseverance. With its strong performances, gripping storyline, and vivid cinematography, the movie is a must-see for fans of sports dramas and character-driven stories.

title: Womb
tagline: What are the consequences of giving birth to your dead boyfriend?
overview: A woman's consuming love forces her to bear the clone of her dead beloved. From his infancy to manhood, she faces the unavoidable complexities of her controversial decision.
plot:
The film begins on a beach during a foggy day. A woman (Eva Green) is thinking while she is having tea on the porch of her house. She is in an advanced state of pregnancy. She knows that the father of her child will not return, but she thinks that perhaps her unborn child was the only thing she needed from him. She smiles sinisterly and begins to reminisce about the events leading up to that moment.
A love story is then told between two children, Rebecca and Tommy, who swear each other eternal love. When Rebecca departs suddenly for Japan with her mother, the two are separated. Twelve years later, Rebecca returns as a young woman to find that Tommy (Matt Smith) not only remembers her, but still cares deeply for her. The two begin a new relationship.
Tommy is a political activist fighting against the biotech corporations, who plan to open a new natural park populated by animals artificially created by cloning. Tommy plans to spoil the inauguration ceremony by letting loose rucksacks filled with cockroaches. Rebecca, herself a computer programmer of leak detection sonar software for underground storage containers, insists on accompanying Tommy.
Driving to the site of the new natural park through a lonely wilderness, Rebecca asks Tommy to stop the car so that she can relieve herself at the side of the road. Meanwhile, Tommy leaves the car and is struck and killed suddenly by a passing vehicle.
Rebecca and Tommy's parents are stricken with grief. Rebecca wants to use new scientific advancements to have Tommy cloned because she can’t live without him, and wants to have his child. She offers to be impregnated using Tommy's DNA. Though Tommy's mother objects, his father agrees to give Rebecca Tommy's cell material, but urges her to think through her decision carefully before proceeding. Rebecca continues and conceives Tommy's clone in her womb. She visits original Tommy's grave while pregnant with his clone before giving birth by Caesarean section.
Tommy is now raised by Rebecca as a son, and the two are close. Tommy and his playmates observe a neighbourhood girl, described as a clone, and the children try to determine if she has a "copy smell." The neighbourhood mothers display prejudice against "copies," expecting Rebecca to forbid Tommy from associating with them. Rebecca, though upset, agrees in order not to isolate her son. Eventually rumours about Tommy spread, and Tommy is forced to celebrate his birthday alone with his mother, his playmates all being barred from attending by their mothers.
Rebecca moves to a more remote location with Tommy. Rebecca presents to him a pleo. Tommy begins to ask questions about his father, wanting to know how his father died. He buries the pleo his mother gave him for his birthday while out playing with a friend. His mother finds out and gives him back the pleo, which no longer works.
Years later, Tommy is a young adult, still living with Rebecca. Tommy has become more and more similar to the original Tommy.

title: Cave of Forgotten Dreams
tagline: Humanity's Lost Masterpiece... in 3D
overview: Werner Herzog gains exclusive access to film inside the Chauvet caves of Southern France, capturing the oldest known pictorial creations of humankind in their astonishing natural setting.
plot:
Cave of Forgotten Dreams is a 2010 3D documentary written, directed and narrated by Werner Herzog about the Chauvet Cave in the Ardèche region of southern France, whose walls hold some of the oldest human-made images yet discovered, created more than 30,000 years ago. Herzog's interest was sparked by Judith Thurman's 2008 New Yorker article "First Impressions", and Thurman became one of the film's co-producers. The project was sponsored by the French Ministry of Culture and partly financed by the History channel.

Discovered in 1994, the cave had been sealed for millennia by a rockfall at its entrance, preserving some 420 painted or engraved animal figures, as well as hand prints, animal bones and glittering mineral formations. The film moves slowly through the chambers, letting the camera dwell on the drawings while Herzog muses on what they reveal about the people who made them and about the origins of human imagination. Between these passages he interviews scientists and specialists connected with the site, among them Jean Clottes, Dominique Baffier and Jean-Michel Geneste, along with researchers such as Carole Fritz, Gilles Tosello, Julien Monney and Nicholas J. Conard. The film also visits the nearby Pont d'Arc natural bridge and the nuclear power station at Cruas, and ends with a dedication to Roger Ebert.

Access to Chauvet is tightly restricted. Herzog obtained special permission for six shooting days of four hours each, working with a crew of three, cinematographer Peter Zeitlinger, a sound recordist and an assistant, while lighting the scenes himself with cool, battery-powered lamps. The team had to stay on a narrow metal walkway, wear protective suits and limit their time inside because of high levels of carbon dioxide and radon. Initially sceptical of 3D, Herzog adopted it after visiting the cave, to capture how the painters used the bulges and contours of the rock. The score is by Ernst Reijseger.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2010, and IFC Films acquired U.S. rights days later. Released in 2011, it became the year's highest-grossing independently released documentary in the United States. Critics acclaimed it, with a 96% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 86, and it won best documentary awards from groups including the Los Angeles Film Critics Association and the National Society of Film Critics.

title: Attack the Block
tagline: Inner City vs. Outer Space
overview: A teen gang in a South London housing estate must team up with the other residents to protect their neighbourhood from a terrifying alien invasion.
plot:
On Guy Fawkes Night, trainee nurse Samantha Adams is mugged by a gang of teenage hoodlums from South London: Pest, Dennis, Jerome, Biggz, and leader Moses. When a meteorite falls from the sky into a nearby car, Samantha escapes. As Moses searches the wreck of the car for valuables, his face is scratched by a dog-sized alien creature. The creature runs away, but the gang chase and kill it. Hoping to gain fame and fortune, they take the dead animal to their acquaintance, cannabis dealer Ron and his boss Hi-Hatz, a local gang leader, who instead recruits Moses to work for him.
More objects fall from the sky. The gang arm themselves and go after them; however, these aliens are much larger and more threatening. After one kills Dennis's pitbull Pogo, the gang flee but are intercepted by two police officers accompanying Samantha, and Moses is arrested. The aliens kill the officers, and Samantha and Moses escape. A henchman of local drug lord Hi-Hatz is killed by aliens. The gang flee, and Biggz hides in a recycling bin, though he is saved by a pair of their young neighbours who kill the alien. An alien bursts into Samantha's flat, and Moses kills it with a samurai sword, so she joins them.
The gang move upstairs to the flat where Tia, Dimples, Dionna, and Gloria live, but two aliens attack from outside, smashing through the windows and decapitating Dennis. Samantha kills an alien, saving Moses, while Tia and Dimples kill the other one. The girls believe the boys to be the focus of the creatures and kick them out of the flat. Hi-Hatz and two more henchmen arrive to attack the gang but are attacked by aliens; only Hi-Hatz makes it out alive.
The gang run into more aliens but use fireworks as a distraction. Jerome becomes disorientated in the smoke and is killed by an alien. Entering Ron's flat, they find Hi-Hatz, who prepares to shoot Moses but is attacked and killed by the rest of the aliens, who break in through the window. The group flee and are joined by Brewis, one of Ron's customers and a zoology student. Moses, Pest, and Samantha retreat into the weed room, while Ron hides in the flat.
In the weed room, Brewis notices a luminescent stain on Moses's jacket under the ultraviolet light. title: 2012: Ice Age
tagline: A World Frozen Over ... A Family Torn Apart.
overview: A volcanic eruption in Iceland sends a glacier towards North America, causing everything in it's path to freeze. A family man struggles to escape the onslaught of the coming ice age.
plot:
2012: Ice Age is a 2011 American science fiction disaster film directed by Travis Fort and written by Paul Sinor and Victoria Dadi. Produced by David Michael Latt for The Asylum, the independent studio known for low-budget "mockbusters", it is the third and final installment of the company's 2012 trilogy, following 2012: Doomsday (2008) and 2012: Supernova (2009), all riding on the release of Roland Emmerich's 2012. Patrick Labyorteaux stars as the scientist Bill Hart, with Julie McCullough as his wife Teri, Nick Afanasiev as their son Nelson and Katie Wilson as their daughter Julia.

In Maine, Bill drops Julia at the airport for her flight back to New York City, where she studies. Soon afterwards his colleague Dr. Divya, flying over Iceland, warns him that violent volcanic eruptions have broken loose an enormous mass of glacial ice hundreds of kilometers wide, which is now hurtling across the Atlantic toward North America; Divya is killed moments later. Bill picks up Teri at the office of the senator she works for, and the family sets out for New York to rescue Julia as the advancing ice brings a summer blizzard, closes airports and flattens Boston, while Air Force jets fail to break it apart.

The journey becomes a struggle for survival in temperatures of forty below. After crashing into an abandoned car, the Harts find a van, only to lose it to Gary, a desperate man heading for California who threatens them with a gun and later drowns when the van plunges through a frozen river. Sheltering in a house, they free Gerald, a man pinned beneath a fallen shelf, and in gratitude he lends them his light aircraft. Meanwhile Julia and her friend Logan try to escape the freezing city on foot through the subway and the Lincoln Tunnel. From the air the Harts witness a second failed attempt to stop the ice, then make an emergency landing when the plane leaks fuel. Tracking Julia's phone, they find her and Logan and take refuge at the Statue of Liberty, from where they watch the military finally destroy the glacier with a nuclear weapon, leaving New York buried in snow but saved.

Shot on a budget estimated at about $250,000 at The Asylum's Los Angeles studio and other locations including the Lacy Street Production Center and a movie ranch in Agua Dulce, the film premiered in the United States on 28 June 2011 and was later released direct to video in other countries, including France in 2012.

title: This Means War

overview: Two top CIA operatives wage an epic battle against one another after they discover they are dating the same woman.
plot:
CIA agents and best friends Franklin "FDR" Foster and Tuck Hansen are deployed to Hong Kong to prevent international criminal Karl Heinrich from acquiring a weapon of mass destruction. However, the mission goes awry, resulting in the death of Heinrich's brother, Jonas. Heinrich swears vengeance against them. Upon their return to the United States, their boss, Collins, assigns them to desk duty for their protection.
Tuck is divorced with a young son, Joe. After attending one of Joe's karate classes, he attempts to rekindle his connection to his family, but is rebuffed by his ex-wife Katie. Tuck sees a commercial for online dating and signs up. He matches with Lauren Scott, a product-testing executive dealing with the recent engagement of her ex-boyfriend. Her best friend, Trish, enrolled her on the dating website. FDR insists on being Tuck's backup for the date and hides nearby, but Tuck and Lauren hit it off.
FDR runs into Lauren at a video store and hits on her, but she ignores him. Intrigued, he gatecrashes one of Lauren's test groups and coerces her into going on a date with him. FDR and Tuck discover that they are seeing the same woman, and decide not to tell her that they know each other, letting her instead decide between them.
The date with FDR does not go well at the start, and Lauren storms out. After arguing with him, she sees her ex-boyfriend and his fiancée approaching. Desperate, Lauren grabs FDR and kisses him, then lies to her ex that they are together and FDR plays along. FDR demands she explain what happened; they then talk seriously and hit it off. After dating both men a few times, including FDR taking her to privately view a collection of Gustav Klimt's major artworks, Lauren feels guilty and gives herself a week to make up her mind.

Lauren has decided to be with FDR, and Tuck makes amends with him.

plot:
Abduction is a 2011 American action thriller film directed by John Singleton and written by Ridley Scott and Tony Gilroy. The movie stars Taylor Lautner, Lily Collins, Alfred Molina, Jason Patric, Sigourney Weaver, and Michael Nyqvist.

The story follows Nathan Harper (Taylor Lautner), an 18-year-old high school student who lives with his mother, Stephanie (Lily Collins), in a small town. Nathan's life is turned upside down when he discovers that he has been kidnapped as a child and raised by a group of people known as "The Syndicate," a secret organization that harvests children from around the world to use for their own purposes.

Nathan's memories of his childhood are fragmented, but he begins to experience strange flashbacks and nightmares. He soon realizes that he is being hunted by The Syndicate, who will stop at nothing to keep him from revealing their secrets.

As Nathan tries to uncover the truth about his past, he meets Sarah (Lily Collins), a beautiful and mysterious woman who claims to be an FBI agent. She helps Nathan evade The Syndicate's agents and begins to teach him how to fight and defend himself.

Meanwhile, Nathan discovers that he has a unique genetic marker that makes him a valuable asset to The Syndicate. He also learns that his mother is still alive and working for the organization, which adds a personal dimension to his quest for revenge.

As the stakes escalate, Nathan and Sarah find themselves in a cat-and-mouse game with The Syndicate's leader, Emil (Michael Nyqvist), who will stop at nothing to capture Nathan and exploit his genetic marker. Along the way, Nathan must confront his own identity and the true nature of his past.

The movie builds towards an action-packed climax as Nathan and Sarah face off against The Syndicate in a thrilling showdown. In the end, Nathan is able to outsmart Emil and destroy The Syndicate's operation, but not before discovering that his mother has been killed by the organization.

Throughout the movie, Taylor Lautner delivers a strong performance as the protagonist, bringing a sense of vulnerability and determination to the role. Lily Collins shines as Sarah, adding depth and complexity to the story. The supporting cast, including Alfred Molina and Sigourney Weaver, adds to the tension and suspense.

Overall, Abduction is an action-packed thriller that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption. While it may not be a perfect film, it delivers plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

title: Legends of Oz: Dorothy's Return
tagline: There's trouble in OZ...
overview: Dorothy wakes up in post-tornado Kansas, only to be whisked back to Oz to try to save her old friends the Scarecrow, the Lion, the Tin Man and Glinda from a devious new villain, the Jester. Wiser the owl, Marshal Mallow, China Princess and Tugg the tugboat join Dorothy on her latest magical journey through the colorful landscape of Oz to restore order and happiness to Emerald City.
plot:
Inside the Emerald City, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, now the city's co-leaders, discover that the Wicked Witch of the West's broomstick has been stolen. With the Land of Oz's future imperiled, the Scarecrow decides to activate his invention, the Rainbow Mover, to contact Dorothy Gale. Meanwhile, back in Kansas, she awakens to discover that a different tornado has wrecked her family's farm, leaving it in disrepair. A man posing as a government appraiser condemns the farmhouse and evicts her family. After a few failed attempts to repair her farm, Dorothy discovers her fellow townspeople have been similarly notified. Noticing a rainbow approaching her, she attempts to escape from it, but it ultimately absorbs her and Toto. Holographically, the trio reappear before Dorothy, and the Scarecrow attempts to explain what is happening. Before he can finish, Winged monkeys break into the Wizard of Oz's chamber, causing the trio to flee. The rainbow deposits Dorothy and Toto in Oz, albeit far from the Emerald City.
Dorothy first befriends Wiser, an overweight and intelligent but flightless owl. The pair enters Candy Country, where everything is made out of candy, including the inhabitants. Due to the manipulated signs, Marshal Mallow promptly arrests the duo for breaking the "no eating anything made of candy" rule and brings them to court. Upon recognizing Dorothy, Judge Jawbreaker exonerates and releases her and Wiser. Mallow joins the group, thus turning it into a trio, to fulfill a promise he made to find the missing General Candy Apple. Meanwhile, Glinda confronts the Jester, who has constructed a magic scepter from his sister's broomstick and crystal ball to turn the leaders of the territories of Oz, including General Candy Apple, into subservient marionettes. Glinda is similarly victimized, giving him complete control of Oz.
Entering the Dainty China Country, the trio is informed that they are restricted from passing through her kingdom. Inside her castle, the China Princess rejects potential suitors, but Mallow poses as a suitor and enchants her with his singing. After the Jester damages the land by causing an earthquake, the Princess angrily blames Dorothy for the Jester's torment, but agrees to accompany Dorothy and her traveling group, thus granting them passage through the land. Finding a bridge to the Emerald City destroyed, the group decides to construct a boat, but all the talking trees in the nearby forest decline except for an 978-year-old tree named Tugg, who agrees to be carved into a galleon. Dorothy's group sails into the abandoned Emerald City, but upon an ambush by the Flying Monkeys, the unit escapes into a cave system but tumbles down a waterfall and is separated.
Shattered by the fall and presumed dead, the China Princess is mourned by Mallow, who then surprisingly discovers she is still alive and repairs her.

title: Judy Moody and the Not Bummer Summer

tagline: Supermegatotally thrilladelic
overview: Third-grader Judy Moody sets out to have the most thrilling summer of her life.
plot:
Judy Moody and the Not Bummer Summer is a 2011 American family comedy based on Megan McDonald's Judy Moody book series. Directed by John Schultz from a screenplay by McDonald and Kathy Waugh, it stars Jordana Beatty as Judy, a spirited third-grader, with Parris Mosteller as her younger brother Stink, Heather Graham as her free-spirited Aunt Opal, Janet Varney, Kristoffer Winters, Preston Bailey, Taylar Hender and Garrett Ryan. It was released in June 2011.

On the last day of the school year, Judy's teacher, Mr. Todd, announces that any student who finds him over the summer will win a prize. Judy organizes a contest with her best friends, Amy and Rocky, to see who can have the most thrilling summer, earning "thrill points" for daring adventures. But her plans fall apart when Amy reveals that she is going to Borneo and Rocky announces that he is off to circus camp, leaving Judy stuck at home with her nerdy, insecure friend Frank. Her parents refuse to let her join either of her friends and leave for California, putting Judy and Stink in the care of their eccentric Aunt Opal, whom they barely know.

Judy turns the contest into a race, emailing her friends to keep score, while also searching for Mr. Todd. Her attempts at thrills go hilariously wrong: Frank accidentally knocks her off a homemade tightrope inspired by Rocky's circus act, throws up on her on a roller coaster called the Scream Monster, refuses to surf after being hit by a wave and abandons a horror-movie marathon halfway through. Meanwhile Stink is obsessed with tracking down Bigfoot, and Aunt Opal, an artist, encourages the children to see adventure in ordinary things. Gradually Judy realizes that her summer can be thrilling after all, as Frank proves a loyal friend, the Bigfoot hunt brings unexpected excitement and the family's adventures culminate in a memorable event in their hometown.

Judy Moody and the Not Bummer Summer received negative reviews from critics, who found it loud and frenetic, though some appreciated its bright, colorful style and Beatty's energetic performance. It performed poorly at the box office, grossing about $15 million.

title: A Separation
tagline: Ugly truth, sweet lies.
overview: A married couple are faced with a difficult decision - to improve the life of their child by moving to another country or to stay in Iran and look after a deteriorating parent who has Alzheimer's disease.
plot:
Nader, Simin, and their 10-year-old daughter, Termeh, are an upper-middle-class family living in a flat in Tehran. Simin wants the whole family to leave Iran and has prepared the visas, but Nader wishes to stay to care for his father, who lives with them and has Alzheimer's disease. Simin therefore files for divorce, but the family court considers the grounds to be insufficient and rejects the application. Simin moves back to her parents’ home and Termeh stays with her father.
Nader hires Razieh, a deeply religious woman from a poor and distant suburb, to take care of his father during the day. She comes each day with her young daughter, Somayeh. She soon finds that she cannot cope, in particular because the old man has become incontinent. One day, when Razieh and Somayeh are busy, he slips out and wanders in the street. Razieh hastens out and dodges through the traffic to get to him.
The next day, Nader and Termeh come home early and discover the old man lying unconscious on the floor in his bedroom, tied to the bed. Razieh and Somayeh are out. When they return, Razieh says she had some urgent personal business; Nader accuses her of neglecting his father and stealing some money (which Simin had in fact used to pay some movers). When Razieh refuses to leave until he pays her, he pushes her out of the flat. She apparently falls down some steps. Nader and Simin later learn that Razieh has suffered a miscarriage.
If Nader knew of Razieh's pregnancy and caused the miscarriage, he could be guilty of murder. There is now a series of claims and counter-claims before a criminal judge: on one side, Nader, with Simin and Termeh; on the other, Razieh and her husband, Hodjat. He is a hot-tempered man, embittered and humiliated by the loss of his long-time job as a cobbler, and harassed by creditors. More than once, he attempts to assault Nader.
Razieh says that Nader knew of her pregnancy because he heard a conversation in the flat between her and Termeh's tutor, in which the tutor recommended a doctor to her. Nader denies this, and the tutor gives evidence in his support. Termeh finds reasons to believe this is not true, and Nader at last admits to her that he has lied for her sake and his father's: he cannot go to prison. The tutor withdraws her evidence. To protect her father, Termeh tells the judge that her father did not know of the pregnancy until she told him.
Nader claims that when he pushed Razieh out of the flat, she could not have fallen down the steps, but would have been protected by the railing. Razieh confesses to Simin that when she went out to bring back the old man, she was hit by a car and was in pain that night; this was the day before Nader pushed her, and she had gone out that day to see a doctor.
Hodjat is violent, and Simin fears for Termeh's safety. Simin persuades Nader to make a payment to Hodjat, but Nader first asks Razieh to swear on the Qur'an that he is the cause of her miscarriage. She cannot do so.

Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Rodrick Rules is a 2011 American comedy directed by David Bowers and written by Jeff Judah and Gabe Sachs, based on Jeff Kinney's 2008 novel. title: The Silence
overview: 13-year-old Sinikka vanishes on a hot summer night. Her bicycle is found in the exact place where a girl was killed 23 years ago. The dramatic present forces those involved in the original case to face their past.
plot:
The Silence (German: Das letzte Schweigen) is a 2010 German thriller film directed by Baran bo Odar, adapted from the crime novel The Silence by Jan Costin Wagner. Its ensemble cast includes Ulrich Thomsen as Peer Sommer, Wotan Wilke Möhring as Timo Friedrich, Sebastian Blomberg as detective David Jahn, Burghart Klaußner as retired detective Krischan Mittich, Katrin Sass as Elena Lange and Oliver Stokowski as Matthias Grimmer.

In the summer of 1986, eleven-year-old Pia is raped and murdered in a wheat field outside a small German town by one man while another watches silently from the passenger seat of a red car. Her body is taken away and her bicycle is left behind. Exactly 23 years later, in 2009, thirteen-year-old Sinikka Weghamm disappears after leaving the local fair, and her bicycle is found at the same spot. Krischan Mittich, the detective who never solved Pia's murder, has just retired, and the new investigation falls to David Jahn, who is still overwhelmed by grief after the death of his wife five months earlier, under the leadership of the stubborn senior detective Matthias Grimmer, who keeps Mittich at arm's length. Flashbacks reveal how the killer, a Dane named Peer Sommer, met Timo, a student with whom he shared a collection of child pornography, and how Timo fled after witnessing Pia's death. Timo has since built a respectable life as an architect, married and become a father, but news of Sinikka's disappearance sends him back to the town and to Sommer, who is pleased to see him again. Racked with shame, Timo visits Pia's grieving mother, Elena, whose suspicions about the stranger lead Mittich and Jahn to his home, while Jahn proposes cross-checking lists of red cars registered near the old crime scenes. As the police close in from different directions, the investigation is shadowed by the anguish of Sinikka's parents and the guilt of the two men who have kept silent for more than two decades, and the question of whether the new crime was committed by the same killer becomes ever more pressing.

The Guardian's Peter Bradshaw gave the film a favorable review, calling it an icy, gripping police procedural thriller that is easy to recommend to fans of The Killing and to anyone else. It won a Special Jury Award at the Beaune film festival in 2011, the Best Adaptation Award at the 2010 Frankfurt Book Fair and an audience award at the German Thriller Awards, and it was nominated for the German Film Critics Award.

title: Sundays at Tiffany's
overview: Jane, a soon-to-be-married woman, is reunited with her imaginary friend Michael who returns in a human form. Soon, Jane begins doubting her feelings for her fiance as she gets attracted to Michael.
plot:
Sundays at Tiffany's is a 2010 American romantic fantasy television film directed by Mark Piznarski for Lifetime, adapted from the 2008 novel of the same name by James Patterson and Gabrielle Charbonnet. Alyssa Milano, who also served as an executive producer, stars as Jane Claremont, with Eric Winter as her imaginary friend Michael, Ivan Sergei as her fiancé Hugh and Stockard Channing as her mother Vivian; Kristin Booth and Emily Alyn Lind, as the young Jane, also appear. The score is by Mateo Messina.

As a lonely girl in New York, Jane spends her Sundays at Tiffany's with her mother, a cold, controlling theatre producer embittered by her divorce, and brings along Michael, a boy of her own age whom only she can see. On Christmas Eve, which is also Jane's birthday, Michael explains that under the rules governing imaginary friends he must leave once she turns ten, and he vanishes from her life. Years later Jane is a successful businesswoman working alongside her mother at the theatre and is engaged to Hugh, a famous actor who seems more in love with his career than with her, with the wedding set for her birthday on Christmas Eve. Outwardly she insists that her life is perfect, but she has doubts, and her mother is more interested in controlling her than supporting her. Then Michael unexpectedly reappears, now a grown man and visible to everyone, having been summoned without her realizing it because she needs guidance. At first shocked and in denial, Jane gradually grows attached to him, rediscovering the value of simple things, while Michael adapts to the human world, finds work as a chef and begins to experience human feelings. Their friendship turns into love, and Hugh comes to see Michael as a threat. When Michael admits that the rules require him to leave her again on her birthday, the hurt Jane refuses to see him. On Christmas Eve, during the ceremony itself, she realizes her relationship with Hugh is loveless and calls off the wedding, only to find that Michael, against all expectations, has not disappeared and has become human, free to stay with her.

The film was shot in Toronto and on location between September 8 and October 1, 2010. Milano said she was drawn to the original concept and its flawed characters, and enjoyed reuniting with Winter and Sergei, with whom she had worked on Charmed. It premiered on Lifetime on December 6, 2010, drawing about 2.1 million viewers.

The story begins with a group of teenagers living in the small town of Evergreen, Colorado, where they are preparing for their high school prom. The main characters include Jed Eckert (Chris Hemsworth), his brother Matt (Wiley Wiggins), and their friends Chris Hargensen (Alexandra Daddario) and Gage (Josh Peck).

As tensions rise between the United States and China, a group of Chinese soldiers invade Evergreen, killing many of the townspeople. The surviving teenagers take up arms to fight back against the invaders, with Jed becoming the leader of the resistance.

The group consists of Jed's brother Matt, Chris, Gage, and several other local teenagers who are determined to defend their home. They use guerrilla warfare tactics, including ambushes and sabotage, to harass and disrupt the Chinese forces.

As the battle between the Americans and the Chinese intensifies, Jed becomes increasingly obsessed with avenging his family's death and defeating the enemy. He also begins to develop feelings for Chris, who is initially hesitant to join the fight but eventually becomes a key member of the resistance.

The movie follows the group as they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, limited resources, and internal conflicts. Along the way, Jed and his team encounter other groups of rebels, including a group of Russian soldiers who are fighting against the Chinese invasion.

As the final battle approaches, Jed's leadership is tested, and he must make difficult decisions to ensure the survival of his team. The movie culminates in an intense showdown between the Americans and the Chinese forces, with Jed facing off against the enemy commander.

In the end, Jed emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. The movie ends on a bittersweet note, with Jed reflecting on the cost of war and the importance of protecting one's home.

Overall, Red Dawn is an action-packed thriller that explores themes of patriotism, loyalty, and sacrifice. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans among action enthusiasts who appreciate its intense fight scenes and suspenseful plot.

plot:
The Suite Life Movie is a 2011 American science fiction comedy-drama television film directed by Sean McNamara and written by Michael Saltzman. A Disney Channel Original Movie based on the sitcom The Suite Life on Deck, itself a spin-off of The Suite Life of Zack & Cody, it stars Dylan and Cole Sprouse, who also served as executive producers, alongside Brenda Song, Debby Ryan, Matthew Timmons, John Ducey, Matthew Glave and Phill Lewis. It premiered on Disney Channel on March 25, 2011.

Cody Martin cancels his spring break plans with his girlfriend Bailey Pickett and leaves the cruise ship SS Tipton, where he attends school, to take an internship with Dr. Donald Spaulding at a prestigious research institute, hoping to win a scholarship to Yale. Bailey is so upset that she stops speaking to him. Meanwhile, his twin brother Zack wants the car their parents promised Cody for college, and Cody refuses to give it up. When Zack crashes a billion-dollar research submarine into a seawall while showing off, and Cody wrecks another trying to stop him, Cody is fired and angrily declares that, though they are twins, they are not brothers. Elsewhere, heiress London Tipton eats a fruit meant for the institute's dolphins and gains the ability to understand them.

The estranged brothers are then recruited for the Gemini Project, run by Dr. Ronald Olsen, who studies the physical and emotional connections between twins. On a remote island filled with hundreds of other twin pairs, Olsen claims his goal is to create bonds of empathy that could end evil in the world. Using the same fruit, the experiment allows Zack and Cody to feel each other's sensations and then emotions, and each comes to understand the other: Cody wants the scholarship so he can be with Bailey, while Zack needs the car to find his own purpose. Soon after reconciling, they discover that Olsen has sinister plans. As the island's twins fall under mind control and hunt them down, Bailey, who has finally read Cody's letter explaining his choices, sets out with London, Woody and the ship's manager Mr. Moseby to rescue them, helped by information London receives from a dolphin. Working together, the brothers must use their new connection to defeat Olsen.

The film drew 5.2 million viewers on its premiere. It later aired around the world, and it has streamed on Disney+ since November 2019. BSC Kids rated it seven out of ten, calling it typical but surprisingly funny and a good choice for younger viewers.

plot:
The Thing is a 2011 American science fiction horror film directed by Matthijs van Heijningen Jr. and written by Eric Heisserer. A direct prequel to John Carpenter's 1982 film of the same name, itself adapted from a 1938 John W. Campbell novella, it depicts the fate of the Norwegian Antarctic research team that uncovers a shape-shifting alien in the ice. The ensemble cast is led by Mary Elizabeth Winstead as paleontologist Kate Lloyd, Joel Edgerton as helicopter pilot Sam Carter, Ulrich Thomsen as scientist Sander Halvorson, Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje as co-pilot Derek Jameson and Eric Christian Olsen as research assistant Adam Finch.

In the winter of 1982, the Norwegian station Thule discovers an alien spacecraft buried in the Antarctic ice, along with the frozen body of a creature. Halvorson and Finch recruit Kate, who flies to the station with Carter, Jameson and crewman Griggs. The creature bursts out of its block of ice, kills a dog and absorbs a team member before being burned. An autopsy shows that its cells were copying those of its victim. When the helicopter leaves to take an injured man for treatment, Griggs transforms and attacks, and the aircraft crashes. Finding bloody dental fillings in a shower, Kate realizes that the alien can absorb and imitate its victims but cannot reproduce inorganic material. The geologist Juliette reveals herself as a Thing and is destroyed with a flamethrower, and the group quarantines itself.

Carter and Jameson stagger back from the crash and are isolated under suspicion. Kate's test of checking everyone for metal fillings clears all but four people, including Halvorson. In the chaos that follows, Carter and Jameson break in, station chief Edvard transforms and merges with Finch into a two-headed creature, and Kate and Carter burn it. The assimilated Halvorson flees to the spacecraft, which comes to life; Kate destroys him with a grenade, shutting it down. Realizing that Carter is wearing his earring in the wrong ear, she burns him too, then sets off for a Soviet base. The next morning, the surviving Lars confronts the returning pilot Matias as the station's dog, actually a Thing, runs off, and the two pursue it by helicopter.

The film opened in the United States on October 14, 2011. It was a box-office bomb, grossing $31.5 million worldwide against a $38 million budget. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes gave it 34% approval, calling it a slave to Carpenter's superior version, and Metacritic gave it 49.

Silent Hill: Revelation 3D is a 2012 American supernatural horror film directed by Michael J. Bassett, written by Ron Schmidt and Frank Cappello, and starring Adelaide Clemens, Sean Bean, and Kit Harington.

The movie takes place four years after the events of Silent Hill: Revelation (2012). The story begins with Alex Shepherd (Adelaide Clemens), a young woman who has been searching for her adopted father, Harry Mason (Sean Bean), in the haunted town of Silent Hill. After receiving a mysterious letter from an unknown sender, Alex finally finds herself back in Silent Hill.

Upon arrival, she discovers that Harry is missing and sets out to find him. As she delves deeper into the town's mysteries, she encounters a group of cultists who are searching for their own god, known as "The God" or "The Otherworldly Being." The cultists believe that by sacrificing themselves, they can bring about the return of this being and gain ultimate power.

As Alex navigates through Silent Hill, she meets Sean (Kit Harington), a young man who claims to be Harry's son. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to uncover the truth behind Harry's disappearance and the cultists' sinister plans.

Throughout their adventure, Alex and Sean encounter various monsters from Silent Hill's eerie landscape, including Pyramid Head, Nurses, and other iconic creatures. Along the way, they also discover that the town is filled with alternate realities and dimensions, which are connected to the Otherworldly Being.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Harry has been searching for a way to save his daughter, Rose (Sienna Guillory), who was taken by the cultists. The group soon realizes that they must stop the cultists before it's too late and prevent the return of the Otherworldly Being.

The climax of the movie features an intense showdown between Alex, Sean, and the cultists in a desperate bid to save Harry and Rose. In the end, Alex manages to defeat the cult leader and shatter the portal that would have brought about the Otherworldly Being's return.

However, as the dust settles, it becomes clear that the movie has an ambiguous ending. The fate of Harry and Rose is left uncertain, leaving the audience wondering if they were truly saved or if there are still more challenges ahead for Alex and Sean.

Overall, Silent Hill: Revelation 3D offers a thrilling and suspenseful ride through the haunted world of Silent Hill. While it may not be as well-received as its predecessor, the movie provides an entertaining and terrifying experience for fans of the series.

title: Diary of a Sex Addict
overview: A restaurant owner leads a double life.
plot:
Diary of a Sex Addict is a 2001 American erotic drama directed by Joseph Brutsman, who wrote the screenplay with Anthony Peck, the son of Gregory Peck. Produced by Nu Image and Millennium Films, it stars Michael Des Barres, Rosanna Arquette, Nastassja Kinski and Ed Begley Jr. The film premiered at the 58th Venice International Film Festival in August 2001 and was released on DVD in the United States on 13 November 2001.

Sammy Horn is a charming, middle-aged English chef who owns a luxurious restaurant and appears to be a devoted family man. He genuinely loves his wife, Grace, their young son and his work, but he is also a sex addict, driven to seek pleasure at any time and with almost any woman he meets. To feed his compulsion he builds an elaborate double life, juggling affairs and casual encounters while keeping them hidden from his family, and becomes increasingly trapped in a web of lies that threatens his marriage and everything he cares about.

Sincerely wanting to break the pattern, Sammy begins therapy with the psychiatrist Dr. Jane Bordeaux, and the story unfolds largely through his sessions with her, as he confesses the details of his secret life and tries to understand what drives it. The film follows his mounting anxiety as the gap between his public and private selves becomes harder to manage and the consequences of his behaviour close in on him.

Des Barres plays Sammy, with Arquette as Grace, Kinski as Dr. Bordeaux and Ed Begley Jr. as Dr. Aaron Spencer. The supporting cast includes Alexandra Paul as Katherine, Eva Jeníčková as Tatiana and A.J. Benza as a police detective, while the twins Cole and Dylan Sprouse share the role of Sammy's son, Sammy Jr. Brutsman shot the film on digital video, using jump cuts to convey the character's unravelling state of mind.

Critical response was mixed. Reviewing it for Radio Times, Jason Caro gave it three stars out of five, calling it less trashy than its title suggests and a frank, troubling attempt to take a genuine addiction seriously. He felt Des Barres struck the right balance of charm and sleaze, and that Arquette and Kinski lent the film credibility, though he found its plotless structure and barrage of rough sexual encounters wearing. Other reviewers were harsher, dismissing it as amateurish and exploitative.
