overview: A highly intelligent chimpanzee named Caeser has been living a peaceful suburban life ever since he was born. But when he gets taken to a cruel primate facility, Caeser decides to revolt against those who have harmed him.
plot:
In San Francisco, pharmaceutical chemist Will Rodman tests the viral-based drug ALZ-112 on chimpanzees at the biotechnology company Gen-Sys to find a cure for Alzheimer's disease. ALZ-112 is given to a chimpanzee named Bright Eyes, greatly increasing her intelligence. However, during Will's presentation for the drug, Bright Eyes is forced from her cage, goes on a rampage, and is shot to death. Will's superior Steven Jacobs terminates the project and has the chimpanzees euthanized. However, Will's assistant Robert Franklin reveals that the reason for Bright Eyes' rampage was that she had recently given birth. Will reluctantly takes in the infant chimpanzee, eventually naming him Caesar. Discovering that Caesar has inherited his mother's intelligence through being exposed to ALZ-112, Will decides to raise him. Three years pass, Caesar becomes highly intelligent; he can communicate through sign language. Will begins a romantic relationship with primatologist Caroline Aranha. Will and Caroline introduce Caesar to the redwood forest at Muir Woods National Monument so he can roam. Meanwhile, Will treats his father, Charles, with ALZ-112, which seems to restore his cognitive ability.
Five years later, Caesar, now entering adulthood, questions his origins and place in the world. Charles's condition returns as his immune system becomes resistant to ALZ-112. Caesar injures an aggressive neighbor, Douglas Hunsiker, while defending a confused Charles. The local animal control subsequently takes him to an ape shelter. Caesar is tormented by the alpha chimpanzee, Rocket, and the chief guard, Dodge Landon. However, Caesar befriends Maurice, a former circus orangutan who also knows sign language. Caesar learns to unlock his cage, gaining free access to the common area. With the assistance of Buck, a gorilla, Caesar claims the position of alpha. Meanwhile, Jacobs clears the development of a more powerful gaseous version of the drug, the ALZ-113, when Will tells him it can improve intelligence. Will takes the drug home for his father, but Charles declines further treatment and dies overnight. title: 30 Minutes or Less

plot:
30 Minutes or Less is a 2011 American action comedy film directed by Ruben Fleischer and produced by Stuart Cornfeld, Ben Stiller and Jeremy Kramer. Jesse Eisenberg stars as Nick, a pizza delivery driver, with Aziz Ansari as his friend Chet, Danny McBride and Nick Swardson as a pair of inept criminals, Michael Peña and Fred Ward. Released by Sony Pictures on 12 August 2011, it was filmed in Grand Rapids, Michigan, where the story is set.

Nick is an aimless young man in Grand Rapids who rarely manages to deliver pizzas within his employer's thirty-minute guarantee. His friendship with Chet, a schoolteacher, falls apart when Chet learns that Nick slept with his twin sister, Kate, on the night of their high school graduation; Nick also learns that Kate is about to leave for a job in Atlanta. Meanwhile, Dwayne and his friend Travis live in the shadow of Dwayne's domineering father, known as the Major, who won a large lottery jackpot years earlier. Eager to get his inheritance, Dwayne learns from a stripper, Juicy, that a hitman named Chango could kill his father, but he needs $100,000 to pay him.

Dwayne and Travis decide to kidnap a stranger, strap a bomb to him and force him to steal the money. They order a pizza, knock Nick unconscious when he arrives and lock him into a vest rigged with explosives, which they threaten to detonate if he goes to the police or fails to bring them the money within ten hours. Nick turns to Chet, who reluctantly helps him rob a bank. The heist is chaotic, but the two escape with the cash. When Dwayne and Travis demand the money and take Kate hostage, the situation escalates into a showdown at a scrapyard with Chango, involving bluffs, a flamethrower and the bomb itself, which Nick eventually turns against his captors.

The film received mixed reviews, with critics finding the cast's comic energy engaging but the story slight and the humor uneven. It grossed about $40 million worldwide against a $28 million budget. It also attracted controversy for its resemblance to the real 2003 death of Brian Wells, a pizza delivery man in Erie, Pennsylvania, who was killed by a bomb locked around his neck during a bank robbery; the filmmakers said they had not been aware of the case.

Victoria becomes entangled in the web of supernatural events unfolding around her, including the ghostly apparitions of the past, including Josette du Pres (Michelle Pfeiffer), who was Angelique's lover and Barnaby's wife. As Victoria delves deeper into the mystery, she uncovers a dark family secret that has been hidden for centuries.

As the story unfolds, Victoria finds herself caught between her growing feelings for David and her desire to help Barnaby break free from Angelique's spell. Along the way, she must confront the evil forces of Angelique, who will stop at nothing to destroy those who threaten her power.

The film builds towards a climactic showdown between good and evil, with Victoria playing a key role in breaking the curse that has haunted the Collins family for centuries. In the end, Barnaby is freed from his vampiric state, and he and Victoria share a romantic moment, as the supernatural forces are vanquished.

Throughout the film, Tim Burton's signature style and visual flair bring the world of Dark Shadows to life, with stunning costumes, sets, and special effects. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Johnny Depp, who brings his trademark eccentricity to the role of Barnaby Collins.

Overall, Dark Shadows is a visually stunning and entertaining film that pays homage to the original TV series while offering something new and unique for fans of Tim Burton's work.

title: Home
tagline: A stunning visual portrayal of Earth
overview: In 200,000 years of existence, man has upset the balance on which the Earth had lived for 4 billion years. Global warming, resource depletion, species extinction: man has endangered his own home. But it is too late to be pessimistic: humanity has barely ten years left to reverse the trend, become aware of its excessive exploitation of the Earth's riches, and change its consumption pattern.
plot:
Home is a 2009 French documentary directed by the photographer Yann Arthus-Bertrand and produced by Luc Besson, Denis Carot and François-Henri Pinault, with music by Armand Amar. Inspired by the director's photography book Earth from Above, the film is built almost entirely from aerial footage combined with a voice-over, and it is conceived as a travel journal about the bond between humanity and the planet. Its narrators varied by language: Glenn Close read the English version, Salma Hayek the Spanish, Isabella Rossellini the Italian and Zhou Xun the Chinese, while Jacques Gamblin voiced the French theatrical cut and Arthus-Bertrand himself the French television version.

The film begins with the formation of the Earth and the emergence of life, then traces how human societies spread across continents and, especially in the past few decades, began to reshape the planet at unprecedented speed. Sweeping images of deserts, forests, ice caps, farmland and megacities illustrate its central themes: water shortages, deforestation, melting ice, the depletion of natural resources and the impact of human activity on climate change. Rather than presenting a disaster film, Arthus-Bertrand frames it as a message of hope, arguing that humanity still has roughly ten years to change course.

The shoot took about eighteen months, with the director, a cameraman, a camera engineer and a pilot flying a small helicopter over more than fifty countries on every continent, including Antarctica. Stabilized high-definition Cineflex cameras mounted beneath the helicopter gave the footage its smooth, crane-like quality, and nearly 500 hours of raw material were recorded. With a budget of about 12 million euros, largely funded by the PPR group (later Kering), Home was released on World Environment Day, 5 June 2009, simultaneously in cinemas, on television, on DVD and free on YouTube in 181 countries, and it was screened outdoors on the Champ de Mars in Paris. It drew more than 8 million viewers on France 2 and tens of millions of views online. Critics praised its imagery but questioned its preachy narration and the contrast between its message and its luxury-goods sponsor. It was nominated for the César Award for Best Documentary.

title: The Devil's Double
tagline: The 80's were brilliant, if you were in charge.
overview: A chilling vision of the House of Saddam Hussein comes to life through the eyes of the man who was forced to become the double of Hussein's sadistic son.
plot:
In 1987, Latif Yahia, an Iraqi soldier fighting in the Iran–Iraq War, is called to become a "fedai" ("body double" or political decoy) for Uday Hussein, the son of president Saddam. Latif comes from an upper-class family and attended school with Uday, where students would remark on their likeness. He refuses the position. Furious, Uday has him imprisoned and tortured. Latif relents when his family is threatened. Latif undergoes cosmetic surgery to perfect his resemblance to Uday and practises emulating the latter's mannerisms and persona. Latif tries to resist Uday's exorbitant merrymaking and erratic behaviour, at one point fleeing a nightclub to attempt to see his family, who believe that he died in the war. However, he is apprehended by Uday's bodyguards and beaten by Uday. After an appearance at a conference with Kuwaiti leaders, an attempt is made on Uday's (Latif's) life, apparently by a member of a rebel opposition group, possibly a Kurd. The real Uday, though, is more concerned with the Kuwaitis, whom he believes were slant drilling into Iraq's Rumaila oil field. The First Gulf War is launched.
Uday eventually kidnaps a 14-year-old girl and forces her to escort him to a party. There, Uday becomes enraged with Saddam's personal bodyguard Kamel Hana Gegeo. Uday believes that Gegeo facilitated an affair Saddam had, which devastated his mother. Uday is also jealous at the trust Saddam places in Gegeo. When Gegeo passes sarcastic comments about Uday's advances towards the girl and drunkenly fires an AK-47 in the air, Uday butchers him with an electric knife in front of the guests. The next morning, Uday's bodyguards dump the girl's beaten, partially naked body. Furious, Saddam goes to the hospital, where Uday is overdosed on sleeping pills. Saddam beats Uday and nearly castrates him. Only the intervention of a doctor saves him. As the war is in full swing, Latif tries to distance himself from Uday and begins an affair with Sarrab, one of Uday's lovers.
Latif, acting as Uday, is later sent to Basra to rally support among Republican Guard soldiers as Coalition forces take control of the war. At Basra, another attempt is made on Latif's life. Latif nearly loses a finger in the assault, which would mean Uday would have to amputate his own finger to maintain their resemblance. Uday enters a hospital and threatens to slaughter everyone in it if they fail to save his finger. The doctors succeed.
Afterwards, Uday, accompanied by his usual party, crashes a wedding, eventually raping and beating the bride, who then commits suicide. Angry, Latif assaults Uday but is corralled by the latter's bodyguards, who threaten to kill him. Uday stops them. Later, Latif is confronted by the father of the girl Uday killed. Uday overhears them and is outraged by the man's pleas for "justice" and "compassion". Uday orders Latif to kill the man, but Latif refuses and instead slits his own wrists. He is dumped half-dead on his family's front door.

The story begins with King Agnarr (Martin Klebba), the father of Queen Grimhilde (Julianne Moore) and her two daughters, Snow White (Lily Collins) and Ravenna (Milla Jovovich). The movie takes place in a fictional kingdom, where magic is real and mythical creatures roam free.

Years pass, and Queen Grimhilde becomes increasingly bitter and resentful towards Snow White, who is now the princess of the kingdom. She orders her huntsman to take Snow White into the forest and kill her, but the huntsman takes pity on Snow White and tells her to run away.

Snow White finds herself in a small cottage belonging to seven dwarfs: Doc (Nathan Lane), Grumpy (Billy Barty), Happy (Robert Carlyle), Sleepy (Martin Klebba), Bashful (Julian Sands), Sneezy (Stephen Mackintosh), and Dopey (Bo Peep's voice actor, not the same person as the other 6). The dwarfs welcome Snow White into their home, and she stays with them.

Meanwhile, Queen Grimhilde discovers that Snow White is still alive and orders her huntsman to bring back Snow White's heart. However, the huntsman tricks the queen by telling her that he has killed Snow White and brought back her heart in a box. The queen then disposes of the box, unaware that it contains a fake heart.

As time passes, Queen Grimhilde becomes increasingly vain and obsessed with staying young and beautiful. She orders her magic mirror to show her who is the fairest of them all, but the mirror reveals that Snow White is now the fairest of them all.

Enraged, Queen Grimhilde orders a huntsman to take Snow White into the forest and kill her again. However, this time, the huntsman tells Snow White about the queen's plan and advises her to escape. Snow White and the dwarfs come up with a plan to trick the queen and expose her true nature.

In the end, Queen Grimhilde is defeated by Snow White and her friends, who use magic and wit to outsmart her. The movie ends with Snow White and Prince Charming (Armie Hammer) falling in love and getting married, while Queen Grimhilde is banished from the kingdom.

Overall, Mirror Mirror is a fun and lighthearted retelling of the classic fairy tale Snow White. The movie features stunning visuals, witty dialogue, and memorable performances from its cast.

title: Dolphin Tale
tagline: Inspired by the amazing true story of Winter
overview: A story centered on the friendship between a boy and a dolphin whose tail was lost in a crab trap.
plot:
Sawyer Nelson is a lonely 11-year-old who has been falling behind academically in school since his father's abandonment five years earlier. Sawyer spends his time playing video games and building model airplanes and helicopters in his garage. His only friend is his college-aged cousin Kyle Connellan, a champion swimmer who hopes to compete in the Olympics. Kyle leaves to spend time in the army, to help pay for Olympic training. With his only friend gone, Sawyer becomes even more isolated and Sawyer's failing grades have required him to take summer school.
One day, while riding his bike to summer school, Sawyer finds a fisherman attempting to help an injured dolphin tangled in a crab trap. The dolphin is taken for treatment to Clearwater Marine Hospital (CMH), run by Dr. Clay Haskett. Clay's daughter Hazel names the dolphin Winter, after two prior dolphins, Summer and Autumn, had been treated successfully and returned to the ocean. Sawyer sneaks in to see Winter, and later starts to visit each day, being harassed by a crazy pelican named Rufus. Sawyer's mother, Lorraine, and Clay are hesitant, due to Sawyer's inexperience with marine animals, and repeatedly skipping summer school, but they realize that the friendship seems to benefit both Winter and Sawyer. Clay allows the visits to continue, and Lorraine withdraws Sawyer from summer school and lets him volunteer at CMA, and gives him a new wetsuit.
However, Winter's tail is wounded and must be amputated. Winter learns to swim without a tail by developing a side-to-side motion like a fish, but after an X-ray, Clay notices the unnatural motion is causing stress on her spine, which, if continued, will handicap and eventually kill her.
The news comes that Kyle has been injured severely in an explosion and is returning home for treatment. Sawyer is excited to see him, but devastated when Kyle skips his own welcoming party and stays at the local Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, where Dr. Cameron McCarthy develops prosthetic limbs. Sawyer and his mother visit Kyle there, but Sawyer is insulted when Kyle asks them to leave. Not wanting to upset Sawyer, Kyle takes Sawyer for a walk and explains his situation and that he needs some time. At Sawyer's request, McCarthy agrees to make a prosthetic tail for Winter and convinces his prosthetic supplier Hanger Prosthetics and Orthotics to supply the parts at no cost. McCarthy manufactures a "homemade" model tail while waiting for the real one to arrive, but Winter rejects it by banging it against the pool wall. Meanwhile, Kyle gets more depressed when his friend and swimming partner, Donovan Peck, beats his old swimming records. McCarthy persuades Kyle to go home.
Faced with financial trouble, the CMA is heavily damaged by a hurricane. The board of directors agrees to close up and sell the land to a real estate developer. It finds homes for all the animals except Winter, who is not wanted due to her disability and may have to be euthanized.

title: Megan Is Missing
tagline: Megan and Amy are best friends. They share secrets. They chat with guys online. And in a few days, they will never be seen again.
overview: Fourteen-year–old Megan and her best friend Amy spend a lot of time on the internet, posting videos of themselves and chatting with guys online. One night Megan chats with a guy named Josh who convinces her to meet him for a date. The next day, Megan is missing—forever. Based on actual cases of child abduction.
plot:
Megan Stewart and Amy Herman are 14-year-old best friends from North Hollywood who went missing in January 2007. An unidentified, seemingly tech-savvy and omniscient narrator has assembled web-chat recordings, home movies, news reports and previously classified police material into a linear narrative of the weeks surrounding their disappearances. Whether this compiled documentary is meant to be a cautionary tale about online safety, or rather something more sinister, is left open to speculation.
Despite their friendship, the two girls share little in common. Megan is a popular high school honors student, but she also has a dysfunctional relationship with her mother who has a reckless and promiscuous sex life and a drug addiction. Amy, on the other hand, lives in Sherman Oaks, has a healthy relationship with her parents, is still a virgin and enjoys stuffed toys.
This friendship does not exempt Amy from bullying by Megan's friends. To help her fit in, Megan invites Amy to a rave party. Amy's experience in the party is unpleasant all round: she is slapped after refusing the advances of a male attendee, walks in on Megan performing fellatio on the party's host, and vomits on Megan's bisexual friend Lexie while she is making out with another girl.
Megan later assuages Amy's feelings of shame and inadequacy regarding the party, and explains that she first performed oral sex at age 10 with a 17-year-old camp counselor. On her birthday, Amy records a video diary with Megan on her new camera, during which Megan reveals that her stepfather had raped her at the age of nine, and continued to do so for two years, which led to his imprisonment and her self-destructive lifestyle. Her mother resents her for reporting him to authorities, which leads to their volatile relationship. Amy quickly hugs and comforts Megan.
Megan video chats with Lexie. It is strongly implied during this conversation that they share a brief sexual past and Lexie retains a crush on Megan. Lexie gives Megan's social media handle to Josh, who presents himself as a teenager from a nearby school. He only shares one picture and remains anonymous on video chat, claiming his webcam is broken. Despite several suspicions and contradictions, Megan is charmed by him. They agree to meet at a party, but he fails to reveal himself. She confronts him online but forgives him when he accurately describes what she was wearing and insists he is shy. Later, when Amy comes over to her house, Megan introduces her to him.
Josh convinces Megan to meet him behind a diner. She does not attend class the next day, and Amy's initial inquiries are brushed off by Lexie and her friend Kathy. News reports, however, later declare Megan officially missing. Grainy footage from the diner's security camera shows her being grabbed by the wrist by an indistinct older man. Amy investigates Megan's disappearance and talks online with Josh.

title: The Skin I Live In
tagline: The things the love of a madman can do...
overview: A brilliant plastic surgeon creates a synthetic skin that withstands any kind of damage. His guinea pig: a mysterious and volatile woman who holds the key to his obsession.
plot:
The Skin I Live In is a psychological thriller film directed by Pedro Almodóvar, released in 2011 under the production company El Deseo. The movie tells the story of Dr. Robert Ledgard, a brilliant and obsessive scientist who seeks revenge against those he believes wronged him.

The film begins with an elderly Robert (played by Antonio Banderas), a renowned plastic surgeon, living in a remote estate in Ireland. He is revealed to be a former prisoner, having spent 15 years behind bars for a crime he committed as a young man. The story then flashes back to Robert's past, where we see him as a young doctor (also played by Antonio Banderas) who becomes infatuated with a woman named Vera (played by Elena Anaya), the daughter of a wealthy and influential family.

Robert's obsession with Vera leads him to kidnap her and subject her to a series of gruesome experiments. He surgically alters her face, transforming her into a man, which he names Norman. Robert's goal is to create the perfect "son" for himself, someone who will be loyal and obedient only to him.

As the story unfolds, we see Robert's relationship with Norman (also played by Eduardo Noriega), his creation, evolve from one of paternal love to one of twisted obsession. Norman becomes a skilled and deadly assassin, carrying out Robert's orders without question. However, as time passes, Norman begins to develop his own identity and sense of self, which threatens Robert's control over him.

Meanwhile, Vera (Elena Anaya) is revealed to be alive and working as a nurse at the local hospital. She becomes embroiled in a complicated love triangle with her husband, Dr. General (played by Marisa Paredes), and her former lover, Norman.

The plot thickens as Robert's past catches up with him, and he is forced to confront the consequences of his actions. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Vera was actually the one who betrayed Robert to the authorities, leading to his imprisonment. This revelation sets off a chain reaction of events that ultimately leads to Norman's betrayal of Robert.

The film builds towards a tense and violent climax as Robert's world begins to unravel. In the end, Norman turns against Robert, killing him in a brutal and satisfying manner. The movie concludes with Vera, now free from her past, embracing her true identity and finding love with Dr. General.

Throughout the film, Almodóvar explores themes of obsession, identity, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The Skin I Live In is a masterclass in suspense and tension, with outstanding performances from its cast. The film's use of symbolism, particularly the skin that Robert uses to cover his face, adds depth and complexity to the narrative.

Overall, The Skin I Live In is a gripping and unsettling thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

title: My Babysitter's a Vampire
tagline: No parents. No rules. No pulse.
overview: Geeky 14-year old Ethan is left to babysit his younger sister, Jane, with his best friend Benny but after Ethan inadvertently puts Jane in harm's way, his parents hire a professional babysitter, the beautiful yet mysterious 17-year-old Sarah who, unbeknownst to them, is actually a fledgling vampire.
plot:
Ethan Morgan is a geeky high school freshman, not trusted by his parents to take care of his little sister Jane on his own. They hire Erica, a teenage girl from Ethan's school who is a huge fan of Dusk (a parody of Twilight), as a babysitter. Erica instead decides to attend a party thrown by Jesse, the vampire ex-boyfriend of her best friend Sarah. During a fight between Sarah and Jesse, Sarah ends up at Ethan's house and tells Ethan's parents that she was asked to babysit instead. Ethan becomes infatuated with Sarah. Ethan suddenly has a vision when touching Sarah, and notices she has no reflection in the mirror.
Sarah leaves to get Erica back from the party, knowing the party is full of bloodthirsty vampires. Curious, Ethan and his dorky best friend Benny follow Sarah. They see her feed on a rat and realize she is a vampire. Sarah explains that she is only a fledgling, a vampire who has not drunk human blood. The three of them are attacked by a vampire sent by Jesse, and head to the party to save Erica and their dimwitted friend, Rory. However, Erica has already been bitten and also bites Rory.
The next day, Ethan has a vision in which he sees a gravestone with the number 219 and a mysterious box, which is then uncovered by the vampires. The box is called the Cubile Animus or "Nest of Souls". Ethan and Sarah figure out Jesse's plan from an old book, learning that in the original settlement of the town, a man named Reverend Horace Black who led an evil cabal of vampires. During a lunar eclipse, the townspeople burned the members, leading to all '219' of their deaths. Ethan realizes that Jesse is, in fact, Horace Black, and plans to use the box to trap the souls of teens going to see the premiere of the new Dusk movie so he can resurrect the souls of his ancient group during the lunar eclipse.
Benny's grandmother, who reveals that she is an Earth Priestess, gives Ethan, Benny and Sarah enchanted daggers and a spell book to defeat the vampires. She explains that Ethan sees visions because he is a Seer, which enables him to see visions through touch, and Benny is a spellmaster, allowing him to cast spells. At the theater, the vampires begin to steal the souls of the teens, but are thwarted by the trio. In a vision, Ethan sees the tree he saw inside the old book, realizing it's the tree in his backyard, where they find Jesse. As the eclipse begins, Jesse attempts to hold Ethan and Benny down and resurrect the souls he already obtained from the Cubile Animus, but Sarah intervenes. When the box lands in Ethan's hands, he releases the vengeful souls that were captured, which destroy Jesse and return to their bodies.
The next day, Ethan, Benny and Sarah meet Erica and Rory, who have decided to live peacefully as vampires.

title: Honey 2
tagline: Go every step of the way.
overview: After a brush with the law, Maria has returned to her gritty Bronx roots to rebuild her life with nothing but a talent for street dance and a burning ambition to prove herself.
plot:
Honey 2 is a 2011 American dance film directed by Bille Woodruff and a sequel to his 2003 film Honey. Kat Graham stars as Maria Ramirez, a talented street dancer, with Randy Wayne, Seychelle Gabriel, Audrina Patridge, Melissa Molinaro and Lonette McKee, who reprises her role as Connie Daniels, the mother of the first film's heroine, Honey Daniels. The film was released in cinemas in the United Kingdom in June 2011 and went straight to DVD and Blu-ray in the United States in February 2012.

Seventeen-year-old Maria returns to the Bronx after a spell in juvenile detention, determined to rebuild her life with nothing but her talent for street dance and a burning desire to prove herself. She finds refuge at the neighborhood recreation center where, as a child, Honey's lively classes first sparked her passion for dancing. To stay out of trouble, she lives with Honey's mother, Connie, and holds down a job, while trying to avoid her old crew, the 718, and her controlling ex-boyfriend Luis, whose influence landed her in trouble in the first place.

At the center Maria meets Brandon, who runs the place and leads a group of dancers called the HD crew, a collection of talented misfits who lack direction. Maria joins them and pushes them to audition for "Dance Battlezone," a televised dance competition, even though it means going up against the 718, now led by Luis. The rival crew tries to intimidate HD in a street dance-off and temporarily lures away one of its members, Tina, involving her in crimes until she realizes what kind of people they are. As the competition progresses, Maria grows closer to Brandon, struggles to keep her past from catching up with her and must hold the HD crew together through setbacks, rivalries and doubts, as they work toward a final showdown with the 718 on national television.

Like the first film, Honey 2 received negative reviews from critics. It holds a 10 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it an unwanted sequel of banal missteps. Reviewers found the story formulaic, though some acknowledged the energy of the dance sequences and Graham's screen presence. The film was followed by two more straight-to-video sequels, Honey 3: Dare to Dance (2016) and Honey: Rise Up and Dance (2018), each with new characters.

title: The Muppets
tagline: One girl has his dream.
overview: When Kermit the Frog and the Muppets learn that their beloved theater is slated for demolition, a sympathetic human, Gary, and his puppet brother, Walter, swoop in to help the gang put on a show and raise the $10 million they need to save the day.
plot:
The Muppets is a 2011 American musical comedy directed by James Bobin and written by Jason Segel and Nicholas Stoller, the seventh theatrical feature starring Jim Henson's Muppets. It stars Segel as Gary, Amy Adams as his girlfriend Mary, Chris Cooper as the oil magnate Tex Richman and Rashida Jones as television executive Veronica Martin, alongside Muppet performers including Steve Whitmire as Kermit the Frog, Eric Jacobson as Miss Piggy and Fozzie Bear, Dave Goelz as Gonzo and Peter Linz as Walter. Bret McKenzie served as music supervisor and wrote most of the original songs.

Walter, a Muppet growing up in Smalltown alongside his human brother Gary, is the Muppets' most devoted fan. When Gary takes his longtime girlfriend Mary on a trip to Los Angeles on vacation, Walter comes along. During a tour of the run-down Muppet Studios, Walter overhears Tex Richman plotting to buy the Muppet Theatre and drill for the oil beneath it. The Muppets can only save the theatre by raising ten million dollars before their contract expires.

Walter, Gary and Mary track down Kermit, who agrees to reunite the long-disbanded troupe to stage a telethon. Fozzie is performing in Reno with a crude tribute band called the Moopets, Gonzo has become a plumbing magnate, Animal is in anger management, and Miss Piggy is working as an editor at Vogue Paris. Once the gang is reassembled, they persuade a network to air the show, but must find a celebrity host, refurbish the theatre and fill the program, while Walter searches for his own talent. Meanwhile, Mary feels neglected by Gary's devotion to his brother, and Tex does everything he can to sabotage the telethon.

The film is a nostalgic celebration of the Muppets' history and a story about friendship and growing up, mixing classic songs such as "Rainbow Connection" with new numbers and guest appearances by celebrities such as Jack Black.

Released by Walt Disney Studios on 23 November 2011, The Muppets grossed over 171 million dollars worldwide on a 45 million dollar budget. It received widespread acclaim, with 95 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 75, and McKenzie's "Man or Muppet" won the Academy Award for Best Original Song. A sequel, Muppets Most Wanted, followed in 2014.

title: Total Recall
tagline: What Is Real?
overview: Welcome to Rekall, the company that can turn your dreams into real memories. For a factory worker named Douglas Quaid, even though he's got a beautiful wife who he loves, the mind-trip sounds like the perfect vacation from his frustrating life - real memories of life as a super-spy might be just what he needs. But when the procedure goes horribly wrong, Quaid becomes a hunted man. Finding himself on the run from the police - controlled by Chancellor Cohaagen, the leader of the free world - Quaid teams up with a rebel fighter to find the head of the underground resistance and stop Cohaagen. The line between fantasy and reality gets blurred and the fate of his world hangs in the balance as Quaid discovers his true identity, his true love, and his true fate.
plot:
Total Recall is a 2012 American science fiction action film directed by Len Wiseman from a screenplay by Kurt Wimmer and Mark Bomback, an adaptation of the 1990 film inspired by Philip K. Dick's 1966 short story "We Can Remember It for You Wholesale". It stars Colin Farrell, Kate Beckinsale and Jessica Biel, with Bryan Cranston, Bokeem Woodbine, John Cho and Bill Nighy, and unlike the original it is set entirely on Earth.

At the end of the 21st century, chemical warfare has left only two habitable regions: the wealthy United Federation of Britain and the Colony in Australia, whose workers commute daily through the planet's core on a gravity elevator called "The Fall". A Resistance branded as terrorists fights for better conditions in the Colony. Factory worker Douglas Quaid, troubled by dreams of being a spy with a mysterious woman, visits Rekall, a company that implants artificial memories, and chooses a secret-agent fantasy, but the technician finds he already holds real spy memories. Police storm the clinic and Quaid instinctively kills the entire squad. At home his wife, Lori, tries to kill him, revealing that she is a UFB agent and that their seven-year marriage is a six-week fiction.

Guided by a message from his former colleague Hammond and a recording he left himself, Quaid flees to the UFB, where he is rescued from Lori by Melina, the woman from his dreams. Another recording reveals that he is Carl Hauser, an agent of Chancellor Cohaagen who defected to the Resistance after learning of a kill code that could stop the robot army Cohaagen plans to use to seize the Colony. When his friend Harry claims Quaid is still dreaming and must kill Melina to wake, Quaid shoots Harry instead. Resistance leader Matthias begins searching Quaid's memories, but Cohaagen, who invented the kill code to locate him, storms the base, kills Matthias and captures Melina. title: Straw Dogs
tagline: Everyone Has A Breaking Point
overview: L.A. screenwriter David Sumner relocates with his wife, Amy, to her hometown in the deep South. There, while tensions build between them, a brewing conflict with locals becomes a threat to them both.
plot:
Straw Dogs is a 2011 American Southern Gothic psychological thriller written, produced and directed by Rod Lurie. A remake of Sam Peckinpah's 1971 film, itself adapted from Gordon Williams's novel The Siege of Trencher's Farm, it moves the story from Cornwall to rural Mississippi. James Marsden and Kate Bosworth star as David and Amy Sumner, with Alexander Skarsgård as Charlie, Amy's former boyfriend.

Screenwriter David and his actress wife, Amy, move to her hometown of Blackwater, Mississippi, to live in her late father's house while David finishes a script. In town David meets Charlie and his friends Norman, Chris and Bic, who have already been hired to repair the roof of the couple's barn, and Tom Heddon, an alcoholic former high school football coach who bullies Jeremy Niles, an intellectually disabled man he wrongly believes is stalking his teenage daughter, Janice. The workmen soon harass David, leer at Amy and drag out the job, and Amy grows resentful that David will not stand up to them. When the couple's cat is found strangled, the men deny involvement. Charlie invites David on a deer hunt, then returns to the house and rapes Amy, and Norman rapes her as well. Amy keeps silent but urges David to fire the crew, and he pays them off.

At a football game, Janice lures Jeremy into a locker room and forces herself on him; when Heddon comes looking for her, the panicked Jeremy holds her silent and accidentally smothers her. Haunted by memories of the assault, Amy asks to leave the game and, on the drive home, David accidentally hits Jeremy with the car and brings him home to await an ambulance. Learning of this over a police scanner, Heddon and Charlie's gang besiege the house demanding Jeremy, and Heddon kills the sheriff when he tries to intervene. David barricades the house and fights back killing Chris, Heddon and Bic, while Amy shoots Norman as he tries to rape her again. Charlie beats David and prepares to shoot him, but David snaps a bear trap shut on Charlie's neck, killing him, and as sirens approach and the barn burns, he declares that he got them all.

Filming began on August 16, 2009, in Shreveport and Vivian, Louisiana, and Sony Pictures Releasing released the film on September 16, 2011. It opened with $5.1 million and grossed about $11.2 million against a $25 million budget. Reviews were mixed to negative, with many critics comparing it unfavorably with the original; Rotten Tomatoes gave it 42%.

title: The Art of Getting By
tagline: The toughest lesson is love.
overview: George, a lonely and fatalistic teen who's made it all the way to his senior year without ever having done a real day of work, is befriended by Sally, a popular but complicated girl who recognizes in him a kindred spirit.
plot:
George Zinavoy is a lonely senior at a Manhattan preparatory school with a penchant for drawing and a nihilistic worldview. Obsessed with the inevitability of death, he never does homework and skips school frequently; as a result, he is placed on academic probation. One day while on the school roof, George encounters classmate Sally Howe smoking. When a teacher appears, he pulls out a cigarette and takes the fall for her. They become friends.
On Career Day at school, George meets young artist Dustin Heath, who becomes a mentor of sorts to George. He brings Sally with him to visit Dustin at his studio in Brooklyn and it becomes apparent that Dustin finds her attractive. She invites George to a New Year's Eve party, where she dances with an ex-boyfriend while George gets drunk, goes outside, throws up, and falls asleep on the street. Finding him there, Sally takes him to her place, putting him to bed on a pull-out next to her bed. They grow closer and George becomes more involved in school.
On Valentine's Day, George and Sally go out to dinner, and she starts asking questions about what he thinks of her. He is evasive, and she asks him if he will have sex with her. When George freezes, Sally backtracks and claims she was joking, as she considers him her only real friend. He becomes withdrawn and leaves early. As George continually avoids Sally and ignores her calls, she meets with Dustin at a bar one evening and flirts with him. Though Dustin initially resists Sally's advances out of respect for George, they soon begin a relationship.
After failing to write his English term paper, George is again sent to the principal's office. He is given two choices: be expelled, or make up all of the homework he has not done all year. Confronted by his mother and stepfather at home, he responds by telling his mother that his stepfather has been pretending to go to work for weeks. The stepfather attacks him and George knocks him down before taking off. He goes to Sally's and, in the hallway, kisses her. Sally kisses him back but pulls away, revealing Dustin in her apartment. Devastated, George leaves.
The next morning, George finds his mother in the park and she tells him she is divorcing his stepfather. Consoling her, he begins to rethink his life. He decides to make the effort to do his assignments. His art teacher gives him only one project, which must be honest and fearless. George completes the assignments and takes his final exams. Meanwhile, Sally continues seeing Dustin.
One day, George receives a text message from Sally. They meet and she tells him she is going backpacking with Dustin through Europe and skipping graduation. He tells her he is in love with her and they go back to her apartment, where they kiss. Sally tells him she loves him too and promises they will be together one day.
George turns in all his assignments and the principal tells him he will know he has passed if his name is called at graduation.

title: The Great Gatsby
tagline: Reserving judgments is a matter of infinite hope... I come to the admission that it has a limit.
overview: An adaptation of F. Scott Fitzgerald's Long Island-set novel, where Midwesterner Nick Carraway is lured into the lavish world of his neighbor, Jay Gatsby. Soon enough, however, Carraway will see through the cracks of Gatsby's nouveau riche existence, where obsession, madness, and tragedy await.
plot:
The Great Gatsby is a 2013 American drama film directed by Baz Luhrmann, based on F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel of the same name. The film stars Leonardo DiCaprio as Jay Gatsby, Tobey Maguire as Nick Carraway, Carey Mulligan as Daisy Buchanan, and Joel Edgerton as Tom Buchanan.

The story begins in 1922, with Nick Carraway (Tobey Maguire), a young man from the Midwest who moves to Long Island's West Egg to work in the bond business. Nick rents a small house next to a grand mansion owned by Jay Gatsby (Leonardo DiCaprio), who throws extravagant parties that attract wealthy and glamorous guests.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Gatsby's true intention is to win back his lost love, Daisy Buchanan (Carey Mulligan), who is now married to the wealthy and brutish Tom Buchanan (Joel Edgerton). Through Nick, Gatsby meets Daisy again, and they rekindle their romance. However, their love is complicated by the fact that Daisy is still married to Tom, and Gatsby's wealth and social status are not enough to overcome the obstacles in their way.

As the summer progresses, Gatsby and Daisy's affair becomes more intense, but it also puts them at risk of being discovered by Tom, who will stop at nothing to keep his marriage intact. Meanwhile, Nick is drawn into Gatsby's world and becomes increasingly fascinated by the enigmatic millionaire.

The tension between Gatsby and Tom comes to a head when George Wilson (Jason Clarke), the owner of a gas station in the Valley of Ashes, seeks revenge against Gatsby for allegedly killing his wife, Myrtle. Unbeknownst to Gatsby, it was actually Daisy who was driving the car that killed Myrtle.

In the climax of the film, Tom's mistress, Myrtle, is killed in a car accident, and George Wilson mistakenly believes that Gatsby was responsible. In a fit of rage, George shoots Gatsby in his own pool, killing him. Daisy returns to Tom, and Nick moves away from Long Island, disillusioned with the excesses and superficiality of the wealthy elite.

The film ends with Nick reflecting on the tragic events that have unfolded, and the emptiness and decay of the wealthy communities he has observed. The final shot is of Gatsby's empty pool, a symbol of the lost love and the shattered dreams of the characters.

Overall, The Great Gatsby is a visually stunning and emotionally charged adaptation of Fitzgerald's classic novel, with outstanding performances from its cast. The film explores themes of love, greed, class, and the corrupting influence of wealth, set against the backdrop of the roaring twenties in New York City.

title: Extremely Loud & Incredibly Close
tagline: This is not a story about September 11th, it's a story about every day after.
overview: A year after his father's death, Oskar, a troubled young boy, discovers a mysterious key he believes was left for him by his father and embarks on a scavenger hunt to find the matching lock.
plot:
Nine-year-old Oskar Schell is autistic and lives in New York City with his parents Linda and Thomas Schell. He is close to his father, who stimulates him with missions to hunt for clues to New York City's "lost Sixth Borough". The tasks he is given force him to explore his surroundings and communicate with others, which is not easy for him.
On September 11, 2001, schools close early, so Oskar arrives home alone to find six answering machine messages left by his father from the World Trade Center. He hides under his bed, where his grandmother finds him and stays until Linda returns. Oskar is angry at his father's funeral, especially as the casket is empty, unable to make sense of his death.
A year later, Oskar has a secret hiding place with memories of his father, including the answering machine with its messages. In his father's room, he accidentally shatters a vase, and inside finds a key in an envelope with the word "Black" on it. He becomes obsessed with finding the lock the key fits, believing it a clue from his father.
Oskar finds 472 Blacks in the New York phone book, so plans to visit each one. He lies to his mother, with whom he is becoming increasingly distant, about his outings. He first meets Abby Black, who is in the starting process of a divorce, but she tells Oskar she did not know his father. Further encounters continue to be fruitless, but he meets a variety of people, photographing and recording notes on each one in a scrapbook.
One day, Oskar ventures into his grandmother's apartment, but instead of finding her there, encounters the reclusive elderly renter that has been living there, whom his grandmother had warned him to avoid. The renter does not speak, communicating instead with the words "yes" and "no" tattooed on his hands and a writing pad. Oskar confides in him, and the man offers to accompany Oskar on his outings.
As they explore the city together, Oskar learns to face his fears, such as those of public transport and bridges. Eventually, he concludes that the stranger is his grandfather. Oskar plays the increasingly desperate answering machine recordings for him, but the man becomes agitated. He refuses to listen to the final one, and tells Oskar to stop his search. Later, Oskar sees him arguing with his grandmother and packing to leave, so he angrily tries to confront him as his taxi pulls away, saying he knows he is his long-estranged grandfather.
Oskar then notices a phone number for an estate sale circled on the back of a newspaper clipping of his father's. When he dials the number, he reaches a surprised Abby, who takes Oskar to meet her ex-husband William. William realizes that Oskar's key is the one he has been looking for, which had been left to him in the vase by his own now deceased father. William had not known the key was in the vase when he had sold the vase to Oskar's father at the estate sale.

title: 47 Ronin
tagline: For courage. For loyalty. For honor.
overview: Kai—an outcast—joins Oishi, the leader of 47 outcast samurai.  Together they seek vengeance upon the treacherous overlord who killed their master and banished their kind.  To restore honour to their homeland, the warriors embark upon a quest that challenges them with a series of trials that would destroy ordinary warriors.
plot:
47 Ronin is a 2013 American fantasy action film directed by Carl Rinsch, his only theatrical feature, and written by Chris Morgan and Hossein Amini from a story by Morgan and Walter Hamada. It is a fantastical reimagining of Chūshingura, the story of the forty-seven ronin, real masterless samurai of 18th-century Japan who avenged the death of their lord, Asano Naganori, by killing his rival, Kira Yoshinaka. Keanu Reeves stars as Kai, a half-English, half-Japanese outcast, with Hiroyuki Sanada as Oishi, Tadanobu Asano as Lord Kira, Rinko Kikuchi as the witch Mizuki and Kou Shibasaki as Mika. Universal Pictures released it in December 2013.

Kai, found as a boy in a forest, is taken in by Lord Asano, the benevolent ruler of the Akō domain. He and Asano's daughter, Mika, fall in love, despite the contempt of Asano's samurai for Kai's mixed ancestry. Lord Kira, the shogun's master of ceremonies, plots to seize Akō with the help of Mizuki, a shape-shifting witch. During a hunt, a monstrous creature attacks Asano's party, and Kai kills it. When Shogun Tsunayoshi visits Akō, Kai recognizes one of Kira's concubines as the witch, but the chief counselor, Oishi, ignores his warning.

At a tournament for the shogun's entertainment, Kira's champion, a giant armored warrior, is pitted against Asano's chosen samurai, whom Mizuki incapacitates with magic. Kai fights in his place but is unmasked and beaten. That night, Mizuki bewitches Asano into attacking the unarmed Kira, and Asano is ordered to commit ritual suicide. His samurai are made ronin, forbidden to seek revenge, while Kai is sold into slavery and Mika is given a year to mourn before she must marry Kira. A year later, Oishi, released from imprisonment, gathers the scattered ronin and frees Kai, and together they seek weapons from mysterious forest demons who raised Kai, and plan to infiltrate Kira's castle during the wedding to avenge their lord, knowing that their act of loyalty will cost them their lives.

47 Ronin received negative reviews, with critics finding its fantasy elements at odds with the classic story and its characters underdeveloped, though the visuals and Sanada's performance were praised. It was a major box-office failure, grossing about $151 million worldwide against a budget estimated at over $175 million.

title: Drive
tagline: There are no clean getaways.
overview: Driver is a skilled Hollywood stuntman who moonlights as a getaway driver for criminals. plot:
Drive is a 2011 neo-noir crime thriller film directed by Nicolas Winding Refn, produced by Bold Films, and written by Hossein Amini.

The film takes place in Los Angeles, California, and follows the story of Driver (played by Ryan Gosling), a mysterious and introverted stunt driver who lives a solitary life. He is haunted by his past and struggles to form connections with others.

Driver's life changes when he meets Irene (played by Carey Mulligan), a single mother working as a waitress at a diner. She hires him to drive her and her son, Benicio (played by Kaden Leos), to a new home on the outskirts of town. Driver is drawn to Irene and begins to form a bond with her and her son.

However, their lives are disrupted when Irene's ex-boyfriend, Standard (played by Oscar Isaac), comes back into the picture. Standard is involved in a life of crime and has a history of violence. He becomes increasingly aggressive towards Irene and Benicio, putting them in danger.

As Driver tries to protect Irene and her son, he also becomes embroiled in Standard's world of crime. Driver agrees to drive Standard's partner, Bernie (played by Albert Brooks), on a series of heists, which puts him at odds with the law.

Throughout the film, Refn uses long takes and atmospheric soundscapes to create a sense of tension and unease. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the dark and gritty underbelly of Los Angeles.

As the story unfolds, Driver's past begins to surface. It is revealed that he was once involved in a violent incident with Standard, which left him with emotional scars. This backstory adds depth to Driver's character, making him more than just a stoic protagonist.

The film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Driver and Standard, which ends in tragedy. In the end, Driver must confront his own demons and make a choice that will determine the fate of Irene and Benicio.

Drive is a critically acclaimed film known for its atmospheric tension, stunning cinematography, and Ryan Gosling's nuanced performance as Driver. The film has been praised for its exploration of themes such as loneliness, violence, and redemption.

title: It's Not You, It's Me
overview: Javier se ha casado con María, el amor de su vida, y ahora lo único que desea es estar feliz con ella el resto de su vida, pero el destino se la quita poco después de la boda. plot:
It's Not You, It's Me (Spanish: No eres tú, soy yo) is a 2010 Mexican romantic comedy directed by Alejandro Springall and starring Eugenio Derbez, Alejandra Barros and Martina García, with Juan Ramírez and Alberto Estrella in supporting roles. It is a remake of the 2004 Argentine film No sos vos, soy yo, written and directed by Juan Taratuto. Produced by Matthias Ehrenberg and shot in Mexico City, it was one of Derbez's first leading roles in a feature film, several years before his international success with Instructions Not Included.

Javier Herrera is a cardiovascular surgeon who has just married his longtime partner, María, and believes their future together is secure. Shortly after the wedding, however, María tells him that she has fallen in love with someone else and is leaving him. Javier suddenly finds himself with no wife, no work, no money and no home of his own, and he is forced to start his life over from scratch.

Unable to stop thinking about María, Javier slides into a comic depression. He sees therapists and even tries esoteric treatments in search of a cure for his broken heart. Following advice that a pet will help him meet women, he adopts a dog, but his attempts to date only remind him of his ex-wife. Things begin to change when he meets Julia, a free-spirited young single mother who works at a pet shop. Julia offers him friendship and affection without conditions, and the two begin a relationship. Yet Javier remains unable to let go of his past, and when María reappears, he must decide whether to cling to the life he lost or take a chance on the future Julia represents.

The film was released in Mexican cinemas in August 2010. It closely follows the structure and humor of the Argentine original while transferring the story to Mexico City, and it gave Derbez, then best known for his sketch comedy work on television, the chance to play a more grounded romantic lead, with Alejandra Barros as the departing wife and Colombian actress Martina García as Julia.

title: Take Shelter
tagline: Far away from the cruel world.
overview: Plagued by a series of apocalyptic visions, a young husband and father questions whether to shelter his family from a coming storm, or from himself.
plot:
Take Shelter is a 2011 American psychological thriller written and directed by Jeff Nichols, starring Michael Shannon as Curtis LaForche, a young husband and father, and Jessica Chastain as his wife Samantha. The film follows a man tormented by apocalyptic visions, who must decide whether to protect his family from a coming storm or from his own fear that he is losing his mind.

In the small town of LaGrange, Ohio, Curtis, a construction worker, begins to suffer vivid nightmares and hallucinations: rain falling like motor oil, menacing flocks of birds and people close to him turning violent. He hides his visions from Samantha and their deaf daughter Hannah, instead channeling his anxiety into an obsessive project to expand the storm shelter in his backyard.

His behavior becomes increasingly strange. He cuts off people who have hurt him only in his dreams, borrows heavy equipment from his employer without permission and takes out a risky loan for the shelter without telling his wife. Aware that his mother developed paranoid schizophrenia at about his age, Curtis seeks help at a free clinic, fearing that he has inherited the illness. When Samantha discovers what he has been doing, the strain on their marriage grows, even as the family prepares for Hannah's cochlear implant surgery. Losing his job and his health insurance, alienating friends and becoming the subject of gossip in the close-knit community, Curtis is torn between his conviction that a devastating storm is coming and the possibility that the threat lies within his own mind.

The film explores mental illness, family responsibility and fear in a small working-class community, building tension through ambiguity rather than spectacle.

Take Shelter premiered at the Sundance Film Festival and won the Critics' Week Grand Prix at Cannes in 2011 before its release by Sony Pictures Classics. It received critical acclaim, with 92 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 85, and won Saturn Awards for Nichols's writing and Shannon's performance.

title: Inception: The Cobol Job
overview: The Cobol Job is a fourteen-minute animated prequel to Christopher Nolan’s award-winning movie: Inception, detailing the heist on Mr. Kaneda's mind by Nash, Cobb, Arthur, and several Cobol Engineering thugs.
plot:
Inception: The Cobol Job is a 2010 animated motion comic that serves as a prequel to Christopher Nolan's science fiction thriller Inception, leading directly into the dream heist that opens the film. Written by Jordan Goldberg and directed by Ian Kirby, it runs roughly fourteen minutes and adapts a comic illustrated by Long Vo, Joe Ng and Crystal Reid of the studio Udon. The comic was first published online on Inception's official website and on Yahoo! Movies as part of Warner Bros.' viral marketing campaign for the film, and the animated version was later included among the bonus features on the second disc of the film's Blu-ray release in December 2010.

The story opens with Cobb recalling the lessons of his mentor Miles, who taught him the art of shared dreaming and insisted that creation should be for its own sake rather than for profit. Cobb, his point man Arthur and Nash, an unreliable architect chosen only because he was available, have been hired by Cobol Engineering to extract a secret from the mind of Mr. Kaneda, a paranoid executive. The dream takes the form of a downtown district of skyscrapers, a bank and an office tower, and Cobol insists on sending along several armed thugs as "tourists" to make sure the job gets done. Early on Cobb is distracted by a vision of his late wife Mal and is nearly killed by a bus, saved only by Arthur.

While Arthur and the tourists stage a jewellery-store robbery to draw off the police, Nash guides Cobb to Kaneda's office. Cobb threatens the executive and produces a bomb, but the dream begins to collapse after Nash is killed by Kaneda's receptionist. When Kaneda finally unlocks his computer, Cobb finds that the file he wants, the RDS-1 Energy Expansion Program, is protected by a password that only its originator, Saito, knows. The bomb goes off and Cobb wakes in a hostage room guarded by Cobol's men. The firm's chief, Woodruff, reveals that the information was meant to win Fischer Morrow's backing for an oil pipeline along Africa's eastern coast. Cobb agrees to go after Saito himself, on condition that there are no tourists and only he, Arthur and Nash take part, since Saito is trained in dream-sharing and will be on guard from the start. The prequel ends as Cobb prepares the plan that becomes the opening sequence of Inception.

title: Too Big to Fail
tagline: Main Street took the fall. Wall Street got the check.
overview: An intimate look at the epochal financial crisis of 2008 and the powerful men and women who decided the fate of the world's economy in a matter of a few weeks.
plot:
Too Big to Fail is a 2011 American biographical drama television film directed by Curtis Hanson and written by Peter Gould, based on Andrew Ross Sorkin's 2009 non-fiction book of the same name. Its ensemble cast includes William Hurt as Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson and Paul Giamatti as Federal Reserve Chair Ben Bernanke, along with Edward Asner, Billy Crudup, Topher Grace, Cynthia Nixon, Bill Pullman, Tony Shalhoub and James Woods. The film premiered on HBO on May 23, 2011, and chronicles the 2008 financial crisis, centering on the collapse of the investment bank Lehman Brothers and its effects on the global economy.

In 2008, in the middle of an election year, the subprime mortgage crisis is battering investment banks loaded with real estate assets. Having already guaranteed the sale of Bear Stearns to JPMorgan Chase at a fraction of its value, Paulson is wary of another bailout and refuses to intervene as shares of Lehman Brothers plunge. Lehman's chief executive, Richard Fuld, makes a series of poor decisions, and by Friday, September 12, the bank's stock has fallen to single digits. Timothy Geithner, head of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, urges Paulson to support a merger between Lehman and Bank of America, but Paulson insists that the other major banks guarantee any deal and summons their chief executives to an emergency weekend meeting at the Federal Reserve. While they negotiate, Bank of America unexpectedly agrees to buy Merrill Lynch instead, and a last-ditch sale to the British bank Barclays is blocked by regulators in London. Lehman files for bankruptcy on September 15, and the consequences are immediate: the stock market crashes, investors pull out their money, lending freezes and the insurance giant AIG faces a liquidity crisis that threatens the entire international financial system. With Bernanke warning of another Great Depression, Paulson and his team scramble to rescue AIG and to find a way to restore credit, debating plans to buy toxic assets or to inject capital directly into the banks while trying to persuade Congress and Wall Street to cooperate.

The film received generally favorable reviews, with a 74% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 67 out of 100. It earned 11 nominations at the 63rd Primetime Emmy Awards, and Giamatti won the Screen Actors Guild Award for his portrayal of Bernanke.

plot:
Shark Night 3D is an action-thriller film that revolves around a group of college students who embark on a disastrous boat trip to a lake in search of thrills and adventure. The movie's narrative is driven by the theme of reckless abandon, as the characters' desire for excitement and freedom ultimately leads them into a perilous situation.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not with the sharks themselves, but with the characters' own flaws and weaknesses. The film expertly weaves together elements of suspense, terror, and social commentary, highlighting the dangers of peer pressure, impulsive behavior, and the consequences of underestimating the power of nature.

Throughout the movie, the characters are forced to confront their own mortality and the fragility of human life in the face of the natural world. The film's portrayal of the sharks as mindless killers serves as a metaphor for the unpredictable and often deadly forces that can be unleashed when humans overstep their boundaries.

Ultimately, Shark Night 3D is a cautionary tale about the importance of responsibility, respect, and self-awareness in the face of nature's fury. The movie's over-the-top action sequences and gruesome special effects serve as a reminder of the devastating consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

title: Green Lantern: Emerald Knights
tagline: Witness the Color of Will.
overview: As the home planet of the Green Lantern Corps faces a battle with an ancient enemy, Hal Jordan prepares new recruit Arisia for the coming conflict by relating stories of the first Green Lantern and several of Hal's comrades.
plot:
Green Lantern: Emerald Knights is a 2011 animated film that serves as a companion piece to the 2011 live-action film Green Lantern, directed by Martin Campbell. The movie takes place during the events of the original film and explores the history of the Green Lantern Corps through a series of vignettes.

The story begins with Hal Jordan (voiced by Jason O'Mara), who is struggling to come to terms with his failure as a test pilot and his subsequent recruitment into the Green Lantern Corps. He is visited by the Guardians of the Universe, who inform him that he has been chosen to be the new Green Lantern.

However, things take a turn when Hal discovers that the Guardians are planning to destroy the planet Oa, which serves as their homeworld, in order to prevent it from falling into the wrong hands. The Guardians believe that this is necessary to protect the universe from the evil Sinestro, who seeks to use the power of the yellow ring to conquer the cosmos.

As Hal tries to convince the Guardians to reconsider their decision, he is joined by other Green Lanterns, including John Stewart (voiced by Kevin Tanaka), Carol Ferris (voiced by Kyra Sedgwick), and Tom Kalmaku (voiced by Michael Dorn). Together, they embark on a series of adventures that take them across the galaxy.

One of these adventures takes Hal to the planet Poltarax, where he encounters the Green Lantern who was killed in action during the events of the original film. The Lantern's spirit is revealed to be that of Abin Sur (voiced by Nolan North), who had been a member of the Corps before his death.

Through a series of flashbacks, we learn about Abin's backstory and his struggles with the power of the ring. We also see how he came to be killed by Sinestro, who was seeking revenge against the Corps for their interference in his plans.

As Hal continues on his journey, he is joined by other Lanterns, including Laira (voiced by Mae Whitman) and Sojourner (voiced by Jennifer Hale). Together, they face off against Sinestro and his army of yellow-clad warriors.

The final battle takes place on the planet Oa, where Hal and the Guardians engage in a fierce struggle to prevent the destruction of their homeworld. In the end, it is revealed that the Guardians' plan was not entirely altruistic - they had been using the power of the ring to maintain control over the Corps for centuries.

The film ends with Hal coming to terms with his new role as a Green Lantern and his responsibilities to the Corps. He also begins to understand the true nature of the ring and its power, which he will continue to explore in future adventures.

Overall, Green Lantern: Emerald Knights is a visually stunning and action-packed film that explores the history and mythology of the Green Lantern Corps. While it may not be as well-known as some other DC Comics properties, it offers a unique perspective on the universe and its characters, and provides a compelling companion piece to the original live-action film.

title: Sexual Predator
tagline: The hunt for pleasure is the most basic instinct of all.
overview: A female parole officer unwittingly gets involved with a handsome photographer who might be a serial killer.
plot:
Sexual Predator, also known as Last Cry, is a 2001 American erotic thriller directed by Robert Angelo from a screenplay by Ed Silverstein. Produced by Marc Lawrence for Magic Hour Pictures and MRG Entertainment, with cinematography by David Trulli and music by Michael Vista, it stars Angie Everhart and Richard Grieco, with Kevin Fry, Elizabeth Barondes, Julian Christopher, Ray Valenti and Roy Abrahamson. Made for cable and home video, it belongs to the wave of softcore psychological thrillers popular in the late 1990s and early 2000s, and Angelo had already worked in the genre with films such as Mutual Needs and Forbidden Sins.

J.C. Gale (Grieco) is a photographer known for provocative erotic work. He is charged with the death of a woman who died during an act of erotic asphyxiation, and although he is found guilty, the conviction is reduced to manslaughter and he receives five years' probation. The victim was the best friend of Beth Spinella (Everhart), a probation officer who specializes in sex offenders, and she is assigned as his case officer. Beth sets out to build a sexual profile of Gale, but instead he gradually draws her into a world of erotic experiences, photographing her in his studio and taking her to a sex club, until he succeeds in seducing her. At the same time, someone begins stalking Beth, killing her cat and then murdering one of Gale's models. Her boyfriend Joe (Fry) is convinced that Gale is the killer, but Beth, fearing for her job, cannot reveal that she has been sleeping with the man she is supposed to supervise. The film ends with a twist revealing that the murderer is none of the characters the script has led the audience to suspect.

The film was released on DVD by Columbia TriStar. Critical reaction was sharply divided. Moria's Richard Scheib gave it three stars, calling it surprisingly slick and well photographed, praising the time it devotes to its plot, the unexpected complexity of its two leads and Grieco's darkly ambiguous performance, and describing the final twist as excellent, though he found it implausible that Beth would be allowed to supervise the man accused of killing her friend. Walter Chaw of Film Freak Central gave it zero stars, dismissing it as cheap and exploitative and criticizing its production values, acting, direction and screenplay.

title: Student Services
overview: Nineteen-year-old Laura is stressed by her first year at college when money worries distract her from her studies and so, desperate for cash, she answers an online advertisement for intimate companionship that leads her down a dangerous path.
plot:
Student Services (French: Mes chères études) is a 2010 French television drama written and directed by Emmanuelle Bercot, adapted from Laura D.'s autobiographical book Mes chères études (2008). Déborah François stars as a cash-strapped first-year university student who drifts into selling sex to pay for her studies. The film was first broadcast by Canal+ on January 18, 2010, and later had a theatrical release in Poland and Italy.

Laura, 19, is determined to succeed at university, but the money from her job at a call centre is not enough to live on. She faints during a lecture because she has not been eating properly, and her working-class parents cannot afford to give her more. When her electricity is cut off over unpaid bills, she searches online for extra work and finds an advertisement from Joe, a 57-year-old man offering a hundred euros an hour to a student willing to keep him company. Telling herself it will happen only once, she meets him in a hotel room three days later. She is nervous and ashamed, but the practised Joe smooths things over, telling her that it is all about fantasy and that nowadays everything, fantasy included, is for sale. His money pays her bills and even a small party, and the episode becomes the start of a downward spiral. Exhilarated by money that seems so easily earned, she tries to forget the experiences themselves and remember only the envelopes of cash, and she keeps meeting men she finds online, with Joe becoming a regular. From the second client onward she wants to stop, but she never grows used to what is demanded of her. Clients push past her limits and cheat her out of payment, among them an abusive photographer and a man who meets her in a car park, and eventually even Joe betrays her. Strained further by her relationships with her callous first love Manu and the indolent Benjamin, Laura finally breaks down.

François plays Laura, with Alain Cauchi as Joe, Benjamin Siksou as Manu, Mathieu Demy as Benjamin, Anna Sigalevitch as Fanny and Marc Chapiteau as the photographer. Produced by Les Films du Kiosque, it was shot mainly in the centre of Besançon. François later said one sex scene, in which she lay trapped beneath a very heavy naked actor, was especially hard to film. Critics praised her performance, with MaryAnn Johanson calling the film well-acted and far more sad than scandalous, but several found the screenplay unconvincing for its thin character development.

title: The Good Doctor
tagline: Do no harm.
overview: Dr. Martin Blake, who has spent his life looking for respect, meets an 18-year-old patient named Diane, suffering from a kidney infection, and gets a much-needed boost of self-esteem. plot:
The Good Doctor is a 2011 American psychological thriller directed by Lance Daly and written by John Enbom. Orlando Bloom, who also produced the film, stars as Martin Blake, an ambitious young doctor, with Riley Keough, Taraji P. Henson, Rob Morrow, Michael Peña and J. K. Simmons in supporting roles. It premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2011.

Martin Blake, a British doctor, begins his residency at a hospital in Southern California. Outwardly charming and polite, he is in fact a deeply insecure narcissist who craves respect and control over others. His aloof manner alienates the nurses, especially the experienced Nurse Theresa, whom he believes do not show him the deference he deserves, and his first encounters with patients go poorly, leaving him on uncertain ground with his superiors.

Everything changes when Diane Nixon, an eighteen-year-old patient, is admitted with a kidney infection. Martin treats her successfully, and Diane and her family treat him as a hero, giving him the admiration he craves. As Diane recovers and is about to leave the hospital, Martin, unwilling to lose her attention and the validation she provides, begins secretly tampering with her medication to keep her ill, all while presenting himself as devoted to her care. Their relationship becomes increasingly inappropriate as he continues to visit her after she returns home. His manipulations eventually spiral out of control and lead to tragedy. An orderly named Jimmy discovers evidence of what Martin has done and blackmails him, and a police detective begins investigating, forcing Martin to go to ever greater lengths to protect himself and his career while maintaining the facade of the caring, dedicated doctor.

The film received mixed reviews, with a 66 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 52. Ronnie Scheib of Variety noted the black comedy lurking beneath its suspenseful surface, with more than a hint of Lolita-esque absurdity, and Sura Wood of The Hollywood Reporter called it a tense psychosexual film. Critics generally praised Bloom's unsettling performance against type.

plot:
The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is a 2011 psychological thriller film directed by David Fincher, based on the bestselling novel of the same name by Stieg Larsson. The movie stars Daniel Craig as Mikael Blomkvist, a journalist, and Rooney Mara as Lisbeth Salander, a young hacker.

The story begins with Mikael Blomkvist, a successful but troubled journalist who has lost his job due to an article he wrote that was deemed too critical of the wealthy elite. He is approached by Henrik Vanger, the patriarch of a wealthy family in Sweden, who hires him to investigate the disappearance of his niece, Harriet, 40 years ago.

Henrik believes that Harriet's disappearance is connected to an ancient family curse and asks Blomkvist to uncover the truth. As Blomkvist delves deeper into the case, he meets Lisbeth Salander, a brilliant but troubled young hacker who has been institutionalized for her mental health issues. Despite their initial reluctance, they form an unlikely partnership to solve the mystery.

As they dig deeper, they uncover a web of dark secrets and corruption within the Vanger family, including a possible murder that may be connected to Harriet's disappearance. Lisbeth's hacking skills prove invaluable in uncovering evidence that Blomkvist would have otherwise missed.

Throughout their investigation, Blomkvist and Lisbeth develop a complex and intense relationship, with Lisbeth's troubled past slowly revealed. They face numerous obstacles, including the family's attempts to silence them and Lisbeth's own demons.

As they get closer to the truth, they discover that Harriet was not just any ordinary victim but had been involved in some shady dealings within the family. The investigation leads them to a shocking revelation: Harriet's disappearance is linked to an ancient ritual that has been passed down through generations of Vangers.

In the climactic final act, Blomkvist and Lisbeth confront the mastermind behind the ritual, who is revealed to be Henrik himself. In a stunning twist, it is revealed that Henrik had orchestrated Harriet's murder to cover up his own dark secrets and protect the family's reputation.

The film ends with Blomkvist and Lisbeth finally solving the mystery, but not without scars. Lisbeth has found a sense of purpose and belonging with Blomkvist, while he has gained a new appreciation for her unique skills and perspective. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Lisbeth finally finding some measure of peace and acceptance.

Overall, The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is a gripping thriller that explores themes of corruption, power, and redemption. With its complex characters, intricate plot, and Fincher's masterful direction, it's no wonder this film has become a modern classic in the world of cinema.

title: Happy Feet Two
tagline: Every step counts.
overview: Mumble the penguin has a problem: his son Erik, who is reluctant to dance, encounters The Mighty Sven, a penguin who can fly! Things get worse for Mumble when the world is shaken by powerful forces, causing him to brings together the penguin nations and their allies to set things right.
plot:
Happy Feet Two is a 2011 animated musical comedy-drama film produced by Warner Bros. Animation and directed by George Miller, the director of the original Happy Feet.

The movie takes place two years after the events of the first film. Mumble (voiced by Elijah Wood), the tap-dancing Emperor Penguin, has become an international celebrity for his unique talent. However, with fame comes pressure to conform to traditional penguin norms, and Mumble struggles to balance his love for dance with the expectations of his colony.

The story begins with Mumble's father, Ramón (voiced by Hugo Weaving), who is struggling to find a suitable mate for his son due to Mumble's unusual appearance. Meanwhile, a new threat emerges in the form of a group of Adelie penguins from Antarctica, led by the ruthless and cunning Adelie (voiced by Brittany Murphy). The Adelies are determined to take over the Antarctic ice sheet and destroy the Emperor Penguins' home.

As Mumble navigates his relationships with his family and friends, he also discovers that he has a special connection to the Adelies. He learns that they possess a unique genetic trait that allows them to survive in the harsh Antarctic environment. However, this trait comes at a cost: it makes them aggressive and violent towards other penguins.

Mumble soon realizes that his tap-dancing abilities are not just a quirk, but a key to understanding the Adelies' behavior. He uses his dance moves to communicate with the Adelies and learn more about their motivations. Along the way, he befriends a young Adelie named Erik (voiced by Robyn Moore), who becomes his ally in the fight against the Adelies.

As tensions between the Emperors and Adelies escalate, Mumble must use his unique talents to bring peace to the two groups. He performs an epic dance battle with the Adelies, using his tap-dancing skills to outsmart and outmaneuver them. The dance battle is a thrilling display of penguin agility and creativity, showcasing the unique abilities of each species.

In the end, Mumble's efforts pay off, and the Emperors and Adelies are able to coexist peacefully. The movie concludes with Mumble returning home to his colony, where he is celebrated as a hero for his bravery and ingenuity. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Mumble's message of acceptance and understanding resonating throughout the penguin community.

Overall, Happy Feet Two is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, community, and the power of dance to bring people together. With its stunning animation, catchy musical numbers, and lovable characters, it is a must-see for fans of animated films and music lovers alike.
