plot:
Beavis and Butt-Head open the film with a special cameo, and an explanation of 3D technology. In a matter typical for the characters, they start arguing and quickly get into a slap-fight, with several of the moves especially animated to come out of the screen in a 3D setting. The opening sequence features each of the cast members lining up, standing in each color of the rainbow, while an operatic version of the Jackass theme song "Corona" plays. Once Johnny Knoxville introduces the film, each cast member does small stunts by various objects in slow-motion to the tune of "The Kids Are Back" by Twisted Sister. The opening sequence, as well as many of the stunts, were filmed with Phantom high speed cameras, which shoot at 1,000 frames per second.
The most notable stunts and pranks include: Johnny Knoxville being camouflage-painted as a bull charges at him; Bam Margera falling into a pit filled with snakes while attempting to prank director and producer Jeff Tremaine; Ryan Dunn and Steve-O playing instruments while a male sheep rams them; Steve-O drinking Preston Lacy's sweat after riding an elliptical machine; Bam gluing his hands to Preston Lacy and Phil Margera's chest with super glue; Ehren McGhehey getting his crooked tooth pulled by Bam's Lamborghini; Dave England playing tetherball with a beehive against Steve-O; Preston Lacy getting a football kicked into his face by professional NFL kicker Josh Brown; Wee Man participating in a bar brawl with other little people; and Chris Pontius flying an RC helicopter while it is tied to his penis.
The final stunt involves Steve-O being launched high into the air while inside a full port-a-potty connected to bungee cords. The following closing skit is done in a similar fashion as the introduction, as Knoxville announces he's about to "end the movie", then triggers an old-fashioned dynamite plunger; after the rest of the crew is disappointed by the initial explosion being a mere puff of air out of a nearby piñata, everything in the room is destroyed in a series of large explosions, as the blown-up objects are thrown at the cast (like the opening, all shown in slow-motion) to the tune of Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture. After the explosions are finished, the cast members are flushed away by a wave pool. As in the past two Jackass films, comedian Rip Taylor makes an appearance before the credits roll, celebrating the end of the film in overly dramatic fashion.

title: Arctic Predator
overview: A team searching for a long-lost ship in the Arctic unwittingly unleash an alien creature that looks like it's made of ice.
plot:
Arctic Predator, released in the United States as Frost Giant, is a 2010 science fiction horror thriller made for television, directed by Víctor García from a screenplay by Rafael Jordan and produced by UFO Films and Arctic Productions. It stars Dean Cain, the former television Superman, as J.C., the dedicated leader of an expedition searching the Arctic for a lost ship, with Steven Waddington, Lucy Brown and Louisa Clein in supporting roles.

J.C. and his small team of explorers and scientists are hunting for the wreck of a 19th-century sailing ship that vanished in the ice near an Arctic island nearly two hundred years earlier. J.C.'s interest is personal: the ship was captained by one of his distant ancestors, and his own life comes to mirror that of his forefather. When the team finally locates the frozen vessel and begins carefully thawing its centuries-old artefacts, they unwittingly release something that has been entombed in the ice alongside it: an alien creature that appears to be made of ice itself.

Once free, the creature begins stalking the members of the expedition one by one at their isolated base, killing them to absorb the heat and energy it needs to recover its strength and return to where it came from, and leaving its victims frozen solid. As a violent storm cuts the survivors off, a desperate attempt to escape by helicopter ends when the injured pilot crashes, and the team is forced to improvise crude solutions, at one point cauterising a wound with a household iron. J.C. must find a way to stop the monster before it kills everyone and reaches the mainland.

The cast also includes Mike Johnson, Laia Gonzàlez, Iliana Lazarova, Mike Straub, Erbi Ago and Velizar Binev. Reviews were largely negative. Critics described it as a low-budget stalk-and-slay picture borrowing heavily from The Thing, with a creature reminiscent of the Predator; Dread Central found it blandly assembled and frequently tedious, while others criticised its cheap computer-generated effects, repetitive deaths and stock characters. The Exploding Helicopter blog nonetheless singled out the subplot linking the hero to the ship's captain as one genuinely good idea, and several reviewers felt Cain did what he could with weak material.

title: Think Like a Man
tagline: Let the mind games begin.
overview: The balance of power in four couples’ relationships is upset when the women start using the advice in Steve Harvey’s book, Act Like A Lady, Think Like A Man, to get more of what they want from their men. When the men realize that the women have gotten a hold of their relationship “playbook,” they decide that the best defense is a good offense and come up with a plan to use this information to their advantage.
plot:
Think Like a Man is a 2012 American romantic comedy directed by Tim Story, written by Keith Merryman and David A. Newman and produced by Will Packer. It is based on comedian Steve Harvey's 2009 relationship advice book Act Like a Lady, Think Like a Man. The ensemble cast includes Kevin Hart, Meagan Good, Jerry Ferrara, Regina Hall, Michael Ealy, Terrence J, Taraji P. Henson, Romany Malco, Chris Brown and Gabrielle Union.

The film follows four couples in Los Angeles whose stories are presented through archetypes drawn from Harvey's book: "The Mama's Boy" and "The Single Mom", "The Non-Committer" and "The Girl Who Wants the Ring", "The Dreamer" and "The Woman Who Is Her Own Man", and "The Player" and "The 90 Day Rule Girl". The men are a group of friends who play basketball together, while each of the women turns to Harvey's book for guidance in dealing with the men in her life.

Following the book's advice, the women begin to gain the upper hand in their relationships, setting rules and pushing their partners to change. When the men discover the source of the women's sudden insight, they obtain copies of the book and try to use its advice to turn the tables on their partners, a strategy that soon backfires. As the romantic games escalate, each couple must confront what they really want, and the men and women learn that honesty and compromise matter more than any strategy.

Production took place in Los Angeles and Culver City, California, in 2011, and the film includes cameo appearances by several professional basketball players, including Lisa Leslie, Metta World Peace and Matt Barnes, who appear as themselves, while Harvey's book is central to the plot.

Think Like a Man was released by Screen Gems on April 20, 2012, and was a major box office success, grossing 96.1 million dollars worldwide on a budget of 12.5 million dollars and ending The Hunger Games' four-week run at the top of the North American box office. Reviews were mixed, with 55 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 51. A sequel, Think Like a Man Too, was released in 2014.

title: Glee: The Concert Movie
tagline: The embodiment of popular culture.
overview: A concert documentary shot during the Glee Live! In Concert! summer 2011 tour, featuring song performances and Glee fans' life stories and how the show influenced them.
plot:
Glee: The Concert Movie is a musical comedy-drama film that explores the themes of self-discovery, friendship, and the power of music to bring people together. The movie follows the glee club members as they prepare for their concert, navigating personal struggles, relationships, and conflicts along the way.

At its core, Glee: The Concert Movie is a story about finding one's identity and voice, both literally and figuratively. The characters are on a journey of self-discovery, trying to figure out who they are and where they fit in. Through their experiences with music, they learn valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and the importance of embracing their individuality.

The movie also explores the theme of community and the impact that music can have on people's lives. The glee club is more than just a group of friends singing together; it's a support system, a safe space where they can be themselves and express themselves freely. As they prepare for their concert, they learn to come together as a team, supporting each other through the ups and downs of life.

Furthermore, Glee: The Concert Movie touches on the theme of social hierarchy and cliques. The characters are often divided into different groups, with some struggling to fit in or find their place within the group. However, through music, they learn to bridge these gaps and form connections with others who may seem different from them.

Overall, Glee: The Concert Movie is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of music and the importance of finding one's voice and community.

title: The Guard
tagline: The FBI are about to discover that things work a little differently around here.
overview: When a small-town Irish cop with a crass personality is partnered with a straight-laced FBI agent to bust an international drug-trafficking ring, they must settle their differences in order to take down a dangerous gang.
plot:
Sergeant Gerry Boyle is an officer of the Garda Síochána (police) in the Connemara district in the west of Ireland. He is crass and confrontational, regularly indulging in drugs and alcohol even while on duty. He is also shown to be well read and highly intelligent as well as having a softer side, showing concern for his ailing mother, Eileen.
Boyle and his new subordinate, Aidan McBride, investigate a murder, with evidence apparently pointing to an occult serial killer. Shortly after, Boyle attends a briefing by an American Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) agent Wendell Everett, sent to liaise with the Garda in hunting four Irish drug traffickers led by Francis Sheehy-Skeffington, who is believed to be awaiting a massive seaborne delivery of cocaine from Jamaica. Boyle recognises one of the men in Everett's presentation as the victim of the murder he and McBride had been investigating. McBride pulls over a car driven by Sheehy and his lieutenants Clive Cornell and Liam O'Leary and is shot dead. McBride's wife, Gabriela, reports McBride's disappearance to Boyle, who promises to look into it.
The strait-laced Everett suggests that he and the unorthodox Boyle team up to track down Sheehy and his men. Everett makes the rounds, encountering Irish-speaking residents who pretend not to understand English rather than deal with an outsider. Boyle has a sexual encounter with a pair of sex workers at a hotel in town. On his way back from the hotel, Boyle spots McBride's Garda car at a "suicide hotspot" along the coast but does not believe that McBride killed himself. Gabriela, an immigrant from Croatia, tells Boyle that McBride is gay and that she married him to obtain an Irish visa as well as to make McBride "look respectable".
Meeting Everett at a local pub, Boyle notices a closed-circuit television camera and remembers that the original suspect in the murder case claimed to be frequenting it at the time of the killing. Looking over the footage from the time of the murder, they see that the suspect's alibi is valid – and Everett also spots Sheehy and Cornell at the pub. Cornell delivers a payoff to the Garda inspectors to keep them off the case and is warned that Boyle "is too unpredictable". After Sheehy meets with Boyle to half-heartedly attempt blackmail and then to offer a bribe, both are refused. Tipped off by a young boy named Eugene, Boyle discovers a cache of weapons hidden in the bog by the Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) and says he will arrange its return. (It is later revealed that Boyle kept a few of the guns.) Shortly after having her last wish to hear a live pub band fulfilled, Boyle's mother kills herself by overdosing on pills.
Meeting at the bar again, Everett tells Boyle that Garda sources indicate Sheehy's shipment will be coming into County Cork and that he is leaving to investigate. Returning home, Boyle is confronted in his living room by O'Leary, who has been ordered by Sheehy to murder him.

plot:
Escape from Planet Earth is a 3D animated science fiction comedy film directed by Cal Brunker and produced by The Weinstein Company, Blue Sky Studios, and eOne Films. Released on March 9, 2012, the movie follows the story of Scorch Supernova, an astronaut who embarks on a perilous journey to rescue his son, Gary, from the clutches of an evil alien overlord.

The film begins with Scorch (voiced by Brendan Fraser) and his wife, Bonnie (voiced by Sarah Jessica Parker), living on Earth with their young son, Gary. However, when Gary is kidnapped by the evil alien, Zorgon (voiced by John Cleese), who seeks to use him as a pawn in his plan for intergalactic domination, Scorch sets out on an epic journey to rescue his son.

Scorch's spaceship, the "Mother Ship," is destroyed, and he crash-lands on the planet Earth. With the help of a group of eccentric and lovable aliens, including Gary (voiced by Tom Cavanagh), B.O.B. (voiced by Ken Jeong), and Rastapopoulos (voiced by Seth MacFarlane), Scorch navigates through the dangers of Earth's surface to reach Zorgon's fortress.

As Scorch faces various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and human adversaries, he also learns valuable lessons about his son and himself. Along the way, Gary grows up and becomes more confident in his abilities, eventually helping his father on their quest.

The climax of the movie features an epic battle between Scorch's team and Zorgon's minions. In the end, Scorch and his allies successfully defeat Zorgon, rescue Gary, and return to Earth as heroes.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a mix of humor, action, and heartwarming moments. The voice cast delivers memorable performances, bringing depth and emotion to their characters.

Overall, Escape from Planet Earth is an entertaining and family-friendly adventure that explores themes of love, perseverance, and self-discovery. While it may not be as well-known as some other animated films, it has its own unique charm and is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

title: Death Note Relight 2: L's Successors

overview: After the events of the first movie Yagami Light faces two new adversaries as he is trying to create a perfect world without crime or criminals. This movie continues the first tv special and is a summary of the last 12 episodes of the tv anime
plot:
Death Note Relight 2: L's Successors (Japanese: Desu Nōto Riraito 2: L o Tsugu Mono) is a Japanese animated television film, the second of two compilation films condensing the anime series Death Note, which was directed by Tetsurō Araki at Madhouse and based on the manga by Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata. It follows Death Note Relight: Visions of a God, which aired in August 2007 and was advertised as the complete conclusion; the popularity of the series prompted this second special, which summarizes the second part of the anime, roughly its last dozen episodes. The voice cast includes Mamoru Miyano, Kappei Yamaguchi, Shidō Nakamura, Aya Hirano, Noriko Hidaka as Near and Masaya Matsukaze as Teru Mikami.

The story picks up after the death of the detective L. High school prodigy turned college student Light Yagami, who has been secretly killing criminals as "Kira" with a supernatural notebook that kills anyone whose name is written in it, now leads the Japanese Kira investigation as the new L, while the shinigami Ryuk watches in amusement. Years later, with cults worshipping Kira, two young potential successors to L emerge: Near, who works with the United States government, and Mello, who obtains a Death Note of his own and turns it against Near's team; the hunt for Mello costs Light's father, Soichiro, his life. As suspicion falls once more on Misa Amane, Light passes her notebook to the fervent Kira supporter Teru Mikami and makes the newscaster Kiyomi Takada Kira's public spokesperson. Mello kidnaps Takada, who kills him before Light silences her. Near then arranges a meeting between Light and the remaining task force members, where Mikami tries to kill them all, but his notebook has been replaced with a decoy. Exposed as Kira and badly wounded, Light begs Ryuk for help, but the shinigami writes Light's name in his own notebook, as he had promised when they first met.

The film was broadcast by Nippon Television on 22 August 2008, nearly a year after the first Relight special. Like its predecessor, it reworks the material rather than simply replaying it, adding and omitting scenes; it contains more new footage than the first special and drops the mafia subplot, concentrating on the confrontation between Kira and L's successors Near and Mello. The original series, broadcast from October 2006 to June 2007, is widely acclaimed.

title: Iron Man 3
tagline: Unleash the power behind the armor.
overview: When Tony Stark's world is torn apart by a formidable terrorist called the Mandarin, he starts an odyssey of rebuilding and retribution.
plot:
At a New Year's Eve party in 1999, Tony Stark meets scientist Maya Hansen, the inventor of Extremis, an experimental regenerative treatment that allows recovery from crippling injuries. Disabled scientist Aldrich Killian offers them a place in his company Advanced Idea Mechanics (A.I.M.), but Stark rejects him. Thirteen years later, Stark is suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder and has frequent panic attacks due to his experiences during the alien invasion of New York. He has built dozens of new Iron Man suits to cope with his insomnia, creating friction with his girlfriend Pepper Potts.
Meanwhile, a string of bombings is claimed by a terrorist known as the Mandarin. Stark's security chief Happy Hogan is badly injured in one such attack and is put into a coma, prompting Stark to issue a televised threat to the Mandarin, revealing his home address in the process. The Mandarin sends gunship helicopters to destroy Stark's home. Hansen, who came to warn Stark, survives the attack with Potts. Stark escapes in an experimental new Iron Man suit, which his artificial intelligence J.A.R.V.I.S. pilots to rural Tennessee, following a flight plan from Stark's investigation into the Mandarin. Stark's new armor is not fully functional and lacks sufficient power to return to Malibu, leading the world to believe that he died.
With the help of Harley Keener, a local boy, Stark investigates the remains of a local explosion bearing the hallmarks of a Mandarin attack. However, it occurred years before any known attack by a terrorist. He discovers the "bombings" were triggered by soldiers subjected to Extremis whose bodies explosively rejected the treatment, and were falsely attributed by A.I.M. as a terrorist plot to cover up Extremis' flaws. Stark witnesses Extremis firsthand when Mandarin agents Savin and Brandt attack him. Stark kills Brandt and incapacitates Savin. Meanwhile, Killian resurfaces and kidnaps Potts with assistance from Hansen. American intelligence agencies continue to search for the Mandarin, with James Rhodes—the former War Machine, now re-branded as the Iron Patriot—lured into a trap to steal his armor.
Tracing the Mandarin to Miami, Stark infiltrates his headquarters using improvised weapons. Inside, he discovers the Mandarin is English actor Trevor Slattery, who is oblivious to the actions carried out in his image. Killian, the mastermind behind Slattery's cover, captures Stark. Killian, who appropriated Hansen's Extremis research as a cure for his own disability and expanded the program to include injured war veterans, reveals he has subjected Potts to Extremis in the hope Stark will help fix Extremis' flaws while trying to save her. When Hansen betrays Killian by threatening to jeopardize his operations, Killian kills her.
Stark escapes and reunites with Rhodes, discovering that Killian intends to attack President Ellis aboard Air Force One, using the Iron Patriot armor, controlled by Savin.

overview: Freddie, a volatile, heavy-drinking veteran who suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder, finds some semblance of a family when he stumbles onto the ship of Lancaster Dodd, the charismatic leader of a new "religion" he forms after World War II.
plot:
The Master is a 2012 American period psychological drama film written and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, starring Joaquin Phoenix as Freddie Quell, a troubled World War II Navy veteran, and Philip Seymour Hoffman as Lancaster Dodd, the charismatic leader of a movement called The Cause, with Amy Adams, Laura Dern and Jesse Plemons in supporting roles. Its inspirations included Scientology founder L. Ron Hubbard, Thomas Pynchon's novel V., John Huston's documentary about traumatized veterans Let There Be Light, and stories told to Anderson by Jason Robards. Produced by Annapurna Pictures and Ghoulardi Film Company and distributed by The Weinstein Company, it was shot almost entirely on 65 mm film, the first fiction feature shot and released in 70 mm since Hamlet in 1996.

In 1950, Freddie is a violent, sex-obsessed alcoholic who drifts from job to job, losing work as a department store photographer after a fight and fleeing a California farm when a colleague collapses after drinking his homemade liquor. In San Francisco he stows away on the yacht of one of Dodd's followers, and Dodd takes an interest in him, invites him to stay for his daughter's wedding and develops a taste for his potent moonshine. Dodd subjects Freddie to "processing", an intense series of psychological questions that brings him to tears over Doris, a girl he left behind at home. Freddie joins Dodd's family as they spread The Cause along the East Coast, but his loyalty takes the form of violence against anyone who challenges his mentor, troubling Dodd's wife Peggy, while Dodd's son Val confides that his father is making it up as he goes. After Dodd is arrested for practicing medicine without qualifications and Freddie attacks the police, the two clash furiously in their jail cells before reconciling, even as members of the movement come to fear Freddie. Dodd insists that rigorous conditioning can cure him, but Freddie struggles to submit, and he eventually rides off alone into the desert during a game on a salt flat, though the two men's story is not yet over.

The film premiered at the Venice Film Festival, winning the Silver Lion for Anderson's direction and a shared Volpi Cup for Phoenix and Hoffman, and opened in the United States on September 14, 2012, to wide acclaim. It received three Academy Award nominations, for Phoenix, Hoffman and Adams.

title: Elysium
tagline: He can save us all.
overview: In the year 2159, two classes of people exist: the very wealthy who live on a pristine man-made space station called Elysium, and the rest, who live on an overpopulated, ruined Earth. Secretary Rhodes, a hard line government ofﬁcial, will stop at nothing to enforce anti-immigration laws and preserve the luxurious lifestyle of the citizens of Elysium. That doesn’t stop the people of Earth from trying to get in, by any means they can. When unlucky Max is backed into a corner, he agrees to take on a daunting mission that, if successful, will not only save his life, but could bring equality to these polarized worlds.
plot:
Elysium is a 2013 science fiction action film directed by Neill Blomkamp and produced by TriStar Pictures and Sony Pictures. The movie takes place in a dystopian future where the world has been ravaged by poverty, crime, and corruption.

The story follows Max Da Costa (played by Matt Damon), a former soldier who works as a cleaner on the spaceship Elysium, a luxurious space station that serves as a refuge for the wealthy and powerful. The ship is home to the ruling class, who live in opulence and luxury, while the rest of humanity is left to struggle on Earth.

Max's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Frey (played by Sharlto Copley), a fellow cleaner who has been injured during a botched assassination attempt. Max helps Frey escape from the ship's security forces, and in return, Frey gives Max a tour of Elysium and reveals its true nature.

As they explore the ship, Max learns that Elysium is actually a prison for the wealthy and powerful, who have escaped the chaos on Earth by fleeing to the ship. The ruling class has created a system where they can live in luxury while the rest of humanity is left to suffer on a desolate and polluted Earth.

Max becomes determined to take revenge against the people responsible for his sister's death, which was caused by the corrupt government that allowed the wealthy to escape to Elysium. He teams up with Frey and a group of rebels, including Tsele (played by Jodie Foster), a high-ranking official on Elysium who has grown disillusioned with the ship's ruling class.

As Max and his team plan their attack on Elysium, they realize that the only way to reach the ship is through a small airlock that can be opened for a limited time. The team must navigate the ship's security systems and fight off the ruling class's henchmen in order to reach the upper levels of the ship.

The final confrontation takes place on the upper deck of Elysium, where Max and his team face off against the ship's ruler, President Patrick Shaw (played by William Fichtner). In a tense showdown, Max manages to defeat Shaw and destroy the airlock, allowing him and Frey to escape from the ship.

However, as they make their way back to Earth, Max realizes that he has become a symbol of hope for the oppressed people on the planet. He decides to stay on Earth and fight for justice, using his newfound status to bring about change and equality.

The movie ends with Max standing on the surface of Earth, looking out at the desolate landscape, but also seeing a glimmer of hope for a better future. The final shot is of Elysium, now empty and abandoned, a symbol of the corrupt system that has been brought down by Max's actions.

Overall, Elysium is a thought-provoking sci-fi action film that explores themes of class struggle, corruption, and redemption. The movie features impressive visuals and a gripping storyline, making it a must-see for fans of science fiction and action movies.

title: Pacific Rim
tagline: To fight monsters, we created monsters.
overview: As war between humankind and monstrous sea creatures wages on, a former pilot and a trainee are paired up to drive a seemingly obsolete special weapon in a desperate effort to save the world.
plot:
Pacific Rim is a science fiction monster film directed by Guillermo del Toro and written by Travis Beacham. The movie takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where humanity is on the brink of extinction due to an invasion by giant monsters known as Kaijus from another dimension.

The story begins with a flashback of a catastrophic event that occurred 30 years ago, when a group of scientists discovered a way to harness the power of the Earth's core to create massive robots called Jaegers. The Jaegers are designed to fight against the Kaijus, which are enormous creatures that emerge from a portal in the ocean and wreak havoc on coastal cities.

The movie then jumps forward to the present day, where we meet our protagonist, Raleigh Becket (played by Charlie Hunnam), a former Jaeger pilot who lost his co-pilot and best friend, Yancy, during a mission. Raleigh is haunted by guilt and grief over Yancy's death and struggles to find purpose in his life.

Raleigh is recruited by the Jaeger program, led by Dr. Newton Geiszler (played by Idris Elba), who has developed a new technology that allows humans to control the Jaegers using brain-computer interfaces. Raleigh is paired with Mako Mori (played by Rinko Kikuchi), a young and talented pilot from Japan.

As they prepare for their first mission together, Raleigh and Mako are tasked with fighting against a Kaiju known as Gipsy Danger, which is terrorizing the city of San Francisco. The Jaegers are massive machines that require two pilots to operate, one on each side of the machine. The pilots must work in tandem to control the Jaeger's movements and attacks.

The battle against Gipsy Danger is intense and chaotic, with both Raleigh and Mako struggling to coordinate their efforts. Despite their differences, they begin to develop a bond as they fight for their lives.

As the movie progresses, we learn that the Kaijus are not just mindless monsters, but are actually creatures from another dimension that feed on human emotions. The Jaegers are designed to harness the power of the Earth's core to create energy blasts that can kill the Kaijus.

The final battle takes place in Hong Kong, where Raleigh and Mako face off against a massive Kaiju known as Knifehead. The fight is epic and intense, with both sides suffering heavy losses. In the end, Raleigh and Mako emerge victorious, but not without sacrifices.

The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Raleigh and Mako reflecting on their experiences and the bond they formed during their mission. Raleigh finally finds closure and purpose in his life, and we see him and Mako flying off into the sunset together.

Overall, Pacific Rim is an action-packed and visually stunning film that explores themes of grief, loss, and redemption. The movie features impressive practical effects and a talented cast, making it a must-see for fans of science fiction and monster movies.

title: Trance
tagline: Don't be a hero.
overview: A violent gang enlists the help of a hypnotherapist in an attempt to locate a painting which somehow vanished in the middle of a heist.
plot:
Trance is a psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of human psychology, exploring the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The film's narrative is layered with themes of identity, deception, and the power dynamics at play in relationships.

At its core, Trance is a story about the fragility of human perception and how easily it can be manipulated. The main character, Aaron (played by James McAvoy), is a charismatic art auctioneer who becomes embroiled in a complex web of deceit and manipulation. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems, and the lines between reality and fantasy are constantly shifting.

The film also explores the theme of identity, particularly in relation to Aaron's dual personas. His ability to adopt different identities and personas raises questions about the nature of self and how easily it can be manipulated by external forces. This theme is further complicated by his relationships with those around him, including his girlfriend, Sophie (played by Rosamund Pike), and his rival, Izzy (played by Vincent Cassel).

Furthermore, Trance examines the power dynamics at play in relationships, particularly in the context of art and commerce. The film's portrayal of the high-stakes world of art auctioneering highlights the ways in which people will do whatever it takes to get what they want, even if it means manipulating or deceiving others.

Overall, Trance is a thought-provoking thriller that explores the complexities of human psychology and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. Its themes of identity, deception, and power dynamics are expertly woven throughout the narrative, creating a tense and suspenseful viewing experience.

title: Oz the Great and Powerful
tagline: In Oz, nothing is what it seems.
overview: Oscar Diggs, a small-time circus illusionist and con-artist, is whisked from Kansas to the Land of Oz where the inhabitants assume he's the great wizard of prophecy, there to save Oz from the clutches of evil.
plot:
Oz the Great and Powerful is a 2013 American fantasy adventure film directed by Sam Raimi and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is set in the late 19th century, about 20 years before the events of L. Frank Baum's classic novel "The Wonderful Wizard of Oz".

The story begins with Oscar Diggs (James Franco), a charming but unscrupulous magician who travels from town to town performing illusions and swindling people out of their money. One day, he arrives in Kansas, where he meets a young girl named Dorothy Gale (Mila Kunis) and her dog Toto. However, instead of being charmed by Oscar's tricks, Dorothy is skeptical of his abilities.

Despite his initial failure to impress Dorothy, Oscar soon finds himself drawn into the world of Oz, which is threatened by the evil witch Mombasa (Michelle Williams). The witches are a group of powerful sorceresses who rule over different regions of Oz, and they are at odds with each other. Mombasa seeks to overthrow the ruling council of witches and take control of the entire land.

As Oscar navigates this new world, he meets three witches - Glinda (Rachel Weisz), the Good Witch of the North; China Girl (Lindsay Duncan), a witch from the East; and the Wicked Witch of the West (Julianne Moore), Mombasa's sister. The witches are wary of Oscar's intentions, but they also see an opportunity to use him as a pawn in their struggle for power.

Oscar soon discovers that he has a special connection to Oz, which is revealed when he touches a magical crystal. This connection allows him to tap into the land's magic and perform incredible feats. However, it also makes him vulnerable to the witches' manipulation.

As the story unfolds, Oscar becomes embroiled in the conflict between the witches and must decide where his loyalties lie. Along the way, he forms a bond with Dorothy, who is struggling to find her place in Oz. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Mombasa's plans and save the land from destruction.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Oscar and Mombasa, with the fate of Oz hanging in the balance. In the end, Oscar emerges victorious, but not without scars. He realizes that his connection to Oz has changed him, and he must come to terms with his new role as a hero.

Throughout the movie, Raimi explores themes of power, identity, and redemption. Oscar's journey is one of self-discovery, as he learns to harness his magic and find his place in the world. The film also features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and memorable performances from its cast.

Overall, Oz the Great and Powerful is a captivating tale that expands on the classic Wizard of Oz story while maintaining its essence. With its rich characters, engaging plot, and breathtaking visuals, it's a must-see for fans of fantasy adventure films.

title: Silence
tagline: Sometimes silence is the deadliest sound.
overview: Two Jesuit priests travel to seventeenth century Japan which has, under the Tokugawa shogunate, banned Catholicism and almost all foreign contact.
plot:
Silence is a 2016 American epic drama film directed by Martin Scorsese, based on the 1967 novel of the same name by Shusaku Endo. The film stars Andrew Garfield, Adam Driver, and Liam Neeson.

The story takes place in the late 17th century, during the Edo period in Japan. The plot follows two Jesuit priests, Father Ferdinand (Adam Driver) and Father Garrpe (Liam Neeson), who are sent to Japan by their superior, Father Valdés (John Iserey), to find their missing companion, Father Rodrigues (Andrew Garfield).

Father Rodrigues had been in Japan for 16 years, studying the local language and culture. He was last seen on a ship that sailed from Portugal, bound for Japan. The two priests are tasked with finding him and bringing back any information they can gather about his fate.

Upon their arrival in Japan, the priests are met with hostility by the Japanese authorities, who view Christianity as a threat to their country's traditions and way of life. The priests are forced to go into hiding, using disguises and assumed identities to avoid detection.

As they journey through rural Japan, the priests encounter various challenges, including poverty, hunger, and illness. They also meet with local villagers, who are often skeptical of their intentions but eventually warm up to them.

Meanwhile, Father Rodrigues is revealed to be alive, having been captured by Japanese authorities and subjected to torture and forced conversion. He has become a devout follower of the Shinto faith, and his experiences have left him traumatized and disillusioned with Christianity.

The priests are reunited with Father Rodrigues, who shares his story with them. However, their reunion is short-lived, as they soon discover that Rodrigues' experiences have changed him profoundly. He is no longer the man he once was, and his faith has been shaken to its core.

As the story unfolds, Scorsese explores themes of faith, doubt, and redemption. The priests are forced to confront the harsh realities of their mission in Japan, where they must navigate a complex web of cultural and religious differences.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a tragic conclusion, as Father Rodrigues is forced to make a choice between his faith and his life. The ending is both heartbreaking and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the complexities of faith and redemption in a world torn apart by conflict and uncertainty.

Overall, Silence is a powerful and moving film that explores themes of faith, doubt, and redemption in a richly detailed and atmospheric setting. Scorsese's direction is masterful, using long takes and sweeping cinematography to create a sense of scope and scale that is both breathtaking and humbling.

title: Argo
tagline: The movie was fake. The mission was real.
overview: As the Iranian revolution reaches a boiling point, a CIA 'exfiltration' specialist concocts a risky plan to free six Americans who have found shelter at the home of the Canadian ambassador.
plot:
Argo is a 2012 American thriller film directed by Ben Affleck, written by Chris Terrio, and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The film is based on the true story of the CIA's rescue of six American diplomats from Iran during the 1979 hostage crisis. The story begins in November 1979, when a group of Iranian students storm the American embassy in Tehran, taking several American diplomats hostage. The situation escalates, and the United States government decides to send a team of CIA operatives to rescue the hostages.

The CIA identifies six Americans who are still in the country: Ambassador Bruce Laingen, his wife, and four other diplomats. However, due to the sensitive nature of their work, they cannot be extracted directly from Iran. Instead, the CIA comes up with a plan to use a Canadian filmmaker named John Chambers to pose as a Canadian film crew.

The CIA creates a fake movie production company called "Canada Films" and sends Chambers to Tehran to pretend to be filming a science fiction movie. The plan is for Chambers to gain the trust of the Iranian authorities, who are eager to cooperate with the Canadians in exchange for concessions on the hostage crisis.

Chambers meets with the Iranian officials and convinces them that he needs access to the American embassy to film a scene. He gains permission to enter the embassy, where he meets with the six American diplomats who are still being held captive. Chambers pretends to be filming a movie, but in reality, he is gathering information about the hostages' location and working with the CIA to come up with a plan for their rescue.

As the situation becomes more dire, Chambers realizes that his cover has been blown, and the Iranians have discovered that he is not who he claims to be. He must use all of his wits and charm to convince the Iranians that he is still a legitimate filmmaker, while also working with the CIA to come up with a plan for the rescue.

The film's climax features a tense and suspenseful sequence in which Chambers and the CIA operatives work together to extract the six American diplomats from Iran. The operation is fraught with danger, but ultimately, it is successful, and the hostages are safely evacuated.

Argo was widely praised by critics and audiences alike, and it won several awards, including three Academy Awards for Best Picture, Best Adapted Screenplay, and Best Film Editing. The film's success can be attributed to its gripping storyline, well-developed characters, and outstanding performances from the cast, particularly Ben Affleck as John Chambers.

Overall, Argo is a thrilling and suspenseful film that tells an incredible true story of bravery and ingenuity in the face of danger.

title: Warcraft
tagline: Two worlds. One home.
overview: The peaceful realm of Azeroth stands on the brink of war as its civilization faces a fearsome race of invaders: orc warriors fleeing their dying home to colonize another. As a portal opens to connect the two worlds, one army faces destruction and the other faces extinction. From opposing sides, two heroes are set on a collision course that will decide the fate of their family, their people, and their home.
plot:
Warcraft (also known as Warcraft: The Beginning) is a 2016 American action fantasy film based on Blizzard Entertainment's video game series, directed by Duncan Jones, who co-wrote it with Charles Leavitt. It stars Travis Fimmel as the human commander Anduin Lothar, Paula Patton as the half-orc Garona, Ben Foster as the guardian Medivh, Dominic Cooper as King Llane Wrynn and Toby Kebbell as the orc chieftain Durotan.

Draenor, the orcs' homeworld, is dying, consumed by fel magic. The warlock Gul'dan unites the orc clans into the Horde and opens a portal to the world of Azeroth by draining the life from captives. He leads an advance warband through, including Durotan of the Frostwolf Clan, his pregnant mate Draka and his friend Orgrim Doomhammer, to capture prisoners whose sacrifice will bring the rest of the Horde. On arrival, Gul'dan revives Durotan's dying newborn son, Go'el, with fel magic. As the orcs raid Azeroth, Lothar and the young mage Khadgar find traces of fel magic and are sent by King Llane to the guardian Medivh. A skirmish with the orcs yields a prisoner, Garona, who agrees to serve Stormwind and leads the humans to spy on Gul'dan's camp.

Despite Orgrim's objections, Durotan secretly meets Llane to propose an alliance, but the meeting is ambushed by the warchief Blackhand, who kills Lothar's son Callan. Khadgar discovers that Medivh, corrupted by fel magic, has been helping Gul'dan open the portal. Blackhand wipes out the Frostwolves; Draka sends Go'el down a river in a basket before she is killed. Durotan challenges Gul'dan to a ritual duel, but Gul'dan kills him by cheating with magic. As the humans attack the orc camp to free the prisoners, Lothar and Khadgar mortally wound Medivh, who uses his last strength to close the portal to Draenor and open one to Stormwind for the freed captives. Trapped, Llane orders Garona to kill him so she can win power among the orcs and someday make peace. Lothar kills Blackhand in a duel and is allowed to leave with the king's body. At Llane's funeral, the human nations, elves and dwarves form an alliance led by Lothar, while the infant Go'el is found by a human.

Warcraft premiered in Paris on May 24, 2016, and was released by Universal Pictures. It grossed $439.1 million worldwide, including $225.5 million in China, but was considered a financial disappointment given its $160 million budget. Critics found it visually impressive but derivative; Rotten Tomatoes reported 29% approval.

title: Seventh Son
tagline: When darkness falls, the son will rise. When the son falls, the dark knight will rise.
overview: John Gregory, who is a seventh son of a seventh son and also the local spook, has protected the country from witches, boggarts, ghouls and all manner of things that go bump in the night. However John is not young anymore, and has been seeking an apprentice to carry on his trade. Most have failed to survive. The last hope is a young farmer's son named Thomas Ward. Will he survive the training to become the spook that so many others couldn't?
plot:
Seventh Son is a 2014 American fantasy adventure film directed by Jonathan Levine, based on the 2004 novel of the same name by Joseph Delaney.

The story takes place in 16th-century England and follows the journey of Thomas Ward (played by Ben Barnes), a young orphan who discovers he has magical abilities. Thomas's mother had been a witch hunter, but she was killed by a powerful witch named Mother Malkin (played by Olivia Williams) when Thomas was just a baby.

Thomas is taken in by John Gregory (played by Jeff Bridges), a veteran witch hunter and the leader of the Witchfinders, an elite group tasked with ridding England of witches. As Thomas grows up, he learns that he has inherited his mother's magical abilities and becomes a skilled young witch hunter.

However, Mother Malkin returns to exact her revenge on Thomas, who is now a powerful young man. She sends her most trusted servant, the White Lady (played by Olivia Williams), to kill Thomas. The White Lady is a formidable foe, with supernatural strength and agility.

As the story unfolds, Thomas must navigate his newfound powers and confront the evil forces of Mother Malkin. Along the way, he meets a young girl named Alice (played by Hannah Tointon) who becomes his ally in the fight against the witches.

The film's plot is driven by the cat-and-mouse game between Thomas and Mother Malkin, with each side trying to outmaneuver the other. As the stakes grow higher, Thomas must confront his own destiny and decide whether to follow in his mother's footsteps as a witch hunter or forge his own path.

Throughout the film, there are moments of action, suspense, and humor, as Thomas navigates the complexities of being a young witch hunter. The film also explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

Ultimately, Thomas must face Mother Malkin in an epic showdown to determine the fate of England. With his newfound powers and the help of his friends, Thomas is able to defeat the evil witch and save the kingdom from destruction.

Overall, Seventh Son is a thrilling adventure film that explores the world of magic and the complexities of growing up with extraordinary abilities.

title: Footloose
tagline: There comes a time to cut loose
overview: Ren MacCormack is transplanted from Boston to the small southern town of Bomont where loud music and dancing are prohibited. Not one to bow to the status quo, Ren challenges the ban, revitalizing the town and falling in love with the minister’s troubled daughter Ariel in the process.
plot:
Footloose is an American musical drama of 2011 and a remake of the 1984 film, directed by Craig Brewer from a script he wrote with Dean Pitchford. Kenny Wormald stars as Ren McCormack, a Boston teenager who challenges a small Southern town's ban on dancing, with Julianne Hough as Ariel Moore, Dennis Quaid as her father, Reverend Shaw Moore, Andie MacDowell as her mother Vi, Miles Teller as Ren's friend Willard and Patrick John Flueger as Chuck.

After a night of partying, the reverend's son Bobby and his friends are killed in a head-on collision with a truck on a bridge outside Bomont, Georgia. In his grief, Shaw persuades the city council to pass a series of strict ordinances, including a ban on unsupervised dancing within the town limits. Three years later, Ren arrives in Bomont to live with his uncle Wes, aunt Lulu and their daughters after his mother's death from leukemia and his father's desertion. He befriends Willard and is drawn to Ariel, the reverend's rebellious daughter, who is secretly seeing the dirt-track racer Chuck. Provoked by Chuck, Ren wins a school bus race despite the bus catching fire. Shaw distrusts Ren and forbids his daughter to see him.

Ren and his classmates want to overturn the ban and hold a prom. As Ariel falls for Ren, her father complains to Wes, who tells him about Ren's mother and suggests that perhaps Ren is the one too good for Ariel. Ariel breaks up with Chuck, who hits her and leaves her with a black eye. At church, Shaw blames Ren and demands his arrest, but Ariel says he cannot blame everything on Ren as he did over Bobby and taunts him about her sex life; he slaps her, shocking Vi, who later tells him he has gone too far and that dancing and music are not the problem. Ren reads Bible passages to the city council showing that people danced even in ancient times, but Shaw has the votes to defeat him.

Ren's boss Andy Beamis offers his cotton mill, just across the line in neighboring Bayson, for the prom. Ren visits Shaw at the church, and the two find common ground in losing someone they loved; Ren insists the dance will happen anyway and politely asks permission to take Ariel, which Shaw grants. On prom night, Ren, Ariel, Willard, Ariel's friend Rusty and Andy run off Chuck's gang, and everyone dances to a country version of "Footloose".

Shot around Atlanta in late 2010 on a $24 million budget, the film was released by Paramount in October 2011 and grossed $63 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed to positive.

title: Battlestar Galactica: Razor
tagline: Fear gets you killed. Anger keeps you alive.
overview: A two-hour Battlestar Galactica special that tells the story of the Battlestar Pegasus several months prior to it finding the Galactica.
plot:
Battlestar Galactica: Razor is a 2004 television miniseries that serves as a prequel to the re-imagined series, and it explores several key themes. At its core, the story delves into the consequences of war and the moral dilemmas faced by those who fight it.

The main character, Captain William Adama, grapples with the weight of his responsibilities as a military leader, particularly in regards to the fate of the Cylons, an artificial intelligence that has become self-aware and is now at war with humanity. As Adama navigates this complex situation, he must confront the harsh realities of conflict and the difficult choices that come with it.

One of the primary themes of Battlestar Galactica: Razor is the exploration of identity and what it means to be human in a world where technology has blurred the lines between man and machine. The Cylons, as artificial intelligences, challenge Adama's understanding of humanity and force him to question his own values and principles.

The miniseries also touches on the theme of sacrifice and the true cost of war. As Adama faces difficult decisions that will impact the lives of those around him, he must weigh the greater good against personal relationships and loyalties. This internal conflict serves as a powerful commentary on the human condition and the sacrifices we make in the name of duty and honor.

Overall, Battlestar Galactica: Razor is a thought-provoking exploration of the complexities of war, identity, and humanity, raising important questions about what it means to be alive and to fight for something greater than oneself.

title: Dream House
tagline: Once upon a time, there were two little girls who lived in a house.
overview: Publisher Will Atenton quits a lucrative job in New York to relocate his wife, Libby, and their daughters to a quaint town in New England. However, as they settle into their home the Atentons discover that a woman and her children were murdered there, and the surviving husband is the town's prime suspect. With help from a neighbor who was close to the murdered family, Will pieces together a horrifying chain of events.
plot:
Dream House is a 2011 American psychological thriller directed by Jim Sheridan and produced by Morgan Creek Productions, starring Daniel Craig as Will Atenton, Rachel Weisz as his wife Libby, Naomi Watts as their neighbor Ann and Marton Csokas as Ann's estranged husband Jack. The film follows a man who discovers that the house he has moved into with his family was the scene of a terrible crime.

Will Atenton, a successful editor at a New York publishing house, quits his job to write a novel and spend more time with Libby and their two young daughters at their new home in a quiet Connecticut town. The family's happiness soon gives way to unease as a series of unsettling events occurs and their neighbors react to Will with suspicion. He learns that five years earlier a man named Peter Ward murdered his wife and two children in the house and was committed to a psychiatric hospital, from which he was recently released for lack of evidence.

Seeking answers, Will turns to his neighbor Ann, who is reluctant to help, while her estranged husband Jack is openly hostile. When Will visits the psychiatric facility, he discovers the truth: he himself is Peter Ward. Shot in the head during the attack, he has no memory of the killings and has constructed a new identity and the illusion that his family is still alive, living in a house that is in reality abandoned and condemned. Taken in by Ann, who believes in his innocence, Peter sets out to discover what really happened on the night of the murders and who was responsible, leading to a confrontation with the real killers.

The production was troubled: Sheridan reportedly clashed with Morgan Creek over the script and tried to remove his name from the film, and Sheridan, Craig and Weisz were said to dislike the final cut. The trailer was criticized for revealing the main plot twist.

Dream House was released by Universal Pictures on September 30, 2011, without advance screenings for critics. It was a critical and commercial failure, with 7 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 35.

title: The Inbetweeners Movie
tagline: Out of school. Out of their league.
overview: High school graduation just wouldn’t be complete without an un-chaperoned, uninhibited and unforgettable final holiday. At least that’s what Will, Jay, Simon and Neil think when they book a two-week stay on an exotic Greek island. As their dreams of sun-drenched days and booze-filled nights are left hopelessly unfulfilled, the lads fight their way into the party scene with hilariously humiliating results in this smash hit UK raunchy comedy.
plot:
The Inbetweeners Movie, known in North America simply as The Inbetweeners, is a 2011 British coming-of-age comedy based on the E4 sitcom The Inbetweeners. Written by series creators Damon Beesley and Iain Morris and directed by Ben Palmer, it was intended as the conclusion of the television series and stars Simon Bird, Joe Thomas, James Buckley and Blake Harrison, reprising their roles, with Emily Head, Laura Haddock, Tamla Kari and Lydia Rose Bewley. It was released in the United Kingdom and Ireland on 17 August 2011 by Entertainment Film Distributors.

Will McKenzie, Simon Cooper, Jay Cartwright and Neil Sutherland finish their A-levels and leave Rudge Park Comprehensive. Jay's grandfather has died and Simon has been dumped by his long-time crush and girlfriend, Carli. To celebrate the end of school and cheer up their friends, the four boys book a holiday in the party resort of Malia, on the Greek island of Crete. After a coach ride shared with chanting football supporters, they discover that their hotel is a rundown dump and head out into Malia's nightlife.

Tricked into visiting a deserted bar, the boys meet four girls on holiday: Alison, Lucy, Lisa and Jane. Will and Alison connect over their shared sense of humor, Simon frustrates Lucy by talking endlessly about Carli, Neil and Lisa sit in awkward silence, and Jay is annoyed when Jane takes an interest in him. Their first encounter goes badly, but the boys keep running into the girls over the course of the week. The holiday becomes a series of humiliating misadventures, as the friends fail to fit in at the resort's clubs, quarrel among themselves and wrestle with their own insecurities. Simon's obsession with Carli, who is also holidaying in Malia, threatens his chance with Lucy, while Jay must decide whether to stop boasting and admit his real feelings, and Will tries to win over Alison. By the end of the trip, the four friends come to appreciate each other and the girls they have met.

The film was a huge commercial success in the United Kingdom, becoming one of the highest-grossing comedies in British box-office history, and it received generally favorable reviews there, though its later release in the United States was greeted less warmly. It was followed by The Inbetweeners 2 in 2014.

title: Never Back Down 2: The Beatdown
overview: Four fighters from different backgrounds come together to train under an ex MMA rising star and then ultimately have to fight each other and the traitor in their midst.
plot:
Never Back Down 2: The Beatdown, also released as The Fighters 2: The Beatdown in some markets, is a 2011 American martial arts film directed by Michael Jai White from a script by Chris Hauty. A sequel to Never Back Down (2008) and the second film in the series, it marked White's directorial debut. Michael Jai White stars as the mixed martial arts trainer Casey "Case" Walker Jr., alongside Dean Geyer as Mike Stokes, Alex Meraz as Zack Gomes, Todd Duffee as Tim Newhouse, Scott Epstein as Justin Epstein, Evan Peters as the promoter Max Cooperman and Jillian Murray as Eve, with Lyoto Machida and "Big" John McCarthy appearing as themselves.

Max is organizing another round of "The Beatdown", an underground fighting event, and four fighters are training in a vacant lot under the veteran martial artist Case. Zack has recently quit boxing after suffering a partially detached retina; Tim, a skilled MMA fighter, has a family sunk in debt since his father's death; Mike, a champion college wrestler, is struggling with his father having left his mother for another man; and Justin, a comic book store clerk, is a frequent target of bullies. A few weeks in, the trainees quarrel over who deserves to be there most, with Justin and Zack hurting each other. When police officers harass Case and threaten him with a probation violation, the team builds a new gym in which to train and hold the Beatdown. Snapping under constant bullying, Justin turns on his tormentors and then on the group itself, framing his mentor in an effort to send him to jail. The others unite to confront him in the tournament. Mike defeats Zack, while Justin attacks Tim in the restroom and knocks him out of the competition. In a gruelling final, Mike beats Justin by breaking his right shoulder with an omoplata submission hold, and when Justin tries to jump him from behind, he responds with a superman punch. Celebrating his win, Mike finally calls his father and invites him to dinner because they have much to discuss, and Case receives a call from McCarthy confirming his return to MMA.

The film premiered at the ActionFest festival in Asheville, North Carolina, on April 8, 2011, and was released on DVD by Sony Pictures Home Entertainment on September 13. Reviews were mixed, with critics praising the fight scenes, especially White's, while finding the story formulaic.

title: Dragon
tagline: Blood Always Leaves a Trail.
overview: A sinful martial arts expert wants to start a new tranquil life, only to be hunted by a determined detective and his former master.
plot:
Dragon (Chinese title Wu Xia) is a 2011 Hong Kong-Chinese martial arts film from director Peter Chan, starring Donnie Yen, who also served as action director, alongside Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tang Wei, with Jimmy Wang Yu and Kara Hui in support. Conceived as a remake of Chang Cheh's 1967 classic The One-Armed Swordsman, it soon became an original story, though it retains echoes of that film, including the casting of Wang, its original star.

In 1917, Liu Jinxi lives quietly in a village in Yunnan with his wife, Yu, her son Fangzheng and their younger son Xiaotian. When two bandits try to rob a shop while Liu is inside, a scuffle breaks out and both robbers end up dead, apparently through Liu's clumsy luck. The villagers hail him as a hero, but Xu Baijiu, a Sichuanese-speaking detective sent to look into the case, is suspicious, since one of the dead men was a feared fighter. By performing an autopsy he discovers that the robber died of a brain haemorrhage caused by a precise blow to the vagus nerve, and further evidence convinces him that Liu is a master martial artist hiding his skill behind misdirection and a former member of the 72 Demons, a savage gang of killers.

Confronted, Liu admits his past but insists he has changed. Xu nevertheless obtains a warrant for his arrest, and the corrupt magistrate sells Liu's location to the Master of the 72 Demons in hope of a reward. The Master, revealing that Liu is his son, kills the magistrate and sends his men to bring Liu back. Liu kills them and sends the villagers to shelter in a fortress, and Xu uses his knowledge of anatomy to help him fake his death, but the deception fails. To prove he has broken with the gang, Liu cuts off his own left arm. The Master, holding Liu's family hostage, agrees to release him only if Xiaotian takes his place. Liu attacks, but the Master's qigong makes him impervious to blades. Xu slips in beneath the floorboards and drives acupuncture needles into the Master's heel and neck, weakening him; the Master mortally wounds the detective but is then struck dead by lightning, drawn by the needles. Xu declares the case closed with his last breath, and Liu returns to peaceful family life.

The film premiered in the Midnight Screenings section at Cannes in May 2011 and topped the Chinese box office with more than 100 million yuan in its first week. Critics were positive; Variety likened it to A History of Violence set in 1917 China. It won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Cinematography.

title: The Hunger Games
tagline: May The Odds Be Ever In Your Favor.
overview: Every year in the ruins of what was once North America, the nation of Panem forces each of its twelve districts to send a teenage boy and girl to compete in the Hunger Games.  Part twisted entertainment, part government intimidation tactic, the Hunger Games are a nationally televised event in which “Tributes” must fight with one another until one survivor remains.  Pitted against highly-trained Tributes who have prepared for these Games their entire lives, Katniss is forced to rely upon her sharp instincts as well as the mentorship of drunken former victor Haymitch Abernathy.  If she’s ever to return home to District 12, Katniss must make impossible choices in the arena that weigh survival against humanity and life against love. The world will be watching.
plot:
The Hunger Games is a dystopian science fiction film directed by Gary Ross, based on the novel of the same name by Suzanne Collins. The movie was released in 2012 and produced by Lionsgate.

In a post-apocalyptic future, the country of Panem is ruled by the tyrannical Capitol. As punishment for a past rebellion, the Capitol forces each of the 12 districts to participate in the Hunger Games, a brutal annual event where 24 tributes, 12 boys and 12 girls, are chosen to fight to the death in a televised event.

The story follows Katniss Everdeen (played by Jennifer Lawrence), a 16-year-old girl from District 12 who volunteers to participate in the Games in place of her younger sister Prim. Katniss is skilled with a bow and arrow and has experience hunting to feed her family after their father's death.

Katniss, along with fellow tribute Peeta Mellark (played by Josh Hutcherson), is transported to the Capitol to prepare for the Games. They are trained, interviewed, and paraded in front of the cameras to gain sympathy and sponsorships from the audience.

Once the Games begin, Katniss and Peeta must use their wits, skills, and alliances to survive against the other tributes. The Gamemakers, who control the arena, introduce various challenges and obstacles to make the game more exciting for the audience.

As the Games progress, Katniss forms alliances with Rue (played by Amandla Stenberg) from District 11 and Thresh (played by Dayo Okeniyi), a strong and skilled tribute from District 11. However, when Rue is killed by Career Tributes, Katniss becomes more determined to survive.

Meanwhile, Peeta's actions in the arena are carefully scripted to gain sympathy from the audience, making it difficult for Katniss to determine his true intentions. As the Games near their end, Katniss and Peeta are the last two survivors, and they threaten to eat poisonous berries rather than kill each other.

In a surprising twist, President Snow (played by Donald Sutherland) intervenes, and Katniss and Peeta declare their love for each other, forcing them to be declared co-winners of the Games. However, this act of defiance against the Capitol is seen as a threat, and Katniss becomes the face of the growing rebellion in District 12.

The movie ends with Katniss and Peeta's victory, but also sets the stage for the rest of the series, as Katniss becomes the Mockingjay, the symbol of the rebellion against the Capitol.

A Fairly Odd Movie: Grow Up, Timmy Turner! (2011) is an animated film that explores several significant themes. At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of growing up and the challenges that come with it.

The main character, Timmy Turner, finds himself at a crossroads as he navigates the transition from boyhood to manhood. Furthermore, the movie explores the idea of letting go and embracing change. Timmy's fairy godparents, who have been so integral to his life, are forced to confront their own limitations and the fact that they can no longer be there for him in the same way. This serves as a poignant reminder that all good things must come to an end, and that growth and progress often require us to let go of what we know and love.

Lastly, the film offers a commentary on the importance of relationships and human connections. Despite the fantastical elements of the story, the movie ultimately focuses on Timmy's relationships with his family, friends, and even his fairy godparents. It highlights the significance of nurturing these relationships and learning to communicate effectively with others as we navigate the complexities of life.

Overall, A Fairly Odd Movie: Grow Up, Timmy Turner! is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores the challenges and joys of growing up, identity, change, and human connection.

title: The Raven
tagline: The only one who can stop a serial killer is the man who inspired him.
overview: A fictionalized account of the last days of Edgar Allan Poe's life, in which the poet is in pursuit of a serial killer whose murders mirror those in the writer's stories.
plot:
The Raven is a 2012 American horror film directed by James McTeigue and starring John Cusack as Edgar Allan Poe. 

The movie begins with Poe's life in Baltimore, where he has just lost his young wife, Virginia. He becomes obsessed with solving the murder of a young woman named Lenore, who bears an uncanny resemblance to his late wife.

As Poe delves deeper into the mystery, he encounters a series of eerie and supernatural events that lead him to believe that the killer is trying to communicate with him through cryptic messages and riddles. The film's plot is heavily influenced by Poe's own works, particularly "The Murders in the Rue Morgue" and "The Pit and the Pendulum".

Throughout the movie, Poe's character grapples with his own demons, including his grief over Virginia's death and his struggles with addiction and poverty. The film also explores themes of love, loss, and the power of art to transcend mortality.

As the story unfolds, Poe becomes increasingly entangled in a web of mystery and horror, ultimately leading him to confront the killer in a thrilling showdown. Along the way, he must also navigate the complexities of his own psyche and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

The Raven features a blend of historical fact and fiction, drawing on Poe's life and works to create a unique and captivating narrative. The film's themes of love, loss, and the power of art are timeless and universal, making it a compelling watch for fans of horror and mystery alike.

Overall, The Raven is a gripping and atmospheric horror film that explores the darker corners of the human psyche, all while paying homage to one of literature's most iconic figures.

title: Trespass
tagline: When terror is at your doorstep. You can run. Or you can fight.
overview: Kyle and Sarah Miller have it all: a huge gated house on the water, fancy cars, and the potential for romance in their relationship. He's just back from a business trip and their teen daughter Avery is sneaking out to a party, when four thugs in security uniforms and ski masks stage a home invasion. They want what's in the safe: cash and diamonds. As Kyle stalls them, trying to negotiate for Sarah's freedom, the fault lines in Kyle and Sarah's marriage and the pasts of the four robbers come into play. Is there room here for heroism?
plot:
Trespass is a 2011 American crime thriller film directed by Joel Schumacher, his final film, and written by Karl Gajdusek. Nicolas Cage and Nicole Kidman star as Kyle and Sarah Miller, a wealthy couple taken hostage in their home, with Ben Mendelsohn, Cam Gigandet, Liana Liberato, Jordana Spiro, Dash Mihok, Emily Meade and Nico Tortorella. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2011 and was released by Millennium Entertainment in a limited theatrical release and on video on demand in October 2011.

The Millers live in a luxurious, high-security mansion in Shreveport, Louisiana, where Kyle works as a diamond dealer. Their teenage daughter, Avery, sneaks out to a party against her parents' wishes but returns home upset after being harassed by the host. Meanwhile, a gang of robbers posing as police officers forces its way into the house: their leader, Elias, his girlfriend, Petal, his younger brother, Jonah, and an enforcer named Ty. They demand that Kyle open his safe, and when Avery returns, she too is taken captive.

The intruders soon discover that the family's wealth is an illusion: Kyle is effectively bankrupt, having bought everything on credit, and makes only a modest income appraising diamonds for former clients to keep up with the mortgage. Even Sarah's diamond necklace turns out to be a fake. As tempers rise, Elias breaks Kyle's hand, and an escape attempt by Kyle and Avery ends with Kyle shot in the leg. It emerges that Elias is a drug dealer working for a criminal syndicate who was robbed of $180,000 worth of drugs and committed the robbery under threat of retribution, and that Jonah, who once worked on the Millers' security system, had become obsessed with Sarah. As secrets about the family and the criminals are revealed, including suspicions that Sarah had an affair, the captors turn on one another, and the Millers must outwit them to survive the night.

Trespass was panned by critics, who found it overwrought, implausible and repetitive, filled with constant shouting and twists, and it was considered a waste of its talented stars. It was a box-office failure, earning only a small fraction of its reported $35 million budget, having been released in very few theaters at the same time as its on-demand debut.

title: Hellraiser: Revelations
tagline: The Return of Pinhead.
overview: Two friends in Mexico discover the Lament Configuration and unleash Pinhead, but one decides to try to survive by swapping himself with someone else. Once they go missing, family members go in search of them, but find Pinhead instead.
plot:
Hellraiser: Revelations is a 2011 American horror film written by Gary J. Tunnicliffe and directed by Víctor Garcia, the ninth installment in the Hellraiser series based on the work of Clive Barker. It stars Steven Brand, Nick Eversman and Tracey Fairaway, with Stephan Smith Collins as Pinhead, the leader of the sadomasochistic otherworldly beings known as the Cenobites.

Best friends Nico Bradley and Steven Craven run away from home and travel to Mexico, where they film themselves partying for days before vanishing without a trace. The Mexican authorities later return their belongings to their families, including a videotape recorded by Steven and an ornate puzzle box. A year later, the two families gather for an uneasy dinner. Steven's sister Emma, who was also Nico's girlfriend, is frustrated by the lack of answers and demands to know what is on the tape that her mother Sarah has been watching in secret.

When Emma views the footage, the story of the boys' final days begins to emerge in flashbacks. In Mexico, Nico killed a young woman they had picked up in a bar and used the crime to force Steven to keep traveling with him. Nico was then given the puzzle box by a vagrant who promised him unimaginable pleasures. At the house, Emma finds the box and tries to work it, and Steven suddenly reappears, bloodied and terrified. The families find themselves unable to leave as Steven warns that the Cenobites are coming, and the secrets and desires of everyone in the house come to the surface as the demons arrive to claim what they are owed.

The film was produced in a matter of weeks because Dimension Films needed to release a new Hellraiser film to retain the rights to the franchise. Because of the rushed schedule, longtime star Doug Bradley declined to take part, making it the first entry in which he did not play Pinhead.

Revelations received a single theatrical screening in March 2011, ostensibly open to the public, before being released on DVD on October 18, 2011. Reviews were overwhelmingly negative: none of the critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes gave it a positive review, and Dread Central wrote that it made all the earlier sequels look great by comparison.

title: Setup
overview: A group of friends plan out a detailed heist that turns deadly when one betrays the other by taking off with the goods. plot:
Setup is a 2011 direct-to-video action thriller heist film directed by Mike Gunther, who wrote it with Mike Behrman. Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson stars as Sonny, with Bruce Willis as the mob boss Biggs and Ryan Phillippe as Vincent, and the cast also includes Jenna Dewan as Mia, Randy Couture as Petey, James Remar as William and Brett Granstaff as Dave. It was shot in Grand Rapids, Michigan, in late 2010.

In Detroit, three friends, Sonny, Dave and Vincent, carefully plan a heist of $5 million in diamonds, but Vincent betrays the others and shoots them both. Dave dies, while Sonny survives and seeks revenge by allying himself with Biggs, the most dangerous mob boss in town, in order to recover the money from the heist. Biggs sends Sonny with his henchman Petey to dig up $2 million buried in a cemetery, but Petey accidentally shoots himself. Sonny follows a woman named Mia to the home of the fence who handled the stolen goods and threatens him, and the frightened fence warns Vincent that he must deal with the loose end he left behind, only to be killed by Vincent. While Biggs's men brutally interrogate others to learn what happened to Petey, Vincent seeks help to eliminate Sonny, and Sonny visits Dave's grave and then Vincent's imprisoned father, asking whether there is anything he would like said to his son before Sonny kills him. Mia is murdered by the owner of the diamonds, who wants them back. In prison, an inmate named Saunders extorts $100,000 from Vincent to keep his father safe. Sonny hides part of Biggs's $2 million in a teddy bear packed in a box, then falsely tells Biggs that Vincent has his money, and a meeting between Biggs and Vincent ends in a deadly shootout. Vincent escapes, kills the owner of the diamonds when he breaks into his home, and is finally ambushed by Sonny at his car. Doused in oil and forced to dig his own grave, Vincent confesses that he betrayed his friends because Saunders had threatened his father and he needed the money. Sonny spares him, but Vincent's father is then killed in prison. Dave's girlfriend receives the teddy bear with the money, and Sonny drives away reflecting that while he could live with Vincent remaining alive, the question was whether Vincent could.

Lionsgate's Grindstone Entertainment Group released Setup on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on September 20, 2011. In a handful of international markets it grossed about $2.1 million.

This camaraderie is forged in the face of adversity, demonstrating that even in the most challenging situations, human connection can be a powerful force for survival.

Overall, Kon-Tiki is a film about the human condition, exploring our capacity for resilience, adaptability, and connection with the world around us.

title: Brownian Movement
overview: A psychiatrist's adulterous past continues to haunt her and her husband after they move to India.
plot:
Brownian Movement is a 2010 Dutch drama written and directed by Nanouk Leopold, a Dutch–German–Belgian co-production made by Serendipity Films, Circe Films and Coin Film with Bella Cohen Films and the broadcaster VPRO. It stars Sandra Hüller as Charlotte, a German doctor working in Brussels, and Dragan Bakema as her husband Max. The title alludes to Brownian motion, the seemingly random movement of particles suspended in a gas or liquid, though the film itself never explains it.

Charlotte appears to have a perfect life with Max, an attentive and handsome architect, and their young son Benjamin, to whom she reads the Brothers Grimm tale "The Girl Without Hands" at bedtime. Her marriage is affectionate and the couple's intimacy is warm and trusting. Yet she secretly rents a bare apartment where she meets men she picks from among her patients, most of them physically unprepossessing, for impulsive sexual encounters. When she unexpectedly runs into one of these men again and he tries to get close to her, she breaks down, attacks him and collapses.

Her affairs come to light, she is struck off the medical register and her marriage nearly falls apart. In couples therapy and a psychiatric assessment she struggles, or declines, to explain her behaviour, admitting she does not really know what she is supposed to feel. In the film's third section, two years later, the family has moved to India, where Max works as an architect; twins have been born and their happiness seems restored, but Max cannot shake his mistrust and begins following Charlotte on her solitary morning walks, which take her to a building under construction.

The cast also includes Sabine Timoteo, Ryan Brodie as Benjamin and Nicole Shirer. The film was shot by Frank van den Eeden and edited by Leopold's long-time collaborator Katharina Wartena, with music by Harry de Wit. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2010 and screened in the Forum section of the 2011 Berlin International Film Festival. Critics praised Hüller's subtle, empathetic performance and the luminous cinematography, but many found the film's long takes, sparse dialogue and elliptical storytelling slow and opaque; The Hollywood Reporter called it an inert endurance test, while Screen Daily detected powerful emotions beneath its cold surface.

title: Superior Firepower: Making 'Aliens'
overview: This feature-length documentary, made especially for the 2003 Aliens (1986) DVD release, is incredibly informative with all its interviews with both the cast and crew, as well as behind the scenes footage filmed during the making of the film.
