plot:
Superior Firepower: Making 'Aliens' is a 2003 American documentary film directed and produced by Charles de Lauzirika about the production of James Cameron's 1986 science fiction film Aliens. Made by the Lauzirika Motion Picture Company for 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment, it was created for the Alien Quadrilogy DVD box set released in December 2003, following his documentary on the first film, The Beast Within: Making 'Alien', and preceding Wreckage and Rage: Making 'Alien 3'. It runs 185 minutes and has no narrator, telling its story instead through new interviews, archival interview clips and behind-the-scenes footage. Participants include producers Gale Anne Hurd and David Giler, Sigourney Weaver, Carrie Henn, Michael Biehn, Lance Henriksen, Bill Paxton, Jenette Goldstein and Mark Rolston, concept artists Syd Mead and Ron Cobb, production designer Peter Lamont, casting director Mary Selway, creature effects creator Stan Winston, effects supervisor John Richardson and composer James Horner, with Cameron appearing in archival interviews.

The documentary is divided into eleven chapters. It begins with the stalled early attempts at a sequel, Cameron's recruitment and the pay dispute that briefly threatened Weaver's return as Ripley, then moves to the design of the colony, the spaceships and the armored personnel carrier, and to the casting of the Colonial Marines and their military-style training. A chapter on the shoot at Pinewood Studios in 1985 details tensions between the American director and the British crew, including the replacement of the original cinematographer, and the late casting of Biehn. Further chapters examine the Marines' weapons and the action sequences, the redesigned facehuggers and warrior aliens, the bond between Weaver and the nine-year-old Henn, and the construction of the full-size Alien Queen puppet and the Power Loader for their climactic duel. The last chapters cover Horner's struggle to compose the score in very little time, which soured his relationship with Cameron for years, the miniature visual effects, and the film's reception, including Weaver's Academy Award nomination for Best Actress.

The documentary was later included in the Aliens collector's edition DVD and, in a reformatted widescreen version, in the Alien Anthology Blu-ray set, which added deleted segments known as enhancement pods.

She feels suffocated by the expectations placed upon her as a wife and mother, and longs for independence and autonomy. Jill's life is marked by the constant need to prioritize her family over her own desires and aspirations. This dichotomy creates tension and conflict within her, as she grapples with the desire for independence and the expectation to be a perfect homemaker.

The movie suggests that even in seemingly happy marriages, there can be a sense of disconnection and unhappiness lurking beneath the surface.

Ultimately, I Don't Know How She Does It is a poignant exploration of the human experience, one that encourages viewers to reflect on their own relationships, desires, and aspirations. As he navigates the harsh and unforgiving environment of the Antarctic wilderness, he begins to confront his own demons and grapple with the consequences of his actions.

Will's interactions with a young Inuit girl, who is on a research expedition in Antarctica, serve as a catalyst for him to re-examine his life choices and consider the impact he has on those around him.

Furthermore, The Hunter touches upon the theme of class and privilege, highlighting the stark contrast between the wealthy individuals who commission Will's services and the people who are affected by their desires. plot:
Prometheus is a 2012 science fiction film directed by Ridley Scott, produced by 20th Century Fox, and distributed by 20th Century Studios. The movie takes place in the year 2093 and serves as a prequel to the Alien franchise.

The story begins with a prologue that shows a group of humans who are searching for answers about the origins of humanity. They discover an ancient alien artifact on Earth, which leads them to a spaceship called the Prometheus. The crew of the Prometheus is led by Captain Janek (played by Guy Pearce) and includes scientists like Dr. Elizabeth Shaw (played by Noomi Rapace), Dr. Charlie Holloway (played by Logan Marshall-Green), and Dr. Peter Weyland (played by Michael Fassbender).

The crew of the Prometheus sets out on a mission to find the origins of humanity, which they believe is connected to an ancient alien species known as the Engineers. They travel through space and eventually arrive at a distant planet called LV-223, where they discover a massive structure that appears to be some sort of temple.

As the crew explores the temple, they begin to uncover clues about the origins of humanity and the purpose of their mission. However, they soon realize that they are not alone on the planet, and that something is hunting them. The crew discovers that the Engineers were responsible for creating life on Earth, but also created a deadly creature known as the Xenomorph.

As the crew delves deeper into the temple, they begin to experience strange occurrences and equipment malfunctions. It becomes clear that the planet's atmosphere is toxic, and that the crew is being hunted by the Xenomorph. The crew tries to escape, but it's too late, and many of them are killed by the creature.

In the end, only a few members of the crew manage to survive, including Dr. Shaw and her partner, Charlie Holloway. They discover that the Engineers had created the Xenomorph as a failsafe to prevent humanity from becoming too powerful. The movie ends with Dr. Shaw and Charlie Holloway escaping the planet in a shuttle, but not before they realize that the true purpose of their mission was not what they expected.

Throughout the movie, there are themes of creation, responsibility, and the dangers of playing god. The film also explores the idea of humanity's place in the universe and our relationship with technology. Overall, Prometheus is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that sets the stage for the Alien franchise.

The Deathgames is an illegal internet broadcast in which kidnapped combatants fight to the death in a modern gladiatorial arena for a paying online audience. David Lord loses his pregnant girlfriend, Lori, in a car accident. Grief-stricken, he drinks at a bar, where a mysterious woman, Milla, watches him easily subdue a bouncer. She seduces him, then drugs him so that he can be abducted. Milla is a recruiter for the Deathgames, run by the smooth and confident Logan.

David wakes up as a prisoner in a hidden facility and is forced to fight. Logan promises him his freedom if he wins ten bouts in a row, and David agrees on one condition: that his tenth and final opponent must be Kaden, Logan's top fighter and enforcer. David wins fight after fight, becoming a hit with the online audience. For the penultimate match, Kaden arranges the release of a South African serial killer, Brutus Jackson, but David defeats him, which convinces Logan that Kaden fears him. Distressed by the risk to his business, Logan has a doctor inject David with a drug that will slow him down and make him easy prey for Kaden. As the final fight begins, flashbacks reveal that David's story is not what it seems: "David Lord" is the cover identity of an undercover government agent sent to infiltrate the Deathgames and bring down the organization, and the outcome of the battle will determine whether his mission succeeds.

Arena received mostly negative reviews, with critics focusing on its clichéd script and shallow plot, although Jackson's flamboyant performance and some of the fight choreography were noted as highlights. The film went straight to home video, where its star pairing of Lutz and Jackson was its main selling point.

Jim Levenstein (Jason Biggs), Michelle Flaherty (Alyson Hannigan), Stifler (Seann William Scott), Oz (Eddie Kaye Thomas), and Kevin (Thomas Ian Nicholas) are now in their mid-to-late 30s. They have all moved on with their lives, but the group is reunited when Jim's high school reunion invitation arrives.

The movie begins with Jim, who has just gone through a divorce, trying to reconnect with his friends and figure out what he wants from life. The group reunites at Jim's house for a weekend, where they reminisce about old times and try to recapture their youth. However, things quickly become complicated as the group faces various challenges, including marriage problems, career struggles, and midlife crises.

As the reunion progresses, the group discovers that some of them are still stuck in their high school ways, while others have grown up and moved on. Stifler, who has been struggling with his own identity crisis, tries to relive his glory days by hooking up with a younger woman (Anna Faris). Meanwhile, Oz is trying to balance his family life with his desire for freedom.

Throughout the movie, the group's dynamics are put to the test as they navigate their relationships and try to find their place in the world. The film features plenty of humor, including raunchy jokes and awkward moments, but also explores more serious themes like marriage, parenthood, and growing up.

As the reunion comes to a close, Jim realizes that he needs to take responsibility for his life and make some changes. He starts to reconnect with an old flame (Emma Stone), who has been a constant presence in his life throughout the series. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with the group having learned valuable lessons about friendship, love, and growing up.

Overall, American Reunion is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores the ups and downs of adulthood. While it may not be as edgy or raunchy as some of its predecessors, it still delivers plenty of laughs and heartwarming moments.

Calloway's plan is to use the piranhas as a means to terrorize and control the town, thereby increasing property values and making him rich.

Throughout the film, Burt and his friends face numerous challenges as they try to outsmart the piranhas and stop Calloway's sinister plans. Along the way, they also encounter other characters who are trying to help them, including a local fisherman named Tom (played by Jake Abel) and a mysterious woman named Liz (played by Kelly Overton).

In the end, Burt and his friends manage to defeat the piranhas and stop Calloway's plans, but not before many lives have been lost. The film ends with Burt reflecting on the events that transpired, and realizing that he has a newfound appreciation for his father's bravery and sacrifice.

Overall, Piranha 3DD is a campy and over-the-top horror film that delivers plenty of gore and suspense. While it may not be as well-received as its predecessor, it still provides an entertaining ride for fans of the genre.

However, things become increasingly complicated when Josh discovers that he has been chosen as the main attraction for a wealthy client's twisted game. The client, known only as "The Collector," is willing to pay top dollar for Josh's services, which include being subjected to various forms of physical and psychological torture.

As the story unfolds, Josh must use all his wits and resourcefulness to survive the hostel's brutal games and ultimately escape. Along the way, he faces off against Mr. Henkel and The Collector in a battle of wills that will determine his fate.

Throughout the film, Roth explores themes of human exploitation, voyeurism, and the darker aspects of human nature. The movie is known for its graphic violence, gore, and dark humor, which have become hallmarks of Roth's style.

Ultimately, Josh manages to outsmart The Collector and escape El Mariachi, but not without scars both physical and emotional. The film ends with Josh reflecting on his experience and the true cost of survival in a world where humanity has been reduced to mere entertainment for the wealthy and powerful.

Overall, Hostel: Part III is a thought-provoking and unflinching exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, with a strong performance from Derek Richardson as the protagonist.

Wrong Turn 4: Bloody Beginnings is a 2011 slasher film written and directed by Declan O'Brien. It is the fourth installment of the Wrong Turn series and the first part of a prequel story to the original 2003 film, exploring the origins of the deformed cannibal brothers Saw Tooth, One Eye and Three Finger. The cast includes Jennifer Pudavick, Tenika Davis, Kaitlyn Wong and Terra Vnesa.

In 1974, at the Glenville Sanatorium in West Virginia, the head doctor shows a new colleague around the building, including the cell where the young Hillicker brothers, three cannibalistic patients, are held. After the doctors leave, the brothers escape, kill a guard and release the other inmates, starting a riot in which the staff are massacred.

In 2003, a group of college students set out on a winter break snowmobiling trip to a friend's cabin in the mountains. Caught in a snowstorm, they take shelter in the abandoned Glenville Sanatorium, unaware that the Hillicker brothers still live there. One of the students tells the others stories about the asylum and its cannibals, but her friends dismiss them. During the night, one of the group goes exploring and is killed, and the next day the students discover the cannibals butchering their missing friend's body. When they try to leave, they find that the brothers have sabotaged their snowmobiles. One student sets off on skis to find help while the others remain trapped in the building, and the brothers hunt them down one by one in a series of increasingly gruesome killings, as the survivors try to fight back and escape through the snow.

The film follows the series' formula of isolated victims and graphic violence, moving the setting to a snowbound asylum and offering a glimpse of the cannibals' early years.

Wrong Turn 4: Bloody Beginnings was released directly to DVD and Blu-ray by 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment on October 25, 2011. It received mixed reviews; Dread Central called it an objectively bad film that is still enjoyable to watch, while Little White Lies found the characters interchangeable and the plot derivative. It was followed by Wrong Turn 5: Bloodlines in 2012.

The climax of the film features an epic showdown between Blaze and Mephisto, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Blaze is able to defeat Mephisto and save Robbie from becoming a vessel for the Devil's Son.

However, the film ends on a bleak note, as Blaze is left feeling empty and unfulfilled after his victory. He realizes that he has lost himself to the Ghost Rider persona, and that he needs to find a way to reconcile his dual identity.

Overall, Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance is a dark and action-packed take on the Ghost Rider franchise. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the series will appreciate the film's over-the-top action sequences and supernatural thrills.

plot:
Assassination Games is a 2011 American action thriller directed by Ernie Barbarash from a screenplay by Aaron Rahsaan Thomas, starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and Scott Adkins as rival contract killers, with Ivan Kaye as their common enemy. Produced by the Motion Picture Corporation of America with Mediapro Studios and Rodin Entertainment on a budget of about $8 million, it was shot in Bucharest, Romania, and New Orleans in the autumn of 2010, with a score by Neal Acree.

Vincent Brazil is an assassin and master of bladed weapons who will take any job if the price is right. Roland Flint, a top marksman, has walked away from the profession since the drug kingpin Polo Yakur launched a brutal attack that left Flint's wife, Anna, in a coma from which she has never awoken. When a contract is put out on Yakur, both men want it: Brazil for the money, Flint for revenge. The two strangers start out as competitors working the same target, but with crooked Interpol agents protecting the dealer and vicious members of the criminal underworld closing in on them both, they reluctantly join forces to take Yakur down before they themselves are eliminated.

Van Damme plays Brazil and Adkins plays Flint, with Kevin Chapman as Culley, Valentin Teodosiu as Blanchard, Alin Panc as Kovacs, Michael Higgs as Godfrey and Marija Karan as October, Bianca Bree as Anna Flint and Kris Van Damme as Schell.

The project began life under the working title The Weapon, with Russell Mulcahy attached to direct and Steven Seagal set to co-star with Van Damme. After Seagal dropped out, Vinnie Jones was considered for the part before it went to Adkins. The film received a limited theatrical release in the United States on 29 July 2011, followed by a DVD release from Sony Pictures Home Entertainment that September, and opened in France and Russia later in 2011 and 2012.

title: The Iron Lady
tagline: Never Compromise.
overview: A look at the life of Margaret Thatcher, the former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, with a focus on the price she paid for power.
plot:
The Iron Lady is a 2011 biographical drama about Margaret Thatcher, the longest-serving British prime minister of the 20th century and the first woman to hold the office. Phyllida Lloyd directed from a screenplay by Abi Morgan, loosely based on John Campbell's biography. Meryl Streep plays Thatcher, with Alexandra Roach as the young Margaret. Jim Broadbent and Harry Lloyd play her husband, Denis, and Anthony Head plays Geoffrey Howe.

In the present day, the elderly Thatcher, now suffering from dementia, keeps seeing and talking to Denis, who has died. Her memories take the story back through her life. As a girl, Margaret Roberts works in her family's grocery shop in Grantham and absorbs the political speeches of the father she idolizes, while her relationship with her mother is distant. She wins a place at Somerville College, Oxford, and later fights to break into a snobbish, male-dominated Conservative Party and win a seat in the House of Commons. She accepts Denis's proposal only after warning him that she will never be content as a housewife: "I don't want to die cleaning a teacup."

The flashbacks follow her through life as one of the few women in Parliament and as education secretary under Edward Heath. They show her friendship with Airey Neave, her run for party leader and her image makeover. As prime minister after the 1979 election, she pushes through monetarist policies and the austere 1981 budget over the doubts of the "wets" in her cabinet. She faces unemployment, riots, the miners' strike and the 1984 Brighton bombing. She sends a task force to recover the Falkland Islands from Argentina, forms an alliance with Ronald Reagan and presides over the late-1980s boom. By 1990, she has become imperious, berating her ministers, defending the poll tax amid riots and resisting European integration. Howe resigns after she humiliates him, Michael Heseltine challenges her and she is forced to resign after eleven years. In the present, Thatcher finally packs away Denis's belongings and tells him to go. As his ghost departs, he assures her that she will be fine on her own, and she washes a teacup alone in her kitchen.

Filming began on December 31, 2010. The film grossed $115 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, and Thatcher's children and biographer criticized its portrayal. Streep's performance was widely acclaimed and won her a third Academy Award, as well as a Golden Globe and a BAFTA. The film also won the Oscar for Best Makeup.

title: The Odd Life of Timothy Green

overview: A childless couple bury a box in their backyard, containing all of their wishes for an infant. Soon, a child is born, though Timothy Green is not all that he appears.
plot:
The Odd Life of Timothy Green is a heartwarming and poignant film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, loss, and the transformative power of imagination. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of grief and how it can shape us in profound ways.

The story follows a widowed mother, Susan, who struggles to connect with her son, Josh, after the sudden loss of his father. As she navigates this difficult time, she begins to see the world through the eyes of her son's imaginary friend, Timothy Green, a magical and endearing character who embodies the innocence and wonder of childhood.

Through Timothy's presence, Susan is forced to confront her own emotional baggage and learn to let go of her grief. The film beautifully captures the bittersweet nature of loss and the ways in which it can both break us and ultimately set us free.

The movie also explores the theme of love and its many forms. Susan's relationship with Josh is tender and loving, but also fraught with tension and uncertainty. As she navigates her new role as a single mother, she must find a way to balance her own needs with those of her son, all while learning to trust herself and her abilities.

One of the most striking aspects of The Odd Life of Timothy Green is its use of fantasy and imagination as a means of healing and transformation. Through Timothy's magical presence, Susan is able to tap into a sense of wonder and possibility that she had lost in her grief. This serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of holding onto hope and finding joy in the midst of sorrow.

Overall, The Odd Life of Timothy Green is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of human relationships, love, loss, and the transformative power of imagination. With its poignant performances, stunning visuals, and thoughtful storytelling, it is a movie that will leave audiences moved and inspired long after the credits roll.

title: Jack and Jill
tagline: His twin sister is coming for the holidays... ...and it ain't pretty.
overview: Jack Sadelstein, a successful advertising executive in Los Angeles with a beautiful wife and kids, dreads one event each year: the Thanksgiving visit of his twin sister Jill. Jill's neediness and passive-aggressiveness is maddening to Jack, turning his normally tranquil life upside down.
plot:
Jack and Jill is a 2011 American comedy directed by Dennis Dugan and co-written by Adam Sandler, who stars in a dual role as twin siblings Jack and Jill Sadelstein. Katie Holmes plays Jack's wife Erin, and Al Pacino appears as a fictionalised version of himself. The film features numerous celebrity cameos, including Johnny Depp, Shaquille O'Neal, Drew Carey, John McEnroe and Regis Philbin, in his final film appearance. Its story follows a successful advertising executive whose holiday season is upended by a visit from his twin sister.

As children in the Bronx, Jill constantly sought the attention of her gifted twin brother, often in disastrous ways. As an adult, Jack is a successful advertising executive living in Los Angeles with Erin, their daughter Sofia and their adopted son Gary. Jill, unemployed and single, still lives alone in the family home in the Bronx, which she inherited after their mother's death the previous year.

Jill comes to stay for Thanksgiving and announces, to Jack's dismay, that she intends to remain until the end of Hanukkah, since her ticket is open-ended. Her loud, tactless behaviour embarrasses Jack in front of his guests, and after he snaps at her she runs off into the woods with her pet cockatoo, prompting Erin to insist that he apologise. Jill works her way through a list of activities she has planned, including an appearance on The Price Is Right. Meanwhile, Jack's biggest client demands that he persuade Al Pacino to appear in a Dunkin' Donuts commercial. When Pacino unexpectedly falls for Jill, Jack sees an opportunity to save his career by encouraging the romance, even though Jill has little interest in the actor, setting up a series of increasingly absurd situations that culminate in the making of the commercial.

The comedy relies heavily on Sandler's cross-dressing performance as Jill, product placement and Pacino's self-parody, and its underlying theme is the reconciliation between two very different siblings.

Jack and Jill was panned by critics, with about 3 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it is often cited as one of the worst films ever made. At the 32nd Golden Raspberry Awards it became the first film to sweep every category, although it grossed about 149 million dollars worldwide.

title: Redline
tagline: The most violent race in the universe!
overview: The most dangerous and exciting car race in the universe is held only once every five years. And that's tonight. The competitors are lined up at the starting block. In his vehicle, JP, the most daredevil driver on the circuit, is ready for the green light. Female driver Sonoshee, with whom he is secretly in love, is also on the starting line. She will stop at nothing to get on to that podium. In this race, not only is anything possible, but also anything is allowed. In fact, their adversaries have modified their vehicles to equip them with highly destructive weapons; with such participants, it is hardly surprising that Redline is forbidden by the authorities, who will try anything to halt the proceedings.
plot:
Redline is a 2009 Japanese animated science fiction racing film produced by Madhouse and directed by Takeshi Koike in his directorial debut, written by Katsuhito Ishii, Yōji Enokido and Yoshiki Sakurai from Ishii's story. Its voice cast includes Takuya Kimura, Yū Aoi, Tatsuya Gashūin, Takeshi Aono and Tadanobu Asano.

On the planet Dorothy, "Sweet" JP competes in the Yellowline, the last qualifier for the Redline. His mechanic and friend Frisbee has fixed the race with a mafia boss, and when JP pushes for first instead of second, Frisbee remotely detonates a bomb hidden in JP's car, handing victory to the racer Sonoshee McLaren. Recovering in the hospital, JP learns he has been voted into the Redline after two qualifiers withdraw, because the race will be held on Roboworld, a planet ruled by militant cyborgs whose President has threatened to hang anyone involved. The racers gather on a demilitarized moon of Roboworld, where JP recruits the junk dealer Old Man Mole, who reluctantly accepts Frisbee and his dangerously powerful engine, and Roboworld's Colonel Volton warns the racers that the military will crush the event.

Saboteurs hired by the race commission disable an orbital cannon meant to destroy the Redline mothership as it exits hyperspace, while rebellious miners attack the military's power station. Furious, the President sends his army against the racers as they head into a mined zone hiding Funky Boy, a giant illegal bioweapon that awakens as they approach. The army shells it, wrecking much of the field; JP rights his overturned car and picks up Sonoshee, whose vehicle is destroyed, and Volton defeats Funky Boy by merging with another bioweapon. Frisbee, offered the same rigged deal, refuses to trigger the bomb this time and is rescued from the mobsters by Old Man Mole. In a neck-and-neck finish with the reigning champion, Machinehead, a drunken Mole accidentally sets off the explosive, hurling JP and Sonoshee over the line, and JP wins by the length of his pompadour before the two declare their love.

Redline took seven years to make and used more than 100,000 hand-drawn frames. It premiered at the Locarno International Film Festival on August 14, 2009, and opened in Japan on October 9, 2010. A box-office failure, it found success on home video and became a cult film; Anime News Network gave it an A+, calling it insanely exhilarating.

plot:
Yu-Gi-Oh!: Bonds Beyond Time is a 2010 Japanese 3D animated science fantasy action film produced to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the anime Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters. It unites the heroes of three series, Yugi Muto of the original, Jaden Yuki of Yu-Gi-Oh! GX and Yusei Fudo of Yu-Gi-Oh! 5D's, against a time-travelling villain. Released in Japanese cinemas on January 23, 2010, it debuted at number six at the box office, and an English-language version was produced by 4Kids Entertainment.

In New Domino City, Yusei Fudo's friends Jack Atlas and Crow Hogan try to lift his spirits with a ride on their Duel Runners. A mysterious Turbo Duelist called Paradox appears and challenges Yusei, then seals his signature monster, Stardust Dragon, inside a card and vanishes. Soon afterwards they find a record of a strange battle in the past in Venice, Italy, which Yusei knows never happened, and New Domino City itself begins to disappear. The Crimson Dragon appears and grants Yusei's Duel Runner the power to travel through time.

In the past, Jaden Yuki is being attacked in Venice by corrupted versions of stolen monsters, among them Stardust Dragon. Yusei arrives with the Crimson Dragon just in time to protect him, and Paradox escapes further back in time. Jaden explains that he had been pursuing Paradox, who stole cards from his friends, and the two agree to join forces.

Years earlier, Maximillion Pegasus is hosting a Duel Monsters tournament in Domino City attended by Yugi Muto and his grandfather. Paradox unleashes his stolen monsters, killing Pegasus, Yugi's grandfather and many others, though Yugi survives. Because Pegasus's death would change the course of history, the Crimson Dragon sends Yusei, Jaden and Yugi thirty minutes back in time to prevent the attack. Yugi agrees to help, and his ancient alter ego takes over.

Confronted, Paradox explains that he comes from a ruined future far beyond Yusei's and believes the world can only be saved by erasing Duel Monsters, created by Pegasus, from history. The three heroes object that this would erase everyone connected with the game, and challenge him to a duel. Combining the powers of their monsters, they defeat him. The three say goodbye and promise to meet again, history is restored, and Yusei returns to his own time, hopeful for the future. Its DVD and Blu-ray releases reached number two on their respective Japanese sales charts.

plot:
Ted is a 2012 American adult animated comedy film directed by Seth MacFarlane, who also co-wrote the screenplay with Alec Sulkin, David Zucker, and Chris Henchy. The film begins on Christmas Eve in 1980, where we see the story of how John Bennett received the teddy bear from his mother. As he grows up, John's love for the teddy bear never fades, and he keeps it as a symbol of his childhood innocence. On Christmas Eve, John's mother dies, leaving him alone with Ted.

Years later, John is now a successful businessman living in Boston. He has moved on from his childhood and is engaged to be married to Samantha (Mila Kunis), but he still keeps Ted as a memento. However, when John's fiancée discovers the teddy bear, she becomes upset, feeling that it's childish.

On the night before their wedding, John decides to take Ted out for one last night of fun and partying. They go to a bar where they meet a group of eccentric characters, including Donny (Giovanni Ribisi), a stoner who is obsessed with the movie "The Big Lebowski." The next morning, John wakes up to find that he has gotten drunk and married a woman named Tami-Lynn (Jessica Barth) in Las Vegas.

Meanwhile, Ted becomes fast friends with Tami-Lynn's brother, Donny, and they start causing chaos in Boston. As the story unfolds, John realizes that he needs to win back Samantha's heart and prove to her that he can be responsible enough to take care of a family.

The plot thickens when John discovers that Ted has become an internet sensation, with millions of fans around the world who love him. However, this newfound fame also attracts the attention of a group of eccentric characters, including a group of hipsters and a group of conservative Christians who are determined to destroy Ted.

As the story reaches its climax, John must confront his own immaturity and learn to grow up in order to save Samantha and win back her love. In the end, John and Samantha reconcile, and John learns to let go of his childhood innocence and accept that he can be a responsible adult.

Throughout the film, Seth MacFarlane's signature humor and wit are on full display, with plenty of references to pop culture and irreverent jokes about sex, relationships, and growing up. The movie features a talented voice cast, including Mark Wahlberg, Mila Kunis, and Giovanni Ribisi, who all deliver memorable performances.

Overall, Ted is a hilarious and heartwarming film that explores the complexities of adulthood and the power of childhood innocence. With its witty dialogue, colorful characters, and irreverent humor, it's no wonder that Ted became a box office hit and spawned a sequel.

plot:
World War Z is a 2013 apocalyptic horror film directed by Marc Forster, starring Brad Pitt as the main character, Gerry Lane.

The movie begins with Gerry Lane, a former United Nations employee, who is tasked with finding a way to stop the rapid spread of a zombie pandemic that has devastated the world. The zombies, known as "fast zombies," are highly aggressive and can move quickly, making them nearly impossible to kill.

Gerry's wife, Karin (Mireille Enos), is infected while trying to protect their children from the zombies, and he sets out on a perilous journey across the globe to find a way to stop the outbreak. He travels to Israel, South Korea, and Wales, where he meets various survivors who share their experiences with him.

As Gerry navigates through the treacherous landscape, he encounters numerous obstacles, including hordes of zombies, hostile human groups, and government conspiracies. Along the way, he also discovers that the zombies are not just mindless creatures but are actually reanimated corpses that have been infected by a virus.

Gerry's quest takes him to Jerusalem, where he meets a young girl named Segen (Fana Mokoena), who has managed to survive the outbreak by hiding in an underground bunker. Gerry and Segen form an unlikely alliance, and together they embark on a mission to find a way to stop the zombies.

The movie culminates with Gerry discovering that the key to stopping the zombies lies in a small town in Wales, where he finds a group of survivors who have developed a vaccine against the virus. However, just as Gerry is about to leave with the vaccine, he realizes that it may not be enough to save humanity.

Throughout the movie, Brad Pitt delivers a strong performance as Gerry Lane, conveying his determination and desperation as he navigates through the zombie-infested world. The film's action sequences are intense and suspenseful, making for an thrilling ride.

While World War Z received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a cult classic among fans of the zombie genre. Its unique take on the zombie apocalypse and its focus on human survival make it a compelling watch.

title: Safe
tagline: She has the code. He is the key.
overview: After a former elite agent rescues a 12-year-old Chinese girl who's been abducted, they find themselves in the middle of a standoff between Triads, the Russian Mafia and high-level corrupt New York City politicians and police.
plot:
Safe is a 2012 American action thriller written and directed by Boaz Yakin. Jason Statham stars as Luke Wright, an ex-cop and former cage fighter who ends up protecting a gifted child hunted by the Russian mafia, Chinese triads and corrupt New York police, with Chris Sarandon, Robert John Burke and James Hong in supporting roles.

After Luke accidentally wins a fixed fight, Russian mob boss Emile Docheski has his son Vassily and his men murder Luke's pregnant wife and vows to kill anyone Luke grows close to, leaving him homeless and adrift. In China, the young math prodigy Mei is abducted by triad boss Han Jiao, who uses her as a human calculator so his operation leaves no digital trail, and is sent to New York under the watch of the brutal Quan Chang. A year later Han has her memorize a long number, but the Russians ambush them and seize her, only to be attacked in turn by police working for the corrupt Captain Wolf, who is in Han's pay. Mei escapes into a subway station where Luke is contemplating suicide; recognizing one of his wife's killers among her pursuers, Luke kills the Russians, saves her from two crooked detectives and flees with her. In a hotel she explains the number, which Luke guesses is a safe combination, but Quan tracks her through her phone and recaptures her.

The mayor, Danny Tremello, warns Wolf that Luke was really a government assassin lent to the city after 9/11 alongside his former partner, Alex Rosen, to eliminate crime bosses, until Luke quit after exposing Wolf's corrupt squad. Luke kidnaps Vassily and forces Emile to reveal that the number opens a guarded Chinatown safe holding $30 million. He recruits Wolf's detectives with the promise of money, fights through the triads to the safe, then kills the detectives when Wolf betrays him. He bribes Alex, now the mayor's aide, to rescue Mei, and learns that a second safe holds the mayor's disc of evidence against every crime syndicate in the city. After Alex kills Quan to take Mei, Luke obtains a copy of the disc, and Mei wounds Alex during a standoff, letting Luke finish him. Luke returns Vassily through Wolf, pays Han for Mei's freedom, hides copies of the disc as insurance and heads to Seattle so Mei can attend a school for gifted children.

Shot in Philadelphia and New York on a $30 million budget, Safe was released by Lionsgate on April 27, 2012, and grossed $40.6 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with 59% on Rotten Tomatoes and 55 on Metacritic.

Marley, a puppy some call the world's worst dog, is in the care of Bodi, a boy who has long begged his mother for a dog of his own. While Carol is away on a business trip, Bodi and Marley stay with Fred, a strict grandfather who insists on chores. On a walk, Bodi meets Kaycee, whose parents run a pug rescue center and who plans to enter three of her pugs in a puppy championship to raise money for it. Because each team needs three dogs, she introduces Bodi to Mrs. Crouch, whose two Labrador puppies, Fuchsia and Moose, join Marley, and the trio begin training for the course.

Meanwhile, Hans, whose three dogs, Turbo, Liesl and Axel, were the previous year's champions, trains them cruelly with shock collars. The day before the contest, Hans's assistant Henkle, posing as a spa worker, kidnaps Bodi's puppies along with Dundee, an Australian Shepherd also entered in the event, and locks them up with two German Shepherds, Trouble and Chipper. After pretending to menace the pups, the big dogs help them escape with a homemade seesaw that catapults them out, and the dirty puppies make it back to Bodi.

Since Marley belongs to a relative, Bodi cannot keep him, but Hans loses his dogs: a family adopts Liesl and Axel, and Carol, now convinced her son is responsible, lets him adopt Turbo instead of sending him to a shelter. 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment released the film on DVD on June 1, 2011.

Overall, Red Tails is a powerful tribute to the Tuskegee Airmen, who played a crucial role in the Allied victory during World War II. The film's themes of perseverance, courage, and identity are timeless and universal, making it a compelling watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, The Loft is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of friendship, trauma, and the darker aspects of human nature. With its twisty plot and complex characters, it is a must-see for fans of psychological thrillers.

title: Carjacked
tagline: It's her car. Don't tell her what to do with it.
overview: A single mom and her child are carjacked by a bank robber who has no intention of letting them go.
plot:
Carjacked is a 2011 American thriller directed by John Bonito, whose previous feature was the action film The Marine, from a screenplay by Michael and Sherry Compton. Produced by Hollywood Media Bridge and released direct to video, it stars Maria Bello as Lorraine Burton and Stephen Dorff as Roy, with Connor Hill as Lorraine's young son Chad, Joanna Cassidy as an irascible member of a therapy group. The film runs 89 minutes.

Lorraine is a recently separated single mother with a low-paying job, struggling to make ends meet while raising her ten-year-old son. She buys gas a few dollars at a time, settles for frozen convenience-store snacks instead of pizza, attends group therapy sessions where she is encouraged to stand up for herself, and has to fend off her estranged husband, a soldier, who is seeking sole custody of Chad. One night, during a stop at a gas station, mother and son are carjacked by Roy, a charismatic bank robber on the run, who takes over the car and orders Lorraine to drive toward an uncertain destination, with no intention of letting them go. Much of the story unfolds inside the vehicle as the two adults trade barbs, alternate between moments of uneasy rapport and failed escape attempts, and engage in a power struggle over her and the boy's fate. Lorraine misses several chances to alert others, including at a police roadblock, and resorts to writing her license plate number and a plea for help in a diner restroom and to bouts of reckless driving. In the final stretch, the film turns into an action thriller, as Lorraine, who has finally had enough, takes up a shotgun and the chase ends in a massive pile-up.

Released on DVD in the United States in November 2011, Carjacked received largely negative reviews, with critics complaining that the promising premise and capable leads were wasted on a flat, implausible script. David Nusair of Reel Film Reviews gave it one star out of four, finding no menace or suspense, unconvincing dialogue and a heavy-handed self-empowerment subplot. Jason Rugaard of Movie Mavericks likened it to a lesser version of A Perfect World, praising Dorff's screen presence but faulting the static staging and a laughable script, with action arriving only after an hour. Jim McLennan of Film Blitz considered Bello and Dorff well cast and some of their conversations almost engaging, and enjoyed the outlandish climax, but wished the rest of the film had shared its energy.

title: Tom and Jerry & The Wizard of Oz

tagline: They're off to see the Wizard, the wonderful Wizard of Oz!
overview: After a deadly storm, Tom and Jerry find themselves stranded on an unknown island ruled by the evil Wizard of Oz. As they try to find their way back home, they worry for their master Dorothy's safety.
plot:
Tom and Jerry & The Wizard of Oz is a 2011 American animated musical fantasy comedy released direct to video, retelling Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer's 1939 film The Wizard of Oz, itself based on L. Frank Baum's 1900 novel, with the cat and mouse Tom and Jerry and other MGM cartoon characters written into the story and seen from their point of view. Directed by Spike Brandt and Tony Cervone, who also produced, from a script by Gene Grillo, it was made by Warner Bros. Animation and Turner Entertainment, with music by Michael Tavera and Sam Register as executive producer. Film scholar David McGowan has observed that the crossover was only possible because a series of mergers and acquisitions brought both properties under one media conglomerate.

On a Kansas farm, Aunt Em asks Tom and Jerry, here Dorothy Gale's pets alongside her dog Toto, to keep an eye on the girl. When a cyclone strikes, the pair are swept away to the Land of Oz and land on the yellow brick road. From Tuffy, a young Munchkin mouse, they learn that Dorothy and Toto have already set off for the Emerald City, and the three follow. Along the way they save Dorothy and her new companions, the Scarecrow, the Tin Man and the Cowardly Lion, from a rockslide engineered by the Wicked Witch of the West, and run into familiar faces such as Butch and Droopy.

The Wizard agrees to grant the travellers' wishes only if they bring him the Witch's broomstick. At her castle, the Witch's guards corner Dorothy and her friends and the Witch sets the Scarecrow on fire, but Tom, Jerry and Tuffy douse him with a bucket of water that also splashes the Witch, who melts away. When the Wizard then refuses to keep his promise, Jerry spots the man behind the curtain and, with Tom's help, exposes him. Back home in Kansas, no one believes Dorothy's story except Tom and Jerry, who confirm it.

Grey DeLisle voices Dorothy, with Nikki Yanofsky providing her singing voice; Joe Alaskey voices the Wizard, Butch and Droopy, Michael Gough the Scarecrow, Rob Paulsen the Tin Man, Todd Stashwick the Lion, Frances Conroy Aunt Em and Glinda, Laraine Newman the Wicked Witch, Stephen Root Uncle Henry and Kath Soucie Tuffy. Warner Home Video released it on DVD and Blu-ray on 23 August 2011. Common Sense Media gave it three stars out of five, and a sequel, Tom and Jerry: Back to Oz, followed in 2016.

title: Lincoln
tagline: The hours that changed history.
overview: The revealing story of the 16th US President's tumultuous final months in office. In a nation divided by war and the strong winds of change, Lincoln pursues a course of action designed to end the war, unite the country and abolish slavery. With the moral courage and fierce determination to succeed, his choices during this critical moment will change the fate of generations to come.
plot:
Lincoln is a 2012 American historical drama directed and produced by Steven Spielberg, starring Daniel Day-Lewis as President Abraham Lincoln. The screenplay by Tony Kushner was loosely based on Doris Kearns Goodwin's biography Team of Rivals: The Political Genius of Abraham Lincoln. The cast includes Sally Field as Mary Todd Lincoln, David Strathairn as Secretary of State William Seward, Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Robert Lincoln, James Spader, Hal Holbrook and Tommy Lee Jones as Thaddeus Stevens.

The film covers the final months of Lincoln's life, focusing on his campaign in January 1865 to have the House of Representatives pass the Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution, which would abolish slavery. With the Civil War nearing its end, Lincoln fears that his Emancipation Proclamation, issued as a wartime measure, could be overturned by the courts once peace returns, and that the amendment will be impossible to pass after the Southern states rejoin the Union. He is determined to secure its approval before the war ends.

The amendment needs the support of conservative Republicans and of several Democrats, many of them lame ducks who lost their seats in the 1864 elections. Lincoln agrees to let Francis Preston Blair open peace negotiations with the Confederacy in return for his influence over conservative votes, a risky move because news of peace talks could doom the amendment. With Seward, Lincoln enlists political operatives who offer government jobs to wavering Democrats, while the radical abolitionist Thaddeus Stevens must be persuaded to moderate his views for the sake of victory. At the same time, Lincoln struggles with family tensions, including Mary's grief over the death of their son Willie and his eldest son Robert's desire to enlist.

Spielberg's film is a dialogue-driven portrait of political maneuvering, showing Lincoln as both a moral leader and a shrewd tactician.

Lincoln was released in November 2012 and grossed about 275.3 million dollars worldwide against a 65 million dollar budget. Critics acclaimed it, giving it 90 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes. At the 85th Academy Awards it received twelve nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director, and won Best Production Design and Best Actor for Day-Lewis, his third win in that category.

tagline: There's a Princess in every girl!
overview: Barbie stars as Blair Willows, a kind-hearted girl who is chosen to attend Princess Charm School: a magical, modern place that teaches dancing, how to have tea parties, and proper princess manners. plot:
Barbie: Princess Charm School is a 2011 computer-animated fantasy film directed by Zeke Norton and written by Elise Allen, produced by Mattel Entertainment under the Barbie Entertainment name together with Rainmaker Entertainment. The twentieth installment in the Barbie film series, it was released on DVD on September 13, 2011, and made its television debut on Nickelodeon two months later. Barbie stars as Blair Willows, an ordinary girl who discovers a hidden royal destiny.

In the kingdom of Gardania, teenage Blair works as a waitress in a small café to help support her adoptive mother and her younger sister, Emily. One day she learns from a television broadcast that she has won the lottery for a scholarship to Princess Charm School, a magical academy where princesses from many kingdoms are educated and where commoners can train as Lady Royals, the advisors to princesses. Emily confesses that she entered Blair's name many times, and their mother encourages her to seize the opportunity.

At the school, Blair is welcomed by a golden retriever named Prince and Headmistress Privet, and is assigned a fairy assistant called Grace. She befriends her roommates, Princess Isla, who mixes electronic music, and the sporty Princess Hadley. She also meets the haughty Dame Devin, sister-in-law of the late queen, and her daughter Delancy, who is due to be crowned ruler of Gardania at graduation. Clumsy and struggling in her classes, Blair improves with the headmistress's help despite repeated sabotage by Devin and Delancy. Exploring the palace, the girls notice Blair's striking resemblance to the late Queen Isabella and come to suspect that she may be the long-lost Princess Sophia, believed to have died with the royal family. Determined to find the legendary crown that glows only for the true heir, Blair and her friends must outwit Dame Devin before the coronation.

The film is a lighthearted fairy tale about friendship, kindness and self-confidence, emphasizing that true royalty comes from character.

Like other entries in the long-running series, Princess Charm School was made for a young audience and distributed primarily on home video, following its DVD debut in September 2011 with a Nickelodeon broadcast that November.

The movie also touches on the idea of identity, particularly in relation to one's cultural background and the expectations placed upon women by their families.

Throughout the film, the director skillfully weaves together elements of comedy, drama, and romance, creating a narrative that is both humorous and poignant. As Olya grapples with her own desires and sense of self, she must also confront the societal pressures and family obligations that threaten to undermine her autonomy and happiness.

Ultimately, You May Not Kiss the Bride is a heartwarming and engaging film that celebrates the complexities and nuances of human relationships, while also offering a humorous and relatable take on the challenges of love and identity.

title: The Lorax
tagline: Meet the original force of nature.
overview: A 12-year-old boy searches for the one thing that will enable him to win the affection of the girl of his dreams. To find it he must discover the story of the Lorax, the grumpy yet charming creature who fights to protect his world.
plot:
The Lorax is a 2012 American animated musical fantasy comedy film directed by Chris Renaud and Kyle Balda, and produced by Illumination Entertainment. The movie is based on the children's book of the same name by Dr. Seuss.

In the beginning, we are introduced to the beautiful and vibrant forest of Thneedville, where a young boy named Ted (voiced by Zac Efron) lives with his mother. Ted loves to play outside and explore nature, but his mother is more concerned about making money and buying things for him. She buys him a Truffula tree seed, which she hopes will grow into a beautiful Truffula tree.

However, the seed is actually a Truffula tuft, which is a small, colorful tuft that grows on the Truffula trees. Ted plants the tuft in his backyard and takes care of it, but he soon realizes that it's not growing into a real tree. He decides to buy more tufts from the Once-ler (voiced by Ed Helms), who claims they will grow into beautiful Truffula trees.

The Once-ler tells Ted that the only way to make the tufts grow is to chop down all the Truffula trees in the forest and use their tufts to make a product called Thneed. The Once-ler explains that he needs the tufts to make the Thneeds, which are a type of plastic-like material used for various products.

As the story progresses, we see the devastating effects of the Once-ler's actions on the environment and the Truffula trees. The forest becomes barren and polluted, and the creatures that live there begin to disappear. The Lorax (voiced by Danny DeVito), a small, furry creature who speaks up for the environment, tries to stop the Once-ler from chopping down the trees.

The Once-ler ignores the Lorax's warnings and continues to chop down the Truffula trees, using their tufts to make Thneeds. The forest becomes increasingly polluted, and the creatures begin to disappear. Ted realizes that his mother's actions have contributed to the destruction of the forest and decides to take action.

In the end, Ted convinces his mother to stop buying Thneeds and instead focus on taking care of nature. The Once-ler is left alone, surrounded by the remnants of his destructive actions. The Lorax appears one last time, and the Once-ler finally understands the importance of preserving the environment.

The movie ends with a message about the importance of taking care of our planet and respecting the natural world. The Truffula trees begin to grow again, and the forest is restored to its former beauty. Ted and his mother are seen playing in the forest, surrounded by the beautiful Truffula trees, and the Lorax is seen watching over them.

Overall, The Lorax is a heartwarming story about the importance of environmental conservation and the power of individual actions to make a difference.

title: Vamps
tagline: Dating Sucks
overview: The modern-day story focuses on two beautiful young vampires who are living the good nightlife in New York until love enters the picture and each has to make a choice that will jeopardize their immortality.
plot:
Vamps is a 2012 American comedy horror film written and directed by Amy Heckerling. Alicia Silverstone and Krysten Ritter lead a cast that includes Dan Stevens, Richard Lewis, Wallace Shawn, Justin Kirk, Kristen Johnston, Malcolm McDowell and Sigourney Weaver. The story follows two vampires who try to keep up with trends and stay youthful while living without human blood and dealing with the malevolent vampire who created them.

Goody and Stacy are vampires enjoying life in New York City. Goody was turned in 1841 by the vampire Cisserus, and after leaving the man she loved in the 1960s she struggled with her existence until Cisserus turned Stacy in 1992. Goody taught Stacy to live on rat blood and use her new powers, while Stacy helps Goody stay young and fashionable. Goody hides her true age, fearing that Stacy will see her as old. At a vampire support meeting she learns that if their maker, or "stem", Cisserus is killed, they will revert to their human ages. Working as an exterminator at a hospital, Goody meets her former boyfriend Danny for the first time since the 1960s. They reconnect while she pretends to be her own daughter, but Danny discovers the truth when he sees her bite a man to stop a stroke, and she explains that she left so that he could build a life with someone who could grow old with him.

When the government uses the Patriot Act to hunt vampires, Goody devises a plan to alter the records of every vampire in the New York area during a solar eclipse, and the vampires celebrate its success with a party, though Cisserus massacres a restaurant full of people. Stacy begins dating Joey, a college student who turns out to be the son of the vampire hunter Dr. Van Helsing. After seeing Stacy climb down his building before dawn, Joey accepts what she is. Stacy then becomes pregnant and learns that the baby can survive only if she becomes human again, which requires killing Cisserus. With Joey and Van Helsing, the two women kill him. Stacy, now forty, looks much the same, but Goody ages rapidly. Revealing her true age, she visits Times Square with Stacy and Joey to reminisce and crumbles to dust as the sun rises. Years later, Van Helsing plays with Stacy and Joey's daughter, named after Goody, and is amused to see that she has fangs.

The film received a limited theatrical release on November 2, 2012, followed by Blu-ray and DVD editions. Reviews were mixed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting a 56% approval rating from 18 critics.

title: The Big Year
tagline: Everyone is searching for something.
overview: Three fanatical bird-watchers spend an entire year competing to spot the highest number of species as El Nino sends an extraordinary variety of rare breeds flying up into the U.S., but they quickly discover that there are more important things than coming out on top of the competition.
plot:
The Big Year is a 2011 American comedy directed by David Frankel from a screenplay by Howard Franklin, starring Steve Martin, Jack Black and Owen Wilson, with Rashida Jones and Jim Parsons in supporting roles. It is loosely based on Mark Obmascik's 2004 non-fiction book The Big Year: A Tale of Man, Nature and Fowl Obsession, which chronicled three real birders competing to spot the most bird species in North America in a single calendar year. The film keeps that premise but replaces the real participants with fictional characters.

Three men set out to complete a Big Year. Kenny Bostick, a roofing contractor played by Wilson, holds the existing record of 732 birds and guards it obsessively, even though his wife Jessica had hoped this would be the year they focused on having a child, and his fixation on birding has already cost him two marriages. Brad Harris, played by Black, is a 36-year-old Baltimore computer programmer who can identify almost any bird by its call alone; divorced, living with his parents and stuck in a job he dislikes, he hopes the challenge will give him purpose and earn his father's respect. Stu Preissler, played by Martin, is the founder of a successful Manhattan chemical company who wants to retire, but a pending merger means his two successors keep summoning him back to New York.

Over the course of the year the three criss-cross the continent chasing sightings, while competing with each other and many other birders. Brad and Stu become friends and help one another, and Brad falls for a fellow birder named Ellie. Bostick, meanwhile, uses underhanded tricks to inflate his own count and sabotage his rivals, at the expense of his marriage.

By December, Stu has happily retired and is enjoying his new grandson, Brad has begun a relationship with Ellie, and Bostick finds himself alone after his wife leaves him. When the results are published, Bostick has set a new record of 755 species, with Brad second and Stu fourth. Brad reflects that although Bostick got more birds, he and Stu got more of everything else. The film closes with Brad and Ellie birding together on a rocky coast and Stu hiking in the Rockies with his grandson, while Bostick birds alone in China.

Shot in and around Vancouver in 2010, the film drew mixed reviews, though the three leads were praised, and it was a box-office bomb, grossing about $7.4 million against a $41 million budget.

title: A Cinderella Story: Once Upon a Song

overview: In this modern telling of the classic tale, aspiring singer Katie Gibbs falls for the new boy at her performing arts high school. But Katie's wicked stepmother and stepsister are scheming to crush her dream before she can sing her way into his heart.
plot:
A Cinderella Story: Once Upon a Song is a 2011 American musical teen comedy film directed by Damon Santostefano, a standalone sequel to Another Cinderella Story (2008) and the third installment in the A Cinderella Story series. Lucy Hale stars as Katie Gibbs, an aspiring singer, with Freddie Stroma as Luke Morgan, Missi Pyle as her stepmother, Gail, Megan Park as her stepsister, Bev, and Matthew Lintz as her stepbrother, Victor. It was released on DVD and digital platforms in September 2011 and premiered on ABC Family in January 2012.

Katie, an orphaned teenager with a beautiful voice, lives with her adoptive family, the Van Ravensways, who treat her as a servant: the shallow Gail, the spoiled Bev and the mischievous Victor. She accepts their mistreatment without complaint, fearing that Gail will send her back to foster care. Gail is the headmistress of the Wellesley Academy of the Arts, where Guy Morgan, the English head of Kensington Records, enrolls his son, Luke. Hoping to change her life, Katie slips her demo CD into Guy's briefcase. Guy asks Luke to produce an upcoming showcase at the academy, though Luke is reluctant to follow in his father's footsteps.

title: God Bless America
tagline: Taking out the trash, one jerk at a time.
overview: Fed up with the cruelty and stupidity of American culture, an unlikely duo goes on a killing spree, killing reality TV stars, bigots and others they find repugnant.
plot:
God Bless America is a 2011 American black comedy film written and directed by Bobcat Goldthwait. Blending political satire with dark humor, it stars Joel Murray as Frank Murdoch, a middle-aged man, and Tara Lynne Barr as Roxy, a teenage girl, who embark on a killing spree after bonding over their shared disgust with what American culture has become in the years after 9/11. The cast also includes Alexie Gilmore, Mackenzie Brooke Smith and Travis Wester.

Frank is an insurance salesman who is sickened by the cruelty and vapidity he sees in television, talk radio and the internet. Divorced, he is kept awake by his neighbors' screaming baby, while his spoiled young daughter Ava lives with his ex-wife. In a single stretch he is fired from his job and told by an indifferent doctor that he has a terminal brain tumor. Watching television that night, he sees a talent show mocking a disabled contestant named Steven Clark and then a reality program about Chloe, a monstrously spoiled teenager. On the verge of suicide, Frank instead steals his neighbor's car, drives to Chloe's school and shoots her. Her classmate Roxanne "Roxy" Harmon witnesses the killing, applauds it and follows Frank to his motel, where she talks him out of killing himself. Insisting that only genuinely awful people should die, the pair go on to murder Chloe's parents and then roam the country targeting rude moviegoers, a man who double-parks, extremist protesters and a right-wing political commentator, while Roxy dreams of escaping with Frank to France. Frank's world shifts when his doctor calls to say the tumor diagnosis was a mix-up with another patient, and again when he learns that Roxy has lied about her troubled home life; her parents are in fact respectable and worried about her. After the two part ways, Frank arms himself with an assault rifle and storms the studio of the talent show, where he takes the audience hostage and delivers a speech about the state of American society as police surround the building.

God Bless America premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 9, 2011, and also screened at South by Southwest, before a video-on-demand release in April 2012 and a theatrical release in May. It holds a 65% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it uneven and somewhat thin but with ideas of primal appeal, and a Metacritic score of 56.

title: Special Forces

overview: Afghanistan. War correspondent Elsa Casanova is taken hostage by the Taliban. Faced with her imminent execution, a Special Forces unit is dispatched to free her. plot:
Special Forces (French: Forces spéciales) is a 2011 French war action film directed by Stéphane Rybojad, starring Diane Kruger, Djimon Hounsou, Benoît Magimel, Denis Ménochet, Mehdi Nebbou, Raphaël Personnaz and Tchéky Karyo. Shot on location in France, Djibouti and Tajikistan, it follows a team of elite French commandos on a desperate hostage-rescue mission on the border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

Elsa Casanova, a French journalist based in Kabul, publishes an article branding the warlord Zaief "the butcher of Kabul". Her informant Maina warns her that Zaief will seek revenge, and returns to him expecting to be killed in an honour killing. Elsa, refusing to abandon her, tries to save her with the help of her friend and colleague Amen, who has urged her to leave the country. Zaief's men ambush and capture them both. Amen tells Elsa to show no fear, but she breaks down when their friend Salemani is brutally murdered in front of her, and Zaief releases a video of the killing that reaches the French government.

A small team of French special forces operators, drawn mainly from the naval commandos, is sent in to rescue the hostages. They locate Zaief's hideout in Pakistan and witness Maina's execution before freeing Elsa and Amen. But a bullet destroys their radio during the escape, leaving them unable to contact their base or call for extraction. With no other choice, the commandos set out on foot across the mountains toward the Khyber Pass and the Afghan border, pursued relentlessly by Zaief and his gunmen.

The journey becomes a brutal ordeal. In a village where Elsa asks for shelter, one commando is killed by a sniper, and when Zaief's fighters arrive the warlord himself kills Amen. One by one the soldiers fall: the team's marksman dies drawing the enemy away, another succumbs to his wounds in a snowstorm, and a fourth is killed in a further attack, in which the commando Kovax finally kills Zaief after the warlord seizes Elsa as a hostage. An avalanche then strikes the survivors; Kovax saves Elsa and his wounded comrade Tic-Tac but breaks his leg, and the two men persuade Elsa to go on alone. Exhausted, she reaches a road and is rescued, then refuses to be sent home, and Admiral Guezennec carries her to a helicopter to lead the search that finds both men alive.

The film was poorly received by English-language critics, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 15% approval; the Los Angeles Times called it a leaden, video-game-style war film.

The film's protagonist, Jay, is a complex character whose sense of self is constantly challenged as he navigates a world that seems to be spiraling out of control. As he becomes more entrenched in the cult, his grip on reality begins to slip, and he finds himself questioning what is real and what is just a product of his own paranoia.

Furthermore, Kill List is a film that critiques the notion of masculinity and the societal expectations placed upon men. Jay's character is a prime example of this, as he struggles to reconcile his own desires and needs with the expectations of those around him. The cult, in particular, serves as a symbol of toxic masculinity, where men are encouraged to suppress their emotions and vulnerabilities in order to conform to societal norms.

Overall, Kill List is a thought-provoking film that challenges its audience to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the ways in which we navigate the complexities of our own identities.

plot:
The Human Centipede 2 (Full Sequence) is a 2011 psychological body horror film written, directed and co-produced by Tom Six, a Dutch and British co-production and the sequel to The Human Centipede (First Sequence) (2009). Shot mostly in black and white, it stars Laurence R. Harvey as a disturbed Londoner obsessed with the first film, with Ashlynn Yennie, who appeared in the original, playing a fictionalised version of herself. The British Board of Film Classification initially refused it a certificate, and it was only released in the UK after extensive cuts.

Martin Lomax is a short, asthmatic and mentally impaired man who works the night shift as a security attendant in an East London car park, where he watches The Human Centipede over and over on his laptop. He lives in a squalid council flat with his cruel mother, who blames him for his father's imprisonment for abusing him as a child. His psychiatrist, Dr. Sebring, behaves inappropriately towards him and keeps him heavily medicated, dismissing his fixation on the film and on his pet centipede as a passing phase linked to his childhood trauma.

Martin's obsession turns into a plan to build his own twelve-person centipede. He rents a run-down warehouse and begins abducting people from the car park and elsewhere, including a young couple, a pregnant woman and her partner, and two drunk young women. When his mother discovers and destroys his scrapbook and tries to get rid of his centipede, he kills her, then lures his hostile neighbour into a trap. He murders Dr. Sebring after spotting him on a security camera and abducts the people with him. His final victim is Ashlynn Yennie herself, whom he lures to London with a fake audition for a Quentin Tarantino film.

With no medical training, Martin assembles his centipede from his crude sketches using hammers, staple guns and duct tape, and several victims die or are left for dead. The film depicts the ensuing torture in graphic, deliberately repellent detail. The pregnant woman revives, flees and escapes by car after giving birth. When the chain breaks apart, Martin kills most of the captives, but Ashlynn turns on him before he fatally wounds her. In a final scene he is back in his tollbooth watching the first film, leaving it unclear how much was real.

The film was widely condemned by critics for its extreme content, holding a 28% Rotten Tomatoes approval rating, and was followed by The Human Centipede 3 (Final Sequence) in 2015.

As Gary delves deeper into the case, he discovers that Segal is involved in some shady dealings and has connections to the police department. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Gary's obsession with finding the perpetrator is not just about justice, but also about redemption and proving himself as a father. The film builds towards a tense confrontation between Gary and Segal, which ultimately leads to a dramatic showdown.

Throughout the movie, Cage delivers a powerful performance as Gary Fencik, bringing depth and nuance to the character's complex emotions. January Jones provides solid support as his wife Maureen, who is struggling to cope with their situation. As Ottway and Danny journey deeper into the wilderness, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and encounters with the wolves. Along the way, Ottway begins to see parallels between his own grief and the struggles of the wolves.

In a dramatic turn of events, Ottway and Danny are forced to flee from the pack after they stumble upon one of their dens. As they try to outrun the wolves, Ottway is gravely injured by Bear's attack.

As Ottway lies dying, he comes to terms with his own mortality and finds a sense of peace in the natural world around him. He also begins to see that the wolves are not just mindless killers, but are actually an integral part of the ecosystem.

In the end, Ottway dies from his injuries, but not before passing on his knowledge and understanding of the wolves to Danny. The film ends with Danny standing alone in the wilderness, surrounded by the very creatures that had brought him closer to healing and finding peace.

plot:
Oblivion is a 2013 science fiction film directed by Joseph Kosinski and written by Josie McClelland, Karl Gajdusek, and Michael DeLuise. The movie stars Tom Cruise as Jack Harper, a repairman who lives on a post-apocalyptic Earth.

The story begins in the year 2177, where humanity has retreated to a generation ship called the Ark, fleeing a catastrophic event known as "The Great War" that devastated the planet. The war was caused by an alien invasion, which wiped out most of human civilization and left behind only a few scattered settlements.

Jack Harper is one of these survivors, living on a floating city called New York, where he works as a repairman for the company that maintains the city's defenses against the alien threat. Jack's life is mundane and lonely, with his only companion being his AI assistant, Sara (Andrea Riseborough).

However, Jack's life takes a dramatic turn when he encounters a mysterious woman named Julia (Olga Kurylenko), who claims to be from the Ark. She reveals that she has been sent to Earth to investigate the alien threat and that she needs Jack's help to complete his mission.

As they journey across the planet, Jack and Julia discover that the aliens have created a massive machine known as "The Oblivion," which is destroying entire cities on Earth in order to harvest their resources. The machine is also creating a rift in space-time, causing time dilation effects that are accelerating the aging process of those who live on Earth.

Jack and Julia soon realize that they are not alone in their quest. A group of rogue soldiers, led by Colonel Spear (Morgan Freeman), are also searching for the Oblivion, but with sinister intentions. The soldiers plan to use the machine's power to gain control over the Ark and rule humanity.

As Jack and Julia navigate through the treacherous landscape, they encounter various obstacles and challenges, including hostile alien creatures and treacherous terrain. Along the way, Jack begins to question his own identity and purpose, as he grapples with the consequences of his actions in the past.

The climax of the movie takes place at the Oblivion's core, where Jack and Julia must confront Colonel Spear and his team. In a thrilling showdown, Jack uses his knowledge of the machine's mechanics to disable it, saving humanity from destruction.

In the end, Jack and Julia succeed in their mission, but not without sacrifices. The movie concludes with Jack returning to New York, where he is welcomed as a hero. However, as he looks out at the city, he realizes that he has been given a new purpose: to protect humanity from the alien threat and ensure its survival.

Overall, Oblivion is a visually stunning film with impressive special effects, but it also explores themes of identity, sacrifice, and redemption in a thought-provoking way.

title: Naruto Shippuden the Movie: Blood Prison

overview: After his capture for attempted assassination of the Raikage, leader of Kumogakure, as well as killing Jōnin from Kirigakure and Iwagakure, Naruto is imprisoned in Hōzukijou: A criminal containment facility known as the Blood Prison. Mui, the castle master, uses the ultimate imprisonment technique to steal power from the prisoners, which is when Naruto notices his life has been targeted. Thus begins the battle to uncover the truth behind the mysterious murders and prove Naruto's innocence.
plot:
Naruto Shippuden the Movie: Blood Prison (also titled Naruto the Movie: Blood Prison) is a 2011 Japanese animated action fantasy film based on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga and anime. Directed by Masahiko Murata for Studio Pierrot from a script by Akira Higashiyama, it is the eighth Naruto film and the fifth in the Shippuden era, and it sends its hero into a notorious prison after he is accused of an attempted assassination.

A hooded figure attacks the Fourth Raikage of the Hidden Cloud Village and, when unmasked, appears to be Naruto Uzumaki. Back in the Hidden Leaf, Tsunade announces that Naruto is wanted for the assassination attempt and for killing ninja of other villages, and despite his protests he is sent to Hōzuki Castle, the "Blood Prison" in the Hidden Grass Village. Its warden, Mui, places a seal on him that cripples his chakra, so every escape attempt and every challenge to Mui ends in agony and solitary confinement. Admired by the other inmates, Naruto tries again to flee by sea and is rescued from a whirlpool by Ryūzetsu, a Hidden Grass agent working undercover, who reveals that Mui framed him and sacrificed his own son Muku to the mysterious Box of Ultimate Bliss years earlier. Aided by the scheming inmate Maroi, the pair stage a riot, but Mui captures Naruto and uses his chakra to open the box, wishing for his son's return. A grown Muku emerges, stabs his father and transforms into the demon Satori, which can anticipate its enemies' attacks. Naruto, in Sage Mode, and the toad Gamabunta are overwhelmed until Killer B and Naruto's friends arrive, and Tsunade reveals that the arrest was a ruse to get Naruto inside to destroy the box. Realising Satori reads fears rather than thoughts, Naruto fights it on even terms and, with the dying Mui's help, defeats it with his Rasenshuriken. Muku ends both his father's life and his own, and Ryūzetsu gives her life to revive the mortally wounded Naruto. At her grave he ties on her headband and vows to cherish the life she gave him.

Junko Takeuchi voices Naruto, with Masaki Terasoma as Mui, Mie Sonozaki as Ryūzetsu and Yūichi Nakamura as Muku; the English dub stars Maile Flanagan, Matthew Mercer and Carrie Keranen. Distributed by Toho, it opened in Japan in July 2011 and grossed about ¥800 million. Yusuke Kamiji performed the theme song "Otakebi", and Viz Media released the film in North America on February 18, 2014.

title: Zombie Apocalypse
tagline: Mankind Survived... But Not Alive.
overview: Months after a zombie plague has wiped out 90 percent of the American population, a small group of survivors fight their way cross-country to a rumored refuge on the island of Catalina.
plot:
Zombie Apocalypse, also released as 2012: Zombie Apocalypse, is a 2011 American zombie horror film produced by The Asylum for the Syfy channel. Directed by Nick Lyon, it stars Ving Rhames, Taryn Manning, Johnny Pacar, Lesley-Ann Brandt and Gary Weeks. It premiered on Syfy on October 29, 2011, and was released on DVD and Blu-ray that December.

Flashbacks explain that in June 2012 a virus known as VM2 was discovered in a woman in France. Within a month most of Europe was infected, and the disease spread around the world, turning its victims into flesh-eating zombies. Six months later, the plague has killed about ninety percent of the population of the United States.

Near Los Angeles, three survivors, Ramona, Billie and Kevin, are searching an auto repair shop for supplies when the noise draws a horde of zombies. Kevin is bitten before another group of survivors, Henry, Julian, Cassie and Mack, arrives to fight off the attackers; Cassie kills Kevin as he begins to turn. The two groups join forces, and Mack reveals that they are heading for Catalina Island, where a survivor camp is said to await anyone who can reach the ferry. On the way, they scavenge a surf shop, are attacked by a fast-moving "runner" zombie, and are forced to kill a stray dog that becomes infected. A supposed safe zone at a high school turns out to be abandoned, and when the gym is suddenly flooded with zombies, Billie is bitten.

The group is split apart in a burning neighborhood. Mack, Julian and Ramona are rescued by a band of archers, Brockton, Myrah and Sarah, while Henry and Cassie continue on alone. Julian is bitten when a zombie bursts out of a portable toilet, and before he can sacrifice himself as a distraction he begins to turn, forcing Mack to kill him. Henry and Cassie collect grenades from an abandoned army post, and an explosion they set off helps the others escape. The groups reunite on the rooftops and fight their way to the docks, where they find supplies and quarantine instructions, but also a pair of infected tigers. Brockton is killed and Henry is bitten, and Cassie grants his request to end his life. In the final scene, the remaining survivors watch as the ferry approaches.

Reviews were mixed to negative. The A.V. Club dismissed it as a dull riff on The Walking Dead, and Dread Central and DVD Talk found it routine, while Starburst considered it a cheap and cheerful genre film with enough good ideas and performances to entertain.

title: Jack Reacher
