plot:
Jack Reacher is a 2012 American action thriller film directed by Christopher McQuarrie and based on the novel of the same name by Lee Child.

The movie begins with Jack Reacher (Tom Cruise), a former Major in the United States Army Military Police Corps, who has been traveling across the country for months. He arrives in Margrave, Georgia, where he meets a local police chief, Captain Will Sword (David Morse). Reacher is initially mistaken for a fugitive and arrested by the police, but he soon proves himself to be an innocent man.

Reacher's attention is drawn to a mysterious case involving a former Army officer, Major General James Greer (Robert Duvall), who has been accused of murdering his wife. The general claims that he was framed and wants Reacher's help in clearing his name. Reacher agrees to assist the general, but soon discovers that there are more complex forces at play.

As Reacher delves deeper into the case, he uncovers a conspiracy involving a corrupt government agent, Captain Susan Turner (Rosamund Pike), who is working with a private military company called Enoch Edwards Inc. The company is involved in a plot to sell advanced military technology to the highest bidder, and they will stop at nothing to achieve their goals.

Reacher's investigation puts him directly in the crosshairs of the conspirators, and he must use his unique skills and experience to stay one step ahead of them. Along the way, he meets a local woman, Joan (Alicia Lively), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

As the story unfolds, Reacher discovers that Captain Turner is being framed by her own colleagues, including Enoch Edwards Inc.'s CEO, Bob Brown (Richard Jenkins). The conspirators will do anything to silence Reacher and maintain their cover, but he refuses to back down.

title: The Sorcerer and the White Snake
overview: The Sorcerer and the White Snake is an ancient Chinese fable about a woman demon who falls in love with a mortal is brought to life through the latest advances in CGI and action techniques.
plot:
The Sorcerer and the White Snake, previously known as It's Love and Madame White Snake, is a 2011 Chinese-Hong Kong action fantasy film directed by Ching Siu-tung and starring Jet Li as the Buddhist abbot Fahai. Based on the Chinese folk tale Legend of the White Snake, it co-stars Raymond Lam as the herbalist Xu Xian, Eva Huang as the White Snake Susu, Charlene Choi as the Green Snake Qingqing and Wen Zhang as Fahai's apprentice Neng Ren, with Vivian Hsu, Miriam Yeung and Chapman To in supporting roles.

Abbot Fahai and his young apprentice Neng Ren travel the land subduing demons and imprisoning them in the Lei Feng Pagoda, as they do after capturing an ice harpy on a mountaintop. On another mountain, two snake spirits, Susu and her sister Qingqing, watch a young herbalist, Xu Xian, gathering herbs. When Qingqing frightens him into a lake, Susu takes human form and saves him by breathing her own life essence into him with a kiss. Enchanted by the encounter, Susu follows Xu Xian to the city, where the two fall in love and marry, while he remains unaware that his bride is a snake demon.

Meanwhile, during a fight with bat demons, Neng Ren is bitten and begins turning into a bat demon himself. Fleeing his master, he is befriended by the playful Qingqing and discovers that he has kept his human feelings despite his transformation. Fahai, who believes that humans and demons cannot coexist, becomes suspicious of Susu and gives Xu Xian a dagger capable of killing demons. When Fahai sets out to expose Susu's true nature, she risks everything to protect Xu Xian and their love, defying the abbot in a spectacular confrontation between demon magic and Buddhist power.

The film reinterprets the classic legend as a romantic fantasy about love between humans and spirits, using extensive computer-generated effects and wire-work martial arts.

The film was shot in 3-D and was screened out of competition at the 68th Venice International Film Festival on 3 September 2011. It was released in mainland China on 28 September 2011 and in Hong Kong the following day.

title: The Phantom of the Opera at the Royal Albert Hall
original_title: The Phantom of the Opera at the Royal Albert Hall
tagline: The 25th anniversary of the first public performance of Phantom of the Opera.
overview: A disfigured musical genius, hidden away in the Paris Opera House, terrorises the opera company for the unwitting benefit of a young protégée whom he trains and loves. The 25th anniversary of the first public performance of Phantom of the Opera was celebrated with a grand performance at the Royal Albert Hall in London.
plot:
The Phantom of the Opera at the Royal Albert Hall is a 2011 British concert film of Andrew Lloyd Webber's 1986 stage musical, itself based on Gaston Leroux's 1910 novel. Staged in full to mark the show's 25th anniversary, it stars Ramin Karimloo as the Phantom, Sierra Boggess as Christine Daaé and Hadley Fraser as Raoul, Vicomte de Chagny, with Wendy Ferguson as Carlotta, Liz Robertson as Madame Giry and Daisy Maywood as Meg Giry.

At an auction in Paris in 1905, Raoul buys a music box as a restored chandelier recalls "the strange affair of the Phantom of the Opera". In 1881, as new managers take over the Opéra Populaire, a falling backdrop sends the prima donna Carlotta storming out, and young Christine, secretly tutored by an unseen "Angel of Music", triumphs in her place, catching the eye of her childhood friend Raoul, the company's new patron. The masked Phantom reveals himself as her teacher and leads her through her mirror to his lair across an underground lake, where she unmasks him in curiosity before he returns her to the theater. When the managers defy his demand that Christine take the lead in Il Muto, he reduces Carlotta's voice to a croak and hangs the stagehand Joseph Buquet. On the roof, Raoul and Christine pledge their love, and the eavesdropping Phantom brings down the chandelier in revenge.

Six months later, at a masked ball, the Phantom orders the company to stage his opera Don Juan Triumphant with Christine, now secretly engaged to Raoul, in the lead, and Madame Giry reveals that he is a disfigured prodigy who escaped from a traveling fair. Raoul plans to trap him at the premiere; Christine, torn, visits her father's grave, where the Phantom nearly bewitches her before Raoul intervenes. During the performance the Phantom takes the place of Piangi, who is found strangled, and Christine unmasks him before the audience. He carries her to his lair and threatens to kill the captive Raoul unless she stays, but her compassionate kiss moves him to free them both, and when the mob arrives, Meg finds only his mask.

Three performances were filmed on October 1 and 2, 2011, the last broadcast live to cinemas worldwide, and footage from all three was edited for release. In a grand finale, Lloyd Webber brought out the original creative team and London cast, including Michael Crawford and Sarah Brightman, who sang the title song with four former Phantoms. Home video releases followed in Britain in November 2011 and North America in February 2012.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Mr. Church is not just a simple arms dealer, but a mastermind who has been manipulating events from behind the scenes. He reveals that he has been using Medivac to further his own agenda, which involves selling advanced military technology to the highest bidder.

In the end, The Expendables must use all their skills and resources to take down Mr. Church and his minions. The movie culminates in an epic showdown between Ross and Church, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance.

The documentary shows how these elements helped shape the narrative and characters of the trilogy, making it more relatable and engaging for audiences.

Ultimately, Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy is a testament to the enduring power of storytelling and the impact it can have on our lives. title: Percy Jackson: Sea of Monsters
tagline: Where There Are Gods, There Are Monsters.
overview: In their quest to confront the ultimate evil, Percy and his friends battle swarms of mythical creatures to find the mythical Golden Fleece and to stop an ancient evil from rising.
plot:
Percy Jackson: Sea of Monsters is a 2013 fantasy adventure directed by Thor Freudenthal and written by Marc Guggenheim, adapted from Rick Riordan's 2006 novel The Sea of Monsters. A sequel to Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief (2010), it stars Logan Lerman as the demigod son of Poseidon, with Alexandra Daddario as Annabeth Chase, Brandon T. Jackson as the satyr Grover Underwood, Douglas Smith as Tyson, Leven Rambin as Clarisse La Rue, Jake Abel as Luke Castellan, and Stanley Tucci and Nathan Fillion as the gods Dionysus and Hermes.

Years earlier, Zeus's daughter Thalia gave her life to save her friends from monsters and was transformed into a tree whose magic shields Camp Half-Blood. Now Percy, mocked as a one-quest wonder by the camp bully Clarisse, meets Tyson, a young Cyclops who turns out to be his half-brother. When the tree is found to have been poisoned by the treacherous Luke and the barrier begins to fail, Annabeth proposes retrieving the Golden Fleece, which can heal it and which Grover senses lies across the Sea of Monsters, the place humans call the Bermuda Triangle. The camp director, Mr. D, gives the quest to Clarisse instead, while an oracle warns of a prophecy that a child of one of the three eldest gods will either save or destroy Olympus, possibly meaning Percy.

Percy, Annabeth, Grover and Tyson set off anyway. After a ride in a taxi driven by the Graeae, Luke's followers seize Grover, and the friends end up captive on Luke's yacht, where he reveals his plan to use the Fleece to revive the Titan Kronos. They escape, are swallowed with Clarisse's ship by Charybdis, blast their way free and land on the Florida coast at the lair of the Cyclops Polyphemus, where they rescue Grover and seize the Fleece. Luke ambushes them and starts raising Kronos, but Percy defeats the Titan with his sword; Annabeth, killed by the Manticore, is revived by the Fleece. Back at camp, the Fleece heals the tree and restores Thalia to life, so the prophecy may refer to her.

Filming began in April 2012 in British Columbia and New Orleans. Released on August 7, 2013, the film grossed about $202 million worldwide, but critics were lukewarm: Rotten Tomatoes gave it 42% approval, Metacritic 39, and CinemaScore audiences a "B+".

Thor: The Dark World is a 2013 superhero film directed by Alan Taylor and produced by Kevin Feige. The movie is the sequel to Thor (2011) and the eighth film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).

The story begins with Thor (Chris Hemsworth), the crown prince of Asgard, who has been imprisoned on Earth for 12 months as punishment for his actions during the events of Thor. Meanwhile, Jane Foster (Natalie Portman), a scientist and Thor's love interest, is struggling to cope with her newfound powers as the wielder of Mjolnir, Thor's hammer.

The Dark Elves, led by Malekith (Christopher Eccleston), have returned to Asgard seeking to harness the power of the Aether, a powerful energy source that can be used to destroy entire galaxies. The Dark Elves plan to use the Aether to break free from their prison and conquer the universe.

Thor is freed from his imprisonment and returns to Asgard, where he reunites with his brother Loki (Tom Hiddleston), who has been working with the Dark Elves. However, it becomes clear that Loki's intentions are not entirely pure, and he is struggling with his own morality.

As the story unfolds, Thor and Jane team up with Erik Selvig (Stellan Skarsgård) and Darcy Lewis (Kat Dennings) to stop Malekith and his minions from unleashing the Aether on Asgard. Along the way, they encounter the Warriors Three, a group of Asgardian warriors who are tasked with protecting the realm.

The plot thickens as Thor discovers that Loki is working to prevent the Dark Elves from obtaining the Aether, which would allow them to destroy Asgard and rule over the universe. However, it becomes clear that Loki's actions are motivated by a desire to protect his adopted brother and the people of Asgard.

In the climactic final battle, Thor and his allies face off against Malekith and the Dark Elves. The Aether is unleashed, causing chaos and destruction throughout Asgard. In the end, Thor manages to defeat Malekith and banish the Dark Elves from the realm.

The movie concludes with Loki's redemption arc coming full circle as he sacrifices himself to save his brother and the people of Asgard. Thor and Jane share a moment of intimacy, and the movie ends on a hopeful note, setting the stage for the events of Avengers: Age of Ultron.

Overall, Thor: The Dark World is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of family, loyalty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans and provides an exciting addition to the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

title: The Devil Inside
tagline: No soul is safe.
overview: In Italy, a woman becomes involved in a series of unauthorized exorcisms during her mission to discover what happened to her mother, who allegedly murdered three people during her own exorcism.
plot:
The Devil Inside is a 2012 American supernatural horror film directed by William Brent Bell, who co-wrote it with Matthew Peterman. Presented as found footage, it stars Fernanda Andrade as Isabella Rossi, a woman drawn into a series of exorcisms while trying to understand why her mother killed three people, with Simon Quarterman and Evan Helmuth as the priests Ben Rawlings and David Keane.

On October 30, 1989, Maria Rossi killed three people during an exorcism performed on her, and has since been held in a church psychiatric hospital in Rome. Her daughter, Isabella, learned of the killings from her father, who died three days after telling her. Twenty years later, Isabella is making a documentary about exorcism with filmmaker Michael Schaefer and travels to Rome to visit her mother, meeting priests Ben and David, who perform unauthorized exorcisms. Maria speaks in shifting accents and bears inverted crosses carved into her skin. She tells Isabella that killing a child is against God's will, seemingly alluding to an abortion her mother could not have known about.

The priests take her to the exorcism of a young woman, Rosalita, who calls Isabella by name and attacks the crew. During an exorcism of Maria, she taunts Ben about his past, and the ritual fails, but she appears to pass demons on to David and Isabella. Ben finds that four demons speak through Maria at once. While performing a baptism, David begins forcing the infant under the holy water before collapsing, and Ben later finds him at home with his forearms covered in blood, as Maria's had been. When police arrive, David seizes an officer's gun and, unable to finish reciting the Lord's Prayer, shoots himself. Isabella has a seizure and in the hospital slashes a nurse's throat. As Ben and Michael drive her to seek help, she breathes into Michael's mouth, possessing him, and he steers into oncoming traffic, killing himself and Ben, while Isabella vanishes from the wreck. A closing title says the case remains unresolved.

Peterman conceived the idea in 2005 after reading about the Catholic Church's exorcism school. Shot in 2010 in Bucharest and Rome, it was acquired by Paramount's low-budget label Insurge Pictures and released on January 6, 2012. It was not screened for critics, who panned it, giving it 6% on Rotten Tomatoes and 18 on Metacritic, with an F CinemaScore and a widely mocked ending. Even so, it grossed $101.8 million on a $1 million budget.

Hotel Transylvania is a 3D computer-animated comedy-horror film directed by Genndy Tartakovsky and produced by Sony Pictures Animation. The movie was released on September 21, 2012.

In the beginning of the story, Count Dracula (voiced by Adam Sandler) has grown tired of his solitary life as a vampire. He longs for companionship and decides to open a hotel specifically designed for monsters from all over the world. The hotel is called Hotel Transylvania, and it's a place where creatures of the night can live in peace without humans knowing about them.

The story revolves around Jonathan (voiced by Andy Samberg), a human who accidentally stumbles upon the hotel while on a road trip with his friend Mavis (voiced by Selena Gomez). Unbeknownst to Jonathan, he is the son of Van Helsing (voiced by Jon Lovitz), a famous vampire hunter.

As Jonathan and Mavis spend more time together, they develop feelings for each other. However, their love is threatened when Dracula discovers that Jonathan is not just any ordinary human but the son of his arch-nemesis. The Count tries to keep Jonathan away from Mavis, fearing that he will be killed by Van Helsing.

Meanwhile, a group of humans, led by Frankenstein's monster (voiced by Kevin James), werewolves (voiced by David Spade and Steve Buscemi), and other creatures, arrive at the hotel for a monster convention. However, things take a turn when an army of human hunters, led by Van Helsing, arrives at the hotel to destroy all the monsters.

As the humans and monsters clash, Jonathan and Mavis must work together to stop the villains and save their love. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about acceptance, understanding, and the importance of being true to oneself.

In the end, Jonathan and Mavis confess their love for each other, and Dracula finally accepts that his daughter has found someone who truly loves her for who she is. The movie ends with a grand monster party, where all the creatures come together in peace and harmony.

Hotel Transylvania was well-received by critics and audiences alike, praised for its witty humor, lovable characters, and positive message about acceptance and inclusivity. The movie spawned two sequels, Hotel Transylvania 2 (2015) and Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation (2018), as well as an animated series and a live-action film in development.

plot:
The Dictator is a 2012 comedy film directed by Larry Charles and written by Sacha Baron Cohen and Jay Roach. The movie follows the story of Adolfo Rivas, a fictional dictator from North Africa.

The film begins with Adolfo (played by Sacha Baron Cohen) as a young boy growing up in Sudan, where he witnesses his father's brutal murder at the hands of a group of rebels. This traumatic event shapes Adolfo's future ambitions and fuels his desire for power and revenge against those who wronged him.

As Adolfo grows older, he becomes a ruthless dictator, ruling over a small North African country with an iron fist. He is known for his brutal tactics, including torture, executions, and forced conscription of young men into his army.

However, Adolfo's life takes a dramatic turn when he falls in love with a beautiful woman named Zoey (played by Anna Faris), who is working as a human rights activist in the country. Despite their differences, the two begin a romantic relationship, which challenges Adolfo's worldview and forces him to confront his own humanity.

As Adolfo navigates his feelings for Zoey, he also faces opposition from his own people, who are tired of his brutal rule. A group of rebels, led by a charismatic leader named General Aladeen (played by Sacha Baron Cohen), emerges to challenge Adolfo's authority and bring about change.

The film takes a satirical turn as it pokes fun at the absurdity of dictatorships and the complexities of international politics. Adolfo's character is both lovable and despicable, making him a compelling and unpredictable protagonist.

Throughout the movie, Sacha Baron Cohen delivers a tour-de-force performance, playing multiple roles including General Aladeen, who is also Adolfo's twin brother. The film's humor is clever and irreverent, with plenty of laughs to be had at the expense of politics and societal norms.

In the end, Adolfo must confront his own mortality and the consequences of his actions. In a surprising twist, he decides to step down as dictator and allow Zoey to take over as the new leader of the country. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Adolfo and Zoey embracing their love for each other and working towards a brighter future.

Overall, The Dictator is a hilarious and thought-provoking comedy that uses satire to comment on the absurdities of politics and power. With Sacha Baron Cohen's masterful performance at its center, the film is a must-see for fans of comedy and international intrigue.

title: Justice League: Doom
tagline: The end of justice.
overview: An adaptation of Mark Waid's "Tower of Babel" story from the JLA comic. Vandal Savage steals confidential files Batman has compiled on the members of the Justice League, and learns all their weaknesses.
plot:
Justice League: Doom is an American animated superhero film of 2012 directed by Lauren Montgomery and written by Dwayne McDuffie, his last script before his death. Loosely based on the 2000 JLA storyline "Tower of Babel" and a standalone sequel to Justice League: Crisis on Two Earths, it was the 13th DC Universe Animated Original Movie. Kevin Conroy voices Batman, Tim Daly Superman, Susan Eisenberg Wonder Woman, Nathan Fillion Green Lantern, Carl Lumbly Martian Manhunter, Michael Rosenbaum the Flash and Phil Morris Vandal Savage, many reprising roles from the earlier animated series.

The immortal Vandal Savage plans to wipe out two thirds of humanity and found a new civilisation. He has Mirror Master steal from the Batcomputer the contingency plans Batman devised to neutralise his teammates should they go rogue, alters them to be lethal, and recruits Cheetah, Star Sapphire, Metallo, Bane, Mirror Master and Ma'alefa'ak as the Legion of Doom. Bane lures Batman to his parents' empty graves and buries him alive in his father's coffin. Martian Manhunter is poisoned at his own birthday party and set ablaze with magnesium; Cheetah infects Wonder Woman with nanomachines that make everyone look like Cheetah; Mirror Master straps a bomb to the Flash that will explode if he slows; Star Sapphire breaks Green Lantern's will until he renounces his ring; and Metallo, disguised as a suicidal man on the Daily Planet roof, shoots Superman with a Kryptonite bullet.

Spurred by Bane's taunting recording, Batman escapes, while Cyborg disables Wonder Woman's nanites. Together they save Martian Manhunter, Batman guides the Flash to leave the bomb inside an Arctic iceberg and shows Green Lantern that the hostages he failed were androids, and the heroes cut the bullet from Superman. Using a tracer Batman hid in his files, the League defeats the Legion, but Savage launches a rocket to trigger a devastating solar flare; the heroes use the Hall of Doom's technology to phase the whole planet so that the flare passes harmlessly. Savage is jailed for life, Cyborg joins the team and Batman resigns, telling Superman that the League itself is his plan should Superman ever turn.

Released on home video on 28 February 2012, it earned over $7.5 million in domestic sales, and IGN rated it 7 out of 10, calling it a highly enjoyable ride but a short adaptation.

title: Chronicle

overview: Three high school students make an incredible discovery, leading to their developing uncanny powers beyond their understanding. As they learn to control their abilities and use them to their advantage, their lives start to spin out of control, and their darker sides begin to take over.
plot:
Chronicle is a 2012 American science fiction thriller film directed by Josh Trank and written by Max Landis. The movie follows the story of three high school outcasts who discover they have superhuman powers after being bitten by a genetically modified spider.

The film begins with Andrew Detmer (Dane DeHaan), a troubled teenager struggling to cope with his father's death in a car accident. He is joined by Steven Monarch (Alex Russell) and Matt Gannon (Michael B. Jordan), two outcasts who share similar feelings of isolation and anger towards the world.

One day, while exploring an abandoned warehouse, Andrew bites into a genetically modified spider that has been left behind by a scientist. Unbeknownst to him, this spider is carrying a unique genetic code that will grant its victims superhuman powers.

As the days pass, each of the three teenagers begins to exhibit extraordinary abilities: Andrew develops telekinetic powers, Steven gains the ability to manipulate and control electricity, and Matt can fly using his newfound strength. Initially, they use their powers for personal gain and revenge against those who have wronged them.

However, as they delve deeper into their new abilities, they realize that their powers are not just physical but also emotional. They begin to experience intense emotions such as anger, fear, and sadness, which can be both a blessing and a curse.

As the story unfolds, Andrew becomes increasingly obsessed with his powers and begins to lose control of them. He starts to use his abilities for destructive purposes, causing chaos in his town. Meanwhile, Steven's powers become more erratic, and he starts to experience terrifying hallucinations.

Matt, who has been struggling to cope with his own demons, finds solace in his newfound ability to fly. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that Matt is hiding a dark secret: he is actually the son of a powerful and sinister figure known as the Monarch.

The film's climax revolves around Andrew's descent into madness and his ultimate confrontation with Steven. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Andrew has been using his powers to manipulate and control those around him, including his friends and family.

In the end, Matt uses his powers to save Andrew from himself, sacrificing his own life in the process. The film concludes with Steven, who has lost his powers, reflecting on the devastating consequences of their actions. As he looks up at the sky, it is revealed that Matt's spirit has been transformed into a being with wings, symbolizing his newfound freedom and redemption.

The protagonist, Jupiter Jones (played by Mila Kunis), is a young woman who discovers that she is actually an immortal being from the planet Cukelar, which was destroyed by the Mortals.

Jupiter's life takes a dramatic turn when she meets Balem Abrasax (played by Eddie Redmayne), the son of the powerful and ruthless leader of the Mortals, Stinger Abrasax. Balem reveals to Jupiter that she is the reincarnation of Queen Lyta, an immortal being who was once the queen of Cukelar.

As Jupiter learns more about her past and her true identity, she becomes embroiled in a rebellion against the Mortals. She meets Caine Wise (played by Channing Tatum), a skilled warrior from the planet Cukelar, who is tasked with protecting Jupiter on her journey to reclaim her rightful place as queen.

The plot thickens as Jupiter and Caine embark on a perilous quest to gather allies and resources for their rebellion. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, deadly creatures, and rival factions vying for power.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Balem's intentions are not entirely pure. He seeks to use Jupiter's powers to overthrow his father and take control of the Mortals' empire. Meanwhile, Stinger Abrasax is determined to crush the rebellion and maintain his family's grip on power.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the rebels and the Mortals, with Jupiter at its center. In a surprising twist, it is revealed that Balem has been manipulating events from behind the scenes, using Jupiter's powers to further his own ambitions.

In the end, Jupiter must make a choice between her loyalty to Caine and her destiny as queen. With the help of her new allies, she manages to defeat Balem and shatter the Mortals' hold on humanity. However, the film concludes with a sense of uncertainty, leaving the audience wondering about the future of this new world order.

Throughout the movie, the Wachowskis explore themes of identity, power, and rebellion, weaving together elements of science fiction, fantasy, and adventure. While Jupiter Ascending received mixed reviews from critics, it has developed a loyal fan base over the years, particularly among those who appreciate its unique blend of action, drama, and visual spectacle.

title: Black Butterfly
overview: Paul is a down-on-his-luck screenwriter who picks up a drifter and offers him a place to stay. However, when the deranged stranger takes Paul hostage and forces him to write, their unhinged relationship brings buried secrets to light.
plot:
Black Butterfly is a 2017 American thriller directed by Brian Goodman from a screenplay by Marc Frydman and Justin Stanley, based on Papillon Noir, a 2008 French television film directed by Christian Faure. It stars Antonio Banderas, Jonathan Rhys Meyers and Piper Perabo, with Abel Ferrara, Vincent Riotta and Nathalie Rapti Gomez, and was released by Lionsgate Premiere on May 26, 2017.

Paul, a reclusive writer, sits in his remote cabin typing "I'm stuck" over and over. His real-estate agent, Laura, is trying to sell the property, and Paul, whose wife has left him, wants to move away. In town he clashes with an aggressive truck driver, and when the trucker confronts him at a diner, a stranger throws the man out. Paul later picks up the stranger, a drifter named Jack, and offers him a place to stay for a few days finding on the way that the power and communication lines are down. Jack cooks and does odd jobs around the house, but keeps needling Paul about his lack of ideas.

One morning Jack wakes Paul with a knife at his throat and, at gunpoint, makes him a prisoner in his own home, and when Paul writes a few pages of a screenplay, Jack throws them into the fire. Jack makes Paul accept a grocery delivery without raising suspicion, forces him and Laura to sink her car in the pond and shoots the local sheriff, before dragging Laura into another room. Freeing himself and seizing his rifle, Paul thanks Jack for arriving just in time to take the blame for the murders Paul himself has committed, and plants his souvenirs of the killings in Jack's bag. But the rifle is loaded with blanks. Paul wakes handcuffed as FBI agents search the house: Laura and the sheriff are alive and are agents too, and the FBI has been tracking Paul for years for four murders, beginning with his wife. When Paul refuses to reveal where the bodies are, Jack notices that an old photograph shows the farm before the pond existed and realizes where Paul's wife is buried. Paul then wakes on his couch, realizes the whole story was a dream, and types the title "Black Butterfly" on a fresh page.

Banderas plays Paul, Rhys Meyers plays Jack and Perabo plays Laura, with Ferrara as Pat and Riotta as Lieutenant Carcano. Critics were divided, with 40% of the 20 reviews collected by Rotten Tomatoes positive and a Metacritic score of 43, indicating mixed or average reviews.

The movie tells the true story of the unlikely friendship between Philippe Pozzo di Borgo (played by François Cluzet) and Driss (played by Omar Sy), two men from different backgrounds who become caregivers for each other.

The film begins with Philippe, a wealthy quadriplegic who has lost the use of his arms and legs in an accident. He is forced to rely on others for his daily needs, which he finds humiliating and dehumanizing. One day, while browsing through a newspaper, Philippe comes across an ad for a caregiver from Morocco named Driss. Despite initial reservations, Philippe decides to hire Driss, who is initially hesitant due to cultural differences.

As the story unfolds, we see how Driss, a young man from a poor background in Paris's 18th arrondissement, takes on the role of Philippe's caregiver. Initially, their relationship is strained, with Driss struggling to understand Philippe's needs and Philippe feeling frustrated by Driss's lack of understanding. However, as they spend more time together, they begin to develop an unlikely bond.

Through a series of comedic misadventures, we see how Driss learns to navigate the complexities of Philippe's life, including his medical equipment, medication, and daily routines. Meanwhile, Philippe begins to appreciate Driss's kindness, humor, and resilience in the face of adversity.

As their friendship deepens, we learn about the challenges faced by both men. Philippe struggles with feelings of isolation and depression, while Driss faces racism and xenophobia from his community. Despite these obstacles, they find solace in each other's company, and their relationship becomes a source of strength and inspiration for both.

The film takes a poignant turn as we see how Driss's presence helps Philippe to re-engage with the world around him. He begins to rediscover his passion for life, including his love of music and art. Meanwhile, Driss finds a sense of purpose and belonging in his new role as Philippe's caregiver.

The movie concludes on a heartwarming note, as we see how Philippe and Driss have transformed each other's lives. Despite their differences, they have formed an unbreakable bond that transcends cultural and social boundaries. The film ends with a powerful message about the importance of empathy, understanding, and human connection in breaking down barriers.

Overall, The Intouchables is a beautifully crafted film that celebrates the power of friendship and the human spirit. With outstanding performances from François Cluzet and Omar Sy, the movie has become a beloved classic around the world, inspiring audiences with its uplifting story and memorable characters.

Excited by his newfound abilities, Theo sets out on an adventure to become a racing champion. He meets a group of street-smart racers who teach him how to navigate the high-speed world of racing. There's Guy Gagne, a cocky and arrogant car driver; Tito, a wise-cracking and fast-talking street rat; and Burn, a tough and intimidating motorcycle rider.

However, not everyone is happy about Theo's newfound success. Guy Gagne, in particular, sees Theo as a threat to his own racing career and tries to sabotage him at every turn. The two engage in an epic rivalry that takes them on a wild ride through the streets of New York City.

As the big racing championship approaches, Theo must confront his own doubts and fears. Can he overcome his slow start and become the champion? Will he be able to balance his love for racing with his newfound fame?

The film's climax features an action-packed racing sequence that takes Theo and his friends on a thrilling ride through the streets of New York City. In the end, Theo emerges victorious, but not without learning valuable lessons about perseverance, friendship, and believing in himself.

Turbo is a heartwarming and hilarious animated film that celebrates the power of dreams and determination. With its colorful characters, witty humor, and high-speed action sequences, it's a movie that will leave audiences cheering for more.

plot:
The Scorpion King 3: Battle for Redemption is a 2012 American direct-to-video sword-and-sorcery action film directed by Roel Reiné and the third entry in The Scorpion King series. Victor Webster takes over the role of Mathayus from Dwayne Johnson, with Bostin Christopher, Temuera Morrison, Krystal Vee, Selina Lo, Kimbo Slice, Dave Bautista, Billy Zane as Talus and Ron Perlman as Horus. Universal Studios Home Entertainment released it on home video in January 2012.

Years after becoming the Scorpion King, Mathayus loses his wife, Queen Cassandra, to a plague, just as she had once foreseen that his peaceful reign could not last. Grief-stricken, he lets his kingdom crumble and returns to life as a sword for hire. In Egypt, Talus resents his elder brother Horus, who was made king instead of him, and plans to take his throne. To do so he marches into the Far East to seize the Book of the Dead from Ramusan, a king allied to Horus. Horus hires Mathayus to stop him, pairing him with the boisterous Teutonic warrior Olaf.

Talus abducts Ramusan's daughter, Princess Silda, and Ramusan promises that whoever saves her may marry her and with her claim a kingdom. Before Mathayus can reach her, she is carried off by ninja warriors under a mysterious leader known as Cobra. Talus hires Mathayus and Olaf to bring back the princess and Cobra's head, and the pair find their way to an outlaw camp, where they discover that Cobra is Silda herself. Talus, meanwhile, overruns Ramusan's palace, wounds the king and takes the book, using it to raise three dead champions, Zulu Kondo, Agromael and Tsukai, who prove their power by slaughtering his own best men.

Talus sends Tsukai and Zulu Kondo against the exiles' camp; Mathayus, Olaf and Silda's ninjas defeat Zulu Kondo, but Tsukai escapes. Posing as Silda's rescuers and offering a fake head of Cobra, Mathayus and Olaf enter the palace. In the battle that follows, Silda duels Tsukai and Olaf battles Agromael, while Mathayus reaches the dying Ramusan; using the Book of the Dead, they turn the undead warriors against Talus. Ramusan dies, the ninjas overwhelm Talus, and the champions kneel to Mathayus as ruler of both kingdoms. When Horus reaches the gates, he finds Mathayus restored as the Scorpion King.

Reviews were poor; IGN rated it 4 out of 10, faulting its dialogue, acting and stagey action.

The film begins with Lieutenant Stig Engstrom (played by Mikkel Abels), Lieutenant Sverre Okken (played by Anders Baasmo Christiansen), and Lieutenant Magnus Isaksen (played by Jonas Holm) on a mission to bomb German airfields. As the situation becomes more desperate, the two groups must work together to survive. They share what little food they have, and the Germans teach the Norwegians how to navigate using a compass. The Norwegians, in turn, show the Germans the beauty of the Norwegian wilderness.

Despite their differences, the pilots begin to form bonds with each other. Stig, Sverre, and Magnus learn about the human cost of war from their German counterparts, while Hauptmann Müller and his men are forced to confront the harsh realities of their own actions.

As the days turn into weeks, the pilots realize that they must find a way to escape the forest before it's too late. They hatch a plan to make a break for it, but things don't go according to plan. The Germans are discovered by their superiors, and the Norwegians are forced to flee.

In the end, only one of the Norwegian pilots is able to escape, while the others are captured or killed. The film ends with Stig, Sverre, and Magnus reflecting on the experience they shared in the forest. They realize that despite being on opposite sides of the war, they formed a bond that will stay with them for the rest of their lives.

Into the White is a powerful and emotional film that explores the human cost of war. The movie features stunning cinematography and outstanding performances from its cast. The film's themes of survival, sacrifice, and redemption are timeless and universal, making it a must-see for anyone interested in World War II history or drama.

overview: One Piece 3D: Straw Hat Chase is the 11th One Piece film of the series, and is set before the time-skip. This is One Piece's first movie release to be in 3D CGI. The movie is also the first One Piece film since Movie 3 to be a double-feature. This time, the film was featured with "Toriko 3D: Gourmet Adventure", both being billed as the "Jump Heroes Film". The double-feature was released on March 19, 2011.granmaster
plot:
One Piece 3D: Straw Hat Chase is a 2011 Japanese computer-animated short film produced by Toei Animation and the eleventh theatrical release based on Eiichiro Oda's manga One Piece. Directed by Hiroyuki Satō from a screenplay by Yasuyuki Tsutsumi, it was the first film in the series made entirely in CGI and in stereoscopic 3D, as well as its first short, running about 30 minutes. It was released on 19 March 2011 as part of the "Jump Heroes Film" double bill with Toriko 3D: Gourmet Adventure. Oda supervised the original characters' designs, and the music, including the instrumental theme "Break into the Light", was provided by the Tokyo Ska Paradise Orchestra. The regular voice cast returns, led by Mayumi Tanaka as Luffy, with Kazuya Nakai, Akemi Okamura, Kappei Yamaguchi, Hiroaki Hirata, Ikue Otani, Yuriko Yamaguchi, Kazuki Yao and Chō, while comedian Tomomitsu Yamaguchi voices all three original characters.

Schneider, an aging pirate who senses that he does not have long to live, decides to disband his tiny crew, which consists only of himself and his old dog Buzz, in order to spare his companion. Buzz refuses to leave, so Schneider sets him an impossible challenge: if he can steal the straw hat of the famous pirate Monkey D. Luffy, the crew will stay together. Buzz, who ate a Devil Fruit that allows him to transform into a giant eagle, succeeds, snatching the treasured hat that Luffy received from Shanks. The Straw Hat Pirates, who had rescued Schneider from a drifting ship, set off in a long, frantic pursuit of the eagle, while Chopper tends to the ailing old man. The chase eventually leads Luffy and Buzz into a Navy base, where the crew fights its way through the Marines and wins. In the end Luffy recovers his hat, Schneider and Buzz befriend the Straw Hats, and the old pirate promises not to break up his crew. A closing flashback shows Shanks entrusting the hat to the young Luffy.

The film was the last of the series set before the story's two-year time skip. Its release came days after the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, which forced the postponement of stage greetings in the Kanto region and closures of some theaters; it opened seventh at the box office and ultimately earned about ¥790 million, the lowest total in the film series. It received an animation award at the 65th Motion Picture and Television Engineering Society of Japan awards.

title: Assassin's Creed: Embers
overview: Taking place after the events of Assassin's Creed: Revelations in the year 1524 in Tuscany, follow the retired Assassin Ezio Auditore as he teams up with Shao Jun during his final battles.
plot:
Assassin's Creed: Embers is a Canadian animated short film of 2011 produced by UbiWorkshop and written by Darby McDevitt, based on the Assassin's Creed games. It concludes the story of Ezio Auditore da Firenze, the hero of Assassin's Creed II, Brotherhood and Revelations, who is voiced again by Roger Craig Smith. Angela Galuppo voices both the Chinese Assassin Shao Jun and Ezio's daughter Flavia, Anna Tuveri voices his wife Sofia Sartor and Peter Arpesella plays a young Italian man. The film was included as a bonus with the Signature and Collector's Editions of Assassin's Creed: Revelations.

The story is set in 1524, twelve years after Ezio discovered the secret library of Altaïr. Having retired from the Assassin Order, he lives quietly in the Tuscan countryside with Sofia and their children Flavia and Marcello, and writes his memoirs. Then a stranger arrives: Shao Jun, a Chinese Assassin who has come to learn from him about his life in the Brotherhood. Ezio wants her gone, but Sofia lets her stay the night. When he catches her reading his memoirs he orders her out, but relents when she asks what being an Assassin means.

On a visit to Florence, his birthplace, he tells her how the execution of his father and brothers in the town square drove him to become an Assassin, and that such a life brings only suffering. Leaving the city, they are attacked by a man who also seems to be Asian. After killing him, Shao Jun explains that she was once a concubine of the Jiajing Emperor and is being hunted by his agents, and that her former master freed her from the emperor's grip. Back at the villa, Ezio sends his family away, knowing more killers will follow, and teaches Shao Jun the key to freeing her people. That night more of her pursuers attack, and the two Assassins defeat them all, though Ezio is left exhausted. In the morning he gives her a small box to use only if she loses her way and sends her off as two riders approach.

Some time later, Ezio, now suffering from heart trouble, travels to Florence with Sofia and Flavia. Resting on a bench, he is approached by a young man with a scarred face who complains about the women of Florence, reminding Ezio of his own youth. The young man leaves, and Ezio dies of a heart attack in front of his family. The film closes with a final letter to Sofia, in which Ezio writes that of everything that sustained him through life, his love for the world and for the people around him was the strongest.

title: A Princess for Christmas
tagline: Sometimes dreams come true
overview: After her sister and brother-in-law's tragic deaths, an American woman who is the guardian for her young niece and nephew is invited to a royal European castle for Christmas by her late brother-in-law's father, the Duke of Castlebury. Feeling out of place as a commoner, she is determined to give her family a merry Christmas and surprises herself when she falls for a handsome prince.
plot:
A Princess for Christmas, billed in the United Kingdom as A Christmas Princess and previously known as Christmas at Castlebury Hall, is an American television comedy drama of 2011 directed by Michael Damian. Katie McGrath stars as Jules Daly, Sam Heughan as Prince Ashton, and Roger Moore as Edward, Duke of Castlebury, with Travis Turner and Leilah de Meza as Jules's nephew Milo and niece Maddie, Miles Richardson as the butler Paisley and Charlotte Salt as Ashton's girlfriend, Lady Arabella.

Jules works in an antique shop in Buffalo, New York, and has become guardian to Milo and Maddie since the death of her sister and brother-in-law. Maddie is mischievous and Milo a rebellious teenager who hates Christmas because it reminds him of his parents. Laid off just before the holidays, and with the babysitter quitting over Maddie's pranks, Jules is visited by Paisley, butler to the children's wealthy paternal grandfather, Duke Edward, who invites them to spend Christmas at his castle in Castlebury. Told that the Duke is ill, Jules reluctantly accepts, only to find him in perfect health. She is immediately smitten with Ashton, brother of the children's late father, Charles, whom the Duke disowned for marrying Jules's sister.

Finding no Christmas trees in the palace because the Duke dislikes them, Jules and Maddie bring one in anyway. Edward is furious until Maddie hands him an ornament identical to one his brother gave him as a boy, and, his heart thawing, he orders a Christmas Eve ball. Ashton teaches Milo archery and tells him about Charles. Overhearing the Duke and Ashton disparaging an unrefined guest they would rather not invite, Jules assumes they mean her, and after her gown is accidentally burned she quietly heads home. The housekeeper, Mrs. Birch, and Paisley fetch her back from the train station with a dress from Vienna. At the ball Ashton realises that Arabella cares only for his title, and he explains to Jules that their remarks were about Bunny McCracken, a woman who hates children. The two dance, Arabella's family fails to turn the Duke against Jules and storms out, and Jules agrees to stay longer. The family catch Santa leaving gifts, and later Jules and Ashton marry and ride away in a carriage.

Shot in early 2011 at Peleș Castle and other locations around Bucharest, Romania, the film premiered on the Hallmark Channel on 3 December 2011.

title: Ice Age: A Mammoth Christmas
tagline: Get ready for a chilling fun holiday adventure with the Ice Age herd!
overview: When Sid accidentally destroys Manny's heirloom Christmas rock and ends up on Santa's naughty list, he leads a hilarious quest to the North Pole to make things right and ends up making things much worse. Now it's up to Manny and his prehistoric posse to band together and save Christmas for the entire world!
plot:
Ice Age: A Mammoth Christmas is a 2011 American animated Christmas television special produced by Blue Sky Studios and directed by Karen Disher, part of the Ice Age franchise. Ray Romano, John Leguizamo, Denis Leary and Queen Latifah reprise their roles as Manny, Sid, Diego and Ellie, with Billy Gardell as Santa Claus. Much of the animation was produced by Reel FX Creative Studios. It premiered on Fox in the United States on 24 November 2011, aired on Channel 4 and E4 in the United Kingdom at Christmas, and was released on DVD and Blu-ray two days after its American broadcast.

Set between the events of Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs and Ice Age: Continental Drift, the special follows the herd as Christmas approaches. Manny brings out the Christmas Rock, a family heirloom from his childhood that is said to help Santa find them, as a surprise for his daughter, Peaches. He warns the clumsy sloth Sid to stay away from it. Sid, doubting that Santa could find the rock, decides to make his own decoration and chooses a tree, which Crash and Eddie help him decorate. But when he tops it with an ice star, the star flies off and shatters the Christmas Rock.

Furious, Manny declares that Sid is on Santa's "Naughty List," while dismissing the idea of Santa to Ellie. Peaches overhears and is upset that her father does not believe, and angry at how he treated Sid. Determined to make amends and get off the Naughty List, Sid sets out for the North Pole to apologize to Santa in person, accompanied by Peaches, Crash and Eddie, with Manny, Ellie and Diego following to bring them home. Along the way the group meets a tiny reindeer named Prancer, who guides them to Santa's workshop, where Sid's well-meaning blunders cause chaos that threatens to ruin Christmas. To save the holiday, the herd must help Santa deliver presents, inventing several Christmas traditions along the way, and Manny learns to believe again. Meanwhile, Scrat pursues his acorn in a holiday-themed subplot.

In keeping with the franchise's playful approach to prehistory, the special offered prehistoric origins for familiar Christmas customs such as the Christmas tree, the naughty-and-nice list and Santa's flying reindeer.

title: Devil's Due
tagline: The Devil Always Gets His Due
overview: An unexpected pregnancy takes a terrifying turn for newlyweds Zach and Samantha McCall.
plot:
Devil's Due is a 2014 American found-footage supernatural horror film directed by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett in their feature directorial debut and written by Lindsay Devlin. It stars Allison Miller as Samantha McCall and Zach Gilford as her husband Zach, with Sam Anderson as Father Thomas. Produced for 20th Century Fox, the film was developed after the directors' segment 10/31/98 in the 2012 horror anthology V/H/S attracted studio attention.

Zach McCall begins recording a video diary on the eve of his wedding to Sam, so that their future children will have a record of the family's history. The newlyweds spend their honeymoon in the Dominican Republic, where a fortune teller unsettles Sam by telling her that she was born from death and that they have been waiting for her. Later that night, lost in an unfamiliar part of the city, the couple accepts a ride from a taxi driver who takes them to an underground nightclub. After drinking heavily, they black out, and Sam is taken to a hidden chamber where she is subjected to a satanic ritual. The next morning they wake up in their hotel remembering nothing.

A few weeks after returning home, Sam discovers that she is pregnant despite having taken birth control pills. The couple is delighted at first, but Zach continues filming everything, and the footage gradually reveals that something is wrong. During the first ultrasound the monitor briefly turns to static, and as the pregnancy progresses, Sam develops nosebleeds, bruising, a craving for raw meat despite being a vegetarian, sudden bursts of violent rage and frightening displays of strength and telekinesis. Strangers seem to be watching the house, and hidden cameras are secretly installed to monitor her. As Zach investigates, he uncovers evidence that a cult has chosen Sam to carry a child for a sinister purpose and that their lives are in grave danger.

The film combines the found-footage format with the themes of Rosemary's Baby, using home video, security cameras and other recording devices to tell its story.

Devil's Due was released on January 17, 2014. It received negative reviews, with 21 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it derivative and mostly uninspired, and a Metacritic score of 34.

title: Book of Dragons
tagline: All New Dragons
overview: So you want to be a dragon trainer do you? Prepare yourself for adventure, excitement and training as Hiccup, Astrid, Toothless and Gobber tell the legend behind the Book of Dragons and reveal insider training secrets about new, never-before-seen dragons.
plot:
Book of Dragons is an animated fantasy adventure film that revolves around the story of Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III, a young Viking who befriends a dragon and learns about the importance of understanding and empathy. The movie explores themes of acceptance, prejudice, and the power of friendship.

At its core, Book of Dragons is a tale about challenging one's own biases and preconceptions. Hiccup, initially seen as an outcast among his people due to his fascination with dragons, must navigate the complexities of Viking culture and learn to see things from different perspectives. Through his journey, he discovers that even the most fearsome creatures can possess hidden depths and vulnerabilities.

The film also delves into the consequences of fear-mongering and the dangers of allowing prejudice to dictate our actions. The Vikings' initial hostility towards dragons is rooted in a deep-seated fear, which ultimately leads to chaos and destruction. By contrast, Hiccup's willingness to engage with the dragon, Toothless, allows him to forge an unlikely bond that transcends their differences.

Ultimately, Book of Dragons presents a message about the importance of empathy, understanding, and compassion. The movie encourages viewers to look beyond surface-level appearances and to seek out common ground with others, even if they seem vastly different from ourselves.

title: The Smurfs: A Christmas Carol
overview: When Grouchy Smurf behaves badly to everyone and refuses to celebrate Christmas, the Smurfs of Christmas Past, Present and Future teach him to appreciate Christmas.
plot:
The Smurfs: A Christmas Carol is a 2011 American animated short film based on the Smurfs comics created by the Belgian artist Peyo and adapted from Charles Dickens's 1843 novella A Christmas Carol. Directed by Troy Quane from a script by Todd Berger, it was produced by Sony Pictures Animation, with animation by Sony Pictures Imageworks and Duck Studios. The voice cast includes George Lopez as Grouchy Smurf, Jack Angel as Papa Smurf, Melissa Sturm as Smurfette, and Fred Armisen, Gary Basaraba, Anton Yelchin and Hank Azaria.

On Christmas Eve, the Smurfs prepare for their holiday celebration. Grouchy refuses to take part and declares that he hates Christmas, to everyone's dismay. Papa Smurf brews a potion intended to restore Grouchy's festive spirit, and it ends up in Grouchy's mug of smurfberry nog. After drinking it he passes out, and when he wakes, the world around him, and he himself, has turned into hand-drawn animation.

Smurfette appears as the Smurf of Christmas Past and shows him earlier holidays, when Grouchy, longing for a hang glider, was disappointed year after year to receive yet another new hat from Papa Smurf, until a prank by Jokey made him lose his temper and turn against Christmas. Brainy, as the Smurf of Christmas Present, reveals how Grouchy's refusal to help has forced the others to take on extra work, leading Clumsy to set the tree on fire, and shows Papa lovingly crafting each Smurf's hat. Hefty, as the Smurf of Christmas Future, warns that if Grouchy does not change, the Smurfs will wander into the forest trying to cheer him up and fall into the clutches of Gargamel and his cat Azrael.

Grouchy wakes on Christmas morning transformed, admits he was wrong and realizes that the holiday is about a family that loves him. Papa gives him his gift first, a hat made especially for him, and after placing the star on the tree Grouchy uses it as a makeshift hang glider before crash-landing in the snow, joking that he hates that Christmas comes only once a year.

The short's hand-drawn sequence was based on Peyo's original designs. Melissa Sturm voiced Smurfette in place of Katy Perry, who was unavailable because of her concert tour. The short was released on DVD on December 2, 2011, as part of a holiday gift set with The Smurfs, and as a stand-alone DVD in 2013.

title: Gone
tagline: No one believes her. Nothing will stop her.
overview: Jill Conway is trying to rebuild her life after surviving a terrifying kidnapping attempt. Though she is having a difficult time, she takes small steps toward normalcy by starting a new job and inviting her sister, Molly, to move in with her. Returning home from work one morning, Jill discovers that Molly has vanished, and she is certain that the same man who previously abducted her has returned for revenge.
plot:
Gone is a 2012 American thriller directed by Heitor Dhalia from a screenplay by Allison Burnett, starring Amanda Seyfried. Her casting in the lead was announced in February 2011. Set in Portland, Oregon, the story follows a young woman whose claims about a serial killer have never been believed and who must find him herself when her sister disappears.

A year earlier, Jill Conway was abducted by a brutal killer and held in a pit among the remains of his previous victims. She escaped, but because she had once been institutionalized, the police concluded that the attack never happened. Now she shares a house with her sister, Molly, and works as a waitress at the Lucky Star Diner. Returning home after work, Jill finds that Molly has vanished. The police again dismiss her, with the exception of Detective Hood, who has just joined the homicide unit, so Jill sets out to investigate on her own.

Following a trail of clues, Jill learns that a locksmith's van was parked outside her home overnight, rented by the owner's son, Nick, to a man calling himself Digger. A receipt leads her to a hardware store and then to the Royal Hotel, where she discovers that his real name is Jim LaPointe and finds duct tape, pet food and matches from her own diner in his abandoned room. Getting his phone number from her coworker Sharon, she calls him, and he directs her to a remote spot in Forest Park, insisting he does not have Molly. Meanwhile Molly, who had been held under Jill's own house, breaks free and tells the police what happened, proving that Jill was right all along. In the woods Jill photographs the remains of earlier victims and finds the hole where she was once kept. LaPointe attacks her; she shoots him and, after he admits he took Molly as bait to lure her back, pours kerosene into the pit and sets him on fire despite his pleas. At home she tells the police that the man existed only in her head, but an anonymous package containing photographs of the victims and a map to the grave later arrives at the police department.

The film was poorly received. Rotten Tomatoes reported 12% approval, Metacritic scored it 36 and CinemaScore audiences gave it a C+; critics found it formulaic and forgettable, although one reviewer found Seyfried as reliable as anyone could hope. It was a box office disappointment, grossing about $18.1 million worldwide.

title: Aliens vs Avatars
overview: Six college friends blowing off steam on a camping trip, find themselves caught up in a cat and mouse hunt with an Alien monster. Not knowing what to do or who to trust, they struggle to protect themselves. Reluctantly, they join forces with another, seemingly friendly, alien, Ava, who orbits the Earth and appears to them in the form of an avatar. Having only one chance at stopping the monster, they must race to locate and repair the Ava’s earth sent robot, before it slaughters them one by one.
plot:
Aliens vs Avatars is a 2011 American low-budget science fiction horror film directed by Lewis Schoenbrun from a script credited to Ted Chalmers and David S. Sterling, produced by Sterling Entertainment and Tom Cat Films. A mockbuster riffing on the titles of Alien vs. Predator and James Cameron's Avatar, it follows a conflict between a vicious alien species and shape-shifting extraterrestrials, with six college friends caught in the middle. Its distributor, Summer Hill Entertainment, later retitled it Alien vs. Alien.

Six college friends head into the wilderness on a camping trip to blow off steam, only to find themselves the quarry of a monstrous alien that begins hunting them in a deadly game of cat and mouse. Unsure what they are facing or whom to trust, the group struggles to defend itself as the creature closes in. Help appears in the form of Ava, another, seemingly friendly alien who orbits the Earth and can reach them only by appearing in the form of an avatar. Reluctantly joining forces with her, the survivors learn that they have just one chance to stop the monster: they must find and repair the robot Ava has sent down to Earth before the creature slaughters them one by one.

The cast is led by Jason Lockhart as Tyler, Kim Argetsinger as Jesse and Cassie Fliegel as Ava, with Dylan Vox as Jake, Marlene Mc'Cohen as Tiffany, Ginny You as Dana and Georgina Tolentino as Crystal. The film was shot in Los Angeles in the summer of 2010, while Schoenbrun was finishing post-production on The Amazing Bulk; he considered it the harder production of the two because of its many shooting locations.

The film received no theatrical release and was issued directly to video, DVD and television on 20 September 2011, becoming Schoenbrun's most widely released film that year. Reviews were overwhelmingly negative. The horror blogger Baron Craze dismissed its dialogue as half-baked drivel and found it boring, and Richard Scheib called it only marginally better made than the kind of film teenagers shoot on a camcorder over successive weekends, though it found some fans on home video in Japan. In 2012 Tom Cat Films sued hundreds of anonymous "John Doe" defendants in U.S. federal court for allegedly downloading the film illegally, a suit that commentators described as copyright trolling.

title: The Apparition
tagline: Once you believe, you die.
overview: Plagued by frightening occurrences in their home, Kelly and Ben learn that a university's parapsychology experiment produced an entity that is now haunting them. The malevolent spirit feeds on fear and torments the couple no matter where they run. Desperate, Kelly and Ben turn to a paranormal researcher, but even with his aid, it may already be too late to save themselves from the terrifying presence.
plot:
The Apparition is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human psychology and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of obsession and possession, as the main character, Heather, becomes increasingly entangled in a world of paranormal activity. As she delves deeper into the mystery, her grip on reality begins to slip, and she finds herself torn between her desire for answers and her growing dependence on the malevolent entity that has taken hold of her life.

The film also touches on the idea of grief and loss, as Heather's character is haunted by a tragic event in her past. Her obsession with the supernatural becomes a way to cope with her emotional pain, but ultimately serves to exacerbate her situation.

Furthermore, The Apparition raises questions about the nature of reality and the blurred lines between the spiritual and the physical worlds. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that there are forces at work that defy explanation, leaving the characters – and the audience – questioning what is real and what is just a product of their own paranoia.

Overall, The Apparition is a tense, unsettling film that masterfully crafts an atmosphere of creeping dread and unease, keeping viewers on the edge of their seats as they follow Heather's downward spiral into madness.

title: In the Land of Blood and Honey
original_title: In the Land of Blood and Honey
tagline: Love can change what we want… war can change who we are
overview: During the Bosnian War, Danijel, a soldier fighting for the Serbs, re-encounters Ajla, a Bosnian who's now a captive in his camp he oversees. Their once promising connection has become ambiguous as their motives have changed.
plot:
In the Land of Blood and Honey is a 2011 war drama film that explores the complexities of human nature during times of conflict. The movie delves into the theme of love amidst war, highlighting the resilience of the human spirit in the face of unimaginable violence.

The story revolves around two characters, Danica (played by Zana Marjanovic), a Bosnian Serb woman, and Ajla (played by Goran Kostic), a Bosniak man. Their relationship is forbidden due to their conflicting ethnic backgrounds, yet they find solace in each other's company amidst the chaos of war.

The film critiques the senseless violence and brutality that often accompanies conflict, particularly in the context of the Bosnian War. It portrays the devastating effects of war on civilians, including women and children, who are often caught in the crossfire.

Through Danica and Ajla's story, the movie sheds light on the human cost of war, where individuals are reduced to mere pawns in a larger game of politics and power struggles. The film also touches upon themes of identity, loyalty, and survival, as characters navigate the treacherous landscape of war-torn Bosnia.

Ultimately, In the Land of Blood and Honey is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the harsh realities of war and its impact on individuals and communities.

title: Pastorela
overview: Agent Jesus Juarez (aka Chucho) has always played the Devil in his town's Nativity Play. This Christmas, when the new pastor of the church recasts the role, the two men engage in a battle between good and evil.
plot:
Pastorela is a 2011 Mexican Christmas black comedy written and directed by Emilio Portes, his second feature after the award-winning black comedy Conozca la cabeza de Juan Pérez. A Las Producciones del Patrón production made with support from IMCINE and FIDECINE, it stars Joaquín Cosío as Jesús "Chucho" Juárez, Carlos Cobos as Father Edmundo Posadas and Eduardo España as Vulmaro, with Ana Serradilla as a nun, Dagoberto Gama as a police commander, Melissa Bahnsen as Magdalena, Héctor Jiménez as a possessed man, José Sefami as "El Tuerto", Silverio Palacios as Doctor Godínez and Eduardo Manzano as a cardinal.

Chucho Juárez is a judicial agent of the federal police who lives with his daughter Magdalena in the Mexico City neighborhood of San Miguel de Nenepilco. For as long as he can remember, he has played the Devil every year in the parish pastorela, the traditional Nativity play organized by Father Benito. This Christmas, however, things change. While Chucho is busy investigating the murder of a deputy prosecutor, he fails to notice that Father Benito has suffered a fatal heart attack in the middle of an affair with a nun, and he misses the casting session held by the new parish priest, the exorcist Edmundo Posadas. The newcomer leaves him out of the play and gives the coveted role of the Devil to Vulmaro, Chucho's compadre. Unwilling to give up a part he regards as his by tradition, the policeman launches a fierce struggle against the priest, a classic battle between good and evil in which both men go to any lengths, tearing apart the venerable tradition along the way.

Portes, a graduate of the Centro de Capacitación Cinematográfica, reworked the script in a 2007 screenwriting workshop supervised by the writer Vicente Leñero, and the film was shot between December 2008 and February 2009. He described it as an acid, unbridled comedy with touches of police action and fantasy, and as a portrait of a society that loves to live by its traditions and their absurdity, adding that he hoped the main characters would move beyond the archetypes of cop and priest to become more complex and endearing. Pastorela opened in Mexico on 11 November 2011 and was released in the United States by Pantelion. At the 54th Ariel Awards in 2012 it received fourteen nominations and was the big winner, taking best picture, best director and best original screenplay along with costume design, makeup and visual effects awards.

plot:
The Watch is a 2012 American science fiction comedy film directed by Akiva Schaffer and written by Rafe Young. The movie stars Ben Stiller, Vince Vaughn, Jonah Hill, and Richard Ayoade.

The story begins with Evan Treborn (Ben Stiller), a suburban father who has just moved to the suburbs with his wife, Trish (Vicky Krieps). Evan is excited to start a new life but soon discovers that he's not alone in the neighborhood. He meets his neighbors, Jay (Jonah Hill) and Steve (Richard Ayoade), who are both eccentric and paranoid.

The three men form an unlikely friendship as they try to protect their homes from an alien invasion. They soon discover that aliens have landed on Earth and are planning to destroy humanity. The aliens, known as the "Slugs," are small, slimy creatures that can blend into human society and are nearly invisible.

As the Slugs begin to infiltrate the neighborhood, Evan, Jay, and Steve must band together to stop them. Along the way, they encounter a series of wacky misadventures, including a run-in with a group of bumbling Slugs who are trying to take over a local convenience store.

Throughout the movie, the three main characters struggle with their own personal demons. Evan is a suburban dad trying to balance his family life with his desire for adventure and excitement. Jay is a slacker who has lost touch with reality, while Steve is a socially awkward scientist who is obsessed with aliens.

As the Slugs become more aggressive in their attacks, the three men must put aside their differences and work together to save humanity. Along the way, they discover that the Slugs are not just mindless monsters but rather a complex species with their own culture and motivations.

In the end, Evan, Jay, and Steve come up with a plan to defeat the Slugs by using a combination of science and humor. The movie ends with a comedic twist as the three men successfully defeat the aliens, but not before they realize that they've become more like each other than they ever thought possible.

Overall, The Watch is a hilarious and action-packed comedy that explores themes of friendship, paranoia, and the absurdity of modern life. With its talented cast and witty script, the movie is sure to delight fans of science fiction and comedy alike.

title: Ender's Game
tagline: This is not a game.
overview: Based on the classic novel by Orson Scott Card, Ender's Game is the story of the Earth's most gifted children training to defend their homeplanet in the space wars of the future.
plot:
Ender's Game is a science fiction film directed by Gavin Hood, based on the novel of the same name by Orson Scott Card. The movie was released in 2013 and produced by Gavin Hood, Gail Katz, and Ted Field.

The story takes place in a future where humanity is under attack by an alien species known as the Formics. To counter this threat, the International Fleet (IF) has been searching for a commander who can lead the war effort against the Formics. The IF discovers a young boy named Andrew "Ender" Wiggin, who is six years old and has exceptional intelligence.

Ender's mother, Mazer Rackham, was a renowned military commander who led the IF to victory in the first contact with the Formics. However, she died shortly after the war, leaving behind her three children: Peter, Valentine, and Ender. The International Fleet takes Ender away from his family and enrolls him in Battle School, a rigorous training program designed to prepare young students for command.

At Battle School, Ender is forced to fight against other students in simulated battles, known as "games." He quickly rises through the ranks due to his exceptional strategic thinking and leadership skills. However, Ender struggles with the moral implications of war and the pressure to conform to the IF's expectations.

As Ender progresses through the games, he forms close relationships with his fellow students, including Bean, a talented but awkward student who becomes one of Ender's closest friends. Meanwhile, Valentine, Ender's older sister, begins to question the morality of the war effort and the IF's motives.

The final game pits Ender against the most skilled opponents in the school, including a ruthless commander named Graff. In the end, Ender emerges victorious but at great emotional cost. He is forced to confront the harsh realities of war and the true nature of his training.

After graduating from Battle School, Ender is promoted to command a fleet of ships against the Formics. However, he soon realizes that the IF has been manipulating him throughout his training, using him as a pawn in their own game. The film ends with Ender's realization that he was used to lead a suicidal mission against the Formics, and that he may have become the very thing he was trained to destroy.

The movie received mixed reviews from critics but was praised for its visual effects and performances by Asa Butterfield as Ender Wiggin. However, some fans of the book criticized the film's adaptation, feeling that it did not accurately capture the complexity and nuance of Orson Scott Card's novel.

The Impossible is a 2012 disaster drama film directed by Juan Antonio Bayona, based on the true story of a family's survival during the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. The film stars Ewan McGregor and Naomi Watts as the parents, Henry and Maria Bennett, and their three children.

The movie begins with the Bennett family - Henry (Ewan McGregor), Maria (Naomi Watts), and their three children, Lucas (Tom Holland), Thomas (Samuel Joslin), and Simon (Oaklee Pendergast) - on vacation in Thailand. The family is enjoying a relaxing day at the beach when the tsunami hits, catching them off guard.

The film's opening scenes show the devastating effects of the tsunami, with widespread destruction and chaos. The Bennett family finds themselves separated from each other as they try to survive the disaster. Maria (Naomi Watts) manages to find her children, but Henry is nowhere to be found.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of the events leading up to the tsunami, including a conversation between Henry and his wife about their decision to take their children on vacation. We also see glimpses of the family's life before the disaster, showcasing their love for each other and their struggles as parents.

The majority of the film takes place in the aftermath of the tsunami, with Maria (Naomi Watts) desperately searching for her husband and trying to care for her injured children. The scenes are intense and emotional, capturing the fear, panic, and desperation that the characters experience during this traumatic event.

As Maria navigates the treacherous waters and debris-filled streets, she encounters other survivors who have lost loved ones or are struggling to cope with their new reality. Along the way, she meets a kind-hearted stranger (Martin McCann) who helps her on her journey.

Meanwhile, Henry (Ewan McGregor) is shown to be trapped under a pile of rubble, desperately trying to free himself and find his family. The scenes are intense and suspenseful, keeping the audience on the edge of their seats as they wonder if Henry will survive.

As the story reaches its climax, Maria finally finds her husband, but not before he has suffered severe injuries. The film's final act is a heart-wrenching portrayal of the family's reunion, with Maria nursing her injured husband and caring for their children.

The Impossible ends on a hopeful note, with the Bennett family slowly rebuilding their lives together. The film's conclusion is both poignant and uplifting, leaving the audience with a sense of hope and resilience in the face of adversity.

Overall, The Impossible is a powerful and emotional drama that captures the true story of one family's survival during the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. The film features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Naomi Watts and Ewan McGregor, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

title: [REC]³ Genesis
tagline: You may kiss the bride.
overview: A pair of newlyweds must fight to survive when their wedding reception descends into chaos and carnage when their guests become infected by a virus that turns them into hungry zombies.
plot:
[REC]³ Genesis is a 2012 Spanish action horror film directed and co-written by Paco Plaza. The third installment in the [REC] series, it largely abandons the found-footage format of the earlier films and runs concurrently with the first. Diego Martín and Leticia Dolera star as Koldo and Clara, newlyweds whose reception is overrun by the series' infection.

At their reception at a country estate, a veterinarian recently bitten by a dog turns violent, and the infection spreads through the party. The couple are separated in the chaos. Koldo hides in the kitchen with his cousin Adrián, Clara's sister Tita, the wedding photographer Atun and a copyright inspector nicknamed "Royalties", and all but the heavyset Atun escape through the air ducts. Outside, Royalties is killed by an infected policeman. The survivors take refuge in a chapel the infected cannot enter. Over the public address system, Koldo hears Clara say that she is alive and pregnant, and he sets out to find her.

Clara, hiding in the security room with the priest, flees with friends Rafa and Natalie while the priest holds off the infected with prayer. Koldo reaches the security room just in time to watch Adrián, Tita, his grandmother and others being killed. Natalie is bitten, and the entertainer "Sponge John" shoots Clara's infected mother before being bitten himself. Hearing a song Koldo is playing in the ballroom, Clara turns back, takes up a chainsaw and fights her way through the crowd, and is forced to kill Rafa after he is bitten. The reunited couple are surrounded until the priest's voice reading scripture over the speakers paralyzes the infected. In the garden, however, Clara is bitten by Koldo's grandfather, who is immune to the prayer because he is deaf. Koldo amputates her arm to stop the infection, but it fails. At the estate gates, surrounded by police and a GEO special operations unit, the couple share a last kiss before Clara turns and bites him, and both are shot dead holding hands.

Filmax greenlit the third and fourth films in 2010. Unlike the earlier installments, they were directed separately, with Plaza making Genesis and Jaume Balagueró the fourth. It was shot in Barcelona in 2011. The film premiered at the Grand Rex in Paris, screened at South by Southwest and opened in Spain on 30 March 2012. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 40% approval, faulting the loss of the handheld style. [REC] 4: Apocalypse followed in 2014.
