The story begins with Alex the lion (voiced by Ben Stiller), Marty the zebra (voiced by Chris Rock), Gloria the hippopotamus (voiced by Jada Pinkett Smith), and Melman the giraffe (voiced by David Schwimmer) living on a traveling circus, led by Stefano the lion tamer. However, their lives are turned upside down when they discover that the circus is in danger of being shut down due to financial difficulties.

The group decides to embark on a journey to Europe, where they hope to find a new home for the circus and save it from extinction. Along the way, they meet a new character, Vitaly (voiced by Sacha Baron Cohen), a Russian circus performer who becomes an ally to the group.

Upon arriving in Europe, the group discovers that Vitaly is being pursued by Interpol agents, led by Captain Chantel DuBois (voiced by Frances McDormand). The agents believe that Vitaly is wanted for his involvement in a jewel heist. However, it is revealed that Vitaly is actually innocent and has been framed.

As the group navigates through Europe, they face various challenges and obstacles, including being pursued by the Interpol agents and dealing with their own personal struggles. Meanwhile, Alex begins to question his identity as a lion and his role in the circus.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when the group discovers that Vitaly's real target is a valuable diamond necklace worth millions of dollars. The group decides to help Vitaly clear his name and find the real thief.

In the end, the group successfully outsmarts the Interpol agents and retrieves the stolen necklace. However, in the process, they also discover that the true mastermind behind the heist is none other than Stefano, who had been seeking revenge against the circus for abandoning him.

The movie concludes with the group returning to New York City, where they are welcomed back as heroes. Alex finally finds his place in the circus and comes to terms with his identity as a lion. The movie ends on a high note, with the group performing a musical number together, celebrating their newfound freedom and happiness.

Overall, Madagascar 3: Europe's Most Wanted is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and redemption. With its catchy musical numbers and lovable characters, it is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

plot:
In the Name of the King 2: Two Worlds is a 2011 fantasy adventure film directed by Uwe Boll and the sequel to In the Name of the King: A Dungeon Siege Tale (2007), which starred Jason Statham. Dolph Lundgren stars as Granger, a former special forces soldier, with Natassia Malthe, Lochlyn Munro, Aleks Paunovic and Natalie Burn. Shot in British Columbia, it was released on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States and Canada on 27 December 2011, with a 3D version included in the German Blu-ray edition.

Granger, a veteran of the special forces, lives a quiet life in modern-day Vancouver until a group of hooded assassins attack him in his home. After fighting them off, he is pulled through a time portal and finds himself hundreds of years in the past, in the forested medieval Kingdom of Ehb, a land torn apart by war. He learns that he is the subject of an ancient prophecy that foretells the arrival of a warrior from another world who will save the kingdom.

Reluctantly accepting his role, Granger joins an unlikely band of allies, including a female healer known as Manhattan, who accompanies him on his quest. His task is to destroy the leader of the sinister Dark Ones, a witch known only as the Holy Mother, whose power threatens the realm. As he travels through the war-ravaged countryside, Granger fights monsters, assassins and enemy soldiers, using both his modern military training and the medieval weapons of his new surroundings. Along the way he must earn the trust of his companions, who are suspicious of the strange warrior and his modern ways. Fighting against overwhelming odds, Granger must free the land from the evil tyrant Raven, save the kingdom from destruction and find a way to return to his own time.

The film received negative reviews, as was typical of Boll's films, with critics deriding its low budget, script and effects, although some reviewers noted that Lundgren brought a degree of conviction to the role. It was followed by a third installment, In the Name of the King 3: The Last Mission (2014), also directed by Boll.

plot:
Fullmetal Alchemist: The Sacred Star of Milos (Japanese: 鋼の錬金術師 嘆きの丘の聖なる星) is a 2011 Japanese animated fantasy action film based on Hiromu Arakawa's manga Fullmetal Alchemist. Produced by Bones following the success of the television series Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood and directed by Kazuya Murata, it features Romi Park as Edward Elric and Rie Kugimiya as his brother Alphonse, with Maaya Sakamoto, Toshiyuki Morikawa and Sakiko Tamagawa. It premiered in Japan on 2 July 2011, with audiences receiving an exclusive manga booklet, and was licensed by Funimation for release in North America in 2012.

The Elric brothers, Edward and Alphonse, pursue an escaped convict, Melvin Voyager, who uses an unusual form of alchemy, but he gets away. They learn that he escaped with only two months of his sentence remaining, and among his belongings they find a newspaper page from which a photograph has been cut. The missing image shows Julia Crichton, a young woman arrested for illegally entering Table City, a remote town on the border between Amestris and the neighboring country of Creta.

Intrigued, the brothers travel to Table City aboard a prison train, which is attacked by a wolf-chimera and by the Black Bats, flying fighters seeking to free what they believe are Milosian prisoners. Pursuing Melvin, the Elrics reach a prison, where he breaks through the walls to find Julia, and Miranda, the leader of the Black Bats, also tries to rescue her. Julia and Al fall into the Valley, a slum in the vast chasm surrounding Table City where the oppressed Milos people live, and Melvin reveals his true identity. The brothers learn that the Milosians, whose land was taken by Creta and Amestris, dream of reclaiming their homeland, and that their hopes rest on a legendary object known as the Sacred Star of Milos. As the Elrics become involved in the Milosians' struggle, they discover a terrible secret about the source of the star's power and a plot involving a dangerous form of alchemy.

The film received mixed reviews. Critics praised its animation, action sequences and the voice cast's return, but many felt it was a standard side story that added little to the franchise and that its new characters lacked depth compared with those of Brotherhood.

Upon reaching the top of the beanstalk, Jack and Isabelle discover that Riddoch is not just a mindless beast but a complex character with his own motivations and backstory. The giant's true intention is to steal the magical golden harp, which has the power to heal any wound.

As Jack navigates the giant's lair, he also discovers that Riddoch was once a human king who was cursed by an evil sorcerer. The curse transformed him into a giant, and he has been searching for a way to break it ever since.

Meanwhile, back in England, King Braemar is facing his own struggles as he prepares for war against the giants. He must also contend with his own son's disappearance and the pressure from his advisors to launch an attack on the giants before they can be defeated.

As Jack and Isabelle continue their journey, they face numerous challenges and obstacles, including a treacherous path that leads them deeper into the giant's lair. Along the way, Jack also discovers that he has a special connection to the magical harp and that it holds the key to breaking Riddoch's curse.

In the end, Jack and Isabelle successfully defeat Riddoch and shatter the curse that has been cast upon him. The golden harp is recovered, and King Braemar is able to launch a successful attack on the giants. However, the movie ends with a twist: Jack returns home as a hero, but he also carries with him the knowledge of his own destiny and the secrets of the magical world.

Overall, Jack the Giant Slayer offers a unique take on the classic fairy tale, exploring themes of identity, redemption, and the power of music. The film features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and a talented cast, making it a must-see for fans of fantasy adventure movies.

At the airport, Bob tells Teddy that she can go if she pays for the plane ticket herself. When the flight turns out to be overbooked and the airline offers a free ticket to anyone who gives up a seat, Teddy volunteers, and Amy leaves the plane to follow her.

Mother and daughter soon discover that the next available flight will not arrive until after Christmas. After Amy's argument with an airline employee gets them thrown out of the airport, the two set off on a chaotic cross-country journey by bus, by a battered rental car that does not survive the trip, and by hitchhiking, meeting a series of eccentric strangers along the way. Meanwhile, the rest of the family has its own troubles in Palm Springs: Bob suffers constant criticism from his disapproving mother-in-law, Charlie breaks things around the house, PJ gets a painful sunburn, and Gabe accidentally turns his grandfather into a video-game addict. As the holiday approaches, Teddy and Amy learn to appreciate each other while racing to reunite with the family in time for Christmas.

The film mixes road-movie misadventures with the family humor of the series, focusing on the relationship between a teenage daughter and her mother.

Good Luck Charlie, It's Christmas! premiered on Disney Channel on December 2, 2011, and drew about 6.9 million viewers on its original broadcast.

title: Small Fry
overview: A fast food restaurant mini variant of Buzz forcibly switches places with the real Buzz and his friends have to deal with the obnoxious impostor.
plot:
Small Fry, released as Toy Story Toons: Small Fry, is a 2011 American animated short film written and directed by Angus MacLane. The second short in the Toy Story Toons series built around characters from the Toy Story features, it premiered in theaters alongside the feature film The Muppets on November 23, 2011.

At the Poultry Palace, a fast-food chicken restaurant, Bonnie is disappointed with the Zurg belt buckle that comes with her kids' meal and asks for a Mini Buzz Lightyear instead, but the remaining ones are only for display. Inside the display case, one Mini Buzz complains that they will never be played with, while a Mini Zurg is happy to stay put. When Bonnie plays in the ball pit with Rex and the real Buzz, whom she has brought along, Mini Buzz slips out of the case, drags Buzz under the balls and takes his place. Bonnie's mother packs up the toys without noticing the switch. Mini Buzz convinces Rex that the ball pit plastic shrank him, but the other toys at Bonnie's house see through the impostor at once.

Buzz climbs out of the pit to find the restaurant closed for the night. Looking for a way out, he stumbles into a storeroom where discarded fast-food toys hold a support group for abandoned toys led by a mermaid named Neptuna. Taking Buzz for another castaway, the group makes him join the meeting, but during a role-playing therapy exercise he befriends Gary Grappling Hook and uses him to escape. At home, the other toys interrogate Mini Buzz and plot a rescue mission, only for Buzz to walk in on his own and confront the little impostor. Mini Buzz later opens up at the support group with Buzz beside him as his sponsor, and in a post-credits scene Mini Zurg is delighted with the electronic belt buckle as his new companion.

Tim Allen voices Buzz and Teddy Newton voices Mini Buzz, with Tom Hanks, Joan Cusack, Don Rickles, Estelle Harris, Wallace Shawn, John Ratzenberger and Timothy Dalton voicing Bonnie's other toys and Emily Hahn as Bonnie. Jane Lynch voices Neptuna and MacLane voices several characters, including Gary Grappling Hook. The toys in the short include a Condorman figure, a nod to the 1981 Disney adventure comedy Condorman, which MacLane joked might stir up interest in a gritty reboot.

title: Hamilton: In the Interest of the Nation
overview: Carl Hamilton manages to infiltrate an international gang that has stolen advanced Swedish GPS-guided missiles. plot:
Hamilton: In the Interest of the Nation (Swedish: Hamilton – I nationens intresse) is a 2012 Swedish spy thriller directed by the Danish filmmaker Kathrine Windfeld and supported by the Swedish Film Institute. Mikael Persbrandt stars as Carl Hamilton, the intelligence officer created by the novelist Jan Guillou, with Saba Mubarak, Jason Flemyng, Pernilla August and Gustaf Hammarsten in supporting roles. Conceived as the first part of a planned trilogy, it was followed by Agent Hamilton: But Not If It Concerns Your Daughter.

Carl Hamilton is a commander in Sweden's foreign intelligence service. After a rare moment of peace with his girlfriend, a Polish doctor living in Stockholm, he is sent on an undercover assignment in Central Asia to infiltrate an international gang of smugglers and arms dealers who are about to sell Swedish-made GPS-guided artillery shells to terrorists. His survival depends on convincing the criminals that he is Russian. When the dealers meet the buyers, the transaction collapses into violence, and Hamilton is forced to kill and flee, leaving the weapons behind.

Back in Sweden, he is reprimanded by a new superior and returns, after a four-month unexplained absence, to his girlfriend, telling her he wants to leave the service. But the trauma of his mission follows him into his sleep, and a nightmare ends in a tragedy that shatters his attempt at a normal life. His mentor, known as DG, persuades him not to turn himself in and sends him abroad to rescue a Swedish technician linked to the smuggled munitions. Hamilton uncovers a plot by Sectragon, an American private military company that hopes to ignite a new war for profit and even plans to assassinate a foreign head of state on Swedish soil, and he works with the PLO operative Mouna al Fathar to stop it.

The film was a box-office hit in Sweden, topping the charts on its release in January 2012 and becoming the most successful Swedish film of the year domestically, with more than 500,000 admissions. By the end of that month it had been sold to more than ten foreign markets. On its release Hamilton was frequently compared with James Bond, and reviews were mostly positive. Much of the film was shot in Jordan, standing in for several foreign locations.

Lawless is a 2012 American crime drama film directed by John Hillcoat, written by Andrew Dominik, and starring Tom Hardy, Shia LaBeouf, Jason Clarke, and Jessica Chastain.

The film is set in the early 1950s in rural Virginia, USA. The story revolves around the Bondurant brothers - Forrest (Tom Hardy), Howard (Jason Clarke), and Boot (Shia LaBeouf) - who live with their mother, Maggie (Margo Martindale), on a farm.

The family's life is disrupted when Forrest returns from World War II, bringing with him a newfound sense of purpose and a desire to leave the lawless world behind. However, his plans are soon derailed when he meets a local bootlegger named Pappy Bondurant (Tommy Lee Jones), who offers him a job as a driver.

As Forrest becomes more deeply embroiled in the world of organized crime, he begins to question his moral compass and the true nature of his work. Meanwhile, Howard and Boot struggle with their own demons, including Boot's troubled past and Howard's increasing instability.

The story takes a dark turn when Pappy Bondurant is murdered by a rival gangster, and Forrest is forced to take revenge on those responsible. The brothers embark on a violent and bloody quest for justice, which ultimately leads them down a path of destruction and chaos.

Throughout the film, Hillcoat explores themes of family, loyalty, and redemption, as well as the harsh realities of life in rural America during the 1950s. The cinematography is stark and unforgiving, capturing the bleak beauty of the Virginia countryside and the brutal violence that unfolds on screen.

The performances from the cast are outstanding, with Hardy delivering a nuanced and complex portrayal of Forrest, who struggles to reconcile his desire for redemption with the harsh realities of his world. LaBeouf brings a raw energy to his role as Boot, while Clarke is equally impressive as Howard, whose instability threatens to tear the family apart.

Overall, Lawless is a gripping and unflinching drama that explores the darker side of human nature. With its stunning cinematography and outstanding performances, it's a must-see for fans of crime dramas and those interested in exploring the complexities of the American South during the 1950s.

The movie ends on a positive note, with Greg reflecting on what he's learned from his summer vacation. Despite the ups and downs, Greg is grateful for the experiences he had and the friends who stood by him throughout it all.

title: Taken 2

overview: In Istanbul, retired CIA operative Bryan Mills and his wife are taken hostage by the father of a kidnapper Mills killed while rescuing his daughter.
plot:
Taken 2 is a 2012 action-thriller film directed by Olivier Megaton and written by Luc Besson and Robert Mark Kamen. The movie stars Liam Neeson, Maggie Grace, Famke Janssen, and Jon Voight.

The story begins with Bryan Mills (Liam Neeson), a former CIA operative who has retired to Istanbul, Turkey, where he lives with his wife Kim (Famke Janssen) and their young daughter Molly (Maggie Grace). However, their peaceful life is disrupted when Kim's family is kidnapped by the Abductions Club, a Turkish crime syndicate that demands $10 million in exchange for her safe return.

The kidnappers reveal that they have been tracking Bryan since his last adventure, and they are determined to make him pay for killing their leader, Murad (Arben Bajraktaraj), during his previous encounter with the Abductions Club. The group's leader, Rana (Ariane Labed), is a ruthless and cunning woman who will stop at nothing to get what she wants.

As Bryan tries to navigate this new threat, he must also contend with the Turkish authorities, who are skeptical of his claims that Kim was kidnapped by the Abductions Club. With the help of his daughter Molly, who has been trained in hand-to-hand combat and surveillance skills, Bryan sets out on a mission to rescue Kim and take down the Abductions Club.

As the story unfolds, Bryan's past comes back to haunt him, and he is forced to confront his own demons in order to save his family. The movie features plenty of intense action sequences, including a memorable fight scene between Bryan and Rana's henchmen at a nightclub.

Throughout the film, Liam Neeson delivers his signature performance as Bryan Mills, bringing his trademark blend of grit, humor, and vulnerability to the role. Maggie Grace shines as Molly, who proves herself to be a capable and resourceful young woman in her own right.

The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Bryan and Rana, which culminates in a thrilling finale that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats. In the end, Bryan emerges victorious, but not without scars - both physical and emotional.

Overall, Taken 2 is a gripping and entertaining action-thriller that delivers plenty of excitement and suspense. While it may not be as tightly wound as its predecessor, the movie still has all the ingredients that made the first film so successful: high-octane action, memorable characters, and a healthy dose of humor.

plot:
Wreck-It Ralph is a 2012 animated science fiction comedy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie takes place in a world where arcade games are alive, and follows the story of Ralph, an antagonist character from the classic arcade game Fix-It Felix.

The film begins with Ralph (voiced by John C. Reilly), a large, green, hulking monster who lives in the Nicelanders' arcade game "Fix-It Felix." In this game, Ralph's job is to wreck the apartment building so that Felix (voiced by Jack McBrayer) can fix it and earn points for the game. However, Ralph feels unappreciated and lonely, as he is only allowed to play with the Nicelanders' arcade games when no one else is around.

One day, Ralph decides to explore other arcade games to find a new purpose in life. He visits Sugar Rush, a fast-paced racing game where he meets Vanellope von Schweetz (voiced by Sarah Silverman), a glitchy and energetic character who becomes his friend. However, their fun is short-lived as Ralph discovers that the game's main character, Vanellope, has been banned from competing in the Sugar Rush Grand Prix due to her glitch.

Ralph decides to help Vanellope enter the tournament, but things become complicated when he realizes that the only way for her to compete is by exploiting a bug in the game. Ralph and Vanellope's friendship deepens as they work together to fix the bug and save the Sugar Rush Grand Prix.

Meanwhile, Felix becomes jealous of Ralph's newfound friendships and tries to sabotage his efforts. However, Ralph eventually finds a new purpose in life when he realizes that being an antagonist is not all bad - it allows him to have fun and be himself.

In the end, Ralph and Vanellope successfully fix the bug, and Vanellope wins the Sugar Rush Grand Prix. The movie ends with Ralph returning to Nicelanders' arcade game, but this time as a hero, having found a new sense of belonging and purpose in life.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a mix of 8-bit and 16-bit graphics that pay homage to classic video games. The voice acting is also excellent, with John C. Reilly bringing Ralph's lovable but gruff personality to life, while Sarah Silverman adds a fun and quirky touch to Vanellope.

Overall, Wreck-It Ralph is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and finding one's purpose in life. The movie features a talented voice cast, stunning animation, and a story that will leave audiences laughing and cheering for more.

title: Silver Linings Playbook

overview: After spending eight months in a mental institution, a former teacher moves back in with his parents and tries to reconcile with his ex-wife.
plot:
Silver Linings Playbook is a 2012 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by David O. Russell, written by David O. Russell and Chris Terrio, and starring Jennifer Lawrence, Bradley Cooper, and Robert De Niro.

The story revolves around Pat Solitano (played by Bradley Cooper), a former teacher who has just been released from a mental institution after being diagnosed with bipolar disorder. Pat's life is turned upside down when his wife, Nikki (played by Brea Bee), leaves him due to his erratic behavior and inability to cope with the pressures of everyday life.

Pat moves back in with his parents, Pat Sr. (played by Robert De Niro) and Dolores (played by Jacki Weaver), who are struggling to care for their son. Pat's father is a retired mechanic who has become increasingly reclusive since Pat's mother passed away, while his mother is trying to keep the family together.

Pat meets Tiffany Maxwell (played by Jennifer Lawrence), a young widow with her own emotional baggage. Tiffany is still grieving the loss of her husband, who died in a car accident, and is struggling to cope with her new reality. The two meet at a support group for people with mental health issues, where Pat is trying to work through his own demons.

As Pat and Tiffany spend more time together, they develop an unlikely friendship that gradually blossoms into romance. However, their relationship is complicated by Pat's ongoing struggles with bipolar disorder, as well as Tiffany's emotional unavailability due to her recent loss.

Meanwhile, Pat becomes obsessed with winning back his estranged wife, Nikki, who has moved on and started a new life with another man. Pat's fixation on Nikki drives him to participate in a dance competition at the local community center, where he meets Tiffany again.

As the story unfolds, Pat and Tiffany face numerous challenges, including their own personal demons, family conflicts, and societal expectations. Through a series of comedic misadventures and poignant moments, they learn to confront their emotions and find solace in each other's company.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Pat's father is diagnosed with dementia, forcing Pat to re-evaluate his priorities and take responsibility for his own life. In the end, Pat and Tiffany come together to support each other through a series of emotional breakthroughs, ultimately finding love and acceptance in each other's arms.

Throughout the film, David O. Russell masterfully balances humor and pathos, creating a narrative that is both heartwarming and heartbreaking. The performances by Bradley Cooper and Jennifer Lawrence are particularly noteworthy, as they bring depth and nuance to their characters' emotional journeys.

Overall, Silver Linings Playbook is a beautifully crafted film that explores the complexities of mental health, relationships, and personal growth. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and poignant storytelling, it has become a modern classic in the world of romantic comedies.

overview: An adaptation of the successful stage musical based on Victor Hugo's classic novel set in 19th-century France, in which a paroled prisoner named Jean Valjean seeks redemption.
plot:
Les Misérables is a musical drama film directed by Tom Hooper, released in 2012 by Universal Pictures. The film is based on the novel of the same name by Victor Hugo and features an all-star cast, including Hugh Jackman, Anne Hathaway, Eddie Redmayne, Amanda Seyfried, and Samantha Barks.

The story begins in 1815, six months after the June Rebellion in Paris. Jean Valjean (Hugh Jackman), a former prisoner who was released from prison after serving nineteen years for stealing a loaf of bread to feed his sister's seven children, is pursued by the ruthless police inspector Javert (Russell Crowe). Valjean seeks redemption and a new life, but Javert is determined to capture him.

Valjean meets Bishop Myriel (Mark Addy), who shows him kindness and compassion, teaching him the value of humanity. Valjean vows to use his newfound wealth and influence for good, and he becomes a successful businessman and mayor of Montreuil-sur-Mer.

However, Javert's obsession with capturing Valjean continues, and he eventually tracks him down in Paris. Valjean is forced to flee, but not before he rescues a young girl named Fantine (Anne Hathaway), who is forced into prostitution to support her daughter Cosette.

Valjean promises to care for Cosette after Fantine's death, and he raises her as his own. As Cosette grows up, she falls in love with Marius Pontmercy (Eddie Redmayne), a young revolutionary who joins the student-led uprising against the French government.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Javert is killed by Valjean during a confrontation at the barricades during the June Rebellion. Meanwhile, Cosette and Marius are separated from each other, and Cosette becomes ill with tuberculosis.

In the end, Marius finds Cosette again, and they reunite. The film ends with the characters coming together to mourn the loss of Javert and to celebrate their newfound freedom and love for one another.

Throughout the film, the music plays a crucial role in conveying the emotions and themes of the story. The iconic songs, such as "I Dreamed a Dream," "Do You Hear the People Sing?," and "One Day More," bring depth and complexity to the characters and their struggles.

The film received widespread critical acclaim for its performances, direction, and music. Anne Hathaway's powerful performance in "I Dreamed a Dream" earned her an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress.

title: Mr. Peabody & Sherman
tagline: He's Leaving His Mark On History
overview: A young boy and his dog, who happens to have a genius-level IQ, spring into action when their time-machine is stolen and moments in history begin to be changed.
plot:
Mr. Peabody & Sherman is a 2014 American computer-animated science fiction comedy produced by DreamWorks Animation, based on the "Peabody's Improbable History" segments of the animated series Rocky & Friends. Directed by Rob Minkoff and written by Craig Wright, it features the voices of Ty Burrell, Max Charles, Ariel Winter, Stephen Colbert, Leslie Mann and Allison Janney. The project was first conceived as a hybrid live-action film before being redeveloped as a fully animated feature in 2006, when Minkoff joined DreamWorks Animation to direct.

Mr. Peabody is a genius beagle, a Nobel laureate, inventor and gourmet, who has legally adopted a human boy, Sherman. Using his time machine, the WABAC, he teaches his son history first-hand. On Sherman's first day of school, he contradicts his classmate Penny Peterson about the legend of George Washington and the cherry tree, and a scuffle ensues in which Penny taunts him as a dog and Sherman bites her. The incident brings in Ms. Grunion, a child protective services agent who threatens to take Sherman away if she judges Peabody an unfit parent.

To smooth things over, Peabody invites Penny's family to dinner, but Sherman secretly takes Penny on a trip in the WABAC. She stays behind in ancient Egypt intending to marry King Tut, and Peabody and Sherman must rescue her. A power failure strands them in Renaissance Florence with Leonardo da Vinci, where the children crash his flying machine, and further adventures take them to the Trojan War. Strains emerge between father and son as Sherman learns of Grunion's plans, and when Sherman breaks the rules of time travel, a rip in the space-time continuum sends historical figures pouring into present-day New York. Peabody and Sherman must repair history together, with Sherman standing up for his father and those around them affirming that a dog can indeed be a loving parent.

Released by 20th Century Fox in March 2014, the film opened against 300: Rise of an Empire and earned about $275.7 million worldwide. Against a budget of $145 million, it was considered an underperformer, and DreamWorks Animation took a $57 million write-down. Critics generally responded favorably to its humor and visual inventiveness. It was followed by the Netflix series The Mr. Peabody & Sherman Show, with Chris Parnell voicing Peabody.

In the end, Katie is able to confront the spirit and break its hold on her family. However, not before it unleashes a terrifying attack on them, leaving them shaken and traumatized.

Throughout the movie, the filmmakers use clever camera work and editing techniques to create a sense of tension and unease. The use of found footage adds to the realism of the film, making the audience feel like they are experiencing the events firsthand.

Overall, Paranormal Activity 4 is a chilling horror film that builds on the success of its predecessors. It's a gripping story that explores themes of family, trauma, and the supernatural, leaving viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: From Up on Poppy Hill

overview: Two high schoolers find hope as they fight to save an old wartime era clubhouse from destruction during the preparations for the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.
plot:
From Up on Poppy Hill is a 2011 Japanese animated drama film written and directed by Gorō Miyazaki, the eldest son of Studio Ghibli's co-founder Hayao Miyazaki. The film is set in 1964, during the height of Japan's post-war economic boom.

The story takes place in the seaside town of Shirokane, where a group of high school students are struggling to find their place in the world. The main character, Umi Kitano, is a shy and introverted girl who has just transferred to Shirokane High School from a rural area. She becomes fast friends with Shun Kazama, a charismatic and confident student who is also an avid photographer.

As they explore the town together, Umi and Shun stumble upon a mysterious clubhouse hidden in the attic of a former school building. The clubhouse was once the hangout spot for the school's baseball team, but it has been abandoned since the team disbanded years ago. The two friends decide to restore the clubhouse to its former glory and make it their own secret hideout.

As they work on the clubhouse, Umi and Shun begin to uncover the town's history and secrets. They learn about the town's past glories as a major industrial center and the struggles of its people during World War II. They also discover that the clubhouse was once the site of a tragic accident that resulted in the death of several students.

Through their research, Umi and Shun develop feelings for each other, but they are hesitant to express them due to their different personalities and social status. Meanwhile, the town is facing a crisis as the local factory, which has been the backbone of the economy, announces its closure due to declining profits.

As the school year comes to a close, Umi and Shun must confront their own feelings for each other and find a way to save the clubhouse from being demolished. In the process, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, love, and the importance of preserving the past.

The film's title, "From Up on Poppy Hill," refers to the iconic poppy hill that dominates the town's landscape. The hill is a symbol of the town's history and resilience, and it serves as a backdrop for Umi and Shun's journey of self-discovery.

Throughout the film, Miyazaki explores themes of identity, community, and the power of human connection. He also pays tribute to the post-war generation in Japan, who were shaped by the country's tumultuous history and struggled to find their place in the world.

Overall, From Up on Poppy Hill is a poignant and beautifully animated film that celebrates the beauty of small-town life and the importance of preserving our collective past.

title: Cloud Atlas
tagline: Everything is Connected
overview: A set of six nested stories spanning time between the 19th century and a distant post-apocalyptic future. Cloud Atlas explores how the actions and consequences of individual lives impact one another throughout the past, the present and the future. Action, mystery and romance weave through the story as one soul is shaped from a killer into a hero and a single act of kindness ripples across centuries to inspire a revolution in the distant future.  Based on the award winning novel by David Mitchell. Directed by Tom Tykwer and the Wachowskis.
plot:
Cloud Atlas is a 2012 epic science fiction film directed by the Wachowskis and Tom Tykwer, based on the novel of the same name by David Mitchell. The film is presented as a series of interconnected stories that take place across different time periods.

The story begins in the present day (2034), where we meet Adam Ewing (Tom Hanks), an American lawyer who witnesses a ship's captain being attacked by a group of pirates. As he tries to help the captain, he discovers a mysterious tattoo on his hand that seems to be connected to a larger narrative.

The story then shifts to 1850, where we find ourselves in the midst of the Pacific Ocean, aboard the clipper ship "Rabha". We meet Dr. Henry Goose (Jim Sturgess), a young doctor who is traveling with his friend Autua (Ben Whishaw) on a mission to deliver medicine to the people of Rabha. As they navigate the treacherous waters, they encounter the enigmatic Captain Mace (David Gyasi).

The story then jumps forward in time to 1926, where we find ourselves in the midst of a lavish party hosted by the wealthy and influential Vidal (Hugo Weaving). However, as the night wears on, it becomes clear that something sinister is at play, and the guests begin to realize that they are trapped in a mysterious and deadly game.

The story then shifts again, this time to 2012, where we meet Sonmi-451 (Doona Bae), a young woman who is being held captive by the corporation Cloud Atlas. As she tries to escape, she discovers that she has a crucial role to play in the fate of humanity.

Throughout the film, we see these different storylines intersect and overlap, revealing a larger narrative that spans centuries and continents. Along the way, we meet a range of characters, each with their own unique struggles and triumphs.

One of the most striking aspects of Cloud Atlas is its use of non-linear storytelling. The film jumps back and forth in time, often without warning, and it can be difficult to keep track of the different storylines. However, this also allows for a rich and complex exploration of themes such as reincarnation, karma, and the interconnectedness of all things.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Sonmi-451 and the forces of oppression that seek to control her. As she fights to free herself and bring about change, we see glimpses of the other storylines coming together in unexpected ways.

The ending of Cloud Atlas is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the meaning and significance of the events that have unfolded. However, one thing is clear: this film is a masterpiece of storytelling, weaving together multiple narratives into a rich tapestry of human experience.

On the Road is a 2012 film that explores the themes of freedom, nonconformity, and the search for meaning in post-war America. The movie delves into the lives of its characters as they embark on a journey across the country, seeking adventure, love, and connection.

At its core, On the Road is a film about the allure of the open road and the sense of liberation that comes with it. The characters are drawn to the freedom and spontaneity that travel offers, and their journeys become a metaphor for the search for identity and purpose in life. As they move from place to place, they encounter various experiences, people, and landscapes that shape their perspectives and inform their values.

The film also explores the tension between individualism and conformity, as embodied by the characters' desire for independence and nonconformity versus the societal expectations of the time. The characters are drawn to the Beats, a literary and cultural movement that celebrated creativity, spontaneity, and nonconformity, but they also struggle with the constraints of mainstream society.

Furthermore, On the Road touches on the theme of love and relationships in a way that is both intimate and ephemeral. The film's portrayal of romantic relationships is marked by a sense of longing and impermanence, reflecting the characters' desire for connection and community in a world that often seems hostile to their values.

Ultimately, On the Road presents a vision of America as a land of possibility and promise, where individuals can come together to create something new and meaningful. The film's characters are drawn to this vision, but they also grapple with its elusiveness, reflecting the complexities and challenges of finding one's place in the world.

It is worth noting that the movie adaptation took some creative liberties with the original novel by Jack Kerouac, so while it captures the essence of the book, it may not be a direct representation of the author's vision.

plot:
Frenemies is a 2012 Disney Channel Original Movie, a teen comedy-drama anthology based on Alexa Young's novel of the same name. Daisy Mayer directed from a script by Dava Savel, Wendy Weiner and Jim Krieg, and the cast is led by Bella Thorne and Zendaya, then the leads of Shake It Up, alongside Nick Robinson, Stefanie Scott, Mary Mouser in a dual role, Connor Price, Dylan Everett and Jascha Washington, in his final film role. Set in the fictional town of Waterbury, New Jersey, it weaves together three stories of friends who turn into rivals and back again.

In the first, science prodigy Jake Logan is inseparable from his dog Murray. Popular classmate Julianne wants Jake as her science-project partner to secure another A, and the dog seems to see through her. To get Murray out of the way, she soaks Jake's prized NASA certificate in her perfume and slips it through his door; Murray, mistaking it for one of her love notes, tries to flush it, and the furious Jake tells him to leave. The runaway dog is taken in by Savannah, a skateboarder with a crush on Jake. When Jake uncovers the plot, Savannah exposes Julianne's habit of using people for grades, and Murray returns home.

In the second, best friends Avalon and Halley run a fashion web magazine called GeeklyChic. Cherie St. Claire of the New York publisher Burns Publications offers to buy it, but says only one of them can be senior editor and asks each to write a cover story to decide. Their rivalry escalates over an interview with a French pop singer, until he admits he is really an American named Johnny Frankewski. The girls choose to share the byline, which costs them the deal, but a television show picks up their story and GeeklyChic goes global.

In the third, tomboy Savannah and wealthy private-school girl Emma, who look exactly alike, swap lives, each believing the other has it better. Complications follow when Emma, posing as Savannah, flirts with Jake, and Savannah goes out with Emma's boyfriend Lance, but at Emma's birthday ball the girls make up and switch back, and the film closes with a dance.

The film was shot in Richmond Hill, Ontario, in the spring of 2011, and premiered on Disney Channel in the United States and Canada on 13 January 2012, drawing about 4.2 million viewers on its debut.

title: Compliance

Compliance is a 2012 American thriller written and directed by Craig Zobel, starring Ann Dowd, Dreama Walker, Pat Healy and Bill Camp. Based on his description, Sandra identifies Becky, a young cashier, as the suspect and brings her into the back office. Becky denies the accusation, but the caller insists that Sandra detain her until police officers arrive.

Speaking with calm authority and invoking legal consequences, the caller persuades Sandra to search Becky's belongings and then to strip-search her, claiming that the alternative is jail. Over the course of several hours, as Sandra returns to running the busy restaurant, the caller enlists other employees and finally Sandra's fiancé, Van, to watch over Becky, escalating his demands into increasingly degrading and abusive acts. Only when an older maintenance worker refuses to cooperate and Sandra calls her regional manager does the deception unravel. The police eventually trace the calls to a family man working as a telemarketer, and in the aftermath Sandra insists that she too was a victim.

The film examines obedience to authority and the ease with which ordinary people can be manipulated into participating in abuse.

Compliance premiered at the 2012 Sundance Film Festival, where it provoked strong reactions, and received a limited release in the United States in August 2012. It received generally positive reviews, with 89 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised its sensitive direction and strong performances. Dowd's performance as Sandra won the National Board of Review Award for Best Supporting Actress.

title: The Day
tagline: Fight. Or die.
overview: Open war against humanity rages. For five survivors – lost and on the run – the pursuit is relentless, the bullets are dwindling and the battle is everywhere. This is a 24-hour look into their lives.
plot:
The Day is a 2011 Canadian post-apocalyptic thriller film directed by Douglas Aarniokoski from a screenplay by Luke Passmore. It stars Shawn Ashmore as Adam, Dominic Monaghan as Rick, Shannyn Sossamon as Shannon, Cory Hardrict as Henson and Ashley Bell as Mary, with Michael Eklund as the leader of a cannibal tribe.

In a ravaged countryside, five survivors, the last of a group that once numbered twelve, wander in search of food and shelter while avoiding the savage cannibal tribes that roam the land, carrying two jars of seeds they hope to plant. Adam is haunted by flashbacks of the day he left his wife and daughter in the car while he searched a house for supplies, only for them to be taken. With Henson ill, the group shelters in an abandoned farmhouse. While cleaning up at a stream, Mary is chased by a tribal scout and shoots him. In the basement, the men find boxes of tins that turn out to hold rocks, setting off a trap that sounds an alarm, seals them in and kills Rick. Shannon and Mary kill the cannibals who come for the men, but one of them recognizes a tribal mark on Mary's thigh before she kills him. After freeing the men, Shannon knocks Mary out, and the survivors tie her to a chair. Adam, enraged by Rick's death, tortures her, cutting the mark from her skin until Henson stops him. Mary finally explains that she had nothing to do with the loss of Adam's family; she had slaughtered her own tribe in their sleep after they killed and ate her younger sister, who had broken her leg. She warns that the tribe that laid the trap is coming. The four burn Rick's body and fortify the house, and at night waves of attackers storm it. Henson dies saving Shannon, and when Shannon accidentally kills the tribal leader's young son, the leader sends his daughter to take revenge. At dawn the cannibals set the house ablaze with Molotov cocktails. Mary stays behind so the others can escape, only to find that Shannon has taken her shotgun shells, and Adam returns to save her, dying of his wounds. In the woods, the leader's daughter cuts Shannon's throat. After cremating Adam, Mary meets the girl, who feigns innocence before reaching for a blade, but Mary kills her first and walks away.

Shot in Ottawa in the fall of 2010, the film premiered at the 2011 Toronto International Film Festival and opened in 12 US theaters in August 2012, grossing $20,984. Reviews were mixed, with 31% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 41.

title: Julia X
overview: Meeting a man on the Internet, Julia decides to see him in person, only to get abducted and branded with the letter "x" by that guy. A game of cat and mouse follows, but the story has an unexpected twist.
plot:
Julia X (released in 3D as Julia X 3D) is a 2011 American horror thriller with darkly comic touches, directed by P.J. Pettiette, who devised the story, from a screenplay by Matt Cunningham, and produced by Dixie Theatrical Corporation on a budget of about $4 million. It stars Valerie Azlynn as Julia, Kevin Sorbo as a serial killer known only as the Stranger, and Alicia Leigh Willis as her sister Jessica, with Joel David Moore and Ving Rhames. It premiered on 24 September 2011.

Julia meets a man she has been chatting with online for a date at a restaurant but, uneasy, cuts the evening short. As she heads home he overpowers her in her car and forces her to drive to his lair, where he strings her up from a hook in his garage. She briefly frees herself and hides, but he catches her and brands her with the letter X, the mark he leaves on his victims. Bound in the back of his van, she discovers the body of a previous victim, branded W; while he is burying it she gets hold of the keys to her handcuffs and escapes, fleeing through fields and swamp to a derelict house and then an abandoned school building. There she ambushes him and knocks him out, and her sister Jessica drives up to collect her.

The tables turn. The sisters, it emerges, are predators themselves who lure men like him, and they take the unconscious Stranger home, tie him to a chair with barbed wire and torment him. Flashbacks reveal their abusive childhood, and tension grows between protective Julia and Jessica, who resents always playing second fiddle and wants to be the bait for once. When Jessica kidnaps Sam, a young mechanic from across the street, the situation spirals: the Stranger breaks free and a frantic chase through the house follows. In the end Jessica betrays her sister, stabbing Julia, killing the Stranger and setting the house on fire, then resumes the game under the name Julia Y, while a final shot suggests Julia may have survived.

Joel David Moore plays Sam and Ving Rhames appears in a role credited simply as The Man. In Germany the film ran into trouble with the ratings board, which refused it a theatrical certificate, and the uncut version was later placed on the country's index of media harmful to minors. Critic Christian Ihle of the taz praised its socio-political subtext and its entertaining middle section but found the opening chase dreadful.

title: The Imposter

overview: In 1994 a 13-year-old boy disappeared without a trace from his home in San Antonio, Texas. plot:
The Imposter is a thought-provoking documentary that delves into the complexities of identity, deception, and the human psyche. At its core, the film explores the theme of imposture, where one individual assumes the identity of another, often with devastating consequences.

Through the story of Frenchman Frédéric Bourdin, who impersonated a missing Texas boy named Nicholas Barclay, the documentary sheds light on the darker aspects of human nature. Bourdin's ability to convincingly adopt the persona of Nicholas, complete with fabricated memories and emotions, raises questions about the fragility of identity and the ease with which it can be manipulated.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. The Barclay family's experience is marked by a sense of loss and disorientation, as they struggle to come to terms with the fact that their son was not who he claimed to be. This narrative thread serves as a poignant reminder of the long-term effects of deception and the importance of authenticity in personal relationships.

Furthermore, The Imposter raises important questions about the nature of truth and how it can be distorted or manipulated. Bourdin's ability to create an elaborate web of lies and half-truths highlights the ease with which people can deceive others, often with devastating consequences. This theme is particularly relevant in today's world, where the spread of misinformation and disinformation has become a pressing concern.

Ultimately, The Imposter is a gripping and thought-provoking documentary that challenges viewers to confront the complexities of human nature and the fragility of identity. Through its exploration of imposture, trauma, and deception, the film offers a nuanced and unsettling portrayal of the darker aspects of human behavior.

plot:
Liberal Arts is a 2012 American romantic comedy-drama written and directed by Josh Radnor, who also stars as Jesse Fisher, a thirty-five-year-old college admissions officer. Elizabeth Olsen plays Zibby, a nineteen-year-old student, with Richard Jenkins, Allison Janney, Elizabeth Reaser, John Magaro and Zac Efron. Jesse, a New York college admissions officer who loves literature, is newly single and dissatisfied with his life and career. He believes that the happiest time of his life was his years at a small liberal arts college in Ohio, where he could read and study surrounded by like-minded people. When his favorite former professor, Peter Hoberg, invites him back to campus for his retirement dinner, Jesse eagerly returns.

There he meets Zibby, a sophomore drama student and the daughter of Peter's friends. They run into each other at a campus party and spend the next day together walking around the campus, talking about life, books and music. Jesse also reconnects with Judith Fairfield, his former professor of Romantic literature, whom he has long admired, and meets Nat, an eccentric free spirit, and Dean, a brilliant but depressed student who, like Jesse, always carries a book. After Jesse returns to New York, he and Zibby begin a correspondence through handwritten letters, sharing music and growing closer. Meanwhile, Peter, lost at the prospect of retirement, asks to stay on but learns that his replacement has already been hired. When Zibby invites Jesse back to campus, hinting that she is ready to take their relationship further, he must confront the sixteen-year age difference between them, his own nostalgia for a past that may not have been as perfect as he remembers, and what it means to grow up.

Liberal Arts received generally positive reviews, with a 71 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that, while it could have used more bite, it succeeded as a good-natured and surprisingly clever look at the addictive pull of nostalgia for youth. It scored 55 on Metacritic, and critics praised Olsen's and Jenkins's performances.

plot:
The Perks of Being a Wallflower is a 2012 American coming-of-age drama written and directed by Stephen Chbosky, based on his 1999 novel. Logan Lerman stars as Charlie, a withdrawn freshman, with Emma Watson as Sam and Ezra Miller as Patrick. Mae Whitman, Nina Dobrev, Kate Walsh and Paul Rudd, as his English teacher, co-star.

In 1991, Charlie, depressed since childhood and recently out of a psychiatric hospital, starts high school with no friends but his English teacher. He meets two seniors, the stepsiblings Patrick and Sam, who invite him to a party after the homecoming dance. There he discovers that Patrick is secretly seeing Brad, the closeted star quarterback. When Charlie reveals that his best friend killed himself the year before, Sam and Patrick take him into their group. Driving home, Sam stands in the back of the pickup in the Fort Pitt Tunnel as an unknown song plays. Charlie tutors Sam for the SAT so she can get into Penn State, and they grow close. Learning he has never been kissed, she gives him his first kiss, despite her crush on Craig. At a New Year's party, Charlie takes LSD and is overwhelmed by memories of his beloved Aunt Helen, who died in a car crash while buying his seventh birthday present.

Dating Mary Elizabeth, Charlie kisses Sam on a dare in front of her, and the group shuts him out. After Brad's father catches him with Patrick, Brad publicly turns on Patrick. When Brad's friends beat Patrick in the cafeteria, Charlie blacks out and fights them off, regaining his friends. The night before she leaves, she and Charlie kiss, but her touch triggers a disturbing flashback. Once she is gone, his mental state collapses, and he calls Candace, blaming himself for Helen's death. Candace sends the police. In the hospital, a psychiatrist helps him recover the repressed memory that Helen sexually abused him. When he is released, Sam and Patrick return, and the three drive through the tunnel to the now-identified song, David Bowie's "Heroes". Charlie stands in the truck bed, feeling alive and infinite.

Chbosky insisted on writing and directing. Filming took place in Pittsburgh in 2011. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival to a standing ovation and was released by Summit Entertainment on September 21, 2012, grossing about $33.4 million worldwide. title: Boyhood

overview: The film tells a story of a divorced couple trying to raise their young son. The story follows the boy for twelve years, from first grade at age 6 through 12th grade at age 17-18, and examines his relationship with his parents as he grows.
plot:
Boyhood is a coming-of-age drama film written and directed by Richard Linklater, released in 2014. The film follows the life of Mason Jr., played by Ellar Coltrane, from age 6 to 18 over the course of 12 years.

The film begins with Mason Jr. (played as a child) living with his parents, Mason Sr. (played by Ethan Hawke) and Olivia (played by Patricia Arquette), in Austin, Texas. The family is shown to be struggling financially, but they are loving and supportive. As the story progresses, we see Mason Jr. grow up alongside his siblings, including his older sister Samantha (played by Lorelei Linklater).

The early years of Mason Jr.'s life are marked by a sense of stability and normalcy, with his parents trying to provide for him and his siblings despite their financial struggles. However, as the years pass, we see Mason Jr. face various challenges, including bullying at school, romantic relationships, and family conflicts.

One of the most significant plot points in the film is the divorce of Mason Sr. and Olivia, which occurs when Mason Jr. is 14. This event has a profound impact on Mason Jr., who struggles to come to terms with his parents' separation. The film also explores Mason Jr.'s relationships with his friends, including his best friend, Joe (played by Kyle Chandler), and his romantic interests, including his first love, Jessica (played by Emma Wright).

title: A Few Best Men
tagline: You are cordially invited to absolute mayhem
overview: A groom and his three best men travel to the Australian outback for a wedding.
plot:
A Few Best Men is a 2011 Australian comedy film directed by Stephan Elliott from a screenplay by Dean Craig. Xavier Samuel stars as David Locking, a young British man who travels to the Blue Mountains of Australia for his wedding, accompanied by his three best men. The cast also includes Kris Marshall as Tom, Kevin Bishop as Graham, Tim Draxl as Luke, Laura Brent as the bride, Mia Ramme, Olivia Newton-John as her mother, Barbara, Jonathan Biggins as her father, Jim, Rebel Wilson as Daphne Ramme, Steve Le Marquand as Ray and Elizabeth Debicki as Maureen.

David meets Mia while on holiday in Tuvalu, and only a week later he proposes. The couple plan to marry at her family's home in the Blue Mountains, and David rounds up his three best friends from Britain to fly out and serve as his best men. Mia's father, Jim, is a politician, and the arrival of the rowdy groomsmen at a family wedding with so much at stake for appearances is a recipe for disaster.

Once the friends arrive, the wedding weekend quickly spirals out of control. The three accidentally make off with a stash of drugs belonging to Ray, a local drug dealer, who comes after them to get his property back. Further trouble follows when the father-in-law's prized ram ends up stoned, and the guests' antics escalate through a series of increasingly outrageous mishaps that threaten to derail the ceremony, embarrass the bride's family and test David's relationship with Mia before the couple can finally make it down the aisle.

A Few Best Men premiered at the Mill Valley Film Festival in California on 14 October 2011 and was released in Australia on 26 January 2012 and in the United Kingdom on 31 August 2012. Newton-John sang most of the soundtrack, which Universal Music Australia released in January 2012. The film opened on 235 Australian screens with $1.9 million, third for the week, and went on to earn about $5.3 million locally, the fourth most successful Australian film of the year. Reviews were mostly negative, with 18% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; SBS's Fiona Williams gave it one star and called it overlong and flimsy. However, David Stratton and Margaret Pomeranz each gave it four stars on At the Movies, Stratton singling out Newton-John as hilarious. The film was nominated for the AACTA Award for Best Original Music Score, and a sequel, A Few Less Men, followed in 2017.

title: Le Chef
tagline: Competition Can Be Delicious
overview: A veteran chef faces off against his restaurant group's new CEO, who wants to the establishment to lose a star from its rating in order to bring in a younger chef who specializes in molecular gastronomy.
plot:
Le Chef (French: Comme un chef) is a 2012 French comedy film directed by Daniel Cohen, starring Jean Reno as the celebrated chef Alexandre Lagarde and Michaël Youn as Jacky Bonnot, a talented but stubborn self-taught cook. The cast also includes Raphaëlle Agogué as Jacky's pregnant girlfriend Beatrice, Julien Boisselier as the restaurant's ambitious shareholder Stanislas Matter, Santiago Segura as a self-proclaimed expert in molecular gastronomy, Salomé Stévenin as Alexandre's daughter, Pierre Vernier as the restaurant's main shareholder Paul Matter and Kentaro as Alexandre's right-hand man.

Jacky Bonnot dreams of becoming a great chef, but his perfectionism and refusal to compromise keep getting him fired from restaurant jobs. With his girlfriend expecting a baby, he promises to take any work he can find and is hired as a painter at a retirement home, where he secretly helps the cooks transform the menu. News of his talent reaches Alexandre Lagarde, the star chef of the Cargo Lagarde restaurant and host of a television cooking show, who is facing a crisis of his own.

Lagarde's restaurant is at risk of losing one of its stars, and Stanislas Matter, the son of its main shareholder, wants to replace him with a younger chef specializing in fashionable molecular cuisine. Lagarde hires Jacky as an unpaid intern to help him reinvent his menu, but their clashing temperaments lead to constant conflict. As Jacky hides his new job from his girlfriend and their relationship suffers, the two chefs, aided by the retirement home's cooks, set out to understand molecular gastronomy and win over the critics who will decide the restaurant's fate.

The film satirizes trends in haute cuisine and the rivalry between traditional French cooking and molecular gastronomy, while telling a story of mentorship and second chances.

Le Chef had its international premiere at the 62nd Berlin International Film Festival in 2012 before its release in France in March 2012. Cohen Media Group distributed it in the United States.

title: Pixie Hollow Games
overview: Rosetta and new arrival Chloe band together to try to break the garden fairies' legendary losing streak in the Pixie Hollow Games, a sports spectacle filled with pixie pageantry, fantastic fairy events and hilarious surprises.
plot:
Pixie Hollow Games is a 23-minute animated television special based on Disney's Disney Fairies franchise, first broadcast on Disney Channel on 19 November 2011. Produced by Disneytoon Studios and animated by Prana Studios, it features the voices of Megan Hilty as Rosetta, Brenda Song as the newcomer Chloe, Jason Dolley, Tiffany Thornton and Zendaya, along with returning cast members Mae Whitman as Tinker Bell, Lucy Liu, Raven-Symoné, Pamela Adlon and Angela Bartys. Inspired loosely by J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan by way of Disney's adaptation, the story follows the fairies of Pixie Hollow as they compete in an Olympic-style tournament.

Rosetta, an elegant garden fairy who prefers beauty and comfort to hard work, meets Chloe, an enthusiastic new garden fairy who has been training for the Pixie Hollow Games, a contest between the different fairy talents. The garden fairies have never won and are expected to lose again, but Chloe is convinced they can change their luck. When the teams are chosen, Chloe has already volunteered, and to her dismay Rosetta is selected as her partner. Certain that they will be eliminated in the first round, Rosetta shows up for the opening night in a fancy gown.

The heavy favorites are the storm fairies Rumble and Glimmer, whose long winning streak has earned them championship rings for almost every finger. The first event is a frog-riding race, in which Rosetta's reluctance to get onto her frog causes chaos on the track, but the pair advance when another team's equipment fails. Over the following days, Rosetta and Chloe compete in dragonfly water-skiing, a game played with twig spheres and mouse polo, gradually climbing the rankings. As the competition becomes more intense, Rosetta begins to take the games, and her partner, seriously, but tensions arise between the two as they reach the final event, where they must face Rumble and Glimmer and discover what being a team really means.

The special was released on DVD in 2012, along with other short films from the franchise. It was originally planned as part of a series of specials and features in the Tinker Bell series and was followed by the theatrical feature Secret of the Wings (2012). Like the other entries in the franchise, it centers on friendship and on the different talents of the fairies, here celebrated through teamwork and sportsmanship.

title: Desire
tagline: Love, desire and complications...
overview: In a social context deteriorated by a countrywide economic crisis, the life of several people will be turned upside down after they meet Cécile, a character who symbolizes desire.
plot:
Q, released in the United States as Desire, is a 2011 French erotic drama written and directed by Laurent Bouhnik. Set in Cherbourg, the film follows a loose group of young people whose lives are disrupted by a woman who embodies desire. The cast includes Déborah Révy, Hélène Zimmer, Gowan Didi, Johnny Amaro and Johan Libéreau. The film attracted attention for its unsimulated sex scenes, which members of its cast later discussed publicly.

Cécile is a 20-year-old woman whose father has recently died. Unable to confront her grief, she throws herself into sexual encounters with a succession of partners, friends and strangers alike. At the same time she appoints herself a guide to the people around her, sometimes seducing them and sometimes counseling patience, offering frank advice on how to give and receive pleasure. Her sometime boyfriend is Chance, a small-time criminal who loves her but cannot satisfy her. His friend Matt, who works as a mechanic, keeps pressuring his girlfriend Alice to sleep with him, but Alice does not feel ready. Meanwhile Chance and his friends scramble to earn money while trying to stay out of reach of rival criminals they have crossed.

On a ferry, Cécile eavesdrops on a married couple, flirts with the husband and slips him her number. It emerges that the wife has suffered a traumatic experience that makes intimacy difficult for her, and the couple's discussions about Cécile become a way of approaching their own problems. Alice, too, becomes involved in helping them, arranging a meeting in which the husband and wife come together blindfolded in an attempt to repair their relationship.

At a party organized by a group of women, Chance arrives carrying the urn holding the ashes of Cécile's father, which she has never been able to deal with. He tells her that he loves her and challenges her to take care of herself as she tries to care for everyone else. They leave together, and as they drive along the coast Cécile finally scatters her father's ashes. Having failed to find peace through her many encounters, including ones with Chance, Matt and Alice, she discovers another path toward healing and tells Chance that she loves him, though she knows it will not be easy.

The film's explicit content made it a subject of controversy. Hélène Zimmer, one of the lead actresses, said in 2015 that she had taken the role because of the challenge it represented, but admitted that she would happily remove the unsimulated sex scenes if she could.

"2-Headed Shark Attack" is a campy, over-the-top horror-comedy that explores the theme of survival in the face of absurd and terrifying circumstances. The movie takes a satirical approach to the shark attack genre, exaggerating the dangers posed by a genetically mutated two-headed shark.

At its core, the film is about human resilience and the will to survive against all odds. The protagonist, Jill (played by Darlene Vogel), finds herself in a desperate fight for her life as she navigates the treacherous waters of the ocean. As the two-headed shark closes in, Jill must use her wits and resourcefulness to outsmart the beast and stay alive.

The movie also touches on themes of paranoia and the breakdown of social order in the face of chaos. As the shark attack escalates, the characters' behavior becomes increasingly erratic, revealing deeper psychological flaws and fears. This descent into madness serves as a commentary on how quickly society can unravel when faced with an existential threat.

Furthermore, "2-Headed Shark Attack" can be seen as a tongue-in-cheek critique of modern society's obsession with sensationalized media and the 24-hour news cycle. The film's absurdity and over-the-top plot twists serve as a commentary on how easily we can become desensitized to the horrors of the world around us.

Overall, "2-Headed Shark Attack" is a lighthearted, entertaining horror-comedy that uses its absurd premise to explore themes of survival, paranoia, and the human condition.

title: Absolutely Anything
tagline: Great power. Total irresponsibility.
overview: Eccentric aliens give a man the power to do anything he wants to determine if Earth is worth saving.
plot:
Absolutely Anything is a 2015 British science fiction comedy film directed by Terry Jones, written by Terry Jones and Graham Linehan, and produced by Phoenix Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Neil Clarke (played by Simon Pegg), an ordinary man who lives in London. On his 65th birthday, he receives a letter from God (voiced by Alan Rickman) informing him that he has been chosen to receive five gifts: anything he wants, and they will be granted instantly.

Neil is initially skeptical but decides to use the gifts for personal gain. He chooses a private island, a spaceship, a million pounds, an infinite supply of his favorite food (pizza), and the ability to make anyone do what he wants. However, things quickly take a turn when Neil's new life becomes too much to handle.

Neil soon realizes that having unlimited power and wealth comes with its own set of problems. He starts to use his gifts to manipulate those around him, including his friends and family. His newfound abilities also attract the attention of various celebrities, who are all vying for a chance to receive one of Neil's gifts.

As Neil navigates his new life, he begins to question the morality of his actions and the true nature of his gifts. He starts to realize that having absolute power can be both liberating and suffocating. Meanwhile, God (Alan Rickman) is watching from above, occasionally intervening in Neil's life to guide him towards a more positive path.

Throughout the movie, Neil encounters various characters who are all trying to get their hands on one of his gifts. These include a group of eccentric billionaires, a pop star, and even a group of aliens who are interested in studying human behavior.

As the story unfolds, Neil begins to understand that true happiness comes from within and that having absolute power is not as fulfilling as he thought it would be. In the end, Neil decides to give up his gifts and return to his ordinary life, realizing that being human is what truly makes him special.

The movie ends with Neil reflecting on the lessons he has learned and the importance of humility and gratitude. The film features a talented ensemble cast, including Kate Ashfield, Joanna Lumley, and Bill Nighy, among others.

Overall, Absolutely Anything is a witty and entertaining comedy that explores themes of power, morality, and the human condition. With its unique blend of humor and heart, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction and comedy alike.

title: Inside Llewyn Davis
tagline: At a crossroads in the music world, where success remains elusive.
overview: In Greenwich Village in the early 1960s, gifted but volatile folk musician Llewyn Davis struggles with money, relationships, and his uncertain future.
plot:
Inside Llewyn Davis is a 2013 black comedy-drama written, directed, produced and edited by Joel and Ethan Coen. Oscar Isaac, in his breakthrough role, plays a struggling folk singer in Greenwich Village in 1961, with Carey Mulligan, Justin Timberlake, John Goodman, Garrett Hedlund, F. Murray Abraham and Adam Driver. Loosely inspired by Dave Van Ronk's memoir, it features folk songs performed live in full, with music produced by T Bone Burnett. It premiered at Cannes in May 2013, winning the Grand Prix.

In February 1961, Llewyn Davis's solo album is not selling, he has no money and sleeps on friends' couches. After a set at the Gaslight Café he is beaten in an alley by a stranger in a suit. Waking in the apartment of the Gorfeins, an academic couple, he accidentally lets their ginger cat out, and ends up carrying it around the city. Staying with the singers Jim and Jean Berkey, he learns that Jean is pregnant and may be carrying his child; she furiously demands that he pay for an abortion. His sister urges him to go back to the merchant marine.

To raise money he joins Jim and Al Cody in recording a silly novelty song about space travel, taking a $200 fee instead of royalties. At the clinic he discovers that a former girlfriend he had paid to have an abortion two years earlier had in fact kept the child. At dinner with the Gorfeins he lashes out when Mrs. Gorfein sings the harmony of his late partner Mike, who killed himself, and the cat he returned turns out to be the wrong one.

Llewyn rides to Chicago with the gruff jazz musician Roland Turner and the silent beat poet Johnny Five. When Johnny is arrested and Roland lies unconscious after an overdose, Llewyn abandons the car and the cat. In Chicago he plays for the impresario Bud Grossman, who is unmoved and suggests he join a trio, which he refuses. Hitchhiking home, he hits a cat on the road. Back in New York he cannot ship out because his sister threw away his seaman's licence, and he drunkenly heckles a performer at the Gaslight. The Gorfeins' real cat, Ulysses, has found its own way home. The story loops back to the opening night: as a young Bob Dylan takes the stage, Llewyn is beaten in the alley by the heckled singer's husband.

Widely acclaimed, the film holds 92% on Rotten Tomatoes and earned two Academy Award nominations.

title: Noah
tagline: The end of the world is just the beginning.
overview: A man who suffers visions of an apocalyptic deluge takes measures to protect his family from the coming flood.
plot:
Noah is a 2014 American epic drama directed by Darren Aronofsky, who co-wrote the screenplay with Ari Handel. Inspired by the biblical story of Noah's Ark in the Book of Genesis and drawing on the Book of Enoch, it stars Russell Crowe as Noah, with Jennifer Connelly, Ray Winstone, Emma Watson, Logan Lerman and Anthony Hopkins. Paramount Pictures released it in North America on 28 March 2014, in 2D and IMAX, with a 3D conversion in other countries.

As a boy, Noah witnesses the murder of his father, Lamech, by Tubal-cain, a descendant of Cain who covets their land. Years later, Noah lives quietly with his wife Naameh and their sons Shem, Ham and Japheth. After a vision of a great flood, he takes his family to seek the counsel of his grandfather, Methuselah. On the way they find a massacred village and adopt its sole survivor, a young girl named Ila, whose wound leaves her unable to bear children. Pursued by the killers, they flee into the land of the Watchers, fallen angels who were turned into giant stone creatures as punishment for helping Adam and Eve after their banishment from Eden.

Methuselah helps Noah interpret his visions and gives him a seed from the Garden of Eden. When Noah plants it, water springs up and a forest grows instantly, convincing the Watchers that he is doing the Creator's work, and they help him build an enormous ark. Years later, as birds, snakes and other animals stream toward the nearly completed vessel, Tubal-cain and his army arrive to claim it. Noah defies him, declaring that there is no escape for the descendants of Cain, and the Watchers defend the ark. As the rains begin and Tubal-cain launches a desperate assault, Noah comes to believe that the Creator intends humanity, including his own family, to perish after the animals have been saved. His grim conviction tears his family apart, particularly when Ila, now married to Shem, unexpectedly becomes pregnant, and Noah must choose between obedience to what he believes is divine will and mercy.

Noah received generally positive reviews, with praise for its ambition, visuals and performances, although it drew criticism and controversy from some religious groups over its departures from scripture and was banned in several countries. It grossed over $359 million worldwide, making it Aronofsky's highest-grossing film.

Based on the Marvel Comics hero, it closely adapts "Who Is the Black Panther?", the story arc written by Reginald Hudlin and drawn by John Romita Jr., both of whom supervised the production, with Hudlin then serving as BET's president of entertainment; the main change from the comic is that Juggernaut replaces the Rhino. title: Terminator Genisys
tagline: Reset the future
overview: The year is 2029. John Connor, leader of the resistance continues the war against the machines. At the Los Angeles offensive, John's fears of the unknown future begin to emerge when TECOM spies reveal a new plot by SkyNet that will attack him from both fronts; past and future, and will ultimately change warfare forever.
plot:
Terminator Genisys is a 2015 science fiction action film directed by Alan Taylor, produced by Skydance Productions and Paramount Pictures.

The movie takes place in 2029, where humanity is on the brink of extinction due to Skynet's (a self-aware artificial intelligence system) takeover. The story follows John Connor (Jason Clarke), the future leader of the human resistance against Skynet, who sends a cyborg assassin, T-800 Model 101 (Arnold Schwarzenegger), back in time to 1984 to protect his mother, Sarah Connor (Emilia Clarke).

However, things don't go as planned. The T-800 is sent back in time but instead of protecting Sarah, it kills her and a young Kyle Reese (Jai Courtney) who was sent to be her protector. This event creates a new timeline where Skynet has already taken over the world.

In this new timeline, John Connor is now a grown man living with his foster family, the Furlans. However, he begins to experience strange visions and flashbacks of his future life as the leader of the human resistance. He soon discovers that the T-800 sent back in time has become a protector for him instead of his mother.

As John navigates this new reality, he teams up with a young Kyle Reese who is also trying to protect Sarah from the T-800. Together, they embark on a mission to prevent Skynet's creation and change the course of history.

Throughout the movie, there are several twists and turns that keep the audience guessing. The film features plenty of action sequences, including a memorable showdown between John Connor and the T-800 in a shopping mall.

While Terminator Genisys received mixed reviews from critics, it has its fans who appreciate the nostalgic value of seeing Arnold Schwarzenegger reprise his iconic role as the T-800. However, some viewers felt that the movie's plot was convoluted and didn't live up to the standards set by the original Terminator films.

Overall, Terminator Genisys is a fun, action-packed ride that explores the complexities of time travel and the consequences of altering the past.
