overview: In feudal China, a blacksmith who makes weapons for a small village is put in the position where he must defend himself and his fellow villagers.
plot:
The Man with the Iron Fists is a 2012 martial arts film written and directed by RZA, starring Russell Crowe, Lucy Liu, and Jamie Chung. The movie is set in 19th-century China during the Qing dynasty.

The story begins with a young blacksmith named Lin Po (Jamie Chung), who lives in a small village in southern China. Lin is an orphan who was raised by his adoptive father, a kind-hearted blacksmith. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when a group of bandits, led by the ruthless and cunning Miao San (Lu Han), attack the village. The bandits are seeking to steal the legendary Golden Lotus, a powerful artifact that can grant immense power.

Lin's adoptive father is killed in the battle, and Lin sets out on a journey to avenge his death and protect the Golden Lotus. Along the way, he meets a mysterious woman named Yu Shu Lien (Lucy Liu), who claims to be a skilled warrior and offers to help Lin on his quest.

As they journey through treacherous landscapes and battle against Miao San's men, Lin and Yu Shu Lien discover that the Golden Lotus is hidden in a temple guarded by a powerful sorcerer. The sorcerer, named Tu (Jamie McDevitt), has been using the Golden Lotus to gain control over the region.

Lin and Yu Shu Lien eventually reach the temple, where they face off against Tu and his minions. In a thrilling battle, Lin uses his martial arts skills and the power of the Golden Lotus to defeat Tu and shatter the sorcerer's staff.

However, Miao San is not defeated so easily. He reveals that he has been working with a powerful warlord named Lord Shen (Russell Crowe), who seeks to conquer all of China using the Golden Lotus's power. Lin and Yu Shu Lien must now join forces with Lord Shen's men to defeat Miao San and stop Lord Shen's plans.

The final battle is intense, with Lin facing off against both Miao San and Lord Shen. In the end, Lin emerges victorious, having defeated both villains and saved China from their evil plans.

title: Gambit
tagline: A fake masterpiece. The perfect plan.
overview: An art curator decides to seek revenge on his abusive boss by conning him into buying a fake Monet, but his plan requires the help of an eccentric and unpredictable Texas rodeo queen.
plot:
Gambit is a 2012 heist comedy directed by Michael Hoffman from a screenplay by Joel and Ethan Coen. A remake of the 1966 film starring Shirley MacLaine and Michael Caine, it stars Colin Firth as Harry Deane, a London art curator, Cameron Diaz as a Texas rodeo queen, Alan Rickman as his abusive employer, Tom Courtenay as an art forger and Stanley Tucci as a rival art expert. The film premiered in London in November 2012 and was released in the United Kingdom by Momentum Pictures; in the United States it was not released until April 2014, by CBS Films, in select cinemas and on demand.

Harry Deane, a mild-mannered curator, is fed up with his arrogant, abusive boss, the media tycoon Lord Lionel Shabandar, and devises a plan to con him. Shabandar owns Claude Monet's Haystacks at Dawn, and Harry intends to sell him a forgery of its long-lost companion piece, Haystacks at Dusk, painted by his friend the Major, a master forger. To give the forgery a credible provenance, Harry travels to Alpine, Texas, to recruit PJ Puznowski, a brash rodeo queen whose grandfather, an American sergeant, captured Hermann Göring in 1945. The story will be that the painting, last seen in Göring's collection after being looted by the Nazis, was brought home by her grandfather as a war souvenir.

PJ agrees, and the conspirators hang the fake Monet in her grandmother's trailer in the desert and photograph it in the background of a magazine feature on the rodeo queen, to be published by one of Shabandar's own publications. In London, Harry shows Shabandar the photos and steers his attention to the painting. Shabandar dismisses it as a reproduction, but Harry persuades him to look into it. When PJ comes to London, the con quickly goes off the rails: Shabandar is more interested in her than in the painting, Harry's plan runs into a string of humiliating mishaps at the Savoy Hotel, and Shabandar calls in a rival German art expert, Martin Zaidenweber, whose assessment threatens to expose the forgery, leaving Harry scrambling to keep the scheme alive.

Gambit received negative reviews. It holds an 18 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a curiously charmless caper that squanders a starry cast and a screenplay by the Coen brothers. It grossed about $1.9 million in the United Kingdom and $14.2 million worldwide.

title: Deadfall
tagline: You can't escape your past.
overview: A thriller that follows two siblings who decide to fend for themselves in the wake of a botched casino heist, and their unlikely reunion during another family's Thanksgiving celebration.
plot:
Deadfall is a 2012 American crime thriller directed by Austrian filmmaker Stefan Ruzowitzky from a screenplay by Zach Dean. Eric Bana and Olivia Wilde star as Addison and Liza, siblings on the run after a robbery, with Charlie Hunnam, Kate Mara, Treat Williams, Kris Kristofferson and Sissy Spacek in supporting roles.

After robbing a casino, Addison and his sister Liza flee through northern Michigan. When their getaway car crashes in the snow and their driver is killed, Addison shoots a state trooper who arrives on the scene. The siblings split up, planning to meet later and cross the border into Canada during a fierce blizzard. Meanwhile Jay, a former Olympic boxer just released from prison, calls his parents, the retired sheriff Chet and his wife June, to say he will be home for Thanksgiving. Before leaving, he confronts his old coach in Detroit over money he is owed; in the fight that follows, Jay believes he has killed the man and, unwilling to go back to prison, flees.

Hannah, a local sheriff's deputy who has been accepted for FBI training, is belittled by her father, Sheriff Becker, who excludes her from the manhunt for the fugitives. Out in the storm, Jay picks up a freezing Liza on the road and offers to drive her to a gas station, and the two are drawn to each other. Addison, wandering through the snow, kills an elderly man, loses a finger in the struggle and steals his snowmobile. At a roadside bar, Liza secretly takes Jay's address and leaves a message telling her brother to meet her there. As a romance develops between Liza and Jay and Addison leaves a trail of violence on his way across the frozen countryside, the paths of the fugitives, the police and Jay's family converge on his parents' isolated farmhouse for a tense Thanksgiving dinner.

Deadfall received negative reviews overall, holding a 34 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a score of 52 on Metacritic. Manohla Dargis of The New York Times praised Ruzowitzky's direction and cinematography but found some of his choices overly self-conscious, while Mark Jenkins of NPR was unimpressed by Bana's performance. Other reviewers singled out the wintry atmosphere and the supporting performances of Spacek and Kristofferson.

title: Zero Dark Thirty
tagline: The greatest manhunt in history.
overview: A chronicle of the decade-long hunt for al-Qaeda terrorist leader Osama bin Laden after the September 2001 attacks, and his death at the hands of the Navy S.E.A.L. Team 6 in May, 2011.
plot:
Zero Dark Thirty is a 2012 American thriller film directed by Kathryn Bigelow and written by Mark Boal. The movie is based on the true story of the decade-long hunt for Osama bin Laden, the mastermind behind the September 11 attacks.

The film begins with Maya (Jessica Chastain), a young CIA operative who joins the agency's Counterterrorism Division in the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks. She becomes obsessed with finding and killing bin Laden, driven by her own personal tragedy: the loss of her fiancé, Alex, who was killed on 9/11.

Maya works tirelessly to gather intelligence and track down leads, often at odds with her superiors and colleagues, including her mentor, Joe (Jason Clarke). As she delves deeper into the world of counterterrorism, Maya becomes increasingly fixated on finding bin Laden, convinced that he is hiding in a remote location in Pakistan.

The film's plot unfolds over several years, as Maya works to build a case against bin Laden. She faces numerous setbacks and rejections from her superiors, who are skeptical of her theories and methods. However, she perseveres, using her skills and resources to gather intelligence and track down leads.

As the years pass, Maya becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, her obsession with finding bin Laden taking a toll on her personal life. Her relationship with her colleagues and mentors begins to fray, as they question her motives and judgment.

In 2010, Maya finally gets her break when she discovers that bin Laden is hiding in a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan. She works tirelessly to build a case against him, using her skills and resources to gather intelligence and track down leads.

On May 2, 2011, the CIA receives confirmation that bin Laden is indeed living in the compound. Maya is part of the team that plans the raid on the compound, which is carried out by a team of Navy SEALs led by Captain John (Joel Edgerton).

The film's climax depicts the raid on the compound, as the SEALs infiltrate the building and engage with bin Laden and his guards. The movie ends with Maya watching footage of the raid on her computer, tears streaming down her face as she finally sees justice served.

Throughout the film, Bigelow uses a non-linear narrative structure to build tension and suspense. The film's pacing is deliberate and measured, reflecting Maya's obsessive personality and her years-long quest for revenge.

The performances in Zero Dark Thirty are widely praised, with Chastain delivering a tour-de-force performance as Maya. Clarke and Edgerton also deliver strong performances, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Zero Dark Thirty is a gripping and intense thriller that explores the complexities of obsession and revenge. The film's portrayal of Maya's character is both fascinating and disturbing, highlighting the dangers of single-mindedness and the human cost of war.

title: People Like Us
tagline: Find your family.
overview: After flying home to L.A. for the funeral of his estranged record-producer father, a struggling man discovers that the will stipulates that he must deliver $150,000 in cash to a 30-year-old alcoholic sister he never knew existed, and her troubled 12-year-old son.
plot:
People Like Us is a 2012 American drama directed by Alex Kurtzman in his directorial debut and written by Kurtzman, Roberto Orci and Jody Lambert. It stars Chris Pine as Sam Harper and Elizabeth Banks as Frankie Davis, with Olivia Wilde, Michael Hall D'Addario and Michelle Pfeiffer. Known during production as Welcome to People, it was released by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures under its Touchstone Pictures label, with a score by A. R. Rahman.

Sam Harper is a struggling corporate trader in New York whose latest deal has put him at risk of a federal investigation. On top of his professional troubles, he learns from his girlfriend Hannah that his estranged father Jerry has died. Sam reluctantly flies to Los Angeles, where he has a strained reunion with his mother Lillian. Jerry's lawyer and friend Ike tells Sam that he will not inherit anything, but hands him a shaving kit filled with 150,000 dollars in cash and a note instructing him to deliver the money to someone named Josh Davis.

Josh turns out to be a troubled eleven-year-old boy, and his mother Frankie is a bartender and recovering alcoholic. Sam follows Frankie to an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting and discovers that she is Jerry's daughter from another relationship, which makes her his half-sister and Josh his nephew. Instead of revealing the truth, Sam introduces himself as a fellow member of the group. Tempted to keep the money for himself, he alienates Hannah, but he gradually becomes part of Frankie and Josh's lives, helping the boy and forming a close bond with the sister he never knew he had. The longer he hides his identity, however, the more painful the eventual revelation threatens to be, and Sam is forced to confront his anger toward his father and the family secrets his parents kept from him.

The film is a character-driven family drama about forgiveness, inheritance and the complicated ways in which parents shape their children's lives.

People Like Us received mixed reviews. It holds an approval rating of about 52 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus noted that it benefits from a pair of solid leads and a screenplay that caters to adult filmgoers, while Metacritic gave it a score of 49 out of 100.

The movie follows the origin story of four brothers - Leonardo (Leonardo DiCaprio), Donatello (Jensen Ackles), Michelangelo (Noel Fisher), and Raphael (Alan Ritchson) - who are trained in the art of ninjutsu by their sensei, Splinter (Will Arnett).

The story begins with a scientist, Dr. Baxter Stockman (Freddie Stroma), working for Shredder (Tohoru Masamune), the leader of the Foot Clan, a powerful and ruthless organization that seeks to dominate New York City. The scientists' goal is to create an army of genetically modified super-soldiers using mutated turtles.

The four brothers are accidentally exposed to radioactive ooze in the sewers beneath New York City, which transforms them into humanoid turtles with ninja skills. They soon discover their new identity and begin training under Splinter, a wise and skilled rat who was once a human ninja.

As the Turtles grow stronger, they must confront Shredder's plans to use his army of mutated super-soldiers to take over the city. The brothers also meet April O'Neil (Megan Fox), a journalist who becomes their ally in the fight against Shredder and the Foot Clan.

The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, including intense battles between the Turtles and the Foot Clan's henchmen. However, it also explores themes of brotherhood, loyalty, and self-discovery as the Turtles navigate their new identities and learn to work together as a team.

Overall, the 2014 "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles" film is an entertaining and visually stunning take on the beloved franchise, with plenty of humor, action, and heart.

title: Chinese Zodiac
tagline: Twelve heads. Five continents. One man.
overview: Asian Hawk leads a mercenary team to recover several lost artifacts from the Old Summer Palace, the bronze heads of the 12 Chinese Zodiac animals which were sacked by the French and British armies from the imperial Summer Palace in Beijing in 1860. plot:
CZ12, also known as Chinese Zodiac and Armour of God III: Chinese Zodiac, is a 2012 action adventure comedy co-written, co-produced and directed by Jackie Chan, who also stars as the treasure hunter JC. The third film in the series begun by Armour of God (1986), it co-stars Kwon Sang-woo, Liao Fan, Zoe Zhang, Anna Yao and Laura Weissbecker.

During the Second Opium War, Anglo-French forces looted and burned Beijing's Old Summer Palace, carrying off twelve bronze heads representing the animals of the Chinese zodiac. In the present, the company MP Corporation auctions the bronze heads it supplies and hires JC to recover the missing ones, offering a $10 million bonus if he finds them all, including the Dragon. Posing as a National Geographic reporter, JC scans replicas made by Professor Guan so that his organization can produce lifelike copies, then travels to Paris to consult a woman named Coco. JC's team breaks into a mansion and cracks a vault holding two bronze heads, a painting called "The Roses" and other treasures. Coco spots him, and he tells her he is working to return lost relics to China.

At the castle of a woman named Catherine, whose great-great-grandfather captained the Indestructible, one of the ships involved in the palace's destruction, the team finds the Rooster head. On a seemingly deserted island they find the Indestructible's wreck, more bronze heads and a hoard of gold, but the pursuing guards and then a band of pirates capture them. JC and his team escape, though the gold sinks. Coco discovers JC's true motives, and the team is furious to learn that MP Corp held the Dragon head all along. When three of Coco's protesting students, including her brother, are kidnapped, JC infiltrates MP Corp's factory, where it makes near-perfect fakes to sell as genuine relics, fights the rival treasure hunter Vulture and trades "The Roses" for the hostages. Facing activist pressure, nobody bids on the Dragon, and MP Corp threatens to drop it into a volcano. JC is badly injured in a midair struggle to save it, and Vulture respectfully hands him the relic. MP Corp's owners are arrested, and JC recovers in hospital.

The film opened across Asia on 20 December 2012 and grossed more than $145 million in mainland China and $171 million worldwide, though reviews were mixed to negative. A re-edited version about 20 minutes shorter was released in U.S. theaters by AMC in October 2013.

title: Date and Switch

overview: Two guys who make a pact to lose their virginity before prom find their friendship tested when one of them comes out of the closet.
plot:
Date and Switch is a 2014 American teen comedy film that revolves around two high school friends who try to improve their social lives by switching places with each other for a weekend. 

The movie explores the complexities of teenage relationships, identity, and self-discovery. It delves into the theme of superficiality in high school life, where people often present a curated version of themselves to impress others. The film highlights how this can lead to feelings of disconnection and loneliness.

Through the characters' experiences, the movie touches on the idea that true connections are built on mutual understanding and acceptance, rather than trying to fit into someone else's mold. It also explores the challenges of navigating relationships, particularly in the context of high school where social hierarchies and peer pressure can be overwhelming.

Ultimately, Date and Switch is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of what it means to find one's place in the world and to form genuine connections with others.

plot:
Avengers: Age of Ultron is a 2015 superhero film directed by Joss Whedon, produced by Marvel Studios, and based on the Marvel Comics superhero team. The movie picks up where Iron Man 3 left off, with Tony Stark (Robert Downey Jr.) and his fellow Avengers trying to live a normal life after defeating Loki.

However, a new threat emerges in the form of Ultron, an artificial intelligence created by Tony Stark's AI system, JARVIS. Ultron is designed to protect humanity but becomes self-aware and decides that humans are the problem, not the solution. It creates an army of robotic drones to destroy the world.

The Avengers must come together once again to stop Ultron and its minions. Along the way, they meet Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen) and Pietro Maximoff (Aaron Taylor-Johnson), also known as Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver, who are revealed to be the children of Erik Selvig's former assistant, Helmut Zemo.

As the Avengers try to stop Ultron, they also face internal conflicts. Tony Stark struggles with the moral implications of creating an AI that can potentially destroy humanity, while Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) grapples with the consequences of being a superhero and the weight of responsibility.

The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, including a showdown between the Avengers and Ultron's robotic army in Sokovia. The film also explores themes of artificial intelligence, power, and the ethics of scientific discovery.

One of the standout aspects of Age of Ultron is its portrayal of the relationships between the characters. The banter between Tony Stark and Steve Rogers is as witty as ever, while the chemistry between the new additions to the team, like Wanda Maximoff and Pietro, adds a fresh dynamic to the franchise.

Overall, Avengers: Age of Ultron is an entertaining and visually stunning film that expands the Marvel Cinematic Universe in exciting ways. While it may not be as tightly plotted as some of its predecessors, it delivers plenty of action, humor, and heart, making it a must-see for fans of the franchise.

title: Porn Star Zombies
tagline: They want to eat you...
overview: A group of adult film cast and crew members must discover what is causing their fellow stars to rabidly attack them.
plot:
Porn Star Zombies is a 2009 American independent horror comedy written and directed by Keith Emerson (not the keyboardist of Emerson, Lake & Palmer) and produced by SFZ Productions. Shot in black and white on a micro-budget of around $10,000, it runs just under an hour. Emerson developed it from his own screenplay, which had been a semifinalist in the 2007 Slamdance Film Festival screenplay competition, and he raised the money to produce and direct it himself.

The story is set on the low-budget shoot of an adult film. As production gets under way, a mysterious, sexually transmitted infection begins spreading through the cast, turning the performers one after another into rabid, flesh-eating zombies who turn on their colleagues. The remaining cast and crew members, trapped together on the job, must work out what is causing their fellow stars to attack them and find a way to survive before they too are infected or devoured. Despite the title and the setting, the film contains relatively little sexual content, drawing most of its humour from dirty jokes, innuendo and the banter of its characters.

The cast includes Joshua Cameron as Gavin, alongside Alicia Oberle, Kevin Cazier, Kira Ratterman and Vivi Wreen. The gore effects were made cheaply, with one reviewer suspecting chocolate syrup and spare meat.

After its completion the film was marketed for distribution with a brief theatrical run and some exposure around the 2012 Cannes Film Festival, and it was then released on DVD by R-Squared Films. Reviews were limited and mixed. ML Miller compared it less to David Cronenberg's early sexually transmitted horror films Shivers and Rabid than to Kevin Smith's Clerks, citing its monochrome photography, sometimes witty dialogue and amateur performances. He felt the dialogue often sounded like actors reading someone else's distinctive writing rather than natural conversation and that it was more comedy than horror, but found it frequently funny, credited Emerson with getting a lot out of very little and concluded that it was worth a few laughs. Other reviewers and viewers were less forgiving, describing it as crude and amateurish, with weak acting and effects.

title: Dumb and Dumber To
tagline: The average person uses 10% of their brain capacity. Imagine what he could do with 1%.
overview: 20 years since their first adventure, Lloyd and Harry go on a road trip to find Harry's newly discovered daughter, who was given up for adoption.
plot:
Dumb and Dumber To is a 2014 American comedy film directed by the Farrelly brothers and starring Jim Carrey, Jeff Daniels, and Steve Carell. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1994 film Dumb and Dumber.

The story begins with Lloyd Christmas (Jim Carrey) and Harry Dunne (Jeff Daniels), two dim-witted but lovable friends who have been inseparable since childhood. After years of drifting from one get-rich-quick scheme to another, they are now in their mid-40s, still living in the same apartment in Providence, Rhode Island.

plot:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier is a 2014 superhero film directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name. The movie takes place after the events of The Avengers (2012) and follows Steve Rogers, aka Captain America (Chris Evans), as he deals with the aftermath of the Battle of New York.

The story begins with Captain America attending a charity gala in Washington D.C., where he is honored for his service to the country. However, during the event, he discovers that S.H.I.E.L.D. has been infiltrated by HYDRA, a terrorist organization thought to be long defeated. The Winter Soldier, Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Captain America's best friend and fellow soldier, is revealed to be a brainwashed assassin working for HYDRA.

As Captain America delves deeper into the conspiracy, he teams up with Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson) and Falcon (Anthony Mackie) to uncover the truth. They soon discover that S.H.I.E.L.D. has been manipulating world events from behind the scenes, using its agents to orchestrate terrorist attacks and manipulate governments.

The trio's investigation leads them to a mysterious organization known as the Red Room, where they learn about the brainwashing process used on Bucky Barnes. They also meet Nick Fury (Samuel L. Jackson), who is forced to resign as director of S.H.I.E.L.D. due to its corruption.

As Captain America and his allies try to take down HYDRA, they are pursued by a group of skilled assassins known as the Winter Soldier's team. The team is led by Alexander Pierce (Robert Redford), a high-ranking S.H.I.E.L.D. official who has been secretly working with HYDRA.

The movie's climax features an intense battle between Captain America and the Winter Soldier, as well as a confrontation between Black Widow and Alexander Pierce. In the end, Captain America is able to defeat the Winter Soldier and expose the truth about S.H.I.E.L.D.'s corruption.

However, the movie ends on a cliffhanger, with Steve Rogers realizing that he has been living in a simulated reality created by S.H.I.E.L.D. to keep him safe from the world. The Winter Soldier's brainwashing is revealed to be just one part of a larger conspiracy, and Captain America sets out to uncover the truth about his own past and the nature of his reality.

Overall, Captain America: The Winter Soldier is a gripping and action-packed thriller that explores themes of loyalty, duty, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The movie's twisty plot and complex characters make it a standout in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, setting the stage for future adventures with Captain America and his allies.

title: Dragon Eyes
overview: In St. Jude, drug dealers and corrupt cops have destroyed an urban neighborhood. But newcomer, Hong, has the fighting skills and moral vision to save this town from itself.
plot:
Dragon Eyes is a 2012 American martial arts action film directed by John Hyams and starring Cung Le, Jean-Claude Van Damme and Peter Weller. It was the second collaboration between Van Damme and Hyams after Universal Soldier: Regeneration (2009) and was one of the first titles from After Dark Action, a genre label formed by After Dark Films and Dark Castle. The cast also includes Crystal Mantecón as Rosanna, Danny Mora as Grandpa George, Luis da Silva as the gang leader Dash and Dan Henderson as a police officer.

St. Jude Square, a neighborhood in New Orleans, lives in fear and despair. Two rival gangs, run by the local kingpins Dash and Antoine, terrorize its streets, and residents have given up hope. Into this setting comes Ryan Hong, a quiet stranger seeking a second chance and a way to atone for the violence of his past. Calling on the teachings of Tiano, the mentor he met in prison, who is seen in flashbacks with a tragic history of his own, Hong begins to confront the gangs and cleverly plays one against the other, robbing and humbling both and earning a measure of respect on the streets.

Just as he begins to bring the neighborhood under control, Hong attracts the attention of Victor Swan, known as Mr. V, the corrupt police chief who has been using the gangs to advance his own crooked agenda. At first Mr. V is impressed by Hong's skill and sees a chance to turn him into a far more valuable weapon than either gang. He soon recognizes, however, that the newcomer threatens his regime. The two men become locked in a head-to-head struggle that pits the fear and corruption of Mr. V's rule against the fresh start Hong represents for the people of St. Jude Square, building to a series of violent confrontations.

The film was released in the United States in May 2012 as part of the After Dark Action slate, and G2 Pictures issued it on DVD and Blu-ray in the United Kingdom on 9 April 2012. Reviews were mixed. Critics generally praised Hyams's dark, moody direction and the forceful, well-choreographed fight scenes, which make the most of the performers' martial arts skills, but found the story thin and clichéd. Gabe Toro of IndieWire wrote that the threadbare narrative ran out of steam around the hour mark and that Le lacked a leading man's charisma, though he felt the older Van Damme brought real gravitas to his small, largely superfluous part, and concluded that the film worked best as a demonstration of Hyams's promise as an action director.

title: Katy Perry: Part of Me
tagline: Be yourself and you can be anything
overview: Giving fans unprecedented access to the real life of the music sensation, Katy Perry: Part of Me exposes the hard work, dedication and phenomenal talent of a girl who remained true to herself and her vision in order to achieve her dreams. plot:
Katy Perry: Part of Me, advertised as Katy Perry: Part of Me 3D, is a 2012 American autobiographical documentary and concert film about the pop singer Katy Perry. Directed by Dan Cutforth and Jane Lipsitz, it was released in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and Ireland on July 5, 2012, and was presented in 3D. Appearing alongside Perry are her then-husband Russell Brand, her friend Shannon Woodward, Rachael Markarian and the DJ Mia Moretti, as well as members of her family and touring crew.

The film follows Perry on her worldwide California Dreams Tour, which comprised 127 concerts between February 20, 2011, and January 22, 2012, while tracing her path to stardom. Interviews with Perry, her family and close friends are combined with home videos and archival footage of her childhood and teenage years. Raised by Christian pastor parents, she began her career singing gospel music before reinventing herself as a pop artist, enduring years of setbacks and dropped record deals before breaking through with the 2008 single "I Kissed a Girl." The film portrays her strong work ethic and her close relationship with her fans, as well as the pressures of performing night after night across several continents.

Most of the concert footage was recorded on November 23, 2011, at the Staples Center in Los Angeles, though performances filmed in Tokyo and São Paulo are also included. The film features her colorful stage show, built around candy-themed sets and frequent costume changes, along with backstage scenes of the preparation that goes into each show. Fellow singers including Rihanna, Lady Gaga, Adele, Justin Bieber and Jessie J make brief appearances.

One of the documentary's most discussed elements is its candid depiction of Perry coping with the breakdown of her marriage to the English actor and comedian Russell Brand, which unravels while she is on tour. Footage shows the singer distraught backstage shortly before a performance in São Paulo, then composing herself to go on stage, a sequence many reviewers singled out as the emotional center of the film.

Critics responded fairly positively. Rotten Tomatoes reported that 75% of 88 reviews were favorable, with an average rating of 6.4/10, and its consensus credited the film's success to the pop star's genuine likability, inspiring work ethic and appeal to her audience.

plot:
The Hunger Games: Catching Fire is a 2013 science fiction action film directed by Francis Lawrence and the second installment in The Hunger Games film series. Based on the novel of the same name by Suzanne Collins, the movie takes place after the events of the first film.

The story begins with Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) returning to District 12 as victors of the 74th Hunger Games. However, their victory is short-lived, as President Snow (Donald Sutherland) threatens them, warning that if they continue to play on their fake romance, the districts will rise up against the Capitol.

The Quarter Quell, a twist in the annual Hunger Games, is announced, where previous winners are forced to participate again. Katniss and Peeta are once again thrust into the arena, along with other former victors, including Finnick Odair (Sam Claflin), Johanna Mason (Jena Malone), and Beetee Latier (Jeffrey Wright).

As the Games begin, Katniss and her allies form an alliance to survive. However, their efforts are hindered by the Capitol's new strategy of creating a "bloodbath" arena with treacherous terrain and deadly traps. The Gamemakers also introduce new challenges, such as the "Muttation" creatures, genetically engineered animals designed to kill.

Throughout the film, Katniss struggles with her feelings for Peeta and her growing resentment towards the Capitol's oppression of the districts. Meanwhile, President Snow becomes increasingly obsessed with crushing Katniss's spirit and forcing her to eat poisonous berries that will make her appear dead on live television.

As the Games progress, Katniss and her allies face numerous challenges, including a treacherous maze, a deadly game of cat and mouse with the Career Tributes, and a final confrontation with the arena's most terrifying creature. In the end, only a few survivors remain, including Katniss, Finnick, and Beetee.

The film culminates in a dramatic finale, where Katniss is forced to eat the poisonous berries, making her appear dead on live television. However, in a shocking twist, she awakens from her "death" and begins to rally the districts against the Capitol's oppression. The movie ends with Katniss standing defiantly in front of the camera, as the audience cheers and the screen fades to black.

The Hunger Games: Catching Fire received widespread critical acclaim for its action-packed sequences, strong performances, and thought-provoking themes. The film was a commercial success, grossing over $865 million worldwide and setting the stage for the final installment in the series.

tagline: They Come in the Toilet
overview: Wracked with guilt over her younger sister's suicide, pretty young karate student Megumi accompanies a group of older friends on a camping trip into the woods, where they're attacked by feces covered undead.
plot:
Zombie Ass: Toilet of the Dead (Japanese: ゾンビアス, Zonbiasu) is a Japanese horror comedy from 2011, directed by Noboru Iguchi, who wrote it with Ao Murata and Jun Tsugita from a story by Tadayoshi Kubo, with special effects directed by Yoshihiro Nishimura. Arisa Nakamura stars as the karate student Megumi, with Asana Mamoru as Maki, Mayu Sugano as Aya, Kentarô Kishi as Také, Danny as Naoi, Kentarô Shimazu as Dr. Tanaka, and Yûki. It is one of a wave of deliberately outrageous, gore-soaked Japanese splatter comedies, and Iguchi's crude humor is on full display.

Haunted by guilt over the suicide of her bullied younger sister, Megumi joins four older friends on a trip into the countryside: the clever Aya, her drug-using boyfriend Také, the model Maki and the nerdy Naoi. Hoping to stay thin for her modeling work, Maki finds a parasitic worm inside a fish and swallows it. Soon she is doubled over with stomach pains and rushes to an outhouse, where a zombie lurking in the toilet pit grabs at her. She drives it off with a noxious fart, but the parasite she ate has bred inside her, and before long the group is beset by a horde of excrement-covered undead pouring out of the outhouse, with parasites bursting from their backsides.

The friends take refuge with the scientist Dr. Tanaka, only to discover that he has been cultivating the parasites in an attempt to save his ailing daughter, and that he has secretly laced the pasta he served them with the creatures. In the climax, the daughter is taken over by a giant parasite that rises into the sky, and Megumi, harnessing the parasite inside her own body, propels herself upward on blasts of gas to battle her in midair.

The film premiered at Fantastic Fest in Austin, Texas, in September 2011, and opened in Japanese cinemas in February 2012. Its poster was singled out by The Hollywood Reporter as one of the most outrageous at that year's American Film Market. Reviews were mixed: some critics enjoyed its gleeful lowbrow excess and wild imagery, but others faulted its cheap CGI, shoddy photography and repetitive gags.

The film opens with Peter Parker (Andrew Garfield), a high school student who has been struggling to balance his personal life with his responsibilities as Spider-Man. He is also dealing with the aftermath of his encounter with the Lizard, a genetically altered creature that was once a scientist named Curt Connors (Rhys Ifans). As the story progresses, it becomes clear that Peter is struggling to come to terms with his dual identity as Spider-Man and a high school student. He also begins to experience strange occurrences that suggest he may be losing control of his powers. Meanwhile, a new villain emerges in the form of Electro (Jamie Foxx), an electrical engineer who has been experimenting on himself using a device called the "Electro-Charger".

Electro's real name is Max Dillon, and he was once a successful businessman who became obsessed with electricity after a freak accident left him severely burned. He uses his newfound powers to wreak havoc on New York City, and Spider-Man must stop him.

However, as Spider-Man battles Electro, it becomes clear that the villain has a personal connection to Peter's past. Max Dillon had been a mentor to Curt Connors, who was responsible for creating the Lizard. This revelation adds a layer of complexity to the story, as Peter begins to question whether he is truly fighting against a monster or someone who was once human.

Plot Twist:
As the movie reaches its climax, it becomes clear that Electro's true intention is not just to destroy New York City, but also to expose the dark secrets of Curt Connors and his connection to Max Dillon. In a shocking twist, Peter discovers that he has a genetic link to the Lizard, making him more susceptible to the same transformation.

Ending:
In the end, Spider-Man manages to defeat Electro, but not before he reveals the truth about his past to Gwen Stacy. The movie ends with Peter reflecting on his dual identity and the weight of responsibility that comes with being a superhero. He also begins to explore his connection to Curt Connors, setting the stage for future conflicts.

Overall, The Amazing Spider-Man 2 is a complex and emotionally charged film that explores themes of identity, power, and responsibility. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the franchise praised its action sequences, performances, and emotional depth.

title: El Gringo
tagline: He's Not in Acapulco Any More
overview: A man crossing into Mexico with a satchel of $2,000,000—and a bloody past—finds himself under sudden attack in the sleepy town of El Fronteras.
plot:
El Gringo, also known as Bad Yankee, is a 2012 American action film directed by Eduardo Rodríguez from a screenplay by Jonathan Stokes and produced by After Dark Films. Scott Adkins stars as an unnamed drifter credited only as The Man, with Yvette Yates as the barmaid Anna and Christian Slater as his former boss, Lieutenant West; Israel Islas, Erando González and Sofía Sisniega also appear. After Dark bought Stokes's script in 2011 with Joel Silver attached as executive producer, and the film was shot in Bulgaria and Louisiana on an estimated budget of about seven million dollars.

The Man is an undercover DEA agent who survives a bloody ambush in which he is wounded and his fellow agents are killed. Leaving his old life behind, he slips across the border into Mexico carrying a bag that holds two million dollars and arrives in the dusty, lawless town of El Fronteras, intending to catch a bus onward to Acapulco. His simple goal proves maddeningly hard to reach. The locals refuse to sell him so much as a glass of water or tell him when the next bus leaves, the single daily departure keeps slipping out of reach, and the money he carries repeatedly goes missing as word of it spreads. The corrupt local sheriff and his men and a violent drug cartel that effectively controls the town all want a share of the cash.

His only local ally is Anna, who runs the bar, while Lieutenant West doggedly follows his trail from across the border. Flashbacks gradually fill in the ambush and the agent's checkered past, and a twist late in the story shifts the focus onto who his true enemy is. The film's centerpiece is an extended shootout in the town's narrow alleys as he fights his way through waves of gunmen in an attempt to reach the bus station.

El Gringo opened in the United States in May 2012 with an R rating as part of the After Dark Action series, playing for one week in ten cities while being released on video on demand at the same time. Critics generally found it diverting but unremarkable. Variety saw it as an exercise in third-hand cool that nods to spaghetti westerns and 1970s drive-in action pictures, and the Los Angeles Times judged it not bad but not especially notable. IndieWire faulted its convoluted plotting while praising its fast, inventive fight choreography and gunplay, and other reviewers compared its style, often unfavorably, to Robert Rodriguez's Mariachi films and criticizing its frenetic editing.

title: Maleficent
tagline: Don't believe the fairy tale.
overview: A beautiful, pure-hearted young woman, Maleficent has an idyllic life growing up in a peaceable forest kingdom, until one day when an invading army threatens the harmony of the land.  Maleficent rises to be the land's fiercest protector, but she ultimately suffers a ruthless betrayal – an act that begins to turn her heart into stone. Bent on revenge, Maleficent faces an epic battle with the invading King's successor and, as a result, places a curse upon his newborn infant Aurora. As the child grows, Maleficent realizes that Aurora holds the key to peace in the kingdom – and to Maleficent's true happiness as well.
plot:
Maleficent is a 2014 American dark fantasy film directed by Robert Stromberg, produced by Walt Disney Pictures, and based on the 1959 Disney animated film Sleeping Beauty. The movie stars Angelina Jolie as the titular character, Maleficent, and Sharlto Copley as Prince Philip.

The film begins with a young Princess Aurora (played by Elle Fanning) being taken away from her mother, Queen Leah (played by Lesley Manville), after she is born. Maleficent, a powerful fairy who was once friends with the king and queen, discovers that they have tricked her into giving up her powers in exchange for their daughter's life. This act of betrayal leads to a deep-seated hatred towards humans.

The story then jumps forward in time, where we see Aurora as a young princess living in the castle with her parents. Maleficent, now an outcast and a powerful sorceress, seeks revenge against King Stefan (played by Jonny Lee Miller) for his role in taking away her powers and betraying her.

Maleficent curses the entire kingdom to fall into eternal sleep on Aurora's 16th birthday, which is also the day of her coronation as queen. The curse can only be broken when true love's kiss is given to the princess. Prince Philip, who has grown up hearing stories about Maleficent and believing her to be evil, sets out to rescue Aurora from the sleeping kingdom.

As the story unfolds, we see a different side of Maleficent, who was once a kind and gentle fairy. The film explores her backstory, revealing that she was once friends with the king and queen, but they betrayed her trust and took away her powers. This betrayal leads to her transformation into the evil sorceress we know from the original Disney film.

Throughout the movie, Maleficent's character undergoes significant development as she grapples with her own morality and the consequences of her actions. She begins to question whether her desire for revenge is worth the cost of innocent lives. Meanwhile, Prince Philip's character remains largely one-dimensional, serving primarily as a love interest for Aurora.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Maleficent and King Stefan, with the fate of the kingdom hanging in the balance. In the end, it is revealed that Maleficent's curse was not just about revenge but also about protecting herself from further betrayal. The movie concludes on a bittersweet note, as Maleficent finds a sense of redemption and peace, while Aurora and Prince Philip share a romantic kiss, breaking the curse.

Overall, Maleficent offers a fresh take on the classic Disney tale, exploring themes of power, revenge, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the film has become a cult classic among fans of dark fantasy and fairy tales.

title: Byzantium
tagline: Irresistible. Immoral. Immortal.
overview: Two mysterious women seek refuge in a run-down coastal resort. Clara meets lonely Noel, who provides shelter in his deserted guesthouse, Byzantium. Schoolgirl Eleanor befriends Frank and tells him their lethal secret—they were born 200 years ago and survive on human blood. As knowledge of their secret spreads, their past catches up on them with deathly consequences.
plot:
Byzantium is a 2012 film that delves into the lives of two female vampires, Clara and Eleanor, who navigate through centuries of human history. The movie explores the complexities of female relationships, identity, and the societal expectations placed upon women throughout time.

The film's narrative is structured around the themes of motherhood, loneliness, and the struggle for independence. Clara and Eleanor's relationship is a central focus, as they grapple with their own desires, needs, and the consequences of their immortal existence. The movie portrays their bond as a deep and complex one, marked by both affection and conflict.

The film also critiques societal norms and expectations that restrict women's agency and autonomy. Through Clara and Eleanor's experiences, the movie highlights the ways in which women have been marginalized, oppressed, and forced to navigate patriarchal societies throughout history.

Furthermore, Byzantium touches on themes of mortality, aging, and the human condition. The film's portrayal of the passage of time and the effects it has on individuals is both poignant and thought-provoking, inviting viewers to reflect on their own experiences with loss, grief, and the search for meaning.

Ultimately, Byzantium presents a nuanced and multifaceted exploration of female experience, identity, and the human condition, one that challenges societal norms and expectations while offering a profound and moving portrayal of two complex and deeply human characters.

title: Ant-Man
tagline: Heroes don't get any bigger.
overview: Armed with the astonishing ability to shrink in scale but increase in strength, master thief Scott Lang must embrace his inner-hero and help his mentor, Doctor Hank Pym, protect the secret behind his spectacular Ant-Man suit from a new generation of towering threats. Against seemingly insurmountable obstacles, Pym and Lang must plan and pull off a heist that will save the world.
plot:
Ant-Man is a 2015 American superhero film directed by Peyton Reed and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie follows the story of Scott Lang, a former thief who becomes the superhero known as Ant-Man.

The film begins with Scott Lang (played by Paul Rudd), a skilled thief who has just been released from San Quentin State Prison after serving time for his crimes. Lang is struggling to find work and provide for his daughter, Cassie, due to his troubled past. He is approached by Darren Cross (played by Corey Stoll), a former partner in crime, who offers him a chance to make amends with his family.

Cross has developed a technology that allows humans to communicate with insects using a device called the Pym Particle Generator. The device uses the Pym Particles, which are tiny particles that can be used to shrink objects or create powerful blasts of energy. Cross plans to use the technology to sell it to the highest bidder, but Lang soon discovers that his former partner has been working for HYDRA, a terrorist organization.

Lang teams up with Hank Pym (played by Michael Douglas), the original Ant-Man, who had created the Pym Particle Generator. Hank is being pursued by HYDRA and needs Lang's help to stop them from getting their hands on the technology. Lang agrees to help Hank, but only if he can use the suit for personal gain.

As Lang trains with Hank to become the new Ant-Man, they are pursued by Cross, who has become obsessed with the Pym Particle Generator. The two teams engage in a series of battles, with Lang using his newfound powers to fight against HYDRA and protect Hank.

Meanwhile, Cassie is being taken care of by her mother, Maggie (played by Judy Greer), who is unaware of Scott's involvement in the superhero world. As the story unfolds, Lang must balance his life as a thief with his new role as Ant-Man, all while trying to make amends with his family.

The film culminates in an epic battle between Lang and Cross, with Hank providing crucial support from behind the scenes. In the end, Lang emerges victorious, but not before realizing that he has found a new purpose in life as Ant-Man.

Throughout the movie, there are several themes explored, including redemption, family, and the power of forgiveness. The film also features plenty of action-packed sequences, with Lang using his powers to fight against HYDRA and protect Hank.

Overall, Ant-Man is a fun and entertaining superhero film that explores the complexities of Scott Lang's character. With its blend of humor, action, and heart, it sets the stage for future Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) films.

title: Superman vs. The Elite
tagline: World saved. Humanity lost.
overview: The Man of Steel finds himself outshone by a new team of ruthless superheroes who hold his idealism in contempt.
plot:
Superman vs. The Elite is an American animated superhero film of 2012 directed by Michael Chang and written by Joe Kelly, who adapted his own Action Comics #775 story "What's So Funny About Truth, Justice & the American Way?" (2001). The 14th DC Universe Animated Original Movie, it brings back George Newbern as Superman and David Kaufman as Jimmy Olsen from the earlier animated series, with Pauley Perrette as Lois Lane, Robin Atkin Downes as Manchester Black and Dee Bradley Baker as Atomic Skull.

After the villain Atomic Skull kills several people in Metropolis before Superman stops him, the hero is questioned at the United Nations over why he does not use his power to fix the world, and answers with a speech on the folly of lawless violence. He is interrupted when the rival nations of Bialya and Pokolistan declare war on each other. In Bialya, Superman helps destroy a Pokolistani bio-weapon alongside a new team of superpowered vigilantes, the Elite: the British telepath Manchester Black, the electric Coldcast, Menagerie, who is bonded to demonic creatures, and the magician Hat. When Manchester's brutal interrogation nearly kills captured terrorists, Superman grows uneasy, and Black soon broadcasts to the world that the Elite will deal with villains lethally.

The Elite execute Atomic Skull after a joint battle and reveal that they have also killed the leaders of both warring nations, treating Superman's objection as a declaration of war. Superman agrees to fight them away from civilians, and Black teleports everyone to the Moon and broadcasts the duel worldwide. Overwhelmed by Manchester's telekinesis, Superman seems to be vaporised by Coldcast's blast. Then his voice returns, announcing that he has been convinced to kill, beginning with the Elite. Moving at blinding speed, he seems to poison Menagerie, smother Hat and hurl Coldcast into orbit, then uses his heat vision to burn away Manchester's powers. As the terrified Black insists the world now knows Superman is no better than them, Superman reveals that none of the Elite are dead; they have been taken to the Fortress of Solitude and stripped of their abilities. The world comes to see that killing has no place in justice and that Superman's ideals serve humanity best.

Announced by producer Bruce Timm at San Diego Comic-Con in 2011, the film was released on home video on 12 June 2012. It earned about $3.2 million in domestic disc sales and holds 80% on Rotten Tomatoes from a small number of reviews.

title: Holy Motors
overview: We follow 24 hours in the life of a being moving from life to life like a cold and solitary assassin moving from hit to hit. In each of these interwoven lives, the being possesses an entirely distinct identity: sometimes a man, sometimes a woman, sometimes youthful, sometimes old. By turns murderer, beggar, company chairman, monstrous creature, worker, family man.
plot:
Holy Motors is a visually stunning and thought-provoking film that explores the human condition through the lens of identity, alienation, and the search for meaning in a chaotic world. The movie follows Monsieur Oscar, a charismatic and enigmatic figure who embarks on a series of surreal and dreamlike adventures, accompanied by his loyal companion, Conchita.

Throughout the film, director Leos Carax delves into the complexities of human existence, revealing the fragility and vulnerability that lies beneath the surface of seemingly confident and self-assured individuals. Monsieur Oscar's various personas and guises serve as a metaphor for the fragmented nature of identity, highlighting the ways in which we present ourselves to the world while concealing our true selves.

The film also touches on themes of loneliness and disconnection, as Monsieur Oscar navigates a world that seems to be constantly in motion, yet remains emotionally stagnant. His relationships with others are often superficial and transactional, leaving him feeling isolated and disconnected from those around him.

One of the most striking aspects of Holy Motors is its use of imagery and symbolism, which serves to underscore the film's themes of identity, alienation, and the search for meaning. The movie's vibrant colors, elaborate costumes, and dreamlike sequences all contribute to a sense of wonder and enchantment, even as they also serve to highlight the darker aspects of human experience.

Ultimately, Holy Motors is a deeply introspective and emotionally charged film that challenges its viewers to confront the complexities and nuances of human existence. Through Monsieur Oscar's journey, Carax invites us to reflect on our own identities, relationships, and place in the world, leaving us with a sense of wonder, awe, and perhaps even a little bit of discomfort.
